title: Evaluating a large language model-powered system for semi-structured interview in health research.
abstract: Objectives: Conducting qualitative health research with marginalized populations presents persistent challenges related to trust, disclosure, and resource constraints. Traditional in-person interviews can be costly and difficult to scale, while participants may hesitate to share sensitive experiences openly. This study assessed the feasibility and acceptability of a large language model (LLM)-powered conversational interview system as an alternative to semi-structured qualitative interviews with marginalized populations in a community-engaged health research context. Materials and Methods: We developed a web-based, LLM-powered interview system informed by a community-based participatory research framework. The system was tested with 28 caregivers of children with asthma living in subsidized housing. Postinterview evaluation sessions and researcher observation notes were analyzed to assess the system's feasibility and acceptability and identify usability, accessibility, technical, and implementation considerations. Results: Participants reported that the system was easy to use and appreciated its empathetic and nonjudgmental tone. They also rated the system positively for clarity, comfort, and accessibility, indicating that conversational artificial intelligence (AI) systems can be adapted to support qualitative data collection in underserved communities. Identified challenges i…

title: Comparative evaluation of multiple linear regression, ARIMA, and artificial neural network models for electricity price forecasting in energy planning and cost optimization
abstract: Accurately predicting electricity prices may facilitate better planning of energy expenditures and enable utilities to make informed decisions regarding resource utilization and budget allocation. This paper examines forecasting models for electricity power rate prediction to support future energy cost optimization and management. Monthly energy consumption data were collected from January 2020 to June 2025, including average power rates (APR), average generation charge (AGC), average electricity consumption (AEC), and total demand (TD). Three forecasting models were compared: multiple linear regression (MLR), autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), and artificial neural networks (ANN). Model performance was evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) using validation data from July 2024 to June 2025. The ANN model achieved the most accurate forecast, with an MAE of 0.5922 PHP/kWh, RMSE of 0.7685 PHP/kWh, and MAPE of 6.81%. MLR yielded MAE, RMSE, and MAPE values of 0.9232 PHP/kWh, 1.1488 PHP/kWh, and 11.31%, respectively, while ARIMA (0,1,3) yielded 2.8820 PHP/kWh, 3.9610 PHP/kWh, and 25.78%, respectively. The findings indicate that ANN can accurately forecast electricity rates and support energy cost optimization, planning, budgeting, and decision-making process.

title: The Impacts of Climate Risk on the UK Economy: Time-Varying Evidence
abstract: This paper investigates the macroeconomic effects of climate change in the United Kingdom using a TVP-VAR model, which captures the evolving relationships between climate risk and key economic variables. To achieve this, we employ a novel Climate Risk Score Index. Our results demonstrate significant and time-varying impacts of climate risk on economic policy uncertainty and GDP, with pronounced effects observed during the Global Financial Crisis and the 2016 Brexit referendum. These findings underscore the importance of adaptive policy frameworks.

title: Low-loss frequency-tunable Josephson junction array cavities on Ge/SiGe heterostructures with a tapered etching approach
abstract: Abstract Ge/SiGe heterostructures represent a promising platform for hosting various quantum devices such as quantum dot spin qubits, Andreev spin qubits and gate-tunable transmons. However, the compatibility of such heterostructures with high-quality-factor microwave superconducting cavities remains a challenge due to defects in the material stack. In this work, we present an approach to enhance the coherence of cavity modes on a reverse-graded Ge/SiGe heterostructure, which consists of etching the full ∼ 1.6 μ m -thick Ge/SiGe stack down to its starting high-resistivity Si substrate, in order to pattern superconducting cavities directly on it. We engineer the mesa step to be tapered, so that it can be easily climbed by the superconducting cavities to reach the structures defined above the Ge quantum well. Using this approach, we observe internal quality factors of Q i ≈ 10 000 − 20 000 for high-impedance frequency-tunable Josephson junction array resonators, limited by the junction fabrication, and Q i ≈ 100 000 for 50 Ω coplanar waveguide Nb lift-off resonators. These Q i are preserved despite the overlap with the mesa structure in the climbing region, and are comparable to the ones obtained for identical resonators fabricated on a high-resistivity Si wafer reference. Thereby, this work paves a practical path toward superconductor-semiconductor hybrid devices, immediately ap…

title: WAEMU’s Urban Jungle: Can Good Governance Tame the Green Monster?
abstract: Urbanization in West African Monetary Union (WAEMU) has been rapid but can lead to environmental degradation. This study investigates the relationship between urbanization and environmental degradation from 2002 to 2022. While urbanization alone is not a major culprit, it can exacerbate environmental problems when combined with other factors. Strong institutions, particularly effective governance, are crucial for mitigating these impacts. The study recommends strengthening institutions, improving regulations, and fostering regional cooperation to address WAEMU’s environmental challenges.

title: Relational dynamics and experiences of inpatient and intensive community care for children and young people: matters for service engagement and recovery
abstract: Previous research on young people’s experiences of inpatient and community services has often relied on carers’ and relevant practitioners’ responses. This qualitative study was part of the wider IVY study, a Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) examining the effectiveness of Intensive Community Care Service (ICCS) versus Treatment as Usual (TAU; inpatient or core community Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services; CAMHS). The present study explored young people’s lived experiences of mental health care, with particular attention to the relational dimensions of service engagement and recovery. Fourteen young people participated in a semi-structured visual interview study to reflect on their service experiences, focusing on their recovery journey and engagement with services. A thematic decomposition analysis was conducted on the data, and specific themes of relational experiences of services were examined in-depth. Relational dynamics were central to young people’s accounts. Professional relationships characterized by trust, continuity, responsiveness and feeling listened to were described as important to engagement, while inflexibility, discontinuity and insufficient attention could constrain engagement. Peer relationships could provide understanding, solidarity and connection, although experiences varied. Family relationships could provide emotional safety, practical support …

Is There a Connection Between the Sino-US Tensions and Global Energy Market Uncertainty? Statistical Evidence From the GETS-VAR
abstract: We investigate the connection between Sino-US tensions and global energy market uncertainty using the GETS-VAR methodology for the period Jan 2001 to Oct 2022. The results indicate that increased tensions significantly boost energy uncertainty, with reciprocal effects intensifying geopolitical tensions. The investigation emphasizes the more pronounced influence of Sino-US tensions on energy uncertainty and accentuates the importance of economic policy uncertainty and energy prices. Suggested policy actions include improving energy management, expanding energy source variety, encouraging diplomatic interactions, and stimulating innovation to stabilize the global energy market.

title: Effect of FinTech and Energy Consumption in G-20 Countries: Evidence From Carbon Emission, Ecological Footprint, and Load Capacity Factor
abstract: This study investigates the interplay between FinTech, energy consumption, and environmental sustainability among G-20 countries from 2005 to 2022 using a Panel-VAR approach. The findings reveal that FinTech has a notable positive influence on environmental outcomes, non-fossil fuel energy use, and economic growth, while its impact on fossil fuel consumption is negative. Additionally, increased fossil fuel usage contributes to higher carbon emissions, whereas greater adoption of non-fossil fuel energy helps reduce emissions. Changes in the ecological footprint and load capacity factor are comparatively less pronounced. The research highlights the potential of FinTech platforms to foster green practices and support the adoption of cleaner technologies, suggesting that digital innovation can play a key role in advancing environmental sustainability within major economies.

title: Cryo-EM reveals a transmembrane allosteric site and activation mechanism for the SERCA calcium pump
abstract: Impaired sarco-endoplasmic reticulum Ca 2+ -ATPase (SERCA) activity contributes to defective calcium handling and cellular dysfunction in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, yet the structural basis of small-molecule SERCA activation has remained unknown. SERCA is a ubiquitous P-type ATPase that restores cytosolic Ca 2+ to the sarco-endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for cardiac Ca 2+ cycling and cellular energy homeostasis. Here, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to define how two chemically distinct activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, enhance SERCA function. Structures at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å resolution show that both compounds bind the same previously unrecognized activation hotspot in the transmembrane domain, a shallow groove formed by helices M3 and M4 and capped by M1. Despite limited chemical similarity, both activators share conserved interactions with Ser265 and Trp272 and stimulate Ca 2+ -dependent ATPase activity. Activator binding promotes a catalytically competent, calcium-bound E1-like conformation of SERCA that may involve altered protein-lipid interactions. These findings establish a structural framework for rational design of potent next-generation SERCA activators.

title: A Note on the Spillover of Geopolitical Risks in Nigeria Into Global Energy Markets
abstract: This study investigates whether domestic geopolitical risks in Nigeria extend into global energy-related uncertainties. To fulfil this objective, it employs time-varying Granger causality tests covering the period from January 2012 to October 2022. Observable spillovers are identified during significant events such as the EndSARS protests, herdsmen attacks, and the kidnapping of Chibok schoolgirls. These findings illustrate how Nigeria’s geopolitical turmoil impacts not only the country’s oil production and local economy but also the global energy markets. The results indicate a feedback loop where Nigeria’s geopolitical challenges amplify uncertainties around the world’s energy supply, which can further compromise Nigeria’s internal security.

title: A market-initialised accelerated failure time model for in-play football forecasting
abstract: Abstract In-play football forecasting models are rarely compared with betting exchange prices, which aggregate information from many market participants. We make this comparison for several goal-arrival models, focusing on a Weibull accelerated failure time model with two extensions: initialising team strength parameters from Betfair Exchange prices at kick-off to capture pre-match market information, and including cumulative shots as a time-varying covariate to capture in-play information. The initialisation, which fits team-strength parameters to 1X2 and over/under prices by squared-error minimisation, applies to any intensity-based goal arrival model. Evaluated across 280 English Premier League matches at minute intervals, the market-initialised model remains measurably weaker than Betfair in-play prices (classification accuracy 68.5 % versus 69.5 %, ranked probability score 0.1325 versus 0.1281), but retains interpretable team-level parameters and covariate effects. A comparison with a market-implied Poisson model, a Cox process and a Bayesian birth process, all initialised from the same pre-match odds, confirms that market initialisation is the dominant driver of predictive accuracy. A betting simulation against Betfair in-play odds yields a 1.0 % return on investment over 37,467 bets (95 % interval −3.8 % to 5.9 %), which we regard as preliminary given the limited sample …

Green Takaful as a Sustainable Financial Instrument in Malaysia's Islamic Capital Market
abstract: The growing convergence between Islamic finance and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) principles has opened a critical avenue for Takaful in the Islamic mutual risk-sharing system to formalise as a sustainable instrument within Malaysia’s Islamic Capital Market (ICM). Despite Malaysia’s pre-eminent position in global Islamic finance, green Takaful remains nascent in both scholarship and market practice, particularly relative to the well-established green Sukuk market. Employing qualitative document analysis guided by explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria, this paper examines the philosophical alignment between Maqasid al-Shariah and ESG principles, the current landscape of green Takaful products in Malaysia, and the regulatory enablers, structural challenges, and prospects for green Takaful as a formal ICM instrument. Findings confirm that Maqasid al-Shariah and ESG are deeply coherent, that Malaysia’s regulatory ecosystem in anchored by BNM’s VBIT Framework (2021) and the updated CRMSA Policy Document (2025), which provides a strong institutional foundation, and that green Takaful and green Sukuk are functionally complementary: the latter finances green assets while the former protects them. International benchmarking against the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Indonesia, and Sri Lanka confirms Malaysia’s comparative leadership, though a dedicated green Takaful ICM framework r…

A Pareto Superior Incentive Scheme for Residential Electricity Conservation: A Case Study of Shenzhen City in China
abstract: Shenzhen’s residential inclining tier rates are designed to encourage electricity conservation. However, the rates for customers with relatively low consumption fall below Shenzhen’s estimated marginal generation cost, leading to economically inefficient overconsumption. Therefore, we propose an incentive scheme with voluntary participation to promote residential electricity conservation. We further demonstrate that this scheme is Pareto superior, as its implementation can benefit participating customers without adversely affecting the electric utility or non-participating customers.

title: Likelihood based deep learning for volatility forecasting using Vietnam stock market data
abstract: Abstract Forecasting financial market volatility is essential for risk management, portfolio optimization, and investment decision-making. This study systematically investigates the effectiveness of likelihood-based optimization within a unified deep learning framework for financial volatility forecasting, using the Vietnam VN-Index as an empirical benchmark dataset. Daily closing prices of the VN-Index from 2000 to 2024, comprising 5932 trading days, are employed for empirical evaluation. A classical ARMA–GARCH model and two representative deep learning architectures, namely Deep Neural Networks (DNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), are evaluated under two optimization strategies: the conventional Mean Squared Error (MSE) objective and a likelihood-based optimization framework. Experimental results show that the LSTM model trained using the conventional MSE objective achieves the best overall forecasting performance under the adopted evaluation metrics, while the likelihood-based optimization framework demonstrates competitive predictive performance and stable convergence across different data partitions. The results further indicate that deep learning models generally outperform the ARMA–GARCH benchmark under the adopted experimental setting. Although likelihood-based optimization does not consistently outperform the conventional MSE objective in terms of point forecasting…

Digital Transformation for Traditional Market Competitiveness: a Systematic Literature Review
abstract: This study systematically reviews the fragmented literature on digital transformation in traditional markets to identify dominant themes and future opportunities. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, an initial search of Scopus (2000–2026) identified 1,712 records. After removing 112 duplicates, 1,600 records were screened, of which 270 were excluded at the title/abstract stage. The remaining 1,330 full-text records were assessed for eligibility, and 1,060 were excluded for being outside the subject scope or topically irrelevant. The final eligible corpus comprised 270 studies, comprising 41 core traditional-market studies and 229 contextual MSME/retail studies. All 270 studies were retained for VOSviewer bibliometric analysis, whereas the qualitative thematic synthesis was restricted to the 41 core studies that met the methodological quality threshold following MMAT/CASP appraisal (0 excluded at this stage). Bibliometrics highlight digital transformation (483 occurrences) as the central theme, interconnected with commerce (171), artificial intelligence (156), and competition (139). Despite this, specific research on traditional markets remains limited compared to broader SME studies, revealing significant gaps regarding cultural preservation, institutional support, and digital capability development. This review consolidates existing knowledge and proposes a research agenda to he…

title: The Impact of Recent Changes & Development in Indian Financial Market in Terms of Digi Currency & Tokenization
abstract: The recent initiatives taken by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDC) have led to a whole new dimension for the Indian Financial system. It increases finality for settlements, reduces credit risk and also allows programmable use cases. The ongoing process of expanding the digital rupee and tokenisation in both retail and wholesale sectors allow India to improve liquidity management and reduce value chains both domestically and internationally. In order to answer this research question it would be best to combine secondary research with primary perceptions. Research Design Type: Exploratory and Descriptive. Methodology: Mixed methods. Also the number of wallets being used. Review regulatory guidelines, whitepapers, and financial reports published between 2023 and 2026. Genomic Tools for Forecasting and Adaptive Management of Pink Salmon (Oncorhynchus gorbuscha) in the Sea of Okhotsk Basin
abstract: Pink salmon (Oncorhynchus gorbuscha) is the most abundant species of Pacific salmon in Russia, and its catch volumes largely determine the overall outcome of the salmon fishing season. At the same time, this species is characterized by pronounced interannual fluctuations in abundance, both in the total size of adult returns and in the abundance of individual regional stocks. These fluctuations substantially complicate reliable forecasting, particularly in the Sea of Okhotsk basin. Traditionally, forecasts of adult returns have been based primarily on ichthyological data; however, in recent years, genetic methods have become increasingly important in stock assessment. Genetic stock identification (GSI) allows the proportional contributions of different regional stocks to be estimated to mixed Pacific salmon aggregations (Dann et al. 2013; Van Doornik et al. 2024). In many cases, modern GSI relies on the simultaneous analysis of hundreds or even thousands of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and depends on next-generation sequencing (NGS) platforms for routine analysis (McKinney et al. 2022).

title: Service Quality and Price Perception in Building Materials Retail: Repurchase Intention as Mediator and Satisfaction as Moderator of Customer Loyalty
abstract: Background: Building materials retailing in West Java has become crowded and price-sensitive as construction activity rebounds and material costs rise, making customer retention a central problem for small independent stores. Evidence on how service and price evaluations become loyalty in this business-to-trade setting remains limited. Objective: This study examines the effect of service quality and price perception on customer loyalty through repurchase intention, and tests whether customer satisfaction moderates the link between repurchase intention and loyalty. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to July 2026 among 274 purposively selected customers of TB. Mulia Jaya, Sukabumi, who had purchased at least three times in the previous six months. Data were measured on a five-point Likert scale and analyzed with PLS-SEM using SmartPLS 4.1. Results: Service quality and price perception positively and significantly affect repurchase intention and customer loyalty; repurchase intention significantly affects loyalty and partially mediates both relationships. Customer satisfaction does not moderate the repurchase intention–loyalty link (β = −0.074; p = 0.103), although it has a direct positive effect on loyalty. The model explains 53.8% of loyalty and 31.7% of repurchase intention. Conclusion: Loyalty in building materials retail is built through b…

An Adaptive Knowledge eXploration optimiser with explainable hybrid feature selection for chronic kidney disease prediction
abstract: Early detection is key to limit the damage that can be caused by Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) and to improve the efficiency of treatment. The existing machine learning methods developed for the prediction of CKD employ fixed feature selection methods and optimization is performed without considering the same. To this end, a machine learning approach is developed based on Adaptive Knowledge eXploration Optimizer with Explainable Hybrid Feature Selection framework (AKXO-XHF) by integrating the AKXO algorithm with the XGBoost Classifier and SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP). The AKXO-XHF contains adaptive elements that have the “memory" of the previous solutions at a low computational cost. The model was tested on a set of 5,575 adults that were reconstructed from raw National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data from 2021 to 2023 (972 were labeled as having CKD), and an external set was used for NHANES 2017-March 2020 (8,165 adults), both with repeated nested cross-validation. AKXO-XHF reached an AUC of 0.807 (95% CI 0.800–0.815) with 12.1 of 22 inputs, compared with 0.812 using all inputs, and an AUC of 0.802 on the external cohort. Fusing cardiac ultrasound biomarkers with clinical data for exploratory risk prediction of composite endpoints in ischemic cardiomyopathy: a retrospective nomogram study
abstract: Objective To develop and validate a nomogram integrating echocardiographic biomarkers with clinical data to predict composite endpoint events in patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) and assess its value for individualized risk stratification. Materials and methods This retrospective cohort included 305 ICM patients hospitalized between January 2023 and January 2026, randomly assigned (7:3) to training ( n = 214) and validation ( n = 91) sets. Baseline data included NYHA class, conventional and advanced echocardiographic parameters (including LVEF, LVEDD, WMSI, E/e′, TAPSE, GLS, LASr, RV FWLS, and GWI), and laboratory biomarkers (NT-proBNP, hs-cTn, NLR, eGFR, LDL-C, and Hb). The primary outcome was all-cause death or heart failure (HF) rehospitalization. Independent predictors identified by univariable and multivariable logistic regression were used to build the nomogram; performance was assessed by ROC curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results The composite endpoint occurred in 55/214 (25.7%) training patients (18 deaths, 42 HF rehospitalizations, 5 both) and 23/91 (25.3%) validation patients (7, 18, and 2, respectively). Independent predictors were NYHA class (OR 2.758 per grade, 95% CI 1.698–4.479), GLS (OR 1.208 per 1% reduction in absolute GLS, 95% CI 1.063–1.372), LASr (OR 0.901 per 1%, 95% CI 0.840–0.966), GWI (OR 0.997 per 1 mmHg%, 95%…

title: Association of reduced CDH1 expression with epithelial–immune dysregulation and disease activity in inflammatory bowel disease: a multicohort observational study with development and internal validation of a diagnostic prediction model
abstract: Abstract Background Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by impaired intestinal epithelial barrier and dysregulated mucosal immunity. E-cadherin, encoded by CDH1, maintains epithelial integrity, but its relationship with mucosal inflammation and disease activity in human IBD remains unclear. Reliable biomarkers for active disease are needed. This study integrated public transcriptomic cohorts and a clinical validation cohort to evaluate CDH1 expression in relation to disease activity and immune microenvironment, and to develop and internally validate a diagnostic prediction model for active IBD. Methods Transcriptomic data from GSE75214 and GSE179285 were analyzed using WGCNA, functional enrichment, and immune deconvolution. A clinical cohort ( n = 115; 8 normal, 48 inactive, 59 active IBD) was used for qRT-PCR, immunohistochemistry, and multiplex fluorescence immunohistochemistry (mIHC). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression developed a diagnostic model, internally validated by 10-fold cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. This observational study followed STROBE and TRIPOD guidelines. Results CDH1 was downregulated in active IBD ( p < 0.001), validated across datasets, qRT-PCR, and IHC. title: Development and validation of an interpretable risk prediction model for in-hospital complications after total anomalous pulmonary venous connection repair
abstract: Background Previous studies of total anomalous pulmonary venous connection (TAPVC) repair have predominantly focused on predicting postoperative pulmonary venous obstruction and subsequent reintervention. However, early severe in-hospital complications after TAPVC repair remain insufficiently addressed, despite their immediate clinical relevance. We aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable risk prediction model for early in-hospital complications after TAPVC repair, incorporating both preoperative and intraoperative characteristics to facilitate early postoperative risk stratification. Methods and results A total of 908 pediatric patients who received TAPVC repaired were retrospectively included and then divided into derivation and validation cohorts based on region. We established four models to predict in-hospital complications. In-hospital complications included death and low cardiac output syndrome. After a comprehensive evaluation, the optimal-performing model was employed for patient prediction and stratification. The LR model demonstrated excellent discrimination (AUROC of 0.752, AUPRC of 0.519), outperforming the other ML algorithms in the validation cohort. Patients with a higher LR score had a significantly increased risk of adverse outcomes (adjusted OR: 6.609; P < 0.001). CPB duration, body surface area (BSA), preoperative intubation, emergence s…

title: Machine learning–based injury prediction models in athletes: a systematic review of predictive performance and injury-related outcomes
abstract: Background Machine learning (ML), a subfield of artificial intelligence (AI), is increasingly used to predict injury risk in athletes. However, the predictive performance, methodological reliability, and generalizability of these models across sporting contexts are not yet clear. In this systematic review, ML-based injury prediction models developed for athlete populations were examined in terms of performance metrics, validation approaches, predictor domains, and risk of bias. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus databases were searched from inception to January 15, 2026. Peer-reviewed studies that developed or evaluated machine-learning-based models predicting injury risk in competitive athletes were included in the review. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two researchers. Risk of bias was assessed using PROBAST. Due to heterogeneity among studies, findings were synthesized narratively in accordance with the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guideline. Results Of the 791 records identified, 17 met the inclusion criteria. Among the 15 studies reporting AUC for observed injury outcomes, the descriptive median of the representative study-level AUC values was 0.80 (IQR, 0.75–0.83), with reported values ranging from 0.63 to 0.99. title: Multi-lane highway trajectory prediction using attention-based Temporal Convolution and Transformer Network
abstract: Introduction Accurate trajectory prediction of surrounding traffic participants is essential for autonomous driving to ensure safe motion planning and navigation in complex environments. In this work, we propose a novel attention-based model to predict the behavior of the target vehicle and forecast its 5 s trajectory, with the goal of improving safety and driving efficiency. Methods The proposed model incorporates a multi-head attention mechanism (MHA) and a Temporal Convolution Network (ATCN) to model the temporal correlations and complex non-linear relationships among traffic participants. The model is also constructed by a Transformer (TF) based decoder that decodes the spatial-temporal dependencies efficiently for accurate trajectory predictions. Results and discussion Extensive evaluations on real-world NGSIM and highD datasets show the robustness of the model with a 6% reduction in RMSE for 5 s predictions. The model achieves RMSE of 2.11 m on NGSIM and 1.11 m on highD, outperforming existing methods. In addition, the influence of the driving style on the prediction accuracy is analyzed and the flexibility of the model to different traffic situations is emphasized. The proposed approach improves the ability of trajectory forecasting, which enhances the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems, and makes them better handle real-world traffic conditions.

MULTIMODAL DEEP LEARNING FOR EARLY SEPSIS PREDICTION USING MEDICAL IMAGING AND ICU DATA
abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition caused by a dysregulated response to infection, often leading to organ dysfunction and death. Early prediction remains challenging due to incomplete clinical measurements, variations in patient conditions, and complex ICU data. This study presents an implementation-based comparative investigation of five research papers related to sepsis prediction and artificial intelligence in healthcare. Three experimental methodologies are implemented: BiLSTM and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) for ICU time-series sepsis prediction, DeepCOVID-Fuse for integrating chest X-ray images with clinical variables, and CheXNet for automated chest X-ray classification. The obtained results are compared with those reported in the original publications to examine performance similarities and differences. Additionally, a systematic review of sepsis prediction techniques and a scoping review of Agentic AI in healthcare are analysed. Based on these investigations, a multimodal deep-learning framework is explored by integrating chest X-ray images and ICU clinical data using CNN-based feature extraction, a deep neural network (DNN), and feature-level fusion. SHAP and Grad-CAM are considered for explainability, while an Agentic AI support layer is proposed for data processing, risk analysis, and alert preparation. title: Ring–Core Matching Criterion for Two-Electron Au n (SR) n −2 Nanoclusters: Evaluating Au16(SR)14 Isomers and Guiding Structural Prediction of Au19(SR)17
abstract: Abstract Neutral two-electron thiolate-protected gold nanoclusters can adopt distinct core–shell structures despite having the same electron count. We develop a reference-based ring–core matching criterion to examine three Au16(SR)14 isomers and a proposed Au19(SR)17 structure, using the experimentally supported Au15(SR)13 topology as a benchmark. Calculations on methylthiolate models at four density-functional levels distinguish three geometric responses: Au16(SCH3)14-iso1 has a relatively uniform but outward-shifted core–shell interface; Au16(SCH3)14-iso2 exhibits pronounced Au4-core distortion and interfacial heterogeneity; and Au16(SCH3)14-iso3 retains a less-distorted Au4 core with a near-reference interface. The methylthiolate TD-DFT spectrum of Au16(SCH3)14-iso3 also shows the closest correspondence to the experimental Au16(2-PET)14 absorption features. The proposed Au19(SCH3)17 structure preserves a regular Au4-centered arrangement within a larger protecting shell. Additional PBE-D3(BJ) and PBE0-D3(BJ) full-ligand optimizations of Au15(SCTMS)13 and the three Au16(2-PET)14 isomers retain the principal geometric trends, although relative electronic-energy rankings remain dependent on the functional used. Together, the geometric and spectroscopic comparisons favor Au16(SR)14-iso3 among the Au16(SR)14 candidates examined and establish ring–core matching as a useful criterio…

title: Construction and validation of a prognostic prediction model based on albumin-bilirubin grade after resection of hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: BACKGROUND Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the world's major health problems and high recurrence after curative resection limits long-term survival. Existing prognostic tools, such as Child-Pugh score, are limited by subjective aspects. Albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) grade (objective lab parameters) is shown to have an advantage in assessing liver function and prognosis. Given the limitations of existing prognostic tools and the proven prognostic value of ALBI grade in HCC, there is a need to develop an integrated, objective prediction model for postoperative recurrence risk stratification. AIM To construct and validate a prognostic prediction model based on ALBI grade after HCC resection. METHODS We looked back at clinical data from 596 patients with HCC who had a radical hepatectomy from 2021 to 2023. Using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression, we identified independent predictors of recurrence-free survival (RFS). We then built a nomogram that combines these predictors to estimate 1- and 2-year RFS. RESULTS In the ALBI 2/3 group, the median RFS was 20.0 months. While the median RFS in the ALBI level 1 group was not reached at the end of the study, the differences between the two groups were statistically significant (P < 0.001). Multifactor Cox regression analysis showed that ALBI score, age, tumor size, tumor number, and alpha-fetoprotein levels were independent pred…

title: A transfer learning framework from recognition to functional prediction of antimicrobial peptides
abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are considered promising candidates for novel anti-infective agents due to their broad-spectrum activity and low propensity for inducing resistance. However, traditional wet-lab screening suffers from low throughput and high cost, while existing computational methods exhibit clear limitations in deep semantic representation and handling extreme data imbalance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a deep learning framework named BertAMP for AMP recognition and functional activity prediction. The framework integrates a lightweight BERT pre-trained language model, a multi-scale convolutional neural network (CNN), a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU), and a multi-layer perceptron (MLP). The model is first pre-trained on a binary AMP identification task to learn general sequence semantic representations. Subsequently, transfer learning is employed to inherit the pre-trained parameters into a joint prediction task covering 11 functional activities, and Focal Loss is introduced to mitigate class imbalance. On a constructed high‑quality dataset, systematic ablation experiments confirm the indispensable roles of the multi-scale CNN and BiGRU modules. Horizontal comparisons with mainstream tools show that BertAMP achieves an accuracy of 98.6% and an MCC of 0.964 on the basic identification task, and also performs comparably to or…

title: Development and validation of a postoperative prediction model for residual stones after hepatectomy in patients with hepatolithiasis
abstract: BACKGROUND Residual stones after hepatectomy for hepatolithiasis are associated with recurrent cholangitis, repeat interventions, and long-term biliary morbidity. Current classification systems assist in disease characterization and operative planning but fail to provide individualized risk estimates in the early postoperative period. AIM To develop and internally validate an early postoperative model for predicting residual stones in patients with hepatolithiasis after hepatectomy. METHODS This study included 300 consecutive patients who underwent hepatectomy between January 2019 and December 2022. Residual stones were identified by postoperative imaging within 1 year and classified as incomplete clearance rather than recurrence. The cohort was randomly split into a development dataset (70%) and a held-out internal validation dataset (30%), and 12 candidate prediction models were developed and compared. Within the development dataset, preprocessing, feature shrinkage, hyperparameter tuning, and algorithm selection were performed using repeated nested cross-validation (outer 5-fold cross-validation repeated three times; inner 5-fold cross-validation). The final model was then locked and evaluated in the held-out validation cohort. Model performance was evaluated based on discrimination, prediction error, calibration, threshold-based classification, and decision-curve analysis. …

title: Development of a Machine-learning-based Weld Bead Quality Prediction and Classification Model for Laser-directed Energy Deposition
Reaction Yield Prediction under Distribution Shift via Structured Chemistry-Aware Representation and Conditional Fusion
abstract: Abstract Reaction yield prediction is central to synthesis planning and reaction optimization, but reliable generalization beyond observed chemical space remains challenging. Here we propose a structured chemistry-aware framework for out-of-distribution reaction-yield prediction that encodes reaction-component topology, reaction-center priors, and chemistry-informed descriptors in parallel and integrates them through conditional graph–chemistry fusion. The method is evaluated on two public high-throughput experimentation benchmarks using additive-held-out Buchwald–Hartwig reactions and scaffold-held-out Suzuki–Miyaura reactions. Compared with a graph-only baseline, the proposed model reduces the mean split-level MAE by 17.2% across ten Buchwald–Hartwig additive-identity-held-out splits, while achieving MAE reductions of 19.2–35.5% across three Suzuki–Miyaura ligand-scaffold-held-out splits. Ablation results indicate that reaction-center guidance and chemistry-informed descriptors provide complementary improvements. These results suggest that chemically targeted inductive bias can improve reaction-yield prediction under distribution shift, although strongly shifted chemical regimes remain difficult for all tested methods.

Efficacy and safety of praziquantel, albendazole, and tribendimidine for Clonorchis sinensis infection: an updated systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
abstract: Background Clonorchiasis caused by Clonorchis sinensis remains a major food-borne parasitic disease in East Asia, imposing a substantial public health burden. Previous systematic reviews have predominantly focused on treatment efficacy, with limited systematic evaluation of safety profiles and benefit-risk trade-offs to guide clinical decision-making. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of pharmacological treatments for clonorchiasis. Seven electronic databases were searched from their database inception through the final search performed on 27 December 2025. Mixed binomial regression models were employed to compare cure rates and adverse event rates across regimens, followed by relative dose-response analyses, combined benefit-risk assessment, and stratified analyses by infection intensity. Results Twenty-five eligible studies comprising 67 treatment arms were included. High-dose multi-day praziquantel regimens achieved the highest cure rates (up to 97.2%) but were associated with high adverse event rates (58.3% for the standard 1-day regimen). Long-course albendazole regimens (≥4 days) achieved cure rates of 77%–87% with significantly lower adverse event rates (3.9%–5.3%), presenting the most favorable benefit-risk profile. Tribendimidine showed moderate efficacy with a favorable safety profile. Conclusion Praziquantel remains the efficacy benchmark for…

title: Addressing treatment non-response: A pilot study of inhibitory retrieval–focused exposure therapy
abstract: Background Inhibitory retrieval (IR-) focused exposure treatment may help overcome treatment non-response in anxiety disorders. However, evidence of its feasibility, acceptance, and effectiveness in this crucial patient group is lacking. Method We successfully re-invited patients with spider phobia who had not responded to the previous virtual reality exposure therapy (SpiderVR study) and responders. Additionally, we recruited healthy controls. Non-responders underwent an IR-focused one-session in vivo exposure with two conditions, i.e., with and without additional affect labeling. Pre- and post- treatment and at a 6-month follow-up, participants underwent clinical assessment, including self-reported symptom severity and a behavioral avoidance test. Applying multilevel models, we examined the feasibility, acceptance, and effectiveness. Exploratively, we described individual long-term trajectories. Results The additional IR-focused exposure produced lasting reductions in cognitive and behavioral symptoms in non-responders, with high adherence and acceptance rates. Additional affect labeling during IR-focused exposure had no effect. No associations were found with process variables related to potential mechanisms of change. Conclusion These findings suggest that implementing IR-focused exposure is feasible and well-received, offering clinical benefits to non-responders. Results u…

title: Hepatic pregnancy treated with ultrasound-guided microwave ablation after suboptimal methotrexate response, followed by two spontaneous pregnancies and term deliveries: a case report with 8-year follow-up
abstract: Background Hepatic pregnancy is an extremely rare abdominal pregnancy (<1% of ectopic pregnancies) with maternal mortality about 7.7 times that of tubal pregnancy. Most cases require surgery; reports on long-term fertility after nonsurgical treatment are very rare. Case presentation A 25-year-old G0P0 woman with 50 days of amenorrhea and elevated β -hCG showed no uterine or adnexal abnormalities on transvaginal ultrasound. After 1 week, β -hCG continued to rise. CT/MRI revealed a right hepatic lobe lesion; ultrasound showed a ∼1.5 cm × 1.5 cm lesion at the hepatic capsule in segment VII abutting the diaphragm, with a yolk sac but no embryo or cardiac activity. Given amenorrhea, rising β -hCG, and yolk sac, hepatic pregnancy was considered; “primary” was not used because histology was not obtained and secondary implantation could not be excluded. After informed consent, intramuscular methotrexate (80 mg on days 10 and 14) was given, but β -hCG decline was unsatisfactory and right hepatic pain developed, so treatment was converted to microwave ablation (MWA). Ultrasound-guided MWA was performed on day 16, and β -hCG gradually normalized. At 6 months and 3 years after treatment, she conceived naturally and delivered a son and a daughter at term, respectively. During 8 years of follow-up, she had one induced abortion and no recurrent ectopic pregnancy. Conclusions In reproductiv…

title: Systemic inflammatory dynamics, severe lymphopenia, and early treatment response during definitive chemoradiotherapy for cervical cancer
abstract: Background Chemoradiotherapy can alter circulating immune-cell abundance and inflammation-related indices in cervical cancer. Whether these changes primarily identify hematologic toxicity or provide meaningful information about early tumor response remains uncertain. Methods In a retrospective cohort, 274 records were screened and 240 patients receiving definitive chemoradiotherapy were included. Absolute lymphocyte count (ALC), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), C-reactive protein (CRP), and prognostic nutritional index (PNI) were assessed before treatment, at weeks 2 and 4, and three months after treatment. Grade ≥3 lymphopenia was defined as ALC <0.5 × 10 9 /L during the week-2 or week-4 assessment. Multivariable logistic regressions evaluated baseline determinants of severe lymphopenia and correlates of approximately three-month radiologic complete response (CR). Results Grade ≥3 lymphopenia occurred in 112/240 patients (46.7%), and 179/240 (74.6%) achieved CR. Median ALC decreased from 1.83 × 10 9 /L before treatment to 0.51 × 10 9 /L at week 4, whereas median SII increased from 515 to 1113 and NLR from 2.01 to 5.68. Severe lymphopenia was associated with lower baseline ALC, higher baseline SII and extended-field irradiation. Greater early ALC reduction and SII increase were observed among non-CR patients in unadjusted compar…

title: First-spike latency errors may distort spatiotemporal response patterns in a rapidly adapting afferent model
abstract: Introduction Rapidly adapting type 1 (RA) afferent neurons are thought to support tactile perception through precise spike timing. Accordingly, RA computational models and artificial mechanoreceptors should reproduce this timing accurately, yet the required temporal precision remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the temporal precision required to reproduce RA responses by investigating how delayed first-spike latency (FSL) at the single RA-unit level influences spatiotemporal population-level responses, particularly the formation of spatial event plots (SEPs). Methods We coupled a finite element model of fingertip skin deformation with a leaky integrate-and-fire neuronal model to reproduce RA responses. We performed multi-objective optimization with FSL and firing rate as objective functions and selected parameter sets located on the Pareto front as representative RA response properties. Using these parameter sets, we simulated the effects of delayed FSL on RA population responses to Braille, dot-pattern, and single-dot stimuli. Results The Pareto front included models that closely reproduced FSL and models that reproduced firing rate with delayed FSL. Parameter sets with single-unit FSL delays of tens of milliseconds, quantified under a probe-indentation speed of 9.5 mm s −1 , were associated with narrower SEPs and larger deviations from experimentally reported respons…

title: Blood is Still Thicker Than Water: A Response to Lin’s Reappraisal and Reflections on Historical Political Economy
abstract: A recent reappraisal by Lin expands Wang’s (2022, American Political Science Review 116, 896–910) dataset and questions the robustness of its main finding. In this response, I clarify broader challenges of measurement, case selection, and inference in historical political economy. I show that my original finding—that kinship-network concentration is negatively associated with support for state-building reforms—remains robust across multiple coding strategies. I also acknowledge that two high-leverage cases, the Lü brothers, matter for inference; rather than treating them as removable anomalies, I argue that their extreme values are theoretically meaningful features of kinship-network structure. Finally, I engage Lin’s regional interpretation and show that regional status competition does not account for the observed relationship once measurement and estimation issues are addressed. More broadly, this exchange illustrates how transparent measurement and sustained dialogue between quantitative and qualitative evidence can generate cumulative knowledge from fragmentary historical archives.

title: Author’s Response: Rule and its Wages
abstract: In his magisterial study On Politics , Alan Ryan asserts that “Plato’s political thought is anti political.” 1 A related (if weaker) distinction has been championed by thinkers ranging from Du Bois to Arendt to Rancière to Wolin, opposing two kinds of politics: roughly, politics as hierarchical rule, versus politics as popular participation, struggle, and action. Before and in The Souls of Black Folk , for example, Du Bois adhered to what Robert Gooding-Williams calls “a Platonist picture of the rule of the thinking, knowledgeable few … over the benighted, ignorant many, who can socially integrate their lives by obeying the directives of their betters.” 2 Readers may therefore wonder what is new or distinctive in Of Rule and Office: Plato’s Ideas of the Political. 3 Does this work not simply reiterate the view of Plato as progenitor of hierarchical “rule,” as against a more participatory vision of politics?

title: Dietary carbohydrate quality, ovarian response, and oocyte maturity: evaluating the role of glycemic index and load in assisted reproduction
Сombined laser irradiation effects at the cutaneous infl ammatory response during tattoo pigment removal (an experimental study)
abstract: The authors present results of an experimental study with Wistar rats on the effectiveness of combined laser irradiation at wavelengths 532 nm and 1064 nm for tattoo pigment removal. The aim of this study was to assess morphological changes in the skin and depth of laser light penetration exposure in the discussed combined modality compared to monochromatic irradiation. In the control groups, patients were treated separately with laser wavelengths 532 nm and 1064 nm, while in the experimental group both wavelengths were applied consequently. Histological examination revealed that the combined method gives the deepest penetration (120-150 μm) and nearly complete destruction of pigment in both superficial and deep dermal layers, though it causes a pronounced inflammatory reaction. Monochromatic 532 nm irradiation showed superficial effects (40-70 μm) with pigment retention in deep layers and epidermal atrophy, whereas 1064 nm irradiation demonstrated intermediate penetration depth (80-110 μm) with uniform pigment destruction and minimal damage to surrounding tissues. These findings confirm that the choice of laser therapy should be based on the depth of pigment location and clinical objectives. The combined approach is optimal for complete pigment removal, while monochromatic 1064 nm irradiation may be recommended for cases requiring minimal damage to superficial skin layers.

title: Exploring coping strategies of internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Mogadishu in response to food shortages: a mixed-methods study
Clinical transcriptomics identifies a convergent PPARG-centered transcriptional response to shexiang baoxin pill and suxiao jiuxin pill in stable coronary artery disease
abstract: Shexiang Baoxin Pill (SBP) and Suxiao Jiuxin Pill (SJP) are widely used traditional Chinese medicine formulations for Stable Coronary Artery Disease (SCAD), yet their molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Integrating paired, within-patient peripheral-blood transcriptomics with literature-curated blood-entering metabolites, this study characterizes the shared treatment-associated transcriptional response to SBP and SJP in SCAD. We performed RNA sequencing on paired Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMCs) from 42 SCAD patients pre- and post-administration. Paired analysis identified 289 shared coding DEGs which enriched in monocyte- and lipid-handling-related processes. These findings reveal the commonality of transcriptional changes before and after treatment with SBP and SJP. Reanalysis of an independent mouse sNuc-seq dataset showed directionally concordant Pparg expression patterns in mononuclear-phagocyte clusters and was interpreted as supportive cross-context evidence. These findings provide clinically derived, convergent evidence that SBP and SJP are associated with a coordinated downregulation of monocyte- and foam-cell-related genes centered on PPARG , indicating that PPARG may have the potential to become a therapeutic target. title: Optimized Extraction of Crocins from Crocus sativus L. Stigmas through Response Surface Methodology and HPLC-based Quality Assessment
Digital access and citizen transparency demand in digital governance: evidence from West Africa
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether individual digital access is associated with citizens’ demand for government transparency in West Africa, whether this association is mediated by usage intensity, and whether its association with perceived efficacy in obtaining government information is moderated by national e-government development. Design/methodology/approach Using Afrobarometer Round 9 data for 18,351 respondents across 14 West African countries, merged with UN E-Government Development Index scores, this study estimates multilevel logistic and ordered logistic regressions, a mediation model, a cross-level interaction model and robustness checks. Findings Digital access was associated with support for disclosure of government contracts (odds ratio = 1.17; approximately two percentage points in predicted probability), but not budgets or salaries. The authors found no evidence that this association was mediated by general usage intensity. The interaction between access and e-government development in predicting perceived efficacy was not significant; a random-slope model indicated the contracts–demand association varied across countries, though e-government development did not explain this variation. Originality/value This study extends the digital-empowerment and second-level digital-divide literatures beyond single-country or high-income settings by disaggregating tr…

title: Generation of a CYP2C19-mScarlet reporter hepatic organoid derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells for species-specific drug response and high-content screening
abstract: Introduction Species-specific differences in drug metabolism pose major challenges in preclinical drug discovery and safety assessment, necessitating human-relevant in vitro models. Conventional animal models frequently fail to predict human-specific drug responses because of inherent interspecies differences. In this study, we generate a reporter line to monitor human-specific CYP2C19 regulation. Methods CRISPR/Cas9 genome-editing technology was used to generate a functional human induced pluripotent stem cell reporter line with mScarlet knocked in at the endogenous CYP2C19 locus. This reporter line was subsequently differentiated into 3D hepatic organoids to evaluate its applicability for high-content screening. Results The engineered human induced pluripotent stem cells retained pluripotency, genomic stability, and multilineage differentiation potential and were successfully differentiated into 3D hepatic organoids expressing hepatocyte markers. Upon differentiation into HOs, mScarlet fluorescence was markedly induced and colocalized with endoplasmic reticulum markers, demonstrating precise endogenous reporter expression and subcellular localization. To evaluate functional responsiveness and species selectivity, HOs were treated with human- and rodent-specific nuclear receptor agonists. Treatment with the representative human pregnane X receptor and constitutive androstane r…

title: Naturally Epoxy-Functional Black Seed Oil as a Bio-Derived Modifier for AP1 Ramie-Reinforced Poly(lactic acid): Molecular Evidence, Processing Optimization, and Short-Term Aqueous Response
abstract: Abstract Naturally epoxy-functional black seed oil (BSO), containing inherent oxirane functionality and used without additional epoxidation, was evaluated as a bioderived modifier for AP1 ramie-reinforced poly(lactic acid) (PLA) biocomposites. At 5 wt% BSO, tensile strength, impact strength, and elongation at break increased by 3.5%, 73.3%, and 10.7%, respectively, relative to the BSO-free PLA/AP1 composite. FTIR, NMR, and SEM observations were consistent with BSO-assisted matrix plasticization, improved impregnation and wetting, and more favorable fiber–matrix interactions, while extensive covalent grafting was not established. Box–Behnken optimization identified a practical formulation–processing region near 5 wt% BSO, 172 °C, and 75–76 MPa. Experimental validation yielded tensile strength of 108.01 ± 0.63 MPa, impact strength of 20.84 ± 0.89 kJ m–2, and elongation at break of 15.30 ± 0.72%, with prediction deviations below 2.5%. The optimized composite also showed a lower short-term apparent aqueous mass response than the BSO-free composite across pH 6–8. Complementary 3D RVE–FEM analysis provided comparative insight into elastic stiffness and load-transfer behavior. These findings demonstrate that inherent oxirane-containing BSO can be directly used to modify the processing–property balance of PLA/ramie biocomposites.

title: Mo-induced structure–domain coupling and the trade-off between high-temperature magnetic response and low-expansion performance in Fe–Co–Ni alloys
Potential for Greenhouse Gas Emission Reduction through Social Innovation Programs (Case Study: PT PLN Nusantara Power Tanjung Awar-Awar Power Plant)
abstract: The high volume of agricultural waste and livestock manure, together with greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from fossil-fueled power plant operations, poses environmental and social challenges in Tuban Regency, East Java. In response, PT PLN Nusantara Power UP Tanjung Awar-Awar has implemented social innovation programs to reduce these impacts while empowering local communities. This study analyzes the environmental and social impacts of these programs using a mixed-methods approach. Quantitative data were used to calculate GHG emissions and vegetation carbon stocks, while qualitative data from stakeholder interviews provided information on program operations and field conditions. The results show that six subprograms, namely bioenergy, livestock feed concentrate production, biomass utilization for co-firing, agricultural electrification, bokashi fertilizer processing, and reforestation, reduced GHG emissions, increased carbon sequestration, and supported environmental sustainability. These programs also generated social and economic benefits for the community. The findings demonstrate that community-based environmental management can create integrated value for the environment, the economy, and society.
venue: ENVIBILITY: Journal of Environmental and Sustainability Studies

title: Simultaneous Removal of CO2, NOx, and SO2 from Marine Exhaust Gas Using an Oxidation–Reduction-Coupled In-Situ Activation Absorption System
abstract: Abstract Simultaneous removal of CO2, NOx, and SO2 from marine exhaust remains challenging due to low removal efficiency and excessive nitrate generation. Urea-based oxidation–reduction systems can address this problem but release CO2 during the absorption process. A novel Na2S2O8/Na2S2O3/Na2CO3 oxidation–reduction coupled in situ activation absorption system was proposed. Under the optimal conditions, the removal efficiencies reached 82.5% for CO2, 96.6% for NOx, and 99.9% for SO2, while residual nitrate was reduced to 23.5 mg/L. Na2CO3 mainly governed CO2 removal, whereas Na2S2O8 and Na2S2O3 dominated NOx removal. SO2 removal efficiency remained nearly unaffected and close to 100%. Based on the trends of removal efficiency, nitrate, and nitrite concentration changes, it was inferred that free radicals derived from persulfate might contribute to NO oxidation and CO2 absorption, while Na2S2O3 might inhibit the conversion of NOx to liquid nitrogen. For a representative 17.04 MW engine, net direct operating costs were estimated at 413–419 USD/MWh without NaHCO3 recovery, compared with 184 USD/MWh under an idealized full recovery. This system was chemically different from an early urea-based NOx/SO2 removal system, which avoided CO2 generation during the absorption and enabled integrated removal of CO2, NOx, and SO2, providing a new technological route for ship exhaust emission co…

title: AeroTea-VLM: a UAV-assisted multimodal visual language model for intelligent disease and pest management in terraced tea plantations
abstract: Abstract Current vision-language models (VLMs) that are used for UAV agricultural inspection encounter significant challenges. These problems come from scale distortion when drones fly at different heights, and also from really long delays that happen during visual action planning. In this paper, we introduce AeroTea-VLM, which fixes these issues by using a special new idea called ‘ heavy perception, light control. ’ To make sure perception stays the same regardless of scale in 3D terraced farm areas, we came up with two new methods: altitude-aware position encoding and cross-altitude topological attention. These two methods work together by adding real-time altimeter and depth data, which helps cut down on feature aliasing problems. For how the drone moves around, our Embodied Chain-Of-Action module gets rid of the slow autoregressive image generation step. Instead, it just outputs text commands directly. This change cuts total end-to-end delay by 86.5% (down to 385 ms), and it also keeps peak GPU memory usage at 14.2 GB. We tested this whole system on a new dataset that we collected ourselves, which we call AeroTea-Multimodal RGB-D. The tests show that AeroTea-VLM gets 88.5% accuracy when identifying plant diseases, and has an 84.2% success rate on reasoning tasks. Both of these numbers are better than what existing baseline methods can get.

title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan dan Kualitas Pengasuhan terhadap Kepuasan Orang Tua pada Lembaga PAUD dan Daycare di Jabodetabek
abstract: This study examines the effects of service quality and caregiving quality on parental satisfaction with early childhood education (ECE/PAUD) and daycare institutions in the Greater Jakarta area (Jabodetabek). A quantitative associative approach was employed. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale from 37 parents or guardians selected through purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics. The results show that service quality does not have a significant partial effect on parental satisfaction (t = −0.015; p = 0.988), whereas caregiving quality has a positive and significant partial effect (t = 4.916; p < 0.001). Simultaneously, service quality and caregiving quality significantly affect parental satisfaction (F = 60.825; p < 0.001). The coefficient of determination (R²) is 0.782, indicating that the two independent variables explain 78.2% of the variation in parental satisfaction. These findings highlight the importance of caregiving quality while maintaining service quality as part of the overall management of ECE and daycare institutions.

title: Multidisciplinary perspectives on Shishaldin Volcano: an open-system, deforming volcano
abstract: Abstract The integration of multidisciplinary data across multiple eruptions is essential to improve our understanding of a volcanic system. Shishaldin Volcano is one of the most active volcanoes in Alaska, with several reported eruptions over the last 300 years. We synthesize multidisciplinary datasets going back to 1997 and focus our analyses on the 2014–2015, 2019–2020, and 2023 eruptive periods. We find pronounced periods of volcanic tremor, long-period and volcano-tectonic seismicity; thermal anomalies with a radiative power ranging from 10 to 1000 MW; 1–2 $$^\circ $$ ∘ C increase in the median, low-pass filtered thermal anomaly; SO $$_2$$ 2 emission rates ranging from 30 to 287 kt/year; and previously unrecognized surface deformation that includes two episodes of $$\sim $$ ∼ 1 cm/year inflation preceding the 2014–2015 and the 2019–2020 eruptions, and deflation prior to, during, and after the 2023 eruption in the GNSS records. The new ground-based geodetic observations allow us to refine previous interpretations of the magmatic plumbing system. Borehole tilt records are best explained by a shallow, 1–1.5 km long conduit centered at sea level with a radius of 150 m. From the GNSS records, we find a pressurized sphere between 2 and 4 km below sea level (bsl) depth, and a 10 km long conduit centered at $$\sim $$ ∼ 6 km bsl depth as the most probable inflation and deflation so…

title: Beyond the ecological-economic tradeoff through development model policy innovation: evidence from China’s old revolutionary base areas
abstract: Purpose The tradeoff between ecological protection and economic development remains a core challenge for global sustainable development, particularly in China’s old revolutionary base areas (ORBAs), many of which are less-developed regions. This paper aims to evaluate the effect of the “Two Mountains” Practice and Innovation Bases (TMBs) policy on the synergy between ecology and economy (SEE) and explore sustainable development paths in less developed regions. Design/methodology/approach Based on panel data of 1,414 counties in ORBAs from 2010 to 2024, this study constructs a multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) model for baseline estimation and applies mechanism tests, heterogeneity analysis and a spatial Durbin model to explore transmission paths, regional differences and spatial spillover effects. Findings The TMBs policy significantly promotes the synergistic development of ecological protection and economic growth in ORBAs. It mainly exerts effects through three channels: financial capital accumulation, green technological innovation and green industrial upgrading. The policy effect is not fully realized in high-altitude areas and inter-provincial boundary areas and presents significant spatial spillover effects with indirect effects far stronger than direct effects. Originality/value This study quantitatively evaluates the effectiveness of TMBs in ORBAs using coun…

title: Edukasi Manajemen Risiko K3 dan Pengujian Kebisingan dalam Meningkatkan Pengetahuan dan Keselamatan Pengelola di Objek Wisata Goa Kreo Semarang
abstract: Pengembangan sektor pariwisata tidak hanya berorientasi pada peningkatan daya tarik destinasi dan jumlah kunjungan wisatawan, tetapi juga perlu didukung penerapan aspek keselamatan dan kesehatan. Observasi awal menunjukkan adanya kondisi lingkungan yang berpotensi menimbulkan risiko keselamatan bagi pengunjung, pekerja, dan pengelola wisata. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan pengelola mengenai identifikasi bahaya, pengujian kebisingan, dan pencegahan kecelakaan kerja di kawasan Wisata Goa Kreo. Kegiatan dilaksanakan pada 25 Oktober 2026 dengan melibatkan 10 pengelola. Metode pelaksanaan meliputi edukasi, praktik identifikasi dan analisis risiko menggunakan metode Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment, and Determining Control (HIRADC), diskusi interaktif, pengukuran kebisingan menggunakan Sound Level Meter, pemasangan rambu keselamatan dan kesehatan kerja (K3), pendampingan, serta evaluasi melalui pretest dan posttest. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan partisipasi aktif peserta dalam diskusi dan praktik HIRADC berdasarkan temuan bahaya di lapangan. Nilai rata-rata pengetahuan meningkat dari 98,00 menjadi 100,00. Pengukuran kebisingan pada 10 titik menunjukkan rentang 45,5–55,9 dB(A), seluruhnya di bawah baku tingkat kebisingan kawasan rekreasi sebesar 70 dB(A). Kegiatan ini diharapkan meningkatkan kapasitas pengelola dalam mengidentifikasi da…

title: “We firmly expect to see a further increase in power density”
A satellite-based approach to monitor aboveground forest biomass trends at landscape and carbon project-relevant scales
abstract: Abstract Improved forest management (IFM) is an important climate change mitigation strategy, yet robust carbon accounting for IFM projects remains difficult due to limited spatially and temporally explicit data. High-resolution, repeatable monitoring approaches are needed to establish transparent dynamic baselines, reduce monitoring costs, and support long-term carbon stewardship. We developed a remote sensing–based framework for estimating and monitoring aboveground biomass density (AGBD) trends. Using multi-source remote sensing data (Landsat time series, GEDI lidar) and environmental covariates, we applied machine learning to generate annual 30-m AGBD maps from 1985 to 2023 across two counties on the Olympic Peninsula, Washington, USA. Model performance was adequate (R² = 0.68; MAE = 81 Mg/ha, RMSE = 102 Mg/ha). Across the region, AGBD generally increased over time, but trends varied substantially by ownership. Public forest lands maintained the highest AGBD and the fastest rates of increase, whereas private industrial forests had lower AGBD and experienced the steepest declines. Annual AGBD maps were also used to quantify biomass before and after regeneration harvests across non-federal ownerships. Harvests occurred at an average threshold of 240 ± 73 Mg/ha and reduced AGBD by 57 ± 28%, with thresholds and harvest intensity varying among ownership classes. By combining own…

title: Effectiveness of Interventions for the Prevention and Management of Skin Tears: A Systematic Review of Quasi-Experimental and Randomized Controlled Trials
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aims to evaluate the effectiveness of experimental and quasi-experimental interventions used in the prevention and treatment of skin tears (ST) and to identify evidence-based practices for clinical decision-making. DATA SOURCES: Five databases (PubMed, Cochrane, Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCO) were searched for open-access, English-language studies published between 2010 and 2025. STUDY SELECTION: Conducted in accordance with Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025646088), this review included studies evaluating interventions for the prevention or treatment of ST. Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising 10 randomized controlled trials and 8 quasi-experimental studies. Study selection was performed independently by 2 reviewers through title/abstract screening followed by full-text assessment, with discrepancies resolved by consensus. DATA EXTRACTION: Data were extracted independently by 2 reviewers using a structured data collection form based on the standardized JBI data extraction tool, with discrepancies resolved through discussion and consensus. Methodological quality was assessed using JBI critical appraisal tools. No study was excluded solely due to low methodological quality. DATA SYNTHESIS: Data were narratively synthesized under the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Devel…

title: Data-Rate Dependence of Launch-Power Sensitivity and Transmission Reach in Optical Fiber Communication Systems
abstract: This work investigates the response of optical fiber communication systems to variations of the launch power for data rates between 2.5 and 40 Gb/s. A simulation model with OptiSystem is developed, where launch power and transmission distance are varied systematically for each data rate. The Q-factor and bit error rate (BER) are used to evaluate the maximum QoS-qualified transmission distance and the first-failing distance. The sensitivity to launch power was quantified by the relative change in Q-factor with launch power. The results indicate that the maximum transmission reach is decreasing from 103 km at 2.5 Gb/s to 4 km at 40 Gb/s. In contrast, the relative Q-factor variation decreases from 89.94% to 2.69%, which means that the sensitivity of the transmission quality to the launchpower variation decreases significantly with the increase of the data rate. The study finds different sensitivity regions and shows the correlation between data rate, transmission reach and launch-power sensitivity. These results provide practical guidelines for launch-power adjustment in multi-rate optical networks, particularly showing that power tuning is most effective in the 2.5–10 Gb/s range.

title: System for Monitoring of Lateral Wear of Rails Based on Readings from Automated Diagnostic Tools
abstract: This article studies the system of monitoring lateral wear of rails. An important operational and economic problem is considered – determining the best condition of rails for making decisions on their replacement and performing preventive maintenance. The basics of monitoring lateral wear of rails are presented. The factors that have the greatest impact on the intensity of lateral wear are described, among which the following can be distinguished: curve radius, location (on an ascent, landing, descent), type of rails used, use of pushing and regenerative braking, load intensity of the operating section, use of lubrication and lubrication quality. The analysis carried out by the author shows that determining the actual rate of lateral wear growth and knowledge of the design and operational characteristics of the section allows solving the inverse problem – monitoring the quality of lubrication. The analysis of the results of systematic monitoring of the lateral wear condition is carried out. High quality monitoring is possible only through processing data from automated diagnostic tools, since this ensures accumulation, synchronization and automatic indepth analysis with forecasting of rail wear development and planning of repair work. Therefore, the objective of the work was to study changes in lateral wear of rails, data on which is obtained by diagnostic tools with the subseq…

title: Respecting the boundaries: balancing climate adaptation and Earth system resilience
abstract: Humans have always adapted to their local climate. Today, human activities are also unintentionally changing the global climate. This will require major adaptations, which cannot replace and must not derail efforts to stop climate change. Yet measures such as cooling buildings or irrigating crops can themselves increase environmental pressures on the Earth system. Using the Planetary Boundaries framework, we combine evidence to estimate the current pressures associated with adaptation to (i) Holocene-like climates and (ii) anthropogenic climate change. Our first-order estimates indicate that climate adaptation currently contributes ∼ 25.6 % of annual greenhouse gas emissions and ∼ 74.1 % of annual human freshwater withdrawals. Climate adaptation even affects the stratosphere: cooling technologies have considerably contributed to ozone depletion. This confirms that climate adaptation currently exerts substantial pressures on the Earth system. Only a minority of these pressures are likely to be driven by anthropogenic climate change; most still result from economic, technological, and population growth and might also have occurred without climate change. But as climate change dramatically increases the need for adaptation, these findings underscore the importance of scaling adaptation in ways that protect people without further destabilising the Earth system.

title: Employee Perception of AI Chatbots in Banking: An Empirical Study of Workplace Interaction
abstract: The banking industry is evolving as a result of the quick adoption of technological advances and artificial intelligence, which is changing how employees interact with technology on a daily basis. AI chatbots are now used in digital workplaces, but were primarily linked to customer support. Because of this dynamic role, it's critical to comprehend how employees view and engage with such tools. With an emphasis on bot functionality and interaction quality, the current paper examines employees’ perception of AI chatbots and their workplace interactions with these systems. The study used a structured questionnaire to collect responses from employees of selected private sector banks and examine their experiences with AI chatbots at work. The study considers features of chatbots and interaction quality as important aspects of employee–technology collaboration and examines their relevance to employee perception. Based on 39 eligible responses, the study found a positive and statistically significant relationship between the constructs (r = 0.622, p < .001). By focusing on the employee rather than only the customer perspective, the paper contributes to the discussion on the changing nature of work in tech-enabled banking environments. The paper provides preliminary empirical insight into how employees view artificial intelligence chatbots as part of their workplace and highlights the …

title: Role of the Cardiothoracic Surgeon in the Multidisciplinary Surgical Management of Renal Cell Carcinoma with Supradiaphragmatic Inferior Vena Cava and Right Atrial Tumour Thrombus: A Case Series
abstract: Renal cell carcinoma with tumour thrombus extending into the supradiaphragmatic inferior vena cava and right atrium is rare and presents a major surgical challenge. We report two patients with Mayo level IV tumour thrombus managed through a multidisciplinary approach involving urological and cardiothoracic surgical teams. Both patients underwent radical nephrectomy, right atrial and inferior vena caval thrombectomy under cardiopulmonary bypass. One patient required concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting for significant left anterior descending artery disease. Complete tumour thrombus extraction was achieved without deep hypothermic circulatory arrest. These cases highlight the importance of cardiothoracic surgical involvement, meticulous operative planning, and multidisciplinary management in achieving safe surgical outcomes.
