Malicious UPI QR Code Detection System Using Vision Transformer, YOLO-Based Localization, and Database-Centric Payment Payload Verification
abstract: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) QR codes have also been adopted swiftly in India which has greatly enhanced the convenience of digital payments in India, but considered it has brought along some new risks such as machine-readable payment payloads which are not transparent. It is not possible to visually check whether a digitized parameter such as UPI ID, payee name, amount or transaction parameters have been manipulated. Existing QR scanners simply try to decode the content and pass it on to the payment application without applying strong integrity checks on any trusted customer or merchant records. In this paper, a comprehensive Malicious UPI QR Code Detection System is proposed by dynamically simulating customer data, generating UPI QR codes (both authentic and malicious), localizing QR codes using Model YOLO/OpenCV, decoding codes in UPI payload, verifying codes in the UPI stored in the database, and utilizing Malicious UPI QR code detection based on the Vision Transformer (ViT) method. The proposed framework takes those manipulations like UPI ID change, changed amount, change in payee name, injection of URL parameters etc., and proposes to detect the same changes up to the level of some pixel noise. A balanced synthetic dataset of 20,000 QR images was prepared using 10,000 records from respective customers, and, under experimental conditions, the ViT classifier precisely a…

title: Ethinyl estradiol–cyproterone acetate versus metformin for the management of polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine disorder associated with hyperandrogenism, menstrual irregularity, insulin resistance, and metabolic abnormalities. Ethinyl estradiol–cyproterone acetate (EE/CA, marketed as Diane-35 and as equivalent generic preparations containing ethinyl estradiol 35 µg plus cyproterone acetate 2 mg) is commonly used for androgen-related symptoms, whereas metformin is used mainly for metabolic dysfunction. However, the comparative efficacy of these therapies remains uncertain. Objective To compare the clinical, hormonal, and metabolic effects of EE/CA versus metformin in women with PCOS. Methods This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 statement. The review was registered prospectively in PROSPERO (registration number CRD::::). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to 12 January 2026 and supplemented by backward and forward citation tracking. Studies were eligible if they included women with PCOS and directly compared EE/CA with metformin. Add-on-only studies were excluded from the primary quantitative synthesis. All outcome data were harmonised to a single unit before pooling. Continuous outcomes were pooled as mean difference (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) using a random-effects model with the Hartung–Knapp adjustm…

title: Are the advertisements you watch authentic? Deepfake detection in key opinion leader short-video advertisements with purpose-driven occlusion
abstract: Purpose Short-video advertisements (ads) increasingly rely on key opinion leader (KOL) endorsements to build user trust. While KOL marketing is cost-effective, it has become a target for fraudsters who exploit deepfake technology to replicate KOLs’ appearances and fabricate fake endorsement videos for illicit profit. In contrast to random occlusions, short-video ads contain purpose-driven occlusions (e.g. products or limbs obscuring faces) designed for commercial demonstration. This leads to the dual challenges of static feature degradation and temporal feature discontinuity caused by purposeful occlusion for existing detectors. Design/methodology/approach We propose a novel dual-branch occlusion-aware spatio-temporal model (OA-STM). The intra-frame branch designs an occlusion detection module and an occlusion-aware attention module to enhance features from visible facial regions. The inter-frame branch designs an adaptive gating module and a selective state space module to capture long-term temporal patterns and suppress interference from occluded frames. We also construct and release the FAKE-COMMERCE dataset, a dedicated benchmark featuring realistic advertising scenarios with purpose-based occlusions across 23 product categories. Findings Extensive experiments demonstrate that OA-STM significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on the FAKE-COMMERCE dataset and publi…

title: Reconstructing colonial administrative landscapes: Power, governance, and evolution of the Onderafdeling Lahat in South Sumatra, 1860–1942
abstract: This article examines the evolution of Dutch colonial administration in the Lahat region of South Sumatra between 1860 and 1942, focusing on territorial reorganization, bureaucratic consolidation, and the transformation of Indigenous governance. Rather than treating the Onderafdeling Lahat as a fixed administrative entity, the study traces successive changes in colonial territorial arrangements and institutional structures. Employing a historical research method that combines chronological reconstruction and thematic analysis, it draws on colonial administrative archives, statutory regulations, government reports, historical maps, contemporary newspapers, and relevant scholarly literature. The findings reveal that colonial administrative expansion in Lahat developed through a gradual process of institutional consolidation. The incorporation of Pasemah into the Residency of Palembang in 1868, the establishment of Lahat as the capital of the Afdeeling Palembangsche Bovenlanden in 1906, and subsequent administrative reforms demonstrate the changing territorial organization of colonial rule. The controleur played a central role in supervising local administration and regulating the relationship between colonial authorities and Indigenous institutions, particularly the marga system and its traditional leaders. Meanwhile, railway development, which reached Lahat in 1924 and Lubukling…

title: Auto Regressive Exogenous (ARX) Model-Based System Identification Framework for Finger Straightening Soft Pneumatic Actuator (SSPA)
abstract: Soft pneumatic actuators have attracted increasing attention in rehabilitation and soft robotic applications because of their flexibility and ability to produce compliant motion. However, their nonlinear and time-dependent behaviour makes accurate dynamic modelling challenging, particularly for control- oriented applications. This study presents an experimental system identification approach for modelling a Bioinspired Straightening Soft Pneumatic Actuator (BSSPA) using an Auto-Regressive with eXogenous input (ARX) model. An open-loop experimental setup was developed to obtain the relationship between the pneumatic input and actuator position response using a flex sensor and data acquisition system. Pseudo-Random Binary Sequence (PRBS) signals were applied at three excitation frequencies of 1.2, 1.4, and 1.6 Hz. A total of 30,000 input–output samples were collected, with 10,000 samples obtained for each frequency over 100 s at a sampling time of 0.01 s. Several ARX model structures were evaluated using least-squares parameter estimation, and their performance was assessed based on the fit percentage between the measured and predicted responses. The results show that the ARX (4,4,1) model identified at 1.4 Hz achieved the highest fit of 93.73%. This result indicates that the selected ARX structure and excitation frequency provide a good representation of the SSPA dynamic respons…

title: Integrated pest management in African mahogany (Khaya spp.) plantation systems: synthesis of pest biology, impacts and silvicultural control strategies
Spectral correction factors for the removal of glint perturbations in above-water radiometry
abstract: Spectral correction factors for the removal of glint perturbations in above-water radiometric measurements are theoretically computed for representative inland, coastal and open-ocean waters, accounting for atmospheric dependences. The simulation framework relies on the measurement protocol adopted by AERONET-OC and endorsed by the ocean color community to support the validation of satellite aquatic radiometric products. The theoretical computation of the correction factors, here termed glint correction factors or ρ -factors , is performed in the 340–1020 nm spectral range by coupling (i) a highly accurate plane-parallel scalar code to simulate the angular distribution of the spectral sky-radiance impinging at the water surface, with (ii) a three-dimensional Monte Carlo code to model radiance reflections at a wind-roughened water surface. Glint is conventionally distinguished into contributions from radiance originating in the sun region (sun-glint) and in the remaining portion of the sky-dome (sky-glint); the impact of these terms is separately discussed. Computed glint correction factors – for both the total sky radiance and its sole diffuse component – are available at Zenodo (Bulgarelli et al., 2026; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20609990).

title: Perceived Naturalness and Support for Local Food Products in Côte d'Ivoire: The Mediating Role of Identity Appropriation and the Moderating Role of Local Identity
abstract: In West Africa, governments increasingly promote locally processed foods to reduce import dependence, yet little is known about which product perceptions actually drive consumer support. This study examines how perceived naturalness influences support for local food products in Côte d'Ivoire, through identity appropriation (the extent to which consumers see local products as carriers of national culture and image), and how local identity conditions this effect. Data were collected through a survey of consumers of processed local cereal products in six Ivorian cities; hypotheses were tested by regression analysis on 369 complete responses. Perceived naturalness is the strongest product benefit driving support (β = 0.41, p < 0.001). Part of this effect operates through identity appropriation (indirect effect = 0.08, 95% CI [0.04; 0.12]), while the direct effect remains substantial. Local identity strongly amplifies the naturalness effect: it is null among weakly identified consumers (β = 0.05, n.s.) and large among strongly identified consumers (β = 0.58, p < 0.001). Results are robust to controls for health, taste and cost perceptions. The findings suggest that small agri-food firms and public "buy local" programmes should position local products on naturalness, link this naturalness to national heritage, and target consumers with strong local attachment.

Trials and Tribulations of Setting up a Clinical Prehabilitation Service and Five Tips to Overcome them
abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Studies in prehabilitation for patients undergoing major intracavity surgeries as well as aggressive complex interventions such as solid organ and bone marrow transplantation have increased rapidly in recent years. Previous randomized clinical trials and systematic reviews have shown potential clinical benefits of prehabilitation across multiple populations including reduction in postoperative complications, length of hospital stay and/or enhanced postoperative recovery. However, despite the growth in research, implementation of prehabilitation services is still scarce, and most programs are not offered as standard of care. Implementation of novel interventions such as prehabilitation can be challenging, and include hospital- and patient-related factors. Recent Findings In this commentary, we first highlight common barriers to prehabilitation implementation including concerns regarding lack of cost-effectiveness studies, limited patient adherence outside clinical studies, concerns regarding delaying surgery to accommodate optimal prehabilitation and difficulties in patient selection. In the second part of the paper, we offer some collective approaches that have been used in successful prehabilitation services to overcome those barriers and facilitate implementation and scalability of prehabilitation. Summary This review provides an overview of most co…

title: Brand Image, Service Quality, Marketing Strategy, and Tutoring Choice in Palembang
abstract: Background: Competition among supplementary-education providers has increased the importance of institutional reputation, service experience, and promotional communication in students' and families' selection of tutoring services. This study examines these relationships at BTA 70 PTC Palembang. Objective: This study assesses the separate statistical associations of brand image, service quality, and marketing strategy with the tutoring-provider decisions of twelfth-grade students at BTA 70 PTC Palembang. Methods: A quantitative correlational survey was conducted with 100 respondents drawn from a population of 245 registered twelfth-grade students. Likert-scale responses were analyzed in SPSS 25 using multiple linear regression; however, the documentation of the random-sampling procedure and sample-size justification remains incomplete. Results: All three predictors were positively and statistically associated with tutoring choice: brand image (t = 6.994, p < 0.001), service quality (t = 3.031, p = 0.003), and marketing strategy (t = 4.176, p < 0.001). The model explained 75.1% of the variance in the outcome (R² = 0.751; adjusted R² = 0.743), although the submitted output did not include the joint F-statistic. Conclusion: Within this sample, institutional reputation, perceived service quality, and promotional strategy were each related to students' tutoring preferences. Because t…

title: Rethinking healthcare professional well-being: a service ecosystem perspective on moral tensions in care delivery
abstract: Purpose This conceptual paper adopts a service ecosystem perspective to examine how healthcare professional well-being (HPW) is shaped through the negotiation of competing demands in service interactions. It introduces a moral lens to explain how these tensions carry implications for what is considered right and appropriate in practice across micro, meso, and macro levels within healthcare service ecosystems. Design/methodology/approach Using theory synthesis and adaptation, this paper integrates insights from multiple disciplines to map fragmented research on morality and HPW. It adapts existing perspectives on HPW to develop a multi-level, service-integrated framework that explains how the ongoing negotiation of moral tensions in care delivery shapes how HPW is sustained and eroded within service ecosystems. Findings The framework positions moral injury and moral resilience as interconnected, evolving processes shaped through ongoing negotiation of moral tensions within healthcare service ecosystems. It outlines four interlinked research directions, each with research questions and theoretical framing to guide future study. Research limitations/implications The paper provides a forward-looking agenda with research questions, theoretical lenses, and methodologies, offering conceptual and methodological scaffolding. Practical implications Managers and policymakers can support H…

title: Scientific Paper Writing Training For Students
abstract: Scientific writing (KTI) is scientific work written by following scientific rules. Scientific principles as the main requirement in writing a work are intended so that the work produced can be scientifically justified. The purpose of scientific writing training activities is to foster interest, enthusiasm, and creative and innovative ideas to produce scientific work in accordance with the rules of writing. Based on the results of the implementation of the training activities, it can be concluded that the activities went well and received full support from the school. All training participants attended the activity until the end with an attendance rate of 100%. The participants were enthusiastic to ask questions, explore ideas, and express opinions. Thus, in the future it is hoped that there will be further activities involving accompanying teachers to optimize their role in preparing scientific papers for students.

title: A landscape-based cultural ecosystem service analytical framework (L-CESAF) for mediterranean agricultural landscapes: the case of La Vera (Spain)
abstract: Mediterranean agricultural landscapes are complex social–ecological systems in which long-term interactions between ecological processes and human activities generate Cultural Ecosystem Services (CES) and broader nature’s Contributions to People (NCP). Despite the increasing interest in CES, existing assessment approaches often rely on perception-based methods or ecosystem service inventories, providing limited insight into the socio–ecological mechanisms through which these benefits emerge. This study developed the Landscape-Based Cultural Ecosystem Service Analytical Framework (L-CESAF), a hierarchical framework integrating social–Ecological Systems theory, Landscape Ecology, Cultural Ecosystem Services and Nature’s contributions to people within a single analytical architecture. The framework was implemented in the Agricultural Cultural Landscape of La Vera (Spain) through four hierarchical analytical levels, seven landscape-based analytical dimensions, and the Integrated Cultural Ecosystem Service Index (ICESI). The case study implementation demonstrates how ecological integrity, historical continuity, landscape structure, and sociocultural drivers jointly explain the emergence of Cultural Ecosystem Services and their contribution to broader societal benefits. Rather than functioning as an inventory-based assessment method, the L-CESAF provides a process-based analytical fr…

title: Decision Support System for E-Commerce Service Improvement Based on Digital Survey Using Rule-Based Intelligence Method
abstract: Most micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) selling online decide service improvements intuitively rather than from systematic analysis of customer feedback. This study designed and implemented Analisa Bisnis, a web-based decision support system (DSS) that converts customer experience into prioritized service improvement recommendations. Following the Operational Research-Intelligent Decision Support System (OR-IDSS) framework, it combines a data-driven track (25-item digital survey and categorization) with a knowledge-driven track (weighted IF-THEN rules, forward-chaining inference, highest-weight conflict resolution). Because primary survey collection was ongoing, 831 labeled e-commerce reviews served as a proxy dataset to calibrate and test the lexicon-based categorization module, which maps reviews into five service dimensions. Seller service (80.4%), delivery (62.8%), and general satisfaction (62.3%) had the highest negative-review rates. The module achieved 77.74% accuracy and 77.60% macro-F1, 24.07 percentage points above the 53.67% majority-class baseline, although supervised TF-IDF baselines reached 92–93.5% accuracy. Black-box testing confirmed each module met its specification. Decision-table validation of nine weighted rules found seven scenarios consistent and two input combinations uncovered, so a default rule is recommended. All 19 user acceptance scenarios…

Rethinking justice theory for service recovery in the era of agentic AI
abstract: Purpose As hospitality firms increasingly aspire to deploy agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems capable of autonomous decision-making, service failures involving such systems give rise to responsibility indeterminacy. This paper aims to revisit justice theory to develop a collaborative justice governance framework for understanding and managing service recovery following agentic AI failures. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper critically reviews the service recovery and justice literature to examine how responsibility has been attributed in service failures and how distributive, procedural and interactional justice are operationalised in traditional service recovery and challenged by agentic AI. Building on these insights, each justice dimension is reframed to demonstrate how hospitality firms, frontline employees and customers collectively enact fair recovery. Findings This paper reconceptualises distributive, procedural and interactional justice as a collaborative governance process enacted through complementary stakeholder contributions. Hospitality organisations establish the organisational conditions that enable fair recovery, frontline employees translate these conditions into adaptive recovery practices and customers actively contribute to shaping recovery processes, and outcomes. Practical implications The framework provides actionable guidance for…

title: ‘The little things mean a lot’. Forensic mental health practitioners’ perspectives on delivering Trauma-Informed care in a low secure service
abstract: Purpose There is now significant evidence of the prevalence of trauma experiences, post-traumatic stress disorder and complex interpersonal trauma in forensic populations. Alongside this, has been growing recognition of the benefits of Trauma-Informed Care (TIC). TIC aims to create services which are sensitive and responsive to the different ways trauma can affect development, enabling the use of approaches that promote recovery and reduce potential re-traumatisation. However, applying TIC in practice can create challenges, particularly within forensic settings. This study aims to explore staff perspectives of responsive TIC within a low secure service in Scotland, including challenges and facilitators to implementing this. Design/methodology/approach Seven registered practitioners were recruited through purposive and opportunistic sampling methods. Semi-structured interviews were conducted, and reflexive thematic analysis was used to identify themes within the resulting data set. Findings For promoting responsive TIC, themes generated included: “Responsivity to individual choices and needs”, and “Relationships are key”. For challenges, themes included “Characteristics of the population and setting”, “Trauma-Informed ‘Practice’ helps mitigate challenges to Trauma-Informed ‘Care’’’ and “Beneficial impacts of supporting/investing in staff”. Practical implications This study provi…

title: Evaluation of the Impact of Rail Inclination on their Service Life
abstract: The article considers the influence of rail inclination on the service life of rails under railway transport operation conditions. The relevance of the topic is due to the need to increase the service life of track superstructure elements in order to reduce infrastructure maintenance costs and increase the service life of systems. The objective of the study is to assess the influence of different rail inclination angles on the stress strain state and service life of rails. The tasks include the analysis of contact stresses for different types of contacts and inclination angles, as well as the assessment of changes in the service life of rails during operation. The research methods include numerical modeling using the finite element method to calculate contact stresses and analyze the stress strain state of rails for different inclinations. The calculation is carried out for a new and average network rail profile. The results show that rail inclination significantly affects the stresses in the rail head and, consequently, its service life. The greatest stress changes are observed at an inclination of 1/12, which leads to a significant reduction in the service life of the rail. In the case of central contact, the reduction in service life can reach 10,34 %, with external contact – 5,81 %, and with flange contact – 8,64 %. The conclusions of the work emphasize the importance of ma…

title: AI-Driven Digital Governance: Opportunities and Challenges for Smart Service Delivery in Bangladesh
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping public governance through predictive analytics, task automation, and data-driven decisions, but adoption remains uneven, particularly in developing countries like Bangladesh. With specific reference to agenda-setting, policy formulation, implementation, and evaluation, this study aims to examine how AI can bolster public policy processes and enhance public service delivery in Bangladesh. The study is conceptual and analytical and is based on secondary sources, including academic literature, government publications, and international AI governance frameworks, analyzed through thematic and comparative policy analysis. The results show that AI has a significant potential to drive better administrative efficiency, citizen engagement, evidence-informed policy-making, and service delivery in various sectors, including land administration, healthcare, agriculture, education, and financial services. Despite the promise of the government for utilizing AI for governance, the study identifies numerous challenges, such as the fragmented government databases, lack of data interoperability and authenticity, limited technical expertise, and insufficient regulatory framework. The analysis also notes issues relating to data privacy, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity, and transparency and accountability of institutions. The Singapore, Estonia, India, and C…

title: Integrating TPACK and TAM to explain pre-service teachers’ acceptance of generative AI
abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence is revolutionizing educational practices in higher education, yet its successful application depends on teachers’ acceptance and preparedness. This study investigated pre-service teachers’ perceptions of generative artificial intelligence using the Technology Acceptance Model extended by TPACK, with gender examined as a potential moderating factor and individual differences further explored through prior experience and subject background. Data were collected from 469 pre-service teachers, including 386 females, across teacher-training programs at six universities in G Province, China. Structural equation modeling revealed that technological knowledge and TPACK positively and indirectly predicted behavioral intention via the chain of perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and attitude toward generative artificial intelligence. However, TPACK unexpectedly negatively predicted perceived usefulness, and it showed a negative indirect effect on behavioral intention via perceived usefulness and attitude. Multi-group analysis indicated that male pre-service teachers had higher technological knowledge, TPACK, and perceived ease of use, but gender did not moderate relationships among the factors. In addition, prior experience significantly predicted behavioral intention, whereas gender and subject background were not significant predictor…

title: Empowering The Pkk Group In Sitirejo Village Through Creative Economy And Digital Literacy
abstract: Desa Sitirejo di Kecamatan Wagir, Kabupaten Malang, memiliki lebih dari 6.000 penduduk dengan mayoritas bekerja di sektor pertanian, peternakan, dan informal. Perempuan berperan penting dalam ketahanan ekonomi keluarga, namun sebagian anggota PKK masih memiliki keterbatasan dalam akses pelatihan kewirausahaan dan pemasaran digital. Padahal, mereka memiliki potensi seperti keterampilan membuat kue, memasak, kerajinan, dan mengelola usaha kecil. Keterbatasan pada manajemen usaha, branding, dan literasi digital menjadi hambatan dalam pengembangan ekonomi kelompok. Untuk menjawab masalah tersebut, Program Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PKM) bertajuk Pemberdayaan Kelompok PKK Desa Sitirejo Melalui Ekonomi Kreatif dan Literasi Digital dilaksanakan dengan kegiatan sosialisasi, pelatihan produksi, penguatan manajemen usaha, literasi digital, pemasaran online, serta pendampingan. Sebanyak 20 anggota PKK mengikuti program ini. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan peningkatan pengetahuan dari rata-rata 61,75 (pretest) menjadi 84,5 (posttest), serta peningkatan motivasi berwirausaha dari 57,5 menjadi 80,25. Kepemilikan akun media sosial untuk promosi juga meningkat dari 40% menjadi 100%, dan 65% peserta telah menentukan jenis usaha yang akan dijalankan. Program PKK ini terbukti efektif meningkatkan kapasitas ekonomi perempuan, meskipun pendampingan lanjutan masih diperlukan untuk menjamin keberlanjut…

title: When does a low-carbon marine fuel remain low-carbon in service? A source-traceable technical LCA of fuel pathways, AI-enabled operational optimization, and regulatory performance
abstract: Nominal well-to-wake (WtW) factors do not establish whether a marine fuel remains low-carbon in service. In this study, we develop a source-traceable, scenario-based technical life-cycle assessment framework to test whether an advantage survives production, shipboard conversion, non-CO 2 emissions, phase-resolved energy demand, operational constraints, and regulatory interpretation. The method integrates ISO 14040/14044, IMO lifecycle GHG accounting, literature evidence, and EU regulation; it is not a fleet experiment, meta-analysis, or new measured multi-vessel dataset. Two non-interchangeable outputs are retained: lifecycle energy intensity (gCO 2 e/MJ) and realized transport-service intensity (gCO 2 e/t-nm). The completed workbook evaluates seven source-controlled matched-service scenarios: WtW intensity ranges from 11.75 gCO 2 e/MJ for liquid e-H 2 to 90.77 gCO 2 e/MJ for MGO, with service intensity from 0.551 to 4.728 gCO 2 e/t-nm; scenario-specific reversal thresholds are also calculated. Evidence identifies methane leakage/slip, ammonia-related N 2 O, e-fuel electricity, methanol carbon-source allocation, biofuel feedstock, converter efficiency, cargo utilization, and operating energy as reversal variables. Artificial intelligence receives no emissions credit: only a validated physical energy or service delta enters the inventory, with digital emissions added when materi…

title: Beyond HIV prevention: healthcare-seeking, reproductive health, substance use, and service needs among migrant female sex workers in Ghana
abstract: Abstract Background Evidence on female sex workers (FSWs) in Ghana has largely centered on HIV burden, condom use, testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), and use of HIV prevention services. Less is known about how FSWs navigate broader healthcare, reproductive health, substance use, and unmet service needs. This study explored healthcare-seeking, sexual and reproductive health, HIV prevention, condom negotiation, substance use, coping, and service-access barriers among migrant FSWs in Ghana. Methods We conducted a qualitative descriptive study among 14 Nigerian migrant FSWs working in Accra and Kumasi, Ghana. Participants were recruited through snowball sampling. Semi-structured phone interviews were conducted between November and December 2024, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed thematically. Results Participants described healthcare-seeking as fragmented and pragmatic, involving local nurses, clinics, pharmacies, herbal care, outreach programs, and occasional hospital use. Choices between formal and informal care were shaped by cost, convenience, the flexibility of trusted nurses, lack of a Ghana card, and, for some, control by madams who had arranged their travel. HIV testing, condoms, and outreach services were familiar, but contraception beyond condoms, STI testing, PrEP counseling, routine screening, psychosocial support, and substance-use services were less visible. title: Designing a Service Landscape for an Emergency Department Information System Based on Emergency Assessment Using Enterprise Architecture Planning
abstract: The complexity of emergency care requires information systems that can accommodate clinical activities and the information generated at each stage of patient management. Without a clear architectural structure, the relationship between service processes, clinical records, and system functions may be difficult to establish. This research proposes a Service Landscape blueprint for an Emergency Department (ED) nursing care information system through Enterprise Architecture Planning (EAP), supported by selected phases of the TOGAF Architecture Development Method (ADM). A qualitative descriptive approach was applied to structure the requirements of emergency care into business, data, and application architectures. The resulting design organizes five core services, ranging from primary survey assessment using the ABCD approach to patient disposition. Each service is mapped to relevant clinical data entities and application modules, providing a conceptual overview of how information is recorded and managed throughout the care process. Validation was conducted using 20 indicators across four architectural aspects, yielding an overall score of 4.06. Data Architecture received the highest score (4.23), whereas Service Landscape scored 3.90. The blueprint offers a structured foundation for subsequent system development. Nevertheless, implementation and operational evaluation are still req…

title: Optimizing the design of social services: how policy-related service friction affects social service usage by vulnerable consumers
abstract: Purpose Economically vulnerable consumers rely on government-administered social services for essential resources, yet utilization is often low. This study aims to examine how policy choices can drive variations in social service designs and affect consumers’ perceptions and usage to offer insights into program design improvements. Design/methodology/approach In an analysis of state-level policy decisions about a US social service program (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) and three experiments, the authors examine the impact of policy-driven service friction, e.g. lengthy complex applications, combined with different benefit levels. Findings When the service benefit is low, even moderate compared to low service friction is appraised as unfair and deters usage. When the benefit is high, more friction is tolerated but eventually usage suffers. Overall, the authors show friction costs can deter usage even among vulnerable consumers who genuinely need the benefits. Thus, the authors show the limitations of an economic cost-benefit framework; the cost of friction can be a deterrent irrespective of benefits. Practical implications Policymakers setting policies that impact social service design should calibrate friction versus benefits. Low-benefit programs are especially susceptible to reduced utilization from friction. If friction cannot be removed, a higher benefit can so…

title: Building regulation-compliant chatbots
abstract: Abstract As Large Language Model (LLM)-based chatbots become increasingly prevalent across various sectors, their technical development, quality assurance, and legal compliance have become critical challenges. This paper provides an overview of how to build and operate LLM-driven chatbots in practical settings. It outlines the essential technical components required for implementation, the methods for verifying chatbot functionality to ensure a suitable level of quality, and the importance of aligning development and deployment with relevant legal frameworks. Emphasis is placed on ensuring that chatbot solutions not only perform efficiently but also adhere to applicable norms, regulations, and ethical standards. The approach presented in this paper can serve as a practical blueprint for developers, legal experts, and organizations aiming to deploy LLM-based chatbots responsibly and effectively, ensuring that both technical performance and legal accountability are addressed from the outset.

title: Frequency of technology use is associated with greater technological pedagogical content knowledge confidence among higher education academics in Bahrain
abstract: Introduction Digital transformation in higher education requires academics to integrate technological knowledge with pedagogy and disciplinary content. This study examined higher education academics’ self-reported confidence in Higher Education Teacher Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (HE-TPACK), its relationships with demographic and professional characteristics, and the psychometric properties of the seven HE-TPACK knowledge domains. Methods A quantitative, cross-sectional survey was conducted with 333 academics from 16 higher education institutions in Bahrain using the HE-TPACK instrument. Descriptive statistics, Mann–Whitney U and Kruskal–Wallis tests, Spearman's correlations, and multiple linear regression analyses were performed. Psychometric properties were assessed using exploratory factor analysis and measurement-model assessment. Results Academics reported high confidence across all HE-TPACK domains, with the highest scores for content knowledge and pedagogical content knowledge and the lowest for technological content knowledge. Frequency of technology use in teaching showed the strongest association with technological knowledge (r = .522, p < .001) and was consistently associated with higher confidence across the HE-TPACK domains. Age, academic qualification, academic rank, teaching experience, and contract type were also associated with selected domai…

title: Molecular dynamics and energetic performance of PBX explosives containing Al-Li alloys via binder and content regulation
Integrative phosphoproteomic mapping of site-specific co-regulation networks of STK26 (MST4)
abstract: Background Protein kinases are central regulators of cellular signaling networks. Serine/threonine-protein kinase 26 (STK26), a member of the Ste20 kinase family, plays important roles in cell polarity, proliferation, apoptosis, and stress responses, yet its phosphorylation-dependent regulation remains incompletely understood. Methods Here, we constructed a high-confidence phosphorylation landscape of STK26 by systematically integrating and harmonizing human phosphoproteomic datasets to resolve site-specific regulatory and signaling relationships. Results We identified five predominant phosphorylation sites S4, T172, T178, S300, and S304 that exhibit distinct patterns of co-differential regulation with candidate/predicted upstream kinases (MAPK14, MAST3, LATS1, TLK1, MAP2K2, AKT2, BRAF, PRKCD, STK10, MAP4K4, and PAK4) and multiple downstream effectors. As a component of the Striatin-interacting phosphatase and kinase (STRIPAK) complex, STK26 displayed coordinated co-regulation with multiple STRIPAK subunits and interactors across diverse experimental conditions, linking its phosphorylation state to Hippo pathway modulation. Notably, T172 and T178 are conserved kinase-domain residues shared across Ste20 family members, consistent with a conserved activation and regulatory mechanism. Phosphorylation at these sites is associated with coordinated regulation of downstream factors in…

title: Anxiety sensitivity and insomnia symptoms in graduate students: the mediating role of difficulties in emotion regulation and the differential moderating role of trait mindfulness
Der Ring of European AI Regulation. Technological Neutrality and Simplification in the Digital Omnibus on AI
abstract: Abstract This article examines the role assigned to the Commission’s guidelines by the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) and the “Digital Omnibus on AI” reform (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) meant to simplify the rules governing AI. As the AI guidelines must clarify definitions, incorporate transferred obligations from binding legislation, and underpin the implementation timelines for the high-risk regime, this work argues that they are structurally overburdened. Indeed, AI guidelines lack binding force, and cannot indirectly acquire such power in the absence of a procedural framework analogous to delegated acts or consolidated case law. Furthermore, the persuasive power of the AI guidelines is limited by the quality of their drafting and the scope of their work. This overburdening is due to the Act’s two main choices: technological neutrality as a means of delegating decision-making power, and a risk-based approach that defers the evaluation of risk downstream. True simplification requires sector-specific legislation, which would enable the Commission’s guidelines to fulfil their functions more effectively.

title: Educational-value beliefs and motivational regulation in teachers’ intentions to engage in arts-based practices
abstract: Arts-based practices offer teachers creative, participatory, and flexible ways of enriching teaching and learning, yet their educational use may reflect perceived capability, educational-value beliefs, motivational quality, and professional context. This study examined arts-related self-efficacy, different forms of motivational regulation, educational-value beliefs, and perceived school support within an individual–contextual framework, focusing on their associations with teachers’ arts-based engagement intention and on differences between teachers with and without prior arts-related training. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 408 in-service teachers in Greece (convenience sample); 302 of them were also analyzed in an earlier publication that did not include educational-value beliefs, school support, or training. Reliability, factor-analytic, and discriminant-validity evidence was generally supportive, although the four-construct confirmatory model showed marginal fit and intrinsic motivation and identified regulation were almost indistinguishable at the latent level. Teachers reported high intention, educational-value beliefs, intrinsic motivation, and identified regulation and low amotivation, with marked ceiling and floor effects. In a simultaneous regression (R 2 = 0.338), educational-value beliefs (β = 0.32) and intrinsic motivation (β = 0.29) were the str…

title: SPP1-APOA1 regulation of M2 macrophage glycolysis promotes epithelial remodeling in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps
abstract: Background Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is characterized by persistent type 2 inflammation, epithelial barrier dysfunction, and tissue remodeling. However, how metabolic reprogramming of macrophages contributes to epithelial remodeling, and which molecular regulators control this process, remains poorly understood. Objectives To investigate whether SPP1 regulates M2 macrophage glycolysis to promote epithelial dysfunction and to explore the counter-regulatory role of APOA1 in this process. Methods Public transcriptomic data and clinical samples were analyzed for SPP1 expression and its associations with macrophage infiltration, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and disease severity. SPP1 knockdown and overexpression were performed in THP-1-derived M2 macrophages, followed by metabolic assays and conditioned-medium experiments with human nasal epithelial cells, including primary cells. Transcriptomic analysis, functional rescue experiments, molecular docking, co-immunoprecipitation, and an OVA/SEB-induced CRSwNP mouse model were used for mechanistic and in vivo validation. Results SPP1 was elevated in CRSwNP tissues and nasal secretions and correlated with Lund-Mackay CT scores (ρ=0.634) and SNOT-22 scores (ρ=0.542). SPP1 was preferentially enriched in M2 macrophages. SPP1 knockdown suppressed, whereas SPP1 overexpression enhanced, glycolytic activity …

title: Historical evidence that wildfire frequency modulates debris-flow hazards through sediment-supply limitation
abstract: Southern California is an epicenter of postwildfire debris flows. In this region, steep topography, frequent fire, heavy rainstorms, and large populations along the wildland-urban interface conspire to produce costly debris flows. Wildfire frequency in the region has tripled in recent decades, causing concern about escalating debris-flow hazards. Here, we investigate how wildfire frequency affects the magnitude of postfire erosion by analyzing long-term debris basin records. We identify two contrasting erosional styles. In steep catchments, erosion exhibits a binge-purge behavior: Erosion for 3 years following fire exceeds background rates by ∼17×. In contrast, in low-sloping, soil-mantled catchments, sediment export following fire only exceeds background rates by ∼1.5×. Critically, in the steep catchments, debris-flow volumes decline when wildfires recur more frequently than the ∼30-year interval characteristic of the past century. This observation suggests a sediment-supply limitation in which more frequent wildfire may reduce, rather than amplify, some of Southern California’s most severe debris-flow hazards.

title: Retrospective analysis: frequency and laterality distribution of neovascular glaucoma
abstract: Purpose To investigate the frequency and distribution of neovascular glaucoma (NVG) between right and left eyes. Methods A retrospective, cross-sectional observational study was conducted, including all outpatients presenting to the University Eye Clinic Graz between December 1996 and April 2024. Electronic records were searched for NVG diagnoses. Laterality distribution and secondary variables (diabetes, central retinal vein occlusion, and ocular ischaemic syndrome) were analysed using a Chi-square test and multivariable logistic regression. Results Of 569, 537 examined eyes, 648 (0.11%) were diagnosed with NVG. Left eyes were affected significantly more often than right eyes (366 left [56.5%] vs 282 right [43.5%]; OR = 1.30, 95% CI 1.11–1.52, p = 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression showed a significant association between left-sided NVG and the presence of diabetes (OR = 1.46, 95% CI 1.03–2.07, p = 0.035). All other secondary variables showed no significant independent association. Conclusion NVG affects the left eye significantly more often than the right eye. This disparity is associated with diabetes mellitus, suggesting a potential lateralised metabolic and haemodynamic susceptibility to ischaemic ocular damage.

title: Dermoscopy guided high frequency ultrasound improves noninvasive identification of superficial basal cell carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Superficial basal cell carcinoma (sBCC) is the one common basal cell carcinoma (BCC) subtype amenable to non-surgical, tissue-sparing treatment, yet its identification currently requires an invasive diagnostic biopsy. We assessed whether adding dermoscopy-guided high-frequency ultrasound (DG-HFUS) to clinical and dermoscopic assessment improves reader identification of sBCC. In a fully crossed multi-reader study, six blinded readers (three board-certified dermatologists and three residents) classified 96 histopathologically confirmed BCCs from 82 patients as sBCC or non-sBCC and rated their confidence, first from clinical and dermoscopic images and then from DG-HFUS images of the same lesion, giving 576 paired assessments. Histopathology was the reference standard. Every performance metric improved and no reader deteriorated on any metric. Pooled accuracy rose from 84.2% to 90.5%, specificity from 85.2% to 91.2%, sensitivity from 74.1% to 83.3%, positive predictive value from 34.2% to 49.5%, and mean reader area under the curve from 0.847 to 0.906. Inter-reader agreement also improved, with Gwet’s AC1 rising from 0.742 to 0.836. Mean confidence rose from 4.21 to 4.64, most markedly where DG-HFUS corrected an initially incorrect diagnosis. DG-HFUS improved non-invasive identification of sBCC for every reader but should complement, not replace, histopathology when select…

title: Multi-omics integration reveals gut microbiota-mediated regulation of cerebral amyloid angiopathy via the gut-brain axis
Playing with Rights: Governing AI-Based Toys through the Lens of the Children’s Right to Development
abstract: Abstract The integration of artificial intelligence into children’s toys raises fundamental regulatory questions that existing EU product safety law only partially answers. This article analyses the interplay between the Toy Safety Regulation (TSR) and the AI Act in governing AI-based toys, focusing on their capacity to protect children’s right to development, as elaborated in Article 6 of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. It argues that while the regulatory regime places emphasis on data protection and prevention of physical harm, it largely neglects long-term developmental harms caused by AI toys. Drawing on the UNCRC framework, this article first elaborates the meaning of the child’s right to development in digitally mediated environments, showing how AI-mediated play transforms toys from static objects into continuous data-production systems (a phenomenon we term “play-as-documentation”). This conceptual lens then informs a critical analysis of the TSR and the AI Act, revealing how both instruments, despite formally acknowledging children as rights-holders, leave gaps in protecting the child’s right to development.

title: Regulation of PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling and inhibition of MAO-B mediate the protective effect of Demethyleneberberine on dopaminergic neurons in Parkinson’s disease mice
abstract: Introduction Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a prevalent chronic neurodegenerative disorder marked by progressive dopaminergic neuron loss, elevated monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B) activity, and severe dopamine depletion. Demethyleneberberine (DMB), a demethylated metabolite of berberine (BBR), has good bioavailability and blood–brain barrier permeability, alongside antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and mitochondria-protective activities. Nevertheless, its neuroprotective action and mechanisms against PD remain poorly defined. Methods Chronic 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) -induced PD mouse models and 1-methyl-4-phenylpyridinium (MPP⁺)-challenged SH-SY5Y cell models were established to investigate the neuroprotective effects and underlying mechanisms of DMB. Rotarod, pole climbing, gait, and open-field tests were performed to evaluate motor function. Behavioral readouts, oxidative stress indicators, and tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) levels were examined to assess DMB’s therapeutic efficacy. MAO-B abundance was quantified by ELISA, while TH expression within the nigrostriatal pathway of mice was visualized using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and immunofluorescence (IF). Western blot was adopted to detect protein phosphorylation of the phosphatidylinositol 3‑kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt)/mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) cascade and apoptosis-related markers B-cel…

title: The interaction between glycosylation and gut microbiota in the regulation of cancer
Insight into the Interaction of Telomeric G-Quadruplex with a Positively Charged Lipid at the Air/Water Interface: Vibrational Sum Frequency Generation Study
abstract: Abstract Understanding the interactions of noncanonical DNA structures with charged membrane interfaces is essential for elucidating their biological functions and developing nucleic acid–based therapeutic platforms. Here, vibrational sum-frequency generation (VSFG) spectroscopy is employed to investigate the interfacial interactions of telomeric DNA in hybrid G-quadruplex (G4), antiparallel G4, and double-stranded (ds) conformations with a positively charged DPTAP monolayer at the air/water interface. All three DNA conformations interact with the cationic lipid primarily through electrostatic interactions between the phosphate backbone and the positively charged headgroups of DPTAP. However, the interaction of the telomeric G4 with the positively charged lipid is strongly dependent on its conformation. The hybrid G4 exhibits the strongest interaction, followed by ds-DNA, whereas the antiparallel G4 interacts the weakest with the lipid monolayer. These differences cannot be explained only by the total number of phosphate groups alone but instead arise from the distinct three-dimensional spatial organization of the phosphate backbone. This work depicts that the topology-dependent arrangement of the phosphate backbone is a key determinant of G4–membrane interactions.

title: The New Era of Greenwashing Enforcement
abstract: Abstract Greenwashing cases are recently on the rise. The entry into force of the “Empowering consumers for the green transition” Directive (Directive 2024/825) is expected to further increase scrutiny by supervising authorities and consumers. This paper reviews cases of enforcement against misleading environmental or sustainability claims and argues that limited enforcement in the past cannot be only attributed to the insufficiency of substantive provisions, but rather to the lack of an appropriate mindset among enforcers. It examines the avenues for private and public enforcement in greenwashing cases and discusses the challenges of each approach, having regard to the recent legislative efforts to improve consumer law enforcement. It concludes that public enforcement is more effective in greenwashing cases, while the enhancement of centralised enforcement at the EU level would also be desirable.

title: Huangqi Sijunzi Decoction ameliorates breast cancer-related fatigue via PPARG-mediated regulation of the mitochondrial–immune–metabolic axis: an integrative mechanistic study
abstract: Background Breast cancer-related fatigue (BCRF) substantially impairs patients’ quality of life, yet effective interventions remain limited. Huangqi Sijunzi Decoction (HQSJZD) has demonstrated clinical efficacy in alleviating cancer-associated asthenia; however, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Objective This study aimed to systematically elucidate the core targets and molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of HQSJZD on BCRF using integrated computational approaches. Methods The chemical constituents of HQSJZD were identified using UPLC-QE-MS and screened based on an oral bioavailability threshold of ≥30% and a drug-likeness score of ≥0.18. Drug-disease intersection targets were obtained through network pharmacology. Core genes were identified using 113 combinations of machine-learning algorithms and evaluated using SHAP values. Their expression, prognostic significance, and associations with immune infiltration were validated using TCGA-BRCA data. Two-sample Mendelian randomization, single-cell virtual knockout analysis (scTenifoldKnk), molecular docking, and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations were performed for causal inference, functional characterization, and binding validation. Results A total of 78 constituents were identified, of which 13 were screened as potential active ingredients. Intersecting 234 predicted drug targets with disease-associa…

title: Increasing the Bearing Capacity of Bridge Span Beams
abstract: It is noted that Ibeams have the highest bearing capacity. At the same time, due to the widespread use and availability of rolled pipes, tubular beams are often used in practice. Comparison of these beams by bearing capacity should be carried out provided that they have equal mass per linear meter. An Ibeam according to GOST R 57837–2017 is compared, the mass of a linear meter of which is 194 kg, and a pipe according to GOST 33228–2015, with an indicator of 194 kg/m. The bearing capacity of an Ibeam is almost twice as high as that of a tubular one. There is information about tubular concrete beams, in particular, with a prestressed lower part of the concrete core. The steel pipe in such beams plays the role of external reinforcement – exo reinforcement. The bearing capacity of tubular concrete beams is very significant given their low cost and good manufacturability. The objective of this work is to develop a method for increasing the bearing capacity of tubular beams, which will expand the range of building structures. The technique of geometric optimization and a thought experiment is used. The idea of using a liquid filler for a tubular beam is based on a wellknown property of liquid – its practical incompressibility. A geometric long body, the lateral surface of which has a rectilinear generatrix, has a maximum volume (for a given lateral surface) if its cross section has t…

Co-creating public value in rural micro-municipalities: collaborative governance under proximity and capacity constraints
abstract: Purpose This study addresses a central public management problem: how structurally capacity-constrained public organisations mobilise, coordinate and sustain resources distributed across civic, private and community actors for public service provision. Using a rural micro-municipality as a revealing empirical setting, it examines how organisational capacity and relational proximity condition public value co-creation and collaborative service provision. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts an in-depth qualitative case study of Gagliano Aterno, Italy. Data collected between 2023 and 2025 combine semi-structured interviews, direct observation, participatory action research, participatory mapping and sensemaking activities, enabling a processual and multi-actor analysis of collaborative governance. Findings Capacity constraints encourage the municipality to mobilise distributed resources through adaptive coordination, but also make this orchestration fragile. Public value trajectories are non-linear and may become vulnerable to erosion as successful mobilisation generates additional demands on finite civic and organisational resources, while proximity operates as an ambivalent governance condition: dense relationships facilitate trust, mobilisation and responsiveness, yet can concentrate voice, reinforce dependence on established networks and produce uneven participation. title: The Public Relations Capacity Gap in Policy Communication on Infectious Disease Prevention and Control in Vietnam
abstract: Government public relations in infectious disease prevention and control extends beyond the dissemination of official information. It encompasses the institutional and operational capacity to facilitate dialogue, uphold accountability and foster public trust. Drawing on a survey of 306 health officials across three administrative levels and 27 in-depth interviews, this study examines government public relations capacity along six dimensions. Transparency and accountability received the highest self-rating, at 4.04 on a five-point scale, whereas individual communication capacity ranked last at 3.48. A multiple regression model shows that administrative level and the frequency of specialised training are both associated with individual capacity, although together they explain only eight per cent of its variance. The raw difference between men and women in overall capacity disappears once position and training are controlled, but the difference in confidence in speaking publicly persists. Interview evidence attributes the gap to the dissolution of dedicated communication units and the resulting reliance on staff who perform communication duties alongside clinical work. The findings rest on self-report and should be read as evidence of perceived rather than demonstrated capacity. They indicate that the health communication system satisfies those requirements an institution can meet…

title: Dynamic carrying capacity and real-time early warning systems for tuna aquaculture under thermal stress
abstract: In summer 2025, Atlantic bluefin tuna ( Thunnus thynnus ) farms in Gerence Bay, an enclosed Aegean embayment, suffered a mass mortality caused by capsulated Lactococcus garvieae . No validated early warning system exists for enclosed Mediterranean tuna embayments. We tested whether open-access oceanographic products can support one. We combined a 4.2 km Copernicus reanalysis and a 1 km satellite sea-surface temperature analysis at five farms (four in Gerence Bay, one in Sığacık Bay) with in-situ records from three of them: a 2025 daily farm record, 2026 high-frequency cage probes and 2026 daily dive-time temperature profiles. The reanalysis treated the inner embayment as land, placed its nearest usable grid cell 7–11 km from the Gerence farms and ran consistently cold at cage sites in both bays. The satellite analysis resolved every farm, closely tracked the 2026 in-situ records and revealed a warm inner-bay gradient that the reanalysis could not see. Literature-based lactococcosis thresholds were exceeded throughout every summer, so simple threshold alerts carried no timing information. Cumulative degree-days showed a modest but consistent excess at Gerence relative to Sığacık across thresholds and lags. However, the 2025 summer was not anomalous, and the warmer 2023 and 2024 summers passed without a mass mortality. Temperature therefore acted as a permissive background rather…

title: 4H-pyran and 4H-benzochromene derivatives incorporating the vanillin fragment as cholinesterase and urease inhibitors with antioxidant capacity: synthesis, in vitro, and in silico investigations
Artificial intelligence readiness of higher education in Central Asia: a document-based comparative policy review of national strategies, curriculum reform, and institutional capacity (2017–2026)
abstract: Higher education systems in the five post-Soviet Central Asian states—Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan—have begun to articulate national positions on the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), both as an object of curriculum and as a tool of pedagogy. This review takes stock of that policy effort. We collected and analyzed thirty-one publicly available national policy documents, ministerial decrees, institutional strategies, and international assessments published between 2017 and May 2026, and compared them along seven dimensions: existence and depth of a national AI strategy; curriculum reform of computer-science and adjacent programs; allocation of competitive research funding for AI; faculty preparedness; access to non-Russian-language scientific resources; open-access mandates; and formalized industry–university partnerships. Two analysts independently coded assessable country–dimension cells on an anchor rubric (raw observed agreement p o = 0.89 ; unweighted Cohen’s κ = 0.78 ; linearly weighted κ w = 0.84 ). The comparative picture is uneven. Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan lead, with dedicated AI strategies, substantial curriculum reform, and visible international partnerships; Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan have adopted broader digital-economy strategies that subsume AI but have not invested in matching curriculum reform; Turkmenistan is chara…

title: Followership as organizational capability: a Capacity-Permission Model in a knowledge-intensive setting
abstract: Purpose In response to calls for follower-centric and contextualized followership research, this study proposes followership as an organizational capability and develops the Capacity-Permission Model to explain how internal organizational environment enables or constrains followership enactment. The research examines how structural capacity and psychological permission mechanisms shape followership enactment beyond leader–follower exchanges. Design/methodology/approach Semi-structured interviews were conducted with educators (n = 16) in a higher education institution (HEI) in the Middle East. Thematic analysis was supported by content analysis to identify dominant followership schemas and adaptive behavioral responses. Findings Ideal followership schemas emphasize compliance, role clarity, reliability and competence, whereas constructive voice is framed as conditional and improvement-oriented. Followership enactment depends on two main enabling mechanisms: structural capacity, which is reflected in work design feasibility and organizational stability and psychological permission reflected in trust, transparency and psychological safety. A hierarchical and rule-oriented internal environment constrains autonomy and innovativeness, shaping adaptive responses including peer support, constrained compliance, withdrawal, change fatigue coping and exit orientation. Research limitations…

Polynomial Regression in Assessing the Load- Bearing Capacity of a Car Wheel Set
abstract: In countries where rolling stock with increased axle loads is used, significant damage to wheel sets is recorded, particularly due to wheel shift on the axle. This typically leads to car derailments, with significant economic losses. With the trend toward increasing axle loads, as outlined in the Transport Strategy of the Russian Federation for the period up to 2030, with increasing axle loads to 27–30 tf, an increase in wheel set damage is evident, particularly the potential for damage to the pressed joint of the wheel axle. The objective of this article is to demonstrate the feasibility of using polynomial regression to predict the loadbearing capacity of a car wheel set under all possible combinations of loading factors. The data base for this analysis is the result of a full factorial experiment, i. e., a finite element calculation of the wheel set under all combinations of six loading factors. To verify the adequacy of the proposed polynomial regression model, mathematical statistics methods are used: descriptive statistics, analysis of variance, multiple correlation and determination coefficients, criterion evaluations, evaluation of regression model equation coefficients, assessment of the normality of distribution, evaluation of the regression equation residuals for outliers, and evaluation of the predicted values of the response function. Tabular and graphical presenta…

title: How economic vulnerability shapes citizens evaluations of government conflict resolution capacity in times of insecurity across Africa
abstract: Abstract Across much of Africa, escalating conflict is testing the social contract between citizens and the state. Drawing on Afrobarometer Round 8 data covering 33 African countries, this paper examines how perceived insecurity shapes citizens’ evaluations of government capacity to prevent and resolve violent conflict, and whether economic vulnerability moderates this relationship. Using ordered logistic regression, we show that perceived insecurity is robustly associated with more negative evaluations of government conflict-handling, even after controlling for institutional trust, perceived corruption, perceived inequality, and a wide range of socio-demographic characteristics. Most novel, the negative effect of insecurity is meaningfully attenuated among economically vulnerable respondents: the more deprived a citizen, the less responsive their evaluation of the state becomes to changes in their security environment. The findings extend output-based theories of state legitimacy by showing that citizens’ evaluations of governance are filtered through material conditions, and they suggest that durable legitimacy in insecure environments will require integrated investments in security, institutional quality, and material wellbeing.

title: The Impact of Accounting Information Systems, Information Technology Utilization, Human Resource Capacity, and Internal Control on the Timeliness of Government Agency Financial Reporting
abstract: Background: Public financial accountability depends partly on whether government reports reach users when they are needed. Statutory reporting obligations alone do not explain differences in timeliness, making the organizational conditions surrounding report preparation an important subject of investigation. Objective: The research assesses the relationships of accounting information systems, information technology utilization, human resource capacity, and internal control with financial reporting timeliness in a government agency. Methods: A quantitative, cross-sectional survey was conducted among financial administration personnel at the Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries. Purposive selection produced 80 eligible respondents. Questionnaire data were examined through multiple linear regression using SPSS version 30.0, with the four organizational factors entered as predictors of reporting timeliness. Results: After adjustment for the other predictors, neither accounting information systems nor information technology utilization showed a statistically significant relationship with timeliness. Human resource capacity and internal control, however, each had a positive, statistically significant coefficient. Conclusion: The findings identify staff capacity and internal control as relevant correlates of timely reporting in the surveyed ministry. They provide a basis for prior…

title: Performance Analysis of 8W4L Wheel-Legged Hybrid Mobile Robot with Parallel Mechanism
abstract: This article proposes an 8W4L wheel leg composite mobile robot based on a 2-PUS&PRPR parallel mechanism, equipped with eight omnidirectional wheels and four sets of parallel branched legs, supporting three motion modes: full wheel, leg type, and wheel leg composite. Through the analysis of screw theory, it is concluded that the mechanism has four degrees of freedom, including three directional movement and single axis rotation; Derive the inverse position solution through closed-loop vector method, solve the workspace, and construct the Jacobian matrix to analyze the singular configuration and force transmission performance. The article compares two application modes and applicable scenarios of institutions, completes gait planning for cross gully working conditions, and verifies the effectiveness of the scheme through simulation. Research has shown that the obstacle crossing ability and stability of the robot have been greatly improved, providing a theoretical basis for the application of parallel mechanisms in the field of mobile robots.

Abnormal CCL3-CCR1 signaling in the monocyte/macrophage-osteoclast axis: a crucial mechanism in osteosarcoma lung metastasis
abstract: Background Pulmonary metastasis is the dominant pattern of distant metastasis in osteosarcoma and severely impairs patient survival, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying osteosarcoma lung metastasis remain poorly understood. Methods In this exploratory study, we integrated bioinformatic analyses and experimental validation to examine whether disruption of CCL3-CCR1-mediated crosstalk between monocytes/macrophages and osteoclasts is associated with osteosarcoma pulmonary metastasis. Single-cell transcriptome data (1 osteosarcoma patient with lung metastasis and 5 patients with primary non-metastatic osteosarcoma) and bulk RNA sequencing data were analyzed, followed by experimental validation in an orthotopic osteosarcoma mouse model and in vitro osteoclast assays. Results Osteosarcoma patients with concurrent pulmonary metastasis exhibited decreased monocyte/macrophage infiltration and fewer osteoclasts in primary tumor tissues compared with patients without metastasis. In an orthotopic osteosarcoma mouse model, treatment with an anti-CCL3 antibody suppressed glyoxylate and dicarboxylate metabolism and altered the metabolic reprogramming of osteoclasts, as demonstrated by qPCR of Aco2 and Mdh1 in tumor tissues and by in vitro osteoclast assays, including itaconate measurement; multiplex immunofluorescence and qPCR showed that these changes were accompanied by reduced CD8 + T …

title: SIRT3 alleviates macrophage senescence and peritoneal fibrosis: a BNIP3-mediated mechanism targeting the mPTP-mtDNA-cGAS axis
abstract: Background Long-term peritoneal dialysis (PD) often leads to peritoneal fibrosis (PF) and is closely associated with peritoneal dialysis fluid (PDF)-induced mitochondrial damage and senescence-associated inflammatory responses in macrophages. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms are poorly understood. This study investigated the role of SIRT3 in PDF-induced macrophage senescence and peritoneal fibrosis using a PD mouse model and RAW264.7 macrophages. Methods In the PD-induced PF mouse model and RAW264.7 macrophages, the role of SIRT3 in PDF-induced macrophage senescence was investigated using lentivirus-mediated SIRT3 overexpression and knockdown, proteomics, co-immunoprecipitation, molecular docking, Western blotting, qPCR, in vivo administration of the SIRT3 agonist honokiol (HKL), and in vitro blockade of mPTP with cyclosporine A (CsA). Results PDF treatment downregulated SIRT3 expression in macrophages. This was accompanied by mitochondrial damage, mtDNA release, and upregulation of senescence markers. SIRT3 overexpression or pharmacological activation of SIRT3 reversed these effects, whereas SIRT3 knockdown recapitulated PDF-induced phenotypes. Proteomics identified BNIP3 as a downstream target of SIRT3. Physical interaction between BNIP3 and SIRT3 was validated by co-immunoprecipitation and molecular docking. Mechanistically, SIRT3 blocked mtDNA release by inhibit…

title: The mechanism by which facilitating conditions affect university teachers’ behavioral intention to use GenAI through a chain mediation analysis based on the technology acceptance model
Beyond pain phenotyping: a phenotype–topography–mechanism framework for treatment selection in female pelvic venous disorders
Mucin degradation by Enterocloster sp. M3 as an oncogenic mechanism in colorectal cancer
abstract: Background: Enterocloster sp. M3 (M3) has been implicated in colorectal cancer (CRC) through production of oncogenic metabolites, yet its interactions with colonic cells remain unclear. This study aimed to identify the functional role of M3 in CRC by genomic and proteomic comparison with its closest relative, Enterocloster aldenensis (E. aldenensis), followed by functional validation. Methods: An integrated genomic and proteomic approach compared molecular features between M3 and E. aldenensis. Carbon source utilization assays compared the metabolic flexibility of M3 and E. aldenensis. In vitro mucin degradation and growth assays, alongside an in vivo mouse model, validated M3’s mucin-degrading capacity and its impact on gut barrier function. Results: Compared with E. aldenensis, genomics and proteomics revealed that M3 possesses enhanced metabolic potential for mucin utilization through a coordinated axis spanning extracellular glycan cleavage [e.g., glycoside hydrolases (GHs) / mannosyl-glycoprotein endo-beta-N-acetylglucosaminidases (ENGases)] transmembrane phosphotransferase system (PTS)-mediated internalization, and intracellular metabolic processing [e.g., N-acetylglucosamine-6-phosphate (GlcNAc-6-P) deacetylase, fructose-bisphosphate aldolase, and L-fucose isomerase]. Phenotypic metabolic profiling demonstrated M3’s versatile capacity to utilize diverse carbon and nitrog…

title: Selenium isotopes uncover the mechanism of the deep plate tectonic cycle in the MORB mantle
abstract: Subduction has recycled oceanic crust into Earth’s interior for billions of years, yet how deeply subducted material evolves and contributes to mantle-derived melts, such as mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORBs), remains poorly resolved. Because subducting slab-derived dehydration fluids typically produce isotopically light selenium (Se) in residual eclogites, which is transferred to mantle melts without further fractionation, Se serves as a powerful isotope-based tracer of recycled components into the mantle. Here, we present high-precision Se isotope data for recycled crust–derived garnet pyroxenites that bridge the gap between the primitive mantle and isotopically lighter MORB. Through two-stage thermodynamic modeling, we trace the reactive infiltration of eclogite-derived melts within the convective mantle, leading to the concurrent formation of subduction-derived garnet pyroxenites that preserve residual eclogite cores, both of which contribute to the mantle source of MORBs during adiabatic decompression. Our results establish a petrologically consistent and isotope-validated framework to trace the fate of subducted crust and its long-term imprint on the MORB mantle throughout the deep plate tectonic cycle.

title: Short-video content marketing and sports product purchase intention: a chain mediation mechanism study
abstract: Introduction This study examined the association between short-video content marketing and sports product purchase intention, focusing on the roles of product involvement and perceived value. Methods Survey data from 517 Chinese sports product consumers were analyzed using structural equation modeling and composite-score serial mediation analysis. Results Short-video content marketing was positively associated with purchase intention. Composite-score analysis identified indirect associations through product involvement, perceived value, and their sequential pathway. The total indirect association was B = 0.098 (95% CI: 0.054 -0.153). Discussion Product involvement and perceived value may help explain the association between short-video content marketing and sports product purchase intention. The findings offer guidance for the design of short-video marketing content for sports products.
