title: Strengthening the Capacity of Community Health Cadres Through an Evidence-Based Practice Home Visit Program to Optimize Physical and Psychological Recovery of Postpartum Mothers
abstract: Background: Limited postpartum monitoring after discharge delays detection of physical and psychological complications. Strengthening community health cadres through evidence-based practice (EBP) training and structured home visits may improve community-based care. Purpose: To examine the effect of EBP training on cadres' knowledge and skills, and of cadre-led home visits on mothers' physical and psychological recovery. Methods: A quasi-experimental study with a non-equivalent control group was conducted at Bilokka Primary Health Center, Indonesia, involving 10 cadres and 30 postpartum mothers (intervention, n = 15; control, n = 15). Cadres received EBP training. The intervention group received four home visits over six weeks; controls received routine care. Outcomes were assessed using knowledge and skills instruments, the REEDA Scale, Numeric Rating Scale, and Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). Results: Training significantly increased cadres' knowledge (61.40 to 85.80) and skills (60.80 to 87.10) (both p < 0.001). The intervention group had significantly better wound healing, less bleeding, lower pain, and lower EPDS scores than controls (p ≤ 0.001); mean EPDS fell from 13.67 to 5.93. Controls showed no significant change. Conclusions: EBP training improved cadres' competence, and cadre-led home visits were associated with better postpartum recovery. Integrating bo…

title: Steric Hindrance-Governed Configurational Evolution in Cellulose-Derived Sustainable Multicolor Carbon Dots: Application in Smartphone-Assisted Portable Nitrite Sensing
abstract: Abstract Renewable biomass is a promising precursor for sustainable carbon dots (CDs), yet the controllable synthesis of multicolor emissive CDs remains a major challenge. Herein, we proposed a steric hindrance-mediated strategy to achieve the multicolor emission of cellulose-derived CDs via employing three phenylenediamine isomers, including o-phenylenediamine (OPD), m-phenylenediamine (MPD), and p-phenylenediamine (PPD), as dopants during the hydrothermal process of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC). Changing the dopant from OPD to PPD was beneficial in reducing steric hindrance between the dopants and CMC and thus contributed to the increased percentage of conjugated sp2 carbon (from 3.36% to 13.58%) and graphitic N (from 5.54% to 11.09%) in the three CDs. The synergistic effect of enlarged conjugated structure and enhanced graphitic N content narrowed the energy gap of three CDs from 2.89 to 2.81 eV and further to 2.76 eV, enabling them to emit blue (430.8 nm), green (505.1 nm), and yellow (522.5 nm) fluorescence, respectively. Owing to the high quantum yield of 20.0% and long-wavelength fluorescence, the green-emitted CDs were employed as a sensitive fluorescent probe for nitrite detection with a detection limit of 0.42 µM. Moreover, a paper-based sensing platform was constructed by chemical grafting of the CDs onto filter paper for portable analysis with smartphone assistance…

title: The Role of Gamma Irradiation in Tailoring Carbon-Based Catalysts for Oxygen Reduction in Air-Cathodes: A Review
abstract: Abstract Carbon-based catalysts have emerged as promising alternatives to noble-metal electrocatalysts for air-cathodes in metal-air batteries and fuel cells. Their limited intrinsic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity and durability necessitate effective modification strategies. This review examines the role of gamma (γ) irradiation as a postsynthetic modification approach for carbon-based catalysts used in ORR. It discusses irradiation-induced structural and electronic changes, including defect generation, surface functionalization, pore development, and electronic structure tuning. These modifications increase active-site density, facilitate oxygen adsorption, and improve charge-transfer kinetics, leading to enhanced ORR activity, selectivity, and durability. It also highlighted the influence of irradiation dose and processing conditions, emphasizing the need for optimized irradiation parameters to maximize catalytic performance while avoiding structural degradation. A comprehensive assessment of γ-irradiation-driven engineering of carbon catalysts is analyzed for air-cathodes, establishing structure–property–performance relationships and highlighting γ-irradiation as a scalable, environmentally friendly route for developing high-performance ORR electrocatalysts.

title: Biomass production and carbon storage dynamics across agroforestry systems along an elevational gradient in the North Western Himalaya
abstract: The expansion of agroforestry has substantial potential for carbon storage and mitigating climate-change. Thus, the present study has been carried out in the Shivalik hills of North Western Himalayas at an average elevation of 650 m amsl during 2025–26 to assess the biomass production and the carbon storage potential of existing agroforestry systems. The study area was divided into two altitudinal zones viz. , 500–750 m amsl (A 1 ) and 751–1000 m amsl (A 2 ) and seven agroforestry systems namely Agrisilviculture (AS), Agrisilvipastoral (ASP), Agrisilvihorticulture (ASH), Agrihortisilviculture (AHS), Silvipastoral (SP), Hortipastoral (HP) and Pastoralsilviculture (PS) were identified. Results revealed considerable variation in biomass production among agroforestry systems with total biomass ranging from 11.35 to 24.40 t ha -1 . The maximum above ground biomass, below ground biomassand total biomass were recorded under ASH (18.82 t ha -1 , 5.58 t ha -1 and 24.40 t ha -1 ) whereas the minimum in PS (8.88 t ha -1 , 2.47 t ha -1 and 11.35 t ha -1 ), respectively. In altitudinal gradients, total biomass increased from 17.55 t ha -1 at A 1 to 19.83 t ha -1 at A 2 . Likely to this, the maximum surface soil organic carbon was observed in ASH (14.11 t ha -1 ) and lowest in PS (9.16 t ha -1 ). Vegetation carbon stock ranged from 5.11 t ha -1 under PS to 10.98 t ha -1 under ASH. When veget…

title: CARBON EMISSION DISCLOSURE, CSR, UKURAN PERUSAHAAN, LEVERAGE TERHADAP NILAI PERUSAHAAN ASEAN
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of Carbon Emission Disclosure (CED), Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), firm size, and leverage on firm value in manufacturing sub-sector companies listed in the ASEAN region for the period 2021-2024. This research uses a quantitative approach with secondary data obtained from the annual reports and sustainability reports of the companies. The sampling technique used was purposive sampling, resulting in 36 manufacturing companies from Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, and Singapore, with a total of 144 research observations. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression analysis with the help of the IBM Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 25 program. The research results show that Carbon Emission Disclosure (CED), Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), firm size, and leverage both partially and simultaneously have a negative and significant impact on firm value.

title: Multi-functional analysis of geopolymer concrete reinforced with carbon fibre and graphene powder
abstract: In this study, geopolymer concrete (GPC) reinforced with carbon fibre (CF) and graphene powder (GP) was examined as a sustainable alternative to conventional concrete. The binder in the GPC was a blend of 60% ground granulated blast-furnace slag and 40% fly ash. The aim of this work was to improve the performance of the GPC with different additions of CF and GP, in terms of maximising mechanical strengths, microstructural development and ability to protect against electromagnetic and electroacoustic (EA) interference. An extensive experimental programme was undertaken, incorporating compressive, split tensile and flexural strength tests, ultrasonic pulse velocity measurements. Scanning electron microscopy, energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy were used for microstructural characterisation. The results showed that the GPC with 1% CF and 0.5% GP produced the optimum results, with a high compressive strength of 63.7 MPa and split tensile strength of 5.3 MPa. Moreover, this blend had a high degree of multi-functional capability with an electromagnetic shielding capability of up to 19 dB and EA energy capture of more than 90% in the lower frequencies.

Egg-derived bacterial isolates increase the apparent β-pinene emission rate and reduce fruit acceptance by Curculio dieckmanni, a seed pest of woody Corylus plants
abstract: Curculio dieckmanni Faust is a major seed pest of woody Corylus plants in China. Female oviposition decisions can influence offspring access to limited resources and the spatial distribution of seed damage. We tested whether artificial egg insertion changes hazelnut acceptance and volatiles, and whether egg-associated bacteria can reproduce these responses. Two-choice oviposition assays, gas chromatography–mass spectrometry, gas chromatography–electroantennographic detection, Y-tube assays, bacterial isolation, and reinoculation were combined. Mated females avoided fruits held for 24 or 48 h after insertion of one egg, whereas mechanical puncturing alone did not reduce acceptance. Camphene, 3-methyl-apopinene, and β-pinene elicited repeatable antennal responses; only β-pinene significantly altered orientation. Its effect varied with dose, with avoidance at filter-paper doses of 4–100 ng but no significant preference at 1 ng. Apparent β-pinene emission rates were 0.290 ± 0.082 ng fruit −1 h −1 in untreated control fruits and 4.647 ± 0.677 and 6.227 ± 1.099 ng fruit −1 h −1 at 24 and 48 h, respectively (mean ± standard error; n = 3 samples per treatment). Egg-surface wash and egg-derived Klebsiella and Enterobacter isolates each reproduced reduced fruit acceptance and an increased apparent β-pinene emission rate. These results support bacterial involvement in an altered fruit-odo…

Beyond SAF Certification: Reconciling ISCC CORSIA and ISCC EU through Life-Cycle Carbon Accounting, Feedstock Eligibility and Double-Counting Prevention in International Aviation
abstract: The international expansion of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) has exposed a critical distinction between sustainability certification, quantified life-cycle greenhouse gas reductions, and legal recognition of those reductions. This qualitative literature review examines the relationship between ISCC CORSIA and ISCC EU, emphasizing their different regulatory purposes, life cycle assessment methods, feedstock criteria, and controls against duplicate environmental claims. Drawing on 64 journal articles published during 2020-2026 and authoritative ICAO and European Union documents, the review synthesizes six themes: certification non-equivalence, carbon-intensity methodology, feedstock eligibility, chain-of-custody integrity, market implications, and institutional interoperability. The analysis identifies a recurrent governance error: treating possession of a recognized certificate as sufficient proof that the same emissions benefit can be claimed under multiple compliance or voluntary frameworks. It proposes a three-gate model that separates qualified physical fuel, regime-specific life-cycle calculation, and exclusive claim entitlement. Particular attention is given to the differentiated legal treatment of palm-derived materials, including palm fatty acid distillate, palm oil mill effluent, and empty palm fruit bunches. A linked physical-batch and claims-ledger architecture, sup…

title: Chemical Structure Determination and Separation of a Carbon-Skeleton Dimer Impurity (5,5′-Iminobis[4-oxopentanoic acid]) Derived from 5-Aminolevulinic Acid Phosphate
abstract: Abstract 5-Aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) has garnered considerable attention as a high-purity pharmaceutical and nutraceutical ingredient. Herein, we report the formation of a previously under-recognized hydrophilic impurity, 5,5′-iminobis[4-oxopentanoic acid] (IBOPA), from 5-aminolevulinic acid phosphate (5-ALAP). The conditions for separating IBOPA from 5-ALAP were systematically explored using high-performance liquid chromatography, enabling the preparative fractionation of IBOPA despite its low abundance. The chemical structure of IBOPA was elucidated via liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC/MS) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analyses of the isolated fraction. Although IBOPA has rarely been reported in the literature, its structure was unambiguously determined via independent chemical synthesis, and the LC/MS and NMR spectra of the synthesized compound were consistent with those of the fractionated impurity. A strategy for the separation of IBOPA from 5-ALAP was also developed. Exploiting the higher hydrophilicity and ionic character of IBOPA relative to those of 5-ALAP, we established an anion-exchange resin-based separation method, which enabled the partial separation of 5-ALAP and IBOPA. Overall, this study reports the formation and definitive structural elucidation of IBOPA and provides a separation approach for its separation from 5-ALAP. The findings provid…

title: MODELOS PREDITIVOS DE QUANTIFICAÇÃO DE CARBONO ORGÂNICO POR ESPECTRORRADIOMETRIA EM SOLOS DA CAATINGA
abstract: O carbono orgânico do solo (COS) é indicador primário de qualidade do solo e componente central do ciclo biogeoquímico do carbono, mas sua determinação por métodos laboratoriais convencionais é lenta e onerosa, o que limita o monitoramento em regiões extensas e pouco amostradas, como o semiárido brasileiro. A espectroscopia de reflectância difusa associada à quimiometria é uma alternativa rápida e de baixo custo, porém o desempenho dos modelos depende do pré-processamento espectral, do algoritmo de calibração e da representatividade amostral, aspectos ainda pouco avaliados em solos da Caatinga. Este trabalho testou modelos preditivos de COS em solos de áreas naturais e antropizadas (pastejo) da Caatinga com base em espectros Vis-NIR-SWIR. Foram utilizadas 52 amostras da camada de 0–5 cm, coletadas em 2013 pela Embrapa Semiárido em nove municípios de sete estados, lidas em laboratório com espectrorradiômetro FieldSpec 3 Hi-Res (350–2500 nm). Modelos de Regressão por Mínimos Quadrados Parciais (PLSR) e Random Forest (RF) foram calibrados com o espectro em reflectância (SPEC) e com seis pré-processamentos — absorbância (AB), remoção do contínuo (CRR), correção multiplicativa de espalhamento (MSC), primeira derivada de Savitzky-Golay (SG), suavização (SMO) e variação normal padrão (SNV) — e avaliados por validação cruzada leave-one-out (R², RMSE e RPIQ). Os teores de COS variaram d…

title: RuO 2 -anchored, NiCo-embedded nitrogen-doped carbon nanofibers as a free-standing electrode for efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: Abstract Developing high-performance cathodes for alkaline water electrolysis requires the concurrent optimization of active sites, electron-transport pathways, and electrode architecture. In this work, we report a binder-free, free-standing electrode composed of RuO 2 -anchored, NiCo-embedded N-doped carbon nanofibers (RuO 2 -NiCo/NCNF) for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in alkaline media. NiCo layered double hydroxide, derived from a Co-based zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF-67), was incorporated into electrospun polyacrylonitrile nanofibers and converted into a conductive carbon nanofiber network containing embedded NiCo alloy domains through stabilization and carbonization. These domains provide a favorable environment for the subsequent deposition-precipitation of Ru species, thereby enabling the facile introduction of RuO 2 onto the nanofiber surface. In 1.0 M KOH, RuO 2 -NiCo/NCNF exhibited overpotentials of 48 mV at | j | = 10 mA cm −2 and 208 mV at | j | = 100 mA cm −2 , outperforming NiCo/NCNF, RuO 2 -NCNF, pristine NCNF, and a commercial 10 wt.% Pt/C electrode (0.0385 mg Pt cm −2 ) under identical testing conditions. Furthermore, the electrode maintained stable operation for 50 h. This enhanced alkaline HER performance is attributed to the synergistic integration of amorphous hydrous RuO 2 and NiCo within a conductive and mechanically robust nanofiber scaff…

title: Glucose-Assisted Hydrothermal Carbonization of Defatted Microalgae into N/O-Rich Porous Carbon for Cd2+ Adsorption
abstract: Abstract Defatted microalgal residues provide intrinsic nitrogen for carbon adsorbents. Here, defatted Chlorella pyrenoidosa and glucose were converted into N/O-rich biochar-like solid carbon (BSC-DFCP+G) by hydrothermal carbonization at 200 °C for 5 h followed by calcination at 300 °C for 4 h. Glucose addition increased hydrochar yield, although Maillard-type condensation and enhanced nitrogen recovery were not directly verified. BSC-DFCP+G had a BET surface area of 328 m2/g and a nitrogen content of 5.31 wt %. Batch isotherms measured at 30 °C with 60 mg adsorbent in 50 mL, initial Cd2+ concentrations of 10–100 mg/L, and 10 h contact yielded a fitted Langmuir capacity of 39.19 mg/g. Competitive tests at 5 mg/L initial Cd2+ showed smaller uptake reductions with Ca2+ and Mg2+ than with Cu2+ and Pb2+; mixed-ion uptake retained 82.02% of the Cd-only value. Across five consecutive adsorptions, capacity decreased from 32.0 to 25.6 mg/g, retaining 80.0% after four dilute-HCl regeneration treatments. FTIR/XPS changes and reduced N2-accessible porosity suggest possible O/N-site and pore-related contributions but do not establish specific binding structures or a dominant removal mechanism. The results support laboratory assessment of this residue-to-carbon route. Real-water performance, trace-level removal, practical contact times, quantitative regeneration efficiency, and long-term ma…

title: X-Ray Emission Study of TeV Blazars
abstract: Abstract In this work, we present a systematic X-ray study of 85 TeV-detected blazars based on archival Swift X-Ray Telescope (XRT) and NuSTAR observations available up to 2024 May. We derive unabsorbed X-ray fluxes and photon indices through spectral fitting and investigate their light curves, spectral energy distributions, flux distributions, power spectral densities (PSDs), and flux–index correlations. Using the fractional variability method, we identify 78 sources as variable in the soft X-ray band and 14 sources as variable in the hard X-ray band. For well-sampled soft X-ray light curves, the flux distributions are generally better described by lognormal functions, while the PSD slopes span β PSD = 0.1–1.6, with most values between 1.0 and 1.6, where the PSD is defined as P ( f ) ∝ f − β PSD . We find positive correlations between TeV and X-ray luminosities, supporting a leptonic emission scenario. We also find a correlation between X-ray and disk luminosities, whereas no significant correlation is found between X-ray luminosity and black hole mass.

title: Beyond Double Charging: Reconciling CORSIA and the EU Emissions Trading System through Climate Policy Coherence, Environmental Integrity and Equitable Aviation Governance
abstract: The evolving relationship between the International Civil Aviation Organization’s Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) poses a complex challenge for climate governance. This article uses a critical qualitative literature review of peer-reviewed research published from 2020 through 2026, interpreted alongside authoritative ICAO and European Union materials. It distinguishes overlapping financial obligations from administrative duplication, carbon-credit double claiming, and legitimate concurrent regulation. The thematic synthesis finds that a common global framework improves predictability but does not independently guarantee emissions additionality, while regional cap-and-trade can strengthen carbon-price incentives yet potentially alter competition among air routes and transit hubs. The European Commission’s July 2026 aviation proposal, envisaging expanded geographical application from 2029 if adopted, sharpens these tensions. The article develops an operator–route–year diagnostic framework, assesses carbon-market integrity and distributional effects, and proposes a five-part compatibility architecture covering legal-scope mapping, auditable cost deductions, registry safeguards, competition and equity review, and recurrent ICAO–EU dialogue. For Indonesia and other international aviat…

title: A permissioned blockchain-based transactive architecture for smart contract-driven P2P energy trading in prosumer communities
abstract: The growth of distributed renewable generation has increased the number of prosumers who both generate and consume electricity. This paper proposes a permissioned blockchain architecture for peer-to-peer (P2P) energy settlement in prosumer communities. A structured review of 62 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015, and June 2026 informs the design. The architecture combines a private Ethereum network using Quorum Byzantine Fault Tolerant (QBFT) consensus, four interacting smart contracts, a multi-oracle metering bridge, and a network-feasibility oracle operated by the distribution system operator (DSO). Its contributions are interval-level energy allocation with controls against double assignment, shared-capacity accounting across concurrent contracts, a specification for four forms of oracle redundancy, a smart-contract state-transition model covering normal and error paths, and a token-flow model that reconciles payments and collateral under normal delivery, surplus, shortfall, DSO curtailment, and oracle timeout. The evaluation comprises a synthesis of the coded literature, security threat modelling, and an illustrative settlement reconciliation. Empirical performance evaluation is deferred to a companion testnet study.

title: Thermoresponsive N -Vinylpyrrolidone-Based Copolymer-Coated Palladium Nanoparticles as Catalyst for Suzuki Coupling in Water
abstract: Abstract Polymer-supported palladium nanoparticles represent a promising class of heterogeneous catalysts for sustainable carbon–carbon bond-forming reactions. In the present study, a series of new N-vinylpyrrolidone (NVP)-based polymers with different cloud points (CPs) were synthesized via RAFT polymerization and utilized as stabilizing agents for palladium nanoparticles. Ethyl-substituted NVP (C2NVP) was synthesized and randomly copolymerized with NVP to prepare a set of three copolymers. By changing the feed ratio of the two monomers, the cloud point (CP) of the polymers was varied, which was determined from transmittance and DLS measurements. In situ reduction of K2PdCl4 with NaBH4 in the presence of the polymers yielded well-dispersed Pd nanoparticles, as characterized by UV–vis, XPS, DLS, FESEM, and HR-TEM. The catalytic performance of the resulting nanoparticles was tested in the Suzuki–Miyaura coupling of iodobenzene and phenylboronic acid in water. Under optimized conditions, the catalyst achieved 94% conversion within 30 min at 70 °C. It was found that the catalytic activity was strongly influenced by the cloud point of the polymer. The reaction carried out at temperatures above the cloud point of the coated polymer was completed in significantly less time than that at temperatures below the cloud point. This behavior is attributed to the formation of a hydrophobic m…

title: Rotor-Driven Hinges: Composition of Machines, Rational Coupling Ratios, and the F₁F₀ Composite on the Substituted-Chrysene Lattice
abstract: This article composes rotation, bounded hinge states, and turnover counts in a finite model inspired by F₁F₀ ATP synthase. When two machines are each tightly coupled to a shared shaft, the quotient of their component ratios determines the transport-to-turnover ratio on closed walks. Of 256 reversible rotor rule sets, 14 are tight; exactly one of these also satisfies the declared charge rule. Under binding change, 42 of 512 reversible cam rule sets are tight. Every tight cam rule set that supports synthesis forbids carrying unreacted substrate from the closed to the open conformation. For a rotor with c ion sites, every closed walk in the rigid composite obeys the ratio c/3 ions per ATP, with no fractional individual events. Nonzero transport is checked for c = 3 through 17. If c is not divisible by three, the unequal spacing of ATP events imposes a minimum free-energy climb of twice the ATP free-energy change divided by c at static head. This can alter rates in labeled examples without moving the stall condition. Bounded shaft strain preserves the closed-walk ratio; free play slows the modeled machine in the reported example, while stiffness can accelerate it. The declared chrysene geometry uses an edge-on axle, an extended-arm cam, a threefold stator with in-plane hinges, and a registered six-spoke rotor. Its evenly spaced six-site witness gives two ions per ATP without a mism…

title: Thermo-Mechanical Coupling Simulation and Process Research of Gun Drilling for 15-15hs Max High-Nitrogen Non-Magnetic Steel with Ultra-Large Length-To-Diameter Ratio
abstract: High nitrogen austenitic stainless steel is a typical difficult-to-machine material, due to its high strength and work hardening tendency, presenting significant challenges in machining processes. Focusing on an oil drilling component to analyze the temperature distribution of the workpiece during machining using 15-15 hs Max gun drill. The influence of drilling parameters on drilling temperature during the process is investigated. Simulation results indicate a direct correlation between drilling temperature and spindle speed as well as feed speed. A detailed temperature profile showcasing the rate of increase can provide further insights into the thermal behavior during machining. Taking into account tool longevity and operational efficiency, an optimal process parameter scheme specifically tailored for gun drilling of 15-15 hs Max was derived. Subsequently, the scheme underwent experimental validation to ensure its practical applicability. The axial deviation of the machined hole aligns with the specified processing tolerances, meeting the dimensional accuracy criteria set forth in the machining standards.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and multi-scenario simulation of land use and carbon storage based on the GMOP-PLUS-InVEST model: a case study of Shijiazhuang, China
An Energy-Efficient Dynamic Task Scheduling Algorithm for Green Cloud Computing and Mobile Edge Networks
abstract: The growth of mobile applications and connected devices has pushed computation toward a continuum that spans devices, edge servers, and cloud data centers. Scheduling tasks across this continuum determines both the delay experienced by users and the energy consumed by devices and servers, yet the two goals conflict: offloading can shorten execution but costs transmission energy and keeps remote servers active, while local execution saves communication but drains batteries and may miss deadlines. This paper presents an energy-efficient dynamic task scheduling algorithm for green cloud computing and mobile edge networks. The problem is placed in the mobile Internet of Things cloud setting at the intersection of IoT, cloud, and mobile computing, and is cast as a deadline-constrained multi-objective problem that minimizes average delay and average energy consumption. The proposed algorithm, labelled MOEA-TOMEC, is a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm that encodes placement and speed decisions, handles deadlines through feasibility-first selection, maintains a Pareto archive, and re-optimizes dynamically when tasks arrive or conditions change. Energy-saving mechanisms include voltage and frequency scaling and the consolidation and sleeping of lightly loaded servers. In simulation, MOEA-TOMEC achieved the lowest average delay and energy under all tested settings. After 1,000 iter…

title: INTEGRATION OF CHEMISTRY CONCEPTS IN BASIC SCIENCE LEARNING TO SUPPORT ENGINEERING PROBLEM SOLVING
abstract: This study aimed to analyze changes in students’ assessment scores following Basic Science instruction integrating electrochemical reasoning through corrosion-based cases in the contexts of Mechanical Engineering and Civil Engineering. A quantitative approach with a one-group pretest–posttest design was employed. The participants were 54 students from Universitas Tomakaka, comprising 22 Mechanical Engineering students and 32 Civil Engineering students, selected using total sampling. The intervention was conducted over three weeks through three instructional sessions. Data were collected using a 20-item multiple-choice test and analyzed descriptively and using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. The results showed that the mean score increased from 52.59 on the pretest to 74.81 on the posttest, representing an increase of 22.22 points. All participants (100%) demonstrated improved scores. The Wilcoxon test indicated a statistically significant difference between pretest and posttest scores (W = 0, p < 0.001). These findings indicate that chemistry instruction connecting electrochemical concepts with corrosion cases involving engineering materials was accompanied by improved student assessment performance. However, the absence of a control group limits causal conclusions. This study provides preliminary empirical evidence to inform the development of contextualized chemistry instructi…

title: Housing Rights, Informal Settlements and Policy Durability: A Socio-Legal Analysis of Argentina’s Socio-Urban Integration Policy
abstract: Abstract This article examines the design, implementation and dismantling of Argentina’s Socio-Urban Integration Policy (Política de Integración Socio-Urbana, PISU) between 2018 and 2026. Drawing on documentary analysis, primary legal sources and semi-structured interviews with key actors involved across the full policy cycle, it investigates how housing rights can be institutionalised through legal and administrative mechanisms in contexts of political volatility. The article demonstrates that the PISU achieved significant innovations – a comprehensive national registry, a hybrid financing instrument, participatory governance and an intermediate tenure certificate – that substantially improved living conditions for over one million people. Nevertheless, the policy’s abrupt termination under the Milei administration reveals the fragility of social rights when institutional architecture lacks protection against political alternation, particularly when an incoming government is determined to dismantle it. Attention is devoted to the legal functions of the Certificado de Vivienda Familiar, the limits of expropriation-based regularisation, and the role of litigation following dismantling. The findings contribute to debates on social rights institutionalisation, state capacity and policy durability in the Global South.

title: Quotient Metric-Based Nonconforming Finite Element Analysis and Lower Bound Estimation for the Gross–Pitaevskii Energy Functional in a Rotating Frame
abstract: In this paper, we establish a theoretical framework for the nonconforming finite element approximation of the ground state problem for Bose–Einstein condensates with a rotation term. Due to the phase-invariance of the energy functional, the ground state exhibits high degeneracy. Consequently, based on the (local) quasi-uniqueness assumption, we introduce quotient metrics on $H_0^1(\mathcal{D}; \mathbb{C})$. Under these metrics, we derive a priori error estimates for the discrete minimal energy, discrete eigenvalue, and discrete ground state. Specifically, taking the $EQ_1^{\mathrm{rot}}$ finite element space as an example, we derive the error convergence rates, and prove that for small angular velocities, the discrete minimal energy serves as a lower-bound approximation to the exact minimal energy. Finally, numerical experiments validate the theoretical analysis.

title: Analysis of Individual Burst Time Series and Synthetic Spectral Energy Distribution of FRB 20201124A
abstract: Abstract We present a comprehensive temporal and spectral analysis of bursts from the hyperactive repeating FRB 20201124A, observed with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Radio Telescope (FAST) during two active episodes in 2021. For the first episode (Episode I), we derive the fluence ( F ν ), spectral peak frequency ( ν p ), spectral width ( σ s ), equivalent isotropic energy ( E BWe ), burst duration ( T ), daily event rate ( R ), and waiting time ( WT ) by reanalyzing 1790 bursts, of which 666 satisfy an in-band selection criterion. Time-series analysis shows that F ν , ν p , and σ s are stationary, with ν p and σ s consistent with white noise in the in-band sample but showing significant autocorrelation in the full sample. E BWe is nonstationary but is white noise. The burst rate R and the rotation measure (RM) are both nonstationary and not white noise. The cumulative WT distribution is well described by a Weibull distribution with shape parameter k = 0.722 ± 0.002, and the power-law slope (−1.19 ± 0.08) of the R – WT relation deviates from Poisson expectations, indicating temporal clustering of bursts. Although the distributions of individual burst properties differ between the two episodes, the synthetic spectral energy distributions (SSEDs) constructed from in-band bursts are highly correlated (maximum cross-correlation coefficient r max = 0.95 ) with a spectra…

title: INTEGRATION OF FLEXIBLE PAVEMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT DATA FOR ENHANCING THE RELIABILITY AND OPTIMIZATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENTS (ESIAS) ON THE INZIA BRIDGE–LOANGE BRIDGE SECTION (RN1, DR CONGO): LINKAGES BETWEEN PAVEMENT EVALUATIO
abstract: National Road 1 (RN1), a vital artery of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), exhibits accelerated degradation along the Pont Inzia – Pont Loange section. Conventional Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs) rely on theoretical traffic estimates without incorporating actual pavement condition data. The objective of this paper is to analyze current ESIA practices in road projects in the DRC in order to build sustainable, transparent, and socially accepted road infrastructures, and to make studies more reliable—thereby ensuring project sustainability and fostering a resilient society in the face of climate change threats—by relying on a cross-analysis methodology of technical aspects and impacts linked to the cycle: Auscultation – Reliability – Optimization – Sustainable Global Impact. An auscultation campaign was conducted by the National Laboratory of Public Works (Laboratoire National de Travaux Publics [LNTP]), involving deflection measurements using the Benkelman beam, longitudinal roughness testing, and surface distress surveys. The results indicate an average deflection of 85/100 mm, an average International Roughness Index (IRI) of 6.2 m/km, and a Pavement Condition Index (PCI) of 38/100, reflecting a pavement in a plastic phase nearing the end of its useful life. A global statistical analysis over an extended route of 529.6 km reveals 145.8 km in good …

title: Editorial: Resilient and energy-efficient cities: urban planning for climate adaptation and sustainable development
Semantic-aware multimodal evidence integration with a lightweight large language model for rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Rolling bearings are critical components in industrial rotating machinery, and their failures may cause unexpected downtime, economic loss, and safety risks. Although deep learning and multimodal fusion have improved vibration-based fault diagnosis, two issues remain insufficiently addressed: magnitude-dominated time–frequency representations may discard phase-related impulse timing information, and heterogeneous diagnostic cues are often fused without explicit alignment in a semantically consistent representation space. This paper proposes M2-LLM-FD, a lightweight large language model-assisted framework for semantic-aware multimodal evidence integration in rolling bearing fault diagnosis. The framework converts each vibration segment into three complementary forms: time-domain patch tokens, phase-aware time–frequency tokens, and structured statistical prompts. A phase-preserving complex convolutional dimensionality reduction network is designed to process the real and imaginary components of the time–frequency representations, thereby retaining phase-sensitive information associated with fault-induced impulsive events. A structured multimodal alignment and fusion module then harmonizes temporal granularity and projects the aligned evidence into the pretrained language-model embedding space through semantic-anchor cross-modal attention. Furthermore, domain-specific pri…

title: Ce-Mo Co-Doping Expands Lattice Spacing and Strengthens the TM-O Covalent Network for Enhanced Electrochemical Performance of Li-Rich Mn-Based Cathodes
abstract: Abstract Lithium-rich manganese-based cathode (LRM) materials suffer from irreversible lattice oxygen release and layered structure degradation during high-voltage cycling, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency, rapid capacity fading, and continuous voltage decay. Ce-Mo dual element co-doping strategy was developed to regulate the bulk lattice of LRM(CeMo-LRM). The optimized cathode delivers an initial discharge capacity of 259.75 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C (vs 221.64 mAh g−1 for pristine) and increases the initial Coulombic efficiency from 63.00% for pristine LRM to 75.29%. It also retains 85.34% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C, markedly higher than that of LRM (66.30%). Kinetic analyses show that CeMo-LRM exhibits an increased Li+ diffusion coefficient (2.89 × 10−8 cm2 s−1) and a reduced charge-transfer resistance (56.8 Ω). Structural characterizations and first-principles calculations indicate that Mo6+ doping strengthens the Transition metal oxygen (TM-O) framework through robust Mo-O bonding and increases the resistance of lattice oxygen irreversible release, whereas Ce4+ doping expands the lattice along the c-axis of the material, improving Li+ migration channels, and helps optimize the Mn valence distribution. The complementary functions of Ce and Mo suppress Li/Ni cation mixing, mitigate Jahn-Teller distortion, improve oxygen-redox reversibility. This study demonstr…

title: Cross-species multi-omics integration reveals recurrent inflammatory and model-associated pathway alterations in polycystic ovary syndrome
abstract: Introduction Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a heterogeneous endocrine and metabolic disorder whose molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study used a cross-species multi-omics approach to identify pathways that recur in human PCOS and mouse models and to examine their activity in granulosa-cell preparations. Methods We analyzed five human and mouse bulk transcriptomic datasets, one human single-cell RNA sequencing dataset, and gut microbiota 16S rRNA gene sequencing data from a dehydroepiandrosterone-induced mouse model. Results Differential expression and enrichment analyses identified seven pathways enriched in at least two bulk datasets. Two pathways, cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction and viral protein interaction with cytokine and cytokine receptor, showed concordant enrichment across species. Complement and coagulation cascades showed opposite enrichment directions in human and mouse datasets. Four pathways recurred only in the two mouse datasets: protein digestion and absorption, pattern specification, embryonic organ morphogenesis, and skeletal system development. Single-cell analysis identified five provisional transcriptional states in granulosa-cell preparations. Inflammatory pathway scores were relatively high in the inflammatory/immune-like state, although donor-level comparisons between PCOS and controls did not reach significance afte…

title: From energy crisis to solar boom: the political economy of decentralized clean energy transition in Pakistan
abstract: Abstract Background Since 2022, Pakistan has experienced a rapid surge of rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) adoption as households and businesses increasingly shift toward distributed solar systems to reduce dependence on the national grid. This unprecedented shift raises critical questions for energy governance, energy system sustainability, and energy justice, particularly regarding how distributed, user-driven innovations can reshape a clean energy transition beyond formal policy and planning frameworks. The paper examines the drivers of this solar power boom through an integrative political economy framework combining market, socio-technical, and governance dynamics. It draws on 38 semi-structured interviews with policymakers, representatives of regulatory bodies, electricity utilities, solar businesses, industry experts, and think tanks, alongside documentary analysis. The study offers a distinctive explanation of how distributed, people-led solar adoption can drive rapid transformation and reshape established electricity systems in a large developing country such as Pakistan, despite structural and institutional constraints. Results Our findings show that rising tariffs, declining grid reliability, and governance inertia combined with falling global solar PV prices and affordable equipment imported from China have accelerated solar PV adoption in Pakistan. Informal market p…

title: China, Geopolitics and the Energy Transition: The Cases of Argentina and Mexico
abstract: The global energy transition has turned lithium into a strategic resource. While countries such as Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Australia, and Mexico possess significant lithium reserves, most lack the industrial and technological capacity needed to move up the value chain. In contrast, China dominates the lithium industry, controlling key stages ranging from extraction and refining to the manufacturing of finished batteries. Against this backdrop, the United States seeks to increase its presence in developing the lithium industry. This article argues that the lithium boom, which reproduces geopolitical rivalries centered on territorial control, resource access, and dominance over production chains, provides a structural framework that influences the responses of national governments with access to this resource. However, each country sets its own conditions for lithium benefits based on its internal dynamics. Using a comparative approach, we analyze Argentina and Mexico to examine how each country has responded differently to the growing presence of Chinese and U.S. interests in their lithium sectors. Our analysis combines a review of national policy frameworks, investment patterns, and diplomatic strategies with a critical reading of classical geopolitics. We conclude that these divergent responses reflect how state decisions remain conditioned by entrenched geopolitical imagin…

Design and fabrication of functionally graded 3D polymeric scaffolds for simultaneous cell support and localized microRNA delivery
abstract: Abstract Scaffolds have proven useful as matrices for cell culture, tissue ingrowth, organ formation, mechanical support, drug screening platforms, and localized delivery systems. Their performance depends on multiple structural and material properties that determine their suitability for specific applications. In this study, we developed a multifunctional scaffold designed to provide both cell culture support and gradual microRNA (miRNA) delivery. A method was first introduced for generating heterogeneous triply periodic minimal surface-based scaffold architectures. Compared with existing methods, the proposed approach provides a more user-friendly strategy for generating functionally graded structures and enables irregular architectural variations throughout the scaffold. The scaffolds were fabricated using Fused Filament Deposition and evaluated for printing fidelity. A gelatin/polyethyleneimine-based delivery system was developed to immobilize miRNA on the scaffold surface, and its release profile was optimized. The scaffolds were further evaluated for cell attachment, proliferation, infiltration, and transfection efficiency. The proposed design method successfully generated complex architectural deformations while maintaining printability. The scaffold surface supported favorable cell attachment and proliferation, whereas cell infiltration was influenced by both porosity a…

title: Grounding allocentric procedures in egocentric enactment: a digital design for basic integer arithmetic
abstract: Abstract The rapid evolution of immersive platforms as standard classroom resources has stimulated educational designers to pioneer new activity architectures for mathematics students to ground curricular content in embodied interaction. However, educational research has yet to theorize and operationalize these novel technological interfaces into principled design heuristics. We conjectured the relevance of spatial perspective-taking theory , which demarcates perceptual orientation to the environment as either egocentric or allocentric, as illuminating the cognitive process of symbol-grounding in these architectures. Thirty middle-school students (11–14 years old) participated individually in 45-min evaluation trials of an experimental activity designed for assimilating the negative numbers into addition and subtraction arithmetic. Walking along an interactive floor-projected number line, participants (1) enacted full-body rule-based solution procedures (proximal egocentric action); and then (2) remote-activated an avatar walking along its wall-projected number line (distal allocentric perception). Later, seated at a desk, they (3) manipulated a concrete embodiment of the same avatar to walk it along its tablet number line. Analysis of participants’ (a) multimodal utterances while operating the tablet and (b) pre-to-post-intervention learning gains on paper-based assessments in…

title: How NGO logo design and spokesperson gender shape public support behavior the mediating roles of perceived organizational warmth and competence
abstract: Purpose Drawing on the Stereotype Content Model and Construal Level Theory, this study examines the joint effects of logo design and spokesperson gender on support intention toward nongovernmental organizations (NGOs). It also tests whether perceived organizational warmth and competence mediate these effects. Methods We conducted a 2 (logo design: concrete vs. abstract) × 2 (spokesperson gender: female vs. male) between-subjects experiment. We analyzed 602 valid responses using a moderated parallel mediation model. Results Logo design and spokesperson gender had a significant interaction effect. With a female spokesperson, concrete logos increased perceived organizational warmth. With a male spokesperson, abstract logos produced higher perceived organizational competence. Moderated parallel mediation analyses further showed that perceived warmth and competence mediated the effect of logo design on NGO support intention. These indirect effects depended on spokesperson gender. Discussion These findings extend research on warmth -competence perceptions and construal level in nonprofit visual persuasion. They also give NGOs practical guidance on matching logo style with spokesperson choice in visual communication.

title: Recent Advances in Polymer Electrolytes for High-Voltage Lithium-Metal Batteries: From the Perspective of Molecular Structure Design
abstract: Abstract Global industrial upgrading, accelerating electrification, and the rapid expansion of artificial-intelligence-powered data centers are driving a sustained increase in electricity demand, intensifying the need for energy-storage technologies that combine high energy density with strong safety. To this end, high-voltage solid-state polymer lithium-metal batteries have attracted increasing attention. However, their development is strongly limited by the insufficient oxidative stability of solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). Recent studies suggest that the oxidation behavior of polar functional groups is closely related to the electronic properties and bonding configurations of the polymer, making these features important intrinsic factors in determining the oxidative stability of polymer electrolytes. From this perspective, tailoring the molecular structure of polymer electrolytes has emerged as an effective approach for improving their stability under high-voltage conditions. These design approaches include electronic regulation through substituent effects, designing polar functional groups with enhanced intrinsic oxidative stability and ionic conductivity, optimization of vulnerable sites and polymer backbones, and rational integration of multiple functional units. Beyond intrinsic structural regulation, intermolecular interactions can further stabilize reactive polar si…

title: Design and Performance Investigation of a Novel Composite Sealing Structure for Plunger Pumps
abstract: To tackle the problems of easy leakage, short service life and rapid wear failure of conventional packing seals for plunger pumps, this paper investigates a combined sealing structure. A labyrinth–V-packing combined sealing structure is proposed, and its three-dimensional model is established. Numerical simulations and experiments are used to explore the influence of V-packing structural parameters on sealing performance. Firstly, the structural scheme with a trapezoidal-tooth labyrinth seal on the high-pressure side and a stepped inner stuffing box is determined, and the preliminary design of the combined seal is finished. Secondly, Fluent is utilised to analyse the flow characteristics of the labyrinth seal. Based on the confirmed packing arrangement and cross-sectional profile, single-factor analysis and orthogonal experimental design are adopted to optimise V-packing parameters. Finally, test fixtures are fabricated and a test platform is set up to conduct labyrinth pressure drop tests and contact stress measurements. Experimental results reveal that the maximum error of labyrinth pressure drop between measured data and simulation results is 15%, and roughly 50% pressure reduction can be realised. The contact stress error between the plunger and V-packing is less than 10%. These results verify the reliability of numerical simulations and validate the effectiveness of the st…

title: Impaired activation of STAT5 pathways in the naïve B cell compartment in patients with common variable immunodeficiency harboring CD27bright memory B cells
abstract: Introduction Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) is a heterogeneous primary immunodeficiency characterized by low serum levels of IgG, IgA and/or IgM, recurrent infections and poor vaccination responses. CVID results from a broad spectrum of genetic abnormalities, majority of which have not yet been identified. The hallmark of CVID is impaired B-cell responses. Methods Here we decided to focus on CVID patients who are able to make CD27 bright memory B cells (MBCs), a subset mainly formed in the germinal center. We performed a transcriptomic study on both sorted naïve and CD27 bright MBCs at steady state and after in vitro activation. Results Transcriptomic profiling revealed that even resting naïve B cells in patients with CVID display a dysregulated gene expression signature. Along with reduced activity of STAT5-target genes, several key pathways involved in maintaining cellular integrity and stress resilience were downregulated. Furthermore, we show that the naïve B-cell compartment in this cohort of CVID patients with detectable CD27 bright MBCs shows dysregulated transcriptional activation in response to T-cell-dependent stimuli. This leads to suboptimal activation of pathways normally upregulated during B-cell differentiation toward MBCs and plasma cells in the germinal center reaction, including STAT5 signaling, oxidative phosphorylation and MYC target gene expression…

title: The effect of design thinking on knowledge quality: the role of innovation capability and information technology-enabled capability
abstract: Purpose Organizations increasingly depend on creating and using high-quality knowledge resources to sustain innovation and knowledge-informed decision-making. This study aims to examine how design thinking, conceptualized as a knowledge-mobilization practice, is associated with perceived knowledge quality through innovation capability, and whether IT-enabled capability (measured through customer and market analytics) conditions the first stage of this pathway. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among employees of organizations operating across four sectors: IT/technology, manufacturing, services and education/research. Established measurement scales were adopted or adapted to assess all constructs. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to evaluate the measurement model and to test the hypothesized direct, mediating and moderating relationships. Findings Design thinking was positively associated with both innovation capability and knowledge quality, and innovation capability was positively associated with knowledge quality. The indirect effect through innovation capability was statistically significant but small, a pattern consistent with complementary partial mediation in which innovation capability is a meaningful but incremental mechanism. IT-enabled capability positively moderates the association between desi…

title: Perceived digital exclusion and depressive symptoms among older adults in China: a variable-centered and person-centered analysis
abstract: Introduction As essential services move online, older adults who do not use the internet may feel excluded from daily activities increasingly dependent on digital participation, raising concerns about potential implications for mental health. This study examined the association between perceived digital exclusion (PDE) and depressive symptoms among older adults, as well as the mediating role of social support network. Methods Using data from 9,217 adults aged 60 and older in the 2020 wave of the China Longitudinal Aging Social Survey (CLASS), we employed OLS regression, KHB mediation decomposition and latent class analysis to assess overall and domain-specific patterns of PDE and their associations with depressive symptoms. Results Results showed that non-internet users with higher PDE reported significantly greater depressive symptoms. Social support network mediated only a small proportion of this association. Latent class analysis identified five exclusion profiles among non-internet users: no exclusion, diffuse moderate exclusion, info-social exclusion, practical-service exclusion, and comprehensive exclusion. The info-social exclusion class showed the highest prevalence of depressive symptoms despite comparable overall PDE levels to other groups. Discussion The findings suggest that domain-specific exclusion patterns are more strongly associated with mental health than ove…

title: Comparison of DNA recovery efficiency between variable cross-sectional biodegradable PLA fiber swab and conventional swabs on surface materials for forensic DNA trace evidence collection
Design of a tetranuclear mixed-valence complex for molecular quantum-dot cellular automata using classical electrostatic models
abstract: Quantum-dot cellular automata (QCA) is a promising paradigm for next-generation devices. The classical electrostatic model we previously proposed enables the screening of potential candidate molecules for QCA [K. Tokunaga et al., Bull. Chem. Soc. Jpn. 94 , 397 (2021)]. In this study, this model was used to predict the molecular structural parameters required for proper QCA operations. Our findings reveal that the proper operation window is widest for rectangular cells, requiring a side length of less than approximately 7 Å. As the cell structure deviates from a rectangular shape, the proper operation window narrows. Furthermore, a smaller dot charge results in a wider proper operation window. Based on these guidelines, we designed novel complexes, [M 4 Cl 8 (CO) 8 (pyrazine) 4 ] 2+ (M=Fe, Ru, Os). Using density functional theory calculations, we demonstrated that only the Fe complex, which has the smallest metal–metal distance and is just inside the proper operation window, yields the correct majority logic operation.

title: Syntaxonomy of plant communities with the South Italian narrow endemic Anthemis hydruntina
abstract: Anthemis hydruntina is a narrowly endemic species from southern Italy, known from a few localities in three regions—Apulia, Basilicata, and Calabria—and includes two subspecies: one is assessed as Endangered at the national level, whereas for the other, which occurs only in Calabria, information remains insufficient. Given the limited information available on the plant communities harbouring this species, the present study aims to fill this knowledge gap. A total of 31 phytosociological relevés were conducted across the species’ distribution range using the Braun-Blanquet approach. These were compared, through cluster analysis and non-metric multidimensional scaling, with an additional 155 relevés representative of similar vegetation types. Indicator Species Analysis was performed to identify the floristic distinctions among the main relevé clusters. Results show that A. hydruntina occurs in two ecologically and floristically distinct plant communities belonging to different syntaxonomic classes. The Calabrian populations, assigned to the subspecies A. hydruntina subsp. silensis, grow on siliceous substrates and occur in the association Astragaletum calabrici, within the class Rumici aetnensis-Astragaletea siculi. In contrast, the populations from Basilicata and Apulia, attributed to the autonymous subspecies, are found on carbonate substrates and are associated with Mediterran…

title: Conservation of Mediterranean Plant Species in Stable Forests
abstract: Forests with relatively closed canopies are not common in Mediterranean areas, due to the long summer dryness. Where climate (or permanent groundwater) permits, though, such forests can provide conditions for conservation not only of the forest tree species involved but also of various herbs, shrubs, and arborescents that can grow in the understorey. These may include species targeted for special conservation efforts. The overstorey of Mediterranean forests is often not as densely closed as elsewhere, but it can still provide shade, higher humidity, and better growing conditions for smaller plants. So-called Miyawaki forest plantations may provide these beneficial attributes and are now becoming quite popular in Europe as retrofitted green space in otherwise built-up environments. Such plantations are not large in area, but even smaller forests, if stable over many years, can host and conserve smaller species. The Miyawaki technique was developed for evergreen broad-leaved forests in the humid warm-temperate climate of the southern half of Japan. Adapting it to drier situations is still a work in progress, but some experience in the Mediterranean area does exist. A plantation near Istanbul (Türkiye) already has 15 years of growth. In conservation, success involves not only species but also vegetation types and whole ecosystems, such as stable forests. This requires maintaining …

A new species of Coffea L. (Rubiaceae) from the Western Ghats of Kerala, India
abstract: Kulathupuzha Forest Range, located in the southernmost part of the Western Ghats, is noted for its unique floristic richness, diversity and endemicity. While botanising the geographical area as part of a recent floristic analysis, a new species of Coffea has been identified. The new species is named as Coffea seenii Meenakshi et Nazarudeen, which is allied to C. travancorensis Wall. ex Wight & Arn., but strikingly different from other previously known species by having a comparatively taller stature, slightly ascending to spreading branches, non-glossy broad leaves exhibiting developmental or heteroblastic leaf dimorphism, highly fragrant flowers mostly paired in the leaf axils, a corolla tube with an external red tinge, a multidentate calyx, a shallow cupulate disc and a distinctly spatulate to broadly linear bifid stigma. Colour photographs of both the species and detailed descriptions and illustrations of the new species are provided to highlight their morphological differences.

title: Effects of Aqueous Aloe vera Extracts on Visible Symptoms and Plant Mortality in Field-Grown Tomatoes in Daloa, Côte d’Ivoire
abstract: Tomato production in tropical environments is affected by foliar disorders, stem symptoms and plant mortality. This field experiment compared aqueous Aloe vera leaf preparations for symptom management in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) at Daloa, Côte d’Ivoire. Ten treatments were represented in three blocks, with ten monitored plants per treatment plot (300 plants): an untreated control, four inner-gel fractions (25–100%), four leaf-tissue macerates (15–100 g L⁻¹), and a conventional pesticide reference. Four foliar and basal applications were made at 14-day intervals, and visible symptoms and plant survival were monitored during growth. The untreated control had mean incidences of 43.75% for yellowing, 66.36% for leaf curling and 23.75% for wilting. Under undiluted gel (A100), the corresponding mean incidences were 5.25%, 2.66% and 0.00%, respectively; the differences from the untreated control were 38.50, 63.70 and 23.75 percentage points, respectively. A75 had the lowest necrosis incidence (6.44%). Reported mean mortality was 2.43% with A100, 7.67% with the pesticide reference and 29.22% with no treatment. The field observations indicate that undiluted Aloe vera gel merits further evaluation as a locally available component of tomato health management.

Active and reactive power coordinated optimization model for power quality improvement
abstract: The increased adoption of distributed power generation adversely affects the power quality of distribution networks. The coordinated management of active and reactive power devices provides a novel solution to address this problem. Existing strategies typically focus on single aspects—such as reactive power compensation devices, energy storage, or voltage regulation equipment—in isolation. However, it is critical to comprehensively consider the impacts of network reconfiguration, active and reactive power, and voltage regulation strategies on power quality and their economics. This paper presents a strategy for the coordinated scheduling of active and reactive power equipment, accounting for their regulation and operational constraints. To enhance computational efficiency, we linearize the nonlinear constraints associated with equipment operation and apply a hybrid data-physical-driven method to linearize voltage unbalance current constraints. This approach meets practical engineering accuracy requirements and significantly improves optimization efficiency. Our analysis indicates that the network reconfiguration model and the equipment scheduling model can be decoupled without affecting outcomes, allowing for a two-stage calculation process. Further investigation using a real-world distribution network demonstrates that involving photovoltaic energy in reactive power regulation…

title: CEO structural power and earnings persistence: the moderating role of organizational complexity
abstract: Purpose This paper investigates the association between CEO structural power and earnings persistence and examines the moderating role of organizational complexity in shaping this relationship. We hypothesize that the association is non-linear and becomes more negative in firms with high organizational complexity. Design/methodology/approach We compile a hand collected dataset covering the full population of publicly traded entities listed on Georgia's capital market, comprising 249 firm year observations over 2018–2023. Our empirical strategy applies pooled first order autoregressions of net income and a three-way interaction model that allows the earnings persistence coefficient to vary with CEO structural power and firm complexity. Findings The findings show that CEO structural power has a stronger negative effect on earnings persistence in complex firms than in less complex firms. In complex firms, separating the CEO and board-chair roles signals enhanced internal control and meets external investors' expectations. In less complex firms, however, high CEO structural power may streamline decision-making and improve earnings persistence. Additional tests reveal that the negative association persists but is substantially weakened when a strong controlling owner is present, suggesting that powerful owners can enforce oversight mechanisms that constrain managerial discretion. title: Environmental Analysis Comparison of Solar Power Plant Design on Former Coal Mining Land and Steam Power Plant
abstract: Former coal mining land is hardly revived to the original ecosystem because of the quality of the barren soil. Several ways to utilize the infertile area are decided, including the solar power plant development on the former coal mined area. This option seems interesting to be developed since the solar power plant itself can be classified as the renewable energy. However, the environmental damage of this scenario has been calculated, especially in comparison with the existing steam power plant that uses coal as the resources to produce steam in generating the electricity. This research aims to seek the environmental damages emit by both of systems, which are solar power plant on former coal mined area and existing steam power plant. It also aims to compare them to find the avoided environmental impacts by developing the solar power plant from common power plant. Based on this study, solar power plant development gives 10 times smaller than environmental damage compared to the existing steam power plant. Therefore, the option can be suggested as the one of reclamation activities on the former coal mined area.

title: An integrative framework of trust-building competencies for e-leaders in virtual teams
abstract: Purpose As digitalisation and dispersed work arrangements become increasingly widespread, organisations face a pressing need to identify e-leadership approaches suited to technology-mediated leader–follower relationships. Because employees' trust in their leaders is considered essential for maintaining cooperation and workplace relationships, this study investigates the specific e-leaders’ competencies that are associated with followers' trust in e-leaders in virtual work settings. Design/methodology/approach Four focus groups were conducted and their transcripts were analysed using qualitative content analysis. An iterative inductive coding process resulted in the delineation of individual competencies organised into a multilevel trust-relevant e-leadership competency framework. Findings The framework comprises 43 competencies organised into seven competency fields – professional competencies, communication, digital & media competencies, e-behaviour, diversity competencies, credibility and endurance – and three overarching categories labelled as coordination-and-clarity, relational-behavioural logic and reliability-over-time. The findings suggest that followers' trust is associated with a multifaceted set of professional, relational, communicative and dependability-related capabilities of e-leaders. Research limitations/implications Limitations include concerns related to the …

title: How Aggressive Sales Promotion Dampens the Power of Product Quality in Driving Fortified Milk Purchase Decisions
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to examine the structural mechanism influencing consumer purchase decisions for 20-gram sachet fortified milk powder. Specifically, it investigates the direct effects of product quality and sales promotion, as well as the moderating role of sales promotion in dampening the relationship between product quality and purchase decisions. Methodology: A quantitative explanatory survey design was employed. Primary data were collected from a purposive sample of 119 consumers who had experience purchasing the targeted product. Variables were measured using a 5-point Likert scale. The empirical data were analyzed using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression and moderated regression analysis via Andrew F. Hayes' PROCESS Macro (Model 1), supported by Johnson-Neyman region of significance evaluation. Findings: The statistical analysis reveals that both product quality and sales promotion partially exert a significant positive effect on purchase decisions. However, the moderation test uncovers a significant negative interaction (dampening effect). High intensity of sales promotion severely weakens the influence of product quality on purchase decisions. The Johnson-Neyman analysis indicates that beyond a specific critical threshold of promotional intensity, the positive effect of product quality becomes insignificant, and at extreme levels, it reverses to a significa…

title: ISNCC Cancer Nursing Education Position Statement
Phenotypic diversity of date palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) cultivars based on fruit, seed and physicochemical traits in a desert region of Algeria
abstract: Fruits of 68 cultivars of Algerian dates (Phoenix dactylifera L.) cultivars were collected at the Tamar (fully mature) stage, from date palm groves of Timimoun in desert region of Algeria and were analysed in the laboratory. Results indicate significant genetic diversity and high variability in physical properties and biochemical content among date fruits that form substantial parts of local diet. Water, pH and ashes ranged from 8.00 % to 44.30 %, 5.10 to 7.07 and 1.11 % to 5.78 % respectively. Similarly, reducing sugar, sucrose and total sugar contents ranged consecutively from 18.54 % to 90.75 %, 0.00 % to 51.75 % and 47.00 % to 93.71 %, respectively. Also, length and weight of date, likewise length and weight of seed ranged from one cultivar to another. For instance, for Khanfart Lahmar (KL), these parameters were 5 cm, 13.34 g for dates and 2.89 cm 1.44 g for seeds respectively. The same parameters of Adham Belkacem (AKC), were; 1.98, cm, 4.45 g, for dates and 2.11cm 0.8 g for seeds respectively. The principal component analysis (PCA) revealed a cumulative variation of 100 % across 13 axes; this represented the extent of genetic diversity among the studied cultivars. Hierarchical cluster analysis showed five homogeneous groups of cultivars. Quality assessment revealed that no single cultivar possessed all commercial traits. title: PUBLIC DEBT, SOVEREIGN GUARANTEES AND FISCAL RISK: LEGAL CONTROLS OVER GOVERNMENT BORROWING AND CONTINGENT LIABILITIES IN SOUTH SUDAN
abstract: Public debt is conventionally classified by its financial form: a loan, security, guarantee or arrear. That classification is inadequate where resource-dependent executives can bind future public revenue through prepayments, delivery commitments, corporate undertakings and contracts described as commercial rather than sovereign. Using South Sudan as a doctrinal case study, this article asks when a fiscal commitment should be treated as public indebtedness for constitutional purposes, irrespective of the instrument’s label. It analyses constitutional borrowing approval, statutory debt controls, petroleum-backed obligations, contingent liabilities and the legal consequences of evasion. The article advances a doctrine of substantive fiscal encumbrance: a commitment must enter the public-debt control system where the State, a public institution or an entity acting with State support exposes public assets, revenue or future appropriations to an enforceable repayment or equivalent performance obligation. That duty triggers legislative authorisation, transparent recording, valuation of contingent exposure, independent audit and effective review. The contribution is to connect constitutional supremacy and public finance through a transaction-sensitive legal test rather than to presume that every commercial agreement is a sovereign loan. It proposes differentiated remedies preserving le…

title: How multi-dimensional perceived value of peer feedback shapes knowledge contribution quality? The double-edged moderating role of knowledge breadth and depth
abstract: Purpose This study aims to address the critical need for enhancing high-quality knowledge contributions, which are essential for the survival and sustainable growth of online technical communities (OTCs) by exploring how multi-dimensional perceived value derived from peer feedback influences core users' knowledge contribution quality and identifying boundary conditions. Design/methodology/approach This study proposes a framework testing the effects of information value, positive affective value, and negative affective value on contribution quality, moderated by knowledge breadth and depth. Using Java-based web crawling, we analyze a large-scale dataset from the Top 100 core users on Chinese Software Developer Network (CSDN), a leading Chinese OTC, employing partial least squares regression. Findings While information value and both positive and negative affective values significantly enhance contribution quality, the knowledge base acts as a “double-edged sword”: (1) knowledge breadth negatively moderates the effects of information value and positive affective value; and (2) knowledge depth negatively moderates the effects of information value and negative affective value. Originality/value This study offers three contributions. First, it validates the positive impact of negative affective value within OTCs, supporting the self-discrepancy theory. Second, it clarifies the conti…

Postural Control Alterations in Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness: A Scoping Review
abstract: Background: Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness (PPPD) is a chronic vestibular disorder characterized by persistent dizziness, unsteadiness or non-spinning vertigo exacerbated by upright posture, active or passive motion and visual cues. The absence of objective biomarkers remains a large clinical limitation. In this context, static posturography represents a promising approach that may contribute to the identification of clinically relevant markers in PPPD. Objective : To map the existing evidence on static postural control in individuals with PPPD, including experimental paradigms, posturography metrics, reported postural control patterns, and to identify gaps in the literature. Methods : A scoping review was conducted, and five databases (PubMed, Scopus, Embase, CINHAL and Web of Science) were searched for studies assessing postural control in PPPD using objective measures. A total of 393 records were identified. Based on the eligibility criteria, 12 articles were included in the scoping review. Data extracted from studies included: study population, sample size, research objective, postural control paradigms, postural outcome metrics, comparison populations and main results. Results and Discussion : Most studies reported increased body sway (area and velocity) in PPPD compared to healthy controls, particularly under altered sensory conditions, such as visual deprivatio…

title: Performance Analysis of MIMO and Massive MIMO Systems for 5G and Beyond Wireless Communications
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) processing is the defining physical-layer technology of contemporary wireless systems, and its large-array form, massive MIMO, underpins fifth-generation (5G) New Radio and the emerging sixth-generation (6G) research agenda. This study presents an end-to-end Monte-Carlo study that quantifies the capacity, diversity, and detection behavior of multi-antenna links and validates every measurement against closed-form theory. A flat-fading channel is modeled under additive white Gaussian noise and independent Rayleigh fading, and the bit-error rate (BER), ergodic capacity, and spectral efficiency are measured for antenna configurations from 1×1 up to a 128-antenna massive-MIMO base station. The work contrasts spatial diversity—maximum-ratio combining and Alamouti space-time coding—with spatial multiplexing, compares zero-forcing (ZF), minimum-mean-square-error (MMSE), and maximum-likelihood (ML) detection, and isolates the channel-hardening and favorable-propagation effects that make large arrays attractive. The simulated curves track analytical predictions to within a fraction of a decibel: ergodic capacity grows almost linearly with the number of antennas, fourth-order diversity lowers the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) required for a BER of 10−3 by roughly twenty decibels relative to a single-antenna link, and ML detection recovers an order of ma…

title: E-COMMERCE PARTICIPATION, FACTOR ALLOCATION EFFICIENCY, AND UPWARD CLASS MOBILITY OF RURAL HOUSEHOLDS: EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE FROM THE CHINA FAMILY PANEL STUDIES
abstract: Whether digital commerce can reshape, rather than merely supplement, the economic position of rural households is central to debates on inclusive growth in developing countries. Drawing on nationally representative panel data from six waves (2010-2020) of the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), this paper examines whether e-commerce participation promotes the upward class mobility of rural households and whether the effect operates through improved factor allocation efficiency. A rural household is defined as participating in e-commerce if any member uses the internet for business or operates online sales. Upward mobility is measured by movements across within-wave household income quintiles and by occupational class upgrading of the household head. Two-way fixed-effects estimates indicate that e-commerce participation significantly raises the probability of upward mobility, and the results survive instrumental-variable estimation exploiting the interaction between village terrain ruggedness and national online retail growth, propensity score matching, and alternative mobility measures. Mechanism analysis shows that participation reallocates household labor toward nonfarm activities, encourages farmland transfer-out, and improves access to formal credit, with these factor-reallocation channels jointly accounting for roughly one-third of the total effect.
