Dynamics of adiposity indicators across repeated cycles of intensive lifestyle interventions in adults with obesity: associations with participation patterns and treadmill exercise performance
abstract: Background To examine longitudinal changes in adiposity-related indicators across repeated cycles of intensive lifestyle intervention and their associations with participation patterns and treadmill exercise performance among adults with obesity (BMI ≥28 kg/m 2 ). Methods We included 19, 594 participants from the Dianfeng Weight Loss Center in China between 2017 and 2025. Outcomes included changes in BMI, body fat percentage (BF%), waist circumference (WC), and fat-free mass (FFM). Participation patterns were classified as continuous, short-break, or long-break. Exercise performance improvement was defined as an increase in maximal workload achieved. Linear mixed-effects models assessed longitudinal changes, and group-based trajectory modeling was applied to identify latent trajectory patterns. Results Adjusted cumulative reductions in BMI, BF%, and WC increased across successive cycles, with smaller incremental changes in later cycles. From Cycle 1 to Cycle 3, adjusted reductions increased from 8.22% to 19.28% for BMI, from 7.65% to 21.83% for BF%, and from 7.53% to 16.57% for WC. In Cycle 3, continuous and short-break participation were associated with greater BMI reductions than long-break participation, with adjusted differences of 8.26 (95% CI, 7.65–8.88) and 8.40 (7.69–9.11) percentage points, respectively. Capital Expenditure, Regional Revenue, Financial Performance, and Economic Growth in West Bandung Regency
abstract: Background: Fiscal decentralization expands local fiscal authority, but larger revenue and capital expenditure do not automatically produce economic growth when fiscal independence and financial management remain weak. Objective: This study examines the effects of Capital Expenditure and Regional Revenue on Regional Financial Performance and Economic Growth and tests the mediating role of Regional Financial Performance in West Bandung Regency. Methods: An explanatory quantitative design used 40 quarterly observations for 2016–2025 from official regional financial reports and statistical publications. Descriptive statistics and path analysis in EViews were used to estimate direct and indirect associations among the variables. Results: Capital Expenditure had a negative significant direct association with Economic Growth (β = −0.535; p = 0.006), whereas Regional Revenue was not significant (β = −0.133; p = 0.430). Capital Expenditure (β = 0.641; p < 0.001) and Regional Revenue (β = 0.329; p < 0.001) were positively associated with Regional Financial Performance, which was positively associated with Economic Growth (β = 0.521; p = 0.021). The indirect effect of Capital Expenditure through Regional Financial Performance was significant (β = 0.333; p = 0.028), while the indirect effect of Regional Revenue was not significant at the 5% level (β = 0.171; p = 0.055). title: Formation-Specific CO2 Trapping in Geological Storage: A Review of Classical Mechanisms and Supporting Retention Processes
abstract: The long-term security of geological CO2 storage depends on trapping mechanisms and the geological and hydrodynamic controls governing their effectiveness. Although classical mechanisms are well established, their interactions with formation-specific controls remain insufficiently integrated into comparative assessments. This review examines structural, residual, solubility, mineral and adsorption trapping, and evaluates capillary entry pressure, regional groundwater flow, and geological heterogeneity as controls on CO2 migration and immobilization. Experimental, numerical, and field evidence published between 1979 and 2026 is synthesized across seven settings: onshore and offshore saline aquifers, depleted hydrocarbon reservoirs, basalts, ultramafic formations, organic-rich shales, and coal seams. Quantitative comparisons of residual saturation, capillary breakthrough pressure, adsorption parameters, and mineralization performance reveal how pore architecture, wettability, permeability contrasts, fluid transport, and mineral reactivity alter retention. Structural trapping depends on seal integrity and capillary thresholds, whereas residual trapping reflects pore-scale displacement and saturation hysteresis. Groundwater flow and reservoir heterogeneity influence plume migration, CO2–brine contact, and access to reactive minerals, thereby governing dissolution and carbonation. I…

Formal ergotropy versus Gaussian-accessible work in a nonlinear optomechanical quantum battery
abstract: Abstract Formal ergotropy assumes unrestricted unitary control and can overstate the work available under constrained extraction. We compare it with the established optimum over all single-mode Gaussian unitaries in a coherently driven nonlinear optomechanical quantum battery. Both benchmarks use the same mechanical states and the same interaction-removal energy under an adopted sudden switch-off protocol. At the original 100- and 150-period states, corrected formal ergotropy is positive while corrected Gaussian-accessible work is negative. The small Gaussian-accessible work is associated with small displacement and nearly isotropic covariance, while the number-dephased diagnostic states retain almost all of the formal ergotropy at these times. We extend the comparison over 0–150 mechanical periods, sample five couplings and five detunings at a fixed time, and check a jointly enlarged cutoff. These finite samples do not establish continuous persistence or universal parameter robustness. The sign comparison is conditional on the adopted optical-loss model and sudden interaction removal; it excludes extraction-control costs and a complete charging–extraction work balance. At 100 mechanical periods, the corrected-work sign discrepancy is resolved at all five sampled couplings.

A Thrust-Vectoring Aerial–Aquatic Vehicle for Operation in Currents
abstract: Waterway inspection and marine environmental observation require a vehicle capable of rapid aerial deployment and localized underwater operation while withstanding current disturbances in natural waters. To address the coupling among air-water propulsion-load differences, aerial payload constraints, and underwater maneuvering against currents, this paper presents an H-shaped hybrid aerial-aquatic vehicle with thrust vectoring. Two-speed propulsion units accommodate dual-medium loads within aerial payload constraints, while independently tilting arms provide thrust vectoring for current rejection and cross-medium motion. A thrust-vectoring controller suppresses current-induced drift. The 4.0 kg prototype achieved a root-mean-square horizontal position error of 0.170 m under a 0.32 m/s current. Nearshore marine trials demonstrated automated descent, ascent, and surface takeoff. Together, the tank and nearshore trials verify the platform's current-rejection and cross-medium operating capabilities.

abstract: Abstract This study investigates the aerodynamic interaction between the wing and propeller of a tail-sitter unmanned aerial vehicle over a range of fixed angles of attack relevant to its transition-flight regime. The investigation combines steady-state computational analysis using an actuator-disc representation of the propeller with wind-tunnel experiments on a scaled wing–propeller model. In the computational study, the propeller is simplified as an actuator disc and coupled with a rectangular wing. The coefficient of lift ( C L ) and the coefficient of drag ( C D ) are evaluated as functions of the propeller distance from the wing leading edge, its spanwise position relative to the wing root, and the angle of attack ( α ). The results indicate that positioning the propeller 125 mm from the leading edge and at 50% of the numerical model semi-span, measured from the wing root provides improved aerodynamic performance. For the experimental investigation, a scaled-down UAV model with a scale factor of 0.5 was used. The analysis was conducted at the optimised propeller position under both low and high angles of attack ( α ) at a free-stream velocity of 36 m s −1 . The results show that the propeller slipstream modifies the flow field around the wing. Business entropy as an emerging metric of organizational performance: a leadership perspective
abstract: Purpose This article examines how business entropy can complement traditional financial indicators such as revenue and profit, offering a new framework for assessing the true vitality, resilience, and long term sustainability of organizations. It demonstrates that success can no longer be measured exclusively by financial results, but also by an organization’s ability to create value added while simultaneously managing business entropy. Design/methodology/approach The study applies a combined analytical approach that includes: – conceptual introduction of entropy as a business indicator, – development of a simple model for calculating value added and business entropy, – comparative analysis across different organizations. Findings The analysis shows that organizations with high revenues may simultaneously exhibit high entropy, indicating structural instability and an unsustainable long term growth model. Conversely, organizations with moderate financial results but low entropy demonstrate greater long term sustainability, resilience, and the ability to generate stable added value. Managing entropy therefore emerges as a central leadership task. Originality/value This paper introduces business entropy as an emerging metric of organizational performance and integrates entropy theory with leadership and performance management research. title: Two-Step Bioinspired Mineralization Strategy for Lower-Temperature Curable, Flame Retardant, and Mildew-Resistant Casein-Based Adhesives
abstract: Abstract The practical application of casein-based adhesives is constrained by the high curing temperatures (>120 °C as reported for casein systems) required to achieve industrially viable curing times, along with their inherent susceptibility to microbial attack and high flammability. Herein, we report a two-step bioinspired mineralization strategy that integrates hydroxyapatite (HA) and calcium oxide (CaO) into an activated casein to address these limitations. HA first establishes a network with casein pretreated with Na2CO3 and urea via weak interactions, while calcium ions released from CaO subsequently promote carbonate formation and possible ionic cross-linking, contributing to a secondary dense network structure. This sequential bioinspired mineralization overcomes the excessive viscosity caused by CaO alone and the poor strength resulting from HA alone. The resulting two-step bioinspired mineralized network enables fast, lower-temperature curing at 110 °C compared with previously reported casein systems, while achieving robust shear strengths. Moreover, the resulting adhesive exhibits markedly enhanced thermal stability (char yield: 32.99%) and superior flame-retardancy (LOI: 39.3%; UL-94: V-0 rating). Maintaining Centrality: ASEAN’s Evolving Institutional Strategy on the Climate Change Agenda
abstract: This article examines how ASEAN has built and maintained its centrality in the climate change agenda across 15 ASEAN Joint Statements on Climate Change (AJSCC) issued between 2007 and 2025. It advances two core arguments. First, ASEAN centrality in the climate change domain is not asserted but accumulated: it is constructed through a nested legitimation structure in which the prior legitimation of ASEAN’s climate agenda is a necessary discursive precondition for any centrality claim, deployed through a multimodal architecture combining authorization, moral evaluation, rationalization, and mythopoesis. Second, this centrality is not static. It has evolved from a reactive, entitlement-based posture toward an increasingly assertive coordinating role, driven primarily by internal institutionalization, compounding crises, and physical climate escalation rather than by the Paris Agreement as an external critical juncture. Applying discourse tracing supplemented by van Leeuwen’s legitimation framework to the complete corpus of 15 AJSCCs, the study finds that the Paris Agreement does not produce a discursive rupture. ASEAN’s path-dependent deliberative norms absorb the external governance milestone without fundamental reorientation. These findings contribute to scholarly understanding of how regional organizations construct institutional authority incrementally—through discursive accum…

title: When strategy expires: governing the half-life of strategic assumptions
abstract: Purpose This paper explains why assumptions that once warranted strategy can continue to authorize new commitments after their supporting evidence has weakened. Design/methodology/approach A conceptual model with an embedded governance typology integrates strategic control, planning, persistence and adaptive implementation research. Institutional carriers explain authority persistence; published cases illustrate mechanisms rather than test propositions. Findings Two clocks, evidence validity and review cadence, shape detection lag; formal and enacted authority distinguish withdrawal endpoints. Seven propositions connect these constructs to carriers, exposure and governance. A proposed overdue default suspends permission for new irreversible exposure when no qualifying review occurs. Research limitations/implications Construct measures and propositions require prospective and longitudinal testing, including sensitivity to alternative lag-onset dates. Practical implications A four-state register, exposure-weighted concentration measure and staged executive review connect assumptions shared across commitments to authorization gates. Social implications The design may reduce stranded assets and policy lock-in, but evidence thresholds require safeguards against power, gaming and premature interruption of exploration. title: Building socially responsible global brand identity with AI and sustainability strategy
abstract: Purpose This research is an attempt to systematically review the current body of literature about strategic use of artificial intelligence and sustainability orientation to build a responsible global identity. Design/methodology/approach To conduct a systematic review and present a qualitative synthesis of literature, this research uses a multi-faceted four-stage PRISMA protocol that includes identification, screening, eligibility and inclusion. Findings Our analysis of academic knowledge reveals that available brand strategy literature mainly considers the consumer perspective and does not include the perspective of the global community of stakeholders. To address this gap, this study integrates sustainability orientation and AI strategy with governance, brand resilience and standardization–adaptation theory to explain how organizations can build socially responsible global brand identities. In doing so, the study provides a novel framework for balancing global consistency and local relevance in increasingly transparent and digitally connected markets. Originality/value This research offers a comprehensive analysis of theoretical, methodological and empirical knowledge to find answers to the research questions raised by the current context of sustainability consciousness and new age of artificial technologies.

abstract: Purpose This study examines how AI-driven HRM (ADH) relates to Employee Digital Performance (EDP) through the mediating role of Fear of Missing Out (FoMO) and examines whether Human-Centric Digital Leadership (HCDL) moderates these direct and indirect relationships within Vietnam’s financial services sector. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative design was employed using survey data collected from a purposive sample of 368 full-time employees working in commercial banks, securities, insurance, and financial technology firms in Vietnam. The proposed research model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) following established reliability, validity, and structural path assessment procedures. Findings Results reveal ADH is positively associated with EDP and negatively with FoMO, while FoMO relates negatively to EDP and partially mediates the ADH–EDP relationship. HCDL significantly moderates these relationships, making both the positive ADH–EDP and negative ADH–FoMO associations more pronounced at higher HCDL levels. Moderated mediation analysis confirms the conditional indirect relationship between ADH and EDP through FoMO is stronger under higher HCDL. title: When executable AI advice backfires: feasibility, managerial reliance, and strategic performance
abstract: Purpose This paper examines how the feasibility of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated advice shapes managerial reliance, firm performance, and trust in strategic decision making. It distinguishes advice quality from execution reliability, defined as the probability that an attempted AI-backed action avoids an implementation-failure loss. Design/methodology/approach The study develops a parsimonious expected utility model with stochastic source choice in which managers choose between human judgment and AI advice under demand uncertainty and competitive interaction. The model separates expected operating value, implementation feasibility, and accountability cost. A repeated duopoly simulation is then used to examine how changes in AI feasibility affect reliance, performance, and trust. Findings Higher AI feasibility increases managerial reliance, but its effects on performance and trust are conditional. Under the baseline state-based recommendation and payoff-space source-choice rules, high feasibility increases reliance by 20.08 percentage points and reduces average payoff by 0.242 relative to low feasibility. AI-only trust updating produces rising trust paths in every regime, but average trust is 0.064 lower under high feasibility. title: Robin Hood reachability and Büchi bidding games
abstract: Abstract Two-player graph games are a fundamental model for reasoning about the interaction of agents. These games are played between two players who move a token along a graph. In bidding games, the players have some monetary budget, and at each step they bid for the privilege of moving the token. Typically, the winner of the bid either pays the loser or the bank, or a combination thereof. We introduce Robin Hood bidding games, where at the beginning of every step the richer player pays the poorer a fixed fraction of the difference of their wealth. After the bid, the winner pays the loser. Intuitively, this captures the setting where a regulating entity prevents the accumulation of wealth to some degree. We show that the central property of bidding games, namely the existence of a threshold function, is retained in Robin Hood bidding games for both Reachability and Büchi objectives (in the latter we prove a weaker flavor of threshold). We show that the threshold can be effectively computed (using MILP for reachability objectives, and Linear Real Arithmetic for Büchi objectives). Surprisingly, we show that the games are not always determined exactly at the threshold, unlike their standard counterpart.

title: Dual-Use Discourse and Middle-Power Influence: The Netherlands in Global Climate Governance
abstract: Abstract Global climate governance increasingly depends on actors beyond the largest emitters, whose commitments remain uneven amid domestic polarization and geopolitical rivalry. This article examines how European middle powers influence climate governance amid this context. It develops the concept of dual-use discourse: climate narratives crafted to project credibility in international arenas while managing domestic political and economic constraints. Through a hybrid discourse analysis of Dutch climate diplomacy across Rutte-III, Rutte-IV, and Schoof-I (2017–2025), the article examines speeches, policy documents, and parliamentary debates. The analysis shows how Dutch governments turn flood vulnerability and water-management expertise into diplomatic assets, while building climate niches around adaptation, circularity, and resilience. Such narratives also respond to coalition politics, legal pressures, sectoral interests, and public contestation at home. The article recasts middle-power climate influence as a fragile politics of credibility, sustained when narratives remain anchored in material capacities and credible implementation.

title: Marriage, Patriarchy, and Intergenerational Relational Power
abstract: This study employs a critical narrative literature review with thematic analysis to examine persistent tensions between mothers-in-law (MILs) and daughters-in-law (DILs) as manifestations of broader gendered and intergenerational power relations within marriage and family life. Drawing on scholarship published from 2015 to 2025, the review focuses on the Philippines and selected Asian contexts, including China, Singapore, Taiwan, South Korea, India, and Pakistan. Guided by feminist perspectives on marriage, particularly Clare Chambers’ critique of marriage as a practical and symbolic institution that can reproduce women’s subordination, the review synthesizes empirical studies and cross-cultural research to explore how patriarchal structures, cultural expectations, gendered domestic roles, and generational hierarchies shape MIL-DIL relationships. The thematic synthesis suggests that MIL-DIL tensions cannot be attributed solely to interpersonal incompatibility but are embedded within broader structures of authority, domestic labor, caregiving, and culturally prescribed gender roles. These dynamics are further shaped by intergenerational obligations, kinship arrangements, and expectations surrounding women’s roles within marriage and the household. Results indicate that conflict often arises not from personal animosity alone but from systemic structures that position women within…

title: Making sense of climate distress using the Power Threat Meaning Framework: research with climate activists
abstract: Introduction The climate crisis presents an immediate threat to human health. Despite this reality, psychological distress in the face of the climate breakdown is at risk of being treated as a ‘mental health condition’. The Power Threat Meaning Framework (PTMF) offers a new perspective that centers power and contextualizes distress through the development of narratives. This paper reports on the first peer-reviewed study of the fit between the PTMF and climate-related distress. The focus was on experiences of climate activists who are highly engaged with the climate crisis. Methods Serial semi-structured interviews were held with eight UK-based climate activists to co-construct PTMF narratives. Thirty interviews were analyzed with template analysis. A priori themes from the PTMF were used to inform the coding template. Results Participants’ experiences could readily be mapped onto the five interrelated domains of the PTMF: Power, Threats, Meanings, Threat Responses and Strengths. A meta-narrative was produced through synthesizing participants’ accounts. Discussion People’s distress and experiences of environmental action vary based on operations of power and systemic injustices, both within and outside of activist spaces. Findings support calls to understand individual and collective responses to climate breakdown through the lens of collective trauma. The PTMF may offer a usef…

The Human Edge in Offline Electronics Retail: Interpersonal Communication and Customer Loyalty in an E-Commerce Context
abstract: The growing integration of e-commerce into consumer purchasing journeys has increased the need for offline electronics retailers to understand the relational value of face-to-face customer–employee interaction. This study examines the associations of three interpersonal communication constructs—empathy, responsiveness, and closeness—with customer loyalty in an offline electronics-retail setting. The term human edge is used as an interpretive framing for interpersonal interaction rather than as a separately measured construct, while e-commerce competition serves as the contextual background rather than a variable in the tested model. A quantitative cross-sectional explanatory survey was conducted among 123 customers of MMS Computer in Tangerang, Indonesia, selected through purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Empathy was positively associated with customer loyalty (β = 0.306, t = 3.793, p < 0.001), as was responsiveness (β = 0.542, t = 7.362, p < 0.001). Closeness showed a positive but statistically non-significant association (β = 0.153, t = 1.694, p = 0.090). The three predictors jointly explained 42.0% of the variance in customer loyalty. The findings indicate differentiated associations among interpersonal communication constructs: empathy and responsiveness were independently associated with customer …

title: Factors influencing consumer choice in the informal food retail markets in Ghana
abstract: Purpose The study sought to investigate the factors influencing consumer choice in the informal food retail market. Design/methodology/approach Using a descriptive research design and quantitative methodology, 432 useable questionnaires were obtained from respondents through a convenience sampling method from Accra, Kumasi, Takoradi and Koforidua. The study employed exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis and discriminant validity before conducting the structural equation model to examine why consumers choose informal food retail as their preferred market for shopping. Findings The study established that there exists a positive statistical relationship between the environment and informal food retail market (Coeff = 0.258; p-value <0.001), price and informal food retail market (Coeff = 0.105; p-value = 0.017), convenience and informal food retail market (Coeff = 0.175; p-value <0.001), and food variety and the informal food retail market (Coeff = 0.223; p-value <0.001). Therefore, the study concludes that consumers' choice of the informal food retail market is based on the environment, price, convenience and food variety. Research limitations/implications The study was limited to the major cities in Ghana, namely Accra, Kumasi, Takoradi and Koforidua. It was conducted as a quantitative research study. The study recommends that future research should a…

title: Allies on the frontline, America at a distance? Rethinking alliance politics in Asia
abstract: Abstract This essay examines how recent shifts in US foreign policy, marked by rising unilateralism and receding global commitments, are reshaping regional security dynamics and alliance politics in Asia. While the US-led “hub and spokes” alliance system has historically underpinned regional security, calls for greater burden sharing are occurring amid intensifying US–China competition and widening uncertainty about US strategic priorities. In critiquing the extant literature on US-Asia security and alliance politics, the essay highlights emergent divergences between US and Asian allies’ regional threat perceptions and the potential reversal in moral hazard in the alliance system. These misalignments produce new strains in alliance cohesion, not least with growing expectations and pressure on Asian allies to adopt exclusive alignment and power balancing policies that they might otherwise prefer to avoid, thereby complicating efforts to sustain a stable regional order.

Deciphering Antigen–Antibody Interactions via Geometric Graph Representations and Transfer Learning
abstract: Abstract Deciphering antigen–antibody interactions is pivotal for understanding immune recognition and accelerating therapeutic antibody development. However, experimental characterization remains costly and labor-intensive, while existing computational approaches have not fully exploited protein structural geometry. Moreover, these predictors often struggle to effectively bridge the gap between identifying general protein binding sites, mapping antigen epitopes, and quantifying antigen–antibody binding affinities. Here, we present GALA, a versatile graph learning framework that leverages a structure-aware protein language model and invariant geometric representations to decode these interactions hierarchically. GALA was first pretrained on a large-scale protein binding site corpus and subsequently adapted to antibody-agnostic epitope prediction via transfer learning, substantially outperforming existing methods in both tasks. To enable antibody-specific prediction, we further integrated antibody information into GALA via a cross attention-based bidirectional interaction module. The resulting antibody-specific epitope predictor surpassed state-of-the-art methods, including AlphaFold3 and GEP, and improved the reranking of predicted antigen–antibody complex structures. Finally, fine-tuning this antibody-aware model for antigen–antibody binding affinity prediction yielded substan…

title: Pengaruh Pembelajaran Berdiferensiasi dengan Model Problem Based Learning (PBL) Terhadap Civic Knowledge Siswa SMP Negeri 18 Surakarta
abstract: Tujuan penelitian ini dalam rangka menginvestigasi apakah terdapat pengaruh dari pelaksanaan pembelajaran berdiferensiasi dengan model problem based learning (PBL) terhadap civic knowledge siswa SMP Negeri 18 Surakarta. Jenis penelitian ini adalah quasi eksperimen dengan desain penelitian berupa nonequivalent control group. Sebanyak 255 siswa menjadi populasi penelitian dengan 60 siswa sebagai sampel melalui cluster random sampling sebagai teknik pengambilannya. Pelaksanaan pembelajaran berdiferensiasi dengan model PBL diukur melalui observasi dan civic knowledge diukur melalui tes objektif. Hasil penelitian dianalisis dengan uji normalitas, uji homogenitas, dan uji Wilcoxon Matched Pairs. Perolehan skor civic knowledge siswa kelas eksperimen adalah 80,00 dan 71,22 pada kelas kontrol. Uji hipotesis menunjukkan bahwa nilai signifikansi <0,001, sehingga terdapat pengaruh antara pembelajaran berdiferensiasi dengan model PBL terhadap civic knowledge siswa dan terdapat perbedaan rata-rata yang signifikan antara kedua kelas penelitian, dengan kelas eksperimen mencapai hasil yang lebih tinggi daripada kelas kontrol.

title: On-detector machine learning for beam-induced background rejection at a 10 TeV Muon collider
abstract: Abstract A 10 TeV Muon Collider is a compelling candidate for a future energy-frontier facility, offering unprecedented opportunities to explore the fundamental laws of particle physics. Muon decays in the collider ring produce intense beam-induced background (BIB) that can overwhelm detector occupancy and exceed readout bandwidth constraints. We investigate the potential of on-detector Machine Learning for BIB rejection in the vertex detector, exploiting pixel cluster shapes to distinguish background from collision products. We study three classes of lightweight neural-network architectures, and evaluate the feasibility of their implementation in hardware with high-level synthesis. Selected architectures achieve 88%–90% data reduction at 99% signal efficiency while requiring hardware resources compatible with potential ASIC implementation. These results demonstrate the potential of performing substantial BIB rejection directly in the pixel readout, providing a path towards meeting the tracker readout requirements at a future Muon Collider.

title: Affective drivers of generative AI acceptance in higher education: a UTAUT extension across on-campus and distance learning
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the drivers of students’ intention to intensify generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) use in higher education, focusing on the incremental explanatory value of Affective Evaluation and differences between on-campus and distance-learning students. Design/methodology/approach Building on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), the study analyzes survey data from 502 students at a German university of applied sciences. Hierarchical regression analyses, group comparisons and moderation analyses are used to examine predictor–intention relationships and the role of study mode. Findings The UTAUT-based model explained approximately 62% of the variance in Intention to Intensify GenAI Use. Affective Evaluation contributed significant incremental explanatory power and showed the largest standardized coefficient, alongside significant effects of Performance Expectancy and Social Influence. Distance-learning students reported higher intention than on-campus students, although the effect was small. Moderation analyses provided little overall evidence of systematic differences in predictor–intention relationships; an isolated Social Influence interaction was interpreted as exploratory. Research limitations/implications The study is limited by its cross-sectional, self-reported data from a single institution, unequal study-mode g…

title: Students' learning needs in a general biology course as a basis for designing an SDGs-oriented RADEC learning model
abstract: Background: General Biology underpins later biology courses and offers natural entry points to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), yet its design is rarely grounded in data on students' learning needs, and university students' readiness for the Read-Answer-Discuss-Explain-Create (RADEC) model is largely unknown. Objectives: This study mapped students' learning needs and their readiness for RADEC phases as the needs-analysis stage of developing an SDGs-oriented RADEC model. Methods: A cross-sectional survey with a mixed-methods approach was completed by 343 biology education students (response rate 75.9%) at an Indonesian state Islamic university. Closed items were analyzed descriptively and with chi-square tests; open-ended responses were analyzed through open and axial coding. Results: Five needs emerged: support for terminology and missing prerequisites, because genetics (66.5%) and the chemistry of life (50.1%) were the most difficult topics and unfamiliar terms (54.2%) and insufficient prior knowledge (44.0%) were common barriers; guided and accountable pre-class study, because 84.0% welcomed pre-class materials but only 16.0% often read before class; structured collaboration, because passive members (58.6%) hampered discussion; lecturer consolidation after student presentations; and scaffolding for project ideas (47.8%) with explicit links to sustainability, because …

Multi-task deep learning for crack detection, segmentation and quantification in tunnels
abstract: Crack detection and quantification in tunnel chutes is vital for ensuring infrastructure safety and preventing failures. Traditional methods, reliant on manual checks and basic image processing, are inefficient and inaccurate because they overlook tunnel-specific conditions. This paper introduces a multi-task deep learning model aimed at automating structural health monitoring in this context. The proposed solution integrates the U-shaped convolutional neural network for crack segmentation, version five of the you only look once algorithm for detection and a quantification model to measure crack length, area, density and severity. Utilising the publicly available ‘a crack dataset’ from Kaggle for training and testing, the model incorporates preprocessing techniques such as resizing, noise reduction and contrast enhancement to improve crack detection, segmentation and quantification performance. The framework demonstrates high performance with precision (0.900), recall (0.930), F1 score (0.915), dice (0.900) and intersection over union (0.850), demonstrating effectiveness on the evaluated data set. External data sets were used to assess the generalisation capability of the proposed framework. Although the evaluated data sets provide evidence of the framework’s potential for structural crack inspection, dedicated validation using tunnel chute-specific imagery from real operationa…

title: Continuing professional development in a learning health system: exploring tensions related to learning, culture and system constraints in the delivery of an educational program designed to support humanistic skills development and clinician wellbeing
abstract: The Humanistic Education and Training (HET) and the Extensive Needs Services (ENS) teams from Canada’s largest pediatric rehabilitation hospital recently collaborated on a year-long continuous professional development (CPD) pilot project with the aim of amplifying the emotional and cognitive capacities (optimal functioning) of ENS staff. This quality improvement initiative was selected as a demonstration project in support of our organizational strategic goal of becoming a Learning Health System (LHS) with evaluation embedded into the design to advance our understanding of how to support healthy teams. The participants represented a broad range of roles, including: behavior analysts (5), behavior technicians (8), pharmacist, psychologist, service co-ordinators (2), team lead, registered nurse, clinic flow assistant, project manager, child life specialist, speech pathologist, clinical integration and respite co-ordinator, speech/language pathologist, occupational therapist, registered dietician, family therapist, and nurse practitioner. There were two interventions a month, one emphasizing theory and practice, the other emphasizing small group coaching support that aimed to be both formative and restorative for participants. The project began with 28 participants and finished with 15 participants. Information collected through a participant survey at a third of the way into the …

title: Supporting creative exploration in fashion pattern cutting through a generative human–machine system
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how generative computational systems can support creative exploration in fashion pattern cutting, addressing the underexplored use of computation for open-ended early-stage ideation. Design/methodology/approach The research follows design science research methodology. A software prototype, Re-Cut Lab, was developed to generate and transform patterns through algorithmic constraints and controlled randomness. Its design is informed by Creative Cognition theory and evaluated through system outputs and preliminary user-based evidence from two exploratory workshops involving 23 participants. Findings The system generated diverse and interpretable pattern configurations supporting multiple design trajectories. Across the two workshops, all participants agreed or strongly agreed that Re-Cut Lab could help students overcome the “blank page syndrome” in early-stage design, while 21 of 23 agreed or strongly agreed that its generative approach encouraged greater experimentation. UEQ-S scores were 2.768 at UM and 2.617 at CSDMM-UPM. These findings provide preliminary support for the system’s intended creativity-support role. Research limitations/implications User-based findings derive from small, non-equivalent samples and short-term self-reports. S -matrix constrained equivariant graph neural network for Hamiltonian inversion of Kagome and quasiperiodic non-Hermitian systems
abstract: Abstract Reconstructing Hamiltonian parameters from noisy scattering data is an ill-posed inverse problem in non-Hermitian quantum systems. We propose an S -matrix constrained equivariant graph neural network that embeds two architectural hard constraints to reduce the solution ambiguity. An equivariant message-passing encoder incorporates lattice point-group symmetry and permutation-invariant aggregation (for the Aubry–André–Harper quasiperiodic chain), thereby suppressing symmetry-induced parameter variability. A deterministic S -matrix solver serves as a fixed decoder that enforces the scattering equations within the assumed model, eliminating the need for physics-based residual loss terms. Inference is performed via a two-stage hybrid optimization: offline pre-training on synthetic data, followed by online single-sample fine-tuning in a low-dimensional latent space. On a 48-site Kagome supercell and a 50-site Aubry–André–Harper quasiperiodic chain, using a synthetic dataset of 120 000 samples (100 000 training, 10 000 validation, 10 000 test) with additive white Gaussian noise (0%–10%), the mean absolute percentage error of reconstructed parameters remains around 5% for both systems under 10% noise, with per-parameter standard deviations below 7 % across 20 independent repetitions, and with an empirical inconsistency ratio 1 − ECR ( τ = 0.05 ) around 5 % . title: From learning to coping: an integrated framework for adolescent mental health education
abstract: School mental health education needs to explain how adolescents use coping strategies beyond the classroom. This conceptual analysis uses a purposive narrative synthesis to reformulate an existing curriculum for lower and upper secondary education. It integrates emotion regulation strategies, resilience resources, and the MUSIC Model of Academic Motivation. Social and emotional learning provides a broad educational foundation, while COM-B (capability, opportunity, motivation, and behaviour) identifies general conditions for behaviour. The proposed framework adds a curriculum-specific account of how adolescents transfer learned coping responses to everyday stressful situations. It distinguishes acquiring and rehearsing response options from using them outside lessons, motivation to participate in instruction from motivation to apply coping responses elsewhere, and perceived care from access to responsive support. The proposed contribution of resources depends on the situation and coping response: obtaining help requires responsive support, whereas some responses can be used independently. Four testable propositions address support mapping, participation, continued practice, and contextual conditions for transfer. An annual curriculum and examples of teaching practices illustrate applications across school levels. A staged evaluation strategy assesses learning, subsequent coping,…

title: Task-dependent predictability of gamma passing rates in stereotactic body radiation therapy using UCoMX plan-complexity features: a patient-group-aware machine learning benchmark
abstract: Background Treatment-plan complexity metrics have been proposed for predicting patient-specific quality assurance outcomes, but their predictive value may depend on the gamma criterion and task definition. This study evaluated the task-dependent predictability of gamma passing rates (GPRs) in stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) using Universal Complexity Metrics Extractor (UCoMX) plan-complexity features. Methods The retrospective cohort included 206 SBRT plans from 163 patients. Nineteen numerical UCoMX features were evaluated in patient-group-aware nested cross-validation. The benchmark included full-cohort binary classification of G31 (GPR evaluated using the 3%/1 mm criterion) and G32 (GPR evaluated using the 3%/2 mm criterion), continuous G32 regression, and joint G31–G32 endpoint modeling. A secondary exploratory analysis compared clearly separated G31 outcomes, defined as low-GPR (<90%) and high-GPR (≥98%) groups. Predictions were obtained from pooled outer-fold out-of-fold evaluations. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was performed for the extreme-outcome Logistic Regression model using held-out outer-fold records. Results Predictive performance varied across GPR endpoints and task formulations. title: An elite ant colony prior-guided dual closed-loop adaptive Q-learning algorithm for mobile robot path planning
abstract: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL)-based path planning for mobile robots in complex obstacle environments still suffers from insufficient prior guidance, inefficient exploration, and limited adaptability during policy learning. To address these issues, this study proposes an improved Q-learning (QL) algorithm, termed elite ant colony prior-guided dual closed-loop adaptive Q-learning algorithm (EAS-AQL). First, elite ant colony optimization is adopted to generate prior search knowledge, which is incorporated into QL through pheromone-guided initialization and decision-making. The high-quality paths obtained during elite search are subsequently fed back to update the pheromone distribution, forming an Elite Experience Reverse Feedback Mechanism and establishing an elite pheromone feedback loop between path experience, pheromone guidance, and QL decision-making. Moreover, an adaptive regulation mechanism based on real-time learning performance feedback is designed to dynamically adjust exploration and learning parameters, establishing a learning-process adaptive regulation loop to achieve an improved balance between exploration and exploitation. Extensive experiments conducted on grid maps with different scales and complexities demonstrate that EAS-AQL achieves superior performance in convergence efficiency, path quality, smoothness, and robustness compared with conventional QL …

A Comparative Study of Natural Deep Eutectic Solvent vs Ionic Liquid Microemulsions for Celecoxib Transdermal Delivery
abstract: Abstract The poor aqueous solubility of many active pharmaceutical ingredients remains a major challenge in drug development. This study explores natural deep eutectic solvents (NADES) as a biocompatible platform to enhance the solubility and transdermal delivery of celecoxib, a poorly water-soluble drug. Stable NADES/W microemulsions were formulated using a lactic acid/menthol NADES and a Tween 80/Transcutol HP (3:1) surfactant system. Following pseudoternary phase diagram construction, four optimized formulations were characterized for their physicochemical properties, including droplet size, viscosity, electrical conductivity, and refractive index. These NADES-based systems were directly compared to ionic liquid (IL)/W microemulsions of identical composition. While the NADES/W microemulsions exhibited smaller droplet sizes (232 nm) and superior monodispersity (PDI < 0.25), the IL/W systems with the same composition demonstrated higher celecoxib solubility. The NADES/W systems achieved celecoxib solubility from 0.29 to 1.86 mg·mL–1, lower than the IL/W systems (from 4.72 to 20.88 mg·mL–1). Ex vivo permeation rate of 7.6 μg·cm–2·h–1 for NADES/W versus 49.2 or 65.4 μg·cm–2·h–1 for IL/W, attributable to their greater ionic strength and solubilizing power. The Relationship Between Perceived Social Support and Intolerance of Uncertainty Among University Students Writing Their Final Projects
abstract: Writing a final project confronts students with uncertainty about supervision, revisions, and the time of completion, which may give rise to intolerance of uncertainty (IU). Based on the stress-buffering perspective, perceived social support is expected to be related to lower IU, yet direct evidence among Indonesian students writing their final projects is still limited. This study aimed to examine the relationship between perceived social support and IU among university students who were writing their final projects. A quantitative correlational design was used. The participants were 335 active students who were writing a final project and had attended at least one supervision session, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected online with the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS) and the Indonesian version of the Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale-12 (IUS-12). Because the scores were not normally distributed, the data were analysed with Spearman correlation in Jamovi. Perceived social support was not significantly related to IU (ρ = 0.065, p = 0.236); the direction was positive and the strength very weak, so the hypothesis of a negative relationship was not supported. Social support scores were relatively high, and the limited variation may have reduced the ability to detect a relationship. These findings suggest that perceived social support …

Propagation of CAMS aerosol uncertainty to clear-sky solar irradiance estimates
abstract: Atmospheric aerosols strongly influence surface solar radiation (SSR) through scattering and absorption processes, introducing substantial uncertainties into SSR estimates. Atmospheric reanalysis products are increasingly used for solar resource assessment; however, the propagation of aerosol-related uncertainty into SSR calculations remains insufficiently quantified. In this study, we derive aerosol optical depth (AOD) uncertainties for the fourth-generation ECMWF Atmospheric Composition Reanalysis 4 (EAC4) and investigate their propagation into clear-sky estimates of global horizontal irradiance (GHI) and direct normal irradiance (DNI) over the 60° S–60° N domain for the 2003–2024 period. AOD uncertainties are calculated using collocated EAC4 and Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) observations, yielding a global mean relative AOD uncertainty of approximately 47 %. Radiative kernels are subsequently used to quantify the sensitivity of clear-sky SSR to AOD perturbations, enabling the propagation of AOD uncertainty into GHI and DNI estimates. The results reveal pronounced spatial and seasonal variability, with the largest propagated uncertainties occurring over regions affected by persistent anthropogenic pollution, biomass burning, and desert dust. Relative GHI uncertainties generally remain below 5 %–6 %, whereas relative DNI uncertainties frequently exceed 18 % over major aero…

Model-embedded Gaussian Process Regression for Parameter Estimation and Uncertainty Quantification in Dynamical Systems
abstract: The identification of dynamical systems is a vital task in science and engineering. Traditional methods require numerous calls to the dynamical-system solver, rendering likelihood-based or least-squares inference frameworks impractical. For efficient parameter inference, two state-of-the-art techniques are the kernel method for modeling and the one-step framework for jointly inferring unknown parameters and hyperparameters. The kernel method is a quick and straightforward technique, but it cannot estimate solutions and their derivatives, which must strictly adhere to physical laws. We propose a model-embedded one-step Bayesian framework for joint inference of unknown parameters and hyperparameters by maximizing the marginal likelihood. This approach models the solution and its derivatives using Gaussian process regression (GPR), taking into account smoothness and continuity properties, and treats differential equations as constraints that can be naturally integrated into the Bayesian framework in the linear case. Additionally, we prove convergence of the model-embedded Gaussian process regression (ME-GPR) for theoretical development. Motivated by Taylor expansion, we introduce a piecewise first-order linearization strategy to handle nonlinear dynamical systems. Numerical experiments on simulated linear and nonlinear dynamical systems evaluate the method’s performance in paramet…

title: Evaluation of the effect of scattering uncertainty on photothermal therapy planning
abstract: Abstract Photothermal therapy (PTT) requires accurate prediction of laser-induced temperature increase to achieve effective tumor treatment outcomes. Such prediction is typically obtained through pretreatment planning based on numerical simulations coupling light transport and heat transfer equations. Simulation accuracy is generally guaranteed by the precise determination of the optical properties characterizing the target tissue. Although absorption is the primary driver of heat generation, scattering governs light propagation through tissue, influencing penetration depth and resulting spatial distribution of temperature. Since tumor malignancy alters tissue microstructure and scattering behavior, understanding the sensitivity of the optical and thermal responses to these variations is fundamental for effective treatment planning and optimized PTT outcomes. In this study, the impact of scattering uncertainty on light fluence and laser-induced temperature was investigated using a numerical phantom with a tumor-mimicking inclusion. The temperature sensitivity analysis comprised multiple cases, including different inclusion geometries, irradiation durations, and illumination source multiplicities. title: UQ-SegNet: an instance segmentation method with uncertainty quantification for crystallization processes
abstract: Abstract Reliable crystal detection is critical for crystallization quality control. Small, densely distributed crystals dominate crystallization images. Their blurred boundaries and low contrast make segmentation prone to missing them or merging neighboring crystals. These errors distort the crystal size distribution (CSD) obtained from the segmentation results, so segmentation reliability must also be assessed. We propose uncertainty quantification instance segmentation network (UQ-SegNet) to segment individual crystals and quantify pixel-level uncertainty. A high-frequency fusion multiscale convolutional Attention module combines discrete cosine transform filtering with multiscale attention to retain small-crystal edges. A Position-Aware Head adds positional encoding to ROI features to improve crystal localization, and a Bayesian Decoder estimates epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty with Monte Carlo Dropout. UQ-SegNet achieves the highest AP 75 (72.13%) and AP s (61.30%) among compared models, and its CSD agrees most closely with the annotations. Both uncertainty types correlate positively with pixel errors. The method provides the CSD with pixel-level uncertainty for assessing the underlying segmentation.

title: Information entropy and an AI-enabled framework for managing regulatory uncertainty in essential medicines governance
abstract: Essential medicines are central to public health systems, yet their regulation continues to face persistent challenges involving medicine prices, quality, supply continuity, and rational medicine use. A recurring informational problem is that decision-relevant evidence may be fragmented, incomplete, delayed, inconsistent, or difficult to verify across regulatory actors and stages, thereby contributing to uncertainty in identifying relevant regulatory states. This article develops a theory-informed framework for managing regulatory uncertainty in essential medicines governance. Drawing on information entropy theory and qualitative policy and governance analysis, information entropy is used as a formal conceptual representation of uncertainty over predefined regulatory states rather than as an empirically validated measure of regulatory performance. The framework distinguishes a hypothesized problem-generation pathway from a proposed intervention pathway linking information integration, AI-assisted signal identification and interpretation, verification and professional regulatory judgment, proportionate response, and feedback. To operationalize this framework, the article proposes a two-layer architecture of interconnected regulatory databases. title: Validating and correcting high-resolution urban climate models with a dense sensor network
abstract: Abstract Urban climate models now map nocturnal temperature at metre scale. Planners use these maps directly, yet their contrasts are rarely tested at the scale of use. We test the $${5}\,\text {m}$$ output of the FITNAH-3D model against about 85 low-cost sensors in Mannheim, Germany, on tropical nights, then correct it. The correlation between the model, averaged over a disc of radius R , and the point observations rises from 0.29 at native resolution to 0.71 at $$R = {200}\,\text {m}$$ . A smoothing-only null built from the mislocated $${5}\,\text {m}$$ model reaches a median of at most 0.41, so the rise reflects the scale at which the model is supported by the sensors. Under calm conditions (wind below $${0.6}\,\text {m s}^{-1}$$ ) the amplitude of the model contrasts at that scale is correct, with a regression slope of 0.98 [0.79, 1.17]. On nights with weak synoptic wind the slope falls to about 0.4, which sets how far autochthonous contrasts must be scaled down outside their design regime. Regression kriging (RK) with the averaged model as covariate adds a persistent kilometre-scale pattern from the sensors and reduces the cross-validated error of ordinary kriging by 12% (RK better on 5 of 7 nights, $$p = 0.04$$ ). A regression on scale bands shows that the sensors confirm the model structure down to about $${100}\,\text {m}$$ , the effective resolution at which a point ne…

title: Case Report: Pharmacist-led nutritional pharmaceutical care in patients with malignancy-associated short bowel syndrome–with concurrent interception of drug-induced disorders and optimization of antineoplastic regimens
abstract: Background Short bowel syndrome (SBS) constitutes a severe complication following small intestinal fistulization surgery in patients with advanced colorectal cancer complicated by malignant bowel obstruction, which predisposes patients to water-electrolyte disturbances and malabsorption, as well as cancer cachexia. The role of clinical pharmacists in delivering nutritional pharmaceutical care for such patients has not been fully recognized. Case summary A 41-year-old male patient with stage IV colorectal cancer developed excessive fistula fluid loss (3000–450 mL daily) after small intestinal fistulization surgery, with approximately 150 cm of functional small bowel remaining and a functionally defunctionalized colon. Severe hypokalemia (serum potassium 2.43 mmol/L), hyponatremia (serum sodium 128.9 mmol/L), and cancer cachexia (35 kg weight loss over 6 months) were identified. Clinical pharmacists implemented stepwise parenteral and enteral nutrition support, with an initial energy supply of 1,000 kcal/d administered in a gradual escalating manner, and delivered high-dose potassium supplementation (6.5–8.0 g/d). Drug-induced hypotension and syncope triggered by combined glycyrrhizin and trazodone were identified and intervened. Given the compromised oral drug absorption in patients with SBS, the direct observation of intact tablets in the fistula effluent, and the unavailabilit…

title: Solving the rebar cutting-stock problem with a hybrid mountain Gazelle optimization framework for minimizing waste and procurement in construction projects
abstract: Purpose This study develops a hybrid optimization framework to minimize rebar cutting waste, reduce standard rebar procurement and enhance material reuse, thereby improving cost efficiency and supporting sustainable construction. Design/methodology/approach A hybrid MGO–LP–CG algorithm is developed by integrating Mountain Gazelle Optimization (MGO), Linear Programming (LP) and Column Generation (CG). During CG, a continuous Master Problem (MP) minimizes standard-rebar consumption and provides dual prices to an MGO-based pricing subproblem. MGO searches for integer cutting patterns with negative reduced cost, which are iteratively added to the MP. After termination, the continuous pattern frequencies are converted into executable integer frequencies through upward rounding. At the framework level, generated residuals are subsequently prioritized for hierarchical reuse to reduce final nonreusable material. The framework is validated on three benchmark datasets and a real diaphragm wall project in Ho Chi Minh City. The real project case also incorporates an on-site workflow for the approved closed-loop reuse of residual bars. Findings The results show that MGO–LP–CG becomes more effective as problem scale and cutting-pattern complexity increase. Multiobjective optimization of coaxial three-rotor magnetic gear with dual modulation effects
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to propose and investigate a novel coaxial three-rotor magnetic gear (CTRMG) with dual modulation effects to overcome prevalent issues in magnetic gears, such as weak field modulation, significant leakage flux and suboptimal torque performance, aiming to enhance applicability in renewable energy systems like wind and tidal power generation. Design/methodology/approach A novel topology integrating Z-type pole-pieces and a Halbach permanent magnet array is introduced. The Z-type pole-piece structure enables a dual “Sum” modulation mechanism for enhanced field control and single-input-dual-output functionality. A structured optimization methodology, combining sensitivity analysis, the response surface method (RSM) and the nondominated sorting whale optimization algorithm (NSWOA), is used. The design is validated through three-dimensional (3D) finite element analysis. Findings 3D finite element computational results demonstrate that the optimized CTRMG achieves substantial electromagnetic performance gains. In numerical simulations, the steady-state average torque of output rotor 1 increases by 143.45% (to 87.74N·m), and that of output rotor 2 increases by 120.57% (to 336.52N·m) relative to the initial unoptimized CTRMG (which itself improves outer-rotor torque density by 34.61% over the conventional axial-field flux-focusing magnetic gear via the Z-type mod…

title: Optimization of the YOLOv8-Nano Deep Learning Model Through Knowledge Distillation for Driver Drowsiness Detection on Android Devices
abstract: Driver drowsiness is a major concern in transportation safety and requires an automated detection system capable of operating efficiently on mobile devices. This study aims to optimize the deep learning model YOLOv8-Nano for driver drowsiness detection through Knowledge Distillation while maintaining its lightweight characteristics for Android deployment. The dataset consists of 3,090 images representing six classes, namely eye_closed, eye_open, yawn, no_yawn, head_dropped, and head_straight. A YOLOv8-Large model was trained as the teacher model for 100 epochs using the default random seed, while YOLOv8-Nano was evaluated through four experimental configurations: E0 as the baseline, E1 with logit distillation, E2 with logit and bounding box distillation, and E3 with logit, bounding box, and feature distillation. Each configuration was trained for 30 epochs using random seeds 42, 43, and 44, and the results were summarized using mean and standard deviation. The results show that E3 achieved the highest performance, with a Precision of 0.9260 ± 0.0066, Recall of 0.9018 ± 0.0050, F1-score of 0.9137 ± 0.0036, mAP@0.5 of 0.9323 ± 0.0015, and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.6368 ± 0.0030. Compared with the E0 baseline, E3 improved mAP@0.5 from 0.3845 ± 0.0360 to 0.9323 ± 0.0015. The optimized model maintains 3.2 million parameters, 8.7 GFLOPs, and a model size of 6.2 MB, with an inference time of …

title: Cross-sectional geometry and doping co-optimization in triangular-channel gate-all-around FETs for the 2 nm technology node
abstract: Abstract This work investigates how triangular channel geometry and channel doping jointly govern the electrostatics and transport of silicon gate-all-around field-effect transistors with a 20 nm channel length. Three-dimensional technology computer-aided design simulations compare equilateral, right, acute, and obtuse triangular cross sections at channel doping concentrations N ch of 1 × 10 17 , 2 × 10 17 , and 3 × 10 17 cm −3 . Transfer, output, transconductance, logarithmic-transfer, electron-density, and electron-mobility results are evaluated with one consistent reference condition. At N ch = 1 × 10 17 cm −3 , the obtuse channel increases I ON from 4.40 × 10 −8 –4.56 × 10 −8 A (3.64%), reduces I OFF from 1.94 × 10 −13 –1.00 × 10 −13 A (48.45%), doubles the I ON / I OFF ratio (101.77% increase), raises g m,max by 23.40%, raises J D,sat by 9.47%, and lowers the subthreshold swing (SS) from 68.5 to 62.4 mV dec −1 (8.91%) relative to the equilateral reference. Increasing N ch to 3 × 10 17 cm −3 gives the largest obtuse-channel I ON , but it simultaneously increases leakage by 18.00%, reduces the current ratio by 12.06%, lowers g m,max by 7.12%, and worsens the SS by 5.13% relative to the lowest doping. The obtuse geometry at 1 × 10 17 cm −3 is therefore the best overall compromise in the reported dataset. Spatial maps, plotted over common legend ranges, are consistent with geo…

title: Intelligent bee swarm optimization algorithm with variational regularization method for solving integral equation of the first kind with noisy data
abstract: This work introduces a novel, intelligent, and efficient methodology for solving first-kind integral equations ill-conditioned by noisy data. The methodology commences by approximating the integral equation discretely into a system of linear equations by a suitable numerical approximation technique. For controlling the inherent ill-posedness of such ill-structured inverse problems, the overall discrepancy principle is adopted as a regularizing mechanism for stabilizing and retrieving accurate results. Upon the adaptive and mutually assisting nature of the swarm-based optimum hunt, the Intelligent Bee Swarm Optimization (IBSO) algorithm is utilized to automatically compute the optimum regularizing parameter. This combination harmoniously unites the strength of variational regularizing with the exploration global optimality of the swarm intellect. Numerical experiments extensive and far-reaching authenticate the optimal performance, consistency, and applicability of the introduced methodology in successfully retrieving stable and accurate solutions even when the noise level is high, thus providing a powerful computational tool for ill-structured inverse optimum problems.

title: Multi-scenario evaluation of medical accessibility and layout optimization: a case study of Kunming’s main urban area
abstract: Abstract Medical resources are often concentrated in urban centres while peripheral zones face supply shortages, making the balance between efficiency and spatial equity the core challenge of medical facility layout optimization. Taking central Kunming as the study area, this paper measures medical accessibility under walking, cycling and driving scenarios with the Gaussian two-step floating catchment area (Ga2SFCA) method, identifies medically underserved areas, and simulates three optimization strategies: new hospital construction, capacity expansion of existing facilities, and a combined strategy. Using underserved communities as candidate sites, a Capacitated Maximum Coverage Location Problem (CMCLP) model selects new hospital locations, and an efficiency-equity evaluation system quantifies the effects. Results show that medical accessibility declines from urban centres to peripheries and that optimization effects vary by travel mode. New facilities remedy peripheral shortages, while uniform expansion yields the largest absolute gains where baseline accessibility is already high; the combined strategy achieves the largest overall improvement under the study’s assumptions. The framework provides quantitative planning evidence for building 15-min healthcare service circles and for a balanced public medical resource layout.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND SUSTAINABLE VALUE CREATION AT BYD
abstract: The expansion of new energy vehicle manufacturing creates a strategic challenge: firms must increase output while maintaining resource efficiency, product quality and credible environmental accountability. This article develops a sustainable value creation framework for BYD, connecting digital capabilities with operational decisions and measurable economic, environmental and social outcomes. The study uses a qualitative, documentary case approach anchored in BYD’s 2024 sustainability report and established research on digital transformation, dynamic capabilities and sustainable business models. Four pathways are proposed: digitally enabled production control, supply-chain visibility, knowledge integration and lifecycle accountability. The analysis distinguishes disclosed corporate practices from proposed mechanisms and avoids attributing environmental improvements to digitalization without operational evidence. A measurement matrix and staged implementation roadmap translate the framework into managerial decisions. The central proposition is that digital investment creates sustainable value only when information is converted into accountable organizational action and evaluated against both intensity and absolute environmental indicators. The framework provides a basis for future empirical testing in new energy vehicle firms operating within renewable energy ecosystems.

Living Smarter: IoT Innovations and Behavioral Insights of consumers in Smart Home Landscape
abstract: This study examines the factors influencing the adoption of Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled smart home technologies among middle-aged and older consumers in India. Drawing on an extended Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) that incorporates selected Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) attributes, the research examines cognitive, social, economic, and system-level determinants, including perceived usefulness, ease of use, automation, and interconnection. The study used a mixed-methods approach, combining survey data from 255 Indian consumers aged 50 and above with qualitative insights from five industry experts and five consumers. The findings indicate that perceived usefulness, ease of use, automation, reliability, and subjective norms significantly shape technology acceptance, while perceived cost is negatively associated with behavioral intention. Conversely, enjoyment, complexity, and observability do not demonstrate statistically significant relationships in the hypothesized directions. The findings suggest that functional and economic considerations are particularly relevant to smart home adoption within the population studied. Theoretically, the study extends TAM by demonstrating how system-level capabilities and selected innovation attributes contribute differently to technology acceptance, thereby highlighting the context-dependent relevance of established adoption determinan…

title: Digital Finance, Intelligent Risk Management, and the Alleviation of Financing Constraints among SMEs—An Analysis of National Trends, Taizhou's Pilot Practices, and Regional Comparisons
abstract: The key obstacle to financing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) is information asymmetry between banks and enterprises. Drawing on a literature review, policy document analysis, and comparative analysis, this paper examines how digital finance alleviates financing constraints through banks' intelligent risk management, and assesses this mechanism using national trends, data from the Taizhou pilot zone, and regional comparisons. At the end of 2024, outstanding inclusive loans to micro and small enterprises (MSEs) in China totaled RMB 32.93 trillion, representing year-on-year growth of 14.6%; however, credit loans accounted for only 27.3%, and the loan access rate among technology-based SMEs was 46.9%. In the Taizhou pilot zone, the number of MSEs receiving loans increased from 240,000 to 613,200; the share of credit loans and guarantee-backed loans rose from 40% to 59.60%; the interest rate fell from 8.27% to 4.13%; and the non-performing loan (NPL) ratio declined from 1.58% to 0.72%. On a comparable statistical basis, loans to MSEs accounted for 55.19% of all loans in Taizhou, compared with approximately 31.4% nationwide, while inclusive MSE loans accounted for only about 8.6% in Liaoning. On this basis, the paper identifies four categories of barriers—data provision, model capabilities, enterprise readiness, and institutional arrangements—and proposes corresponding pol…

title: “It’s not just about the app”: managerial responses to customer concerns in digital banking
abstract: Purpose As digital banking becomes central to financial operations, banks face persistent challenges concerning customer complaints, trust, security and uneven digital engagement. This study aims to examine how bank managers interpret and respond to these challenges, foregrounding managerial sensemaking as a critical determinant of institutional practice. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 48 bank managers in Pakistan, this study adopts an abductive application of the Gioia methodology. By mobilizing service recovery logic, trust and perceived risk theory and the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT), the research systematically connects managerial interpretations with established theoretical perspectives. Findings The analysis reveals four aggregate dimensions: accessibility, impact on profit and loss, integrated security and banking practices and digitalization. The findings demonstrate that digital banking challenges are not merely technical; they are organizational tensions managed through complex interpretive work. Specifically, this study reveals how managers reconcile the gap between institutional digital readiness, as defined by UTAUT’s facilitating conditions, and customer-level adoption barriers. Originality/value By foregrounding managerial sensemaking, this study extends service recovery and trust-based perspe…

title: Investigating the driving forces of sustainable finance practices in emerging economies: the case of Bangladesh’s banking sector
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how different stakeholder groups exert distinct forms of pressure to influence sustainable finance practices (SFPs) in publicly listed banks in Bangladesh, an emerging economy. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on stakeholder theory and the new institutional sociology (NIS) perspective of institutional theory, this study adopts a qualitative research design based on 15 in-depth interviews with heads of sustainable finance (or equivalent positions) in listed banks. The interview data were analyzed through both theoretical and pragmatic lenses to examine their consistency with or divergence from, existing empirical evidence and theoretical propositions. Findings The findings reveal that multiple stakeholder groups exert different forms of pressure and banks respond by strengthening SFPs to comply with regulatory requirements, satisfy conditions imposed by funding providers, avoid regulatory sanctions and enhance legitimacy and stakeholder trust. Notably, the nature of stakeholder pressure varies according to a bank’s level of sustainable finance performance. The same stakeholder may exert coercive pressure on moderate-performing banks while exerting mimetic pressure on top-performing banks. This differentiated pattern of stakeholder influence represents a novel contribution to the sustainable finance literature. Practical implications The find…

title: The Role of Islamic Agricultural Finance in Addressing Financial Constraints: A Case Study of Agro Bank’s aPLS Model in Malaysia
abstract: The provision of suitable financing to smallholder farmers and agro entrepreneurs is a longstanding issue in Malaysia. In the agricultural sector, cash flow is not predictable, the risk of climatic and market fluctuations is present, and collateral is limited, which makes it difficult for conventional financing for many agricultural operators, especially small-scale operators. Islamic agricultural financing provides an alternative solution with the principles of risk sharing, fairness, ethical investment and prevention of riba in accordance with Islamic rules. Agro Bank's Agricultural Profit and Loss Sharing (aPLS) is one of the potentially relevant financing models to address the unique financial nature of agricultural activities. This study analyzed the financial constraints faced by agropreneurs in Malaysia and the perception level of the effectiveness of the aPLS model as well as the barriers to its widespread implementation. There was a qualitative study with case study approach using ten participants such as farmers, agro-entrepreneurs, respondents from the Department of Agriculture Malaysia, and Agro Bank officers. Thematic analysis of the interview data aimed to reveal patterns of experiences and perceptions that occur across participants. The results indicate that agropreneurs still face tremendous financial problems such as irregular cash flow; failure in getting star…

title: Does the tone of ESG tweets indicate ESG performance? A signaling theory approach
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether the tone of firms’ environmental, social and governance (ESG)-related Twitter (X) posts is associated with ESG performance, as measured by the LSEG ESG score. Design/methodology/approach The analysis uses an unbalanced panel of 122 Fortune Global 500 firms over 2015–2021, comprising 427 firm-year observations. More than 240,000 tweets were analyzed using a Bloomberg ESG glossary-based keyword approach, while sentiment was measured using the VADER lexicon, and the associations were examined using panel regression models. Findings More positive ESG tweet tone is associated with higher overall ESG scores (contemporaneous and subsequent). Alternative sentiment measures support the main findings, while reverse-causality tests show no evidence that prior ESG scores predict subsequent tweet sentiment. Research limitations/implications This study focuses on large firms with active English-language Twitter (X) accounts. Future research could examine smaller firms, additional platforms, longer periods and alternative ESG rating providers. Practical implications ESG tweet sentiment may provide investors with a timely supplementary signal of contemporaneous and subsequent company ESG score. Managers should align social media communication with underlying ESG practices. Originality/value This study isolates ESG-specific sentiment in corporate socia…

abstract: Periodic, batch-based public financial reporting in developing countries weakens accountability, yet little is known about whether public institutions are ready to adopt permissioned blockchain for real-time reporting. This study examines how technological, human capital, regulatory and legal, organisational, leadership and political will, and data security and privacy readiness shape adoption readiness intent for permissioned blockchain-based financial reporting in Ghana's public sector, an issue central to accountable and transparent institutions (SDG 16) and resilient digital infrastructure and innovation (SDG 9). The study uses survey data from 300 officials in ministries, local government authorities, state-owned enterprises and regulatory bodies, selected through proportional stratified sampling and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling and one-way ANOVA. The results show that all six dimensions have significant positive effects on adoption readiness intent: technological readiness (β = 0.312, p < 0.001), human capital readiness (β = 0.274, p < 0.001), organisational readiness (β = 0.221, p < 0.001), regulatory and legal readiness (β = 0.198, p < 0.001), leadership and political will (β = 0.189, p < 0.001) and data security and privacy readiness (β = 0.163, p = 0.001). The model explains 69.3% of the variance in adoption readiness intent (R² =…
