Postmortem histopathology of the heart in right dominant arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM-R) – a systematic literature review
abstract: Abstract Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM), particularly its classical right-dominant form historically termed arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC), is a rare but important cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD) in young adults, posing significant challenges in forensic practice. Postmortem diagnosis relies primarily on careful macroscopic and histopathological examination, as clinical or genetic information is often unavailable. This review of published autopsy cases highlights fibrofatty replacement of the right ventricular myocardium as the most consistent histological finding, while macroscopic features such as ventricular wall thinning, dilation, or fatty infiltration were less consistently reported. Considerable variability exists in tissue sampling strategies, staining methods and criteria applied for diagnosis. Postmortem genetic testing is rarely performed due to logistical and financial constraints. These limitations complicate the establishment of standardized diagnostic thresholds and may affect forensic determinations of cause of death. Nonetheless, systematic histopathological evaluation remains essential for identifying ACM-R and can guide targeted molecular analyses in selected cases. The findings emphasize the need for standardized protocols for tissue sampling and histological assessment, ideally supported by multicenter reference collections.…

title: Remittances, Exchange Rates, and the Role of Financial Development
abstract: This paper examines the role of financial development as a buffer for the appreciating effects of remittances on exchange rates using annual data from 1996 to 2021 for 146 economies, with a focus on 43 high remittance-receiving economies. A standard panel regression framework is used in the baseline analysis, which remains robust to an instrumental variables approach. The findings reveal that remittance inflows are associated with appreciating effects on real effective exchange rates (REERs), especially in high remittance-receiving economies, consistent with the “Dutch disease” mechanism. Examining subcomponents of financial development, we find that stronger domestic financial markets and market-based financial deepening are critical channels for absorbing the REER appreciation effects of remittances.

title: Proportionality of Administrative and Criminal Authority in Resolving State Financial Losses
abstract: In Indonesia, vague definitions of “financial loss” and “loss to the state” frequently blur the distinction between administrative and criminal liability. This study examines the normative framework governing “loss to the state” and its implications for the scope and extent of administrative and criminal law. It employs a normative legal methodology, drawing particularly on statutory, conceptual, and case-based approaches and referring to Supreme Court rulings. The findings of this study provide a normative contribution by establishing operational parameters, including causality, the materiality of the loss, the status of restitution, and the nature of violations of the General Principles of Good Governance, to affirm that administrative review and restitution must precede criminal proceedings. This study recommends regulatory harmonization between state financial laws and government administration laws to ensure that criminal sanctions are applied proportionally as an ultimum remedium, thereby maintaining legal certainty and the rationality of anti-corruption efforts.

Descriptive analysis of rejected pathology samples and the associated carbon footprint and financial cost
abstract: Abstract Objectives Pathology testing underpins almost all patient pathways and clinical laboratories in England process over 1.4 billion tests annually. Rejected samples provide no clinical benefit, while also costing the NHS financially and having a similar environmental impact as those samples which are accepted. The aim of this service evaluation was to analyse the number of rejected samples at Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (LTHTr) to quantify the financial and environmental impact, and to identify potential areas for improvement. Methods Data from Blood Sciences, Microbiology, and Blood Transfusion were analysed over a 12-month period. The variables analysed were; monthly rejection rates, location rejection rates, and causes of rejection. Results During the study period, of the 1,724,628 Pathology samples received, 0.98 % (n=16,911) were rejected. Blood Sciences and Microbiology had a combined rejection rate of 0.87 % (n=14,615), while Blood Transfusion had a higher rate of 5.1 % (n=2,296). Common rejection causes included insufficient samples (Blood Sciences) and labelling errors (Blood Transfusion and Microbiology). Paediatric areas showed the highest rejection rates. The sample rejection has an estimated to cost over £5,000 and approximately 1,287 kg of CO 2 equivalent (CO 2 e) emissions, equivalent to driving around 8,956 km in an average petrol ca…

title: Sexual orientation, financial risk attitudes and financial literacy
abstract: Purpose Labour market disparities by sexual orientation are well documented, yet little is known about whether sexual-orientation groups differ in financial risk attitudes and financial literacy, two pathways that may contribute to these disparities. We contribute to this strand of the literature using a Canadian sample. Design/methodology/approach This paper used an incentivized investment-game pilot focused on risk attitudes (N = 240) and a larger survey-based study covering both risk attitudes and financial literacy (N = 718). Multivariate regression analysis is employed. Financial risk is distinguished from “social risk” by controlling for the degree of outness of the respondents to others, a proxy for non-financial social risk-taking. Findings Gay and lesbian respondents exhibit greater financial risk aversion than comparable heterosexual respondents, while bisexual men display significantly greater willingness to take financial risks. The analysis further reveals substantial disparities in financial literacy. Gay, lesbian and bisexual female respondents perform significantly worse on a credit literacy question and self-report lower levels of financial literacy. Originality/value This is the first Canadian study assessing sexual orientation-related gaps in risk attitudes and financial literacy.

title: Beyond firm size: green accounting as a driver of financial performance in Indonesian healthcare firms
abstract: Purpose: This work explores the effect of firm size and green accounting on financial performance, using Return on Assets (ROA) and Return on Equity (ROE) as indicators, for healthcare companies registered on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) from 2021 to 2024. Methodology/approach: This study applies a quantitative research design, utilizing panel data regression for analysis. The data come from secondary sources, specifically annual reports and sustainability reports of healthcare companies registered on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). Purposive sampling was applied to select the sample, which produced 17 companies and 68 firm-year observations. Findings: This research reveals that firm size and green accounting jointly affect ROA and ROE in a significant manner. In partial testing, green accounting produces a significant effect on both ROA and ROE, yet firm size fails to yield any significant effect. Practical and Theoritical contribution/Originality: Limited empirical attention has been given to the simultaneous impact of firm size and green accounting on financial performance in healthcare companies listed on the IDX. This study tackles that limitation by presenting new empirical evidence and enriching the existing literature, consequently broadening the insight into factors that shape corporate financial performance in the healthcare field. title: Public Payment Ecosystem, QRIS Usage Behavior, and Financial Satisfaction Among Manokwari MSMEs
abstract: Uniform national payment standardization by Bank Indonesia has not ensured symmetric utilization across peripheral regions, while Eastern Indonesian evidence remains scarce. This study examined how social influence, facilitating conditions, digital financial literacy, and mental accounting associate with Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard usage and financial satisfaction. Survey data from 180 active micro, small, and medium enterprises in Manokwari Regency were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Social influence and facilitating conditions positively associate with usage behavior at comparable magnitudes, where hardware access exceeds technical support, while usage strongly aligns with financial satisfaction and channels significant indirect effects. Conversely, digital financial literacy exhibits no significant direct association, with fraud awareness scoring lowest, and mental accounting moderation remains statistically undetected despite its notable direct contribution to usage variance. Unlike metropolitan studies, this research links public payment infrastructure with behavioral economics, guiding policymakers toward technical support, merchant networks, and fraud safeguards.

Design-oriented assessment of a floating breakwater with a submerged bottom ring
abstract: This study investigates a compact submerged bottom ring as a passive under-body appendage for enhancing the wave-attenuation performance of a box-type floating breakwater. Unlike porous or multi-body concepts, the ring preserves structural simplicity while modifying the energetic oscillatory flow beneath the hull to promote recirculation, shear-layer development, and near-field viscous dissipation. Three-dimensional wave–structure interaction is simulated using an incompressible Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) model coupled with a volume-of-fluid (VOF) formulation under regular waves. A RANS–VOF model benchmarked against published experimental data is employed in a staged parametric assessment under the reference condition of a prescribed inlet wave height of 2.0 m and T = 5 s, followed by a wave-period-dependent evaluation of the selected configuration. The submerged ring reduces the transmission coefficient KT in a wave-period-dependent manner, with improvements in wave attenuation of approximately 10%–50% over the investigated conditions and the largest reduction occurring near the reference condition. The improved performance is associated with under-body flow restructuring, shear-layer development, recirculation, and enhanced near-field viscous dissipation. Overall, a suitably proportioned submerged bottom ring can provide substantial wave-transmission reduction wit…

title: Integrating Design Thinking into Science Education: Mapping the Intellectual Structure, Research Trends, and Emerging Fronts (2016-2026)
abstract: Design thinking has gained increasing attention in science education as an approach to engaging students in complex, authentic problems and developing creative, human-centered, and practical solutions. This study examines the intellectual structure, publication trends, and research directions of design thinking in science education from 2016 to 2026. A bibliometric analysis was conducted on 35 Scopus-indexed documents from 31 sources using Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer. The analyses covered publication trends, citation-based networks, and thematic mapping. The findings indicate growing scholarly interest in the field, with an annual publication growth rate of 34.95%. The citation network reveals connections among the conceptual foundations of design thinking, its educational applications, and methodological literature. Meanwhile, thematic mapping highlights interconnected research themes, ranging from the application of design thinking in science and STEM education to the development of students' cognitive and interdisciplinary competencies. Overall, this study demonstrates the interdisciplinary nature of design thinking research in science education and highlights opportunities to strengthen its integration with STEM-oriented pedagogies, authentic problem solving, and student-centered learning. Keywords: bibliometric analysis, design thinking, science education.

abstract: ABSTRACT The development of three-dimensional (3D) technology in the fashion industry requires vocational fashion education to connect digital design comprehension with pattern construction skills. However, limited computer facilities may restrict students’ opportunities to create digital patterns independently, making it necessary to examine their ability to translate digital pattern information into physical forms. This study aimed to analyze students’ abilities to convert 3D digital fashion designs and patterns into ready-to-use physical patterns. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed, involving 37 students enrolled in a garment pattern-making course. Data were collected through performance tests, observations, and documentation, then analyzed using descriptive statistics. During the learning process, students examined digital designs and patterns provided by the lecturer, interpreted pattern information, identified pattern components, transferred the patterns onto paper, and checked the resulting constructions. The findings revealed a weighted mean score of 89.80, indicating a very good level of performance. Digital pattern interpretation achieved the highest score at 93.24%, whereas measurement and construction accuracy recorded the lowest score at 86.15%. Problems And Reform in The Imposition of Criminal Fines on State-Owned Enterprises in Corruption Offenses
abstract: State-Owned Enterprises often have legal problems when subject to corporate sanctions in the form of fines by the directors or their ranks who commit criminal acts so that it interferes with public services and has the potential to reduce company assets due to incurring fines. The purpose of this research is to find the concept of formulating a criminal model that is in line with Indonesian criminal law reform, especially regarding the application of corporate sanctions within the scope of State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs). The methods used normative law with a legislative, conceptual, comparative, and interview approach. The results of the research show that the criminal penalty of fines against corporations has a legal basis in Law Number 1 of 2026 concerning Criminal Adjustment. However, the punishment depends on the aspect of organizational error, the result obtained is a differential-integrative based criminal model by limiting the difference between personal and institutional responsibility combined with limited fines with asset recovery. Conclusion that can be drawn, the imposition of sanctions against SOE corporate entities must be imposed proportionately and only if corporate wrongdoing has been proven, while the directors or their staff remain personally responsible.

abstract: Climate change is a global challenge affecting various aspects of life, including household waste management. Purwomartani Village, Sleman, Yogyakarta faces problems of increasing food waste volume that has not been properly managed, lack of waste segregation education, and suboptimal TPS3R implementation. This community service program aims to increase public awareness in reducing food waste, strengthen local capacity for sustainable waste management, and support Purwomartani Village towards an Integrated Proklim Village. The implementation method includes three stages: sustainable food planning literacy, action and good practices of household waste management, and advocacy of the Climate Village Program (PROKLIM). Activities were conducted on August 28-29, 2024 at the TPS3R Sorogenen Hangar and 10 points of residents' houses, involving 44 participants on the first day and 25 participants on the second day. Results showed increased public understanding of efficient food planning, installation of 10 biopore infiltration holes and 1 set of compartment trash bins, as well as the formation of PROKLIM organizational structure and WhatsApp coordination group. This program successfully initiated sustainability through planning for PROKLIM registration to the National Registry System in 2025. Freshwater Landlocked Chinook Salmon Behaviour and Use of Habitat Diverge from Source Populations in the Pacific Region—Cross-System Science for a Changing Native Range
abstract: Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha) are a keystone species for ecological stability with substantial socio-economic benefits across the Northern Hemisphere. In their native Pacific range, they serve as a major source of marine-derived nutrients for marine-connected fluvial ecosystems, support multi-billion dollar commercial and recreational industries (Quinn 2005), and are an iconic species in Indigenous cultures (Nesbitt and Moore 2016). Chinook salmon have assumed a similar role in the Laurentian Great Lakes following their successful introduction in the late 1960s (Crawford and Muir 2008) as a top predator to control non-native alewife (Alosa pseudoharengus) (Tanner and Tody 2002) and to support a multi-billion dollar recreational fishery (Melstrom and Lupi 2013; The Great Lakes Valuation Report 2022). This dual economic and ecological importance makes them a focal point in both regions for management decisions, especially given the current declines of some of the species stocks in the Pacific region (Ford 2022; Atlas et al. 2023).

A comparative review of implemented explainable AI techniques in multi-agent systems
abstract: Abstract Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has largely been developed for single-model settings, where the target of explanation is one prediction, model, or decision process. This assumption is limited in multi-agent systems (MAS), where outcomes can depend on coordination, communication, decentralised information, and interaction over time. This paper presents a structured comparative review restricted to studies of implemented and empirically evaluated XAI methods in MAS. Here, implemented means that a concrete explanation mechanism is applied in a MAS and tested. The search covered cooperative, competitive, mixed-motive, planning, ad-hoc teamwork, and LLM-based MAS. The included evidence contains work in cooperative and decentralised MARL, as well as planning-oriented and LLM-based MAS work. The review compares studies by explanatory target (the aspect of the system being explained) and stakeholder orientation (who the explanations are for). Current methods can identify influential agents, summarise policies, interpret local decisions, and diagnose failures, however they struggle to explain how interaction and communication produce a system-level outcome. Future work should therefore develop more interaction-aware, empirically grounded, and human-usable explanations for MAS.

title: Structure of multi-$$\Lambda $$ hypernuclei with a Skyrme-type $$\Lambda \Lambda $$ interaction guided by double-$$\Lambda $$ hypernuclear and neutron-star constraints
Multi-beam FLASH-RT preserves skin sparing and reveals novel tissue oxygen dynamics in a murine model
abstract: Abstract Objective . The goal of this project was to investigate whether the FLASH skin-sparing effect is preserved across multi-beam ultra-high-dose-rate (UHDR) deliveries and to characterize the accompanying in vivo tissue oxygen dynamics near a 5-second total treatment window previously shown to maintain sparing. Approach. Mice were irradiated at three dose levels (23.6, 25.2, and 25.9 Gy) across five experimental groups: single-beam UHDR, two-beam UHDR, six-beam UHDR, twelve-beam UHDR, and conventional dose rate (CDR). To evaluate normal tissue toxicity, a skin damage cohort was monitored photographically for four weeks post-irradiation, with acute reactions evaluated by a trained observer. In a separate cohort, real-time tissue oxygenation ( p O 2 ) was tracked via a fiber-optic phosphorometer using the phosphorescent probe Oxyphor PtG4 to evaluate physiological kinetics independently of the longitudinal toxicity study. Main results. The FLASH skin-sparing effect was statistically indistinguishable for all experimentally tested UHDR configurations at the 23.6 Gy and 25.2 Gy dose levels. Mixed-effects regression analysis demonstrated that all four UHDR groups developed significantly lower skin toxicity scores compared to the CDR group ( p < 0.05). At the highest dose level (25.9 Gy), no significant differences were observed among any radiation groups, which was attributed t…

title: Persistent right ventricular dysfunction and hemodynamic evolution predict in-hospital deterioration in intermediate-high- and high-risk pulmonary embolism
Comparative analysis of domestic and foreign customer relationship management systems. Analysis of market capacity and prospects for the development of CRM systems in Russia
abstract: Subject. This article focuses on the demand for customer relationship management systems as a basic means of increasing the efficiency of wholesale trade enterprises. Objectives. The study aims to identify the possibility of these systems' application, the main advantages and disadvantages. Methods. For the study, we used the methods of classification, comparative analysis and induction. Results. The article shows that the existing CRM systems do not meet the current needs of the wholesale trade enterprises. Conclusions. It is necessary to create a new type of systems that take into account the main features of business processes within the framework of wholesale trade enterprises.

title: Destigmatisation effects of reading poetry written by people with an invisible chronic illness: possibilities for anti-stigma social marketing campaigns
abstract: Purpose The purpose of the research was to examine the effects on a sample of members of the public of their reading poems written by people with chronic illnesses in relation to the former’s stigmatising attitudes towards people with chronic illnesses. This is an important topic considering the large number of individuals suffering chronic illnesses worldwide and the large amounts of stigmatisation they often face. Design/methodology/approach A model to explain stigmatising attitudes towards people with chronic illnesses was constructed to predict an individual’s aesthetic emotions aroused by reading three poems plus the consequences for stigmatising attitudes. The model was estimated using the method of partial least squares. Findings Readers of the poems exhibited significantly more favourable attitudes regarding people with chronic illnesses compared to a control group of individuals who had not read the poems. Age and income categories and religiosity did not exert significant influences on readers’ degrees of stigmatising attitudes. Other variables had significant effects. Originality/value The core argument of the study offers an alternative to information-based government and charity anti-stigma campaigns. Outcomes to the investigation will be of value to healthcare and social marketing professionals responsible for devising anti-stigma communications, involving chronic…

title: A Review of the Impact of High-Frequency Trading on Stock Market Quality: Perspectives on Liquidity, Volatility, and Price Discovery
abstract: High-frequency trading is a new phenomenon resulting from the integration of technology, finance, and the stock market. How to understand the impact of high-frequency trading on the quality of the stock market is a common concern of the academic community and regulatory authorities. Based on clarifying the concept of high-frequency trading and its strategy types, this paper systematically reviews domestic and foreign literature from the perspectives of liquidity, volatility, and price discovery. The study finds that under normal market conditions, high-frequency trading can narrow the price gap, provide liquidity, smooth out noise fluctuations, and accelerate the integration of information into prices, thereby improving market quality. However, in extreme market conditions, its liquidity supply rapidly retreats and presents the characteristic of “illusory liquidity”, and the homogeneity of strategies and crowded trading may amplify fluctuations. The speed advantage leading to reverse selection and short-term trading orientation will also weaken the absorption of price by fundamental information. High-frequency traders are not a homogeneous group, and their impact direction depends on the strategy type and institutional environment. The long-term impact of high-frequency trading on the quality of China's stock market still needs further research.

title: Coupling and coordination of food security and agricultural economic resilience in China: early warning and obstacle diagnosis under climate–market shocks
abstract: Climate risks and market volatility reinforce each other, creating a dual challenge for China's food security and for the stable operation of its agricultural economy. Using entropy-weighted TOPSIS coupled coordination analysis, a GM(1,1)-Markov chain and an obstacle degree model, this study systematically examines the evolution, risk landscape, and differentiated bottlenecks of resilience in food and agriculture. The two types of resilience rise in a fluctuating manner, but with notable regional differences: the eastern region leads, the central and western regions lag, and the northeastern region sits in between while remaining sensitive to changes. The coupling coordination index has moved from imbalance to basic coordination, showing a pattern of “high in the east, low in the west, with a steady gradient.” Systemic synergy has grown; however, the western region remains the weak link. Trend forecasts indicate that the national coupling coordination level will remain in the basic coordination range through 2029, approaching but not yet reaching the 0.50 moderate-coordination threshold; a four-level risk early warning system can identify cross-cycle risk changes. Constraints on urban-unit agricultural employment, rather than technological investment, have become the main constraint on the agricultural economy, while the rural electricity level has become the primary bottleneck…

title: Regional (local) consumer market in the context of digitalization: Theoretical and methodological foundations of research
abstract: Subject. The functioning of the regional (local) consumer market in the context of digitalization and the emergence of the network economy. Objectives. Systematizing and developing conceptual approaches to studying various processes happening in the consumer market. Rethinking classic theories of exchange organization in relation to a reality where physical and virtual spaces interact. Methods. Systems and comparative analyses, conceptual modeling. Results. An author's definition of the regional (local) consumer market has been formulated, taking into account the emergence of electronic platforms and online communities. The functions of the regional (local) consumer market implemented in the digital age have been systematized. Conclusions. Traditional theories of regional economics need to be supplemented with concepts from the digital and network economy. The functional model proposed by the authors allows for a more accurate description and prediction of changes in the structure, the composition of participants, and the way regional consumer markets operate.

title: When Brands Matter Less: Perceived Product Similarity and Brand Switching Intention through Brand Relevance in Makassar's Grab-and-Go Coffee Market
abstract: Affordable grab-and-go coffee outlets in Makassar, Indonesia, increasingly sell comparable drinks at nearly identical prices, raising the question of whether brands still matter when products look alike. This study examines whether perceived product similarity increases brand switching intention by reducing brand relevance, that is, the importance consumers attach to brands when choosing within a category. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 250 consumers domiciled in Makassar who had a usual coffee brand and had tried at least one alternative in the same price range. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling with 10,000 bootstrap subsamples. Perceived product similarity reduced brand relevance, and lower brand relevance increased brand switching intention. The resulting indirect effect of similarity on switching intention through brand relevance was positive and significant, whereas the direct effect was small and only marginally significant. The findings were robust to controlling for variety seeking, which influenced switching intention independently. The study shows that product similarity encourages switching mainly by weakening the role of the brand in consumers' choices rather than by acting on switching directly, which helps explain why earlier studies of brand parity and loyalty have reported inconsistent results. For small…
venue: Journal of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

title: Research on Multi-value Market Realization Mechanism of Green Hydrogen, Ammonia and Alcohol
abstract: This study explores the collaborative mechanism of electricity, green certificate, and carbon markets to address the value realization challenges of renewable hydrogen and green ammonia/alcohol production. By systematically reviewing the development status of China's electricity-green certificate-carbon market system, this paper demonstrates the feasibility of green hydrogen, ammonia, and alcohol participating in multiple markets, analyzes core trading rules, and proposes feasible pathways and cost allocation mechanisms. Results indicate that grid-connected renewable hydrogen projects are highly compatible with electricity market rules in terms of energy value, flexibility value, and capacity reliability. The CCER methodology for renewable hydrogen released in December 2025 provides a methodological foundation for carbon market participation. The green certificate market can facilitate approximately 2%-5% of hydrogen production cost recovery. These findings provide theoretical support and practical guidance for constructing a multi-value market system for hydrogen, ammonia, and alcohol, contributing to energy transition and the achievement of "dual carbon" goals.
venue: Advances in Computer and Materials Scienc Research

title: Investigating the impact of the Joint Market`s on the Dimensions of the Local Economy (Case Study:The Ishkashim Joint Market between Afghanistan and Tajikistan)
abstract: A joint market plays a key role in the economic development of border regions by facilitating trade exchange, reducing costs, creating employment, and attracting investment. The present study was conducted with the aim of investigating the role of the Ishkashim joint market on the local economy, particularly on the income and welfare of the region's residents. The research method was descriptive-analytical and survey-based. Data were collected using a questionnaire distributed to 100 traders, sellers, and buyers who were selected through simple random sampling. The reliability of the questionnaire was confirmed using Cronbach's alpha (0.803). Due to the non-normal distribution of the data, non-parametric tests including Spearman's correlation coefficient and regression analysis were employed. The findings indicated a positive and significant relationship between the joint market and the creation of new employment opportunities (r=0.390, Sig=0.000). Furthermore, the joint market had a positive and significant impact on trade growth and investment (r=0.371, Sig=0.000). Additionally, a positive and significant relationship was observed between the joint market and the improvement of welfare and regional development (r=0.350, Sig=0.000). The results of multiple regression showed that the dimensions of employment, investment, and regional welfare collectively explained 36.1% of the …

title: Guest editorial: What comes after research? Exploring how innovation outcomes can generate real impact for practice, market and society
Serviced Residential Plots in Vietnam and Indonesia: A Functional Comparison of Market-Access Gates
abstract: Developers in Vietnam and Indonesia offer serviced plots before houses exist, so the law must decide when such a plot may enter the consumer market and who bears the risk until a house is built. Vietnam treats land-use rights with technical infrastructure as a tradable object, released only after title, location, infrastructure, disclosure and administrative verification are satisfied. Indonesia defines the kaveling tanah matang (mature, ready-to-build plot) within the planning structure of the Kasiba and Lisiba (ready-to-build areas and environments) and prohibits a Lisiba builder from selling plots without houses, subject to a narrow low-income exception. Using doctrinal and functional comparative analysis across eleven variables, drawn from the market-entry conditions, controls and consequences in the two statutes rather than from theory, this article argues that each system exhibits a product–gate mismatch in opposite forms: the gate controlling market entry is not calibrated to the product sold. Vietnam verifies market entry rigorously but regulates pre-registration payments and post-transfer build-out far less precisely, and its pathway has contracted through administrative reorganisation and urban reclassification without amendment of the Law on Real Estate Business. Indonesia steers sales towards houses, keeping completion with the developer, but its prohibition depends…
venue: Journal of Private and Commercial Law

title: Complementarity of education and risk tolerance in the Russian labor market
abstract: Subject. Education and risk tolerance as complementary factors affecting wages. Objectives. Empirical assessment of the modifying effect of risk-taking on educational returns, as well as identification of the heterogeneity of this effect for different professional groups. Methods. The empirical base of the study is based on data from the 32nd wave of Russian monitoring of the economic situation and public health. Regression analysis methods were used, including the evaluation of Mintzer equations with variables of the interaction of education and risk appetite, as well as logit models for estimating the probability of unemployment and job satisfaction. Results. Calculations have shown that the return on higher and secondary vocational education increases with increasing risk tolerance. The greatest effect of the interaction between the profile of education and risk tolerance is observed among graduates of programs in the field of information technology, economics and law specialties. At the same time, a negative relationship was found between risk-taking and job satisfaction. The results obtained can be used in the development and updating of educational programs, especially in the field of information technology, economics and law, in terms of developing risk management skills, in the practice of HR services to assess the potential of employees, as well as in government policy…

title: Spillovers between global sustainability and the fintech market: evidence from quantiles and frequency bands
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to investigate how fintech market dynamics transmit to global sustainability by examining whether return spillovers vary across market states, investor horizons and time. Design/methodology/approach The authors apply QVAR and TVP-VAR frequency-domain connectedness frameworks to measure return spillovers between a fintech index (FTI) and two sustainability proxies: Solactive’s Global Sustainability Leaders Performance Index (SGSI) and Nasdaq’s Future Global Sustainability Leaders Index (NGSI). This approach allows us to capture tail relationships, dynamic interactions and short-, medium- and long-run spillover structures. Findings Fintech-to-sustainability spillovers are predominantly short-term and intensify during major stress episodes. This pattern may reflect the still-developing nature of both fintech markets and sustainability initiatives, as well as the insufficient integration of these two markets under current regulatory frameworks. The Solactive index records more distinct fintech–sustainability connectedness than the Nasdaq counterpart, which behaves more similarly to the DJIA benchmark. Practical implications Policymakers should promote more stable and long-term fintech–sustainability integration, as spillovers are mainly short-term and event-driven. Investors should incorporate tail-related and time-varying spillovers into portfolio and hedgi…

title: Force-corrected framework for disc cutter wear and service life in abrasive rock
abstract: Reliable prediction of disc cutter wear is essential for replacement scheduling, advance-rate stability, and risk control in abrasive-rock shield tunnel-boring machines (TBM) tunnelling. Existing approaches often combine wear laws with cutter-force models without separately resolving equilibrium adjacent to the cutter flank. This study develops a force-corrected analytical framework for constant cross-section disc cutters integrating force correction, wear calculation, service-life estimation, and engineering comparison. The classical pressure resultant from the Colorado School of Mines model is retained as the baseline load, while a cutter-flank correction is derived from equilibrium of an idealised lateral shear fragment within the same cutter-induced fragmentation process. The corrected vertical force is linked through a lumped effective coefficient to a Rabinowicz-based cutter-scale wear relation and cutterhead kinematics. Comparison with linear cutting machine data gives mean errors of 13.3% for vertical force and 15.2% for rolling force; the 774 m engineering comparison gives mean errors of 12.7% for radial wear and 13.9% for service life under a common nominal effective coefficient. Sensitivity analysis within the investigated range identifies cutter-edge strength as the most influential, followed by edge width and cutter radius. The framework supports cutter design comp…

Research on students’ cognition and acceptance of health service-oriented course content: based on the investigation of self-efficacy in structure-based rational drug use and professional identity
Pengaruh Kualitas Layanan dan Sarana Prasarana, Patients Waiting Time, dan Harga Terhadap Revisit Health Service Dengan Patients Satisfaction Sebagai Variabel Mediasi
abstract: Increasing competition among hospitals requires healthcare institutions to continuously improve service quality in order to enhance patient satisfaction and encourage revisit intention. This study aims to examine the effects of service quality, infrastructure quality, patient waiting time, and price on revisit intention, with patient satisfaction serving as a mediating variable at Prof. Dr. I. G. N. G. Ngoerah General Hospital. This research employed a quantitative approach with a causal associative design. The sample consisted of 230 executive patients selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). The results indicate that service quality, infrastructure quality, and patient waiting time have a positive and significant effect on patient satisfaction, whereas price does not significantly affect patient satisfaction. Furthermore, infrastructure quality, patient waiting time, price, and patient satisfaction have a positive and significant effect on revisit intention, while service quality does not have a significant direct effect on revisit intention. The findings also reveal that patient satisfaction mediates the effects of service quality, infrastructure quality, and patient waiting time on revisit intention. However, patient satisfaction does not mediate…

title: People-centred metrics to improve health service access and reduce travel-time toxicity
abstract: Abstract Geographic accessibility to health services, the ease with which people can reach appropriate care through a transport network, is a matter of quality, equity and the right to health. Yet conventional measures often reduce accessibility to distance or a single journey time, overlooking the burden on patients, families and caregivers, particularly when services are scarce, time-sensitive or repeatedly needed. This matters when health systems are rebuilt or strengthened, as decisions can perpetuate or reduce geographic inequities. Measures should reflect the journeys people actually make. Cumulative travel time can combine outward and return journeys, visit frequency and treatment duration, accounting for traffic and transport modes where appropriate. Developing meaningful measures requires input from patients, caregivers, communities, providers, policymakers, planners and researchers. Population-centred indicators can complement individual estimates of cumulative travel burden and its financial and caregiving costs, providing a common framework for sectors to compare options and coordinate decisions around population needs. We use ‘travel-time toxicity’ to describe the travel component of the time and resources that health care takes from patients’ and caregivers’ lives. Research should identify which burdens matter most, how they are distributed, and whether service or…

title: Formulating Green Data Center Siting Criteria with Stakeholders in Indonesia
abstract: Stakeholders in Indonesia’s data center sector needed a shared framework for screening sites against energy, environmental, infrastructure, and policy considerations. This community engagement initiative developed siting criteria through a literature review, a focus group with 25 participants from government, industry, and academia, a worked example, and public dissemination. Before the activity, the team had a draft list of variables. After the activity, four criteria were available for use in screening: access to clean and renewable energy, climate and physical environment, physical and digital connectivity, and regulatory and socioeconomic support. In a consortium assessment of five candidate regions, the North Sumatra highlands and IKN Nusantara ranked highest under the baseline weights, scoring 7.45 and 7.30, respectively. A two-percentage-point shift from climate suitability to low disaster risk reversed their order. The team shared the framework at the Indonesia International Sustainability Forum (ISF) 2025. The documented outcomes were a common set of criteria and an example of how to apply them. Changes in participant knowledge or institutional uptake were outside the scope of the evaluation.

title: Responsiveness and service demand of a novel consultation service for hoarding and domestic squalor in a metropolitan health district in Sydney, Australia
abstract: Objective To describe the implementation of a novel Hoarding and Squalor Consultancy Service (HSCS) in Sydney, Australia, and to report consultation characteristics and performance indicators. Method The HSCS provides advice and support to professionals and carers of people with hoarding and squalor issues. This observational study involved retrospective analysis of health service data. Service responsiveness was measured by the time between consultation request and consultation. Service demand was measured by the number of consultation requests received per month. Results The HSCS received 150 consultation requests between May 2021 and February 2025, with a significant upward trend in requests received per month over this period (Kendall's Tau=0.414, p = 0.0001). Most consultations were requested by community services ( n = 128, 85%). The median time to respond to requests was seven days (mean 12 days with 95% confidence interval 9-14 days). Conclusions The HSCS is a responsive and accessible service. Future research should evaluate the effectiveness and acceptability of a consultation model to address hoarding and squalor.

title: Organizational resilience and sustainable purchase behavior: a multi-level analysis of employee–consumer engagement with environmental initiatives
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the mechanisms through which organizational resilience capabilities generate sustainable consumer behavior in service organizations, along with integrating organizational and consumer perspectives within a multi-level framework. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on multi-source and time-lagged data collected from 52 hotels, 847 employees, and 1,203 consumers, we tested a moderated sequential-mediation model. The model specifies organizational resilience as the antecedent, employee engagement and consumer engagement as sequential mediators, and sustainable purchase behavior as the outcome. Consumer green values, price sensitivity, and subjective norms are tested as moderators of the indirect pathways. Findings Organizational resilience influences sustainable purchase behavior through a sequential engagement cascade: resilience → Employee engagement → Consumer engagement → Sustainable behavior. This cross-level mechanism operates contingently on individual consumer characteristics. Specifically, consumer green values and subjective norms amplify the engagement cascade, while price sensitivity attenuates it. The findings demonstrate that organizational capabilities do not automatically translate into sustainability outcomes; rather, their effectiveness depends on psychological interpretation and behavioral expression within specific social context…

title: Reconfiguring the Marketing Mix: The Effects of Core Marketing Mix, Customer Interface, and Service Experience on Purchase Decisions through Customer Satisfaction
abstract: Changes in customer behavior require motorcycle repair shops to manage their marketing strategies and customer experiences more strategically. This study examines the effects of Core Marketing Mix, Customer Interface, and Service Experience on Customer Satisfaction and Purchase Decision, as well as the mediating role of Customer Satisfaction. A quantitative approach was applied to data from 200 motorcycle repair shop customers in Malang Regency and Malang Municipality, Indonesia, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. The results show that Core Marketing Mix (β = 0.294, p = 0.002) and Customer Interface (β = 0.288, p = 0.025) positively affect Customer Satisfaction, whereas Service Experience has no significant effect (β = −0.006, p = 0.956). All three constructs positively affect Purchase Decision, with Core Marketing Mix showing the strongest effect (β = 0.386, p < 0.001). Customer Satisfaction also positively affects Purchase Decision (β = 0.320, p < 0.001) and mediates the effects of Core Marketing Mix and Customer Interface, but not Service Experience. This study contributes by grouping the 7P marketing elements into three analytical constructs and demonstrating that Customer Satisfaction acts as a selective rath…

title: The role of age in urban park cultural ecosystem service supply–demand matching: evidence from Chengdu, China
Ophthalmology referral patterns at a tertiary service before, during and after COVID-19
abstract: Background: The Vula Medical digital referral platform connected South African primary-care providers with specialist services. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic disrupted routine healthcare delivery and may have altered referral patterns. This study examined changes in ophthalmology referrals to a tertiary South African hospital submitted via Vula Medical across pre-pandemic, pandemic and post-pandemic periods. Methods: Retrospective comparative descriptive analysis of anonymised referral data for July 2018, July 2020 and July 2025. All ophthalmology referrals submitted via Vula Medical to Tygerberg Hospital were included, excluding duplicate, test or incomplete entries. Referral volume, urgency, diagnostic category and specialist response were compared across periods. Results: A total of 1498 referrals were analysed. Referral volume fell by 46.5% in July 2020 compared with July 2018 and rose to 107% above baseline by July 2025. Urgent referrals increased from 34.0% (2018) to 49.1% (2020) and declined to 21.7% (2025). Cataract referrals fell to 5.4% during the pandemic and became the leading reason for referral (21.5%) by 2025. Advice-only management rose to 42.8% during the pandemic. Conclusion: COVID-19 was associated with substantial changes in ophthalmology referral patterns. The digital referral platform facilitated remote triage during disruption and struc…

title: Assessing digital thinking competence of pre-service primary school teachers: a pilot study in Kazakhstan
abstract: The rapid digital transformation of education requires teachers to move beyond the routine use of digital tools and to develop a broader set of competencies that includes critical evaluation of information, interpretation of data, stepwise problem solving, responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI), and safe participation in digital environments. This pilot study aimed to assess the initial level of digital thinking competence among pre-service primary school teachers in Kazakhstan and to describe the preliminary psychometric properties of an author-developed diagnostic instrument designed for this purpose. In this study, digital thinking is conceptualized as a broader pedagogical construct than computational thinking; computational thinking is treated as one of its technical-logical components rather than as an equivalent concept. A mixed-methods design was employed with 69 third- and fourth-year students enrolled in the 6B01301 “Pedagogy and Methodology of Primary Education” program at K. Zhubanov Aktobe Regional University. The dataset was reconstructed and verified against the original survey materials, and all 69 response patterns were confirmed as unique. The core Likert block consisted of six items (Q1–Q5 and Q18). Internal-consistency analysis yielded Cronbach's alpha = 0.691, standardized alpha = 0.702, McDonald's omega = 0.715, a 95% confidence interval for alpha…

Analisis Komparatif Sistem Inspeksi Konvensional dan Tyre Pressure Monitoring System terhadap Service Life dan Efisiensi Operasional Tyre 24.00R35 pada Off-Highway Truck
abstract: Pengendalian tekanan tyre merupakan salah satu faktor utama yang memengaruhi umur pakai tyre, efisiensi biaya operasional, dan keandalan armada Off-Highway Truck (OHT) pada kegiatan pertambangan terbuka. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis perbandingan performa operasional tyre ukuran 24.00R35 pada Off-Highway Truck Caterpillar 773D, 773E, dan 775F antara periode inspeksi tyre konvensional dan periode implementasi Tyre Pressure Monitoring System di PT Cipta Kridatama site DMP, Sumatera Selatan. Empat parameter yang dievaluasi meliputi persentase kejadian low tyre pressure, service life, tread utilization rate (TUR), dan cost per hour (CPH). Data operasional dikumpulkan dari 35 unit alat angkut dengan 105 event tyre scrap pada tahun 2024 (konvensional) dan 91 event pada tahun 2025 (TPMS). Uji normalitas Kolmogorov-Smirnov menunjukkan distribusi data yang tidak normal pada sebagian besar variabel sehingga analisis dilakukan menggunakan Mann-Whitney U Test dengan Rank-Biserial Correlation sebagai ukuran effect size. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan perbedaan yang signifikan pada seluruh variabel (p < 0,001). Periode TPMS menunjukkan penurunan rata-rata low tyre pressure sebesar 6 poin persentase atau 86,7%, peningkatan rata-rata service life sebesar 1.312 jam atau 15,6%, peningkatan rata-rata tread utilization rate sebesar 9,9 poin persentase atau 15,9%, serta penurunan median …

title: PP041: Frequency of Early Onset Seizures in Acute Stroke Patients
abstract: Abstract Introduction Acute stroke is characterized by the sudden onset of focal neurological deficits resulting from cerebrovascular disease. According to the TOAST classification, ischemic stroke has five major subtypes: large-artery atherosclerosis, small-vessel occlusion, cardioembolism, stroke of other determined etiology, and stroke of undetermined etiology. Early-onset seizures are neurological complications of acute stroke and are generally defined as seizures occurring within the first 7 days after stroke, although definitions extending to 14 days have also been used. This study aimed to determine the frequency of early- onset seizures among patients with acute stroke and identify associated factors. Methodology A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Medicine/Neurology at Akbar Niazi Teaching Hospital, Islamabad, from 10th January 2025 to 10th June 2026. A total of 300 patients were enrolled using non-probability consecutive sampling. The sample size was calculated using WHO sample size software, with a 95% confidence interval, a 2.5% margin of error, and an expected frequency of 5%. Results The mean age of the study participants was 54.7 ± 6.4 years, while the mean duration of stroke at presentation was 12.2 ± 4.6 hours. Males constituted 73.3% of the participants, whereas females accounted for 26.7%. Ischemic stroke was observed in 77.3% of patien…

title: Embodied mindfulness for sleep disturbance in psychotherapy: extending metacognitive models through sensorimotor regulation
abstract: Insomnia is increasingly understood as a disorder of insufficient de-arousal involving interacting cognitive-emotional and physiological processes. Mindfulness-based approaches may reduce insomnia by modifying attentional and metacognitive responses to wakefulness; however, prevailing theoretical accounts and therapeutic practices have predominantly examined mindfulness in formats involving relatively little overt movement, leaving the specific regulatory contributions of sustained movement–breath coordination and dynamically changing sensorimotor feedback comparatively underdeveloped. This hypothesis and theory paper proposes an Embodied Mindfulness Framework that extends established metacognitive accounts of insomnia by conceptualizing mindfulness as a dynamic brain–body process. Embodied mindfulness is defined as present-centered, nonjudgmental awareness cultivated through coordinated attention, breathing, posture, bodily sensation, and intentional movement, with Tai Chi presented as a representative therapeutic format. The framework proposes bodily awareness, intentional movement, and sensorimotor integration as interdependent processes through which embodied regulation is cultivated. At the mechanistic level, we hypothesize that autonomic flexibility, interoceptive reappraisal, and attentional anchoring operate reciprocally to alter how cognitive, emotional, and physiologi…

title: Regulation of RIPK1 in TNF-induced cell death
abstract: Abstract Tumor necrosis factor (TNF) is a pivotal cytokine that triggers diverse cellular outcomes, ranging from cell survival and pro-inflammatory gene expression to regulated cell death via apoptosis and necroptosis. Receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1) acts as a central molecular mediator in TNF signaling, operating both as a kinase-independent scaffold for survival and a kinase-dependent driver of cell death. The transition between these opposing outcomes is tightly orchestrated by post-translational modifications of RIPK1, including ubiquitination, phosphorylation, and proteolytic cleavage, which dictate RIPK1 recruitment, activation thresholds, and the assembly of survival- or death-inducing complexes. Aberrant TNF signaling toward cell death contributes to inflammatory pathologies, positioning RIPK1 and its regulatory networks as promising therapeutic targets. Here, we review the post-translational regulatory networks that control RIPK1 activity, delineate the molecular mechanisms underlying its activation in TNF-induced cell death, and discuss the therapeutic prospects of targeting RIPK1.

The effects of different exercise modalities on cardiac function and exercise capacity via Regulation of BDNF in patients with stable coronary artery disease: a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
abstract: Background Coronary artery disease affects patients' functional activities and quality of life and can even be life-threatening. Abnormal lipid metabolism, chronic inflammation, and psychosocial factors are major contributors to disease progression and adverse events in patients with coronary artery disease. Rehabilitation goals for patients with coronary artery disease include controlling risk factors, improving cardiac function and exercise capacity, and reducing mortality. Cardiac rehabilitation plays a vital role in achieving these goals. Exercise is an essential component of cardiac rehabilitation and plays an irreplaceable role for patients with coronary artery disease. Aerobic exercise is the most common form of exercise for patients with coronary artery disease, and its clinical efficacy is well established. In recent years, many scholars have recommended resistance exercise for cardiac rehabilitation. The efficacy of different exercise modalities for patients with coronary artery disease needs further clarification to guide optimal exercise prescription. In addition, our research group has previously proposed that brain-derived neurotrophic factor is an important mediator of exercise-mediated improvements in cardiovascular health. The role of brain-derived neurotrophic factor in improving cardiac function, exercise, and prognosis in patients with coronary artery diseas…

title: Pretreatment plasma RAS mutant allele frequency and progression-free survival after anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody rechallenge in tissue RAS/BRAF wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer: a retrospective exploratory analysis
abstract: Rechallenge with anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) has shown clinical activity as third-line or later therapy in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) harboring tissue RAS/BRAF wild-type (WT) status, particularly when circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) confirms RAS WT status shortly before rechallenge. However, the mutant allele frequency (MAF) threshold most strongly associated with clinical outcomes after rechallenge has not been established. We retrospectively analyzed patients with tissue RAS/BRAF WT mCRC treated between November 2017 and April 2024 who had previously received fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, and an anti-EGFR mAb, and who underwent plasma ctDNA testing with the OncoBEAM™ RAS CRC assay before anti-EGFR mAb rechallenge. An exploratory RAS MAF cutoff was derived using maximally selected log-rank statistics, and associations between MAF and progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models. Among 24 evaluable patients classified as ctDNA RAS WT by the codon-specific assay cutoffs, the objective response rate was 8% and the disease control rate was 67%. Median PFS and OS were 3.73 months (95% CI, 1.87–5.07) and 9.83 months (95% CI, 5.83–17.37), respectively. The data-derived MAF cutoff most strongly associated with PFS was 0.0191%. Patients with …

title: Angiotensin and systems thinking revisited: from blood pressure regulation to systemic health
abstract: The renin-angiotensin system (RAS) is conventionally described as an endocrine regulator of blood pressure, fluid balance, and electrolytes. This article reassesses eleven propositions reconstructed from a systems model developed in 2004–2013 that treated the RAS as a distributed, stress-responsive regulatory network involved in tissue integrity. A structured critical narrative synthesis integrates mechanistic, preclinical, translational, clinical, and explicit counterevidence. Three propositions are strongly supported; six are conditionally supported with revised dispositions; RAS inhibition in cancer remains mechanistically supported but clinically unresolved; and context dependence is retained as an interpretive principle rather than assigned an independent evidence-status category. The revised model treats RAS signalling as one coordinating influence within overlapping processes of mobilisation, clearance, reconstruction, maturation, and resolution. AT1R-, AT2R-, and angiotensin-(1-7)-associated effects are not assigned fixed beneficial or pathological signs; their consequences depend on tissue, cell state, compartment, response phase, receptor configuration, exposure, interacting systems, and physiological reserve. Persistent disturbance can prevent completion of tissue responses through failed clearance, maladaptive reconstruction, fibrosis, hypoxia, senescence, altered m…

title: Species-specific regulation of photoperiod and end-of-day far-red light on the growth and quality of vegetable crops
abstract: To investigate the effects of different supplemental far-red (FR) strategies on the growth and quality of vegetable crops, this study systematically compared the effects of photoperiod FR and end-of-day FR (EOD-FR) on the morphology, biomass, photosynthetic pigment, PSII fluorescence, and nutritional quality of six vegetable crop entries (lettuce, Chinese kale, green/red perilla, tomato, and cucumber). The regulatory effects of FR and EOD-FR exhibited high species and organ-specificity. In leafy vegetables, the FR treatment significantly promoted biomass accumulation and stem elongation in all species. In contrast, the EOD-FR treatment induced species-differential responses, effectively promoting biomass and canopy architecture in lettuce and Chinese kale, while solely significantly promoting leaf area in green and red perilla. FR generally reduced the total leaf chlorophyll content and altered energy partitioning by decreasing the effective quantum yield of PSII (Y(II)) and increasing the quantum yield of non-regulated energy dissipation (Y(NO)). The EOD-FR treatment selectively elevated the chlorophyll a/b ratio and enhanced regulated thermal dissipation (Y(NPQ)) in lettuce and Chinese kale. The FR treatment increased the soluble sugar content in all leafy vegetables, and also increased the contents of soluble protein, vitamin C, polyphenols and flavonoids in green and red pe…

A neuroeducational model for bias regulation in legal and forensic training
abstract: Expert legal-forensic judgment is assumed to be more reliable than lay judgment because professional training should filter out systematic biases; however, high-stakes legal decisions can shift with case features that are not legally relevant, including how affectively salient a case is. Training in law and forensic science lacks a model that links a defined class of bias to a pedagogical structure, a temporal design, and a calibration-based criterion of success. This article proposes the Neuroeducational Model for Bias Regulation in Legal-Forensic Training (NMBR-LFT), scoped to affect-salience-driven contextual bias and miscalibrated confidence when weighing evidence. The model integrates four components: a neurocognitive basis, treated as a provisional heuristic that contrasts deliberative control with affective-heuristic responses and identifies candidate regions without assuming them; a pedagogical mechanism of structured reflection on matched cases; a temporal component of practice distributed across a semester; and a metacognitive calibration layer that compares confidence with outcome and feeds back into the next cycle. We specify an operational protocol and derive five predictions, tested at the behavioral level in a five-arm design that crosses schedule (distributed or massed) with feedback (adaptive or fixed) at equal total dose and adds an active consider-the-opposit…

title: From Fragmented Regulation to Unified Model: The 1939 Statute and the 1979 Law on the Soviet Bar
abstract: The Regulations of 1939 and the Law of 1979 guided the evolution of the Soviet bar as a legal institution. Neither act could be regarded as codification instruments, yet they systematized legislation across Soviet republics. In this respect, these documents were instruments of functional legal unification that mirrored two distinct stages in the systematization of Soviet law. While the Stalinist period was associated with a rigid bureaucratic centralization, the so-called developed socialism model combined professional autonomy with latent state control. The article describes the institutional development of the Soviet bar, tracing the dynamics of its legal regulation to define the correlations between the norms of unifying legislation and the socio-political changes in the USSR. The Regulations of 1939 consolidated the strict subordination of Soviet bar to the People’s Commissariat of Justice, preserved electoral property qualifications, and prioritized ideological loyalty over professional competence. The Law of 1979 was prompted by the Constitution of the USSR of 1977. It mandated higher legal education, expanded the scope of legal aid (including representation in arbitration and administrative proceedings), abolished the right of non-motivated removal of bar members by justice authorities, and introduced judicial review for decisions terminating advocate status. The shift f…

title: Regulation of Artificial Intelligence in Commercial Use: A Comparative Analysis of India and the European Union AI Act
abstract: Artificial intelligence now sits inside the decision-making machinery of banking, insurance, recruitment, healthcare, and retail, yet the law governing its commercial use differs sharply across jurisdictions. This article offers a comparative doctrinal analysis of two contrasting models: the European Union’s Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024, the world’s first binding horizontal AI law, and India’s deliberately statute-light framework, anchored since November 2025 in the India AI Governance Guidelines, the DPDP Act 2023 and its 2025 Rules, and sectoral instruments. Using the functional method of comparative law, it assesses both regimes across regulatory philosophy, scope, risk classification, transparency, enforcement, liability, and business impact. Two findings are central. First, the European model has come under strain: the 2025 withdrawal of the proposed AI Liability Directive leaves the EU without harmonised fault-based liability rules for AI. Second, India’s absolute-liability doctrine in M.C. Mehta v. Union of India offers a foundation for an AI liability regime the EU currently lacks. The article proposes a contextualised thin statute: a three-tier risk classification, rights of explanation and human review, a liability regime, and statutory footing for the institutions the 2025 Guidelines envisaged.
venue: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities

title: Improving the Legal Regulation of the State Forest Policy
abstract: Modern forest management and the level of forest conservation, protection, and regeneration must meet heightened social, environmental, and economic demands. The prolonged use of an extensive model of forest management, focused on the continuous involvement of new forest areas into cutting operations, has led to a decline in the resource and ecological potential of the forests. The forest sector of the country’s economy needs to adapt to the globalization of markets, technological developments, the emergence of new types of wood products, intensifying competition, and increasingly stringent environmental requirements. Public administration plays a special role here. The article substantiates the importance of state management in the timber industry, analyzes forestry laws and the principles of state forest policy, examines scientific approaches to implementing forest policy, and proposes areas for improving state forest policy.

Repeated Laser Exposure Enhances Electrochemical Response in Ag/Laser-Induced Graphene Electrodes with a Hierarchical Assessment of Fabrication Reproducibility
abstract: Abstract Laser-induced graphene (LIG) provides a scalable, maskless route to porous carbon electrodes, but variability among independently fabricated devices and batches limits reliable manufacturing. Here, a controlled Ag/LIG workflow was used to examine how a one- to three-pass laser sequence affects material structure, electrochemical response, and fabrication reproducibility. SEM indicated pass-dependent network restructuring within the sampled fields, Raman spectroscopy showed greater but spatially nonuniform graphitic ordering, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated greater sp2 character and modest surface deoxygenation with repeated laser exposure. Three-pass electrodes produced an approximately 2.3-fold higher square-wave voltammetric response than one-pass electrodes in ferri/ferrocyanide solution. Cyclic voltammetry, impedance spectroscopy, and direct resistance measurements on representative electrodes showed that the largest resistance decrease occurred between one and two passes, whereas conditional apparent electroactive area continued to increase, with the larger increment occurring between two and three passes; charge-transfer resistance remained comparatively small and showed no systematic dependence on pass number. Reproducibility of the selected three-pass process was evaluated using 18 devices from three fabrication batches and 162 voltammograms: sca…

title: Optimal exercise types and doses for improving balance function among older adults living in residential care: a systematic review and dose–response network meta-analysis
abstract: Background Balance impairment is common among older adults living in residential care facilities and increases the risk of falls and functional decline. Although exercise is recommended to improve balance function, the optimal exercise modalities and doses remain uncertain. This study aims to examine the dose–response relationships of different exercise modalities with balance function in older adults living in residential care facilities. Methods Exercise dose was calculated as the product of duration, frequency, and intensity, expressed in metabolic equivalents of task minutes per week (MET-min/week), to enable comparisons across studies. Bayesian network and dose–response meta-analyses were conducted to compare the effects of different exercise modalities on balance function and model the dose–response relationships. Balance function was assessed using the Berg Balance Scale. Results A total of 24 studies were included in the systematic review. Overall exercise demonstrated a positive dose–response association with balance improvement, with the greatest benefit observed at approximately 900 MET-min/week (MD = 5.56, 95% CrI: 2.68, 8.6). Stratified analyses by exercise modality showed that balance training and combined exercise training were significantly associated with improved balance function, although the optimal doses varied across modalities. The comparative ranking acr…

Drilling of CF/PEEK thermoplastic composites under dry and minimum quantity lubrication conditions: Machining performance, damage mechanisms and multi-response optimization
abstract: This study investigated the drilling performance and damage mechanisms of carbon fibre-reinforced polyetheretherketone (CF/PEEK) thermoplastic composite laminates under dry and minimum quantity lubrication (MQL) conditions. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is among the first systematic studies to compare these environments by combining mechanical responses, hole quality, multiscale damage morphology, and multi-response optimisation. Drilling tests were performed using an uncoated carbide drill with a 30° helix angle and a 120° point angle at cutting speeds of 15, 25, and 35 m/min and feed rates of 0.05, 0.075, and 0.10 mm/rev. MQL was applied at 60 mL/h. Thrust force (F z ), exit delamination factor (F d ), and hole-wall surface roughness (R a ) were evaluated using Taguchi signal-to-noise ratios (S/N), analysis of variance (ANOVA), regression modelling, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and grey relational analysis (GRA). Compared with dry drilling, MQL reduced mean thrust force from 254.4 to 242.1 N (4.8%), surface roughness from 1.090 to 0.950 µm (12.9%), and delamination factor from 1.155 to 1.142 (1.1%). The maximum pointwise thrust force reduction was 14.3%. ANOVA identified feed rate as the dominant factor for thrust force (46.65%), while cutting speed governed delamination (54.95%). Surface roughness was mainly influenced by cutting speed (38.22%) and the e…

title: Correction to: Genome-wide identification and integrative analysis of the cytochrome P450 superfamily in pea (Pisum sativum L.) reveals candidate genes associated with Aphanomyces root rot response
Supporting Students Anywhere, Anytime: The Development of The Counselling Armchair Podcast for On-demand Mental Health Support
abstract: University counselling services frequently struggle with meeting rising demand for services with limited resources. While one-on-one support is essential, group sessions and webinars can only reach students at scheduled times. Podcasts, as on-demand content, offer an accessible, scalable way to address this challenge. Although few university counselling services have explored podcast production, podcasts have surged in popularity due to their accessibility and educational value, especially among 18–34-year-olds—a key university demographic. The Counselling Armchair: Nurturing Well Being and Study podcast was developed at the RMIT University counselling service to enhance capacity to meet student needs. Key steps included upskilling hosts in podcast production (recording, editing, and distribution), creating a podcast design, using data from clients and counsellors to guide episode topics, and promoting episodes through RMIT University's communication channels. Since its launch, the podcast has published 35 episodes with over 4,968 plays. Clinicians refer clients to episodes, and feedback highlights its role in reducing stigma, fostering familiarity with counselling staff, and offering interim support while students await appointments. The project illustrates how low-cost tools and collaborative design can produce meaningful, scalable mental health resources. Future directions i…

title: A Demand-Responsive Composite Scoring Model for Revenue Allocation in Multi-Owner Vehicle Networks
abstract: Proportional revenue-sharing rules that pay vehicle owners strictly by trip volume push deficit-carrying service-area cells past the 30 percent coverage-deficit threshold, an equilibrium reproduced in a 500,000-vehicle simulated multi-owner network on a seven-day settlement cycle. This paper specifies a five-parameter Composite Contribution Score, computed from telemetry-derived readiness, utilization, quality, geographic-coverage, and temporal-alignment terms, whose weight vector is conditioned in real time on network operating state. Elevating the coverage term weight from 0.20 to 0.40 the instant the deficit-cell fraction crosses 30 percent reduces steady-state clustering by 42 percent against a naive proportional-allocation baseline, while the five-term linear decomposition closes full-coalition settlement in under 30 seconds, an 84 percent latency reduction against a parameterized 10,000-sample Monte Carlo Shapley baseline. A predictive settlement layer using an autoregressive projection holds advance-disbursement shortfall below 4 percent across a 36-cycle backtest at a 70 percent advance ceiling. Sensitivity analysis exposes a resource-constraint interdependency the linear formula conceals: a 0.10 increase in temporal demand alignment costs 12 percent in utilization efficiency, since both draw on the same finite vehicle-time budget. A single low-dimensional, state-condit…
