title: Fontan patients with systemic left ventricle have superior response to 6-month exercise program over patients with right ventricle
abstract: Abstract Objectives: In Fontan patients, transpulmonary flow depends on systemic venous pressure, pulmonary vascular resistance, and ventricle preload. Reduction in cardiopulmonary function is common in Fontan patients. Exercise is considered a promising self-care method to harden particularly lower limbs for supporting transpulmonary flow. We studied whether a 6-month exercise program improves cardiopulmonary function in Fontan patients and if the response is dependent on ventricular morphology. Methods: Forty-one paediatric stable Fontan patients with right (RV n = 29) and left (LV n = 12) dominant ventricle morphology were included. Patients with RV were further divided into antegrade (RV-A) and retrograde (RV-R) coronary flow groups. Before the individualised self-guided training, the test subjects were inquired for exercise habits followed by cardiopulmonary exercise testing, body composition, and muscular fitness. Repeat testing was done in 31 patients that completed the exercise prescription. Differences between groups were tested using one-way analysis of variance; within-group changes were analysed using paired t-tests. Results: Thirty-one patients (LV n = 11, RV-A n = 12, RV-R n = 8) completed the exercise intervention without complications. In comparison to RV patients, those with LV had superior baseline peak VO₂ ( p = 0.046) and its improvement by intervention ( p …

title: Spatial drivers and response thresholds of water-related ecosystem services for ecological management zoning in the Yangtze River Basin
abstract: Ecological management zoning requires evidence that connects ecosystem-service condition with spatial associations and interpretable response thresholds. We assessed water yield (WY), a water-purification score (WP) derived from InVEST NDR nitrogen export, and soil conservation (SC) across the Yangtze River Basin in 2000 and 2020. Nitrogen export was retained as a pressure variable and reverse-normalized only when calculating WP; SC was represented by InVEST SDR sediment retention. On a common 1-km grid, we combined weighted service supply (WESS) with an unnormalized benefit–trade-off score to construct WESC and mapped the relationship scores separately after year-specific normalization (WESR). Optimal-parameter geographical detector analysis ranked precipitation (q = 0.3652), temperature (0.2768), elevation (0.1612), NDVI (0.1256), GDP (0.0201), and population (0.0192). Out-of-fold SHAP attribution from a spatially grouped GW-XGBoost model corroborated the prominence of the four biophysical variables, although the order of GDP and population differed. Constraint-line and first-derivative sensitivity analyses identified candidate maximum-supply and rapid-response thresholds. Their logical overlay delineated monitoring-based conservation (10.47%), key conservation (13.44%), monitoring-based enhancement (17.91%), and priority enhancement (58.18%) zones. Together, these analyses l…

title: Severe consumptive coagulopathy in Klippel–Trenaunay syndrome with visceral vascular involvement: sustained hematologic response to sirolimus—a case report
abstract: Background Klippel–Trenaunay syndrome (KTS) is a rare congenital vascular overgrowth disorder characterized by capillary and venous malformations with segmental limb overgrowth. Extensive slow-flow venous malformations may be complicated by severe consumptive coagulopathy, with features ranging from localized intravascular coagulopathy (LIC) to systemic coagulation activation and DIC-like decompensation. Case presentation A 20-year-old woman with longstanding KTS involving the right lower extremity and visceral vascular malformations presented with recurrent hematochezia, progressive fatigue, and severe transfusion-dependent iron deficiency anemia. Laboratory investigations revealed profound anemia (hemoglobin 5.3 g/dL), thrombocytopenia, prolonged coagulation times, severe hypofibrinogenemia (40 mg/dL), and markedly elevated D-dimer, consistent with severe consumptive coagulopathy in the setting of extensive slow-flow venous malformations. Imaging demonstrated extensive slow-flow venous malformations involving the right lower extremity, liver, and spleen. Endoscopic evaluation was considered high risk because of the extensive gastrointestinal vascular involvement. Despite intensive supportive management, including blood products and antifibrinolytic therapy, the patient remained transfusion dependent Given the severity and persistence of the consumptive coagulopathy despite su…

title: Integrated process optimization of vacuum-sintered Al alloys using hybrid machine learning and response surface methodology
abstract: Purpose The development of high-performance aluminium alloys requires precise control of process parameters. Herein, an investigation was made on the synergetic influence of sintering temperature (ST), sintering time (St), ageing temperature (AT), and ageing time (At) on the mechanical properties of a designed aluminium alloy containing Zn, Mg, Cu, Si, Sc, and Fe as strengthening elements. Design/methodology/approach Experimental data from tensile and hardness tests were analysed using both response surface methodology (RSM) and machine learning (ML) models to assess predictive capacity. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) revealed that the contribution of the parameters varied, with St exerting the strongest influence, followed by ST, At, and AT. Findings RSM-based quadratic regression models provided statistically adequate prediction for yield and ultimate strengths and elongation (R2 > 0.96), though hardness was less reliable (R2 > 0.71). ML methods demonstrated superior accuracy across all responses, particularly ensemble gradient boosting models (CatBoost and eXGBoost), which consistently achieved R2 > 0.96. Support Vector Regression also performed competitively for elongation and hardness, while Gaussian Process Regression was highly effective for strength predictions but weaker for ductility and hardness. The complementary application of RSM and ML thus offers a robust…

Gendered risks in mining: Health and safety challenges faced by women in South Africa’s platinum industry
abstract: Orientation: Legislative reforms have been introduced in South Africa to promote gender equality and improve working conditions in the mining sector; however, occupational environments remain structured around male-oriented norms and practices. As a result, women continue to face gender-specific risks which remain insufficiently addressed. Research purpose: The aim of the study was to investigate the health and safety challenges faced by women employed in South Africa’s platinum mining industry. Motivation for the study: There is a need for empirical, context-specific evidence to better understand and address gendered health and safety risks and to inform effective interventions in mining organisations. Research approach/design and method: The study adopted a cross-sectional exploratory research design and a quantitative research approach. Data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire distributed to women employed in mining operations at a platinum mine in South Africa. An availability sampling was used to select the respondents, resulting in 196 completed responses. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and multivariate analyses. Main findings: The findings indicate that gender-specific health and safety risks, including physical and ergonomic mismatches, inadequate PPE fit, deficient ablution and sanitation infrastructure and experiences of discrim…

title: From Forecast Accuracy to Resilience: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Supply Chain Management
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly presented as a general-purpose technology for supply chain management, yet the literature remains fragmented across technology families, functional areas and research designs. This paper develops an integrative account of how AI changes supply chain decisions and outcomes. Drawing on nine conceptual, empirical and review sources published between 1997 and 2024, it identifies four mechanisms through which AI affects supply chains: richer demand signal extraction and forecasting; automated evaluation and monitoring of suppliers and contracts; dynamic optimisation of inventory, production and logistics decisions; and earlier detection of, and faster response to, disruption. These mechanisms operate along a ladder of delegated authority that runs from descriptive analytics to bounded autonomous decision-making, and their realisation depends on data infrastructure, organisational absorptive capacity and governance rather than on algorithms alone. Reported performance effects are positive but conditional: survey evidence associates AI-enabled analytics with operational and environmental performance, whereas benchmarking evidence shows that machine learning does not automatically outperform established statistical methods. The paper concludes that the principal impact of AI is less the substitution of human planners than the compression of …

title: Intervention-Associated Psychosocial and Serum Ferritin Changes Following a Nurse-Led Self-Management Education Programme with a Family-Support Component among Adolescents with Thalassaemia: A Non-Randomised Quasi-Experimental Study
abstract: Introduction: Thalassaemia is a lifelong haematological disorder that requires lifelong blood transfusions and iron chelation therapy. During adolescence, developmental changes and psychosocial challenges often compromise treatment adherence, increasing the risk of iron overload and long-term complications. Grounded in the Middle Range Theory of Self- and Family Management of Chronic Illness, this study examined intervention-associated changes in psychosocial determinants and clinical outcomes following a self-management and family support component among adolescents with thalassaemia. Methods: A non-randomised quasi-experimental pre–post design at the participant level, with a concurrent control group, was conducted among 96 adolescents with thalassaemia. Four eligible hospitals were selected using predefined institutional criteria and randomly allocated at the hospital level to the intervention or control condition; individual adolescents were not randomised (48 intervention; 48 control). The intervention group received an eight-week nurse-led self-management education programme with a family-support component delivered through standardised printed modules, direct education, and monitoring sheets, covering thalassaemia self-management, treatment-related practices, complication prevention, family support, and quality-of-life management, in addition to routine care. Family memb…

title: Reward-based crowdfunding and retail symbiosis: understanding the backers-cum-buyer decision journey
abstract: Purpose Reward-based crowdfunding (RBCF) is evolving beyond a financing tool into a symbiotic retail model in which backers act as both early investors and first buyers. This study examines the hybrid “backer-cum-buyer” decision journey by developing and testing the sympathy–empathy–motives–participation–sharing (SEMPS) model, investigating how narrative-evoked sympathy and empathy activate multiple coexisting motives that drive two parallel outcomes: transactional participation and social sharing. Design/methodology/approach Using survey data from 509 Korean fashion-crowdfunding backers, we tested the SEMPS model through confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modelling with bootstrapping and estimated serial-mediation effects via a phantom-variable approach. Findings Sympathy and empathy activated distinct motives. Altruism, novelty, information and reward enhanced participation intention, which in turn solely drove sharing intention, as no motive affected sharing directly. Sympathy exerted a stronger indirect influence on sharing than empathy, with participation serving as the consistent mediator. Originality/value The study repositions RBCF as a pre-market retail symbiosis and redefines consumers as hybrid “backers-cum-buyers.” The SEMPS model separates sympathy from empathy, incorporates a theory-grounded multidimensional motives structure and treats participa…

title: Honeypot-Based Network Security Monitoring: Design, Implementation and Simulation-Driven Evaluation of a T-Pot Deployment with a Machine-Learning-Ready Control Center
abstract: Signature-driven intrusion detection systems raise many false alarms and cannot recognise attacks for which no signature exists. Honeypots offer a complementary approach: because a decoy has no legitimate users, every interaction with it is suspicious, so the resulting telemetry is both low-noise and rich in attacker behaviour. This paper presents the design and implementation of a honeypot-based network security monitoring system built on the open-source T-Pot platform, which combines the Cowrie, Dionaea, Honeytrap and Conpot decoys with the Suricata intrusion detection engine and an Elasticsearch–Logstash–Kibana analytics stack. The deployment is hosted in an isolated virtual machine with strict outbound containment. On top of the platform we developed Python traffic simulators that generate brute-force, reconnaissance and benign sessions against a local honeypot, together with a web-based Control Center for launching simulations and exploring captured sessions, and a dataset-export path intended for machine-learning classification. We describe the architecture, the configuration of each component, the containment measures, and the validation procedure, and we discuss the limits of a simulation-driven evaluation. The work shows that a complete, safely contained monitoring environment can be assembled from open-source components on modest hardware and used as a repeatable test…
venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management

title: Usability as a feature of an information system for health status measures: the DataCIF concept
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the perceived usability of DataCIF 2.0, a health information system based on the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health. Method: Ten healthcare professionals with expertise in the ICF and/or health information systems explored DataCIF 2.0 for 15 days and subsequently completed the System Usability Scale (SUS), scored from 0 to 100. Results: Nine participants obtained SUS scores of 50 or higher. The overall SUS score was 71.25 (95% CI: 62.5–87.5), indicating good perceived usability. Items related to system integration and willingness to use the software were positively rated, whereas the need for technical support and confidence in using the system indicated opportunities for improvement. Conclusion: DataCIF 2.0 demonstrated good perceived usability among experts. Further evaluation involving users without previous contact with the system is recommended.
authors: Paulo Henrique Ferreira de Araújo Barbosa

title: Non-operative management of penetrating abdominal trauma in a low-volume environment: a single center experience
abstract: Abstract Introduction High-volume trauma centers report that selective non-operative management (NOM) in patients suffering from penetrating abdominal trauma (PAT) is a safe approach. Switzerland is a low-volume environment for PAT. We hypothesize that despite the low number of PAT cases, NOM is a feasible approach with comparable outcomes to those in high incidence environments for PAT. Methods Retrospective analysis of patients aged > 16 years who were treated for PAT between January 1, 2013, and December 31, 2023 at a Level I trauma and academic tertiary referral center in a low-volume environment for PAT. The primary endpoint was the failure rate of NOM. Successful NOM was defined as completion of NOM without the need for surgical intervention. Secondary endpoints included the rates of non-therapeutic operations, hospital length of stay and mortality. Results In total, 57 patients were eligible, with 36 (63.1%) stab wounds (SW), 14 (24.6%) gunshot wounds (GSW) and seven (12.3%) impalements. Median age was 35 years (IQR 24–56) and 73.7% were male. Median ISS was 16 (IQR 4–25). In 28 patients (49.1%) NOM was attempted (23 SW, 1 GSW, 4 impalements). In these patients, median ISS was 4 (IQR 1-16.5), wound localizations were the anterior abdomen in 18 patients (64.3%), the back in 5 patients (17.9%) and the left flank in 4 patients (14.3%). A total of ten patients (35.7%) with N…

title: Terahertz Integrated Sensing and Communication for Ground-to-UAV Channels: A Survey of Channel Modeling, Waveforms, and Beam Management
abstract: Terahertz (THz) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is emerging as a key enabler of sixth generation (6G) networks, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are among its most challenging yet valuable host platforms. Over ground-to-UAV links, THz-ISAC payloads promise ultra-high-rate to backhaul and millimeter-level sensing within the stringent size, weight, and power budget of a hovering drone. Realizing this promise requires a coherent understanding of four tightly coupled pillars: the ground-to-UAV THz channel, beam management, the ISAC waveform and its transceiver realization, and system-level performance. This survey is organized around these four pillars. We first consolidate the propagation fundamentals of aerial THz links, including altitude-dependent molecular absorption and UAV-specific non-stationarity, together with the measurement and modeling literature that underpins them. We then review beam management, covering near-field beam-pattern transformation, alignment and tracking under misalignment, and wideband hybrid beamforming that combats beam squint with true-time-delay architectures. We next contrast the candidate ISAC waveforms — OTFS, DFT-s-OTFS with superimposed pilots, and SI-DFT-s-OFDM with flexible guard intervals — in terms of PAPR, power-amplifier efficiency, Doppler robustness, and sensing accuracy, and assess the transceiver hardware against the UA…

title: Climate financing in the economic management system: Institutional risks and greenwashing
abstract: Subject. The mechanism of mutual influence between climate adaptation financing processes and greenwashing. Objectives. To analyze the institutional and financial-economic factors that determine the relationship between the financing of climate change adaptation measures and the spread of greenwashing practices, as well as to identify the managerial conditions that contribute to the emergence and use of greenwashing practices. Methods. The study employs methods of logical and semantic analysis. Results. The main sources and mechanisms of climate financing are systematized from the perspective of economics and management. It is revealed that the multilevel structure of climate financing and the separation of financial flows create institutional risks that contribute to the spread of greenwashing practices. Based on the analysis of official documents and literature reviews, it is demonstrated that the study of financing practices related to the climate agenda and greenwashing requires the integration of approaches from the fields of marketing, management, corporate finance, law, and environmental sciences. Conclusions and Relevance. Greenwashing in the field of climate change is driven not only by marketing practices but also by institutional gaps in the regulation of climate financing, including the absence of unified criteria for assessing adaptation projects and mechanisms for…

title: Religious Education in Indonesia’s National Education System: Negotiating Faith, Citizenship, and Humanistic Pluralism
abstract: Religious education in Indonesia has historical roots and has secured formal legitimacy through national policy. This study examines the transformation of religious education within Indonesia’s national education system, focusing on the relationship between religious identity, democratic citizenship, and humanistic pluralism in a religiously and culturally diverse society. Employing a qualitative approach with a critical-interpretative design, the study analyzes national education regulations and relevant academic literature published between 2020 and 2025. Data were examined through content analysis and thematic analysis. The findings reveal three interconnected dynamics. First, the institutionalization of religious education reflects a shift from community-based religious authority toward a more formalized relationship between religious institutions and the state. Second, Religious education serves not only to strengthen faith but also to shape religiosity and cultivate civic awareness. Third, Religious education should be developed through a dialogical, inclusive, and non-doctrinaire approach; it should serve as a pedagogical space for cultivating tolerance, openness, and respect for diversity and humanity. Building on these findings, the study proposes a Faith–Citizenship–Humanistic Pluralism framework as an analytical perspective for understanding the intersections between…

title: Artificial Intelligence in Radiology Department: Technologies, Application, Challenges, and Future Direction
abstract: This review synthesizes current artificial intelligence methodologies and evaluates their clinical impact in diagnostic radiology. As artificial intelligence tools increasingly enter clinical workflows, understanding their performance, limitations, and barriers to adoption is critical. Key Words: artificial intelligence, clinical workflow, diagnostic radiology, medical imaging, regulatory governance.
venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management

title: The Role of the Village Government in Increasing Community Participation in Development Implementation in Pattimpa Village, Ponre District, Bone Regency
abstract: Community involvement is one of the key factors in the success of rural development. The village government is responsible for encouraging residents and giving them opportunities to take part in every stage of development, from planning to implementation. This study examines the role of the village government in promoting community participation and identifies the obstacles encountered during the development process in Pattimpa Village, Ponre District, Bone Regency. It employs a descriptive qualitative method with a field research approach. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, using both primary and secondary sources. The findings indicate that the village government mobilises and guides the community through coordination, deliberative meetings, the accommodation of public aspirations, and the setting of development priorities. Community participation takes the form of submitting proposals, joining development activities and cooperating through gotong royong (mutual assistance). However, participation has not been fully optimised because of ineffective information dissemination, limited funds, and varying levels of community awareness. Improving participation therefore requires effective coordination, open information, and closer cooperation between the village government and residents. The study offers input for village governments seeking a …

title: Fragmentation without integration: the unassembled knowledge architecture of AI–entrepreneurship research
Production control, marketing and economic analysis as a single system of corporate value formation
abstract: Subject. The system of economic interrelations of three functions of corporate management – production control, marketing and economic analysis, considered as a single contour of creation and realization of consumer value in conditions of competition and high consumer awareness. Objectives. To substantiate the economic necessity of integrating production control, marketing and economic analysis into a single quality management system and to show the mechanism of such integration, including a formal optimization model. Methods. The research is based on a set of strategic analysis (SWOT analysis and PEST analysis) adapted to the cross-functional formulation of the problem, as well as on the apparatus of economic and mathematical modeling. A model of the total cost of quality is constructed, including the cost of preventive control, internal losses from defects and external (market) losses from inconsistencies, the model is generalized to the case of maximizing profits, taking into account the price premium for quality. Results. It is revealed that the three functions correspond to the three economic dimensions of quality – production, market and analytical, together forming a complete cost management circuit. It is shown that the central connecting category is the total cost of nonconformity, the external component of which transfers the consequences of marriage into the sphere o…

title: Irya: a digital health approach for structured pain documentation and medication management in palliative care
abstract: Objective: To describe the design and development of Irya, an ethically compliant and sustainable mobile health platform for structured pain documentation and medication management in palliative care within the Brazilian public health context. Method: A design‑oriented methodological approach was adopted, integrating validated pain assessment instruments (Visual Analog Scale and Brief Pain Inventory) into a bidirectional mobile health (mHealth) system. The platform was developed using a cross‑platform framework with a modular architecture, aligned with HL7 FHIR standards, national data models, and the Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD), while prioritizing accessibility and low‑literacy usability. Results: A high‑fidelity functional prototype was implemented, enabling real‑time patient self‑reporting of pain and medication intake and providing clinicians with longitudinal visualizations and decision‑support summaries through a web‑based dashboard. Conclusion: Irya demonstrates the feasibility of an interoperable, accessible, and ethically grounded mHealth solution that supports equitable and sustainable digital transformation in Brazilian palliative care.

title: Adaptive Residual-Informed Deep Transfer Learning for Accurate Flood Depth Estimation Using Spatiotemporal Feature Learning
Delegated Leadership in Public Secondary Schools in Temeke Municipality, Tanzania: Practices, Teacher Participation and Delegated Authority
abstract: This study examined delegated leadership practices in selected public secondary schools in Temeke Municipality, Tanzania, with attention to three closely related dimensions: delegation of responsibilities, teacher participation in school decision-making, and the authority granted to teachers when performing delegated leadership roles. A mixed-methods approach was used to combine numerical patterns from teacher questionnaires with explanatory evidence from interviews and school observations. The field evidence comprised 45 teachers who completed questionnaires and five heads of schools who participated in interviews, giving 50 respondents and a 100% response rate. Quantitative data were summarized using frequencies and percentages, while interview and observation evidence was organized thematically and integrated during interpretation. The findings show that delegation was well established in academic work: 91.1% of teachers agreed or strongly agreed that teachers were delegated leadership roles in academic activities. Clear definition of delegated responsibilities received 71.1% positive responses. Teacher participation in decision-making was positive but less pronounced, at 62.2%, with 26.7% neutral responses. Regarding authority, 73.4% reported that department heads were given decision-making authority and 84.4% agreed that school administrations trusted teachers with leaders…

title: Central environmental inspections and environmental emergency-management disclosure: evidence using an industry-linked pollution proxy
abstract: Introduction Central environmental inspections in China were designed to strengthen vertical accountability, but what changes in corporate reporting reveal about organizational implementation remains uncertain. Methods Using 20,641 firm-year observations from 2,831 Chinese listed companies, we compare changes in environmental emergency-management disclosure between firms with positive and zero values of a pre-rollout industry-linked pollution proxy. The proxy is inherited from a research panel and is not a verified statutory designation. Models absorb firm, province-by-year, and sector- or industry-by-year effects, distinguish inspection-transition years, exclude observations from each province’s second-round inspection year onward, and cluster inference by province. The outcome is a provider-coded disclosure item and has not undergone independent validation by two human coders against original reports. Results The longer-window model estimates a 7.7-percentage-point differential increase in emergency-management disclosure. In the primary sample, however, the inspection interaction is identical to a pollution-proxy-specific calendar-time shift beginning in 2017, preventing separate attribution to inspection. Earlier-date placebos and differential-trend adjustment further weaken attribution. The auxiliary rollout comparison is imprecise. The balanced-window confidence set includ…

title: Adaptive Head for Automatic Compensation of Elastic Deformations in the Machining System Affecting Turning Accuracy
abstract: This paper presents a new cartridge solution, developed based on patent PL 245622, that automatically compensates for elastic deformations of the entire MCWT (machine tool – chuck – workpiece – tool) system. This enables improved machining accuracy and turning efficiency. The principle of operation of the cartridge is described, as well as the possibilities of adapting its settings to the conditions in which it is expected to operate effectively. A theoretical and experimental analysis of the effectiveness of this cutting process support is presented.

title: The role of culture throughout the entrepreneurial process
Intelligent Inverse Design of High-Flux Acoustic Metamaterials for Aviation Power Systems
abstract: There is a contradiction between high ventilation capacity and low and medium frequency noise reduction in the confined space of the aviation power and environmental control system. This paper proposes a reverse design framework. The framework combines deep agent model with heuristic algorithm. The framework uses a multi-layer perceptron ( MLP ) to construct an acoustic surrogate model. It reaches a high determination coefficient ( R2 ) of 0.9969 when predicting the first resonance peak frequency. Physical constraints such as wall thickness and manufacturing tolerances are incorporated into the genetic algorithm ( GA ). In this paper, a bottom-up sequential cascade optimization strategy is established. In this paper, a three-layer labyrinth acoustic metamaterial with an outer diameter of 100 mm and a ventilation rate of 16 % is designed by this strategy. The finite element simulation verifies its excellent isolation performance for discrete line spectrum noise at 680 Hz, 1150 Hz and 1550 Hz. The peak sound transmission loss ( STL ) reaches 43 dB. The mechanism analysis shows that the interlayer impedance transition and near-field interference effect significantly enhance the global acoustic attenuation characteristics of the structure. Further extended analysis considers the 25 % limit ventilation rate. The analysis verifies the applicability and robustness of the framework und…

title: From barriers to roadmaps: prioritizing AI adoption challenges in UAE healthcare
abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping global healthcare delivery, yet its adoption remains uneven across regions. The United Arab Emirates (UAE), through the National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031, has positioned healthcare as a key transformation domain. Despite rapid technological advancement and policy support, AI has yet to move consistently from pilot projects into routine clinical practice. Design/methodology/approach This study develops a prioritisation hierarchy of AI adoption barriers in UAE healthcare using a two-stage research design combining the Delphi method and the Ordinal Priority Approach. A total of 18 subfactors organized into six categories were prioritized using responses from 35 healthcare stakeholders. Findings Ethical, legal, and privacy concerns received the highest category weight. However, the differences across category weights are narrow, indicating that the barriers are broadly distributed rather than concentrated in a single domain. At the subfactor level, data security and privacy concerns, lack of facilitating conditions, lack of AI-specific training, poor workflow integration, and perceived complexity emerged as the five highest-ranked constraints. Originality/value The study contributes a stakeholder-informed prioritization of theoretically grounded AI adoption barriers in UAE healthcare. By integrating multiple adoptio…

title: Formulating factor constructs relevant to effective small- and medium-sized enterprises trade credit management in South Africa
abstract: Purpose: To identify and construct relevant factors for small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs)’ effective trade credit management and to obtain SME ratings of these constructs for statistically testing the validity and reliability of the measurement instrument. Design/methodology/approach: A literature review provided criteria for formulating variables for developing a 35-component questionnaire. Employing a quantitative research design with purposive sampling, the study targeted a population of 10 450 SMEs across South Africa. A total of 10 450 questionnaires were distributed, and 434 were returned (response rate: 4.15%). After applying completion criteria, 422 valid responses were used for statistical analysis, based on a calculated sample size of 450 at a 5% margin of error and 95% confidence level. Findings/results: Through descriptive statistical analysis, the application of trade credit management principles was identified as the highest quality trade credit management effectiveness variable. The application of factor analysis resulted in the identification of five SME trade credit management effectiveness factors. Small- and medium-sized enterprises did not rate these factors equally, with effectiveness ranked from highest to lowest as follows: managing trade credit management principles, managing trade credit management aspects, applying credit policy components whe…

Enhanced atmospheric radon forecasting using deep learning and advanced signal denoising techniques
abstract: Abstract The precise forecasting of ambient atmospheric radon concentrations remains exceptionally complex due to high-frequency noise and the non-linear behavior of its values. Although traditional statistical models like Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) are widely used, they often fail to capture complex non-linear patterns in high-resolution environmental data. This study presents a two-phase empirical evaluation of standard Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with Digital Signal Processing (DSP) preprocessing techniques (FFT, Discrete Wavelet Transform, and Butterworth filter). Using a one-year dataset of hourly outdoor radon concentration measurements from Qena city in Upper Egypt, the impact of time-series denoising on model performance was evaluated across extended multi-step horizons (up to 24 h) and compared against Random Forest using Direct and Recursive strategies. The results indicate that applying a Butterworth filter significantly improves short-term predictive accuracy, allowing the LSTM model to achieve a test R² of 0.9668, while performance degrades sharply in long-term recursive forecasting. This research offers a robust, data-driven framework for forecasting outdoor radon levels, which could be adapted for other noisy environmental time series.

title: An IoT-based platform for electrical monitoring, load forecasting, and power quality disturbance detection in three-phase buildings
abstract: Abstract This study presents a unified Internet-of-Things (IoT) platform for real-time monitoring, short-term load forecasting, and power quality disturbance (PQD) detection of three-phase building loads. The proposed low-cost system integrates three PZEM-004T modules, current transformers, and an ESP8266 microcontroller to measure and transmit voltage, current, active power, energy, frequency, and power factor via Wi-Fi. Calibration against Fluke reference instruments achieved mean errors of 0.355% for voltage and 0.324% for current. A 21-day laboratory deployment revealed phase-load imbalance, with L3 having the highest average power demand (959.38 W) and L2 the lowest (460.64 W), while voltage and frequency remained stable. Five optimized exponential-smoothing models were evaluated for short-term forecasting. The Extended Additive Holt–Winters (EAHW) achieved the lowest Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) for daily average power demand (24.53%), while the Double Exponential Smoothing (DES) provided the most accurate cumulative energy prediction (MAPE = 4.58%). The forecasting approach was further validated using the external CLEMD dataset. For PQD detection, an optimization-based offset compensation method combined with IEEE 1159–2019 threshold classification improved three-phase detection accuracy from 97.91 to 98.15% to 98.50–98.70%. The novelty of this work lies in brid…

title: Cryptohub and Sales Forecasting Using Machine Learning
abstract: Cryptocurrency price forecasting remains one of the most demanding challenges in financial machine learning due to extreme non-stationarity, heavy-tailed return distributions, and regime shifts. While numerous studies evaluate isolated predictive models within offline computational notebooks, few investigate the mathematical constraints of tree-based extrapolation or examine how multi-step forecasting degrades across diverse digital asset classes within an operational software framework. In this paper, we present an empirical investigation of statistical, machine learning, and deep learning architectures for cryptocurrency price forecasting integrated into CryptoHub—an open, end-to-end analytics platform. We benchmark five distinct paradigms: classical Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks, and a dynamic Stacking Ensemble Regressor across eight cryptocurrencies (BTC, ETH, BNB, SOL, XRP, ADA, DOGE, AVAX) over short-to-medium horizons (h ∈ {1, 3, 5} days). We demonstrate that direct price regression on raw levels causes decision trees to suffer catastrophic extrapolation failures out-of-sample (yielding R2 < 0), whereas reformulating the objective to stationary percentage returns (Δ%) with dynamic price reconstruction resolves this boundary constraint, enabling t…

title: Dynamic Fusion of Graph-Based Spatial and State-Space Temporal Features for Multi-Horizon Traffic Speed Forecasting
abstract: Reliable traffic speed forecasting in Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled intelligent transportation systems requires effective modelling of spatial dependencies and evolving temporal patterns across traffic conditions. This study proposes GMDF-Net (Graph-Mamba Dynamic Fusion Network), a multi-horizon forecasting architecture that integrates complementary spatial and temporal representations. GMDF-Net combines an adaptive-graph spatial branch, which uses a fixed road-distance graph and a learned adaptive adjacency matrix, with a Mamba-inspired selective state-space temporal branch. An input-dependent, node- and time-aware softmax gate fuses the two representations. The model was evaluated on PeMSD7(M), comprising 228 sensors and five-minute traffic-speed observations, using a 12-step input window and forecast horizons of 15, 30 and 60 minutes. GMDF-Net achieved mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 2.29, 3.15 and 4.27 mph, root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 4.33, 6.10 and 8.11 mph, and mean absolute percentage errors (MAPEs) of 5.45%, 7.89% and 11.48% at the respective horizons. Its MAE was lower than the reported LSTM, GCN and STGCN results at all horizons and lower than the reported STGNN-FAM result at 15 and 30 minutes; the 60-minute MAE was 3.64% higher than STGNN-FAM. The reported DNNF-ITS results were lower across all horizons. Error analysis showed a right-skewed distribution, lar…

title: Forecasting Downside Operating Cash Flow for Corporate Cash Budgeting
abstract: Cash budgets must protect planned activity against weak operating cash flow without reserving more resources than necessary. We estimate lower conditional quantiles of annual reported operating cash flow using information available after original SEC annual disclosures. A rule combining recent cash-flow level and variability provides the historical benchmark. Across 549 evaluation events from 221 non-financial registrants in 2023–2025, a LightGBM model selected in development reduces tenth-percentile pinball loss by 15.10% (95% registrant-cluster interval, 6.09%–23.77%). Several other conditional estimators perform similarly. A fixed-model diagnostic attributes a smaller, less precisely estimated increment to accounting inputs beyond cash-flow history and size. The implied budget buffer falls by 1.20 percentage points of known assets and unused buffer by 1.31 points. The reduction in asset-normalized uncovered shortfall is less precise, and mean dollar shortfall increases. Lower unused provision nevertheless reduces scenario cost at the matching 9:1 shortage-to-idle price ratio. Adjustment using previously disclosed forecast errors buys further shortage protection through a larger buffer, but raises both quantile loss and scenario cost. Conditional forecasting improves allocation chiefly by reducing excess provision; its value for protecting large dollar exposures depends on th…

title: Analisis Peramalan (Forecasting) Harga Saham PT BISI Internasional (BISI) dengan Menggunakan Metode ARIMA
abstract: This study forecasts the stock prices of PT BISI International Tbk (BISI) using the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) method. The analysis uses 120 monthly observations obtained from Investing.com for May 2016–May 2026. Following the Box–Jenkins procedure, the Augmented Dickey–Fuller test indicated stationarity after first-order differencing (d = 1). Candidate models were evaluated using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), with ARIMA(2,1,2) selected for its lowest AIC of 1490.600. Residual diagnostics suggested approximately normal residuals without significant autocorrelation. Forecasts for the following 20 periods indicated relatively stable stock prices around Rp748.38, without a pronounced upward or downward trend. Model evaluation yielded a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 6.66%, indicating relatively low forecasting error. Fundamental analysis showed strong liquidity, with a current ratio of 14.3 in 2025, alongside declining profitability as return on assets and return on equity fell to approximately 5% during 2024–2025. The findings illustrate the potential of ARIMA for forecasting agribusiness stock prices. Nevertheless, projections reflect historical patterns and may change with market conditions and unexpected events.

A Study on Macroeconomic Shocks and the Crude-Oil Price Dynamics
abstract: In the pretext of international business, trade and economic analysis, certain commodities hold a position of exceptional prominence due to their value, utility and global demand. Among these, crude- oil is very important because of its economic significance. Crude- oil is known as Black gold. This particular commodity occupies a central place in international economic discussion and financial systems. Shaping national policies, investors psychology and market sentiment across the world. Its importance is reflected in the vast volume of research, media attention and policy debates surrounding it. This research focuses on crude-oil because of its continued relevance in shaping both macro-economic and micro-economic conditions. The study also highlights the distinctive role of crude-oil in international financial markets. The methodology adopted in this research emphasises simplicity and clarity, focusing on observable patterns and statistical analysis without overcomplicating the interpretive framework. This ensures that the results are accessible and interpretable by a wide range of audiences, including economists, finance professionals and students.
venue: International Journal of Innovations & Research Analysis

title: The winding number of coronal flux ropes. II. Ideal models
abstract: Our aim with this study was to investigate the behaviour of the winding number T_g and an approximating twist metric T_w for synthetic flux ropes. We used semi-analytic flux rope modelling software developed at the University of Helsinki to generate synthetic flux ropes and analysed their twist distributions using the magnetic field analysis tools (MAFIAT) software. We find that T_w can differ significantly from T_g and that expected trends are not always followed. Our results suggest that approximations of the winding number T_g should be used with caution.

title: Research on a spatiotemporal forecasting method for crop prices based on an improved CNN-LSTM hybrid model
Multi-Room Time-Series Forecasting of Indoor Thermal Conditions Using Deep Learning Models
abstract: Temperature and humidity prediction are important aspects of indoor environmental condition monitoring. This study evaluates and compares three models: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). The dataset consists of temperature and humidity measurements collected from four rooms, totaling eight observed variables. Dataset construction was performed using a sliding window approach with a lookback configuration of 6 steps and two forecasting horizons (2-step and 4-step), with a data sampling interval of 30 minutes. The experimental results indicate that model performance varies by variable type and forecasting horizon. For temperature prediction, the TCN model achieves the best performance at the 2-step forecasting horizon, with MAE of 0.281, RMSE of 0.344, and R² of 0.97. At the 4-step forecasting horizon, the GRU model outperforms the other models, achieving MAE of 0.403, RMSE of 0.519, and R² of 0.933. For humidity prediction, the GRU model demonstrates the best performance at both forecasting horizons, with MAE of 1.786 and R² of 0.897 at the 2-step forecasting horizon, and MAE of 2.014 and R² of 0.867 at the 4-step forecasting horizon. Furthermore, longer forecasting horizons lead to higher prediction errors. These findings indicate that the GRU model performs most consistently across the experiments, particularly …

title: Modelling and forecasting monthly TB/HIV coinfection registrations in Sichuan, China
An artificial intelligence-based prediction for suitable sport exercise recommendation using BMI and heart rate
abstract: Artificial intelligence can support personalized exercise guidance, but many fitness recommendation systems require wearable ecosystems, longitudinal activity histories, or complex sensor streams. This study developed an exercise-classification prototype using body mass index (BMI), resting heart rate (RHR), age, and sex to support initial recommendations without prior activity logs. An ESP32 platform integrated MAX30102, HX711, and HC-SR04 modules with a Flask backend communicating through HTTP over Wi-Fi. A dataset of 60,000 labeled records supported model development and internal evaluation. Preprocessing included categorical encoding and training-fitted Min-Max scaling. Candidate classifiers included Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, XGBoost, and XGBoost with SMOTENC oversampling. Hyperparameters were tuned using grid search and five-fold stratified cross-validation. Feature importance and SHAP analyses examined predictor contributions. A separate held-out sensitivity analysis assessed the effect of hypothetical perturbations to BMI and RHR. The results show internal XGBoost accuracy of 99.6%, with precision, recall, and F1-score of 0.996 and ROC-AUC of 0.992. BMI and RHR had the highest global feature importance, followed by age and sex. The prototype demonstrated web-based monitoring, sensor-data logging, and exercise-label display…

title: PolySea: A Multi-Agent Copilot for Polymer Property Prediction, Inverse Design, and Evidence-Grounded Assistance
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) stands at a crossroads in polymer science. General-purpose language models demonstrate remarkable reasoning yet fail at laboratory reliability; domain-specific models achieve accuracy but remain brittle beyond narrow tasks. Here we present PolySea to resolve this trade-off through a multi-agent architecture: the three-tier file-as-bus (FAB3) memory system maintains coherent session state and stores transferable polymer-specific knowledge for reuse; the literature evidence chain (LEC) provides timely access to relevant polymer literature and grounds claims in retrieved literature with explicit citations; agent-based interactive reasoning (AIR) orchestrates these resources while disclosing uncertainty and limitations; and the PolyOpus specialist delivers accurate polymer-specific responses. Unlike opaque chatbots that hide their reasoning, PolySea routes transparently: users see which tool answered, what evidence supports it, and when a requested property lacks a successful prediction tool. We evaluate using a test set containing more than 23,000 polymer-property instruction records, achieving mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 25 °C on glass-transition temperature (Tg), 0.70 eV on band gap (crystal), and 0.062 eV atom−1 on atomization energy, plus an accuracy of 79% on heat-resistance classification. In a set of polymer-related questions coverin…

title: Ultrasound radiomics-based prediction of central lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma coexistent with Hashimoto’s thyroiditis
CONSTRUCTION OF KNOWLEDGE GRAPH OF BIOMEDICINE BASED ON BILAYER EMBEDDING CASCADE FRAMEWORK ABOUT LINK PREDICTION
abstract: Biomedical domains are like complex networks and could therefore be described graphically. With the rapid advances of information technologies, some new approaches for modelling graphs and extracting biomedical knowledge have emerged, which operate by learning low-rank vector representations of graph nodes and edges with the graph’s inherent structure. This paper proposes a bilayer embedding cascade framework for a knowledge graph in the biomedical domain, combining knowledge embedding (KE) and graph embedding (GE). The approach combines both the semantic features of the KE model and the topological features of the GE model for link prediction in the knowledge graph construction. The experimental results show the following performance within the processed biomedical knowledge graph dataset: mean rank of 233 and Hits@10 of 93.28% on the chemogenomic relation, mean rank of 1107 and Hits@10 of 96.19% on the tissue relation, and mean rank of 126 and Hits@10 of 94.72% on the protein relation.

title: LANDSLIDE SUSCEPTIBILITY MAPPING AND PREDICTION UNCERTAINTY USING EXPLAINABLE DEEP LEARNING BASED ON SENTINEL-1 AND TOPOGRAPHIC DERIVATIVES IN SOUTHEAST SULAWESI
abstract: Landslide assessment in Southeast Sulawesi requires susceptibility information that not only indicates risk classes but also explains the prediction basis and model confidence levels. This study employs an "Expectable Deep Learning" development workflow by integrating Sentinel-1 GRD data and topographic derivatives. The initial inventory comprises 54 points across three susceptibility classes; 34 points fall within the raster coverage, forming 128×128 pixel patches with nine channels: VV, VH, RVI, NDPI, CR, elevation, slope, aspect, and curvature. A Light CNN serves as the baseline, while a Squeeze-and-Excitation CNN is used to test attention enhancement. Model interpretability is addressed using Grad-CAM and SHAP (based on a Random Forest surrogate), while uncertainty is quantified via Monte Carlo Dropout and Deep Ensemble methods. The Light CNN achieved 50.00% accuracy, 61.11% macro-precision, 50.00% macro-recall, 52.22% macro-F1, and an AUC-ROC of 45.83%. Although the model achieved 96.38% training accuracy, validation loss rose to 2.0872, indicating overfitting. Monte Carlo Dropout and Deep Ensemble yielded average normalized entropy values ​​of 0.9634 and 0.9976, respectively. Inference across 500 grid positions resulted in 28 low, 31 medium, and 441 high susceptibility classifications; however, 42% of positions exhibited normalized entropy of at least 0.90. title: PP075: Multimodal Deep Learning for Ischaemic Stroke Outcome Prediction: A Sri Lankan Pilot
abstract: Abstract Introduction Multimodal artificial intelligence models combining non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) with clinical variables predict post-stroke functional outcome with area- under-the-curve (AUC) values of 0.80–0.91 in Western and East Asian cohorts. Whether such models generalise to South Asian stroke populations, which are younger, with lower atrial fibrillation prevalence and limited endovascular access, is unknown. We conducted the first such evaluation in a Sri Lankan cohort. Methods Retrospective single-centre study using the Peradeniya Stroke Registry was conducted. Fifty-seven adult patients with acute ischaemic stroke, on-admission National Institute of Health Stroke Scale scores, discharge modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores, and retrievable admission NCCT were analysed. The primary outcome was unfavourable functional outcome (discharge mRS >2). Two deep- learning approaches were compared under an identical evaluation protocol: a three-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on the NCCT alone, and a Bacchi-style multimodal model fusing the same CNN with an artificial neural network of nine routinely available admission clinical features. Performance was estimated by 80/20 train–test splits averaged across five random seeds to mitigate the seed sensitivity inherent to small samples. Results The unfavourable outcome rate was 47%. Averaged …

title: Prediction of Weibo Retweet Volume for the China Internet Joint Rumor-Refutation Platform Based on Uncertain Time Series Analysis
abstract: With the widespread use of social media, the speed and reach of information dissemination have reached unprecedented levels. However, this has also accelerated the spread of misinformation and rumors. The China Internet Joint Rumor-Refutation Platform plays a crucial role in combating rumors and disseminating verified information. This study analyzes retweet data from the platform’s official Weibo account to assess and forecast uncertainty in retweet volume. Using uncertain time series analysis, data from January to June 2024 are modeled to determine the optimal model order and estimate model parameters. Residual analysis and uncertain hypothesis testing show that the selected model reasonably fits the observed data and that the residuals conform to the assumed uncertainty distribution. The forecasting results indicate that the model can provide reliable predictions of future retweet volumes together with prediction intervals, thereby providing a quantitative basis for assessing forecast uncertainty.
venue: Advances in Computer and Materials Scienc Research

title: A Risk-Aware Stratified Undersampling Method for Imbalanced Software Defect Prediction
abstract: Software defect prediction (SDP) suffers from severe class imbalance, as defective samples typically account for less than 20% of the data, which often leads to biased model training and degraded prediction performance. Undersampling has been widely used to address class imbalance and improve prediction performance. However, existing undersampling methods may alter the original data distribution by removing majority-class samples, potentially displacing the learned decision boundary in real-world SDP scenarios. Therefore, this paper proposes a risk-aware undersampling method for software defect prediction, which aims to alleviate class imbalance while reducing discrepancies between the retained and original majority-class distributions. The proposed method quantifies feature importance using SHAP values, incorporates defect distribution patterns to calculate a risk score for each majority-class sample, and performs proportional random sampling within decile-based risk strata. Experiments on 19 public datasets evaluate the proposed method. The results show that RASU achieves the highest average F1-score, MCC, and AUC under the decision-tree classifier and remains competitive under SVM and Random Forest. Ablation and controlled synthetic experiments indicate that the stratification mechanism can mitigate decision-boundary displacement under the evaluated settings.
venue: International Journal of Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering

title: MoodTOX: A Multiscale Interpretable Graph Neural Network for Out-of-Distribution Multiorgan Toxicity Prediction
abstract: Abstract Expanding chemical production, application and environmental discharge raise multiorgan toxic risks originating from emerging contaminants and complicate precise toxicity prediction. Emerging computational toxicology models enable large-scale toxicity screening but suffer from distribution-shift-induced spurious correlations that impair out-of-distribution generalization and substructure toxicity attribution. Here, we present MoodTOX, a multiorgan molecular out-of-distribution toxicity prediction framework tailored to address this challenge. MoodTOX quantifies distributional heterogeneity across molecular structures and physicochemical properties and extracts stable toxicity-related features, thereby reducing model reliance on distribution-specific spurious correlations. It also reveals key structural contributions at chemical bond, atom and molecular-fragment levels to improve out-of-distribution generalization and interpretability. We validate MoodTOX by using public benchmark data sets alongside our self-curated multiorgan toxicity data set (>280,000 chemicals). It achieves mean AUC values ranging from 0.932 to 0.960 for respiratory toxicity, nephrotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, and hERG inhibition. On matched compounds retained within MoodTOX’s high-confidence applicability domain, MoodTOX achieved an average accuracy of 89.2% across four external validation data set…

title: Development and evaluation of an explainable machine learning-based prediction model for workplace bullying among clinical nurses
abstract: Background Workplace bullying harms nurses’ physical and mental health and may compromise care quality and patient safety. Previous studies have investigated its associated factors mainly with traditional statistical methods. However, such models are limited in identifying risk at the individual level, whereas machine learning offers a new way to identify nurses at risk of workplace bullying. Objective This study aimed to develop prediction models for workplace bullying among clinical nurses using seven machine-learning algorithms, compare their performance to identify the best-performing model, and combine Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) with Shiny to visualize the optimal model. Methods Between August and September 2025, clinical nurses were recruited by convenience sampling from three tertiary general hospitals in central China and completed the Negative Acts Questionnaire-Revised online. Participants were randomly allocated to training and validation sets at a 7:3 ratio. Variables were selected by univariate analysis, LASSO regression and the Boruta algorithm (R 4.4.2). Seven models were developed in Python 3.10: logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and K-nearest neighbors (KNN). Performance was compared by the area under the curve…

title: Development and external validation of a prediction model incorporating immunologic and inflammatory biomarkers for new-onset acute kidney injury in older patients with sepsis following cardiac surgery: a multicenter study
abstract: Background Older patients with sepsis after cardiac surgery are at high risk of acute kidney injury (AKI). This study aimed to develop and externally validate a prediction model for new-onset AKI. Methods We conducted a multicenter observational cohort study. We included older patients with sepsis during their postoperative intensive care unit stay following cardiac surgery. We defined time zero as the onset of sepsis, corresponding to the first postoperative time point meeting the Sepsis-3 criteria. We collected predictors within 24 h after time zero. The primary endpoint was new-onset AKI occurring between 24 h and 7 days. Patients were assigned to development and prospective temporal-geographical validation cohorts. In the development cohort, we utilized least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, bootstrap-based stability analysis, random forest recursive feature elimination, and incremental logistic regression for variable selection and model development. Model performance was evaluated in terms of discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, and subgroup and nested model analyses assessed robustness. Results The final model retained chronic kidney disease, CD4 + T-cell count, CD4 + /CD8 + T-cell ratio, procalcitonin, and interleukin-6. The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.963 and 0.959 in the development and external va…

title: Preoperative prediction of high-risk gastrointestinal stromal tumors using CT and ultrasound-based machine learning: a comparative study with radiologists
abstract: Abstract Objectives To develop and validate a machine learning model combining computed tomography (CT) and ultrasound (US) features for preoperative prediction of high-risk gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST), and to compare its performance with that of radiologists. Methods This retrospective study included 144 GIST patients (65 high-risk, 79 non-high-risk) who underwent preoperative CT and US. Three feature sets (clinical + CT, clinical + US, clinical + CT + US) were compared using LASSO-logistic regression (C = 1.0) with 5-fold cross-validation (CV). The best feature set was then used to train six classifiers: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting, Light Gradient Boosting Machine, and Support Vector Machine. The optimal model was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration curve, decision curve analysis (DCA), and SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP). Sensitivity analysis (train/test split), radiologist comparison experiment, and subgroup analysis were performed. Results The clinical + CT + US feature set achieved a mean area under the curve (AUC) of 0.910 (95% bootstrap CI: 0.853–0.947), comparable to clinical + CT (0.904) but higher than clinical + US (0.805); the combined set was selected for its comprehensive information content. Among the six algorithms, RF showed superior performance with a CV AU…

title: Hybrid streaming LSTM and transformer XL model for real-time urban traffic congestion prediction
abstract: Introduction Urban traffic congestion results in substantial economic and environmental costs. However, conventional fixed-timing and linear models (ARIMA) lack the ability to accurately model the intricate and non-linear dynamics of real-time traffic. Even though deep learning models like LSTMs have improved temporal modeling, they cannot handle very long-term dependencies. Methods In this study, we propose a hybrid streaming LSTM-transformer XL model combining LSTM’S strength in capturing short-term patterns with the long-range contextual interpretation of transformer XL, tailored for streaming inference of large-scale spatio-temporal data for sensor-level continuous forecasting. Our experiments were carried out on benchmark datasets METR-LA and PEMS-BAY. Besides that, we employed a robust preprocessing pipeline and an interactive Streamlit-based deployment for real-time visualization. Results For a six-step (30-min) horizon, the reported denormalized results are MAE/RMSE = 4.32/7.91 mph for METR-LA and 2.40/4.39 mph for PEMS-BAY. Discussion The results showed that the accuracy of the prediction, computational efficiency and feasibility of deployment in the context of ITS are well balanced. With the help of an interactive Streamlit dashboard and Ngrok, the live deployment occurs by streaming, making it possible to have live visualization, sensor comparison, and monitoring of …

title: Development, temporal validation, and external validation at a separate center of a prediction model for grade 3 or higher hematologic toxicity during the first chemotherapy cycle in patients with solid tumors
abstract: Objective To develop and validate a model using routinely available prechemotherapy clinical data to predict grade ≥3 hematologic toxicity during the first cycle of cytotoxic chemotherapy in patients with solid tumors. Methods This two-center retrospective cohort study included 1,100 patients treated at Qinghe County Central Hospital from January 2021 to December 2024 as the development cohort, 400 patients treated from January 2025 to June 2026 as the temporal validation cohort, and 560 consecutive patients from Xingtai Central Hospital as the external validation cohort. The primary outcome was any CTCAE version 5.0 grade ≥3 decrease in neutrophil count, anemia, or decrease in platelet count during the first cycle. Seventeen candidate predictors were prespecified. An Elastic Net penalized logistic regression model was developed and internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Model specifications and risk thresholds of 10% and 25% were locked before external validation. Results The primary outcome occurred in 19.4%, 20.5%, and 21.1% of patients in the development, temporal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. The final model included age, ECOG performance status, bone metastasis, hemoglobin, platelet count, albumin, eGFR, combination chemotherapy, platinum-containing regimen, planned relative dose intensity, and planned prophylactic G-CSF. The bo…

title: Testing the collapse-locality loophole in Bell experiments: recorder-scale dependence and a mass–distance scaling prediction
abstract: Bell inequality violations establish correlations incompatible with local hidden-variable theories, but their interpretation depends partly on when measurement outcomes become physically definite. This uncertainty underlies the collapse-locality loophole, which remains incompletely tested for spontaneous-collapse models. We examine this loophole by combining Kent’s causal quantum theory with the Ghirardi–Rimini–Weber (GRW) collapse model to derive a quantitative prediction for the Clauser–Horne–Shimony–Holt (CHSH) Bell parameter. Assuming independent exponential collapse times and effectively instantaneous outcome-dependent amplification, the combined framework predicts S(N,L) = 2√2 exp(−NλL/c), where N is the number of nucleons displaced into distinguishable recording configurations, λ is the GRW collapse rate, and L is the separation between measurement stations. The combined model predicts that increasing the amount of matter displaced by the recording apparatus could progressively weaken and ultimately eliminate the Bell correlations, even though the entangled particles and their detection remain unchanged. In contrast, standard quantum mechanics predicts that these correlations should remain unaffected by recorder scale. We propose systematically varying recorder scale at multiple station separations to map this transition rather than testing a single configuration. The pr…

title: Development and internal validation of a machine learning-based prediction model for radiation dermatitis in cervical cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy: a prospective study
abstract: Objective To develop and internally validate a machine learning-based predictive model for radiation dermatitis (RD) in cervical cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy. Methods A total of 251 cervical cancer patients receiving pelvic external beam radiotherapy were prospectively enrolled and randomly divided into a training set and a validation set at a 7:3 ratio. In the training set, LASSO regression was used to select predictors, and four models—logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and XGBoost—were constructed. Hyperparameter tuning was performed using grid search, model stability was assessed via 5-fold cross-validation, and DeLong tests were used to compare AUC differences among models. Model performance was evaluated in the validation set using AUC, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, precision, and F1 score. Calibration of the optimal model was assessed using calibration curves, the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and the Brier score. Results LASSO regression identified five predictors: age, immobilizer type, total dose, hypertension, and PNI. In the validation set, the LR model achieved an AUC of 0.810, sensitivity of 0.780, specificity of 0.760, accuracy of 0.773, and F1 score of 0.821; the AUCs for RF, SVM, and XGBoost were 0.854, 0.777, and 0.766, respectively. Overall, the LR model demonstrated excellent specificity comparable to the bes…

Computational and statistical approaches for sports injury prediction and risk factor identification: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract This systematic review examined computational and statistical approaches for sports-injury prediction and the identification of injury-related risk factors. A systematic search of six electronic sources covering publications from 1 January 2015 to 15 August 2025 was conducted, with the final search completed on 15 August 2025. Following the revised eligibility audit, 11 studies met the inclusion criteria. The included studies used athlete-related data derived from clinical history, anthropometric measurements, strength and range-of-motion assessments, training-load variables, and wearable or biomechanical sensors. The analytical approaches included conventional statistical models, supervised machine-learning methods, and process-mining approaches. Reported predictive performance varied across studies, populations, outcomes, and validation strategies and should be interpreted within the specific evaluation setting of each study. However, many studies relied on relatively small or selective samples, heterogeneous injury definitions and feature sets, and limited external validation. The evidence indicated that data-driven methods had potential to support sports-injury risk assessment, but their clinical and operational generalisability remained limited by methodological heterogeneity, incomplete validation, and inconsistent reporting. Future research should prioritise lar…

title: A two-network audit shows when conformal prediction intervals for solar irradiance forecasts remain valid at newly commissioned stations
abstract: Abstract A newly commissioned solar site needs trustworthy probabilistic forecasts immediately, yet conformal prediction’s coverage guarantee assumes local calibration data that a new site lacks. We audit this cold-start gap with leave-one-station-out experiments on two networks, 13 continental-US NOAA stations (donors 200–3700 km apart) and 28 PV-Live stations (donors 10–240 km apart), with four forecasters and four horizons (15 min to 6 h). Pooled-donor calibration with zero local data is near-nominal on average but not per station: at 6 h, only 54–69% of station-years stay within ± 2% points. Local calibration restores validity at horizons up to 1 h for three of four forecasters after a median 21–136 days of local data; a prospective self-certification rule reproduces this limit. At 3–6 h, most station-years never sustain coverage within ± 1% point through 182 days, a failure shared by dense donors and even a full local year, consistent with temporal drift. Delayed-feedback donor-seeded adaptive conformal inference holds every station’s marginal coverage near nominal by construction, at a Winkler-score cost of at most about 2% on identical evaluation steps for the learned forecasters, with occasional infinite intervals and a 30–60-day transient. We distill a deployment protocol for new solar sites.

title: Associated factors and exploratory prediction model for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in children with adenoid hypertrophy: a retrospective cross-sectional study with age-stratified analysis and assessment of radiographic–endoscopic agreement
abstract: Background Adenoid hypertrophy is commonly associated with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in children, but which parameters identify moderate-to-severe disease, and whether age modifies their associations, remain uncertain. We examined factors associated with moderate-to-severe OSA and the agreement between radiographic and endoscopic assessment. Methods In this single-center retrospective cross-sectional study, 244 children aged 3–14 years with adenoid hypertrophy who completed polysomnography (PSG), nasopharyngoscopy and radiography were included; moderate-to-severe OSA (obstructive apnea-hypopnea index > 5 events/h) was the outcome. Variables were summarized with effect sizes, 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and adjusted q values. Age interaction was tested; agreement between the adenoidal-nasopharyngeal (A/N) ratio and endoscopic obstruction was assessed with Bland-Altman analysis and concordance correlation (CCC). An exploratory logistic model including a body mass index (BMI)-for-age-and-sex z -score, tonsil grade, A/N ratio, age and sex was evaluated for discrimination and calibration. Results Of the 244 children, 140 had moderate-to-severe OSA, with higher BMI z -score, body weight, adenoid thickness and tonsil grade and lower oxygen saturation (all q < 0.05). No predictor was identified in preschool children, associations in school-age children did not survive adju…

title: Intelligent prediction of high-enthalpy gas environments for arc heaters based on the Bayesian optimization attention-aware network and transfer learning
abstract: Abstract Arc heaters are the core devices for simulating the aerothermal environment of hypersonic vehicles. To meet the demand for rapid and high-accuracy prediction of the high-enthalpy gas environment in segmented arc heaters, this study proposes an intelligent prediction method based on a Bayesian optimization attention-aware network (B-AAN) integrated with transfer learning. First, a feature-attention module is embedded into a multilayer perceptron to perform sample-dependent reweighting of the input features before they are passed to the shared multi-output prediction network. Subsequently, Bayesian optimization is employed to tune the model’s hyperparameters. Meanwhile, SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis is introduced to reveal the contribution mechanisms of different input features to the prediction results. Finally, a model transfer strategy is further incorporated to address the prediction of high-enthalpy gas environments under new operating conditions. The proposed model was validated using a multi-operating-condition database established from an arc heater experimental platform. The results show that, under conditions of different model initialization random seeds and fixed data partitions, this method achieves high prediction accuracy for arc voltage, arc chamber pressure, and enthalpy, with prediction errors below 3%. The transfer learning results further ind…

title: Research on Urban Traffic Flow Prediction Based on Time Series Analysis
abstract: Urban traffic flow prediction is a core component of intelligent transportation systems. Accurate flow prediction is of great significance for alleviating traffic congestion and improving the operating efficiency of road networks. Traffic flow data have complex characteristics such as non-stationarity, seasonality, and spatiotemporal coupling, and time series analysis methods for traffic flow prediction have continuously evolved from statistical models to machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid models. Focusing on temporal dependence modeling, this paper systematically reviews the basic principles, temporal feature processing capabilities, and applicable scenarios of four types of methods, with emphasis on what problems each type of method has solved and what problems remain. The analysis shows that statistical models laid the theoretical foundation for temporal modeling, machine learning expanded nonlinear fitting capability, deep learning has become the current mainstream because of automatic feature extraction and long-range dependence modeling, and hybrid models show advantages in accuracy and robustness in some scenarios. Current research still faces challenges such as insufficient dynamic road network modeling, difficulty in fusing multi-source heterogeneous data, inadequate prediction of abnormal events, poor generalization with small samples, and insufficient model …

title: Proceedings from the 2025 precision public health transdisciplinary conference: capacity building
abstract: Abstract The 2025 Precision Public Health Transdisciplinary Conference brought together over 150 attendees from five continents to discuss innovative research and advances in precision health and promote sharing of insights, with an emphasis on capacity-building in different contexts of precision public health, including non-Western settings and settings with constrained resources. The conference was hosted by the Precision Public Health Network and held virtually on 19–20 November 2025, featuring 11 invited speakers with expertise across key areas of precision public health and genomic medicine, and 20 oral and poster presentations selected from submitted abstracts. This report summarises the conference proceedings and key emerging themes, including the need to strengthen capacity through robust, inclusive data systems that reflect population diversity; meaningful community involvement in genomic medicine; integration of clinical, genomic and national health datasets; and evidence-based incorporation of innovative tools such as artificial intelligence (AI) to support analysis and decision‑making.
