English foundation-journal capacity building-platform empowerment: a three-dimensional integrated training model for the international competence of graduate students in precision agricultural aviation
abstract: Introduction The deep integration of precision agriculture aviation and artificial intelligence has created a global demand for high-level interdisciplinary talent with cross-cultural academic competence. Existing international graduate training in this field faces three persistent constraints: insufficient context-based application of academic English, low student participation in international scholarly publishing, and fragmented international exchange mechanisms that fail to form a continuous learning pathway. Methods This three-cycle action research was conducted from 2023 to 2025, supported by three institutional platforms: the National Center for International Collaboration Research on Precision Agricultural Aviation Pesticide Spraying Technology, the Innovation and Talent Recruitment Base, and the International Journal of Precision Agricultural Aviation (IJPAA). It constructs a three-dimensional integrated training model of “English Foundation – Journal Capacity Building – Platform Empowerment”, integrating dual-track academic English courses, a three-stage journal cultivation mechanism, and full supporting resources including international conferences and targeted global training exchanges. Results Over three years, over 450 graduate students received systematic training. 92.7% of participants met the predefined academic English proficiency standard; each student attend…

title: Data powerization: a structure–mechanism–capacity theory of data integration in China's county medical communities
abstract: Integrated county-level medical communities (CMCs) are China's principal vehicle for coordinating hospitals and grassroots facilities. Yet data integration across their members remains limited despite mature digital technology and repeated central mandates. This Hypothesis and Theory article develops a structure–mechanism–capacity framework to examine this puzzle. Holistic governance theory supplies the normative framework, and resource dependence theory supplies the explanatory framework. We analyse national policy documents from 2017 to 2026 and aggregate indicators from the China Health Statistical Yearbook (2017–2025 editions; indicators for 2019–2024). We introduce data powerization as a theoretically derived construct. It describes the hypothesised conversion of clinical data control into organisational resources protecting revenue, autonomy, and risk positions. This mechanism has not yet been directly observed or tested in Chinese CMCs. National statistics establish structural scope conditions, not organisational motives. Under fragmented governance, fee-for-service payment, and asymmetric resources, we hypothesise that data withholding can be rational. The three levels may then become mutually constitutive and produce circular lock-in. We distinguish this account from standards fragmentation, vendor lock-in, infrastructure deficits, and coordination failure. Three propo…

title: Capacity of driven piles in coral sand with particle breakage and pore pressure hysteresis
abstract: Coral sand area is widespread in coastal island and reef construction, where driven pile bearing capacity is critical. Particle breakage, a key factor distinguishing coral sand from terrigenous sand, is unaccounted for in current codes. This study derives and verifies an exponential relationship between the internal friction angle φs and relative breakage ratio Br. Based on triaxial and model pile tests, particle breakage is quantified as Br, relationships are established with breakage reduction factor βc for tip resistance and particle breakage correction factor α for shaft resistance. On this basis, it is found that lgt50 has a linear relationship with tip resistance, and Dr has a linear relationship with shaft resistance. These are, respectively, defined as pore pressure hysteresis reduction factor and loose filling correction factor. Incorporating these factors into code formulas, this study produces a new bearing capacity calculation method for driven piles in coral sand. A verification example shows less than 10% error compared to static load test, meeting engineering requirements and providing a scientific basis for design.

title: Spatiotemporal configurations of emergency logistics responsiveness capacity: a panel QCA study of Chinese provinces
abstract: Purpose Effective emergency logistics responsiveness capacity (ELRC) is critical for mitigating natural disaster impacts, yet the configurational mechanisms through which ELRC emerges and evolves across both time and space remain inadequately understood. This study aims to identify how multiple conditions combine to produce high ELRC in Chinese provinces, and whether these pathways are temporally stable or spatially heterogeneous. Methodology Drawing on Configurational Field framework, this study employs panel data Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA) to examine provincial ELRC in China from 2017 to 2024. A balanced panel of 29 provinces over eight years (232 observations) is analyzed. Six conditions are calibrated into fuzzy sets: disaster cost, fiscal autonomy, technological infrastructure, digital infrastructure, government attention, and social participation. Consistency is decomposed into pooled, between—unit (temporal), and within—unit (spatial) components to diagnose spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Findings Five equifinal pathways to high ELRC are identified, categorized into four models: Routine Administration, Collaborative Governance, Fiscal Substitution, and Technological Autonomy. Notably, non-high ELRC exhibits a convergent pattern, characterized by a “Structural Vulnerability Trap” where the absence of fiscal and technological foundations prevents social participa…

title: Shift from Flexible Random Coil to Rigid β-Strand-Rich Conformations Is Associated with Impaired HDL Cholesterol-Acceptor Capacity in Familial Hypercholesterolemia
abstract: Abstract Patients with familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) exhibit alterations in high-density lipoprotein (HDL) composition and structure, although the functional consequences of these changes have not been fully characterized. Our objectives are to explore the HDL lipid composition, morphology, and structural properties in patients with FH and healthy controls and to investigate their potential association with HDL cholesterol-acceptor capacity. Dynamic light scattering (DLS) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) showed no differences in HDL particle size or morphology between groups. In contrast, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) showed higher total lipid-to-protein, esterified lipid-to-protein, and cholesteryl ester-to-protein ratios in HDL from patients with FH. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) further revealed a cholesteryl ester (CE) core phase transition in FH-HDL that was not detected in control HDL, indicating differences in the organization of the HDL lipid core. Analysis of the FTIR amide I band revealed a reduced random-coil content and increased β-strand content in HDL proteins from patients with FH compared with controls. Random-coil content was positively associated with HDL cholesterol-acceptor capacity, whereas the β-strand subcomponent at 1620–1626 cm–1 was inversely associated with cholesterol-acceptor capacity in the overall and FH c…

title: Strengthening laboratory capacity for trachoma serological surveillance in Amhara, Ethiopia: use of the lateral flow assay
abstract: Trachoma programs are increasingly using serological tools to complement clinical indicators and to measure current and historical transmission of Chlamydia trachomatis (Ct). In January 2024, the Amhara Trachoma Program in Ethiopia implemented the Pgp3 lateral flow assay (LFA) for trachoma serosurveillance through the regional public health laboratory system. Three Amhara Public Health Institute Trachoma Molecular Laboratory scientists were trained and passed competency testing on the assay. The scientists then conducted LFA testing on dried blood spot (DBS) samples collected during a December 2023 trachoma impact survey in Tach Gaynt, Amhara. During testing, 2,542 DBS samples were processed over 12 days. Age-specific seroprevalence and seroconversion rates (SCRs) were estimated. Among children ages 1–5 years, seroprevalence was 20.8% [95% confidence interval (CI)]: 17.4–24.6%), and the SCR was 7.9 per 100 child-years (95% CI: 4.7–13.5). Among children ages 1–9 years, seroprevalence was 26.0% (95% CI: 22.9–29.4%), and the SCR was 7.0 per 100 child-years (95% CI: 4.0–10.6). Seroprevalence among individuals ages ≥ 15 years was 85.8% (95% CI: 83.9–87.4%). Trachomatous inflammation-follicular prevalence among children ages 1–9 years (TF 1–9 ) was 28.6% (95% CI: 22.1–35.4%), and Ct infection among children ages 1–9 years was 5.7%, suggesting ongoing transmission. The concordance bet…

title: Photocatalytic efficacy and antibacterial capacity of TiO2/SiO2 nanocomposite
abstract: Titanium dioxide (TiO2), a well-known photocatalyst, is used for the degradation of organic dye pollutants and to treat industrial wastewaters by considering its photostability, non-toxicity, high activity, and low cost. In that view, the current study investigates the efficacy of TiO2/SiO2 nanocomposite formed by the hydrothermal synthesis route where the composite has been characterized by the powdered X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray analysis (EDAX), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET), and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) and UV–visible spectroscopies. The TiO2/SiO2 nanocomposite’s crystallinity and crystal structure are confirmed by the XRD, the functionality by the FTIR, and the morphology and elemental composition with SEM/EDAX analysis. From the BET investigations, the nanocomposite showed an improved pore volume, surface area, and voids, while the TiO2 nanoparticles optical properties significantly enhanced following the composite formation with SiO2. On testing towards Rhodamine B degradation, the TiO2/SiO2 nanocomposite (against pure TiO2) confirmed for a high photocatalytic degradation ability due to its large surface area and pore volume that all supported for the effective dye adsorption in aqueous solutions. Further tests of antibacterial activity of TiO2/SiO2 nanocomposite towards Gram-positive and Gram-negative bact…

title: Problems of synchronization of the transmission mechanism of monetary and macroprudential policies
abstract: Subject. The toolkit and transmission mechanism of monetary policy and macroprudential policy in the context of their increasing impact on the banking sector and the economy as a whole. Objectives. The search for ways to synchronize the transmission mechanism of monetary policy and macroprudential regulation to ensure financial stability and sustainable economic growth. Methods. The study is based on a review of international and Russian scientific literature using bibliometric analysis to identify key research areas, as well as on the analysis of regulatory documents of the Bank of Russia and statistical data of the banking sector of the Russian Federation. Results. The coordinated orientation of monetary policy and macroprudential policy enhances their mutual influence, however, their goals, objects and speed of reaction to instruments may differ, giving rise to regulatory asymmetry. A low correlation has been revealed between the minimum capital requirements and the actual capital adequacy values of the banking sector, which casts doubt on the effectiveness of macroprudential allowances as instruments of macroprudential policy. Conclusions. title: Pyrolysis Dechlorination of Sewage Sludge–Fly Ash Co-Hydrothermal Solid Products: Chlorine Distribution, Migration Pathways, and Mechanism
abstract: Abstract This study investigated the effects of pyrolysis temperature (500–900 °C) and sewage sludge (SS)/municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (FA) mass ratio (1:0, 4:1, 2:1, 1:1) on thermal dechlorination of cohydrothermal solid-phase products using a fixed-bed pyrolysis system. The distribution of chlorine (Cl) among pyrolytic products was systematically analyzed, and the migration-transformation pathways and dechlorination mechanisms of Cl during pyrolysis were comprehensively explored. The results demonstrate that pyrolysis can effectively facilitate Cl removal from cohydrothermal solid residues. The dechlorination efficiency is primarily governed by pyrolysis temperature and the SS/FA mass ratio; higher temperatures and elevated SS fractions promote Cl volatilization from the solid matrix, achieving a maximum Cl removal rate of 42% under optimized conditions. In pyrolysis residues, interconversion occurs between water-soluble and acid-soluble inorganic Cl. Ca5(PO4)3Cl and Ca3Al2(SiO4)2Cl4 are the dominant acid-soluble Cl-bearing species, and high-temperature crystal evolution dominates the speciation transformation of inorganic Cl. The migration and transformation of Cl are synergistically modulated by inorganic minerals, organic matter, and carbonaceous components via multiple mechanisms, including mineral-induced Cl immobilization, HCl generation and capture, direc…

title: OP038: Mechanism Study on Platelet miR-200a-3p Abnormality and Endothelial Cell Dysfunction Mediated by Acute Ischemic Stroke
abstract: Abstract Introduction Background and Objective: To investigate the expression changes of miR-200a-3p in platelets of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and its mechanism of regulating endothelial cell function through platelet-derived microvesicles (PMVs). Methods qRT-PCR was used to analyze the expression ofmiR-200a-3p, and logistic regression, ROC curve, and clinical scores (NIHSS, mRs) were combined to analyze correlations. Bioinformatics was applied to predict target genes and enrich pathway analysis. Dual-luciferase assays, cell transfection, and co-culture experiments were used to verify the targeting relationship, PMV-mediated transfer process, and effects on endothelial cell function. Results miR-200a-3p was highly expressed in platelets of AIS patients and was an independent risk factor for disease onset. Target genes were enriched in the atherosclerosis pathway, with MAPK14 as a core gene regulating ET-1 and VEGFA. PMVs (150 nm, positive for CD9/CD63/TSG101) transferred miR- 200a-3p to endothelial cells, downregulating MAPK14 and upregulating ET-1/VEGFA. miR- 200a-3p promoted endothelial cell proliferation, apoptosis, and vascular network formation. Conclusion Platelet miR-200a-3p participates in the pathological process of AIS by targeting and inhibiting the MAPK14/c-Jun pathway through PMVs, providing a new target for diagnosis and treatment.

title: Genesis Mechanism of the Huitang Geothermal Field in Hunan Based on Hydrochemical and Isotopic Characteristics
abstract: The Huitang geothermal area is a significant geothermal resource zone in Hunan Province. Understanding its formation processes is crucial for geothermal development. The study explores the genesis of the Huitang geothermal field. Hydrochemical and isotopic analyses of geothermal and cold waters provide the basis for the interpretation. Two primary heat sources are identified: terrestrial heat flow contributes to the thermal input, while radioactive decay in granite provides additional heat. Calculations using the SiO₂ geothermal temperature scale yield reservoir temperatures ranging from 135.69ºC to 140.98ºC. However, the mixing of cold water leads to an underestimation of these values. Therefore, corrections are required using the silicic acid diagram method. Hydrogen and oxygen isotope analysis reveals lateral recharge originating from higher-elevation terrain to the west. The inferred recharge elevations range from 443.84 to 493.67 m, and the circulation depth is 3411-3562 m. The chemical type of the geothermal water at Huitang is primarily HCO₃<sup>‒</sup>-Na. Gibbs diagram analysis shows that rock alteration dominates hydrothermal-rock interactions. Strontium isotope (δ⁸⁷Sr/δ⁸⁶Sr) signature analysis confirms a significant influence from silicate rock alteration and dissolution. The study integrates these results to propose a geothermal genesis mechanism for the Huitang fie…

title: Academic adaptation and evaluation of an interview-only selection mechanism among undergraduate transfer students in clinical medicine
abstract: Abstract Objectives This study evaluated academic adaptation and the validity of an interview-only selection mechanism for undergraduates transferring into clinical medicine. Methods Academic records of 175 transfer students (2022–2025) and survey data from 91 respondents were analyzed. Subgroup analyses included transfer type, original major, pre-transfer GPA rank, and National College Entrance Examination (NCEE) percentile. Results After transfer, median rank shifted from the top 10–30 % category to the 30 %–50 % category (p<0.001). Pre-transfer GPA rank was significantly associated with post-transfer performance (p<0.001), whereas NCEE percentile was not. Grade-retention students achieved better outcomes (p=0.004) but 40.0 % reported decreased confidence. The most frequently cited deficiencies of the interview-only mechanism were lack of feedback and excessive subjectivity. As only admitted students were included (survivorship bias), the perceived consistency between interview performance and academic outcomes reported by most respondents is a descriptive finding rather than validation of the mechanism. Transfer students showed a structural decline in relative rank, with substantial individual variation. Conclusions The interview-only mechanism has notable limitations; a composite model with written tests, structured interviews, and a trial period merits consideration as a p…

title: Multi-Field Coupling Damage Evolution Mechanism and Life-Cycle Cooperative Reinforcement Theory for Simply Supported Slab Bridges: Mechanism Revelation, Quantitative Model and Engineering Validation
abstract: Simply supported slab bridges account for over 70% of small-to-medium span bridges globally, serving as the backbone of urban-rural transportation networks. However, coupled effects of cyclic vehicle loads, aggressive environmental erosion, material aging, and fatigue damage accumulation have caused widespread concrete cracking, steel corrosion, stiffness degradation, and bearing capacity reduction in in-service bridges, posing a critical challenge to sustainable infrastructure operation. Existing studies predominantly focus on qualitative description of individual diseases and empirical application of single reinforcement technologies, lacking systematic quantitative theories for multi-field coupling damage evolution and life-cycle collaborative design of reinforcement systems. To address this gap, this paper establishes a four-dimensional "load-environment-material-time" coupled damage evolution constitutive model based on field inspection data of 126 in-service simply supported slab bridges, revealing the "cracking-corrosion-further cracking" positive feedback damage mechanism that accelerates structural failure. On this basis, the mechanical-durability collaborative enhancement mechanisms of three classic reinforcement technologies (section enlargement, bonded reinforcement, and external prestressing) are systematically clarified, and refined time-varying mechanical models …

title: A UHPLC-Orbitrap MS-based serum untargeted metabolomics study integrated with network analysis and machine learning reveals the mechanism of acacetin against hepatocellular carcinoma
Exploration of the mechanism of Shenbai Fuzheng granules in improving cancer-related fatigue in non-small cell lung cancer based on network pharmacology and molecular docking
abstract: Abstract: Background: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is frequently complicated by cancer-related fatigue (CRF), which severely impairs quality of life. Shenbai Fuzheng Granules (SFG) have been reported for clinical use, but their mechanisms remain unclear. Objectives: This study aims to generate mechanistic hypotheses for SFG in alleviating CRF secondary to NSCLC using network pharmacology and molecular docking. Methods: In this in silico study, SFG constituents were retrieved from Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology Database and Analysis Platform (TCMSP; oral bioavailability ≥30%, drug-likeness ≥0.18); structures from PubChem; targets predicted via SwissTargetPrediction (probability ≥0.10) and mapped through UniProt. NSCLC/CRF targets were collected from GeneCards and OMIM. A TCM-ingredient-disease-target network was built with Cytoscape 3.10.0; hub nodes were identified by degree, betweenness and closeness centrality. A protein-protein interaction network was constructed using STRING (Homo sapiens; minimum score 0.900). Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment were performed in the Database for Annotation, Visualization and Integrated Discovery (DAVID) with Benjamini–Hochberg correction (adjusted p < 0.05). Molecular docking used AutoDock Vina 1.1.2 with PDB structures; reliability was assessed by re-docking co-crystal…

title: High Temperature Corrosion of UO2 by Sodium: Outward Growth Process, Reaction Mechanism, and Physico-Geometrical Kinetic Model
abstract: Abstract In this paper, focusing on the interaction between UO2 and liquid sodium in the presence of dissolved oxygen, the original experimental setup is used to determine the change in the corrosion layer thickness over time under controlled conditions. Experimental evidence of the outward growth mechanism of the trisodium uranate is provided, based on the markers’ method. The formalism of heterogeneous kinetics is used to model the reaction. To interpret the kinetic data, the use of chemical kinetic concepts is extended to heterogeneous reactions. A reaction mechanism is proposed, specifying that the intermediate species involved in heterogeneous reactions are adsorbed species and point defects. Solving this mechanism offers an expression for how the reaction rate is dependent on temperature and the oxygen molar fraction in sodium. Moreover, based on the assumption of a rate-determining step of diffusion of uranium vacancies, the change in reaction rate over time can be determined and is then successfully compared with the experimental data.

title: Comprehensive system and mechanism of State regulation of scientific and technological development of the Donetsk People's Republic
abstract: Subject. Formation of a comprehensive system of State regulation in the scientific and technological sphere of the Donetsk People's Republic. Objectives. To determine the content of the integrated system and mechanism of State regulation of scientific and technological development of the Donetsk People's Republic. Methods. The validity, reliability and argumentation of the research results are ensured by the use of systems analysis, formal logic, general scientific methods of cognition: analysis and synthesis, induction and deduction, generalization. Results. The possible components of an integrated system of scientific and technological development, which in one form or another can be implemented in the region, are highlighted and presented in the form of rulers. The components that are currently not being implemented in the DPR have been identified. For the purposes of State regulation of scientific and technological development, systematic and functional approaches to the formation of a mechanism of state regulation are proposed. The implementation of a systems approach based on the analysis of the powers and identified relationships of public authorities has allowed us to propose a model of an integrated system that reveals the content of the mechanism of State regulation and the most comprehensive system of State regulation of scientific and technological development of th…

title: The Stressor–Action Mechanism (SAM) model: mediating mechanisms linking job stressors to health impairments by integrating multiple theoretical perspectives
abstract: Although the general association between job stressors and health impairments, including effect sizes and directions, has been well researched, the underlying mechanisms of these effects have received relatively less attention. This study developed a cross-theoretical, integrative, mechanism-based stressor–action mechanism model (SAM model) that incorporates action mechanisms (AMs) from different theoretical perspectives to explain the processes through which stressors exert their health-impairing effects. We theoretically derived potential AMs that may underlie the effects of selected job stressors on health impairment. Based on a comprehensive review of meta-analyses on the effects of different job stressors and stress theories in the respective meta-analyses, three overarching processes comprising 14 AMs can be identified: (1) basic-need-related processes: experienced unsafety, fear of renewed threat or violence, perceived loss of control, and autonomy, competence, and relatedness frustration; (2) energetic processes: resource depletion, experience of acute resource loss, experience of resource threat, experience of failed resource investment, depletion of self-control capacity, and recovery impairment; and (3) self-related processes: self-esteem undermining and moral integrity undermining. Specifically, we propose theoretically derived stressor-to-AM pathways for 23 selecte…

title: Mechanism of Bitterness and Astringency Generation Induced by High Temperature in the Drying of Enshi Yulu Green Tea
abstract: Abstract High-temperature drying can induce bitterness and astringency in green tea, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Using Enshi Yulu as the research object, it was found that drying temperature significantly affects its appearance, color, aroma and taste. UHPLC-MS/MS identified 152 nonvolatile compounds, of which 36 were initially screened as differential metabolites (VIP > 1 and FDR-adjusted p < 0.05). Combined with DOT value analysis, taste recombination, and omission and addition/reduction tests, EGCG, EGC, rutin and l-glutamic acid were identified as the key substances regulating taste. Compared with low-temperature drying (90 °C), the increase in EGCG, EGC and rutin contents, and the decrease in l-glutamic acid content are the core reasons for the intensified bitterness and astringency of taste under high-temperature drying (120 °C). In vitro simulation experiments also verified these patterns of substance changes. In production, a low-temperature long-time drying process at 80–90 °C could be recommended.
venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

title: Engineering sucrose-based carbon foams for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons immobilization in aged industrial soil
abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are persistent and carcinogenic contaminants frequently found in industrial soils. Naturally aged contaminated soils represent a major remediation challenge because long-term sequestration reduces contaminant bioavailability, leaving a residual contamination dominated by persistent high-molecular-weight PAHs. In this work, sustainable sucrose-derived carbon foams were evaluated as soil amendments for PAH immobilization in a naturally aged contaminated soil. Carbon foams with tuneable pore architecture and surface chemistry were synthesized through a simple and scalable self-foaming process. Their remediation performance was assessed by determining both total PAH concentrations and the bioavailable fraction. The soil was characterized by a predominance of high-molecular-weight PAHs of pyrogenic origin, with a total PAH concentration of 17 mg kg - ¹ and a bioavailable fraction below 20%. Among the synthesized sucrose carbon foams, those prepared using citric acid and iron nitrate as additives showed the highest remediation efficiencies, reducing total PAH concentrations by up to 80% and 67%, respectively, while reducing carcinogenic PAHs below the detection limit. However, the amendments differed in their effects on the bioavailability of the remaining PAHs. The citric acid-derived foam increased the relative proportion of bioavailable PAHs…

title: Not all carbon pools recover alike: contrasting vegetation and soil carbon trajectories following agricultural land abandonment in the Alpine forests
abstract: Agricultural land abandonment is widespread across Europe and is often followed by spontaneous forest regeneration. This unintentional rewilding process has considerable potential to mitigate climate change through carbon (C) sequestration. However, the relative contribution of different ecosystem C pools and the factors controlling their recovery across environmental gradients is not yet fully understood. We investigated ecosystem C accumulation trajectories following land abandonment across four Alpine ecoregions (Western Alps, Central Alps, Eastern Alps, Prealps) using a chronosequence approach spanning approximately 80 years of secondary succession. A total of 120 sites representing transitions from croplands and meadows to forests were surveyed. Carbon pools were quantified in all major ecosystem pools, including vegetation, deadwood, litter and soil. Linear mixed-effects models and Random Forest analyses were used to assess the relationships between Cpools, time since abandonment (TSA), previous land use, climatic conditions and topography. Total ecosystem C increased significantly with TSA, primarily through vegetation accumulation, progressively shifting C storage from soil-dominated conditions in recently abandoned sites towards a greater contribution from vegetation in forest stands. However, accumulation trajectories differed among ecoregions, with the Eastern Alps e…
venue: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change

title: P–M INTERACTION ANALYSIS OF ECCENTRICALLY LOADED REINFORCED CONCRETE COLUMNS STRENGTHENED WITH CARBON FIBER REINFORCED POLYMER (CFRP) COMPOSITE MATERIALS
abstract: This paper investigates the structural efficiency of strengthening eccentrically loaded reinforced concrete columns subjected to combined axial compression and bending moment using carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) composite materials. A B20-grade concrete column with a rectangular cross-section of 300×450 mm, a corner rounding radius of r = 25 mm, and 6Ø20 mm (A400 grade) longitudinal reinforcement was analyzed. Based on the plane-sections hypothesis and the ACI 440.2R-17 design methodology, complete P–M interaction diagrams were constructed for three structural configurations: an unstrengthened control column (C0), a column confined solely with two layers of transverse CFRP wrapping (C1), and a hybrid system combining longitudinal CFRP laminates with transverse CFRP wrapping (C2). Analytical results across eccentricity levels (e0 = 0, 50, 120, and 220 mm) reveal that under concentric and low-eccentricity loading (e0 ≤ 50 mm), transverse wrapping increases axial load capacity by 2.7–2.9%, whereas under high eccentricity (e0 = 220 mm), the hybrid C2 scheme enhances ultimate load-carrying capacity by 9.4% and bending moment resistance up to 260.0 kN·m, providing more than twice the gain of transverse wrapping alone.

title: PP005: An Uncommon Clinicoradiological Manifestation of Severe Carbon Monoxide Poisoning: Bilateral Cerebral Watershed Infarction Presenting as Spastic Paraplegia
abstract: Abstract Introduction Carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning commonly causes hypoxic–ischemic brain injury, with basal ganglia and diffuse cerebral involvement being well recognized. Cerebral infarction is a recognized but uncommon complication. Bilateral cerebral watershed infarction presenting with isolated spastic paraplegia is an uncommon clinic radiological pattern. We describe this presentation following severe CO poisoning. Methods The clinical course, neurological findings and cerebral and spinal neuroimaging of a patient with persistent lower-limb weakness following severe CO poisoning were reviewed. Findings were correlated with the distribution of cerebral lesions, while spinal imaging excluded a cord lesion. Results A 29-year-old previously healthy man presented to our unit one month after severe CO poisoning with persistent inability to walk despite recovery of consciousness and general medical condition. He had initially presented to another hospital with profound coma (GCS 3/15), hypotensive shock requiring intensive care, mechanical ventilation and tracheostomy. Initial CT brain showed diffuse cerebral edema consistent with hypoxic–ischemic injury. At present, examination revealed bilateral spastic paraplegia with preserved upper-limb function, no sensory level and no sphincter involvement. Repeat CT showed bilateral parasagittal hypo densities, while MRI demonstrated b…

title: Libration-Driven Nonradiative Decay and Rigidity-Controlled Emission in a PyBox Ligand
abstract: Abstract The optical output of a flexible chromophore depends on how freely it can move, yet the specific motion responsible is usually inferred from structure rather than identified. Here, the emission of IDPD, a pyridine-bis(oxazoline) ligand, is traced to a single identifiable class of low-frequency nuclear motion. Quantum-chemical calculations locate that motion and establish the emitting state as a locally excited transition, excluding a twisted intramolecular charge-transfer pathway. IDPD is essentially nonemissive in mobile solution and brightens continuously as the medium is stiffened across glycerol–ethanol mixtures, on cooling, through a series of imidazolium ionic liquids, and in the solid state, with excited-state lifetimes lengthening in the same order. Identifying the responsible coordinate, rather than inferring it, offers a route to fluorophores whose environmental responsiveness is designed rather than discovered.
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B

title: Life-cycle assessment of carbonation-cured steel slag–cement composites: environmental benefits and pathways toward low-carbon-dioxide construction materials
abstract: Steel slag substitution for cement clinker has been recognised as an effective approach to reducing the carbon dioxide footprint of cement-based materials; however, the life cycle environmental implications of the incorporation of high-volume steel slag and the contribution of carbonation-induced carbon dioxide (CO2) sequestration to environmental performance remain insufficiently understood. This study presents a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) of dry-pressed steel slag–cement composites containing 60 wt% steel slag (S60), benchmarked against a Portland cement composite (S0). The specimens were cured by 2 h carbonation (20 vol.% carbon dioxide) followed by 72 h 20°C water curing. The LCA model was developed in SimaPro 9.3 using CLCD and Ecoinvent databases, with impacts evaluated using ReCiPe 2016 at midpoint and endpoint levels. S60 reduced global warming potential by 48% relative to S0, primarily owing to the substantial reduction in clinker consumption associated with high-volume steel slag substitution, with additional environmental benefits arising from increased carbon dioxide sequestration during carbonation curing (0.0624 t CO2/m3 for S60 as opposed to 0.0478 t CO2/m3 for S0). Midpoint results also showed reductions in fossil resource scarcity (41%), mineral resource scarcity (52%), terrestrial acidification (38%) and freshwater eutrophication (32%). Endpoin…

title: Neutron scattering by clusters of the carbon-12 nucleus
abstract: Above the Hoyle resonance, the excited states of the 12C nucleus begin to overlap strongly. To separate them, various theoretical models are used, which predict different spectra of angular distributions of the decay products (α-particles). This leads to discrepancies of or more in cross-section estimates in the ENDF, JEFF, and JENDL nuclear databases. In this work, we investigate the hypothesis of a possible connection between the population of resonant states of the 12C nucleus and the scattering of a projectile neutron on various clusters of the 12C nucleus with a 3α or α –8Be structure. For this purpose, the interaction of 14 MeV neutrons with a stationary 12C nucleus was investigated, where within a nuclear potential well of depth 45 MeV and width L ∼ 5 fm, the de Broglie wavelength of the incident neutron (λ n ≈ 0.58 fm) allows it to spatially resolve intranuclear clusters (λα ∼ 1.68 fm). Therefore, as a first rough approximation, independent quantum scattering of a neutron off the 12C nuclear clusters is modeled in momentum-energy representation, leading to nuclear excitation. To this end, the partial differential cross sections for nα and n – 8Be scattering were adopted from the phenomenological phase-shift analysis by Tilleessen et al. (IAEA EXFOR Database). Monte Carlo simulations allowed us to calculate the mass-energy distribution of the excited 12C* nucleus and mak…

title: Carbon footprint of 3D-printed orthodontic models for clear aligner therapy: a deterministic modeling study of printer type, layer thickness and model design
abstract: Abstract Background Clear aligner therapy relies on the repeated production of 3D-printed orthodontic models, yet which manufacturing choices govern the resulting carbon footprint is unclear. Layer thickness and printer selection are often presented as the main levers. This study aimed to identify which workflow variable, among layer thickness, printer choice and model design, determines the manufacturing-related carbon footprint of orthodontic model production. Methods A gate-to-gate deterministic model quantified the manufacturing-related carbon footprint of an 80-model, refinement-inclusive orthodontic workflow across three dental systems: the Asiga MAX 2 and SprintRay Pro S (digital light processing, DLP) and the Formlabs Form 3B+ (stereolithography, SLA). Two layer thicknesses (50 and 100 μm) and solid versus hollow designs were compared. Rated power was obtained directly from the manufacturers. The footprint combined resin, electricity and isopropyl alcohol (IPA) post-processing. Each input was varied by ± 20% in a deterministic sensitivity analysis, and 100,000 Monte Carlo iterations sampled eleven inputs across their full plausible ranges. Results Modeled footprints for 80 solid models ranged from 23.3 to 27.9 kg CO 2 eq. Layer thickness changed the total by 0.8–6.0%, below a 10% threshold set in advance. Consumables accounted for 75–89% of the total against 11–25% for …

title: Electric Vehicle Charge Scheduling and Power Trading Using Shuffle Attention Network Enhanced by Star Bison Optimization
abstract: The growth of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has increased the demand for smart charging systems that optimize energy usage and reduce strain on the power grid. The current EV charging strategies are often uncoordinated, resulting in peak load issues and increased energy costs. An efficient scheduling scheme is required to align charging with grid conditions. Hence, a new Shuffle Attention Network with Star Bison Optimization Algorithm (SA-Net_StarBOA) is established for EV Charge Scheduling and Power Trading. Primarily, an EV system with multiple Charge Stations (CS) and EVs is simulated. Then, charging scheduling is performed using the devised StarBOA, which is a combination of Star Fish Optimization (SFOA) and African Bison Optimization (ABO). Here, power prediction is done by the Shuffle Attention-Network (SA-Net) for predicting the availability of charging power. Besides, if the power is not available for charging the vehicle, then optimal electricity trading is done by SA-Net. Here, SA-Net is trained with the developed StarBOA model. Furthermore, SA-Net_StarBOA acquired a low average waiting time of 5.100 seconds (s), distance of 39.464 meters (m), the number of charged EVs of 145 and power of 96.580 Watts (W) at iteration 1,000.
venue: Journal of Circuits, Systems and Computers

title: Transcritical carbon dioxide heat pumps could decarbonize industrial hot-water supply in Kenya
abstract: Industrial hot-water demand in sectors such as food processing, healthcare, hospitality, laundries, and beverage production is often met by combustion-based boilers, creating a significant opportunity for efficient electrification. This perspective assesses the suitability of transcritical carbon dioxide heat pumps for supplying water at 60 °C–120 °C in Kenyan industries using a tiered application-screening framework. Carbon dioxide has negligible ozone-depletion potential and very low global-warming potential, along with favorable heat-transfer properties and a substantial temperature glide in the gas cooler. These characteristics enable high outlet temperatures and the possibility of simultaneous heating and cooling. However, refrigerant selection alone does not guarantee efficient operation. Factors including elevated water-inlet temperatures, suboptimal temperature matching, inadequate high-side pressure control, and intermittent loads can reduce the coefficient of performance and undermine economic viability. Applications approaching 120 °C require closer assessment of equipment capability and operating conditions. Successful deployment requires application-driven design that incorporates low return-water temperatures, stable heat sources, variable-capacity operation, thermal storage, heat recovery, and climate-responsive control. Dairies, beverage plants, commercial laund…

Research on carbon emission efficiency network resilience characteristics and optimization strategies for the Yangtze River Delta urban agglomeration
Evaluating Optimized Potentially Net-Negative Algal Systems and Biochar Production in Global Carbon Sequestration Strategies
abstract: To meet the 1.5 °C climate target established by the Paris Agreement, the deployment of Negative Emission Technologies (NETs) is imperative. Algal systems, comprising microalgae and macroalgae (seaweeds), offer one of the most efficient biological pathways for Carbon Capture and Utilization (CCU). However, the long-term sequestration potential of algal biomass is often limited by rapid decomposition. The integration of algal cultivation with biochar production via thermochemical conversion (pyrolysis) offers a synergistic approach to “net-negative” carbon accounting. This review evaluates recent advancements in optimized algal cultivation, focusing on metabolic engineering and photobioreactor design to maximize CO2 uptake. Furthermore, it analyzes the conversion of algal residues into biochar, assessing its stability, nutrient-recycling potential, and soil-sequestration capacity. Key constraints persist: drying wet algal biomass is energy-intensive, wastewater-grown biomass can carry heavy metals into biochar, and most integrated systems have yet to move beyond the laboratory scale. Most reported productivities, biochar yields and stability estimates come from laboratory experiments or models, and pilot-scale evidence for complete algae-to-biochar chains is still scarce. Where biochar storage is included, life cycle assessments range from net removal (e.g., −3.71 to −2.17 kg CO…

title: An experimental concept for investigating photon emission during positronium formation
abstract: Abstract A theoretical model of an experiment allowing verification of the presence of hypothetical photons emitted during the positronium atom formation has been presented. If such photons exist, they could be used as a new spectroscopic tool for studying the electronic properties of a wide class of molecular materials.
venue: Journal of Physics B: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics

title: Recent Progress on Modulation Strategies of Metal-Organic Framework-Based Catalysts for Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Reduction
abstract: The electrochemical reduction of CO2 offers a promising route for realizing the artificial carbon cycle by producing value-added fuels and chemical feedstocks. In the past decade, metal-organic frameworks (MOF) have emerged as the promising platform for CO2 electrocatalyst design owing to their structural tunability, ultrahigh surface areas, and well-defined active sites. Many efforts have been devoted to the modulation of MOF-based catalysts for enhancing electrochemical CO2 reduction performance. In this review, we present a comprehensive survey of recent advances in the design and modulation strategies of MOF-based catalysts for CO2 electroreduction, covering intrinsic structural regulation, fabrication of MOF-based composite materials and design of MOF-derived materials. Furthermore, the prevailing challenges and future outlooks based on recent research advances are highlighted. These summarized findings and prospects afford critical references for the design of high-performance MOF-based catalysts and help further broaden the application prospect of electrocatalytic CO2 reduction.

title: Valorization of Raphia hookeri seed biomass into carbon nanodots for investigation of their electrochemical capabilities
abstract: Abstract Creating sustainable avenues of transforming agricultural biomass into useful nanomaterials is a strategic feature of the circular bioeconomy and the renewable energy technologies. This article is aimed to carbon nanodots (CNDs) production using the Raphia hookeri seed (RHS) biomass by the controlled hydrothermal carbonization, phosphoric acid activation and their application as the electrochemical energy storage. The CNDs characterized for UV - Vis spectroscopy, Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), powdered x-ray diffraction (pXRD), fourier transform infrared (FTIR), energy dispersive x-ray (EDX) as well as thermogravimetry analysis (TGA). The UV-Vis spectrum showed a typical absorption peak of 280 nm whereas the plot of the Tauc’s showed an optical band gap of 2.40 eV which showed semiconducting behavior. SEM and TEM analysis revealed quasi-spherical nanoparticles of average diameter 6.35 nm, which is in agreement with the crystallite size obtained in pXRD, 3.428 nm. FT-IR spectra revealed electron-rich functional groups at 3485 cm⁻¹, 2980 cm⁻¹, 1650 cm⁻¹, 1350 cm⁻¹, 1150 cm⁻¹ and 550 cm -1 which correspond to hydroxyl (O–H) stretching, aliphatic C–H stretching vibration, carbonyl (C = O) stretching vibration, C–H bending vibration, C–O stretching vibration and O-P-O respectively. EDX verified C (72.7%) and O (27.3%) elemental c…

title: Enhanced Droplet-Mode Brown Carbon Formation at High Relative Humidity in Urban Beijing: Size-Resolved Chromophore Evidence for Aqueous Processing and Its Radiative Impacts
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric brown carbon (BrC) affects radiative forcing, yet how relative humidity (RH) modulates its size-dependent effects remains unclear. We conducted size-resolved measurements in urban Beijing during winter-early spring to investigate how RH modulates BrC size distributions, chromophore composition, and optical properties. Results show that the geometric mean diameter (GMD) of water-soluble BrC (WS-BrC) increased from ∼0.45 μm at low RH (≤40%) to ∼0.80 μm at high RH (≥60%), with less growth for water-insoluble BrC (WI-BrC). This growth was driven by an increased droplet-mode contribution (from ∼45% to ∼80%), and WS-BrC grew 1.6 times faster than WI-BrC. Chromophore analysis links this to aqueous processing: chromophores associated with aqueous formation pathways─nitrosalicylic acids, N-heterocyclics, and nitrocatechols─increased 13.2-, 9.8-, and 7.1-fold in droplet mode at high RH, versus 2.0–3.1-fold for primary emission chromophores. Mie calculations show that the RH-induced GMD shift moves WS-BrC into the steepest declining region of the single scattering albedo (SSA)–size curve, where size growth dominates the decrease of SSA and far outweighs the contribution of composition changes, implying stronger heating under humid conditions. These findings identify RH as a key modulator of BrC size distributions and optical properties via aqueous processing, highligh…

title: Interactive land in E3SM process-level models: impacts of land–atmosphere coupling in SCM and DP-SCREAM
abstract: Process-level modeling is central to diagnosing and improving atmospheric parameterizations in Earth system models, yet continental single-column and convection-permitting process configurations are often run with prescribed surface fluxes, limiting realism and consistency with fully coupled global simulations. Here we develop, document, and demonstrate a reproducible workflow to enable fully interactive land–atmosphere coupling in both the E3SM single-column model (E3SM SCM) and the doubly periodic configuration of SCREAM (DP-SCREAM). The approach leverages a multi-year offline-forced E3SM/ELM integration to provide spun-up land initial conditions and introduces an offline preprocessing method that generates DP-SCREAM–compatible land restart files by extracting and replicating the appropriate ELM grid cell (including its landunit/column/PFT hierarchy) across the doubly periodic domain, avoiding intrusive modifications to ELM I/O. Using daily-initialized two-day hindcast integrations, we apply this framework to two years over GoAmazon and ten years over the Southern Great Plains, and to targeted short process-level cases (CASS and GoAmazon single/double pulse). Interactive land coupling is required to reproduce key near-surface thermodynamic biases characteristic of global coupled simulations, including warm 2 m temperature biases and the elimination of spurious persistent noct…

title: Tolvaptan exposure and longitudinal changes in left ventricular function and right ventricular–pulmonary artery coupling in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
Aperiodic EEG–pupil coupling during naturalistic video viewing in children and adolescents
abstract: Introduction Multimodal physiological approaches can characterize complementary aspects of emotional processing that are not available from a single signal. Methods We analyzed synchronized high-density EEG and eye-tracking recordings from a publicly available developmental dataset of children and adolescents younger than 18 years who viewed negative, neutral, and positive naturalistic videos. The SPRiNT algorithm provided time-resolved aperiodic EEG Exponent and Offset estimates, and their dependence with pupil diameter was quantified using mutual information (MI) and correlation-based coupling metrics within labeled scalp sensor groups. Results In the original analysis, Friedman tests showed a consistent condition effect for both Offset-pupil and Exponent-pupil MI across all six scalp groups (Kendall's W = 0.762 − 0.830, all p FDR < 1 0 - 7 ). Pairwise tests showed greater MI during the negative video than during the neutral or positive videos (standardized r = 0.869 − 0.874, all p FDR < 1 0 - 7 ), whereas no neutral-positive MI difference was detected. Discussion By integrating cortical spectral dynamics with a peripheral measure of arousal and attention, this approach provides a framework for studying brain-autonomic coordination during naturalistic emotional processing in children and adolescents.

BQEB TwinAgentBench: A Reproducibility-First Benchmark for Digital Twins and Multi-Agent AI in Trustworthy Energy Systems
abstract: Digital twins and multi-agent artificial intelligence are increasingly proposed together for intelligent energy management — coordinating distributed energy resources, balancing virtual power plants, and orchestrating demand response across many independently-acting components — yet no reproducible benchmark evaluates this specific combination under a governed, versioned architecture. This paper introduces BQEB (BIO-Quantum Energy Brain) TwinAgentBench, the fifth module of the BQEB research program. Consistent with the architecture established across Papers 1–4, TwinAgentBench introduces no new architectural layer: it registers as the fifth module of the existing Benchmark Evolution Layer, alongside ForecastBench, SecBench, FoundationBench, and ExplainBench. The framework specifies eight benchmark tasks spanning digital twin state estimation, twin synchronization and fidelity assessment, multi-agent coordination, consensus formation, adaptive control, fault recovery, human-in-the-loop intervention, and open-world adaptation, formalized as a 6-tuple B = (W, A, T, C, E, R) over twin models, agent ecosystems, tasks, inter-agent communication, evaluation, and reproducibility artifacts. Eleven component metrics — spanning twin fidelity, synchronization accuracy, temporal consistency, agent coordination, consensus stability, communication efficiency, adaptation quality, fault recover…

title: Information systems utilization and financial reporting quality: evidence from an Indonesian local government
abstract: Purpose: to examine the effects of the regional financial management information system (RFMIS) and the regional management information system for regional assets (RMISRA), both partially and simultaneously, on financial reporting quality (FRQ). Method: this study employed a quantitative approach with an explanatory research design. The research was conducted at the department of public works and spatial planning of Bengkalis regency, Indonesia, involving 34 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using structured questionnaires measured on a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using descriptive statistics, validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, and multiple linear regression analysis. Findings: RFMIS has a positive but statistically insignificant effect on financial reporting quality, whereas RMISRA has a positive and statistically significant effect. Simultaneously, both information systems significantly influence financial reporting quality. These findings suggest that effective regional asset management information systems play an important role in improving the accuracy, completeness, and reliability of local government financial reporting. Implications: the need to optimize information system utilization to improve financial reporting quality and accountability. Originality: lies in examining the combined and individual e…

title: Bypassed Oil Recovery in High-Temperature, High-Salinity Heterogeneous Carbonate Reservoirs by Aqueous Ketone Solution
abstract: Abstract Recent studies have shown that 3-pentanone remains aqueous-stable and non-emulsifying while altering wettability under extremely harsh reservoir conditions (e.g., 372.15 K and 200,000 ppm). This study investigates bypassed-oil recovery using aqueous 3-pentanone in heterogeneous carbonate rock under high-temperature, high-salinity (HTHS) conditions, with an emphasis on how preferential flow affects the ketone’s phase partitioning, in situ accumulation, and convective oil displacement. A spontaneous imbibition (SI) experiment was first conducted using formation brine (FB: 224,358 ppm), sulfate-rich injection brine (IB: 54,471 ppm), and 1.1 wt % 3-pentanone in IB (3pIB) to evaluate 3-pentanone-induced wettability alteration and oil recovery from bypassed regions. Corefloods were then performed by injecting 3-pentanone at its aqueous solubility limit in FB (0.3 wt %) and IB (1.1 wt %) under secondary and tertiary flooding conditions in carbonate cores selected to represent preferential-flow behavior. The SI experiment showed that 3-pentanone enhanced capillary-driven imbibition and recovered additional oil beyond that achieved with IB alone. In corefloods, IB and 3pIB injections improved oil recovery relative to FB injection. Material-balance analysis showed that preferential flow accelerated 3-pentanone breakthrough to 0.27 PVI, compared with the 1.92 PVI predicted by the…

title: The emotional labor of AI integration: a constructivist grounded theory study of academic librarians' work with generative AI tools
abstract: Purpose This study examines how academic librarians in Nigeria experience and manage emotional labor when they integrate generative artificial intelligence (AI) into reference services, and how that labor is carried out through epistemic work. Design/methodology/approach A constructivist grounded theory study was conducted in three academic libraries (federal, state and private) in Kwara State, Nigeria. Twenty-one reference, liaison and systems librarians took part through semi-structured interviews, non-participant observation of AI-mediated reference consultations and artifact analysis. Data were analyzed through initial and focused coding, constant comparison and memo writing. Findings Reference librarians' anxiety centered on professional credibility, liaison librarians' on bias in AI outputs and systems librarians' on technical instability. Librarians managed these feelings through two forms of epistemic work: epistemic vigilance, the alertness that sets how closely an output is checked, and epistemic stewardship, the verification and correction done to protect patrons. Trust calibration linked this work to the confidence librarians could honestly show patrons. Critical incidents restarted the cycle, and its burden was heavier where policy, training and technical support were thin. Originality/value The study proposes epistemic emotional labor as a construct for knowledge …

Aerospace Power Electronics, Energy Management and Power Distribution Architectures for Fuel Cell-Powered Hybrid-Electric Aircraft and eVTOLs: A Review
abstract: Fuel cell-powered hybrid-electric aircraft and electric Vertical Take-Off and Landing (eVTOL) systems are emerging as promising solutions for sustainable aviation due to their potential for low-emission and high-efficiency propulsion. However, integrating multiple onboard energy sources, including hydrogen fuel cells, batteries, and distributed electric propulsion systems, introduces significant challenges for energy management, onboard power distribution, and the integration of aerospace power electronics. This paper reviews energy management strategies and power distribution architectures for fuel cell-powered hybrid-electric aircraft and eVTOL systems. Various propulsion configurations, including series, parallel, turboelectric, and fuel-cell hybrid-electric architectures for regional aircraft, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and urban air mobility platforms, are examined. Energy management approaches, including rule-based, optimization-based, predictive, and intelligent control methods, are evaluated with emphasis on hydrogen consumption, system reliability, component degradation, and mission adaptability. Particular attention is given to aerospace power electronics, including high-voltage DC power distribution, bidirectional DC/DC converters, electric propulsion drives, and wide-bandgap semiconductor technologies such as silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) for…

Clinical utility of dual-energy CT–guided gout management: a single-centre retrospective before-and-after study
abstract: Abstract Background Dual-energy CT (DECT) can visualize monosodium urate (MSU) deposition, but evidence is limited regarding potential clinical benefits of DECT beyond diagnosis in gout. Objectives To evaluate potential clinical benefits of performing DECT beyond diagnosis in patients with gout. Methods We conducted a retrospective pre-/post-implementation study at the rheumatology outpatient clinic of Jeju National University Hospital, Jeju, Republic of Korea (May 2016–April 2020). DECT was introduced in May 2018. Among patients who underwent DECT, DECT positivity and disease-duration discrimination were assessed using ROC/AUC and cutoffs were explored. For prognostic comparisons, analyses were restricted to patients without clinically apparent subcutaneous tophi at baseline and compared the DECT-performed group with the no-DECT group using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Results A total of 722 patients were included (no-DECT n = 506; DECT performed n = 216). Among DECT-performed patients, 110/216 were DECT-positive (50.9%). Disease duration showed limited discrimination for DECT positivity (AUC 0.626). In prognosis analyses ( n = 645), IPTW-weighted flare outcomes were similar between groups (any flare: OR 1.26, 95% CI 0.87–1.83; flare count: IRR 1.37, 95% CI 0.94–2.01), and change in serum urate did not differ (β 0.01 mg/dL, 95% CI − 0.32 to 0.3…

title: Food Waste at the Methodological and Territorial Crossroads: A Comparative Analysis of Urban and Rural Management in Mexico
abstract: The transition from the concept of garbage to municipal solid waste has made it possible to recognize waste as a flow with economic, environmental, and social potential. Within this perspective, food waste can be addressed through prevention, redistribution, and valorization strategies. Globally, nearly 50% of household waste corresponds to organic waste, including food, gardening residues, and fruit and vegetable scraps. It is necessary to design effective strategies to reduce food loss within households through waste differentiation, hierarchy-based management, and intersectoral articulation. In Mexico, the category “food waste” lacks normative precision, limiting the accurate measurement of actual food loss and constraining progress toward the SDG 12.3 target. In this context, the present exploratory study proposes a more detailed classification that distinguishes prepared food waste from broader organic waste, representing a pioneering effort within the constraints of current Mexican regulations. This research employed a quantitative, exploratory–descriptive approach to characterize household food waste in two contrasting localities: Acapulco de Juárez and Cuetzalan del Progreso; different socioeconomic levels were considered in the study. Direct physical measurements of waste generation and composition were carried out, along with structured surveys on consumption and disc…

title: Characterization and application of water–rock interaction on coal-rock stress field during roof drainage
abstract: Abstract As mining advances to greater depths, large‑scale drainage of thick confined aquifers in the roof can induce rock bursts. Existing studies focus mainly on mechanical effects and often overlook the water–rock interactions and their time‑dependent effects. We investigated the effects of the interactions on the coal–rock stress field through laboratory tests, theoretical analysis, and a field case study of a deep, water‑rich longwall face in Shandong, China. Laboratory tests indicate that water–rock interactions arise mainly from physical erosion and chemical dissolution. These processes reduce uniaxial compressive strength, tensile strength, elastic modulus and cohesion, while increasing the internal friction angle of sandstone. It makes the compressive, tensile and shear failure modes of sandstone transform from brittleness to ductility, and the morphology of fracture surfaces evolve from smooth to rough and cracked. The deterioration is flow-velocity dependence, with higher velocities accelerating the process. Under high flow velocity conditions, it is also time‑dependent: compressive strength and elastic modulus are most sensitive within the first 30 days, whereas tensile strength remains sensitive up to 60 days. Based on the premise of rock mass stiffness degradation induced by water–rock interaction, a stress transfer model incorporating the degradation effect of dy…

Integration of environmental, social and managerial risks into the corporate financial risk management system of an industrial organization
abstract: Subject. Financial relations that arise as a result of the transfer of environmental, social and managerial risks of an industrial organization into the parameters of corporate financial decisions. Objectives. Substantiation of a procedure that converts non-financial risks into quantitative financial parameters, and development of an indicator that comparably measures the burden on an organization's ESG risks. Methods. Methods of discounted cash flow analysis, estimation of expected losses, scenario analysis and comparative analysis of corporate reporting were used; calculations were carried out on the basis of consolidated financial statements according to international standards and non-financial statements of a large Russian mining and metallurgical organization for 2025. Results. A six-step algorithm is substantiated that combines three channels for transferring risk into financial parameters, namely, cash flow adjustment, a premium to the discount rate, and redundancy in case of rare catastrophic events. The ESG risk…

title: An Integrated Fracturing Fluid for Sand Stabilization, Permeability Enhancement, and Desorption Promotion in Coalbed Methane Reservoirs: From Molecular Design to Field Application
abstract: Abstract Deep CBM reservoirs exhibit strong adsorption, high sensitivity, and abundant nanopores. The conflict between permeability enhancement and methane desorption during fracturing restricts gas production. A friction reducer FRD-1 was prepared using a fluorinated zwitterionic monomer (FSA), and a staged functional-switching mechanism was established via group association, controllable ester cleavage, and in situ block self-assembly. With a quaternary ammonium-polyether sand-stabilizing/permeability-enhancing agent SCF-1, an integrated multifunctional fracturing fluid was constructed. The dual-network structure of the system improves thermal/shear resistance, drag reduction, and proppant-carrying performance. After gel breaking in the reservoir, it becomes a salt-resistant desorption promoter; wettability regulation of the coal surface and hydrophilic-film control promote methane desorption by up to 2.43 mL/g. Through zeta-potential regulation and bridging, the broken fluid inhibits >80% fines migration and enhances pack conductivity. In >50 Ordos Basin wells, average sand concentration rose by 2–3% and single-well gas output by >15%. This molecular-design/staged-release/multicomponent framework supports efficient deep CBM stimulation.

title: MOLECULAR GLUES IN CANCER THERAPY: FROM SERENDIPITY TO RATIONAL DRUG DESIGN
abstract: Molecular glues modulate protein function by inducing or stabilizing interactions between proteins. Their most clinically established oncological application is targeted protein degradation, in which a compound redirects a ubiquitin ligase towards a therapeutically relevant neosubstrate. The elucidation of cereblon-dependent degradation by thalidomide analogues transformed a longstanding clinical observation into a mechanistic framework for drug discovery. Subsequent discoveries involving DCAF15, DDB1, BCL6 polymerization and conformationally induced BRD4 recruitment revealed that productive proximity can arise through several distinct architectures. Structural biology, genetic perturbation and quantitative proteomics now permit increasingly deliberate optimization of these mechanisms, although general prediction of a successful glue for an arbitrary protein pair remains unresolved. This narrative review examines the transition from phenotypic discovery to rational design, emphasizing the difference between explaining a mechanism, optimizing an established interface and prospectively selecting a new target–partner interaction. It also assesses clinical evidence in multiple myeloma, including the 2026 accelerated approval of an iberdomide-containing regimen and randomized evidence for mezigdomide, while distinguishing these developments from preclinical advances in solid tumors.…

title: Design and biomechanical validation of a zero-profile self-stabilizing 3D-printed titanium mesh cage for anterior cervical corpectomy and fusion
abstract: Background Anterior cervical corpectomy and fusion (ACCF) is an essential surgical procedure for cervical spondylotic myelopathy and other cervical pathologies. Conventional titanium mesh cage (TTMC) combined with anterior plate fixation provides immediate stability but is associated with postoperative dysphagia, subsidence, and screw loosening. To address these drawbacks, a novel 3D-printed self-stabilizing titanium mesh cage (3D-STMC) was designed with patient-specific anti-subsidence rings and integrated self-stabilizing fixation plates for zero-profile reconstruction. Its biomechanical performance was evaluated via finite element (FE) analysis and in vitro ovine cervical testing. Methods A C2–C7 three-dimensional finite element model was reconstructed from cervical computed tomography data. Two reconstruction strategies following C5 corpectomy were simulated. The first employed TTMC supplemented with an anterior cervical plate. The second employed standalone implantation of the 3D-STMC. The range of motion (ROM) of the operative segment was quantified. Peak von Mises stresses at the mesh-endplate interface and screw-bone interface were also measured. Adjacent-segment disc stresses were evaluated. All parameters were assessed under flexion, extension, lateral bending, and axial rotation. In parallel, fresh ovine cervical specimens were used to establish C5 corpectomy models.…

title: Ecological-Restoration-Oriented Planting Design for Urban Waterfront Parks: A Case Study of Shuhe National Wetland Park in Ju County
abstract: Urban waterfront parks are important components of urban ecosystems and provide multiple functions, including ecological regulation, recreation, physical activity, and cultural interpretation. Under current conditions, waterfront spaces face a series of problems, such as habitat fragmentation, biodiversity loss, and ecological degradation. Using ecological restoration as its theoretical framework, this study examines Shuhe National Wetland Park in Ju County, Shandong Province. Field surveys and a literature review were used to systematically identify the principal challenges facing planting design in urban waterfront parks. A three-stage strategy is proposed: ecological matrix restoration, plant community reconstruction, and landscape-function enhancement. The study argues that planting design in urban waterfront parks should shift from an emphasis on visual beautification to an ecological-function-centered approach. By establishing near-natural plant community structures, increasing the proportion of native species, and strengthening ecosystem services, ecological restoration and landscape quality can be improved synergistically. The findings provide theoretical guidance and practical insights for ecological renewal in comparable urban waterfront spaces.

title: Design of a Dual-Branch Soft X-ray and Nano-ARPES Beamline for Operando Electronic Devices at HALF
abstract: Abstract The characterization of state-of-the-art electronic devices requires angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) systems capable of delivering simultaneous high energy resolution, enhanced probing depth, and superior spatial precision. To meet these demands, a soft X-ray beamline based on the Hefei Advanced Light Facility has been developed, serving both SX-ARPES and nano-ARPES endstations. The optical design incorporates a Variable Line Spacing Plane Grating Monochromator with three gratings to ensure continuous spectral coverage, delivering both exceptionally high photon flux and high energy resolution tailored for cutting-edge ARPES measurements. The SX-ARPES branch utilizes a Kirkpatrick-Baez (KB) mirror system to achieve a micro-focused beam spot of approximately 1.5 μm. For the nano-ARPES branch, while Phase I utilizes a Fresnel Zone Plate for hundred-nanometer scale imaging, its performance is constrained by diffraction-induced flux loss and fixed photon energies. Consequently, Phase II transitions to a nano-focusing KB mirror configuration, which significantly enhances photon throughput and enables continuously tunable photon energies. Performance evaluations confirm that the beamline satisfies the rigorous requirements for high-precision spectroscopic investigations across both experimental branches.
