Design of a simple bandpass filter using stub-loaded three-line parallel coupled-line structures
abstract: Introduction A simple wideband bandpass filter with high frequency selectivity is investigated to reduce the need for multiple resonators or complicated coupling networks. Methods The proposed filter employs two stub‐loaded three‐line parallel coupled‐line (TLPC) sections with open stubs. Odd‐/even‐mode analysis is used to investigate the transmission‐zero generation mechanisms and establish a design methodology. A prototype is fabricated on a Rogers 4003C substrate for experimental validation. Results The proposed configuration generates four transmission zeros. The measured prototype exhibits a center frequency of 2.5 GHz, a 3‐dB fractional bandwidth of 48%, covering 1.9‐3.1 GHz, and an insertion loss of 0.31 dB. Discussion The multiple transmission zeros improve the out‐of‐band characteristics, demonstrating the potential of the simple TLPC configuration for wideband filtering applications.

title: Unveiling the layered ecology of family math co-design with mothers, teachers and researchers
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine a family math leadership team (FMLT) within a larger Research-Practice Partnership with a school serving more than 80% of Latine students. The authors center co-design as a means to materialize the equitable aims of their collaboration for family math among nondominant mothers, teachers and researchers and explore: What are the practices that emerge when mothers, teachers and researchers co-design family math activities for their school? How do these practices enable the enactment of an equitable collaboration? Design/methodology/approach Taking a qualitative approach, the authors analyzed the six meetings held during one school academic year. They followed thematic analysis to identify the patterns in the practices enacted in the conversations among mothers, teachers and researchers, engaging the mothers and teachers in the initial stage of the analyses. Findings The practices identified in the FMLT conversations unveil an ecology of family math co-design in elementary schools sustained through three interconnected layers. The individual layer highlights the practices that supported team members in creating a humanizing space and moving beyond institutionalized roles. The relational layer portrays the linguistic and socio-emotional practices enacted to create relationships rooted in authentic cariño and confianza. Finally, a systemic layer ex…

title: Efficacy of home-based physical activity with or without virtual reality or telerehabilitation in people with Parkinson’s disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Parkinson disease (PD) is characterized by impairment in sensorimotor function that manifest itself as bradykinesia or dyskinesia, tremor, rigidity, and postural instability. The aim of this study was to carry out a systematic review and meta-analysis of the literature to determine the efficacy of home-based physical activity with or without virtual reality or telerehabilitation in people with PD. Method PubMED, Embase, Web of Science (WoS), PEDro, and CENTRAL were searched until February 2024. Only randomized controlled trials comparing home-based exercise with a control were included. The data extracted include the characteristics of the participants (age, sex, mental state and duration of the disease), the interventions (intensity, frequency and duration) used for both experimental and the control groups, the baseline, post-intervention and follow-up mean and standard deviation values on outcomes assessed in both experimental and the control groups and the findings of the included studies. Cochrane risks of bias assessment tool and PEDro scale were used to assess the risks of bias and methodological quality of the studies. Narrative synthesis and meta-analysis were used to summarize the results. Result Twenty-five articles from 24 studies ( n = 2067) were included. The experimental group improved more significantly in ADL (SMD = −0.78, 95% CI = −1.03 to −0.26, p =…

title: Antioxidant, antifungal and anti-inflammatory activities and acute toxicity of ethanol extracts from various organs of Capparis spinosa L.
abstract: Capparis spinosa L. is a versatile plant with prospects for biodiversity conservation, pharmaceutical applications and the food industry. The purpose of this study was to assess the composition, antioxidant activity, acute toxicity, anti-inflammatory activity and antifungal activity of extracts from various organs, as well as the total alkaloids and polyphenols of the plant C. spinosa growing in the Southern Aralkum. The antioxidant activity of C. spinosa organ extracts showed the highest activity in the stems-leaves [half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of the lowest IC50 was 155 μg/mL], while the lowest activity was observed in the roots (with the highest IC50 of 535 μg/mL). The IC50 values for the total alkaloids and polyphenols were 124 and 182 µg/mL respectively. The median lethal dose (LD50) of all the obtained substances was determined to be greater than 2000 mg/kg. Regarding anti-exudative effects, the reference drug indomethacin, at a dose of 10 mg/kg, showed 45.9 % inhibition, a level also observed with the stem-leaf and root extracts at doses of 100 mg/kg. The highest inhibition was exhibited by the total alkaloids at 200 mg/kg, demonstrating a 59.4 % anti-exudative effect. Among the tested pathogens, Fusarium oxysporum displayed the highest sensitivity to all the extracts. Specifically, the stem-leaf and root extracts effectively inhibited fungal growth (14 …

title: Projected climatic suitability and spatial overlap with cropland for Lanzhou lily [Lilium davidii var. willmottiae (E.H.Wilson) Raffill]: implications for cultivation assessment
abstract: Introduction Climate change may alter the geographic distribution of climatically suitable areas for Lanzhou lily, but changes in climatic suitability do not necessarily correspond to changes in cropland overlap. Methods Using 72 occurrence records and nine environmental predictors, we modeled the current and future climatic suitability of Lilium davidii var. willmottiae (E.H.Wilson) Raffill with an optimized MaxEnt model under four CMIP6 scenarios and four future periods. We characterized projected changes in climatic suitability and examined the spatial overlap of highly suitable areas with cropland at national and Gansu provincial scales. Results The model achieved a mean AUC of 0.994. Under current conditions, highly suitable areas covered approximately 6.49 × 10 4 km², with 61% located in Gansu Province. Future projections revealed scenario-dependent changes in suitability extent and geographic distribution. Under SSP1-2.6 during 2081-2100, the nationwide highly suitable area increased to 9.40 × 10 4 km², whereas cropland overlap decreased from 1.66 × 10 4 to 1.07 × 10 4 km². In Gansu Province, cropland overlap ranged from 0.81 × 10 4 to 3.53 × 10 4 km² across future projections. Discussion These findings demonstrate that expansion of climatically suitable areas does not necessarily increase their overlap with cropland, providing a preliminary spatial reference for further…

title: Dual-target in silico screening of a phytochemical library against tomato brown rugose fruit virus coat and movement proteins
abstract: We evaluated 98 phytochemicals, structurally related derivatives, and reference antiviral compounds against the coat protein (CP) and movement protein (MP) of Tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV, Tobamovirus fructirugosum) using a dual-target in silico screening approach. CP and MP were selected because they are associated with virion assembly, particle stability, and viral movement. Three-dimensional protein models were generated using AlphaFold, SWISS-MODEL, and Robetta, and the most suitable models were selected according to structural validation parameters. Molecular docking analysis showed binding energy values ranging from −7.5 to −3.9 kcal/mol for CP and from −8.1 to −4.2 kcal/mol for MP. Among the screened compound groups, flavonoid glycosides and alkaloids produced the strongest overall binding profiles. Diosmin, scutellarin, prunin, sanguinarine, and rutaecarpine met the dual-target selection criteria and were selected for detailed interaction analysis. These ligands formed hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, and π-related interactions with residues located in the predicted binding regions of both viral proteins. ADMET evaluation showed clear differences among the selected ligands in terms of polarity, lipophilicity, absorption-related properties, and drug-likeness parameters. Diosmin showed the strongest predicted dual-target affinity, whereas rutaecarpine disp…

title: Investigation of Plant Resources in Karst Landforms of Jiangxi Province, China I: Primula pingxiangensis, a New Karst-Cave Species of Primula (Primulaceae)
abstract: Primula pingxiangensis, a new species of Primula sect. Ranunculoides from Jiangxi Province, China, is described and illustrated. The new species was discovered at the entrance of a karst cave in Lianhua County, Pingxiang City, where it grows on shaded rocks at the cave entrance. It is characterised by pinnately deeply divided to nearly pinnatisect leaves densely covered with short glandular hairs, long-homostylous flowers, a white corolla with an appendage-free yellowish-green throat, emarginate corolla lobes with a small mucro in the sinus, and pale yellowish-brown to brownish-yellow anthers with yellowish pollen. Morphologically, it is most similar to P. xinningensis, but differs in having a white rather than pale red corolla, a smaller corolla limb, a shorter and stouter corolla tube, longer pedicels, and pale yellowish-brown to brownish-yellow anthers with yellowish pollen, rather than black pollen sacs as described in P. xinningensis. A preliminary conservation assessment is provided. A diagnostic comparison with related species and an updated key to Primula sect. Ranunculoides are also presented.

title: Biomass yield and forage quality of sorghum hybrids adapted to cool, short-season environments in the Upper Midwest U.S
abstract: Introduction Forage sorghum could provide a productive and resource-efficient alternative to corn silage in the Upper Midwest, but most available germplasm has been selected under warmer and longer-season conditions. This study evaluated the productivity, forage nutritive value, and environmental responses of sorghum hybrids across the Upper Midwest. Methods Twenty-three dual-purpose (DP), forage (F), and photoperiod-sensitive (PS) sorghum hybrids, including experimental materials developed by the public Iowa State University sorghum breeding program and commercial checks, were evaluated across 14 location–year environments at seven Upper Midwest locations during 2024 and 2025. Biomass yield, harvest dry matter concentration, forage nutritive value traits, and energy-yield indices were analyzed using linear mixed models. Growing-season weather variables were summarized by principal component analysis and used to define three environmental clusters representing warm-dry, warm-wet, and cool conditions. Results Sorghum type significantly affected biomass yield, dry matter concentration, acid and neutral detergent fiber, total digestible nutrients (TDN), and the energy yield index, but not crude protein (CP), lignin, relative forage quality (RFQ), or the energy yield stability index. Forage and PS sorghums produced greater biomass yield and energy yield index values than DP sorghum…

title: Evaluation Framework and Robustness Testing Methodology for AI Applications in Power Grid Operation and Management Information Systems
abstract: With the accelerating digital transformation of power systems, artificial intelligence (AI) technologies have been widely deployed across critical domains including energy management systems (EMS), distribution management systems (DMS), substation automation, and market operations. However, existing AI applications lack unified evaluation standards, particularly in security verification and robustness assessment. This paper proposes a comprehensive evaluation framework for AI applications in power grid operation and management information systems. Experimental validation is conducted on three typical AI tasks: transmission line defect detection, short-term load forecasting, and transient stability assessment. Testing results based on over one million historical data samples and 15,700 PSS/E electromagnetic transient simulation cases demonstrate that the proposed framework can effectively identify potential vulnerabilities of AI systems and quantify their robustness levels. The framework establishes a ten-dimension evaluation system covering functionality, adaptability, accuracy, reliability, security, interactivity, applicability, efficiency, compatibility, and robustness; proposes a four-level risk classification scheme (L1–L4); designs systematic robustness testing protocols covering adversarial attacks, input perturbations, out-of-distribution generalization, and data drift …

Research on a Bridge Virtual Load Test Method Based on Measured Influence Surfaces
abstract: Addressing the limitations of traditional static load testing, which is costly and requires traffic interruption, this paper proposes a virtual load test method based on the measured two-dimensional influence surface of a bridge. Using the two-dimensional strain influence surface identified through moving-vehicle tests, and combined with the principle of linear superposition, the virtual maximum response of a bridge under Highway-Class I standard lane loads is calculated without closing the bridge to traffic. A verification coefficient is obtained by comparison with finite element calculation results, enabling rapid assessment of bridge load-carrying capacity. Taking the old and new bridges of the Songjianghe River Bridge as engineering cases, virtual load tests were conducted on a simply supported hollow slab bridge and a five-span continuous box girder bridge, respectively. The results show that the verification coefficients at all measurement points satisfy the code requirements (0.924–0.995 for the hollow slab bridge and 0.899–0.938 for the continuous box girder bridge); multi-lateral condition analysis based on the influence surface can effectively characterize the force-transfer state of hinge joints in hollow slab bridges, providing a new approach for refined condition assessment of bridges.

title: Hydrogen-rich water enhances salt tolerance in zucchini (Cucurbita pepo L.) seedlings: insights from integrated transcriptomics and metabolomics
abstract: Introduction Soil salinization constrains crop growth and agricultural sustainability. Hydrogen-rich water (HRW), an eco-friendly plant growth regulator, mitigates abiotic stress damage in plants, but the regulatory mechanism underlying its effect on salt tolerance in zucchini seedlings remains unclear. Methods Zucchini seedlings at the one-leaf-one-heart stage were exposed to four treatments—control, NaCl stress, HRW alone, and combined HRW-NaCl—and the molecular basis underlying HRW-mediated salt tolerance was investigated via integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. Results Transcriptomic analysis identified 6,348 differentially expressed genes in response to NaCl stress, whereas HRW alone altered the expression of only 941 genes. Under salt stress, HRW upregulated genes involved in stress response, jasmonic acid signaling, and transcription factor activity and downregulated genes related to transmembrane transport and energy-consuming growth processes. A total of 449 core reversed genes were identified, which were enriched in amino acid metabolism, hormone signal transduction, and glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathways. Metabolomic analysis identified 2,791 metabolites. HRW modulated the phenylpropanoid and salicylic acid-related pathways, partially restoring phenolic acid and flavonoid synthesis suppressed by NaCl and attenuating the overaccumulation of stress-indu…

title: Pigeon manure and wheat bran, alone or together: barley growth and rhizosphere enzyme activity in a greenhouse pot experiment
From Soil Nutrient Stocks to Root-Accessible Flux: Rethinking Soil Fertility in Cropping Systems
abstract: Soil fertility assessments commonly rely on total nutrient stocks, operationally defined extractable pools, and field-calibrated crop responses. Although valuable for nutrient management, these measurements do not fully explain when, where, or how rapidly nutrients become accessible to active roots. This critical review synthesizes the soil chemical, microbial, and plant processes linking nutrient reserves with crop nutrient acquisition. We distinguish nutrient stocks, soil solution concentrations, resupply rates, root-accessible fluxes, and net plant acquisition, emphasizing their distinct meanings and measurement scales. Mineral dissolution, sorption and desorption, organic matter mineralization, diffusion, mass flow, microbial immobilization, and root activity jointly influence nutrient delivery. We critically compare conventional extractions with ion-exchange methods, diffusive gradients in thin films, isotope tracing, rhizosphere imaging, root observations, and serial plant nutrient budgets. Each approach measures a different component of nutrient availability, and no single indicator reliably captures the complete soil–root system across nutrients and cropping environments. We propose a multiscale, testable framework connecting nutrient release, delivery to active roots, actual plant acquisition, and crop performance. It distinguishes three questions: whether nutrients ar…

title: Sustaining Arsenic Control from Soil to Rice Grain under Wetting and Drying
abstract: Soil amendments can reduce arsenic mobility in paddy soils, but their long-term value depends on whether chemical retention translates into sustained protection of rice plants and harvested grain. This critical review examines how wetting, drying, and reflooding influence amendment performance through interactions among soil minerals, microorganisms, and roots. We distinguish three outcomes: persistent restriction of arsenic mobility in soil, reduced plant uptake and physiological injury, and lower inorganic arsenic concentrations in grain. Evidence from mineral investigations, rhizosphere experiments, amendment trials, and field irrigation studies shows that these outcomes do not necessarily coincide. Iron-associated retention can persist for years under some conditions, whereas redox transitions, amendment aging, organic matter interactions, and microbial transformations may alter treatment effectiveness. Root oxygen release, iron plaque formation, silicon availability, and internal arsenic transport further complicate the relationship between soil measurements and grain composition. Consequently, lower extractable soil arsenic or improved crop growth alone cannot establish lasting grain protection. We propose an evaluation framework linking soil and porewater speciation, root exposure, plant performance, and grain composition across water transitions and cropping seasons. Th…

title: Functional significance of microRNAs in plant regeneration
abstract: Abstract Plant regeneration involves the activation and reorganization of developmental programs to form new tissues, organs, or somatic embryos. Depending on the regeneration system, this may require differentiated cells to acquire developmental competence in response to wounding and hormonal cues. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are post-transcriptional regulators that shape developmental and environmental responses and are therefore well positioned to influence these processes. The present review examines current evidence that miRNA–target modules regulate plant regeneration, with emphasis on Arabidopsis. We distinguish functional evidence obtained by manipulating miRNAs or their target interactions in regeneration assays from hypotheses based on target-gene function or developmental expression patterns. Improved understanding of their spatial and temporal activity may help develop more precise strategies to enhance regeneration and transformation in recalcitrant crop genotypes.

title: Differential genetic resistance identified in Parastagonospora nodorum and Pyrenophora tritici-repentis-wheat pathosystems
Where It Takes Three to Tango! What Pasteuria can teach us about plant-parasitic nematodes through their multitrophic interactions
abstract: Summary The Pasteuria group of Gram-positive endospore forming bacteria are invertebrate parasites several of which infect plant-parasitic nematodes and they have for the last 50 years been recognised to have potential to be developed into microbiological control agents. However, there are still two perennial issues prohibiting their commercial development: i ) the inability to mass produce them; and ii ) their variable specificity. In this article I take a prejudicial stance articulating what we have learnt during the last 50 years regarding mass production and specificity, in particular what Pasteuria has taught us about plant-parasitic nematodes and what plant-parasitic nematodes have taught us about Pasteuria . Here, I will discuss: i ) endospores and the role of the collagen-based hair-like nap and other endospore appendages ( e.g. , ‘sporesilk’) and their roles in attachment to the infective juvenile cuticle and infection of the nematode; ii ) the role Caenorhabditis elegans has played in our understanding of bacterial infection of nematodes and its genetics; and iii ) in vivo and in vitro production systems and the potential approaches which are either unexplored or only in their infancy, including protoplast fusion, transgenic Bacillus thuringiensis and nanoparticle technology. In summary, I develop a multitrophic model that requires an understanding of the interactions…

title: Multi-spectral virtual staining for label-free histopathology using deep neural networks
abstract: Abstract Virtual staining (VS) has gained a significant interest for label-free characterization of unstained tissue-sections. The concept of VS lies on translating a label-free imaging technique such as auto-fluorescence for generating an equivalent histologically stained images using deep-neural-networks. Different endogenous fluorophores present in the sample have distinct excitation and emission bands, which can provide stain-free specificity of the molecules. However, conventional technique for studying emission of different molecules, restrict molecular specificity in the measurements. The present study explores multiple-spectral (MS) band pass filters in label-free imaging to gain richer information about distribution and diversity of these fluorophores. Our study includes a comparative analysis using MS and single long-pass (SLP)-approach for VS of unstained tissue-sections. It is observed that MS-approach provides a better training input to the model enhancing discriminative power of the neural network, even when trained for lesser epochs. The structural-similarity-index-measure (SSIM) map shows that use of MS-approach for training the model provides a high-SSIM of 0.94 whereas, SLP-approach provides an SSIM-values of 0.62. The ROC area of a model quantifies the ratio of true-negative and false-positive outputs. The testing results show that MS-approach (ROC ≈ 0.98) ou…

title: The structural alignment of virtual influencers and deepfake endorsers
abstract: Purpose This study aims to understand the effectiveness of virtual influencers versus deepfake endorsers in marketing. It investigates the cognitive processes shaping consumer responses to these digital endorsers. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the structural alignment theory, and across four studies using eye-tracking and experiments, the authors tested various factors, including eeriness, customer engagement, place identity and product manifestations. Findings Deepfake endorsers generally outperform virtual influencers in generating customer engagement and word-of-mouth. Virtual influencers are perceived as more eerie than deepfakes. Deepfakes are more effective in place-based contexts, but virtual influencers are more effective when endorsing NFTs compared to physical products. Research limitations/implications The paper contributes to the structural alignment theory to indicate that customers undergo a cognitive restructuring during the structural alignment process upon perceiving a digital endorser. Practical implications The findings help marketing managers guide the strategic selection of digital endorsers. Developing an endorser portfolio including both deepfake and virtual influencer endorsers is suggested. Matching specific endorsers with campaign target audiences, objectives and product types is recommended. Using different types of digital endorsers at vario…

title: qLWR5-1, a major QTL that modulates the grain length-to-width ratio in rice
abstract: Introduction Grain shape is a critical agronomic trait determining rice yield and grain quality. Mining novel quantitative trait loci (QTLs) and genes underlying grain shape facilitates the dissection of molecular mechanisms for rice grain development and supports breeding for improved yield and quality. Methods A doubled haploid (DH) population derived from grain-shape-differentiated indica restorer Hua 9 and japonica cytoplasmic male sterile line Chunjiang 99A was grown at the experimental base of Lianyungang Academy of Agricultural Sciences across 2023–2024. Using SNP arrays, we constructed a high-density bin genetic map for 140 DH lines. Phenotypic data for grain length, grain width and grain length-to-width ratio were collected for QTL mapping. Within the interval of a stable major QTL, gene annotation and parental sequencing were conducted to predict candidate genes. Homozygous knockout mutants in the Zhonghua 11 background were generated for sequence alignment, protein 3D structural prediction via SWISS-MODEL and phenotypic validation. Results and discussion The genetic map contained 612 bin markers spanning 2,595.12 cM, with an average marker interval of 4.24 cM. In two consecutive years, a total of 49 grain-shape QTLs were detected, each explaining 1.04–46.95% of phenotypic variance; 21 QTLs overlapped with previously reported grain-shape loci, and nine QTLs were stabl…

title: TRANSBOUNDARY WATER GOVERNANCE IN THE NILE BASIN: EQUITABLE UTILIZATION, SOVEREIGN DEVELOPMENT RIGHTS AND SOUTH SUDAN’S INTERNATIONAL LEGAL OBLIGATIONS
abstract: South Sudan’s accession to the Agreement on the Nile River Basin Cooperative Framework (CFA) in August 2024, preceding its entry into force on 13 October 2024, transformed the legal setting in which the country may pursue irrigation, navigation, wetland management and hydropower development. Yet the legal consequences cannot be reduced to a right to exploit an unallocated share of the Nile. The CFA binds its parties, whereas neighbouring non-parties remain connected to South Sudan through customary rules governing shared international watercourses. This article employs doctrinal treaty interpretation, international judicial reasoning and critical comparison of basin institutions to examine the interaction between equitable and reasonable utilisation, prevention of significant harm, prior assessment, planned-measures cooperation and domestic development authority. It identifies an analytical gap in approaches that treat sovereign development and transboundary responsibility as competing absolute claims. The article advances a doctrine of reviewable equitable development: the legal defensibility of a proposed Nile use depends upon a reasoned and revisable record showing the relevant equity factors, projected effects, alternative designs, affected-community interests, reciprocal consultation and adaptive compliance measures. Unlike a simple no-harm veto or a historical-allocation …

title: RESTITUTION AFTER MASS DISPLACEMENT: LEGAL REMEDIES FOR HOUSING, LAND AND PROPERTY CLAIMS OF SOUTH SUDANESE RETURNEES
abstract: This article examines the legal conditions under which South Sudanese returnees may recover housing, land and property lost through conflict-related displacement, and the limits of such recovery where competing occupation, state allocation and family interests have arisen. Reading the Land Act 2009 together with constitutional property guarantees and comparative restitution jurisprudence, it identifies a doctrinal difficulty that a simple preference for either former ownership or present possession cannot resolve: restitution must re-establish the claimant’s surviving legal interest without authorising a new, procedurally arbitrary displacement. The article proposes a doctrine of rights-preserving restitution sequencing. Under this framework an adjudicator separately determines the continuity of the prior right, legality of intervening allocations, evidentiary consequences of displacement, protected interests of secondary occupants and family members, proportionate remedies, and judicial supervision of implementation. The argument distinguishes the Land Act’s historical three-year filing rule from proposed extensions and treats international restitution principles as interpretive guidance rather than automatically applicable national legislation. It concludes that the principal legal task is to connect the recognition of customary and statutory land rights to reviewable, execut…

title: When Extended Peer Communities are not Feasible. “Bounded Science with Local People” and Knowledge Production in Violent Territories
abstract: Post-Normal Science (PNS) is operationalized through Extended Peer Communities (EPCs), which guarantee knowledge quality, legitimacy and policy relevance through participation and public deliberation of stakeholders with interest in a complex problem. Yet the minimum conditions that EPCs require—like trust, safety or freedom of speech—may be absent in violent territories under criminal control. Considering such contexts, in this article we ask whether research inspired by PNS can be operationalized where EPCs are not feasible due to the unacceptable risks that they would bear onto participants; in addition, we reflect on what forms of participatory knowledge production are possible when EPCs cannot be established and ask whether they would qualify as PNS. To address these questions, we conducted a case study in Chulavista, a large-scale lowincome housing development in the peri-urban fringe of Guadalajara (Mexico), which is affected by housing abandonment, criminal governance and violence. Given the safety constraints found, we adapted our methodological strategy and developed a bounded form of “science with the people” that incorporated extended facts but involved no plural deliberation nor extended peer review. We discuss its ethical implications, present our main contributions, and argue that whether such arrangements count as PNS remains an open question.

title: ПОРІВНЯЛЬНА ОЦІНКА ЕНЕРГЕТИЧНОЇ ЕФЕКТИВНОСТІ ГІДРАВЛІЧНИХ ПРИВОДІВ СІЛЬСЬКОГОСПОДАРСЬКИХ МАШИН З РІЗНИМИ СПОСОБАМИ РЕГУЛЮВАННЯ
abstract: The study presents a comparative assessment of three hydraulic drive architectures for controlling the working elements of trailed field sprayers: a constant-flow system with throttling control, a pressure-compensated variable-displacement pump system, and a Load-Sensing system. Technical data for the ELVORTI TETIS 24 and HORSCH Leeb 4 AX sprayers were used to define model limits. A 60-min calculation duty cycle was divided into five operating modes differing in duration, required flow rate, and load pressure. The same overall pump efficiency of 0.90 was assumed for all variants, while maximum operating parameters were equalized to isolate the effect of the control principle from differences between individual components. Under maximum load, the calculated energy indicators of the three systems were practically identical, whereas the differences increased rapidly under partial load. Over the model duty cycle, the constant-flow system consumed 5.46 kWh, the pressure-compensated variable-pump system 3.00 kWh, and the Load-Sensing system 2.06 kWh. The corresponding reduction in energy consumption relative to the baseline was 45.1 and 62.4%, respectively. The greatest contribution to this difference was produced by the long boom-stabilization mode characterized by low hydraulic power demand. Sensitivity analysis for a Load-Sensing pressure margin of 1–3 MPa and pump efficiency of 0…

title: Regulating Mobile Money Transactions In South Sudan: Consumer Redress, Unauthorized Transfers And Provider Liability
abstract: Mobile money has become a legally recognised payment mechanism in South Sudan, yet the validity of electronic value and the enforceability of an individual consumer’s reimbursement claim are distinct legal questions. This article interrogates that distinction through the Electronic Money Regulation 2017, as amended by the instrument published in August 2026, the wider consumer-protection and banking framework, and comparative jurisprudence concerning disputed electronic transfers. It argues that the central regulatory deficiency is no longer a complete absence of complaint procedures: the amended regulation specifies transaction records, system-failure reversals, contracting duties, agent supervision and timelines for complaints. Rather, a liability gap persists between authentication, consent, the production of technical evidence, allocation of loss and effective restoration of the customer’s position. Applying a doctrinal and functional comparative method, the article advances an original Authenticated Consent and Effective Reversal (ACE-R) standard. ACE-R requires proof of meaningful authorisation, provider-controlled auditability, provisional restoration subject to proportionate fraud safeguards, non-delegable responsibility for agent and system failures, and enforceable independent redress. It distinguishes unauthorised transfers from customer-authorised payments induced b…

title: Applicability of Russia's energy strategy for the structural modernization of domestic oil refining
abstract: Subject. This article focuses on the problems of regulatory and legal support for the policy of ensuring the deep modernization of the Russian oil refining. Objectives. The study aims to assess the applicability of Russia's Energy Strategy for the implementation of deep modernization of domestic oil refining. Methods. For the study, I used methods of comparative analysis and generalization of information from State authorities of the Russian Federation. Results. The article reveals that Russia has sufficient potential to tap into reserves of production capacities, with the exception of conditions for the implementation of a stress scenario. It also determines that it is advisable to use the indicator of the light petroleum products yield, while the depth of oil refining is more appropriate as an auxiliary value. Conclusions. The Energy Strategy does not seem to be a significant document from the perspective of ensuring the structural modernization of oil refining yet. It is necessary to review not only the refining indicators of the Energy Strategy, but also the structure of the document itself.

title: Genetic Algorithm-Based Optimization of Inverter Control Parameters for Grid-Connected Battery Energy Storage Systems
abstract: Background: Grid-connected battery energy storage systems (BESS) require current control that balances harmonic distortion and transient response across changing operating conditions. Aims: This study assessed whether genetic algorithm (GA) tuning of the dq-axis proportional–integral (PI) gains could improve inverter performance relative to conventional tuning. Methods: A 100 kW three-phase LCL-filtered inverter was modeled in MATLAB. Four PI gains were optimized on a combined active- and reactive-power step using a normalized objective comprising total harmonic distortion (THD), settling time, overshoot, and tracking error, with a constraint penalty. The best gains were evaluated across six scenarios (ten test cases); repeatability was assessed using 30 independent GA seeds. Two scenarios were cross-checked using a PWM voltage-source model in Simulink/Simscape Electrical. Results: At nominal conditions, THD decreased from 2.30% to 1.94%, settling time from 5.0 to 3.6 ms, and overshoot from 10.4% to 5.43% in the averaged model. THD decreased in all ten reported test cases, whereas settling time and overshoot improved in nine. However, during charge/discharge reversal, settling time increased from 4.2 to 24.7 ms and overshoot increased from 25.6% to 43.4%, revealing a substantial trade-off between harmonic reduction and transient performance. The Simscape cross-check reproduced …

Review of GeTe thermoelectric materials: recent progress, challenges and prospects
abstract: Germanium telluride (GeTe) is a promising lead-free thermoelectric material for intermediate-temperature power generation because of its intrinsically favorable electronic structure and strong anharmonicity. However, its performance is limited by excessive hole concentrations associated with Ge vacancies, the temperature-dependent rhombohedral-to-cubic phase transition, and the trade-off between electrical and thermal transport. This review summarizes recent advances in GeTe-based thermoelectrics from the perspectives of carrier modulation, electronic-band engineering, phonon transport engineering, device fabrication, and service reliability, with dedicated sections on n-type GeTe and thin films. We first discuss the structural, electronic, and phononic origins of the thermoelectric properties of GeTe. We then compare strategies for optimizing carrier concentration and carrier mobility and for enhancing the density-of-states effective mass. We analyze approaches to suppressing lattice thermal conductivity through defect engineering, phase-interface engineering, and nanostructural engineering. Moreover, particular attention is given to improving the conversion efficiency of GeTe thermoelectric devices and to service reliability. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges, including coupled electron-phonon optimization, long-term service stability, n-type GeTe optimization, and…

title: Representation Without A Contemporary Population Census: Electoral Equality, Constituency Delimitation And Constitutional Justice In South Sudan
abstract: This article asks whether a state may conduct constitutionally legitimate legislative elections using inherited constituency boundaries when an up-to-date population census is unavailable. South Sudan supplies an unusually exacting test. Following the decision to separate the scheduled December 2026 elections from a new census, its National Elections Commission declared 102 geographical constituencies derived from the 2010 electoral map, notwithstanding prolonged internal displacement, refugee movements, returns and changes in territorial administration. Existing commentary often presents this question as a binary contest between electoral urgency and demographic precision. Such an account overlooks the distinct legal issues of statutory competence, electoral equality, evidential reliability and judicial remedy. Through doctrinal analysis of South Sudanese constitutional and electoral instruments, official electoral decisions, international suffrage standards and comparative judgments on malapportionment and effective representation, this article develops a doctrine of provisional representational equality. Its central proposition is that an inherited map may be provisionally lawful without enjoying an irrebuttable presumption of contemporary equality. Five linked requirements follow: lawful temporal authority, reasoned disclosure of demographic uncertainty, defensible treatmen…

Low energy availability risk, eating-disorder symptoms, and weight-cutting practices in elite female wrestlers: a cross-national study
abstract: Background Female wrestlers in weight-category sport may be exposed to low energy availability risk, eating-disorder symptoms, and potentially harmful weight-management practices. This study characterized these domains and explored differences between Turkish and Danish national-team cohorts. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 32 elite female wrestlers from Turkey ( n = 17) and Denmark ( n = 15), aged 18–29 years, completed the LEAF-Q, EDE-Q-13, and AWLMS. Country comparisons and Spearman correlations were evaluated with prespecified false-discovery-rate correction; reviewer-requested sensitivity analyses examined weight cutters, AWLMS subscales, and one covariate at a time. Results Twenty-four wrestlers (75.0%) met the LEAF-Q risk threshold, and 23 (71.9%) reported weight cutting in the previous year. No country comparison of LEAF-Q, EDE-Q-13, or AWLMS scores remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. EDE-Q-13 and AWLMS total scores were positively correlated (ρ = 0.551, p = 0.001, q = 0.003); the association remained among weight cutters ( n = 23; ρ = 0.606, p = 0.002) and after separate adjustment for country, age, weight class, sport experience, and training exposure. Subscale analyses linked EDE-Q-13 mainly with AWLMS psychological (ρ = 0.555, q = 0.005) and physiological effects (ρ = 0.474, q = 0.015), rather than behavioral-method subscales. Conclusi…

title: Entrepreneurial preparedness for energy transitions and Sustainable Development Goals
abstract: Entrepreneurial preparedness is critical for energy ventures navigating dynamic challenges and sustainability demands. Existing research lacks an integrated systems perspective examining preparedness. This study examines the interdependence of entrepreneurial preparedness factors in the energy sector, aiming for sustainable development using total interpretive structural modelling and cross-impact matrix multiplication applied to classification (MICMAC). The findings reveal that environmental and social factors are primary drivers within this expert-based model, influencing other factors such as market demand, technological advancement, cultural and societal acceptance, and risk perception and management. These insights highlight the centrality of sustainability, regulatory compliance, and the environmental agenda in preparedness. MICMAC analysis further supports this by identifying infrastructure development and access to talent and expertise as highly dependent factors, meaning their success depends on other enabling factors. Using the antecedents-decisions-outcomes framework, the study proposes future research examining how environmental, behavioral, and technological drivers of entrepreneurial preparedness contribute to infrastructure readiness, skill development, and innovation aligned with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 7 (affordable and clean ener…

Multi-level barriers and facilitators to Baduanjin participation among community-dwelling older adults: a qualitative socio-ecological study
abstract: Objective Participation in physical activity is essential for promoting healthy ageing among older adults. However, the factors influencing Baduanjin participation among community-dwelling older adults remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to explore the perceived multilevel facilitators and barriers to Baduanjin participation using the Socio-Ecological Model (SEM). Methods A qualitative study design was employed using semi-structured interviews with 29 participants, including older adults, family members, exercise instructors, and community staff. Data were analyzed using a hybrid inductive–deductive thematic approach, with initial codes and themes developed inductively and subsequently mapped onto the SEM levels. Results Facilitators and barriers to Baduanjin participation were identified across five SEM levels. Key facilitators included health awareness and self-regulation, perceived physical and psychological benefits, and habit formation at the individual level; family support and peer encouragement at the interpersonal level; structured programmes, professional guidance, incentive mechanisms, and digital learning resources at the organizational level; supportive social environments, accessible facilities, and community-based activities at the community level; and perceived policy support and cultural identity at the culture and policy level. School Board Members’ Participation in Collective Decision-Making for Improving Students’ Academic Performance in Public Secondary Schools in Bukoba District, Tanzania
abstract: This study examined school board members’ participation in collective decision-making for improving students’ academic performance in public secondary schools in Bukoba District, Tanzania. The study was guided by Kurt Lewin’s Participatory Decision-Making Theory and adopted a mixed-methods approach using an explanatory sequential research design. A sample of 207 respondents was selected using systematic, stratified, simple random, and purposive sampling techniques. Quantitative data were collected through questionnaires administered to teachers and students, while qualitative data were obtained through interviews with school board chairpersons, Heads of Schools, and the District Secondary Education Officer. Quantitative data were analysed using frequencies, percentages, means, standard deviations, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression, while qualitative data were analysed thematically. The findings showed that both teachers and students positively viewed school board members’ participation in collective decision-making. Teachers reported that board members actively participated in making academic decisions and that their involvement contributed to improving the quality of education. Similarly, students indicated that active participation by school board members improved educational quality and supported their academic performance. The findings further revealed that schoo…

title: El descontento con “la política” y el compromiso con la democracia: claves de la participación electoral en la vejez (Santa Fe, Argentina)
abstract: Older adults constitute a growing population group, acquiring significant relevance within the electorate. In parallel, given this new demographic landscape, “active aging” is being promoted, recognizing the participation of older adults as a fundamental human right. However, the study of electoral participation in old age —especially from a political science perspective— remains a poorly developed field. Our contribution addresses this gap. This article proposes an approach to electoral participation in old age based on a qualitative analysis of the experiences of older adults, recently conducted in the city of Santa Fe, Argentina, during the years 2017-2023. The results identify discontent with “politics” and commitment to democracy as central dimensions of this participation.

title: Seasonal thermal performance, produce-quality, and thermodynamic characterization of a terracotta clay-pot refrigerator for farm-produce storage
abstract: Introduction Terracotta clay-pot refrigeration is often presented as a low-cost evaporative-cooling option for smallholder post-harvest storage, but most studies report a single season, a single crop, a thermal model only, or produce-quality data only. Methods One commercially available terracotta clay-pot refrigerator was evaluated over three Indian climatic seasons (summer, winter, monsoon) at Loni-Kalbhor, Pune, Maharashtra, with tomato, potato and spinach. Seasonal thermal measurements were combined with a steady-state ANSYS R17.1 thermal simulation, a dual coefficient-of-performance (COP) framework (theoretical, via a Reynolds-flow heat-and-mass-transfer analogy; experimental, via tank water depletion), jute-bag evaporative augmentation, and a 12 V thermoelectric-cooler (TEC) retrofit tested in summer. Results Temperature depression relative to ambient was greatest in summer (≈11 °C, to a compartment dry-bulb temperature of 30 °C without jute), moderate in winter (≈4 °C), and smallest in monsoon (≈3 °C), tracking the wet-bulb depression available in each season. Jute augmentation raised inner relative humidity substantially (e.g., 40% → 60% in summer) but changed inner dry-bulb temperature by only ≈1 °C, and reduced tomato shelf life in every season (summer 4 → 3 days, winter 3 → 2 days, monsoon 1 → 0 days), consistent with humidity-promoted fungal growth. Experimental COP…

title: Assessing the Moderating Effect of Institutional Quality on Petroleum Revenue Allocation and Poverty Reduction in Ghana
abstract: In many developing economies, public spending on agriculture repeatedly fails to translate into poverty reduction. In most instances, the institutional conditions that determine its returns remain uncertain and vague. This study investigates how petroleum-funded agricultural investment influences poverty reduction in Ghana, as well as whether transparency, accountability, and corruption (TAC) moderate these impacts. The study, while grounded in the Endogenous Growth Theory, New Institutional Economics, and Innovation Theory, applied the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) bounds-testing framework to annual data for 2011–2024 (14 observations). For the study, poverty reduction is the dependent variable, while the regressors or independent variables are investment in agricultural infrastructure (IAI), research and development (ARD), agricultural subsidies (AS), and human resource development (HRD). In the study’s moderation model, which was evaluated at zero TAC, IAI (β = −0.534, p < 0.001) and HRD (β = −0.054, p = 0.031) are negatively associated with poverty reduction, whereas ARD is positively associated (β = 0.851, p < 0.001). TAC significantly improved and strengthened the effects of IAI (0.014) and AS (0.006) and weakened that of ARD (−0.024). On the other hand, the moderation of HRD was insignificant. Conditional and restrictive effects at low, mean, and high TAC are rep…

title: Energy storage regimes as a framework for interpreting energy transitions
abstract: Energy transitions are commonly framed as shifts in primary energy supply, with energy storage treated as a technical adjunct rather than a structural feature of socio-technical systems. This paper develops the concept of energy storage regimes to examine the role of storage in the development of human societies and its implications for contemporary decarbonisation. We explore how different forms of storage have enabled the temporal and spatial reorganization of work and heating across successive stages of societal development. Drawing on examples from agrarian societies, the fossil-fuel age, and contemporary energy systems, we show that storage has profoundly shaped patterns of settlement, mobility, production, and social organization. We argue that decarbonisation entails a transition from an energy system in which storage is intrinsic to energy resources and infrastructures toward one that more closely resembles a just-in-time system of energy provision. Drawing on Joseph Tainter's theory of socio-political complexity, we propose the hypothesis that this transition will entail increasing system-wide resource requirements to reproduce functions previously provided implicitly by fossil-fuels and associated infrastructures. Contemporary developments—including battery storage systems, synthetic fuels, and increasingly complex market and system coordination—can be understood as m…

title: A Special Review of Foreign Object Detection for Electric Vehicle Wireless Charging
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) wireless power transfer (WPT) technology provides a new technical approach for automated vehicle charging because of its advantage of contactless energy transmission. However, during wireless charging, a metal object (MO) may produce additional eddy-current loss and a local temperature rise through electromagnetic induction, and a living object (LO) entering the charging area may also create an electromagnetic exposure safety risk. Therefore, foreign object detection (FOD) is an important technology for ensuring the safe operation of an EV-WPT system. Although existing studies have proposed various detection methods and investigated detection algorithms and coil structures, detection performance may still be affected by factors such as power-transfer interference, receiver misalignment, and complex electromagnetic environments. The detection mechanisms, classification bases, and performance evaluation methods of different technical routes also require further systematic review. To address these issues, this paper reviews FOD technology for EV-WPT systems. Starting from the main sensing paths and physical response mechanisms, the working principles, technical characteristics, and interrelationships of different detection methods are summarized and compared. The analysis shows that different detection methods have their own characteristics in terms of sensin…

title: SENSITIVITY OF VEHICLE EMISSIONS TO AVERAGE SPEED ASSUMPTIONS: EVIDENCE FROM MOTORCYCLES IN HANOI
abstract: Average speed is widely used as a key input in macroscopic vehicle-emission models, yet its influence on motorcycle emission estimates remains insufficiently quantified under Vietnamese traffic conditions. This study evaluates the sensitivity of motorcycle emission factors to assumptions about average speed using real-world speed data collected in Hanoi. A total of 8,957 second-by-second speed observations were obtained from GPS measurements and used to derive representative speed scenarios ranging from 13 to 59 km/h. Emission factors for CO2, CO, NOx, and VOC were estimated using the COPERT model, with all vehicle, fuel, and environmental parameters held constant. The results show that average speed substantially influences estimated emission factors. CO2 emissions decreased from 146.8 g/km at 13 km/h to 76.5 g/km at 59 km/h, corresponding to a reduction of approximately 48%. VOC emissions were the most sensitive to speed assumptions, varying by approximately 157% across the investigated speed range, whereas CO and NOx exhibited lower sensitivities of approximately 30% and 31%, respectively. Comparison with experimental measurements reported for Hanoi motorcycles indicated that locally derived speed values produced more realistic emission estimates than generic assumptions. The findings demonstrate that average speed is a critical modeling parameter and may introduce considera…

title: COLLABORATIVE PLANNING AS A SCHOOL MANAGEMENT STRATEGY: TEACHER COLLABORATION AND INCLUSIVE PEDAGOGICAL PRACTICES
abstract: O planejamento colaborativo constitui uma estratégia de gestão escolar que favorece a articulação do trabalho docente e a organização de práticas pedagógicas inclusivas na Educação Básica. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar as contribuições do planejamento colaborativo como estratégia de gestão escolar para a articulação do trabalho docente e o desenvolvimento de práticas pedagógicas inclusivas na Educação Básica. Metodologicamente, caracteriza-se como uma pesquisa qualitativa, de natureza bibliográfica e documental, conduzida por meio de revisão narrativa da literatura. A seleção das publicações fundamentou-se em sua pertinência temática e contribuição para os objetivos propostos, enquanto a análise foi estruturada em três eixos: fundamentos do planejamento colaborativo e sua relação com a gestão escolar; articulação entre professores do ensino regular, profissionais do Atendimento Educacional Especializado (AEE) e comunidade escolar; e contribuições e desafios dessa estratégia para o desenvolvimento de práticas pedagógicas inclusivas. A pesquisa evidenciou que o planejamento colaborativo, associado à gestão escolar, constitui uma estratégia de organização do trabalho pedagógico que favorece a integração entre docentes, profissionais do AEE e comunidade escolar na construção de práticas inclusivas. Foram identificadas contribuições relacionadas à diferenciação pedagógica,…

title: The V-PHONE Program as a Value Education Strategy to Strengthen Social Interaction among Second-Grade Elementary School Students: A Case Study at SD Muhammadiyah Kreatif Kraksaan
abstract: The development of digital technology has brought significant changes to the social interaction patterns of elementary school-aged children, particularly in the ways they communicate, develop emotional bonds, and establish interpersonal relationships within the family environment. This situation highlights the need for value education strategies that emphasize not only cognitive aspects but also the integration of positive behavioral habits into children's daily lives. This study aims to analyze the implementation of the V-PHONE Program (Stop TV and Mobile Phone Use from Maghrib to Isha) as a value education strategy to strengthen social interaction among second-grade students at SD Muhammadiyah Kreatif Kraksaan, identify the values internalized through the program, and examine the supporting and inhibiting factors affecting its implementation.This study employed a qualitative approach with a case study design. The research subjects consisted of Islamic Religious Education teachers, second-grade students, and their parents. Data were collected through participatory observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation, and were subsequently analyzed using the Miles and Huberman interactive model. Data validity was ensured through triangulation, member checking, and peer debriefing. The findings indicate that the V-PHONE Program is implemented by restricting television and mobile …

title: The Implementation of the Blue Ocean Strategy in the Development of Islamic Educational Institutions
abstract: Competition amongst Islamic educational institutions drives the development of service differentiation strategies to create a competitive advantage without neglecting Islamic identity. This study aims to analyse the implementation of the Blue Ocean Strategy (BOS) in the development of Islamic educational institutions at Sekolah Tunas Unggul in Bandung. The study employs a qualitative approach using a case study design. Data were collected through observation, in-depth interviews with 10 informants, and a review of documents, and were subsequently analysed through data condensation, data presentation, and the drawing and verification of conclusions. The research findings indicate that value innovation is developed through the integration of the International Baccalaureate (IB) curriculum, the national curriculum, and the ruhiyah programme. Analysis using the Four Actions Framework (ERRC) identified the structuring of learning practices, the enhancement of global competencies, and the development of educational programmes that characterise the school. The Six Paths Framework is used to map out an approach to service differentiation, whilst the Three Tiers of Non-customers are used to identify potential groups of users of educational services. The implementation of these strategies is supported by alignment between the school’s vision, curriculum and programmes, as well as change …

title: PENDIDIKAN HUMANISTIK DALAM TUTURAN DIREKTIF NASIHAT AYAH: KAJIAN KESANTUNAN BERBAHASA PADA NOVEL AYAHKU (BUKAN) PEMBOHONG DAN SERIBU WAJAH AYAH
abstract: A father’s directive advice in literary works can be read as a form of family education that humanizes the child. Such advice does not merely instruct or prohibit; it also shapes how children understand themselves, their relationships, and life. This study aims to describe the politeness strategies used in fathers’ directive advice, to analyze the most dominant of Leech’s politeness maxims, and to interpret the humanistic educational values embedded in the utterances. The data sources are the novels Ayahku (Bukan) Pembohong by Tere Liye and Seribu Wajah Ayah by Azhar Nurun Ala. This study employs a descriptive-interpretive qualitative approach. A total of 85 utterances were collected through reading, listening, and note-taking techniques, then analyzed using the Miles and Huberman model, which comprises data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The findings show that fathers’ advice is conveyed mainly indirectly through stories, analogies, and questions, accounting for 67.1% of the data. The tact maxim is the most dominant, at 48.2%. In terms of humanistic educational values, exemplary conduct and empowerment are the most frequently realized. These findings indicate that the politeness of fathers’ directive advice is a concrete means of humanistic education that respects children’s dignity and freedom to think. The findings can serve as a reference for parents and e…

title: Criteria for balancing the company's technology development strategy
abstract: Subject. A balanced strategy of technological development in conditions of limited resources. Objectives. Defining criteria and parameters for evaluating a balanced strategy for technological development of companies. Methods. The research is based on the application of nonparametric regression modeling and multidimensional data analysis. Results. The calculation of the predicted average effects of the basic ratio of the efficiency of the use of production assets revealed a parabolic dependence of the criterion with the boundaries of changes in qualitative estimates in the range of 3.25–7 units. The operational component prevails within this gap, while the investment component prevails outside it. The boundaries of the segment correspond to a qualitative change in the criterion values. Conclusions. The results of the study indicate the relevance of monitoring the information consistency of classical financial and economic indicators in the dynamic market environment of the modern economy and can be used as the basis for more analytical studies of various aspects of the qualitative assessment of the balance of technological development of companies, taking into account industry specifics.

title: Analysis of Determinants of Tourist Revisit Intention: Integration of Destination Quality, Pricing Strategy, and Promotion Effectiveness through Tourist Satisfaction
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of digital marketing, promotions, brand image and repeat orders on airline consumer loyalty. The method used is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) by integrating findings from 50 reputable scientific articles sourced from international journals indexed by Scopus, Web of Science, Elsevier, Sage, Emerald, and national journals indexed by SINTA. Literature selection was carried out using strict inclusion and exclusion criteria, with data analysis through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing strengthened by source triangulation. The results of the study indicate that: 1) Destination Quality Integration affects Tourist Satisfaction; 2) Pricing Strategy affects Tourist Satisfaction; 3) Promotion Effectiveness affects Tourist Satisfaction; 4) Destination Quality Integration affects Tourist Revisit Intention; 5) Pricing Strategy affects Tourist Revisit Intention; 6) Promotion Effectiveness affects Tourist Revisit Intention; 7) Tourist Satisfaction affects Tourist Revisit Intention; 8) Destination Quality Integration influences Tourist Revisit Intention through Tourist Satisfaction; 9) Pricing Strategy influences Tourist Revisit Intention through Tourist Satisfaction; 10) Promotion Effectiveness influences Tourist Revisit Intention through Tourist Satisfaction.

abstract: The intensive development of industrial-energy complexes and the increasing anthropogenic pressure on aquatic ecosystems necessitate the search for reliable bioindication methods to assess the ecological status of river basins. The middle reach of the Western Bug River near the Dobrotvir thermal power plant is affected by heated water discharge, coal combustion products, municipal wastewater carried by the Poltva River and agricultural runoff. While the results of physicochemical water monitoring capture the ecological situation only at the exact moment of sampling, aquatic organisms, particularly fish, accumulate and integrate the toxic impact of pollutants over a prolonged period. This study aims to investigate developmental stability, as well as the patterns of accumulation and topographic distribution of Cu, Zn, Fe, and Pb in target organs (muscles, liver, gills) of four fish species with different trophic preferences: roach, bleak, European perch, and Prussian carp. The research was conducted at the monitoring station near the village of Staryi Dobrotvir. Fluctuating asymmetry was assessed from five bilateral meristic traits; metals were determined by atomic absorption spectrophotometry. Fluctuating asymmetry was highest in roach (0.48) and bleak (0.42), intermediate in perch (0.35) and lowest in Prussian carp (0.21), corresponding to environmental quality classes II–IV. T…

title: РОЗРАХУНКОВО-ЕКСПЕРИМЕНТАЛЬНА МЕТОДИКА ПІДВИЩЕННЯ АВТОНОМНОСТІ 10-ДЮЙМОВОГО FPV-БПЛА З Li-ion СИСТЕМОЮ ЖИВЛЕННЯ
abstract: The paper presents a calculation-experimental method for improving the endurance of a multirotor UAV using a custom 10-inch FPV platform as a case study. The proposed approach considers the UAV not as a set of separate components but as an integrated energy-conversion system that includes a Li-ion battery, ESCs, BLDC motors, propellers, frame layout and mass distribution. A key design constraint is the propeller tip Mach number, since approaching the transonic region increases noise, vibration and aerodynamic losses. For the tested platform equipped with 3115 900KV motors and 10-inch propellers, a 6S3P Li-ion battery pack with a capacity of 15 Ah and a mass of 1.3 kg was selected. Flight tests demonstrated 52 min of hovering without payload and 37.5 min with a 0.657 kg payload. The specific efficiency was 8.1 g/W and 6.4 g/W, respectively. The results confirm that endurance improvement requires coordinated matching of the motor KV, battery voltage, propeller diameter, take-off mass and mechanical layout.

title: Odd-even dichotomy in the waveforms of modified Emden oscillators of arbitrary integer power
abstract: Abstract Closed-form waveforms of the modified Emden oscillators x ¨ + ( q + 2 ) k x q x ˙ + k 2 x 2 q + 1 + ω 2 x = 0 of arbitrary natural power q , and of their damped c -deformed versions, are obtained through a generalized commutative factorization that reduces them to Bernoulli equations. We show that commutative factorizations of Liénard equations are gauge-conjugated forms of the nonlocal linearizing transformation of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Kundu and Lakshmanan, the factorization constant being half the difference of the roots of the associated linear oscillator. These oscillators display an odd–even dichotomy: for odd q they are isochronous, with period 2 π / ω independent of the amplitude, within an explicitly bounded range of the integration constant, while for even q the oscillations decay algebraically, as t − 1 / q . The dichotomy is confirmed by an elliptic polar representation, in which the phase rotates uniformly for every q , and, for even q , by the Bendixson–Dulac criterion applied to the divergence of the vector field. We present a dissipative Lagrangian of Lurie–Rayleigh type and, for q = 1 , an autonomous Sundman linearization that yields a rational first integral, a Jacobi last multiplier (JLM) and a non-dissipative Lagrangian; for every q , ω 2 x 2 + ( x ˙ + k x q + 1 ) 2 is a Darboux polynomial providing a global JLM. Explicit waveforms and phase p…

title: One-year changes in astigmatism after wearing three types of myopia control spectacle lenses: a power vector analysis
abstract: Purpose Whether myopia control spectacle lenses alter childhood astigmatism is controversial, most evidence resting on scalar cylinder rather than power vectors. We quantified one-year astigmatic power vector changes across four lens types and their association with concurrent axial elongation. Methods In this single-center retrospective cohort, 661 right eyes fitted with single-vision (SV; n = 123), defocus incorporated multiple segments (DIMS; n = 163), highly aspherical lenslets (HAL; n = 294), or diffusion optics technology (DOT; n = 81) lenses were followed for one year. Refractions were converted to the power vector components J0 and J45, and one-year changes (ΔJ0, ΔJ45, Δ|C|) were compared among groups using generalized linear models adjusted for age, sex, baseline spherical equivalent, the corresponding baseline astigmatic component and baseline axial length, with Bonferroni-corrected pairwise contrasts; associations with axial length change (ΔAL) were examined in adjusted regression models. Results All groups showed a significant with-the-rule drift (ΔJ0 + 0.194 to +0.232 D) and increased total astigmatism (Δ|C| +0.448 to +0.514 D). After adjustment, neither ΔJ0 ( Wald P = 0.446) nor Δ|C| ( P = 0.201) differed among groups; ΔJ45 differed ( P = 0.007), but the only contrast surviving correction (HAL versus DOT, −0.061 D; Bonferroni P = 0.005) was clinically negligible. …

title: RENEWABLE ENERGY DEVELOPMENT IN AN OIL-DEPENDENT ECONOMY: LEGAL AND REGULATORY FRAMEWORKS FOR SOLAR POWER, INDEPENDENT PRODUCERS AND ENERGY INVESTMENT IN SOUTH SUDAN
abstract: South Sudan’s transition from petroleum-dependent electricity provision to solar generation requires more than an invitation to private investment. It requires a lawful allocation of public power over generation licences, procurement, tariffs, land, contingent public liabilities and enforceable remedies. This article examines the Transitional Constitution, the Southern Sudan Electricity Corporation Act 2011, the Investment Promotion Act 2009, procurement instruments and energy-sector assessments, with comparative jurisprudence used as persuasive rather than binding authority. It finds a structural discrepancy between the statutory recognition of independent power producers and the incomplete operational framework for regulating them. The article contributes a doctrine of conditional energy-investment authority: long-term protection of a public electricity bargain should depend on five linked conditions—competent authorisation, contestable selection, transparent fiscal risk, rights-compatible implementation, and continuing independent remedies. Applied to solar IPPs, isolated mini-grids and public off-take contracts, the doctrine distinguishes legitimate contractual reliance from an attempt to immunise unlawful allocations of public authority. It proposes an integrated statute separating policy, regulation and utility operations; proportionate mini-grid licensing; reasoned tarif…

title: Emerging and multidrug-resistant pathogens in retail leafy greens, Cape Winelands, South Africa
abstract: Leafy greens are increasingly linked to outbreaks of foodborne diseases caused by opportunistic foodborne pathogens, such as Listeria monocytogenes and Salmonella species. Additionally, studies have reported antibiotic-resistant organisms, including foodborne pathogens, from fresh produce. Antibiotic resistance is a global health concern, as it may lead to treatment failure for subsequent infections. This study isolated antibiotic-resistant and multidrug-resistant L. monocytogenes, including those resistant to first-line antibiotics such as ampicillin, from ready-to-eat and whole leafy greens sold at major retailers in the Winelands region of the Western Cape, South Africa. Sixty leafy green samples from three commercial retailers were phenotypically screened for Listeria and Salmonella species and confirmed with the VITEK®2 compact automated system. Antibiotic susceptibility testing was done using the Kirby–Bauer disc diffusion method. Three isolates (5%) were confirmed as L. monocytogenes, along with one isolate each of L. seeligeri and L. rocourtiae. Additional species confirmed included emerging opportunistic pathogens such as Kocuria kristinae. No Salmonella spp. were confirmed. Instead, phenotypically presumptive colonies were identified as Enterobacter cloacae complex, Raoultella planticola, Citrobacter species and Klebsiella oxytoca. These isolates presented phenotypic …

title: From omnichannel experience to beauty impulse buying: an affective pathway
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how omnichannel customer experiences shape impulse buying in beauty retailing, focusing on affective mechanisms and boundary conditions. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework and dual-process theory, the study examines how five dimensions of omnichannel experience relate to perceived enjoyment, urge to buy and impulse buying, with showrooming as a moderator. Data from 455 Chinese beauty consumers were analysed using SmartPLS 4.0. Findings All five dimensions are associated with perceived enjoyment and urge to buy, with enjoyment partially mediating their links to urge to buy, which predicts impulse buying. Connectivity, flexibility and personalisation also relate directly to impulse buying; integration and consistency do not. Showrooming is associated with a weaker link between urge to buy and impulse buying. Practical implications Retailers could strengthen connectivity, flexibility and personalisation for immediate conversion, and use integration and consistency to support sustained affective engagement. Managing showrooming requires timely incentives that reduce decision delays during mobile price comparison. Originality/value This study advances understanding of impulse buying in omnichannel settings by revealing heterogeneous associations across experience dimensions, identifying enjoyment as an aff…

title: Outcome uncertainty in the association between thyroid peroxidase antibodies and nodal involvement in papillary thyroid carcinoma with ultrasound-defined thyroiditis
abstract: Background Thyroid peroxidase antibodies (TPOAb) have been associated with nodal involvement in papillary thyroid carcinoma, but incompletely documented outcomes complicate interpretation. Methods This exploratory study evaluated 254 selected surgical patients with ultrasound-defined thyroiditis, including 201 in the paired primary analysis. We assessed source documentation, 32 overlapping model specifications, multifocality adjustment, a within-ward restriction, and outcome reassignment in 232 eligible patients. An exhaustive tipping-point analysis evaluated every allocation of up to four positive outcomes among 29 eligible uncertain records. Results The adjusted odds ratio per standard deviation of log2(TPOAb+1) was 0.654 (95% confidence interval, 0.479–0.894). Focality was available for all 254 patients. In the same 201 primary cases, additional multifocality adjustment gave an odds ratio of 0.598 (0.431–0.831). All 31 uncertain negative-coded records came from one ward; restriction to the other ward gave an odds ratio of 0.666 (0.476–0.931; n = 178). All 4,090 allocations involving zero to three positive reassignments had confidence intervals below one. At four reassignments, two of 23,751 allocations had intervals including one. These counts do not estimate how likely misclassification is. Mean internal area under the curve increased from 0.580 to 0.632 with TPOAb; the con…

title: MEASUREMENT-UNCERTAINTY-DRIVEN TRANSMISSION SCHEDULING FOR INDUSTRIAL WIRELESS SENSOR NETWORKS: A STABILITY DICHOTOMY IN FRESHNESS-FAIR ALLOCATION
abstract: Age of Information (AoI), widely used for scheduling in industrial wireless sensor networks, reflects when a sample was generated but not the accuracy of the instrument that produced it, although instruments on one network can differ in accuracy by orders of magnitude and degrade with age. We determine when freshness-fair scheduling is optimal for remote state estimation and how the allocation should change when it is not. A time-slotted channel serving scalar Gauss–Markov sources observed through instruments of different noise variance is modelled, the periodic estimation cost is derived in closed form, and a continuous-rate relaxation of the allocation problem is solved by bisection on the shadow price of a slot. For integrating sources with common dynamics, freshness-fair allocation is proved strictly suboptimal whenever instrument variances differ; for random-walk sources the converse is also proved, and the optimal rate is shown to increase with instrument noise. For self-regulating sources, the marginal value of a slot is proved to be bounded by an instrument information budget that decreases with instrument noise; under a numerically verified, unproved convexity property, this yields an abandonment threshold that is explicit once the slot price is known. In synthetic tests, a water-filling policy reduces total mean-square error by 11.5% relative to round robin and is wit…
