Managing uncertainty in generative AI interactions: a resource depletion perspective
abstract: Purpose Despite significant investments from organizations, generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) is still not widely used for deeper knowledge production and transformation. Existing research has focused on external constraints (infrastructure, skills and governance) to explain Gen AI withdrawal behaviors, while paying little attention to the internal psychological states that users go through when interacting with Gen AI. Design/methodology/approach This study investigates how users’ cognitive and emotional resources are depleted by the interactional uncertainty present in Gen AI and how this depletion influences withdrawal behaviors associated with Gen AI by utilizing conservation of resources theory (COR). Data are analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling from a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 317 users. Findings The findings show that interactional uncertainty is positively associated with both cognitive and emotional resource depletion. Cognitive resource depletion has a positive association with knowledge feedback withdrawal but does not influence non-transformational use, whereas emotional resource depletion increases non-transformational Gen AI use but does not affect feedback withdrawal. Furthermore, the effect of cognitive – but not emotional – resource depletion is moderated, and non-transformational usage is directly decreased…

title: Metrological framework for the development of plant-based certified reference materials. Part II: Multilaboratory characterisation, provisional value assignment and uncertainty evaluation
abstract: Part I of the MultiBio CRM study described the production of paired strawberry leaf and fruit candidate reference materials, including controlled cultivation, matrix-specific dehydration, comminution, fortification with As, Cd, Pb and Hg, homogenisation, packaging and sterilisation. Part II presents the multilaboratory characterisation, provisional value assignment and uncertainty evaluation. Six laboratories contributed results obtained by ICP-MS, ICP-OES, AAS and TXRF. Because the participants’ uncertainties were reported using non-equivalent conventions, independent laboratory results were equally weighted and their median was used as the provisional assigned value, with a characterisation uncertainty of 1.25s/p. This component was combined with conservative matrix-level homogeneity contributions of 12.5% (leaves) and 27% (fruit). The provisional mass fractions and interim expanded uncertainties U* (k = 2, stability excluded) were: leaves, As (0.55 ± 0.14) mg/kg, Cd (0.55 ± 0.16) mg/kg and Pb (1.25 ± 0.41) mg/kg; fruit, As (0.48 ± 0.29) mg/kg, Cd (0.37 ± 0.24) mg/kg and Pb (1.40 ± 0.87) mg/kg. Mercury, determined by two laboratories with one technique, remained indicative. At the current uncertainty level the materials support quality control, method development and detection of gross bias, whereas certification …

abstract: Введение. Классификация и лечение острого миелоидного лейкоза базируются на комплексе клинических и лабораторных параметров, среди которых важную роль играют генетические особенности опухолевого клона (рекуррентные хромосомные аномалии и генные мутации). Высокопроизводительное секвенирование показало, что спектр мутаций шире, а частота выявления новых вариантов растет, что делает мутационный скрининг необходимым, а не эксклюзивным элементом диагностики. Систематизация редких мутаций необходима для понимания патогенеза и поиска прогностических факторов в рамках национального протокола. Цель. Оптимизировать протокол биоинформационного анализа данных таргетного высокопроизводительного секвенирования на основе определения молекулярно-генетического профиля у пациентов с острым миелоидным лейкозом. Материалы и методы. Материалом послужили образцы костного мозга 98 пациентов с первичным острым миелоидным лейкозом. Генотипирование выполнено методом таргетного секвенирования с последующей верификацией выявленных вариантов. Результаты. Мутации выявлены у 68,4% пациентов (медиана 1). X-ray Absorption Near Edge Structure at Mg K-Edge: Optimization of Theoretical Calculation Based on Experiments
abstract: Abstract Recent emerging developments in the theoretical calculation of X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) prompt the necessity of rational and objective methods for validating calculation results. Given this background, this study proposes a novel approach to validate theoretically calculated XANES spectra based on experimental spectra using spectral similarity measures (SSM). The theoretical Mg K-edge XANES spectra of four Mg compounds were calculated by the program code FDMNES, and the calculated spectra were compared with the corresponding experimental spectra to optimize the calculation parameters based on SSM. The calculation results obtained with the optimized parameters provide an informative theoretical basis to interpret the experimental XANES spectra in terms of electronic structure and local geometrical arrangement. The study also demonstrates the potential of SSM to evaluate the similarity/dissimilarity of any multidimensional data sets in a rational and objective manner.

title: Stabilizing a promiscuous sugar dehydrogenase via covalent immobilization: optimization and characterization
abstract: Abstract Lignocellulosic sugars are a sustainable feedstock for the production of biobased acids via enzymatic biotransformation. However, the homogeneous nature and the limited stability of free enzymes currently limit their industrial application. Enzyme immobilization can address these limitations if properly designed. While sugar dehydrogenases acting on single sugars have previously been immobilized, this work reports, for the first time, the immobilization on crosslinked agarose beads of a promiscuous dehydrogenase from Herbaspirillum seropedicae capable of acting on multiple sugars. After evaluating several immobilization protocols, the biocatalyst immobilized on glyoxyl support and reduced with sodium borohydride showed the best overall performance. Under magnetic stirring, the immobilized enzyme retained 40% of the free enzyme’s activity. Furthermore, the biocatalyst remained active under conditions where the free counterpart displayed little or no activity, such as in sodium carbonate or phosphate buffers at alkaline pH. Moreover, it was stable for over 70 h across all buffer and pH conditions tested, retaining 70% to 100% of its activity, whereas the free enzyme was completely inactivated within 7 h. The immobilized enzyme also showed reduced substrate inhibition by D-galactose and L-arabinose, while fully preserving its promiscuity toward D-xylose, D-glucose, D-gala…

title: Using stochastic modeling within the foresight technology when developing regional strategic development plans
abstract: Subject. Development of forecasting and planning methods that take into account a high level of uncertainty. Objectives. Justifying the need to move from deterministic forecasting to probabilistic scenario methods. Developing and testing a methodology for allocating budget funds that minimizes the risk of not achieving target indicators when dealing with unfavorable scenarios. Methods. Simulation modeling, scenario analysis, stochastic optimization. Results. Using a hypothetical region as an example, it shows that evenly distributing budget funds ultimately gives the highest average effect but has low resilience in a crisis scenario. The maximin strategy, focused on the worst-case scenario, increases the level of guaranteed results but lowers the average effect. The foresight-stochastic strategy helps balance efficiency and risk. Conclusions. The proposed methodology can be used by regional authorities and strategic planning centers as a tool to choose how to allocate resources in situations of high external uncertainty.

title: DSO-AdSEq: optimization-based adaptive step size time domain equalizer for noise compensation in optical fiber communication system
abstract: Abstract In the modern world, optical fiber communication systems are crucial due to their long transmission capabilities, electromagnetic interference resistance, high-speed data transmission, and higher bandwidth range. However, the performance degradation of the optical signal occurs due to noise and interference effects, which lead to signal distortions, optical crosstalk issues, and system instability. Hence, adaptive equalization strategies are considered to rectify the noise issues in optical communication systems. In this research, a Distinctive Search Optimization–based Adaptive Step Size Time Domain Equalizer (DSO-AdSEq) is employed to compensate for noise and interference effects for error correction purposes, which improves the signal quality and reduces the bit error rate (BER). Moreover, the DSO algorithm is adopted to optimize the step-size equalizer, which provides faster convergence and a reliable communication system. In addition, optical channels are adopted to minimize channel impairments, which contributes to providing more accurate and reliable signal recovery. Eventually, the proposed DSO-AdSEq model outperforms the error vector magnitude (EVM), symbol error rate (SER), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), modulational instability (MI), generalized mutual information (GMI), and bit error rate (BER), attaining the values of 1.15, 3.14 %, 0.59 bits/sym, 0.39 bits/s…

title: Low-dose thalidomide add-on versus colchicine optimization for oral ulcers in Behçet disease: a 24-week retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Treatment escalation for persistent oral ulcers in Behçet disease requires balancing mucosal control against tolerability. We compared low-dose thalidomide add-on with colchicine optimization and examined early inflammatory changes in relation to later oral response. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort included adults undergoing treatment adjustment for oral ulcers during 2018–2024. The primary outcome was success of the initial treatment strategy at week 12, defined as no active ulcers and no prior treatment failure. Adjusted success differences were estimated by marginal standardization. Secondary outcomes included week-24 success, success at both visits, treatment persistence, and adverse events. Early C-reactive protein (CRP) and neutrophil changes were assessed in a week-4 landmark analysis. Results Of 224 patients, 109 received colchicine optimization and 115 received thalidomide add-on at 25–50 mg nightly. Week-12 strategy success occurred in 51.4% and 62.6%, respectively (adjusted difference, 14.4 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.2–27.7). Adjusted differences were 13.4 points at week 24 (95% CI, −0.1–26.9) and 17.4 points for success at both visits (95% CI, 4.6–30.2). The adjusted hazard ratio for treatment failure was 0.62 (95% CI, 0.35–1.11). Intolerance-related discontinuation occurred in 4.6% versus 16.5%. Among 177 landmark …

Integrated multi-omics and experimental validation reveal a ZNRF2-MAP4 axis regulating mitophagy and ferroptosis in renal tubular epithelial cells during renal ischemia-reperfusion injury
abstract: Introduction Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (RIRI) involves tubular damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ferroptosis, but the molecular links between mitochondrial quality control and ferroptosis remain unclear. Methods We integrated public transcriptomic datasets using differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network, protein-protein interaction, and machine-learning analyses. Single nucleus RNA sequencing characterized the cellular distribution of core genes and autophagy-related transcriptional activity. ZNRF2 was prioritized because of its reproducible downregulation in RIRI and reported links to autophagy and ferroptosis. We investigated ZNRF2 in a mouse RIRI model and hypoxia/ reoxygenation (H/R)-treated HK-2 cells using gain- and loss-of-function approaches. Autophagic flux, mitophagy-related phenotypes, lipid peroxidation, intracellular Fe2+, and ferroptosis-related proteins were assessed. RNA sequencing, immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry (IP-MS), reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation, immunofluorescence, and MAP4 knockdown rescue experiments explored the underlying mechanism. Results Integrated analyses identified Fn1 , Cd68 , and Znrf2 as core RIRI-associated genes, with Znrf2 consistently downregulated across datasets. ZNRF2 expression changed dynamically during ischemiareperfusion. In H/R-treated HK-2 cells, ZNRF2 overexpression reduced steadystate …

title: Integrated analysis of genomic drivers and microRNA profiles in cutaneous melanoma: clinical and prognostic associations
Динамика интегральных лейкоцитарных индексов при развитии солидной формы аденокарциномы Эрлиха
abstract: Введение. В последние годы в клинической онкологии возрастает интерес к изучению системных иммуновоспалительных реакций, сопровождающих развитие злокачественных новообразований. Одним из перспективных подходов к их оценке является использование интегральных лейкоцитарных индексов, которые отражают выраженность системного воспалительного ответа, эндогенной интоксикации и иммунной реактивности организма и рассматриваются как потенциальные диагностические и прогностические биомаркеры. Однако в условиях экспериментального моделирования опухолевого роста, особенно при использовании модели аденокарциномы Эрлиха, сведения об их динамике остаются ограниченными и недостаточно изученными, что определяет актуальность настоящего исследования. Цель. Проанализировать динамику лейкоцитарных индексов при прогрессировании аденокарциномы Эрлиха у лабораторных мышей и определить их потенциальную прогностическую значимость. Материалы и методы. Исследование выполнено на самцах мышей инбредного стока Af (n=160). Солидную форму аденокарциномы Эрлиха моделировали путем подкожной трансплантации опухолевых клеток в межлопаточную область. В динамике оценивали рост опухоли, общую выживаемость животных, показатели периферической крови и 22 интегральных лейкоцитарных индекса, включая современные показатели системного воспаления. Статистическую обработку данных проводили с использованием критерия Манна – Уит…

title: ТЕОРЕТИЧНЕ ОБҐРУНТУВАННЯ ГІДРАВЛІЧНИХ ТА ФІЗИКО‑ХІМІЧНИХ ПРОЦЕСІВ КОМПЛЕКСНОЇ ПЕРЕРОБКИ ХВОЇ СОСНИ ЗВИЧАЙНОЇ
abstract: This study examines the interrelationship between hydraulic and physicochemical processes in the integrated processing of Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris L.) needles. The research addresses the need to coordinate operating conditions for aqueous extract production and subsequent utilization of the fibrous residue. The aim is to provide a theoretical basis for determining the water volume, extraction time, and material purification conditions. The methodology employs mass and energy balances, phase equilibrium and mass transfer kinetics equations, and differential analysis. Analytical expressions are derived for the extract concentration and the amount of extractives remaining in the material during an isothermal batch process. The effects of liquid retention on the actual product yield and the carryover of soluble substances to the subsequent stage are established. The minimum extraction time and the condition for achieving a specified yield are determined. Under the equilibrium approximation and assuming a linear relationship between specific energy consumption and water volume, an expression for the energy-efficient water volume is obtained. Dimensionless calculations indicate that the yield at maximum energy efficiency is 0.5635, compared with the target value of 0.60. The residue mass balance is coupled with a kinetic model of alkaline treatment. An allowable treatment time in…

title: PP004: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis: A Fatal Secondary Cause of Recurrent Multifocal Cerebral Infarctions
abstract: Abstract Background Secondary stroke causes warrant investigation in recurrent, multi-territorial infarctions unexplained by conventional risk factors. Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System (PACNS) is a rare, CNS-confined inflammatory vasculopathy presenting with strokes and cognitive decline, posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Case Presentation A 54-year-old hypertensive male from Sri Lanka, presented with a 5- month history of vertigo and headache, progressing to ataxia and cognitive impairment.Examination revealed cerebellar ataxia, left hemiparesis, and confusion. MRI showed bilateral cerebellar and frontal infarctions; MRA suggested vasculitis. Systemic inflammatory markers and basic investigations for systemic vasculitis were unremarkable, but CSF showed isolated protein elevation (81 mg/dL). Despite initial improvement on methylprednisolone and cyclophosphamide, he suffered recurrent strokes, seizures, and progressive encephalopathy.He ultimately died from multiorgan failure following sepsis despite escalated immunosuppression and plasma exchange. Discussion This case highlights PACNS as a critical secondary cause of stroke. The absence of systemic inflammation often complicates diagnosis, necessitating high clinical suspicion.Recurrent infarctions despite immunosuppression underscore the aggressive nature of the disease and the limitation…

title: Higher ERAS compliance is associated with shorter hospital stay and lower ICU utilization in a resource-limited healthcare system — a prospective colorectal cohort study
abstract: Abstract ​Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways integrate evidence-based perioperative care to improve recovery after colorectal surgery. Although a compliance threshold of 70–75% has been proposed, outcomes at higher adherence levels remain incompletely characterized, particularly in resource-limited healthcare systems. We aimed to evaluate the achievable compliance and its association with postoperative outcomes in such a setting. This prospective single-center cohort included patients undergoing elective colorectal surgery between 2022 and 2024. Compliance with 20 ERAS elements was assessed in six groups (≤ 75% and 5-percentage-point bands up to 100%). Outcomes included hospital length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit (ICU) utilization, morbidity, readmission, and mortality. Unadjusted analyses were supplemented by exploratory multivariable models. Among 338 patients, mean compliance was 89.3%; median LOS was 6 days (interquartile range 5–7). ICU admission occurred in 23.7%, total morbidity in 28.1%, and early morbidity in 16.9%. Higher compliance correlated with shorter LOS ( R = − 0.36), lower ICU admission ( R = − 0.30), and fewer early complications ( R = − 0.19; all p < 0.001). After adjustment, each 5-percentage-point increase in compliance was associated with a 4.8% relative reduction in geometric mean LOS ( p = 0.0023) and approximately 5.4 h shorter ICU …

Patient satisfaction after implantation of venous port system through different vascular accesses: a pilot study
abstract: Objective: to evaluate patient satisfaction with totally implantable venous port systems placed via three different vascular access routes: the internal jugular vein, the axillary vein, and the basilic vein. Materials and Methods. 158 oncology patients requiring long-term chemotherapy were included in this prospective randomized study. Venous ports were implanted using one of three access routes: v. Basilica (n = 50), v. Axillaris (n = 53), or v. Jugularis interna (n = 55). Patient satisfaction with functional and aesthetic outcomes was assessed 6 months after implantation using a standardized questionnaire developed at the N.N. Petrov National Medical Research Center. Results. Overall satisfaction levels were high across all three groups, with median scores ranging from 29 to 30 points, and no significant differences between access types (p = 0,47). There were no statistically significant differences observed for any of the six questionnaire items (p = 0,162–1,000). The rate of late complications was low and comparable between groups (6-7 cases per group; p = 0,935). Postoperative complications were the only one factor that significantly associated with decreased satisfaction. (p = 0,014). An analysis of the impact of postoperative complications on patient satisfaction revealed a statistically significant and strong inverse relationship. Patients who experienced complications …

title: Hybrid simulations of nonlinear zonal flow generation by multi- n toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes driven by energetic particles
abstract: Abstract In burning plasmas, zonal flows (ZFs) excited by toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes (TAEs) play a crucial role in improving energy confinement. In this work, strong self-generated ZFs are analyzed in a multi- n TAE system through nonlinear hybrid simulations using the CLT-K code, where the ZFs are driven by self-beat interactions of TAEs. The results show that the strong ZFs dominate the nonlinear stage and significantly suppress the TAE activity. The ZF mode structures consist of the m = 0 and m = 1 harmonics, and are directly correlated with the spatial structures of TAEs. Further analysis of the ZF kinetic energy evolution demonstrates that a finite residual between the Reynolds and Maxwell stresses, arising from toroidal geometry, enables net energy transfer from TAEs to ZFs, with an additional contribution from the energetic particles (EPs) pressure response. In addition, the linear Lorentz force contributes either to ZF pumping or damping depending on the stage of the evolution. Strong ZF generation is favored in regimes with high EP pressure and low viscosity. A self-regulating process is identified: stronger TAEs drive stronger ZFs, which in turn regulates the TAE activity. These findings provide both numerical and physical insights into the role of ZFs in regulating EP-driven instabilities in tokamak plasmas.

title: Sustainability assessment of heavy-duty trucks, part I: a multi-criteria assessment method for comparing alternative technologies
abstract: Transitioning heavy-duty road freight towards more sustainable solutions is a complex challenge, with multiple competing technologies—ranging from renewable fuels to battery-electric and hydrogen systems—each offering distinct advantages and drawbacks. Existing sustainability assessments often focus narrowly on climate impacts or single technologies, limiting their usefulness for fair and comprehensive comparisons. This study develops a multi-criteria assessment (MCA) method for broad sustainability evaluation of heavy-duty truck technologies, including a soft, indicator-based framework developed through an iterative, literature-based and participatory process involving researchers, vehicle manufacturers, utilities, and public organisations. The framework covers four key areas—technical, economic, environmental, and social performance—operationalised through 16 indicators with transparent five-level ordinal rating scales defined by numerical thresholds, qualitative descriptions, or both. The method accommodates both established and emerging technologies, including fossil and renewable energy carriers, combustion and electric/fuel-cell drivetrains. During the development, indicator definitions were refined to reduce avoidable duplication, while some conceptual overlap remains. Designed for decision support, the method does not prescribe weights or an aggregation rule, allowing t…

title: LEKOA-Net: a lightweight explainable multi-scale local global attention and adaptive hierarchical fusion network for four class knee stress radiography classification
abstract: Accurate classification of knee stress radiographs requires recognition of subtle joint geometry and directional stress patterns, yet many existing approaches depend on large pretrained networks or annotation-intensive detection and segmentation. This study introduces LEKOA-Net, a compact, detector-free architecture for four-class classification of Valgus, Varus, Lachman, and positioning/stress-system radiographs. Its methodological contribution is the coordinated design of multi-scale depthwise feature extraction, coordinate and spatial attention, lightweight global-context encoding, gated local–global interaction, and input-adaptive fusion of hierarchical representations. Multi-statistic pooling and auxiliary supervision complement these components, while internal attention and fusion analyses alongside Grad-CAM and Grad-CAM++ help examine model behavior. On a dataset of 9,786 grayscale radiographs, LEKOA-Net achieved 96.12% held-out test accuracy and 96.11% Macro-F1 using 3.42 million trainable parameters. The separately reported evaluation on 480 independently annotated images from another center achieved 91.46% accuracy, providing an additional indication of performance under acquisition-domain shift. Quantitative explanation assessment on 120 radiographs yielded a Grad-CAM++ overlap Dice of 0.71 ± 0.10 against consensus clinician-drawn tibiofemoral regions, complementing …

title: LCS.jl v1.0: a high-performance, multi-platform computational model in Julia for turbulent particle-laden flows
abstract: Multiphase turbulent flow phenomena are observed not only in industrial devices but also in environmental flows, and direct numerical simulation plays a key role in their investigation. Many numerical models have been developed; nevertheless, few models are highly optimized for GPU platforms, which represent the current mainstream in high-performance computing. In this study, we developed LCS.jl (Lagrangian Cloud Simulator in Julia), a single-source and multi-platform multiphase turbulence simulation model implemented in the Julia language and KernelAbstractions.jl. Validation results confirmed that the present fluid and particle statistics agree well with those obtained in prior studies. For GPU execution, the GPU-side prefix-scan implementation reduced the particle communication cost by approximately 88 % relative to the CPU-delegated sequential implementation. LCS.jl achieved CPU performance comparable to the original Fortran implementation, with similar intra-node scaling behavior. For GPUs, strong-scaling efficiency was approximately 70 % up to 256 GPUs, and weak-scaling efficiency was approximately 80 % up to 216 GPUs on TSUBAME4.0 (a GPU supercomputer at the Institute of Science Tokyo). LCS.jl achieved a maximum estimated speedup of approximately 16.3× on GPUs over CPUs. Execution on both NVIDIA and AMD GPUs further supported portability across GPU architectures. A trial…

Distributed Multi-Armed Bandit for Satellite-Assisted Integrated Sensing and Communication in Micro-UAV Swarms
abstract: This paper considers micro unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms operating in confined or infrastructure-denied urban environments, where they conduct target sensing, support local communications, and perform remote data backhaul via edge relay nodes. We propose a distributed cooperative multi-armed bandit framework for satellite-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in micro-UAV swarms. Each UAV selects a joint configuration including sensing waveform, frequency channel, transmit power, bandwidth allocation, and modulation scheme as a bandit arm. A perturbation-augmented neighbor-fusion UCB algorithm enables UAVs to share reward statistics while avoiding co-channel clustering, and adapt to satellite handover without a central scheduler. Simulation results show that the proposed method reaches the fastest convergence and handover recovery among UCB-based distributed bandit methods, and that cooperative neighbor fusion yields statistically significant gains over independent learning in convergence speed, throughput, ISAC interference reduction, and handover recovery.

title: Business analytics of information resources and information technology management
abstract: Subject. Business analytics of data management, information resources, technologies and knowledge. Objectives. To propose options for effective methodological approaches, methods and tools for business analysis of data, information resources and information technologies used for their management and optimization based on modern information systems and business intelligence. Methods. Empirical methods (direct observation, conducting surveys, questionnaires and interviews), analytical, descriptive methods, etc. were used. Results. Legislative and regulatory acts, methodologies, standards, and tools for managing data, information resources, and technologies and knowledge aimed at ensuring effective, secure management of IT assets are analyzed. Conclusions. IT enterprises can improve their customer service by using a range of IT technologies and CRM system applications to create large amounts of customer data, manage databases, primarily information resources and knowledge. This guarantees extensive customer feedback and allows you to analyze and interpret, predict and constructively use the obtained business intelligence to make managerial decisions.

title: A Review of Research on the Impact of Digital Transformation on Corporate Accounting Information Quality
abstract: Against the background of the rapid advancement of the digital economy, corporate digital transformation is profoundly reshaping the generation and transmission of accounting information, and the governance effect of digitalization on accounting information quality has become an issue of common concern in practice and academia. Focusing on digital transformation and corporate accounting information quality, this paper reviews the existing relevant literature and conducts a systematic assessment from three dimensions: overall effects, individual attributes of accounting information, and different forms of digitalization. Overall, digital transformation can exert a micro-level governance effect and improve corporate accounting information quality. However, the governance effectiveness of the external digital environment is constrained by firms’ internal conditions, and the actual effects of different digital business models vary. Although existing research has identified multiple pathways, including internal control and information transparency, limitations remain, such as insufficient attention to technological risks and industrial-chain transmission, unclear preconditions for different models, and the lack of an integrated theoretical framework. Future research can draw on publicly available micro-level data and the accumulated literature to further deepen research in this fiel…

title: Investment development of the Ural Federal District regions: a nonparametric approach
abstract: Subject. Regional investment policy aimed at shaping the technological sovereignty of the Russian Federation. Objectives. To identify significant relationships between investment and technological processes that prove the formation of technological sovereignty. Methods. The methodological basis of the study was a nonparametric approach using Spearman and Kendall rank correlation methods to identify relationships; the Mann–Whitney criterion for conducting intergroup comparisons; and the nonparametric Taylor–Sen regression for modeling dependencies, which together ensure the complexity of the analysis in conditions of limited sampling and asymmetry between the objects of analysis. Results. At the regional level of the Ural Federal District, stable relationships between investment and technological indicators are being formed, which creates a technological basis for the progressive development of high-tech industries. Using the example of the regions of the Ural Federal District, a structural paradox of regional development has been identified, which reflects the high level of GRP per capita in oil and gas producing regions and has nothing to do with investment activity in the regions, which generally indicates the development of a resource-dependent development model requiring active economic diversification. Conclusions. The correctness of using a nonparametric approach in the a…

title: How innovation and governance shape the financial development – money laundering risk nexus
abstract: Purpose Financial development is a key objective pursued by countries because it serves as a driving force for economic development. However, its potential unintended consequences, such as money laundering risk, also warrant careful consideration. In the context where quantitative studies examining the impact of financial development on money laundering risk remain limited, existing research has not yet fully addressed whether innovation alters the effect of financial development on money laundering risk, nor whether governance effectiveness continues to shape this relationship across different contexts. Therefore, this article aims to assess the impact of financial development on money laundering risk, while also examining whether and how the presence of innovation and governance alters this relationship. Design/methodology/approach To address endogeneity and sample persistence, this study employs the two-step System Generalized Method of Moment estimator. Furthermore, three regression models are specified, including a baseline model and two interaction models. Findings This study shows that financial development increases money laundering risk. In addition, the moderating analysis of innovation and governance has more notable findings. The moderating role of innovation in the relationship between financial development and money laundering risk is positive and statistically si…

title: Typologization of the subjects of the Russian Federation according to the level of development of the tourism sector in the context of the potential of the tourist tax
abstract: Subject. A set of factors determining the parameters of the regional accommodation industry and their use to build a scientifically based typology of the subjects of the Russian Federation. Objectives. To build a scientifically based typology of the subjects of the Russian Federation based on static and dynamic clustering by indicators of the tourism industry, which makes it possible to identify groups of regions with a comparable tourist tax base, to distinguish regions by the level of development of the tourism industry and by the type of dynamics of its indicators, and to form a methodology for assessing the tax potential of a tourist tax. Methods. Static and dynamic clustering of the subjects of the Russian Federation using k-means and agglomerative clustering algorithms (Ward's method) based on logarithmically transformed and trending indicators of the placement industry for 2002–2025 was used. Results. The optimal number of clusters is from two to three, the silhouette coefficient is calculated in the range of 0.44–0.64, depending on the algorithm used. Static clustering has identified three groups of regions – with large, medium, and poorly developed hosting industries. Based on the obtained typology, a methodology for assessing the tax potential of a tourist tax is proposed, including an assessment of the level of indicators by indicator blocks, calculation of the tax p…

title: Bankruptcy reforms and corporate investment decisions: fresh evidence from founder–CEO firms in India
abstract: Purpose The study aims to investigate the relationship between founder–CEO leadership and their investment decisions. The authors measure investment using two key indicators: (a) capital Expenditure representing investment in long-term assets and (b) research & development expenditure. Further, they examine the influence of bankruptcy reform (Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016, IBC) in moderating the investment decisions of founder–CEO firms. Furthermore, the above relationships are assessed under varying levels of economic policy uncertainty (EPU). Design/methodology/approach The analysis is based on an unbalanced panel dataset comprising 5,250 Indian non-financial firms over the period from 2011 to 2024. The study employs difference-in-differences (DiD) analysis and panel fixed effects across firms, years and industries. In addition, to mitigate potential endogeneity concerns, the authors employ propensity score matching-DiD estimations that corroborate the causal interpretation of the findings. Findings The results show that founder–CEO firms invest significantly more than non-founder-led firms, with this positive association strengthening following the implementation of the IBC. However, elevated EPU attenuates investment decisions among founder–CEO firms, even after the implementation of the IBC. Originality/value This study extends the founder–CEO literature by examining…

title: ZDHHC7 deficiency modulates sex-dependent alterations in prefrontal synaptic transmission following chronic stress
abstract: Introduction Chronic stress (CS) contributes to depression-like behavior in a sex-dependent manner. The palmitoyl acyltransferase ZDHHC7 regulates sex steroid hormone receptors and synaptic proteins, including GABAA receptors, thereby linking stress signaling to synaptic function. Previous studies have associated ZDHHC7 deficiency with resilience to CS, particularly in female mice. Methods This study investigated the effects of CS on synaptic transmission and plasticity in acute brain slices from ZDHHC7-knockout (KO) and wild-type (WT) mice of both sexes, using wholecell recordings in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) and local field potential recordings at the hippocampal CA3-CA1 synapse. Data was analyzed using linear mixed-model. Results We found a significant effect of CS on miniature inhibitory postsynaptic current (mIPSC) amplitude, with a significant reduction in stressed female WT mice. In contrast, miniature excitatory postsynaptic current (mEPSC) inter-event intervals (IEIs) showed a significant sex effect, with longer intervals in female KO mice than in male KO mice and female WT mice under control conditions. Generalized additive mixed models further identified sex-dependent differences in mIPSC and mEPSC IEI distributions, a sex × condition interaction for spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic currents, and a sex × genotype interaction for mEPSCs. In the hippocampus, paire…

title: From low to high transmission: diversity-dependent responses of Plasmodium falciparum population structure to transmission intensity
abstract: Abstract Genetic surveillance is increasingly used to characterize malaria transmission, yet genetic patterns can respond nonlinearly to transmission intensity and depend on diversity already present in parasite populations. To isolate these effects from migration, selection, treatment and host immunity, we developed a neutral stochastic agent-based model of a closed human–mosquito transmission system integrating SEIS (susceptible–exposed–infectious–susceptible) epidemiological dynamics with neutral Plasmodium falciparum haplotypes and mosquito-stage recombination, without mutation or de novo allele generation. By independently varying human biting availability (amax) and initial genetic diversity (π0), we examined their joint effects on infection complexity, recombination and parasite population structure across a continuous transmission gradient. Infection prevalence and within-host infection complexity increased rapidly across low-to-intermediate transmission, whereas the effective recombination ratio and the number of recombinant haplotypes continued to increase across a broader range. Higher transmission was also associated with greater retention of human-stage parasite population genetic diversity (πH) and more even haplotype-frequency distributions, while initial genetic diversity constrained attainable genetic outcomes. Similar late-time population structures could be a…

title: Project-Based Teaching Reform of Mechanical Engineering Course Group Oriented to Engineering Accreditation: A Case Study Based on the Whole Life Cycle of a Precision Transmission Shaft
abstract: Addressing current pedagogical pain points in mechanical engineering programs—such as the fragmentation of courses, the disconnect between theory and practice, and the sporadic integration of ideological and ethical elements—this study aligns with the latest engineering education accreditation standards. These standards impose explicit requirements concerning whole life cycle costs, net-zero carbon, engineering ethics, and sustainable development, which a single course can hardly fulfill independently. Taking a "precision transmission shaft" as the core anchor, this project restructured the content of five core courses: Mechanical Design, Engineering Drawing, Engineering Materials and Heat Treatment, Numerical Control Technology, and Interchangeability and Technical Measurement. This restructuring formed a six-stage progressive module system: "Requirement Analysis→ Material Selection→ Structural Design→ Process Planning→ Precision Machining→ Quality Inspection," The teaching process is integrated throughout by three core thematic threads: craftsmanship, social responsibility, and quality consciousness. Pedagogically, the instruction follows a dual-track pathway in which virtual simulation precedes physical hands-on training. Preliminary practice indicates that the pilot class outperformed the control class in the attainment of four accreditation indicators: "Problem Analysis," …

Development of diagnostic tools for identifying the actual timing of the debtor's insolvency symptoms in the bankruptcy management system
abstract: Subject. Diagnostic tools for identifying the actual timing of the debtor's insolvency symptoms in the bankruptcy management system. Objectives. Improvement of diagnostic tools that contribute to increasing the evidentiary value of the results of financial crisis diagnostics in bankruptcy cases of the debtor, taking into account modern requirements of bankruptcy legislation and lessons from the practice of arbitration management. Methods. Along with general scientific and special methods of financial analysis, an expert-selective method was used to supplement the standardized system of financial indicators with private indicators of the debtor reflecting the real level of solvency at a certain date. Results. The problems of practical quality assurance of financial crisis diagnostics in the framework of debtor bankruptcy cases are considered. A methodological approach to the development of additional diagnostic tools characterizing the debtor's solvency is proposed. Conclusions. The study expands the area of diagnostic paradigms on the specifics of identifying the actual timing of the appearance of signs of insolvency and objective bankruptcy of economic entities in the bankruptcy management system of legal entities.

title: From digital entrepreneurship to financial results: the dynamic capabilities pathway
abstract: Purpose This article aims to determine the direct impact of digital entrepreneurial intention (DEI) on financial performance (FP) and the indirect effects through dynamic capabilities, namely digital transformation (DT), digital capabilities (DC) and digital innovation (DI). Design/methodology/approach Based on the theory of planned behavior (TPB) and resource-based view (RBV), this article examines data collected via internet-mediated questionnaire from 600 SMEs and large firms across multiple countries. Hayes Process Macro is employed to analyze direct and indirect relationships between the research variables. Findings Positive relationships exist among DEI and FP, DEI and dynamic capabilities, and dynamic capabilities and FP. Moreover, dynamic capabilities play complementary partial mediating roles in the DEI–FP relationship. Research limitations/implications This study integrates TPB and the RBV into a unified framework. DEI, as a TPB-based intention that represents mental state, may not lead to superior FP without RBV-based dynamic capabilities that adjust firm operations to meet customer need. Moreover, this article provides a new holistic framework by modeling a single dynamic-capability construct (DT, DC, DI) grounded in the RBV. Practical implications This article highlights the need for training initiatives, incentives and support measures to support digital entrepren…

title: Comparison of econometric approaches and machine learning methods for nowcasting of income and expenses of the consolidated budget of the Russian Federation
abstract: Subject. Nowcasting of revenues and expenditures of the consolidated budget of the Russian Federation based on econometric and neural network models. Objectives. Comparison of the predictive quality of a wide range of machine learning models and classical autoregression with exogenous variables when forecasting total income, individual income items and budget expenditures for one month in advance. Methods. Based on the monthly consolidated budget execution data for January 2012 – May 2025, the forward propagation neural network (FFNN), recurrent network (LSTM), convolutional network (CNN), Transformer architecture, gradient boosting over decision trees (CatBoost), as well as the ARX model and naive prediction as benchmarks were considered. All rows have been converted to growth rates for the corresponding month of the previous year without seasonal adjustment; the number of epochs and trees, as well as the number of ARX lags, are selected from the validation sample; The quality of the forecast is measured by the root of the root mean square error (RMSE) in the test sample (June 2023 – May 2025). Results. title: Technological foundations of centralized and decentralized financial systems: From distributed ledger to central bank digital currencies
abstract: Subject. Technological foundations of centralized and decentralized financial systems, their evolution from traditional banking platforms to modern solutions based on distributed ledger technology and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs). Objectives. To identify the patterns of parallel development of centralized (CeFi) and decentralized (DeFi) financial systems and to define the place of CBDCs as a hybrid solution. Methods. General scientific methods are applied, including historical analysis and expert assessment. Results. It is found that centralized and decentralized approaches have developed in parallel and complement each other rather than being antagonistic. Despite the declared commitment to decentralization, global corporations and states continue to seek centralization of payment systems while integrating elements of DeFi technologies. The central banks of leading countries are actively developing CBDCs, including in the form of hybrid solutions that combine the advantages of centralized control with the technological capabilities of the distributed ledger. However, issues of reliability, security, protection against cyber fraud, and legal regulation remain relevant in both systems. Conclusions. The future of digital finance lies not in the complete replacement of one system by the other, but in the integration of best practices. It is necessary to raise public awa…

Invasive complete hydatidiform mole involving the right mesosalpinx mimicking a ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy: a case report
abstract: Background Invasive hydatidiform mole is a form of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) characterized by the invasion of molar villi and proliferating trophoblasts into the myometrium, vascular spaces, or extrauterine tissues. Extrauterine extension of invasive mole mimicking ectopic pregnancy is extremely rare and may pose a significant diagnostic challenge. Case description A 42-year-old woman received medical management followed by uterine curettage for pregnancy loss, but serum human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) levels were not serially monitored until normalization. After an episode of vaginal bleeding considered to represent menstruation and subsequent resumption of sexual activity, she developed recurrent vaginal bleeding accompanied by progressively elevated hCG levels. Transvaginal ultrasonography revealed a right paraovarian mass with adjacent fluid collection and dilated intramyometrial vessels. Emergency surgery was performed for suspected ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy, and intraoperative examination showed ampullary enlargement of the right fallopian tube with rupture and active bleeding. Histopathological examination revealed hydropic chorionic villi with marked atypical trophoblastic proliferation and stromal and vascular invasion. Immunohistochemical staining showed loss of p57 expression, and short tandem repeat (STR) genotyping demonstrated a monosperm…

title: Validation Under Archetype Shift for Data-Driven Bio-Inspired Lightweight Design: Optimism, Conformal Calibration and Density-Matched Auditing
abstract: Data-driven design rules for bio-inspired lightweight structures are almost always validated with random train–test splits. That tells a designer little about the question that matters: will a rule learned from known architectures hold for a new one? We examine this on two controlled benchmarks with a known governing law, one inside the model library and one outside it (15 draws each), and organise the findings into a four-part archetype-shift protocol. Holding out whole archetypes raises prediction error by 11–36%. The excess squared error is additive in archetype-offset and paper-level variance (leave-one-setting-out R2 of 0.79–0.92), and flexible models pay an extra extrapolation cost. Conformal intervals calibrated on random folds cover only 80–85% of unseen archetypes at a nominal 90%; calibrating on leave-one-archetype-out residuals keeps coverage within three points of nominal from 50 to 95%, at the price of intervals 18–34% wider, and descriptor-distance flags do not show where the failures occur. In a sparse Gibson–Ashby-type law, only the density exponent and its stretching-fraction interaction are recovered in every refit; secondary terms are selected in 38–90% of refits whether or not they exist. Finally, a break-even density exponent applied to a published study of eight honeycomb designs shows that reported energy-absorption gains of 22-47% came with 1.2- to 3.3-f…

Design, Fabrication, and Validation of Low-Cost 3D-Printed Lumbar Spine Anatomical Training Models for Fluoroscopic Guided Injections
abstract: Epidural lumbar spine injections are commonly performed for radicular low back pain and typically require fluoroscopic guidance. However, learning fluoroscopic spatial navigation can be challenging for trainees, and commercially available training phantoms are costly, with few models providing fluoroscopic compatibility. This study describes the design, fabrication, and validation of a low-cost 3D-printed lumbar spine simulator for fluoroscopy-guided epidural injection training. A lumbosacral stereolithography model was printed using radiopaque glass-filled polylactic acid to simulate osseous anatomy, then embedded in modified synthetic ballistic gel to mimic soft tissue needle resistance. Spine phantoms were used during a resident physician training workshop focused on interlaminar and transforaminal epidural injection techniques. The models were durable, provided realistic fluoroscopic visualization, and demonstrated acceptable tactile needle resistance. Total one-time costs were $317 USD, with consumable costs of $92 USD per model. Among 18 workshop participants, self-reported confidence (5-point Likert) significantly improved across all assessed domains ( P <0.05), including anatomy knowledge (3.47 to 4.39), landmark identification (2.79 to 4.00), fluoroscopic image optimization (2.32 to 4.00), interlaminar epidural technique (2.05 to 3.89), and transforaminal epidural tech…

title: In silico design of FOXM1-DNA complex inhibitors as an alternative against triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: FOXM1 is a key transcription factor that promotes cell proliferation, drives genomic stability, increases chemoresistance, and is overexpressed in almost all cancer types. In this context, FOXM1 emerges as an attractive biological target since it is a crucial oncogene and transcriptional regulator overexpressed in breast cancer, especially in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Therefore, there is strong interest in developing Forkhead domain inhibitors (FDIs) as an alternative to treat TNBC. In this work, we performed a detailed structural analysis of canonical and non-canonical FOXM1-DNA complexes to identify binding sites and key residues that govern intermolecular interaction stability. We identified the drug-like binding site "S1" not reported in the literature. Besides, we confirmed "S2", which was previously studied and reported already. We explored the structural dynamics of S1 and S2 using residue atomic fluctuations, generating two new S1 and two new S2 conformations for each FOXM1 crystal structure: CT 1 and CT 2 for S1, and CT 3 and CT 4 for S2. Followed by directed molecular docking of FDIs with known binding affinity ( K i ) to FOXM1. Based on these findings, we used the ligand interaction energy ( E − inter ) and a lipophilicity parameter (LogP) to explain the antiproliferative activity of FDIs in the MDA-MB-231 cell line ( -LogIC 50 ) using a QSAR model, which…

title: Understanding teachers' curriculum reform receptivity: a psychological and cognitive perspective
abstract: Purpose This study examined teachers' curriculum receptivity by integrating pedagogical beliefs, perceived benefits and costs, cognitive load and reform fatigue within a unified psychological framework. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey of 784 in-service teachers in the Teacher Professional Education (PPG) program was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapping to assess measurement validity and structural relationships. Findings Attitude was the strongest predictor of curriculum receptivity. Germane load had the largest positive effect on attitude and contributed to receptivity both directly and indirectly. Perceived benefits positively affect both attitude and receptivity, whereas reform fatigue has a negative effect. Intrinsic load had a small but significant positive effect on attitude and an indirect effect on receptivity, although its direct effect on receptivity was not significant. Pedagogical beliefs, perceived costs and extraneous load showed limited or non-significant effects. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation, and the sample's concentration in Sulawesi may affect generalisability. This study contributes theoretically by treating curriculum receptivity as a psychologically mediated outcome and distinguishing the roles of differen…

title: The Structural Insulation of Transnational Lead Firms from Liability under the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 and a Tripartite Reform Agenda
abstract: The ready-made garment (RMG) sector of Bangladesh remains marked by a stark asymmetry between the economic control that transnational buyers exercise and the legal responsibility that they bear. This article examines why the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 (BLA) produces this insulation, and proposes a coordinated reform agenda as the most suitable means of addressing it. Drawing on doctrinal analysis of statute and case law, comparative private international law and the scholarship on the governance of global value chains, the article advances four claims. First, the territorial scope of the BLA and its bilateral conception of the employment relationship, found principally in sections 1(3), 2(49), 2(65), 3A and 161, render foreign buyers legally invisible across tiered subcontracting networks, a position reinforced by the separate enclave of the Bangladesh EPZ Labour Act, 2019. Second, although the Bangladesh Labour (Amendment) Ordinance, 2025 and the Bangladesh Labour (Amendment) Act, 2026 modernised union registration, harassment governance and penalties, they left this bilateral core untouched and may encourage buyers to shift rising compliance costs onto suppliers through indemnity clauses. Third, neither the Bangladesh Accord and its successors nor home-state due diligence statutes, particularly after the 2026 Omnibus I amendments to the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Dilige…

title: Can Family Policy Reform Shape Marriage and Fertility Intentions Among Never-Married and Childless Individuals? A Factorial Survey Experiment in Japan
abstract: Abstract Existing family policies in East Asia primarily target married couples and working parents, while the region’s fertility decline has been driven largely by decreasing marriage prevalence among unmarried individuals. This mismatch between policy design and the population driving fertility decline has been put forward as one explanation for persistently low fertility. The close linkage between marriage and childbearing in this region, however, proposes an alternative possibility in which never-married and childless individuals form their intentions by reasoning prospectively about family policies in terms of the potential financial benefits and the uncertainty associated with future childbearing. Conducting factorial survey experiments among never-married and childless individuals aged 20–34 in Japan, we examine how changes in six family policy dimensions, i.e., parental leave benefits, child allowance, university tuition, daycare availability, short-time work, and overwork restrictions, affect fertility and marriage intentions. The results show that more generous financial incentives and work-family policies significantly increase both intentions. This finding challenges the mistargeting argument by demonstrating that policies aimed at parents can shape fertility and even marriage intentions of those not yet married. Furthermore, the most generous alternatives generally…

IMPLEMENTING THE ADVANCED ORGANIZER MODEL WITH SNOWBALL THROWING TO IMPROVE STUDENT ENGAGEMENT AND LEARNING OUTCOMES IN INDONESIAN LANGUAGE LEARNING
abstract: This classroom action research examined implementing the Advance Organizer model combined with the Snowball Throwing strategy to improve student engagement and learning outcomes in Indonesian language learning among fourth-grade students at SDN 2 Gereneng, East Lombok, Indonesia. The study employed the Kemmis and McTaggart classroom action research cycle consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The participants were 14 fourth-grade students during the 2025/2026 academic year. Data were collected through a six-indicator student engagement observation sheet and a 10-item multiple-choice achievement test administered at the end of each cycle. Descriptive statistics were used to compare the results between cycles. The mean engagement score increased from 3.07 in Cycle I to 3.64 in Cycle II, while the mean learning outcome increased from 69.28 to 79.28. Classical completeness also increased from 71.42% (10 of 14 students) in Cycle I to 85.71% (12 of 14 students) in Cycle II, exceeding the predetermined 75% criterion. The findings indicate that the combination of Advance Organizer and Snowball Throwing was associated with improved student engagement and learning outcomes in the observed classroom. The study also shows the importance of strengthening classroom management, initial conceptual scaffolding, and opportunities for student interaction when implementing th…

title: THE IMPLEMENTATION OF CONTEXTUAL TEACHING AND LEARNING (CTL) IN NATURAL SCIENCES LESSONS FOR YEAR 3 STUDENTS AT SDN 1 LEPAK TIMUR
abstract: The teaching of IPAS in Year 3 at SDN 1 Lepak Timur continues to face challenges in the form of a predominance of teacher-centred learning and limited pupil involvement. Of the 31 students, 13 (41.9 per cent) achieved a mark of 70 or above, whilst 18 (58.1 per cent) scored below 70, with a class average of 65.3. This study aims to describe the implementation of Contextual Teaching and Learning (CTL) in IPAS lessons and to identify its supporting and inhibiting factors. The study employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive design. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, and were subsequently analysed using the Miles and Huberman interactive model. The analysis focused on seven components of CTL, namely constructivism, inquiry, questioning, the learning community, modelling, reflection, and authentic assessment. The results showed that CTL was implemented by linking the subject matter to everyday experiences, utilising the school environment as a learning resource, conducting group discussions, question-and-answer sessions, hands-on practice, and assessment linked to learning activities. Supporting factors included school support, teachers’ competence and creativity, the utilisation of the environment, and the availability of media and learning resources. Inhibiting factors included time constraints, variations in students’ abilities and par…

title: Digital readiness as an enabling capability for HyFlex-VR learning in vocational education
abstract: Purpose This study examines how perceived HyFlex-VR affordances and digital readiness relate to vocational students' learning experiences and whether readiness operates as a direct enabling capability or moderates the affordance–experience relationship. Design/methodology/approach A quantitatively dominant embedded mixed-method study involved 187 vocational high school students from South Sulawesi, Indonesia. After response quality screening, 169 cases were analysed using disjoint two-stage partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Digital readiness (digital infrastructure and competence) and learning experience (engagement and satisfaction) were modelled as formative higher-order composites. Open-ended survey responses were used to supplement the quantitative analysis. Findings Perceived HyFlex-VR affordances (ß = 0.216, p = 0.008) and digital readiness (ß = 0.584, p < 0.001) were positively associated with the learning experience (R2 = 0.529). Readiness did not significantly moderate the affordance–experience relationship (ß = −0.015, p = 0.728). Qualitative responses highlighted immersion, flexibility and visualisation, alongside connectivity, device constraints and preferences for classroom interaction. Research limitations/implications Cross-sectional, self-reported data from one regional context limit causal inference and generalisability of the fi…

title: PENGARUH PENGGUNAAN MODEL PEMBELAJARAN COOPERATIVE LEARNING TERHADAP KEMAMPUAN SISWA DALAM MEMBANDINGKAN PUISI DIAFAN DAN PRISMATIS KELAS VIII DI SMP NEGERI 2 BAWOLATO
abstract: ABSTRACT Junior high school students frequently encounter obstacles in distinguishing poetry that conveys ideas literally from poetic works laden with symbolic expressions. This issue underpinned a quantitative investigation at SMP Negeri 2 Bawolato to empirically evaluate whether collaborative instruction through the Cooperative Learning model produces a measurable impact on eighth-grade students' proficiency in comparing diaphanous and prismatic poetry. Fifty students participated in a quasi-experimental study utilizing a pretest-posttest control group design, evenly distributed into an experimental group and a control group of 25 learners each. Learning achievement was measured using validated pre-test and post-test instruments and analyzed through prerequisite tests alongside an independent samples t-test at a 5% significance level. Data processing revealed that the experimental group's mean score rose from 49 to 80, whereas the control group increased from 47 to 76. Although the final score difference indicated a four-point lead for the experimental class, hypothesis testing yielded a t-value of 0.608, falling below the critical t-table threshold of 2.011 (df = 48; p = 0.546 > 0.05). Consequently, the application of the Cooperative Learning model was proven not to exert a statistically significant effect on students' ability to compare diaphanous and prismatic poetry. ABST…

Uncovering determinants of anxiety among university students in Brazil: an explainable machine learning approach
abstract: Objetivo: Identificar os principais fatores de risco modificáveis e não modificáveis associados a sintomas de ansiedade em estudantes universitários brasileiros utilizando aprendizado de máquina interpretável. Método: Dados de 6.398 estudantes de 13 universidades de todas as regiões brasileiras foram extraídos do projeto UNILIFE-M. Uma classificação binária foi definida pelo ponto de corte clínico do GAD-7, e cinco modelos foram treinados e comparados. Resultados: Sem diferenças significativas de desempenho entre classificadores, o LightGBM foi selecionado por razões práticas. A análise SHAP revelou que qualidade do sono, sexo, suporte social, orientação sexual e manejo do estresse são os fatores mais influentes. Conclusão: Os achados destacam alvos para políticas de saúde mental universitária e demonstram o valor de combinar modelagem preditiva com técnicas de explicabilidade em saúde populacional.

Predictive Modeling of Heavy Metal Removal in Forward Osmosis Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Abstract Heavy metal accumulation in the aquatic system poses critical challenges for wastewater treatment. Forward osmosis is a promising membrane technology for the rejection of heavy metals in wastewater. However, the prediction of heavy metal removal using membranes remains scarce. To address this gap, various machine learning algorithms including RF, XGBoost, SVR, MLP, and hybrid stacking have been developed to simultaneously predict heavy metal % removal and water flux. Among the evaluated models, XGBoost and hybrid stacking showed the strongest overall predictive performance. Hybrid stacking achieved a removal efficiency R2 of 0.9897, whereas XGBoost achieved R2 0.9977 for water flux. The model was further validated using 5-fold cross-validation. To enhance interpretability, partial dependence plots and Shapley additive explanations were used to evaluate the feature importance. Model interpretability analysis revealed that the contact angle, zeta potential, draw solution concentration, and DS type were the dominant features. The interpretable algorithm provides theoretical guidance on the forward osmosis membrane and various operating conditions for heavy metal rejection.

title: The Influence of Principal Servant Leadership and Subjective Well-Being on Junior High School Students’ Self-Regulated Learning through Emotional Intelligence
abstract: This study examines how principal servant leadership and students’ subjective well-being influence junior high school students' self-regulated learning, both directly and indirectly through students’ emotional intelligence as a mediating variable. Servant leadership is assumed to create a supportive, empathetic, and student-centered school environment. At the same time, subjective well-being is viewed as a personal resource that strengthens students’ emotional and learning competencies. This study employed a quantitative approach with an explanatory survey design. The sample consisted of 250 junior high school students (125 male and 125 female) selected through probability sampling. Data were collected using adapted standardized questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The results show that servant leadership was positively associated with self-regulated learning (β = 0.228) and, to a lesser extent, with emotional intelligence (β = 0.111). Subjective well-being was the strongest predictor of emotional intelligence (β = 0.415; f² = 0.211), whereas its direct path to self-regulated learning was negative and negligible (β = −0.054). Emotional intelligence was positively associated with self-regulated learning (β = 0.181), but the indirect effects through emotional intelligence were small (0.020 for servant leader…

title: The Radio–FIR Correlation in the Context of Deep Radio Source Counts
abstract: Abstract Increasingly deep, confusion-limited radio surveys have pushed direct radio source-count measurements down to tens of μ Jy at 1.4 GHz. Confusion-noise P ( D ) analyses extend the statistical counts to below 1 μ Jy. Radio source counts have allowed for constraints on the radio-derived star formation rate density (SFRD) history through models of the backwards evolution of the local radio luminosity function, using the radio–far-infrared (FIR) correlation, q ∝ log ( L FIR / L 1.4 ) , to convert radio luminosities to FIR luminosities and, hence, star formation rates. Recent deep radio source counts from MeerKAT suggest a potential tension in the SFRD history between radio and UV/IR measurements at 1 ≲ z ≲ 2. This corresponds to a ≳3 σ discrepancy between the predicted and measured source counts near the star-forming galaxy (SFG) source count S 2 n ( S ) peak of ∼30 μ Jy under both a pure luminosity (PLE) and combined luminosity and density evolution (LADE). We consider what the requirement of agreement between radio source counts and the observed UV/IR SFRD indicates about the redshift evolution of the radio–FIR correlation and its intrinsic scatter out to z = 3. We introduce a radio-luminosity based parameterization to q FIR ( z ) based on changing thermal radio fractions alone that agrees with the observed stellar-mass dependent q FIR ( z ) better than a nonevolving or d…

title: Does market-oriented climate policy promote biodiversity?
abstract: Abstract Biodiversity constitutes a crucial foundation for maintaining ecosystem stability and human well-being. Based on the data of birdwatching records from China, this paper measures the biodiversity of Chinese cities and examines the impact of the carbon emission trading pilot policy (CETPP) on biodiversity as well as its underlying mechanism. The results show that CETPP can significantly improve biodiversity in the pilot areas. The promotional effect is more pronounced in regions with high economic development and high industrial agglomeration. CETPP enhances biodiversity by promoting green industrial transformation, protecting green space resources and developing green finance. CETPP has a negative spatial spillover effect on biodiversity in adjacent areas. This paper enriches the research on the impact of environmental regulations on biodiversity and provides empirical evidence for biodiversity conservation in the process of low-carbon transition.

title: The Transmission of Monetary Shocks to the Sharia Capital Market: A Systematic Review and Implications for the Real Sector
abstract: This study examines how monetary shocks are transmitted through Islamic capital markets and under what conditions their effects may reach real-sector financing. It addresses a gap between studies that examine individual assets or channels and the broader question of how sovereign sukuk, corporate sukuk, and Sharia-compliant equities interact with macro-financial conditions and productive investment. The study applies a structured systematic integrative review of peer-reviewed research published mainly during 2015-September 2026, complemented by foundational monetary-transmission literature and official macro-financial statistics. Twelve core studies from leading international journals and Indonesian SINTA 1-2 journals were coded according to the type of shock, instrument, transmission channel, time horizon, and economic outcome. The synthesis indicates that Islamic assets are not uniformly insulated from monetary shocks. Sukuk may display lower sensitivity to unexpected interest-rate news than conventional bonds, while Islamic equities can remain equally or more responsive than conventional equities. Exchange rates, global risk appetite, market liquidity, instrument structure, and the fiscal use of sukuk proceeds condition the transmission. The principal contribution is an integrated framework linking global and domestic monetary shocks to asset prices and liquidity, then to fi…

title: Electricity–Carbon Coupled Market Operation Strategy for Virtual Power Plants Considering Hydropower Regulation Capability
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy resources has introduced challenges in coordinating distributed wind, photovoltaic, and small hydropower resources in hydropower-rich regions, especially under upstream–downstream hydraulic coupling constraints and electricity market competition. This paper proposes an electricity–carbon coupled market operation strategy for a river basin virtual power plant (RBVPP) considering hydropower regulation capability. First, a hydraulic coupling model of cascade small hydropower stations is developed to characterize reservoir storage variation, upstream–downstream water transfer, and water balance constraints. A hybrid pumped storage system is further integrated to enhance the cross-period coordination capability of renewable energy resources. Then, the China Certified Emission Reduction (CCER) mechanism is incorporated into the electricity market framework to quantify the low-carbon value of renewable electricity. Based on this framework, a bi-level optimization model is established, in which the upper level determines the RBVPP bidding strategy to maximize its net revenue, while the lower level jointly determines market-clearing quantities and physically feasible internal operating schedules for each submitted bidding strategy. Under the studied wet-season condition, combined CEA–CCER participation increases RBVPP net revenue and reduce…

title: Trot After Market: A Bi-Coupled Adaptive Network for Stock Prediction via Relation-Adaptive Multimodal Alignment
abstract: Predicting next-day stock returns requires integrating heterogeneous information while tracking evolving inter-stock dependencies. We propose the Bi-Coupled Adaptive Network (BCAN), in which stock relationships learned on the preceding trading day guide the alignment of today’s news and market information. The fused representations update a relation state that the model carries across trading days. We evaluate BCAN on 116 U.S. securities from 2010 to 2022 and 160 Chinese stocks from 2018 to 2025, using nine and seven rolling phases, respectively. Five of the seven price-based baselines have lower mean pointwise errors than the proposed model, which ranks sixth of nine on mean MSE while leading on mean NDCG@5, on the gross Sharpe ratio, and on the gross annualized return. The gross figures are computed under idealized closing prices and zero transaction costs; under an executable protocol that adds a one-trading-day information delay and transaction costs, the U.S. daily rebalanced strategy turns net-negative at 20 bps. In separate comparisons on shared observations, BCAN improves top-of-ranking quality over an OHLCV-only variant and a Simple Fusion model with both modalities. Portfolio metrics complement these comparisons as gross results under idealized closing prices and zero transaction costs. Ablations provide evidence on relation-conditioned alignment and the persistent re…

title: A TEACHING CASE ON HOW TO CREATE A PREMIUM BRAND IN A MASS-MARKET BRAND: THE EXPERIENCE OF MARUTI SUZUKI'S NEXA
abstract: The Case will analyze how India's biggest auto company and established supplier of small, affordable vehicles developed a unique distribution path for selling high-end vehicles. Apart from the company's regular showrooms, this channel was launched in July 2015, which came with its own showrooms, branding and customer experience, and was named NEXA. It grew to a few hundred showrooms and a big percentage of the company's sales over the next decade. The case outlines the problems the company faced, the options they considered when creating NEXA, and how the channel developed and changed over time, as well as the challenges that still existed. It is designed to be used for class discussion about marketing strategy, brand architecture, channel management and retail management. The case asks students to consider how a company can be successful in entering a new business segment without destroying the value of its existing brand and what the company needs to do to its dealers to achieve this.

title: A big data approach to oil cargo trade and its implications for the oil tanker ship charter market
abstract: Analisis menggunakan big data, kecerdasan buatan, dan platform intelijen maritim mengubah perdagangan muatan minyak dan penyewaan kapal tanker. Artikel ini meninjau tiga perkembangan terkait, yaitu perubahan struktural pasar penyewaan tanker, penetapan tarif angkutan secara algoritmik, serta pemanfaatan intelijen maritim untuk keputusan operasional dan komersial. Berdasarkan dokumentasi platform, peraturan, kasus perusahaan yang dilaporkan, dan penelitian peramalan yang ditelaah sejawat, artikel ini berargumen bahwa arus data kini turut menentukan keputusan penyewaan selain arus muatan fisik. Sintesis bukti menunjukkan bahwa ukuran pasokan berbasis AIS dapat menjelaskan perkembangan tarif angkutan ketika indikator pasokan tradisional tidak mampu melakukannya, dan model peramalan hibrida telah menghasilkan nilai ekonomi terukur dalam portofolio penyewaan VLCC. Kajian ini merupakan sintesis bukti; tidak menyajikan estimasi kausal sendiri, dan angka yang dilaporkan perusahaan disampaikan sebagaimana adanya. Kontribusinya adalah mengorganisasikan bukti praktisi dan akademik yang tersebar ke dalam satu kerangka serta mengidentifikasi bagian yang didukung bukti kuat dan bagian yang masih terbatas. Big data analytics, artificial intelligence, and maritime intelligence platforms are reshaping how oil cargo is traded and how tankers are chartered. This paper reviews three related develo…

title: Multi‐Objective Optimization of Electricity Trading for Distribution System Operator Based on Dynamic Pricing Game With Multiple Virtual Power Plants
abstract: ABSTRACT With the rapid development of distributed energy resources, coordinated operation among multiple virtual power plants (VPPs) has become increasingly important in distribution networks, making electricity trading and resource coordination critical for the stable and efficient operation of power systems. To balance the economic interests of DSO, the operational profit of VPPs, and environmental costs during transactions, this article proposes a multi‐objective optimization model for DSO‐led electricity trading and resource coordination based on a dynamic pricing game. The model integrates key factors including power trading between the DSO and multiple VPPs, time‐sharing tariff mechanisms, and control costs of pollutants such as , and . A Stackelberg game framework is constructed where DSO acts as the leader to formulate optimal pricing strategies, and multiple VPPs act as followers to independently optimize their DER scheduling in response to a common pricing signal issued by the DSO. NSGA‐II is adopted to solve the multi‐objective optimization problem, achieving a balance between maximizing DSO's economic profit and minimizing system environmental costs. Simulation results based on a test system with three VPPs show that the proposed method outperforms traditional algorithms in both economic and environmental performance: DSO's average profit is higher than comparative…
