Cross-Border Participation: A False Hope for Fixing Capacity Market Externalities?
abstract: As national capacity markets gain momentum in Europe, their cross-border externalities might become a growing issue. With the hope of mitigating such externalities, EU regulation mandates explicit cross-border participation. In this paper, we assess the effectiveness of this rule in addressing the externalities of a national capacity market on a neighboring energy-only market, using a stylized optimization model. We have two conclusions, based on three findings. First finding, cross-border participation does not entirely mitigate the cross-border externalities. Second finding, implicit and explicit cross-border participation yield equivalent results. Third finding, capacity markets’ cross-border externalities might prevent them from ensuring security of supply. Based on the first and third findings, we conclude for the medium-term, that we may need to evolve from a national toward a European adequacy approach. Based on the second finding, we conclude that in the short-term, implicit cross-border participation could be tolerated, contributing to the Commission’s streamlining objectives. Forecasting stock price crash risk in Vietnam: evidence from machine learning and traditional forecasting methods
abstract: This study compares the efficacy of machine learning algorithms with traditional methods for predicting stock price crash risk in Vietnam. We unveil nuanced insights by analyzing data from 553 listed firms in Vietnam from March 2009 to May 2024. The Decision Tree model performs better for short-term forecasts, while Stepwise delivers more stable, accurate results at long-term horizons, particularly in the manufacturing and services sectors. Moreover, our findings underscore the pivotal role of illiquidity as a leading determinant of crash risks in Vietnam. Furthermore, robustness checks against Autoregressive Distributed Lag and Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity methods confirm the Decision Tree’s superior short-term predictive performance. These findings offer practical implications for managers, investors, and policymakers, enabling them to develop effective risk management strategies and promote sustainable development initiatives in emerging markets.

title: Implementing a Coordinated Translational Research Framework for Addressing Cardiometabolic Health Disparities: Insights From the Forge AHEAD Center
abstract: ABSTRACT Cardiometabolic conditions such as obesity, diabetes, and hypertension frequently co‐occur and are driven by multilevel determinants. However, translational research is often segmented across single diseases, settings, and phases of care, limiting population impact. There is a need for coordinated frameworks that integrate multilevel intervention design, implementation science methods, and harmonized measurements across studies. We developed a coordinated translational research framework within the Forge AHEAD Center, a multi‐institutional, community‐engaged research center focused on cardiometabolic health disparities in the Deep South. The framework integrates five design principles: multilevel intervention design, hybrid effectiveness–implementation orientation, coordinated portfolio‐based study structure across the care continuum, prospective harmonization of common data elements, and sustained community engagement. We operationalized this framework across seven studies spanning prevention, treatment, and management of cardiometabolic disease. Implementation science frameworks were incorporated across the studies, with cost‐effectiveness evaluations included where appropriate, and a “roadmap” model was developed to illustrate cross‐study coordination within the Center. The framework facilitated alignment of various interventions, including digital health, community…

title: A hybrid method for forecasting seasonal rail transport volumes of agricultural products
abstract: The study proposes a hybrid method for predictive analytics of rail freight transportation, taking into account periodic seasonal fluctuations. The method incorporates an autoregressive integrated moving average model and machine learning. Random forest and gradient boosting methods have shown positive results for identifying trends and improving forecasting accuracy. A hybrid method is proposed based on Random Forest, XGBoost, and the ARIMA model. The studied dataset of transportation data was preprocessed, normalized, and filtered. Using a program developed in the functional programming language Python and machine learning libraries, the following research steps were performed: data loading, preprocessing, building forecasting models, calculating accuracy indicators, graphical part of the computational experiment, and plotting graphs. A comparative analysis of the predictive analytics results was conducted using various, commonly used metrics: MAE and RMSE. The results of the computational experiment showed a 9% increase in forecasting accuracy for rail freight transportation using the proposed hybrid method. The developed hybrid method offers the opportunity to improve the quality of predictive analytics for effective management in the field of railway transportation.

Typhoon intensity forecasting using deep learning and physics-guided SHIPS-based predictors
abstract: Abstract Current tropical cyclone intensity forecasting faces a dilemma: deep learning often dilutes explicit physical features by ingesting raw data, while traditional statistical models lose critical spatial structures by compressing screened predictors into 1-Dimentional scalars. To address this, we propose an attention-based deep learning framework that ingests physically screened predictors reconstructed into explicit 2-Dimentional spatial fields. Quantitatively, the proposed model achieves a highly competitive 24-hour mean absolute error of 3.85 m·s⁻¹, outperforming most advanced deep learning baselines. Notably, it demonstrates superior predictive skill over official operational forecasts at 24–48 hour, and maintains robust accuracy comparable to leading official agencies during 72–120 hour. Beyond yielding steady 48–120 hour predictions, our spatial attention analysis reveals that the network intrinsically recognizes the distinct thermodynamic roles of different oceanic variables. Autonomously, the model focuses on the inner-core Sea Surface Temperature for immediate intensity potential, while progressively shifting its attention toward broader Ocean Heat Content to capture long-term environmental interactions. These findings emphasize that the inherent physical meaning of input variables is paramount in meteorological deep learning training. Integrating domain-knowledg…

title: An Integrated Machine Learning Framework for Wind Speed Forecasting and Energy Estimation with Cross-Site Evaluation
abstract: Wind speed (WS) and wind energy (WE) prediction are key to the proper operation of a power system (PS) and the integration of wind turbines. Existing research, however, has primarily focused on prediction accuracy and feature engineering. Model interpretability, statistical validation, energy evaluation, uncertainty quantification, and cross-site validation within a single framework remain understudied. This research introduces an integrated machine learning (ML) framework that combines automated data processing, multidirectional temporal feature engineering, model benchmarking, WE evaluation, statistical validation, explainable prediction, uncertainty analysis, and cross-site estimation. This study also translates forecast errors into wind power density and turbine-energy terms and tests the trained model at independent stations. This research tests five predictive models on 26,304 hourly WS observations: Linear Regression (LR), gradient boosting (GB), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with Attention, Convolutional Neural Network–Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN–GRU) hybrid, and Random Forest (RF). The optimal predictive performance was obtained by GB, with R2 = 0.8026, RMSE = 4.3303 km/h, and MAE = 3.1574 km/h. title: Loss of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 activity during liquid plasma storage is associated with increased fibrinolysis in response to tissue plasminogen activator
abstract: BACKGROUND: In trauma, hyperfibrinolysis influences the need for massive transfusion and mortality. Tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) sensitivity increases during whole blood storage despite rising plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) activity. Liquid plasma demonstrates preserved fibrinogen function in storage, but fibrinolytic regulation in stored liquid plasma remains undescribed. METHODS: Liquid plasma tails (n = 28) were obtained and stored at 4 °C. Thromboelastography was challenged with 75 ng/mL exogenous tPA at three storage time points (day 1–3, 7–10, and 28) to assess resistance to fibrinolysis. PAI-1 activity was measured through a modified enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) that captures only active PAI-1 utilizing immobilized active urokinase. Statistical analysis included two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Spearman correlation. Significance was set at p <0.05. RESULTS: Aging liquid plasma units demonstrated a significant, progressive increase in fibrinolysis (LY30) in response to tPA over time ( p = 0.008). Alpha angle gradually increased, and maximum amplitude remained stable with storage. PAI-1 activity decreased with storage ( p < 0.001) and inversely correlated with tPA-thromboelastography LY30 (Spearman r = -0.40, p = 0.04). CONCLUSIONS: Stored liquid plasma demonstrates declining PAI-1 activity, increased tPA-mediated fibrinolysis, and pre…

Bias-Aware State-of-Charge Estimation with Causal Residual Learning for Battery Energy Storage Systems
abstract: Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is essential for reliable battery energy storage system (BESS) operation. For lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, the flat open-circuit-voltage characteristic weakens voltage-based SOC observability. During dynamic operation, temperature mismatch and uncertain initialization make voltage-model errors difficult to distinguish from SOC errors. Physics-based extended Kalman filter (EKF) observers preserve charge-balance propagation and recursive covariance updates, but a fixed equivalent-circuit model may assign voltage-model error to the SOC correction. Direct neural-network regressors can learn nonlinear sensor-to-SOC relationships, but do not retain the physical correction mechanism of the EKF. Learning a voltage residual within the observer can combine physical propagation with data-driven error compensation, yet reducing voltage residuals alone does not guarantee a more accurate SOC trajectory. To address this problem, we develop a bias-aware EKF with a causal residual-learning interface. An explicit voltage-bias state augments a second-order equivalent-circuit model and separates persistent voltage discrepancy from SOC correction. A convolutional neural network (CNN) uses only preceding current, voltage, and temperature measurements together with the preceding EKF prior to predict the mean of the remaining dynamic voltage discrep…

title: On-Demand Enzymatic Generation of Garlic Bioactive Compounds: Antimicrobial Activity After Component Storage and Associated Survival Outcomes in Vibrio vulnificus-Challenged Zebrafish
abstract: Garlic bioactive compounds (GBCs) are antimicrobial but chemically unstable. We evaluated on-demand enzymatic bioactive compound (EBC) generation using a crude garlic substrate extract and a recombinant BcPatB preparation. Pre-formed GBCs and the separate EBC components were stored for 7 days at 25 ± 2 °C before comparison. GC–MS profiles were assessed in three independently prepared samples per condition, each injected once. Two provisionally labelled chromatographic signals decreased by 95.1% and 84.9% in the GBC workflow and by 23.0% and 24.1% in the EBC workflow. These fixed-reference methyl phenyl sulfide equivalents describe signal changes, not validated concentrations or degradation rates. The GBC inhibition-zone diameter against Vibrio vulnificus decreased from 46.0 ± 0.5 mm on Day 1 to 23.3 ± 0.7 mm on Day 7 (mean ± SD; n = 3 biological replicates). EBCs generated after component storage produced visible inhibition zones, but superiority over stored GBCs was not established by inferential analysis. Adult zebrafish (Danio rerio) received preparations at a nominal 1:100 dilution (v/v) after V. vulnificus challenge and were observed for 72 h. Survival curves were descriptive; treatment effects remain unconfirmed without accounting for shared exposure within wells and independent experiments. Immune-related transcript measurements were exploratory. These observations motiv…

title: Variable-Length Cross-Camera Vehicle Trajectory Reconstruction via Duration-Aware Upstream–Downstream Interaction Modeling
abstract: Continuous vehicle trajectories are essential for traffic analysis, yet discontinuous roadside camera coverage inevitably leaves unobserved trajectory segments. Existing learning-based cross-camera reconstruction methods commonly assume predefined horizons, limiting their ability to accommodate different travel times between fixed camera locations. To address this limitation, this study develops a variable-length cross-camera vehicle trajectory reconstruction framework. The downstream observation sequence is encoded as a temporal boundary condition on the upstream representation, while dynamic target-centered graphs characterize surrounding-vehicle interaction evolution across the sensing gap. Their reliability is further modulated according to the actual reconstruction duration. Temporal queries defined at vehicle-specific missing timestamps drive a shared decoder, decoupling trajectory generation from a fixed output horizon. Experiments on HighD show that, under a fixed 2-s horizon, the proposed model achieves an ADE of 0.1525 m, reducing the error by 3.42% relative to TBTC. Across variable durations of 3–12 s in VISSIM, the proposed model reduces overall ADE by approximately 10.3% relative to a fixed-12-s baseline. Ablation studies support the contributions of downstream temporal boundary conditioning and duration-aware interaction modeling, while the fixed-output comparison…

title: Multi-Stage Quality Control for Doppler Velocity Aiding in Loosely Coupled GNSS/INS Land-Vehicle Navigation
abstract: Doppler-derived velocity can constrain inertial navigation errors, but outliers that survive basic observation screening may degrade the subsequent integrated solution. Here, we develop and evaluate a multi-stage quality-control (QC) procedure for Doppler velocity aiding in loosely coupled Global Navigation Satellite Systems/inertial navigation system (GNSS/INS) integration. The procedure combines pre-fit residual screening, leverage-adjusted post-fit residual screening, and an epoch-level velocity continuity check, followed by residual-based formal precision assessment for measurement weighting and update acceptance. A 53.3 min vehicle field test was used to compare Doppler estimates obtained with basic processing alone and with the additional QC stages. Under the original observation weighting, quality control reduced horizontal velocity root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 1.42 m/s to 0.24 m/s and the 95th-percentile horizontal velocity error from 3.06 m/s to 0.47 m/s over 3133 common valid epochs. Comparisons using the same loosely coupled framework separated the benefit of basic Doppler aiding and additional QC. Relative to INS aided by single point positioning (SPP) position measurements alone, introducing Doppler velocity estimates obtained with basic processing reduced horizontal velocity RMSE by 40.1%. Applying the additional QC stages reduced this RMSE by a further 41.2…

Digital payments, impulsive buying, and financial well-being: A strategic analysis of Generation Z
abstract: This study investigates the determinants and dual consequences of digital payment usage among Generation Z consumers in Vietnam, examining both positive pathways to financial well-being and negative mechanisms through impulsive buying. Extending the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2), we develop a moderated mediation model incorporating perceived financial efficiency and impulsive buying tendency as mediating mechanisms, with financial literacy as a boundary condition. Survey data from 755 Generation Z digital payment users in major Vietnamese cities were analyzed using structural equation modelling (SEM). Results demonstrate that performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, and trust significantly predict digital payment usage. Digital payment usage simultaneously enhances perceived financial efficiency and increases impulsive buying tendency, which, respectively, improves and diminishes perceived financial well-being. Impulsive buying tendency fully mediates the negative relationship between digital payment usage and financial well-being. Critically, financial literacy moderates the digital payment-impulsive buying relationship, weakening the positive effect among financially literate consumers (Venkatesh et al., 2012; Lusardi & Mitchell, 2014). These findings advance financial technology (FinTech) adoption theory while informing str…

title: Bio‐Based Chitosan Schiff Base for Synergistic Flame Retardancy in Silicone–Acrylic Coatings via a Ternary Co‐Doping Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT To address the fire hazards associated with the flammability of plywood and the environmental pollution caused by conventional halogenated flame retardants, this study developed a composite flame‐retardant coating based on a chitosan oligosaccharide–vanillin (COS‐V) Schiff base synergistically modified with melamine polyphosphate (MPP)/zinc phytate (ZnPA) in a silicone–acrylic emulsion (SAE). The effects of the MPP, ZnPA, and COS‐V ratios on the flame‐retardant performance of the coating were systematically investigated through an orthogonal experimental design, and the ternary synergistic flame‐retardant mechanism was elucidated by combining pyrolysis kinetics analysis and regression modeling. The results showed that Z5 (MPP 1.28 g, ZnPA 0.80 g, COS‐V 1.44 g) exhibited the best flame‐retardant performance: an LOI of 30.3%, a UL‐94 V‐0 rating, the pHRR reduced to 81 kW·m −2 , a THR of 23.77 MJ·m −2 , and a char residue of 11.8% at 930°C. Pyrolysis kinetics analysis indicated that Z5 possessed the highest activation energy (363.52 kJ·mol −1 ) in the key charring stage (355°C–430°C), confirming the carbon layer formed by ternary coordination is denser and stronger, and has high protection. The regression model ( R 2 = 0.99) quantitatively described the relationship between the formulation parameters and THR, and the LOOCV predictive R 2 of 0.87 validated the robustness o…

title: Systemwide Quality Improvement Strategy to Reduce Nitrous Oxide Environmental Emissions in a Brazilian Health Network
abstract: Abstract Background Nitrous oxide (N₂O) is a potent greenhouse gas commonly used in perioperative care and with substantial environmental impact. This study evaluated a systemwide quality improvement (QI) initiative designed to achieve 85% reduction in carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) emissions attributable to N₂O across a large private Brazilian hospital network. Methods A multicenter before-after QI protocol was implemented across 54 hospitals between September/2024 and December/2025 using sequential Plan–Do–Study–Act cycles: cycle 1 delivered a systemwide educational program; cycle 2 introduced operational restriction of N₂O through disconnection of anesthesia workstations from the central pipeline with protocol-guided use limited to pediatric inhalational anesthesia induction; and cycle 3 implemented hospital-level benchmarking with structured feedback and leadership engagement. Results Baseline mean N₂O consumption per surgical procedure was 0.7 ± 0.9 kg, with total network consumption of 15,954 kg/month. Hospital operational age was not associated with baseline consumption intensity (β = 0.008; 95% CI − 0.001 to 0.02; p = 0.11). At the network level, baseline N₂O-related CO₂e emissions showed a median of 4.23 kt (IQR 4.11–4.67). Following implementation, median monthly emissions decreased to 0.29 kt (IQR 0.24–0.66). Mean monthly emissions decreased from 4.36 to 0.45 kt, a…

title: Complementing Compendial Compliance: A Turbidity-Based Control Strategy for Benzyl Alcohol Quality in Parenteral Drug Products
abstract: Abstract Benzyl alcohol is widely used as an antimicrobial preservative in multi-dose parenteral products, yet raw material lots that conform to all compendial requirements can still cause particulate formation, solution turbidity, and oxidative degradation in the formulated drug product. Here, we identify the principal water-insoluble impurity responsible for turbidity and develop an objective, instrument-based control for excipient quality. Reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) profiling, supported by orthogonal gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC−MS), identified benzaldehyde dibenzyl acetal (BDBA)an acid-catalyzed condensation product of benzaldehyde and benzyl alcoholas the dominant water-insoluble species, present at levels that evade compendial purity assays. Controlled spiking experiments confirmed that BDBA, and not the other benzyl alcohol impurities, is responsible for the turbidity: on aqueous dilution, BDBA exceeds its low aqueous solubility and phase-separates into sub-micron colloidal particles that scatter light, whereas an equal total load of the other identified impurities remained near 1 nm and essentially clear. A nephelometric turbidity method employing a 0.01% (w/v) poloxamer 188 diluent and a 10 NTU acceptance criterion was developed as a rapid, quantitative alternative to time-consuming RP-HPLC testing and to the subjectiv…

title: Estrategia de Publicidad Digital y su Influencia en las Conductas de Compras Compulsivas de Estudiantes Universitarios
abstract: The objective of this research was to evaluate digital advertising strategies and their influence on the compulsive buying behaviors of university students. The study employs a quantitative approach with a descriptive and explanatory scope, utilizing a non-experimental, cross-sectional research design. The target population consists of 102 female students, from which a sample of 82 was drawn. Data collection was conducted via a survey using a five-point Likert scale. Descriptive statistics were used for the analysis. The results indicate that 39.0% of the respondents reported sometimes receiving digital advertisements related to their personal interests; 24.4% indicated that they receive them almost always, and 14.6% stated that they always do. In contrast, 12.2% reported receiving them almost never, and 9.8% never. These findings demonstrate that a significant proportion of the participants are exposed to digital advertising tailored to their personal interests. In conclusion, digital advertising strategies can influence the compulsive buying behaviors of these students, as they generate stimuli that may encourage rapid, poorly planned purchasing decisions.

The role of entropy production and thermodynamic uncertainty relations in the asymmetric thermalization of open quantum systems
abstract: Abstract The asymmetry between heating and cooling in open quantum systems is a hallmark of nonequilibrium dynamics. Here, we investigate the thermalization of a quantum system weakly coupled to a bosonic thermal bath under detailed balance, focusing on the entropy production rate and the quantum thermokinetic uncertainty relation (TKUR). Within the sector of states that remain diagonal in the energy basis we derive a perturbative expression for the time-dependent entropy production rate by expanding the relative entropy around equilibrium in terms of Liouvillian eigenmodes. Through this expansion, we determine that the spectral gap, the overlap of the initial state with the slowest decay mode, and the mode weight control the entropy production. Particularly for the thermal qubit, the ratio of the initial rates of heating and cooling has an exact closed form. Heating involves a higher initial entropy production, and hence faster thermalization, solely because of its larger spectral gap, i.e. the bath-temperature dependence of the dissipative rate. The TKUR is then used as a diagnostic tool that relates the asymmetry to the precision bounds on heat-current fluctuations. The analysis presented here is intended to clarify the thermodynamic origin of the asymmetry within the well-controlled Markovian case.

How Cost-Effective Were Subsidies for Solar Energy in Germany?
abstract: Abstract We study Germany’s photovoltaic subsidy program, estimating a dynamic model of new technology adoption which accounts for heterogeneity in residential ownership structures. We find that homeowner and landlord investors heavily discount future benefits, highlighting the suboptimality of the feed-in tariff structure and the inefficient use of government funds. Our estimates suggest that administrative costs associated with tenant electricity contracts discourage landlords from investing in new energy technologies. Our analysis suggests that policy design should prioritize upfront investment subsidies over feed-in tariffs to promote renewable energy adoption. Reducing administrative costs associated with tenant electricity programs is key to unlock investments by landlords and expand tenants’ access to solar energy, thereby enhancing cost-effectiveness.

title: The proteotoxicity of azetidine-2-carboxylic acid is associated with reactive oxygen species accumulation
abstract: Introduction Plants make diverse metabolites to outcompete neighboring organisms for space and resources. Some of these toxic metabolites broadly disrupt conserved molecular mechanisms, such as protein biosynthesis. Nonproteinogenic amino acids (NPAAs) are a structurally diverse class of metabolites that interfere with protein biosynthesis. The proline (Pro) analog azetidine-2-carboxylic acid (Aze) inhibits plant growth through misincorporation during protein biosynthesis. However, it is unknown if a cascade of downstream stress responses is triggered following Aze misincorporation. Methods Here, we investigate the morphological and stress responses in Arabidopsis grown on Aze. Results Investigation of root morphological responses show not only reduced root growth, but increased root branching following growth on Aze. Altered root morphology is coupled with a reduced gravitropic response. Aboveground organs were also affected by Aze, including reduced chlorophyll content, reduced photosynthetic efficiency, and increased anthocyanin content. We then tested whether Aze induces reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation using multiple approaches and observed both immediate and sustained accumulation of general ROS and H 2 O 2 following treatment with Aze. When plants were grown on Aze supplemented with Pro, ROS levels were restored to normal levels, suggesting that reducing misinc…

title: Four-Dimensional Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy Nanoscale Phase Mapping of the Lithium-Metal Surface Passivation Layer
abstract: Abstract Mapping microstructural features is vital to developing next-generation materials in renewable energy applications. However, the nanometer-scale dimensions, chemical heterogeneity, and beam sensitivity of these materials make their structural characterization exceptionally challenging. Here, we present a data acquisition and analysis workflow for four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) applied to a beam-sensitive lithium-metal filament sample with a surface passivation layer. By combining data dimensionality reduction with unsupervised machine-learning approaches, we perform real-space clustering to enhance signal-to-noise ratios across large data sets. Automated Bragg reflection analysis was then used to identify distinct crystallographic phases within the surface passivation layer. This approach enables nanoscale phase mapping of dominant species across large fields of view with nanometer-level lateral resolution. We identify lithium oxide and lithium hydroxide as the predominant crystalline phases in the lithium-metal surface passivation layer.

Labor market adjustment to natural disasters: Quasi‐experimental evidence from the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes in Türkiye
abstract: Abstract This study examines the labor market effects of the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes in Türkiye using nationally representative Labor Force Survey data for 2021–2024 and a difference‐in‐differences approach. The results indicate that employment declined by 3.6 percentage points for men and 2.2 percentage points for women in affected regions. Employment losses were concentrated in services, while effects in agriculture and manufacturing were generally insignificant. In contrast, real wages remained largely unchanged. Heterogeneity analyses reveal variation across education groups and employment types. Overall, labor market adjustment occurred primarily through employment losses rather than wage changes.

title: Тенденции и диспропорции аграрного рынка труда сельскохозяйственного региона (на материалах Ростовской области)
abstract: Введение. Основной проблемой аграрного рынка труда является структурное несоответствие спроса и предложения, которое заключается в отсутствии сбалансированности между наличием рабочей силы определенной профессиональной подготовки и уровня квалификации и требованиями вакансий. Динамичные технологические трансформации и масштабная цифровизация сельскохозяйственного производства не обеспечиваются квалифицированными кадрами при в целом трудоизбыточном предложении рабочей силы в отрасли. Сегодня такое несоответствие оценивается как критическое, находится в фокусе внимания государства и бизнеса. Цель исследования – определить современные тенденции развития аграрного рынка труда региона с развитым сельскохозяйственным производством. Материалы и методы. Применялись общенаучные методы: анализ и синтез; индукция, дедукция и аналогия; абстрагирование; обобщение. Результаты исследования. Установлено, что аграрный рынок труда Ростовской области характеризуется диспропорциями развития: дефицитом кадров для АПК, высокой долей занятых в неформальном секторе сельского хозяйства, низкой долей работников массовых профессий с соответствующим образованием. Обсуждение и заключения. Имеющиеся проблемы требуют принятия действенных государственных мер по их решению. С одной стороны, необходимо снабдить стратегическую отрасль сельского хозяйства кадрами высокой квалификации, способными адекватно решать …

title: Child Consumers in the Digital Market: Uncovering the Limits of Business Actors' Responsibilities
abstract: The development of digital-based commerce has significantly increased online buying and selling transactions, including those involving children as consumers. This condition raises legal concerns because children generally lack the legal capacity to conduct independent legal actions, while digital transaction systems allow anyone to make purchases without adequate age verification. This study aims to analyze the obligations of business actors toward child consumers in online smartphone transactions and to examine the form of legal protection provided to child consumers in such transactions. This research applies an empirical legal method with a socio-juridical approach. Data were collected through interviews, observations, and literature studies and were analyzed qualitatively. The findings indicate that business actors generally fulfill basic obligations in online transactions, such as providing product information, prices, and guarantees, as well as compensation when losses occur. However, legal protection for child consumers remains insufficient due to the absence of age verification mechanisms and the lack of specific policies designed to protect child consumers. Therefore, stronger responsibility from business actors and supportive policies from relevant stakeholders are needed to ensure more effective protection for child consumers in online transactions.

title: Normative environment, cultural tightness and market share: a longitudinal perspective on MNEs performance
abstract: Purpose When multinational enterprises (MNEs) enter foreign markets, they face institutional differences: (i) regulatory, (ii) cultural-cognitive and (iii) normative. While regulatory and cultural-cognitive dimensions have received considerable attention, the role of the normative component in firm performance remains underexplored. The authors focus on normative pressures. The purpose of this study is to explore the market share performance of MNEs when the strength of social norms varies (looser or stronger) across host and home markets. Therefore, this study investigates the impact of the cultural tightness-looseness (cultural tightness) difference on MNE market share gains over-time. Design/methodology/approach This study investigates the relationship between cultural tightness difference and market share gain performance of MNEs in foreign markets, adopting quantitative methodology and using multiple linear regression analyses. Using data from Euromonitor Passport, the authors also examine how does market share gain vary in time (tenure) in the market. Findings The authors argue that the tightness difference across host and home countries positively affects market share gains. Furthermore, the authors investigate how factors such as tighter host market and tenure in the market influence firm performance. Findings contribute to theory by suggesting the positive effect of no…

title: Equality of Customary and Granted Rights of Occupancy in Tanzania: Legal Recognition and Practical Realities in the Land Market
abstract: Tanzania’s land tenure framework recognises both customary rights of occupancy and granted rights of occupancy, and expressly provides that a Customary Right of Occupancy is in every respect of equal status and effect to a Granted Right of Occupancy. This article examines whether that statutory equality is reflected in the practical operation of the land market. It draws on a qualitative socio-legal study combining doctrinal analysis of legislation, policy and judicial decisions with empirical interviews conducted in Mwanza Region. The empirical study involved 40 purposively selected respondents, including land administration officials, judicial and tribunal officers, customary landholders and village representatives, advocates, and citizens with experience of land tenure issues. The article reveals that the central difficulty is not the absence of formal legal recognition, but the gap between equal legal status and the administrative and economic conditions through which land rights are documented, verified, transferred, used as security and protected. The Constitution, the Land Act and the Village Land Act, read with authoritative decisions, provide substantial protection for customary interests. Nevertheless, differences in documentation, registration, boundary identification, institutional coordination, awareness and recognition of multiple interests can make customary righ…

title: Forecast Parameters of the Russian Labor Market in the Medium Term
abstract: The article describes the current situation in the Russian labor market, shaped by macroeconomic trends, de-mographic processes, the digital transformation of the economy, and the widespread adoption of self-employment. The study uses general scientific methods, such as analysis and synthesis, comparison, and generalization, as well as specialized methods, including demographic and socio-economic analysis. It identi-fies constituent entities of the Russian Federation at risk of worsening labor-market conditions. Drawing on the official demographic forecast and expert assessments, the article outlines the forecast medium-term trajectory of the Russian labor market. It presents evidence that domestic labor-supply reserved have been exhausted and that foreign workers cannot make up for staffing shortages. The paper also discusses expert views on the impact of artificial intelligence on the labor market and describes young people’s labor-market behavior. Based on the demographic forecast of ROSSTAT, it identifies a “window of opportunity” for technological moderniza-tion of production, which could boost labor productivity and replace human labor. The novelty of the study find-ings lies in determining the timeframe for modernizing production and distinguish a group of regions at in-creased risk of worsening labor-market conditions.

title: The system value of flexible electricity demand in a 100% renewable European energy system
abstract: Flexible and energy-intensive technologies such as power-to-X, smart electric vehicle charging, and energy storage, including thermal storage, are expected to play a critical role in providing system flexibility in renewable energy systems. However, the role and potential of flexible demands in households and industries remain less certain and have not yet been thoroughly investigated. Based on holistic energy system modelling in EnergyPLAN, this study explores the potential of households, industry and electric vehicles to contribute flexibility and the benefits observed at the system level. It is found that there are tangible benefits observed in terms of improved system efficiency, peak power plant operation, and cost savings. Total primary energy savings up to 4.4% (theoretical upper bound, 100% flexible demand on a 4-week basis). Within a plausible range, savings of 2.0-2.9% are identified in a renewable energy system, compared with only 0.5-0.7% in a baseline system.

title: Civil Law Consequences of Non-Performance of the Obligation to Maintain Readiness of Generating Equipment in the Wholesale Capacity Market
abstract: The article examines the relationship between financial settlement and protective consequences of breaching the obligation to maintain the generating equipment in readiness to produce electricity in the wholesale capaci-ty market. Drawing on the Civil Code of the Russian Federation, the Federal Law “On the Electric Power Indus-try”, the Wholesale Market Rules, Russian-language studies of 2018–2024, court decisions of 2024–2026, and System Operator data of United Energy System, four financial consequences of non-performance are distin-guished: determination of the paid volume of capacity, contractual penalty, compensation of damages, and payment for withdrawal from future supply. It is revealed that a reduction in a generator revenue is often treated as a single liability measure, although its components differ in legal nature. Four criteria of distinction are pro-posed: payment basis, calculation base, recipient and the period of protected performance. The need for sepa-rate reflection of settlement adjustment and penalties in the settlement documents and the materials of the independent proof of causation when recovering generator losses from a contractor in the capacity market is noted. The special procedure of applying a zero coefficient to unavailability indicators of damaged equipment introduced into the Wholesale Market Rules in 2026 is taken into account. It is concluded…

title: Does the market reward mandatory sustainability disclosure? Information asymmetry and firm value in Indonesian energy firms
abstract: Indonesian listed companies must publish sustainability reports, yet it is unclear whether investors price this mandatory disclosure and whether lower information asymmetry is the channel. This study examines how environmental and governance disclosure relates to information asymmetry and firm value among energy companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021–2025, and whether information asymmetry mediates this relationship. A 44-item disclosure index based on the Global Reporting Initiative was coded for 51 firms (255 firm-years). Information asymmetry is measured by the quoted bid–ask spread and firm value by the logarithm of Tobin's Q, using panel models with firm-clustered and wild-bootstrap inference. Wider spreads are associated with lower firm value, although only moderately robustly, whereas the annual high–low price range behaves like a volatility measure and shows the opposite sign. Aggregate disclosure is not significantly related to the spread or to firm value, and no mediation is found. Within-firm increases in environmental, but not governance, disclosure are associated with higher value, but not when lagged. Evidence that the market rewards mandatory disclosure is weak, whereas liquidity-related information costs are priced more consistently. Regulators and investors should weigh disclosure quality and assurance, not only the volume of reported item…

title: Mechanical response of stopes and mining-induced surface deformation in cut-and-fill gold mining
abstract: To support the safe and green mining of structurally complex gold deposits, the three-dimensional numerical models at both the panel stope scale and the mine-wide full life-cycle scale were established using FLAC3D, taking the Xiaoshuijing gold mine in Chuxiong County, Yunnan Province as the engineering background, to investigate the stope structural stability and the risk of mining-induced surface deformation under layered cut-and-fill mining conditions. The gravitational stress field initialization method was applied to simulate stress redistribution and displacement responses throughout the cyclic layered excavation-backfilling process. The evolution of plastic zones in pillars, roofs, surrounding rock, drifts, and backfill bodies was also evaluated. The temporal-spatial evolution of surface subsidence at different stoping stages have been predicted. The results demonstrate that, as layered mining and backfilling progressed continuously. The overburden load and mining-induced disturbances were gradually transferred to the pillars and backfill bodies. The maximum pillar shear strain increment was approximately 6.805 × 10 −3 . The development of a through-going plastic failure zone was not observed. After mining, the maximum displacement of the stope roof was 1.67 cm. The overall displacements of the pillars, backfill bodies, and drifts remained relatively small. The ground su…

title: Soil test crop response–based integrated nutrient management for cabbage in alluvial Inceptisols
Early rituximab exposure and interim treatment response in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: a machine learning-assisted predictive study
abstract: Introduction To develop a machine learning (ML) model for predicting rituximab (RTX) concentrations in patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, evaluate the exposure-response relationship between predicted first-cycle trough concentrations (C min, Cycle1 ) and interim efficacy, and develop a graphical user interface (GUI) for personalized dose adjustment. Methods A retrospective study using nested cross-validation to build RTX prediction models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis enhanced interpretability. Predicted C min, Cycle1 was assessed for independent prediction of interim complete remission (CR) via univariate logistic regression. ROC analysis determined the effective threshold for clinical benefit. The final model was packaged into a GUI for concentration prediction and first-dose recommendation. Results 143 plasma concentration data points from 57 patients were included (115 from 45 training, 28 from 12 external validation). The final model used a double-layer ensemble: arithmetic mean of Stack (LightGBM+XGBoost) and independent CatBoost, achieving good performance in both sets. SHAP identified TimeSinceLastDose and Dose_Per_Weight as key predictors. Based on interim efficacy assessment, 19 patients were classified into the CR group and 26 into the non-CR group. Median predicted C min, Cycle1 was significantly higher in the CR group. Higher C min, Cycle…

title: Nutrigenomic variation in response to soy isoflavones on mammographic density in Asian women
abstract: Introduction Observational studies suggested soy isoflavones (ISF) may reduce breast cancer risk, potentially through ERβ-mediated anti-estrogenic effects. However, intervention trials using mammographic density (MD) as biomarker, including the Malaysian Soy and Mammographic Density (MiSo) study, reported inconsistent results, suggesting that conventional MD measures may not fully capture ISF-related biological effects or that genetic variability may influence individual response. Methods Pre- and post-intervention mammograms from 90 participants of MiSo study ( ClinicalTrial.gov : NCT03686098) were analyzed using two AI-based imaging approaches. Primary analyses compared the changes in AI-based risk scores across the study arms (ISF supplement/diet vs. control) and against conventional MD measures from the original study. Exploratory analyses further stratified the study arms by 136 common genetic polymorphisms associated with soy metabolism. Results Similar to conventional MD measures, AI-based risk scores showed no significant changes across study arms, although modest reductions were observed following soy intervention. Exploratory genotype-stratified analyses identified four variants that may influence the response to soy intervention: Genotypes associated with higher ABCG2 (rs4312723) and lower SLCO2B1 (rs2712818) expressions were associated with significant reductions in…

Can Laughter Change Your Response to Stress?
abstract: Did you know that laughing can help keep you healthy? In fact, scientists are now discovering that laughing is not only important for connecting with others, but it may improve overall health by changing your response to stress. When people experience long-lasting stress, their bodies release too much of a hormone called cortisol. Excessive and prolonged cortisol exposure can impact many systems, including the immune system, increasing vulnerability to sickness and disease. But some new and exciting studies suggest that laughing— via activities like laughter yoga—can help “reset” this system. In this article, we will explore the mechanisms underlying how laughter may help keep people healthy.

title: Exploring enhanced self-esteem reactivity in response to social prediction errors in adolescence
abstract: Abstract Self-esteem is a cornerstone of mental health across the lifespan. Throughout life, but particularly during adolescence, self-esteem is shaped by social appraisals. Previous work in adults has shown that momentary fluctuations in self-esteem are explained not only by whether we are liked by others but also by whether we are liked more or less than expected (social prediction errors). Here, we examine age-related differences in how social experiences shape self-esteem in 141 participants aged 10-40 years using an experimental social evaluation task and ecological momentary assessment. In the experiment, self-esteem reactivity to unexpected social feedback follows a non-linear age-related pattern, peaking in late adolescence. In daily life, self-esteem reactivity to perceived pleasantness of social interaction and naturalistic social prediction errors is stronger in younger participants. Individual differences in experimental and daily-life self-esteem reactivity are associated, highlighting heightened self-esteem malleability during adolescence.

title: Tubeimoside II attenuated inflammatory response in model of pediatric pneumonia by inactivating nuclear factor (NF)-κB signaling
abstract: Background Pneumonia is characterized by pulmonary edema and severe hypoxemia, which is a prevalent respiratory disease with high morbidity and mortality. Tubeimoside II has been suggested to possess anti-inflammatory and anticancer properties. This study aims to investigate the protective effect of Tubeimoside II on inflammation in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced pediatric pneumonia. Methods One week old mice were treated with 2 mg/kg of LPS to establish animal model for pediatric pneumonia. The respiratory activity was measured by pulmonary function testing. The histological injury of lungs was evaluated by hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining. The inflammatory cells, total protein, and inflammatory cytokines in BALF were also measured with different methods. At last, the protein level was determined by Western blotting. Results Tubeimoside II ameliorated respiratory dysfunction of pneumonia mice. Besides, LPS-induced pulmonary edema and lung injury were also improved by Tubeimoside II treatment. Additionally, the increased inflammatory cell infiltration and cytokines in BALF of pneumonia mice were reduced by Tubeimoside II treatment. Mechanistically, Tubeimoside II effectively inhibited the activation of AKT/NF- κ B signaling by downregulating phosphorylated AKT and NF- κ B proteins, as well as attenuating I κ B α degradation and nuclear translocation of NF- κ B p65. title: Consumer response to a multi-channel promotional campaign for local olive oil in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq: a mixed-methods evaluation
abstract: Introduction This study looked at how a multi-channel promotional campaign, affected what people know, how they feel, and whether they actually bought local olive oil in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Methods A single cohort of 400 consumers was surveyed before the campaign (September–October 2025) and re-contacted after campaign implementation (July–August 2026). After matching respondents, we were able to compare 165 individuals with confidence. Our questionnaire covered knowledge, attitudes, buying habits, campaign exposure and recognition (distinguishing visibility, engagement, and message recall), message quality, barriers to purchase, and willingness to pay. We used a mix of statistical tools, from simple comparisons to more advanced techniques like regression analysis and clustering. Results Knowledge increased significantly from pre-campaign (2.621 ± 0.904) to post-campaign (2.903 ± 0.992; Δ = +0.282, p = 0.003, Cohen’s dz. = 0.236). No statistically significant overall changes were detected in attitudes (Δ = +0.074, p = 0.328) or purchasing behavior (Δ = −0.012, p = 0.872). Overall campaign exposure was moderate (2.653/5), with social media exposure higher than traditional media. Barriers to purchasing included insufficient label information (3.313), difficulty finding the product (3.275), and weak packaging/branding (3.258). PCA identified eight underlying dimensions e…

title: Early-life exposure to low doses of a glyphosate-based herbicide is associated with post-implantation losses and altered uterine inflammatory response in rats
abstract: Introduction Multiple studies have documented widespread human exposure to glyphosate‐based herbicides (GBHs), reflecting their extensive use and environmental occurrence. This study investigated whether neonatal exposure to a GBH, in doses comparable to and below the chronic reference dose (cRfD: 1 mg/kg/day), affects pregnancy outcomes and inflammatory signaling at the maternal–fetal interface in Wistar rats. Methods Saline solution (control) or a GBH (0.2 or 2 mg/kg/day) was administered by sc. injection to female pups on postnatal day (PND) 1, 3, 5 and 7. On PND90, female rats were mated and pregnant ones were assigned to evaluate (a) fertility outcomes and developmental (feto‐placental) parameters, and (b) mechanistic pathways involved in the regulation of inflammatory state on gestational day (GD) 15 and GD19. Results On GD15, while no changes were detected in fertility parameters, fetal length was decreased in the lower GBH dose group in comparison with control group. By late gestation (GD19), both GBH doses increased post-implantation losses, whereas no differences were detected in feto‐placental parameters. At the molecular level, GBH exposure induced an imbalance in decidual inflammatory pathways, evidenced by increased NF‐κB protein expression, upregulation of NF‐κBrelated genes (Traf2 and Ikbkb), and a gestational stage–dependent shift toward a pro‐inflammatory prof…

title: Long-term care for older adults with disability in China, 2020–2050: projected demand structure and capacity constraints in the care system
abstract: Introduction Rapid population aging is reshaping the structure of older adults with disability in China and shifting long-term care pressure from families to society. We examine how this structural change affects care demand and assess the potential role of early interventions and the system’s capacity to absorb long-term care needs. Methods Using China’s Seventh National Population Census, World Population Prospects 2024 parameters, and the 2005–2018 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey, we applied the cohort-component method and disability state transition model to project China’s population of older adults with disability, care costs, and workforce demand during 2020–2050. System capacity was assessed from service-resource and affordability perspectives by estimating bed and workforce supply–demand gaps, using ROC analysis to examine household income in relation to formal care utilization, and measuring urban–rural differences in per capita care burden. We also conducted an early-intervention scenario analysis for mild disability. Results Under the disability definition adopted in this study, the number of older adults with disability is projected to reach 77.32 million by 2050 (71.3–83.8 million), with concentration at advanced ages, a higher female share, urban–rural differentiation, and a rising proportion of severe disability. title: A CatBoost-based model for predicting early response to radioiodine therapy in intermediate- to high-risk differentiated thyroid cancer: a multicenter retrospective study
abstract: Background Differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) is typically managed with surgery followed by selective I-131 adjuvant therapy (RAT). In intermediate- to high-risk patients, identifying patients who are likely to achieve an excellent response early after RAT could help shape follow-up plans and risk discussions. Current stratification tools rely on clinicopathological categories and may miss much of the individual variation in early treatment response. Methods This retrospective multicenter study enrolled 598 intermediate- to high-risk DTC patients across three hospitals. The development cohort (The First Affiliated Hospital of Guilin Medical University) contributed 410 patients; after preprocessing and building the full four-variable model matrix, 286 were used for training and 124 for internal validation. A separate external validation cohort comprised 188 patients from two other hospitals. We reviewed candidate predictors with careful attention to timing, settling on four variables that are available before response assessment: stimulated thyroglobulin (Tg) level, American Thyroid Association (ATA) risk stratification, thyroglobulin antibody (TgAb) level, and cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM). Nine machine learning algorithms were compared, and CatBoost was chosen for final evaluation. Results In internal validation, CatBoost returned an area under the receiver operating …

title: Seismic response of a thermoelastic gas-bearing seabed sediment layer induced by obliquely incident P waves
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the seismic response of a thermoelastic gas-bearing seabed sediment layer subjected to obliquely incident P waves, focusing on thermo-mechanical coupling and sediment properties. Design/methodology/approach A seawater–gas-bearing sediment–bedrock model is established using the wave theories of ideal fluids, unsaturated porous thermoelastic media and single-phase thermoelastic media. Wave fields are formulated using potential functions and analytical solutions are obtained by imposing interface continuity conditions. Parametric analyses examine the effects of incident angle, temperature, saturation, frequency, sediment thickness, porosity and thermal properties. Findings Thermo-mechanical coupling substantially modifies the wave propagation behavior and dynamic amplification mechanisms of gas-bearing seabed sediments. The horizontal displacement initially increases and subsequently decreases with increasing incident angle, whereas the vertical displacement generally decreases. As saturation increases, the overall displacement response at the seabed surface decreases; meanwhile, the horizontal amplification is enhanced, whereas the vertical amplification is weakened. title: Evaluating bus stop service accessibility equity for older adults in a megacity: a GIS-based analysis of spatial supply–demand mismatch in Shanghai
abstract: Against the backdrop of population aging, the spatial allocation and equity of bus service resources have become important issues in age-friendly urban transportation planning. Taking Pudong New Area, Shanghai, as the study area, this study integrates 100 m × 100 m older-adult population grids, General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) data, and related spatial datasets. The two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) method is employed to measure older adults’ potential accessibility to scheduled bus services at stops. Travel-time threshold sensitivity analysis, Lorenz curves, the Gini coefficient, and GIS-based spatial overlay analysis are further applied to examine spatial disparities, distributional inequality, and supply–demand matching patterns in bus stop service accessibility. The results indicate that: (1) bus stop service accessibility generally exhibits a center–periphery gradient, with higher accessibility in central urban areas and lower accessibility in peripheral areas, while high-accessibility areas account for 10.6% of the study area; (2) under the 30-min baseline scenario, the population-weighted Gini coefficient is 0.42, decreasing from 0.52 to 0.33 as the travel-time threshold increases from 10 to 50 min, indicating that the distribution of accessibility is sensitive to the model’s time threshold; and (3) under the adopted data and classification settings, high…

title: Analysis of clinical characteristics and treatment response to bronchoscopic instillation of amphotericin B in patients with pulmonary aspergillosis
abstract: Background To investigate the feasibility of bronchoscopic local instillation of amphotericin B combined with oral voriconazole, and to describe the observed clinical and radiological outcomes in a small case series of patients with pulmonary aspergillosis. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of 11 patients diagnosed with pulmonary aspergillosis. Demographic characteristics, medical history, clinical symptoms, and laboratory and imaging findings were collected. All patients received oral voriconazole combined with bronchoscopic local instillation of amphotericin B. In selected cases, bronchoscopic removal of fungal masses was performed concurrently. Clinical outcomes were evaluated based on symptom change, follow-up imaging results, and clinical follow-up records. Results Among the 11 patients, 9 were male and 2 were female, with a mean age of 51.18 ± 9.10 years. Most patients had a history of pulmonary tuberculosis and structural lung destruction and cavitary lesions. Following treatment, the majority of patients showed clinical improvement, including alleviation or resolution of cough. Follow-up imaging demonstrated reduction, absorption, or complete disappearance of aspergillomas within pulmonary cavities. One patient discontinued antifungal therapy after combined bronchoscopic forceps removal without recurrence during follow-up. Clinical outc…

Subtherapeutic quetiapine concentrations and behavioral response in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Background Managing behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia in older adults with Alzheimer’s disease remains clinically challenging, particularly given the safety warnings associated with second-generation antipsychotics. Conventional therapeutic drug concentrations for quetiapine, derived largely from schizophrenia populations, may not apply to frail older patients, creating uncertainty regarding optimal dosing. Methods This prospective, single-center observational cohort study evaluated the effectiveness and tolerability of individualized low-dose quetiapine in older adults with Alzheimer’s disease and refractory behavioral symptoms. The full analysis set included 40 patients assessed using the Neuropsychiatric Inventory Questionnaire (NPI-Q), with an embedded pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) sub-study measuring steady-state trough plasma concentrations in 22 patients via therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) to explore the exposure-response relationship. The full analysis set (FAS) included 40 patients. Results Using a lenient but clinically relevant threshold, the overall responder rate (≥20% reduction in neuropsychiatric burden) was 97.5%, though no patient achieved complete clinical control. title: Energy-efficient power allocation in OFDM-based 5G wireless systems for sustainable smart grid applications
abstract: Purpose This study aims to evaluate how simple, channel-aware sub-carrier power allocation in an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) downlink can reduce the transmit energy that a base station needs to serve smart grid Internet of Things devices. It contributes, at the physical layer, towards mitigating the “5G energy paradox” and supports Sustainable Development Goal 7 (affordable and clean energy). Design/methodology/approach A link-level cyclic-prefix OFDM downlink with quadrature phase-shift keying is simulated in MATLAB over a frequency-selective multi-path Rayleigh fading channel. Equal power allocation is compared with threshold-based on/off sub-carrier allocation and exact water-filling under the same total transmit power. The bit error rate (BER), the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) required for a target BER of 10 −3, capacity-based energy efficiency and sub-carrier utilisation are evaluated over an SNR range of 0–40 dB. The on/off threshold is selected analytically and verified by simulation. Findings On/off allocation with threshold θ = 0.5 keeps 60.6% of the sub-carriers active and reaches BER = 10−3 at 8.9 dB, compared with 27.1 dB for equal power allocation, that is, an 18.2 dB reduction in the required transmit power (about 16 dB less energy per delivered bit). Water-filling gives almost no BER gain (0.1 dB) but improves capacity-based energy efficiency…

title: Watching from the sidelines: supporter salience and football governance in England
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to ask if English football supporters are of low stakeholder salience in the governance ecosystem of their clubs. In many contexts, football supporters are widely characterised as highly salient, often definitive, stakeholders. However, the particular characteristics of the UK football industry bring this assumption into question. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper utilises the stakeholder salience model of Mitchell et al. (1997) to assess the position of fans in the governance systems of English football clubs. Findings English football supporters have low salience within club governance eco-systems due to their loyalty which effectively renders clubs as local monopolies, a prevailing socio-political institutional environment that perpetuates owner power, and comparatively low levels of organised supporter movements. Supporter salience is argued to be dependent on socio-political factors as well as managerial prioritisation. Supporters require mechanisms to increase the effect of their voice in club governance. Research limitations/implications The low salience of fans identified in this paper is in contrast to that identified in other contexts and therefore highlights institutional and environmental factors in supporter salience. Practical implications This paper can advance the practice of English football governance by sti…

title: Prioritizing emotional intelligence to mitigate burnout: a study on legal professionals
abstract: Purpose This study aims to offer a model to manage work-related burnout among legal practitioners and to preserve sustainable career growth and well-being in high-pressure work environments. It categorizes the critical elements of emotional intelligence (EI) using a mixed-method approach. Design/methodology/approach It integrates a comprehensive literature review with expert interviews to identify the pertinent EI components. The identified elements were evaluated using the analytical hierarchy process (AHP), involving pairwise comparisons conducted by legal and academic professionals to determine the relative importance of each EI factor in mitigating burnout. Findings The results of this study revealed that self-management and relationship management are the most influential EI components in reducing burnout among legal professionals, followed by emotional well-being, effective communication and work–life balance. Research limitations/implications The findings demonstrate that individuals with higher EI have the capability to manage stress, maintain healthy professional relationships and accomplish long-term career stability. This research fills the gap between EI and professional burnout in the legal sector. Originality/value In addition, this study introduces a novel application of the AHP multi-criteria decision-making method to human resource management. The insights from…

title: Optimized Data Compression and Bandwidth Management in MANETs Using Hybrid Self-Adaptive Neural-Trajectory Genetic Swarm Optimizer (HSANT-GO) and Optimal Velocity Control
abstract: A Hybrid Self-Adaptive Neural-Trajectory and Genetic Swarm Optimizer (HSANT-GO) with an Optimal Velocity Control Algorithm (OVC) is proposed to address the challenges of efficient load balancing and bandwidth control in Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs), particularly in data compression. This algorithm dynamically adjusts network node trajectories and velocities based on real-time conditions by improving load distribution, optimizing bandwidth usage, and enhancing data compression efficiency. The HSANT-GO uses swarm intelligence and self-adaptive mechanisms to ensure equitable resource distribution and robust network functioning, even in dense and congested multi-hop environments. The proposed method significantly increases network throughput and aids real-time applications with strict time limits.

title: Exploring the challenges facing landscape management in smart city studies with the approach of artificial intelligence
abstract: This applied study analyzes the components and development challenges of smart cities in Sanandaj using a descriptive-analytical approach. The main objective of the research is to identify the challenges and key components of the smart city development process, and to assess the performance of these components to pinpoint areas for improvement. Data were collected through documentary sources, organizational records, and a researcher-designed questionnaire distributed to 60 experts and officials across different districts of the city. The study employed several analytical methods, including Fuzzy TOPSIS, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) neural network to rank, assess, and predict the performance of the components. The results showed that the Smart Economy (0.872) and Smart People (0.843) were the most influential components, while Smart Services (0.643) and Smart Transportation ranked lowest, reflecting infrastructural weaknesses in these areas. Correlation analysis revealed a weak link between Smart People and overall smart city realization, highlighting a gap between digital readiness and technological needs. The Smart Environment performed relatively well but had low predictive potential (0.392) in the MLP model. The findings stress the need for stronger digital infrastructure, enhanced digital literacy among citizens, integrated tra…

title: Цифровые валюты центральных банков в мировой финансовой системе: перспективы цифрового рубля
abstract: -Введение. С 2017 по 2024 год число центральных банков, разрабатывающих цифровые валюты (ЦВЦБ), возросло с 35 до 134, охватив 98% мирового ВВП. Цель исследования – оценить место России в глобальной ЦВЦБ-архитектуре и разработать рекомендации по развитию цифрового рубля. Материалы и методы. Методология включает сравнительный институциональный анализ 134 юрисдикций, кейс-стади пяти проектов (e-CNY, цифровой евро, цифровой рубль, mBridge, Project Dunbar) и авторский фреймворк «суверенного платѐжного стека» (SPS). Результаты исследования. Выявлено, что 73% ЦВЦБ-проектов реализуют двухуровневую архитектуру; лидирующую позицию занимает Китай (e-CNY: 22,6 млрд CNY-транзакций в 2024 году). Россия (SPS=7,6/10) сохраняет высокий потенциал, однако отстаѐт от Китая по технологическому суверенитету. Установлено, что цифровой рубль способен стать инструментом «мягкой» дедолларизации и укрепления финансового суверенитета в условиях санкций. Обсуждение и заключения. Предложены пять стратегических рекомендаций: ускоренное масштабирование пилота, интеграция в mBridge, внедрение офлайнрежима, развитие открытого API и формирование БРИКС-альянса цифровых валют. title: Transition to Holacracy and Digital Supply Chain Management
abstract: Digitalization offers great opportunities for improving supply chain management. However, its full potential is limited by the tendency of managers in these chains to rely on hierarchical organizational structures, which prevent the full utilization of employees’ competencies. These competencies are necessary for the creation and use of artificial intelligence that operates on both physical and non-physical management objects. The solution to this problem can be achieved through holacracy, which creates conditions for employees in supply chain links to act as “sensors” and “actuators”. These roles are essential for the development and implementation of a digital twin that can help manage these chains. The purpose of this article is to create theoretical and methodological prerequisites for the use of holacracy in digital supply chain management.To achieve the purpose of this article, we used terminological analysis, descriptive and faceted methods, or a TDF methodology. The article explains the essence of holacracy and the digitalization of supply chain management. It discusses digitized options for supply chains, as well as developed technologies for the interaction of persons involved in digital supply chain management in a holacratic environment. The article also justifies the approach to developing digital management solutions for supply chains based on holacracy.

title: Ecofeminism and foster care: reimagining home, care and power in child welfare
abstract: Out-of-home care (OOHC), particularly the foster care of children removed from their birth families, can be reimagined through an ecofeminist lens. This perspective article applies ecofeminist theory, including its critique of hierarchical power and its ethic of care, to fostering within the Australian OOHC system. This perspective article adopts an autoethnographically informed approach, bringing together contemporary OOHC and ecofeminist scholarship; the author’s published Australian OOHC research from 2012 to 2026, including research concerning foster carers, caregiving and children’s experiences of care and belonging; and critical reflexive analysis grounded in more than two decades of lived experience as a foster carer. These are used as distinct but complementary sources of knowledge; the article does not report a new empirical dataset. The analysis is organized around three interrelated themes: home and belonging as an ecosystem of care; gendered, maternal and embodied care labour; and systemic power, resistance and future directions. It argues that foster homes can operate as relational ecosystems in which love, stability, and belonging support children’s healing, while bureaucratic systems undervalue the caregiving knowledge on which they depend. The article further contends that foster care labour, predominantly performed by women, is culturally and institutionally un…

title: Exercise management for sarcopenia among older patients with mental disorders in China: a best practice implementation project
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction: The prevalence of sarcopenia is relatively high among hospitalized elderly patients with mental disorders. Without timely assessment and intervention, their condition may progress rapidly, elevating the risk of falls. Aim: This project intended to translate evidence into practice by implementing standardized exercise management for sarcopenia in psychiatric wards, with the goals of mitigating patients’ risk of falls and optimizing their quality of life. Methods: This project utilized the JBI Evidence Implementation Framework. A baseline audit was undertaken to assess current practices related to exercise management for sarcopenia in elderly patients with mental disorders, followed by analysis of the audit results. JBI's Getting Research into Practice (GRiP) tool was used to identify barriers and facilitators influencing compliance with best practices. Based on these findings, a targeted exercise management plan was implemented, and a follow-up audit was subsequently performed. Results: The baseline audit revealed generally low compliance, with rates for all seven audit criteria falling below 20%. Through strategies such as interdisciplinary collaboration, standardized protocols, professional training, and patient education, the follow-up audit demonstrated that compliance rates for all criteria improved to more than 85%. Conclusions: Evidence-based, audit…
