Management and treatment of autism spectrum disorder in Saudi Arabian children and adolescents: a systematic literature review
abstract: Introduction Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) requires coordinated, culturally responsive intervention and service-delivery systems that address child outcomes as well as the needs of families, educators, and healthcare professionals. This systematic literature review synthesized recent empirical evidence on ASD management, treatment, intervention, service delivery, and implementation for children and adolescents in Saudi Arabia. Methods In accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched, supplemented by citation chasing, for peer-reviewed studies published from 2020 to 19 April 2026. Results A total of 38 studies met the eligibility criteria, were appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, and were synthesized thematically. Four themes addressed the review questions. First, targeted interventions including culturally adapted visual supports, behavioral, social, sensory, safety, dental, and technology-assisted approaches produced promising but predominantly outcome-specific gains; the clearest controlled evidence concerned culturally adapted Arabic visual preparation for dental care, while evidence for broader and durable developmental change remained limited. Second, knowledge and endorsement of behavioral and evidence-based approaches were stronge…

title: Diagnostic performance and clinical utility of pathogen-targeted next-generation sequencing in suspected central nervous system infections
abstract: Background Evidence on the diagnostic performance and clinical utility of pathogen-targeted next-generation sequencing (t-NGS) in central nervous system infections (CNSIs) remains limited. We evaluated its diagnostic performance relative to culture and the clinical associations of combined testing. Methods This prospective, single-centre observational study enrolled adults with suspected CNSI into contemporaneous, non-randomised t-NGS + culture and culture-only cohorts. Paired diagnostic performance was assessed against a composite clinical reference standard in participants undergoing both tests. Antimicrobial-management patterns within 48 h of report availability and 30-day clinical outcomes were compared between cohorts. Results The analysis included 253 participants: 162 in the t-NGS + culture cohort and 91 in the culture-only cohort. Among the 162 participants with paired testing, 97 were adjudicated as having CNSI. Compared with culture, t-NGS had higher sensitivity (80.4% vs. 25.8%, p < 0.001), negative predictive value (71.6% vs. 46.3%, p < 0.001), and accuracy (77.8% vs. 53.7%, p < 0.001), but lower specificity (73.8% vs. 95.4%, p < 0.001). The area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve was 0.77 vs. 0.61 ( p < 0.01). Among confirmed infections, complete or partial pathogen-level concordance with the reference standard was more frequent with t…

title: Spectral power-laws emerge naturally from realistic tuning curve heterogeneity
abstract: How the brain represents the outside world with precision and allows for generalization is a fundamental question in neuroscience. One way of interpreting activity in neural systems is by contrasting two opposing coding principles: efficient coding, which produces high-dimensional, uncorrelated representations that maximally differentiate stimuli, and robust coding, which produces low-dimensional, smooth representations that generalize across stimuli. The decay of the eigenspectrum of the covariance matrix provides an intuitive perspective on this trade-off and has previously been observed to follow a critical power-law in the brain. While tuning curve heterogeneity has been proposed as a potential mechanism from which these power-laws could emerge, it remains unclear how specific biological properties of tuning curve heterogeneity give rise to them and how the organization of this heterogeneity maps onto the broader computational trade-offs between generalization, capacity, and noise robustness. In this work, we theoretically link tuning curve heterogeneity to spectral power-laws and use this biologically grounded model to investigate how different representations affect generalization, noise robustness, precision, and capacity in a linear decoder. We show mathematically that a population of Gaussian tuning curves with Gamma-distributed widths and a power-law relationship betw…

title: Integrated recombinase-aided amplification–invader system: a closed-tube visual platform for hepatitis B virus detection
abstract: Background Rapid and accurate hepatitis B virus (HBV) detection is essential for the early management of HBV infection. Quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) depends on sophisticated thermal cycling instruments, which greatly restricts its application in point-of-care testing (POCT). Methods Herein, this study developed an Integrated Recombinase-Aided Amplification–invader System (IRIS) for visual and sensitive HBV DNA detection. By adapting the integrated amplification-invader strategy to RAA and optimizing the FEN1 enzyme dosage, we achieved improved reaction compatibility while effectively reducing the overall time cost. Fluorescent signals excited at 490 nm are observable by naked eye and recordable via smartphone imaging with a 520 nm filter, removing reliance on customized detection devices. Results IRIS exhibited favorable specificity and a detection limit of 10 copies per reaction. Furthermore, testing of clinical HBV specimens revealed full diagnostic concordance with commercial qPCR assays. Conclusion This simplified, equipment-independent detection method provides a feasible POCT solution for on-site HBV detection in resource-limited settings.
venue: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

title: The Impact of the US Dollar Exchange Rate Increase on Imported Goods Prices and Consumer Purchasing Power
abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of the appreciation of the United States dollar against the Indonesian rupiah on imported goods prices and consumer purchasing power in Indonesia in 2026. The study employs a quantitative descriptive approach using secondary data from official sources, including Bank Indonesia, Statistics Indonesia (BPS), and relevant government institutions. The analysis focuses on movements in the rupiah–US dollar exchange rate, the import price index, consumer inflation, and their implications for household purchasing power. The descriptive findings indicate mounting external price pressures, as annual import price index inflation reached 25.45% in the second quarter of 2026, up from 9.97% in the first quarter. Meanwhile, year-on-year consumer inflation stood at 3.28% in September 2026. These developments suggest that higher import costs may affect the prices of imported consumer goods, raw materials, intermediate inputs, and capital goods, potentially weakening household purchasing power if nominal incomes do not increase correspondingly. However, exchange rate pass-through to domestic prices is neither immediate nor uniform, as it depends on international commodity prices, distribution costs, firms’ pricing strategies, market competition, and the availability of domestic substitutes. The study highlights the importance of exchange rate stability, stron…

title: Digital Transformation of Military Specialist Training Based on a System of Competency Based Tasks
abstract: The article examines the digital transformation of military specialist training through the introduction of compe-tency-based tasks that involve the use of information-handling techniques using cross-cutting digital technolo-gies. It describes the unifying factor underlying the set of competency-based tasks and provides examples for professional military subjects. The article proposes integrating cross-cutting digital technologies into the educa-tional process, where they serve both as a goal and as a means of learning. It also presents classification of information-handling techniques and examples of interdisciplinary competency-based tasks at the intersection of tactics, topography and the Internet of Things. The article argues that effective digital transformation is achieved by developing learning and cognitive competencies through interdisciplinary connections and digital tools.

title: Bridging Quality to Buying Action: The Mediating Mechanism of Price Perception in Consumer Footwear Purchases
abstract: This study aims to investigate the direct effects of product quality and price on purchase decisions among footwear consumers in Bandung, while examining the mediating role of price in bridging product quality to actual buying decisions. Employing a quantitative explanatory survey design, this research gathered empirical data from 100 consumers who purchased specific brand shoes in Bandung via purposive sampling. The data were evaluated using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), encompassing convergent and discriminant validity, reliability assessments, structural path bootstrapping, as well as predictive metrics including PLSpredict and CVPAT. The measurement model confirmed robust convergent validity, discriminant validity, and composite reliability without multicollinearity issues. The structural assessment revealed that product quality significantly drives price perception (beta = 0.851), while both product quality (beta = 0.487) and price (beta = 0.480) positively determine purchase decisions (R2 = 86.6%). Crucially, price acts as a significant complementary partial mediator (beta = 0.409, p < 0.001), with strong out-of-sample predictive capability confirmed by PLSpredict (Q2predict > 0.70) and negative CVPAT average loss differences. Theoretically, these results enrich consumer behavior literature by validating price as an active value-transmittin…

title: Forecasting non-performing loan ratios: an explainable machine learning approach using multi-country banking data
abstract: Introduction This study evaluates whether machine learning adds predictive value beyond persistence in one-quarter-ahead forecasts of aggregate banking-system non-performing loan (NPL) ratios. Methods The source panel contains 588 country-quarter records for 15 countries. Exact target construction yields 528 usable observations, and the common sample with observed current NPL contains 511 observations, including 407 training and 104 fixed-test cases. Ten model families are compared with and without current NPL against persistence, pooled AR(1), pooled multivariate linear regression, and four NPL-only tree models. Preprocessing and model selection use calendar-quarter validation, and all models are re-tuned and refitted at 20 expanding origins covering 2020Q3-2025Q2. Results In the fixed 2023Q3-2025Q2 test, ExtraTrees with current NPL and the broader predictors has RMSE 0.225, compared with 0.245 for AR(1), 0.262 for persistence, and 0.250 for NPL-only ExtraTrees. Across rolling origins, LASSO has lower pooled RMSE (0.690) than multivariate ExtraTrees (0.756), while AR(1) has lower MAE. Country holdouts weaken multivariate tree forecasts, and current NPL dominates out-of-sample grouped Shapley explanations. Discussion The persistence benchmarks, panel-aware temporal validation, and country-level results do not support a substantial and stable out-of-sample advantage of ensemble …

title: Benchmark-aware multi-horizon forecasting of carbon dioxide emissions in Ghana
abstract: Abstract Reliable national emissions forecasting requires evidence that model complexity improves prediction beyond transparent benchmarks. We analysed Ghana’s fossil carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions for 1970–2024 using EDGAR data. We compared retrospective expanding-origin evaluations at horizons of 1–10 years for persistence, drift, damped trend, ARIMA, elastic net, random forest, support vector regression, and a guarded ensemble. Preprocessing used past-only reconstruction of missing sector values, and inner validation respected horizon-specific target availability. Drift achieved the lowest RMSE among the primary specifications at 1, 3, 5, and 10 years, with gains of 2.4%, 7.0%, 13.7%, and 15.6% over persistence; none was significant after small-sample correction and Holm adjustment. Supervised models predicting emissions levels underperformed. However, diagnostic models predicting changes improved RMSE by 19.6% for elastic net at five years and 23.4% for support vector regression at ten years. These gains were not significant after adjustment across the diagnostic comparisons. The findings implicate target representation and extrapolation alongside sample and predictor limitations, rather than general algorithmic inferiority. An error-calibrated ensemble projects 0.748 t CO₂ per person in 2025 and 0.996 in 2034. Its empirical 2034 95% error band is 0.925–1.095, but sequentia…

title: Методологический подход к прогнозированию развития аграрных рынков в системе международных экономических связей
abstract: Введение. Переориентация торгово-экономических потоков, в том числе в агропромышленном комплексе (далее – АПК), в страны Юго-Восточной Азии в условиях геополитической напряженности и нестабильности мировой экономики актуализирует вопросы обоснования прогнозных сценариев развития аграрных рынков, которые, с одной стороны, являются инструментом корректировки целевых показателей системы документов стратегического планирования, а с другой – выступают стратегическим ориентиром для ключевых участников агропродовольственной сферы. Цель исследования – разработать методологический подход к прогнозированию перспективных направлений развития аграрных рынков в системе международных экономических связей, позволяющий сформировать гибкую экспортно ориентированную стратегию в АПК. Материалы и методы. В работе использовались абстрактно-логический метод, методы экономико-математического и имитационного моделирования, экспертных оценок, сравнительного анализа, монографический метод и другие. Результаты исследования. В работе представлен авторский методологический подход к прогнозированию развития аграрных рынков в системе международных экономических связей, включающий в себя ряд методических положений по стратегическому анализу мирового и отечественного агропродовольственного рынка, формированию информационной базы исследований, определению показателей прогноза и методику прогнозирования перспект…

title: Raw material cost control in a restaurant: A standard cost benchmark and price–quantity variance analysis of two menu items in Manado, Indonesia
abstract: Raw materials are one of the largest cost items in food service, yet small restaurants seldom examine budget deviations at menu level. This exploratory single-case study builds a raw material standard cost benchmark from recipe standards and compares it with actual cost for two regional-cuisine menu items, Ragey (pork skewers) and Ba' Isi Bulu (pork grilled in bamboo), at one branch of the Pelmas Tanta Olla restaurant in Manado, Indonesia. Observation and three semi-structured interviews were combined with a budget–actual comparison and a price–quantity decomposition of material variances based on May 2026 purchase receipts. A 30-day standard cost budget of IDR 247.63 million was compared with actual cost of IDR 262.70 million, an unfavourable variance of IDR 15.07 million (6.09%). About IDR 15.0 million arises from a pork quantity variance in Ragey, consistent with a yield of 18 instead of 20 skewers per kilogram, while the Ba' Isi Bulu variance stems mainly from a chili price variance of IDR 2.36 million. Because actual sales volumes were unavailable, the budget covers 30 of 31 days, and no portion audit was performed, the overrun is uncertain (about 2.7% to 6.1%) and the results are indicative only. Portion control and price monitoring appear to be the most practical points of intervention.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Prediction of 3D Printability of Microgel-Based Bioink
abstract: Abstract High-fidelity 3D bioprinting is essential for producing biomimetic tissue scaffolds for precision medicine. A core challenge arises from the strong nonlinear coupling between microgel viscoelasticity and printing parameters, which governs shape fidelity. Conventional trial-and-error optimization is low-efficiency and fails to quantify these complex relationships. Herein, we developed a data-driven framework for predicting microgel printability using a model microgel composed of gelatin methacrylate and a small-molecule crosslinker with tunable crosslinking densities, sizes, and rheological properties. A multidimensional evaluation system was established to annotate printing outcomes, generating a high-throughput dataset linking viscoelastic properties to process parameters. Of the seven machine learning models evaluated, the multilayer perceptron achieved the highest test accuracy of 79.18%. The optimized model enables accurate prediction across diverse material compositions, geometric patterns, and cell-laden bioinks. This work represents the first data-driven model for printability prediction of microgel-based bioinks, affording a theoretical basis for the reverse design of tailored microgel formulations and optimal process windows.

title: CHARACTER BEHAVIOR EVENT PREDICTION MODEL BASED ON FUSION OF TRAJECTORY AND ENVIRONMENTAL FEATURES
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of predicting human behavior events by integrating trajectory and environmental features. Existing methods often neglect structured associations between trajectories and scenes or decouple trajectory regression from intention classification. To overcome these limitations, we propose an end-to-end framework comprising dual-stream encoding, cross-modal fusion, and multimodal decoding. The dual-stream encoder separately models historical trajectories using a two-layer Transformer and scene environments via a static scene branch (ResNet-50 extracting 64 spatial tokens from semantic segmentation) and an interaction graph branch (two-layer GCN modeling up to 30 neighboring agents). Cross-modal fusion uses trajectory global features as Query and scene tokens/interaction nodes as Key/Value, enabling soft alignment of environmental elements through cross-attention, with residual connections and layer normalization. The multimodal decoder, based on a conditional variational autoencoder, simultaneously predicts future 12-step trajectories and six behavior classes (straight, turn left/right, stop, interact with person/vehicle), jointly optimized by weighted negative log-likelihood and cross-entropy loss. Experiments on ETH/UCY, SDD, and nuScenes demonstrate state-of-the-art performance: on ETH/UCY, ADE=0.61m, FDE=1.10m, behavior accuracy=89.7%; on nuScene…

Prediction of PD-L1 status and characterization of tumor subtype in NSCLC with static and abbreviated dynamic LAFOV [18F]FDG PET
abstract: Abstract Purpose This study aimed to assess the potential of abbreviated dynamic [ 18 F]FDG PET imaging using a long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) scanner for non-invasive characterization of tumor subtypes and prediction of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) status in treatment-naïve patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Methods 51 treatment-naïve patients with histologically confirmed NSCLC (34 adenocarcinomas [LUAD], 17 squamous cell carcinomas [LUSC]) underwent a 20-min dynamic [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT acquisition starting 45-min post-injection on an LAFOV system. Parametric images of net influx rate (Ki) and distribution volume (DV) were reconstructed using a direct Patlak approach with patient-specific scaled population-based input functions. PD-L1 tumor proportion score was determined from one histopathologically sampled lesion per patient. Results PD-L1 positive lesions demonstrated higher SUV max (16.9 ± 9.6 vs. 11.6 ± 5.7; p = 0.04), Ki max (0.077 ± 0.04 vs. 0.054 ± 0.02; p = 0.03), and DV max (428.7 ± 253.5 vs. 278.7 ± 145.2; p = 0.02) than PD-L1 negative lesions. LUSC lesions showed higher SUV max (18.7 ± 8.5 vs. 12.9 ± 8.2; p = 0.008) and Ki max (0.08 ± 0.02 vs. 0.06 ± 0.04; p = 0.02) than LUAD lesions, whereas DV max did not differ ( p = 0.69). title: An Integrated Explainable HR Analytics Framework for employee attrition prediction: combining theory-guided feature engineering, explainable AI, and evidence-based decision support
abstract: Introduction Employee attrition increases recruitment and training costs, disrupts organizational continuity, and affects workforce planning. This study proposes an Integrated Explainable HR Analytics Framework combining theory-guided feature engineering, machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and evidence-based decision support. Methods The framework was evaluated using a publicly available synthetic HR attrition dataset containing 10,000 employee records. Fixed stratified training, validation, and independent test partitions were established in an 80:10:10 ratio to prevent information leakage. The training partition supported statistical screening, feature engineering, and model fitting, while the validation partition supported feature selection, hyperparameter optimization, and model selection. Four algorithms were evaluated: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost. The independent test partition was reserved for final evaluation and post-selection explainability. Results CatBoost achieved a held-out test ROC-AUC of 0.8272 (95% CI: 0.7937–0.8622), PR-AUC of 0.7126 (95% CI: 0.6638–0.7620), F1-score of 0.5471 (95% CI: 0.5137–0.5828), balanced accuracy of 0.7366, and Brier score of 0.1553 at a validation-derived threshold of 0.4609. title: Risk prediction model for refeeding syndrome in Chinese adult ICU patients: a scoping review
abstract: Objective This scoping review aims to systematically summarize risk prediction models for refeeding syndrome (RFS) in Chinese adult intensive care unit patients. We focus on model development approaches, outcome definition criteria, predictive variables, validation methods, predictive performance and bias characteristics, to provide evidence for clinical risk assessment, stratified interventions and future model optimization. Methods Relevant literature was retrieved from Chinese and English databases. Data including study type, RFS incidence, modeling approaches, predictive factors, validation strategies, model performance and risk of bias were extracted. Results A total of 15 studies were included. Substantial discrepancies existed across studies in RFS diagnostic criteria and observation periods. The reported incidence rates ranged from 27.94% to 65.15%. Most studies developed predictive models using logistic regression; predictive factors mainly encompassed patient demographics, laboratory test results, critical illness-related scores, nutrition- and feeding-related factors, and treatment modalities. Most available models only underwent internal validation, and external validation data were scarce. The AUC values of these models ranged from 0.649 to 0.984. Furthermore, most studies presented a high overall risk of bias. Conclusion Currently published RFS risk prediction mod…

title: Early-season prediction of maize lodging risk through multi-source and multi-period data integration
abstract: Abstract Purpose Lodging is a critical constraint on maize production because of its detrimental effects on both grain yield and quality. However, methods for predicting maize lodging risk early enough to support timely management interventions remain limited. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an early-season maize lodging risk prediction framework integrating proximal sensing, crop growth modeling, and machine learning through multi-source data fusion. Methods Maize nitrogen-rate and planting-density experiments were conducted during 2017-2019 in China and the United Kingdom under contrasting agroecological conditions. Maize growth status was estimated by integrating proximal sensing with crop growth modeling, and crop growth, management practices, phenological, soil, and weather variables were aggregated over growth-stage-based periods. Failure wind speed (FWS) at the basal, fifth, and eighth internode positions, calculated using a mechanistic maize lodging model at the R3 stage, was used as the lodging risk indicator. Support vector regression, random forest regression, and gradient boosted decision tree regression were evaluated for predictions made at the V8 and V12 growth stages. Results Random forest regression showed the best overall held-out performance. Across the three internode positions and two prediction stages, random forest regression achieved R 2 values …

abstract: Objective To evaluate whether early gastrointestinal myoelectric parameters combined with clinical data predict vomiting within 7 days after monitoring in intensive care unit (ICU) patients and to develop a risk prediction model. Methods This prospective multicenter cohort included 527 ICU patients: 370 in the development cohort and 157 in an independent external validation cohort. The primary outcome was vomiting within 7 days after monitoring. Nine prespecified candidate predictors—age, sex, surgical status, sedation status, disease type, percentage of normal gastric slow waves, gastric dominant frequency, gastric dominant power ratio, and percentage of intestinal slow waves—were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model. Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Brier score, calibration intercept, calibration slope, and decision curve analysis. Results Overall, 120 patients experienced vomiting (22.8%): 84 (22.7%) in the development cohort and 36 (22.9%) in the external validation cohort. Multivariable analysis showed that a higher gastric dominant power ratio was associated with lower odds of vomiting (OR = 0.758, 95% CI: 0.708 to 0.811, P < 0.001). Compared with patients with respiratory diseases, those with neurological diseases had higher odds of vom…

title: Combining vegetation index, slope and plant spacing factors with machine learning for improved accuracy of UAV-based maize yield prediction
abstract: Maize, as a crucial food crop, is vital for economic development and food security. Understanding the causes of spatial variability in farmland maize yields and precisely estimating these yields are of great significance for maize cultivation and production. However, most existing maize yield studies inadequately account for spatial variability, and the models often lack generalizability. To address this issue, the response of maize yield to vegetation indices (VI), plant spacing factor (PS), and Slope (SL) across three growth stages was investigated. To further reduce redundancy among multiple VIs, correlation analysis was employed to screen input features that were more significantly associated with maize yield. Finally, four machine learning methods (Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN), Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM)) were used to establish complex nonlinear mappings between VI, PS, SL, and maize yield, with the goal of elucidating the predictive capabilities and complementary relationships of single, dual, and triple data sources in estimating maize yield. The study results revealed that SL was significantly negatively correlated with area-based maize yield (r = –0.75), with smaller slope classes tending to have higher yields in the sampled fields. Artificial intelligence and machine learning–driven predictive models for arrhythmia risk prediction and sudden cardiac death stratification: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have rapidly expanded the landscape of cardiovascular risk prediction, with models increasingly developed for atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence, sudden cardiac death (SCD), and malignant ventricular arrhythmias. However, the overall discriminative performance of these models across diverse electrophysiologic applications has not been comprehensively quantified. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the predictive performance and generalizability of AI/ML models for arrhythmia risk stratification. Methods PubMed, Embase, ScienceDirect, Scopus, and Cochrane Library were systematically searched for studies evaluating AI/ML-based prediction models for arrhythmic outcomes. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed to pool the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Prespecified subgroup analyses compared AF recurrence and SCD/ventricular arrhythmia prediction models. Prediction intervals and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate robustness and expected performance across future clinical settings. Results Ten studies comprising 80,133 participants met the inclusion criteria, of which eight studies, encompassing 79,396 participants across their full study cohorts, contributed to the quantitative synthesis. Interpretable dimensions of visual aesthetics reveal robust coupling but weak prediction of human ratings
abstract: Abstract Computational descriptors offer an interpretable way to study image aesthetics, but their correspondence with human perceptual constructs requires evaluation. We examined five descriptors grouped into three operational domains: spectral-residual spatial salience (S), masked-image reconstruction difficulty (T), and Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training (CLIP)-based semantic classification uncertainty (I). Using 2,500 photographs from the Aesthetic Visual Analysis (AVA) dataset, we assessed descriptor correlations, regression models, cross-validated prediction of human ratings, and exploratory clustering. Salience concentration and reconstruction difficulty showed a reproducible inverse association (Pearson r = − 0.545; Spearman ρ = −0.586), whereas aesthetic-rating prediction remained negligible and clustering depended on feature scaling. In an independent fixation-based evaluation on 1,003 MIT1003 images, spectral-residual saliency yielded mean normalized scanpath saliency (NSS) = 0.7275, pixel-based area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) = 0.7019, and similarity (SIM) = 0.2801, below a Gaussian center-prior baseline (1.2511, 0.8107, and 0.3464, respectively). title: Early prediction of acute kidney injury in traumatic intracerebral hemorrhage: a machine learning model using admission laboratory variables
abstract: Background Traumatic intracerebral hemorrhage (tICH) represents a severe subtype of traumatic brain injury, with reported mortality rates ranging from 20% to 60%. Among tICH patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU), acute kidney injury (AKI) occurs in approximately 7.6% to 24% of cases and is associated with increased mortality, prolonged ICU length of stay, and greater healthcare burden. Early identification of AKI risk using admission laboratory parameters may facilitate timely renal protective strategies. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model for early AKI prediction in this population. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included 539 ICU patients with tICH admitted between January 2024 and December 2025. Patients with chronic kidney disease or AKI at ICU admission were excluded. All predictor variables were collected within the first 24 h following ICU admission. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression. Seven machine learning algorithms were compared; the final model was selected based on cross-validated performance within the training set, with comparable discriminative performance among top models confirmed by DeLong tests. Model interpretability was assessed using Shapley Additive Explanations analysis. Results Five variables were retained: serum c…

title: Prediction model of axillary lymph node metastasis in breast cancer based on combined ultrasound and mammography
abstract: Objective To develop and validate a multimodal radiomics model based on ultrasound (US) and mammography (MG) for preoperative prediction of axillary lymph node (ALN) metastatic burden in breast cancer. Methods A total of 557 patients with primary breast cancer were retrospectively enrolled and randomly assigned (7:3) to a training cohort (n=392) and a internal test cohort (n=165). All patients underwent US and MG within two weeks before surgery. Lesions on US were segmented using a deep learning–based automatic method, whereas regions of interest (ROIs) on MG were manually delineated and reviewed by radiologists. Radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics and standardized via Z-score normalization. Feature-level fusion was performed using an equal-weight (1:1) arithmetic scheme. The synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) was applied to address class imbalance in the training cohort. After intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)-based stability analysis, univariate screening, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, a radiomics signature (Rad-score) was constructed. Random Forest (RF) models were developed for binary classification (N0 vs N+) and three-class classification (0/1–3/≥4 metastatic ALNs). title: The effect of common institutional ownership on carbon information disclosure an analysis based on the attention-based view and institutional isomorphism theory
abstract: As China’s carbon peaking and carbon neutrality strategy continues to advance, green, low-carbon development has become an important means of cultivating new-quality productive forces and promoting the green transformation of the economy. Regulators and capital markets are placing increasingly stringent demands on the transparency of firms’ carbon information disclosure. However, carbon information disclosure comprehensiveness remains uneven, making it important to examine whether common institutional ownership can address this problem. Using a sample of Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share listed firms from 2014 to 2023, this study systematically examines the effect of common institutional ownership on carbon information disclosure and the mechanisms underlying that effect. The results indicate that common institutional ownership significantly improves the transparency of firms’ carbon information disclosure. Mechanism tests reveal differentiated mediating effects of internal control quality and internal green governance. Internal control quality has a positive mediating effect, whereas internal green governance produces a suppression effect. Further tests of moderating effects show that external institutional pressures have differentiated effects. title: Canopy morphology and plant biomass exert decoupled seasonal control over sediment organic carbon storage in tropical seagrass meadows
abstract: Introduction Seagrass meadows are among the most effective blue carbon sinks globally; however, the relationships between plant functional traits and sediment organic carbon (SOC) storage remain poorly understood. Methods In this study, we quantified plant biomass and canopy morphological traits in two Enhalus acoroides meadows on Hainan Island, China, during the dry and rainy seasons, and assessed their associations with SOC density using partial correlation, variance partitioning and partial least squares path modeling. Results Plant biomass showed a net negative association with SOC density (standardized total associations of -0.75 and -0.63 in the rainy and dry seasons), whereas canopy morphological traits, specifically shoot density and leaf length, were positively associated with SOC storage (0.57 and 0.59). These opposing associations followed seasonally differing pathways: biomass was consistently associated with SOC through sediment redox properties, whereas morphology was associated with SOC through sediment properties in the rainy season and through the organic carbon deposition rate in the dry season. Discussion These patterns are consistent with enhanced mineralization associated with high biomass and with particle trapping associated with dense canopies, although the underlying mechanisms were not directly measured and remain to be tested experimentally. Our findi…

title: ALMA detection of continuum emission from GQ Lup B
abstract: GQ Lup B is a massive (10-40 M_ Jup ) companion orbiting the young T-Tauri star GQ Lup A at a projected distance of ∼110 au (0.7''). It lies outside the circumprimary disk in the submillimeter continuum , but its ∼,63^̧irc inclined orbit intersects the primary's gas disk twice per period. We report a 5.8σ detection of continuum emission at the location of GQ Lup B, obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 0.89 mm (band 7). We associate this emission with a dusty disk around the companion, already detected by VLT/NACO and JWST/MIRI in the mid-infrared. To date, this is the third disk observed at millimeter wavelengths around a companion spanning the brown dwarf and planetary mass regimes , following PDS 70 c, a gas giant embedded in the parent circumstellar disk, and SR 12 c, a planetary mass companion at 1200 au from the primary. We retrieve a point source with a peak intensity of 54.5 , co-spatial with GRAVITY astrometry. The emission is spatially unresolved, Jy, beam^ -1 placing an upper limit of 2.3 au on the source radius (from a synthesized beam of ∼,29 disks. mas). Formation of Dynamic Nanoporous Shells on Bimetallic Particles During Carbon Dioxide Hydrogenation
abstract: Abstract The hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol relies on dynamic interactions between metal nanoparticles and oxide supports, yet a comprehensive, particle-resolved understanding of catalyst restructuring during activation and reaction remains difficult to obtain via conventional ensemble-averaged or post-reaction characterization. Here, identical-location high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (IL-HRTEM) has been used to track the same PdCu nanoparticles on ZnO, from the as-prepared state, through H2 activation, to subsequent CO2 hydrogenation. The most pronounced restructuring occurred under H2 conditions used for catalyst activation, when the number of observable nanoparticles decreased by a factor of 2, their average size increased, and crystalline lattice features became more readily identifiable. Particle-by-particle tracking directly distinguished migration and coalescence processes from Ostwald ripening, demonstrating that both mechanisms contribute concurrently to particle coarsening. Support-derived atomically thin ZnOx overlayers start to grow over PdCu nanoparticles under H2 and continue during CO2 hydrogenation, concurrent with a slowing of nanoparticle coarsening. The ZnOx shells are dynamic, opening and closing subnanometre pores during reaction. Identical-location single-particle analysis showed that ZnOx shells restrict nanoparticle migration and coale…

title: NiCo–carbonate pillared bentonite clay-doped carbon paste electrode for sensitive electrochemical detection of phenolic and naphtholic pollutants in wastewater
Зелёное финансирование и низкоуглеродная трансформация обрабатывающей промышленности Китая: механизмы, вызовы и направления развития
abstract: Введение. Обрабатывающая промышленность Китая находится на ключевом этапе перехода от модели экстенсивного роста с высоким энергопотреблением и значительными выбросами к экологически устойчивой, низкоуглеродной и высокоэффективной модели хозяйствования. Зелѐные финансы, опирающиеся на кредитное финансирование, инвестиции в облигации и механизмы углеродного рынка, обеспечивают направленное перераспределение капитала в пользу экологически чистых проектов и формируют устойчивый импульс к трансформации промышленного сектора КНР. Несмотря на совершенствование институциональной системы зелѐных финансов, обрабатывающая промышленность страны сталкивается со структурными вызовами, в числе которых индустриализация зелѐных технологий, оптимизация структуры высокоуглеродных отраслей и трансмиссия углеродных издержек. Материалы и методы. На основе актуальных данных 2024–2025 годов о развитии зелѐного финансирования в Китае и низкоуглеродной трансформации обрабатывающей промышленности с использованием методов анализа научной литературы и институционально-политического анализа в работе исследована роль зелѐных финансов в поддержке экологически устойчивого развития промышленного сектора КНР, рассмотрены текущее состояние и ключевые вызовы данного процесса. title: Impact of digital inclusive finance on agricultural carbon emissions: evidence from 30 provinces in China, 2011–2023
abstract: Introduction Amid the low-carbon transition of agriculture and the construction of sustainable food systems, digital inclusive finance has become a vital financial tool to reshape agricultural production patterns and optimize resource allocation. Methods Based on provincial panel data from 30 Chinese provinces spanning 2011 to 2023, this study adopts a two-way fixed-effects model to examine how digital inclusive finance affects agricultural carbon emissions. We use instrumental variable estimation to address endogeneity and conduct a series of robustness tests. Results Digital inclusive finance significantly curbs agricultural carbon emissions. Mechanism tests show that digital inclusive finance reduces agricultural carbon emissions mainly by promoting industrial structure upgrading; the mediating role of agricultural technological progress is statistically insignificant. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the emission-reduction effect varies across subgroups. Usage depth and digitization degree exert prominent carbon reduction effects, while coverage breadth shows no significant impact. Regionally, the inhibitory effect only exists in central and western China. The carbon reduction dividend is more pronounced in low-urbanization areas and major grain-producing regions but insignificant in medium-high urbanization and non-major grain-producing regions. Discussion The low-car…

title: Temperature-regulated microstructural evolution of biotemplated MoS2/carbon composites for enhanced lithium storage
How green finance reduces agricultural carbon emissions: incentivizing green technology innovation and constraining traditional technology inputs
abstract: Can China peak its carbon emissions by 2030 as scheduled? As agricultural decarbonization has become increasingly important in the transition toward carbon neutrality, the role of green finance in supporting low-carbon agricultural development deserves further attention. Using province-level panel data for 30 Chinese provinces from 2007 to 2022, this study constructs a composite Green Finance Index and employs a two-way fixed-effects model to systematically examine the impact and mechanism of green finance on total agricultural carbon emissions. The results show that higher levels of green finance are significantly associated with lower agricultural carbon emissions. Mechanism analyses reveal a dual-channel pathway: green finance promotes green technology innovation while constraining traditional technology inputs, both contributing to emissions abatement. Moreover, rural digitalization attenuates the marginal impact of green finance, indicating an important boundary condition. Heterogeneity analyses show that the abatement effect is stronger in eastern China. Overall, green finance supports the agricultural low-carbon transition by incentivizing green technology innovation and curbing traditional technology inputs, yet its mitigation effects are significantly moderated by rural digitalization. Policy efforts should strengthen the additionality and precision of green finance an…

title: Free vibration of the hybrid laminated nanocomposite beams reinforced with carbon nanotubes and graphene platelets based on the RHSDT and IGA
abstract: This paper employs the refined higher-order shear deformation theory (RHSDT) and the isogeometric analysis (IGA) to formulate a solution for the free vibration problem of hybrid nanocomposite beams simultaneously reinforced with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and graphene platelets (GPLs). Carbon nanotubes and graphene platelets are distributed within polymeric or metallic matrices with various reinforcement patterns. The material properties of FG‑CNTRC are determined based on the rule of mixtures, and FG-GPLRC are characterized using the Halpin–Tsai micromechanical model. The weak form of the governing vibration equation is formulated based on Hamilton’s principle. The obtained results are validated by comparison with several previously published studies. Numerical analyses are presented to evaluate the effects of material and geometric parameters (volume fraction, material distribution pattern, aspect ratio, boundary conditions, etc.) on the natural frequencies of the FG‑CNTRC/GPLRC hybrid beams.

title: Urban digitalization for cleaner development: nonlinear effects on CO2 emission intensity under China’s dual-transition policies
abstract: This study examines the nonlinear relationship between digital empowerment and urban carbon emission intensity using panel data for 295 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2006 to 2023. A two-way fixed-effects model with a quadratic specification is employed, and the inverted U-shaped relationship is further verified using the turning point and the Lind-Mehlum U-test. The results show that digital empowerment initially increases carbon emission intensity but reduces it after a threshold is crossed. The findings remain robust after controlling for industrial structure, excluding 2020–2022, and using lagged explanatory variables. Mechanism analysis provides the strongest support for the energy-intensity channel, while evidence for virtual agglomeration is partial and the results for artificial intelligence are measurement-sensitive. Evidence for the digital-infrastructure channel is interpreted more cautiously because of its potential overlap with the digital empowerment index, although a reconstructed index excluding infrastructure-related components provides additional support. Moreover, complementary policy-based analyses using the Broadband China pilot, including conventional TWFE and stacked difference-in-differences specifications, show a significant reduction in carbon emission intensity, with parallel-trend and placebo tests providing additional support for the credibili…

title: Assessing lymphatic drainage of the colon and rectum by single-photon emission computerised tomography: a feasibility study in patients undergoing standard-of-care colonoscopy
abstract: Objective The splenic flexure (SF) has variable lymphatic drainage due to its heterogeneous vascular supply, contributing to uncertainty regarding optimal oncological resection. This study evaluated the feasibility and safety of in vivo lymphatic mapping of the SF and rectum using endoscopic submucosal Technetium-99 m (Tc-99 m) radiocolloid injection followed by planar lymphoscintigraphy and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), and assessed the reproducibility of identifying a dominant lymphatic pedicle (DLP) consistently. Methods A prospective pilot study was conducted at Concord Repatriation General Hospital, Sydney (2022–2023), in patients undergoing standard-of-care colonoscopy who had macroscopically normal colorectal anatomy. Submucosal radiocolloid injections were administered at the SF ( n = 10), upper rectum ( n = 5) or lower rectum with direct digital massage ( n = 5). Tc-99 m Nanoscan or Tc-99 m antimony trisulfide (40MBq in 1.3 mL, with methylene blue) was used. Serial planar lymphoscintigraphy was performed at 1, 2, 4 and 24 h, with SPECT at 1, 2 and 4 h and additional delayed imaging at 24 and/or 48 h. Imaging was assessed for tracer dispersion, nodal uptake and DLP identification. Results Submucosal injection was technically successful in all 20 patients, without extravasation or adverse events occurred at 1-, 7-, or 30-day follow-up. No consistent…

title: Planning carbon removal landscapes in Africa: land use regulation, spatial justice and the governance of negative emissions
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore whether land-use planning and environmental regulations in seven African countries – Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa, Rwanda and Ethiopia – can effectively manage the use of land for carbon dioxide removal (CDR) technologies. It examine how planning law handles competing land uses for afforestation, bioenergy with carbon capture and storage and soil carbon sequestration, and assesses whether current frameworks address spatial justice, participatory governance and fair land access. Design/methodology/approach The study uses à socio-legal approach that combines three methods: analyzing land use planning laws, environmental regulations and climate policies in the seven countries; reviewing interdisciplinary literature on land governance, legal pluralism and climate mitigation; and examining national policy documents like nationally determined contributions, spatial plans and land tenure laws. The analysis draws on spatial justice theory and legal pluralism. Since the study is based on documents rather than fieldwork, its findings reflect the legal and policy record. Further research would be needed to confirm how these laws work in practice at the community level. Findings In all seven countries, land-use planning systems are not set up to manage CDR projects effectively. There are three main problems: no clear carbon rights in prop…

title: A real-time trading indicator for profitable trade in Indian indexes using machine learning
abstract: Introduction Traditional technical indicators such as Moving Averages, RSI, MACD, and Bollinger Bands often lag behind rapidly changing markets such as NIFTY 50 and BANK NIFTY, resulting in delayed entries, premature exits, and false signals. This paper proposes the low-latency machine learning indicator (RTMLI), an adaptive trading framework that integrates multidimensional feature engineering with Random Forest, XGBoost, and LSTM models to generate low-latency Buy, Hold, and Sell signals. Methods The framework incorporates price, trend, momentum, volatility, volume, and price-action features and uses ensemble meta-learning to capture nonlinear market relationships. Experiments used historical and low-latency data from major Indian indices over 2022-2026. Results RTMLI outperforms individual ML models, including RF, XGBoost, LSTM, and GRU, as well as conventional Buy-and-Hold, EMA, RSI, MACD, and SuperTrend strategies. RTMLI achieved higher Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, ROC-AUC, cumulative return, CAGR, Sharpe Ratio, Sortino Ratio, Profit Factor, and Win Rate, while maintaining lower Maximum Drawdown and signal latency. Statistical validation using the Paired t-test, Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test, and One-Way ANOVA confirmed the significance of the observed improvements at the 95% confidence level ( p < 0.05). Discussion The framework also demonstrated millisecond-leve…

title: From Affordance to Coupling: Reconstructing Foreign Language Pedagogy through an AI-Enabled Production-Oriented Approach
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is now a routine presence in foreign language classrooms, yet the gap between what the technology can do and what it actually teaches remains poorly theorised. This paper argues that the gap is structural, and that it is best analysed at the level of the pedagogic move. Taking the Production-Oriented Approach (POA) as its anchor, the paper identifies three chronic constraints in POA practice: the cost of evaluating student output, the difficulty of matching input to diagnosed gaps, and the delay between production and feedback. It then proposes the construct of an AI-enabled Production-Oriented Approach (AI-POA), which frames AI as a change in the resourcing and pacing of an existing cycle. Three affordances of generative AI (generative, dialogic, evaluative) are specified, together with four conditions under which they couple with instruction: goal alignment, temporal placement, cognitive appropriateness and teacher control. A nine-move cycle is derived, and implications for objectives, materials, assessment, teacher judgement and institutional arrangements are discussed. The framework is offered as a falsifiable middle-range theory rather than a design recipe.

title: Variable electrical conductivity and near-wall electrothermal coupling in reactive Powell–Eyring ternary nanofluid flow over a power-law stretching sheet
Symmetric Molecule, Asymmetric Coupling: Insights from Blinking in Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
abstract: Abstract Electronic asymmetry at metal–molecule interfaces is central to current rectification in nanoscale devices, yet its atomic-scale origin remains difficult to identify in individual single-molecule junctions. Here, we combine surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) spectroscopy with current–voltage (I–V) measurements to probe junction geometry and electron transport in a symmetric naphthalene derivative. Continuous SERS measurements reveal blinking, during which high-intensity SERS states coincide with asymmetric I–V characteristics, identifying a distinct blinking-on state associated with enhanced Raman signals. Vibrational analysis and transport simulations based on density functional theory and tight-binding theory are consistent with an asymmetric contact geometry that produces unequal molecule–electrode coupling and rectification. These results suggest that SERS blinking can serve as a spectroscopic signature of transient asymmetric contacts and provide a route to probing transient atomic configurations that govern single-molecule electron transport.

title: Comparative assessment of DBH- and UAV-derived crown area-based allometric models for aboveground biomass and carbon stock estimation
abstract: Background: Forests mitigate climate change by storing carbon in aboveground biomass. Reliable biomass estimates depend on selecting allometric equations suited to local forest conditions. This study compared aboveground biomass and carbon stock estimates from diameter at breast height (DBH)- and crown area (CA)-based models in the Antutan Village Forest, Bulungan Regency, North Kalimantan, Indonesia. Methods: We collected data from six purposively selected one-hectare plots through terrestrial measurements and aerial mapping using a DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). We processed UAV imagery using photogrammetry, geometric correction, and deep learning-based crown detection to estimate crown area. Biomass was estimated using the DBH-based Basuki model and the CA-based Kuyah model, then converted to carbon using a fraction of 0.47. We compared estimates using Pearson correlation and a paired-sample t-test (α = 0.05). Findings: The Kuyah model produced higher mean aboveground biomass (41.11 tons ha⁻¹) than the Basuki model (33.45 tons ha⁻¹), with corresponding mean carbon stocks of 19.32 and 15.72 tons ha⁻¹. The difference was not statistically significant (t = 2.04, df = 5, p = 0.10). The estimates showed a weak positive correlation (r = 0.19). The coefficient of variation was 12.20% for the Kuyah model and 26.10% for the Basuki model. Conclusion: Although th…

title: Genomic surveillance of antimicrobial resistance in low- and middle-income countries: evolutionary insights, One Health integration, and implementation challenges
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is one of the most pressing global health challenges, endangering the effectiveness of antimicrobial treatments and threatening advances in modern medicine. The burden of resistant infections is particularly concerning in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where limited diagnostic facilities, weak surveillance systems, and inadequate laboratory infrastructure constrain the timely detection and control of resistant pathogens. Genomic epidemiology has strengthened AMR surveillance by enabling detailed characterization of resistance determinants, pathogen evolution, and potential transmission patterns. When integrated within a One Health framework, genomic approaches can provide insights into the interconnected roles of human, animal, and environmental reservoirs in the emergence and dissemination of resistance. This review critically examines the evolutionary mechanisms underlying AMR, advances in genomic epidemiology and next-generation sequencing technologies, and the application of bioinformatics databases, analytical pipelines, and artificial intelligence in resistance surveillance. Particular attention is given to the comparative capabilities and limitations of these approaches, their practical applicability in resource-constrained settings, and the infrastructural, computational, and institutional barriers affecting their implementation…

title: Energy transfer and luminescence efficiency in rare-earth-ion-based materials
abstract: The mechanisms of energy transfer between rare-earth ions and their influence on luminescence efficiency are analysed. On the basis of the Förster–Dexter theory, the dependence of the probability and efficiency of dipole–dipole energy transfer on the donor–acceptor distance is calculated. Using the Inokuti–Hirayama model, the donor luminescence decay curves in a YAG host are simulated for acceptor concentrations of 0.5–5 at.%, and it is shown that for a critical distance R0 = 1.5 nm the energy transfer efficiency increases from 71.7% to 99.3%. The practical significance of sensitisation, cross-relaxation and concentration quenching is discussed using the examples of Yb3+→Er3+ and Nd3+.

title: Generational development of a self-contained dual-axis solar power system—A design evolution
abstract: This paper describes a multi-year engineering development of a self-contained solar power system that uses dual-axis tracking to ensure improved efficiency. This system is designed to operate in remote and rugged environments with minimal human intervention. The iterative design process yielded three generations of systems that were increasingly productive and responsive to design issues identified during development. The generations are labeled T1V1, T1V2, and T1V3, and this nomenclature is used throughout the manuscript. Across the three generations, the systems scaled dramatically at each generation (from 1.58 to 9.28 kW to 18.56 kW of photovoltaic capacity, and from 9.6 to 16.13 to 32.2 kWh of battery storage), while preserving a 48 V direct current (VDC) bus and maintaining the underlying dual-axis tracking approach. A comparison test was used to establish performance metrics and yielded approximately 30% greater incident solar energy and 39% greater delivered electrical energy than the equivalent fixed-tilt array. Field tests at a test facility exposed mechanical and electrical design issues that had to be addressed. Among the most significant issues were tracker binding and emergency stop contacts. The second generation (T1V2) was evaluated over 245 days of operation, including during the winter in a mid-latitude location. The third generation added a containerized shipp…

title: Seasonal variability and pollution assessment using leachate pollution index (LPI) of Khenifra landfill leachate, Morocco
Mass-Conserving, Unconditionally Energy Dissipative and Fully Decoupled Schemes for Nonisothermal Variable Density Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations
abstract: This paper develops a family of efficient numerical schemes for the non-isothermal variable density incompressible Navier-Stokes equations (VDNSEs), a representative multiphysics coupling system that poses significant challenges due to the coexistence of time derivative terms, nonlinear convection terms, the gravity and buoyancy effects. The proposed schemes are linear, fully decoupled, mass conservation and unconditional energy dissipation, achieving first and second order temporal accuracy via the Euler and BDF2 schemes, respectively. The key novelty is the introduction of two $energy-contribution$ $auxiliary$ $variables$ (ECAV) $R$ and $S$, which can treat the difficulties caused by the time derivative terms conveniently and ensure the mass conservation naturally. Combining with other auxiliary variables handle the gravity term and nonlinear terms, an equivalent system of the nonisothermal VDNSEs is reformulated. Using the pressure correction projection method to split the velocity and pressure, the linear and auxiliary terms are treated implicitly, while the nonlinear terms are approximated explicitly, two time-marching fully decoupled schemes (first order Euler and second order BDF2) are constructed. We rigorously prove discrete mass conservation, unconditional energy dissipation and the unique solvability of the numerical solutions for both schemes. Both schemes decompose…

title: Green energy consumption in public transportation: a bibliometric analysis of current trends and future directions
abstract: Purpose Given its considerable carbon footprint, the green energy use in public transportation requires a fundamental transformation towards environmentally sustainable energy options. To achieve this transition, comprehensive research is needed. This study aims to provide critical insights for academics, policymakers and industry stakeholders to guide sustainable transportation strategies. The research also emphasizes a global shift toward integrated, technology-driven and sustainable mobility solutions by identifying knowledge gaps and areas for future investigation. Design/methodology/approach This study employed bibliometric analysis as its primary methodology. A systematic search of Scopus and Web of Science (WoS) databases yielded a total of 1,513 publications. Data analysis and visualization were facilitated through RStudio and VOSviewer software. Findings The findings suggest the need for interdisciplinary collaboration, enhanced international cooperation and policy-driven research to accelerate the adoption of green energy in public transport. The analysis shows an average publication age of 4.78 years suggests that most contributions are relatively recent, pointing to increasing scholarly attention in recent years. While the average citation count per document is 13.87, which is relatively modest, it suggests a moderate level of impact. The study analysis reveals that…

title: A hierarchically structured layered Ni(OH)₂//ZIF-8@rGO electrode delivering superior energy storage with AC counter electrode
Economic Growth, Energy Consumption, Urbanization, and Ecological Footprint in ASEAN: A Panel Analysis
abstract: This study examines how economic growth, energy consumption, and urbanization are associated with the per capita ecological footprint in eight Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) members during 2010–2022, where ecological pressure varies sharply and earlier evidence is inconsistent. An observational associative design was applied to a balanced panel of 104 country-year observations from the World Bank and the Global Footprint Network. The Chow and Hausman tests selected the Fixed Effect Model, followed by diagnostic and robustness checks. In the main model, economic growth (annual GDP per capita growth, %), energy consumption (kilograms of oil equivalent per capita), and urbanization (urban population, % of total) were each positively associated with the ecological footprint (global hectares, gha, per capita) at the 5% level and jointly (Wald F = 16.27, p < 0.001). Holding the other variables constant, a one-percentage-point higher growth rate, a one-percentage-point higher urban share, and an additional 100 kilograms of oil equivalent per capita were associated with 0.012, 0.014, and 0.069 gha per capita more footprint, respectively. These are statistical associations, not causal effects. Energy consumption was the most robust association across alternative specifications, whereas the significance of growth and urbanization depended on the standard-error estimator. …

title: Determinants of trade in renewable energy equipment: an extended gravity model for Belt and Road countries
abstract: International trade in renewable energy equipment plays an important role in the diffusion of technologies supporting the global energy transition, yet the economic, energy-sector, and institutional factors associated with this trade across Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) countries remain insufficiently examined. This study investigates China’s exports of renewable energy equipment to 63 BRI countries over 2010–2019 using an extended gravity model that combines conventional economic and geographical determinants with renewable energy capacity indicators and measures of institutional integration. The panel was compiled from UN Comtrade, World Bank, and IRENA data. Specification tests support a random-effects estimator (Breusch–Pagan LM χ 2 (1) = 849.2, p < 0.001; Hausman χ 2 (5) = 6.09, p = 0.297; Mundlak χ 2 (5) = 3.99, p = 0.551; N = 536). Geographical distance is negatively associated with exports (elasticity −1.42), while importer GDP per capita (1.21), population (1.11), and annual renewable capacity additions in partner countries (0.05) are positively associated with export values. WTO membership is conditionally associated with exports that are about 63% higher, other factors held constant, and this association is robust to cluster-robust and Driscoll–Kraay standard errors, PPML estimation, alternative estimation windows, and identification from accessions alone; SCO an…

title: The growth energy emissions trilemma: evidence from BRICS
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the equilibrium relationship between economic growth, foreign direct investments (FDI), trade openness, fossil fuel energy use and CO2 emissions for Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa (BRICS) countries over a period from 1990 to 2022. Design/methodology/approach Panel data tests are done using the first- and second-generation unit root tests, Pedroni and Johansen Fisher panel co-integration tests, fully modified ordinary least squares (FMOLS) for long-run coefficient and the Dumitrescu–Hurlin panel causality test. Findings There is evidence of cointegration in the long run among the variables. According to the FMOLS estimates, fossil fuel energy consumption (elasticity = 0.847) and inward foreign direct investments (elasticity = 0.031) have a positive and significant effect on CO2 emissions, while trade openness has a negative but insignificant effect. Causality from GDP per capita to CO2 emissions (p < 0.05), and inward FDI to CO2 emissions (p < 0.10) is one-sided. Research limitations/implications The limitation of availability of data restricts the study period from 1990 to 2022. The study uses aggregate data on fossil fuels without differentiating the types of fossil fuels used. Further studies should consider the analysis with country-level asymmetry, structural break models and extended BRICS membership. Originality/valu…

title: Serum tsRNA-Arg-5–0095 and clinical variable integration: an interpretable machine learning model for esophageal carcinoma diagnosis
abstract: Background Esophageal carcinoma (EC) is a highly lethal malignancy with a low detection rate. Current diagnostic modalities are either invasive or insufficiently accurate, highlighting an urgent need for effective non-invasive biomarkers. tRNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) have emerged as stable and promising tumor biomarkers. This study aimed to develop an interpretable eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model integrating serum tsRNA-Arg-5–0095 with routine clinical indicators for the non-invasive diagnosis of EC. Methods Serum tsRNA-Arg-5–0095 was quantified by quantitative real-time PCR in 126 patients with preoperative EC, 32 patients with esophagitis, 101 healthy controls, and 10 postoperative patients. Among 48 routine laboratory parameters, predictive features were selected using Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression combined with bootstrap stability analysis. Using these features, XGBoost hyperparameters were tuned to obtain the narrowest 95% CI for the cross-validated area under the curve (AUC). The resulting model was evaluated using repeated 5 × 10-fold cross-validation, with the five LASSO-selected features held constant across all folds.
