title: Altered audiovisual emotional integration in individuals with subthreshold depression: evidence from behavioral and event-related potentials
Environmental taxation, energy consumption and tourism–growth dynamics: CS-ARDL and panel VAR evidence from EU Mediterranean economies
abstract: Introduction Environmental taxation, energy consumption, and tourism are closely interconnected with economic performance in Mediterranean economies. This study examines these relationships across seven EU Mediterranean countries (Greece, Spain, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, France, and Slovenia) using annual data covering 1995–2023. Methods The analysis combines a Cross-Sectionally Augmented Autoregressive Distributed Lag (CS‐ARDL) model, accounting for cross‐sectional dependence and slope heterogeneity, with a Panel Vector Autoregressive (VAR) model to investigate dynamic interdependencies. Robustness assessments include diagnostic tests, structural-break controls, panel cointegration tests, a Panel Vector Error Correction Model (VECM), alternative variable specifications, and leave‐one‐country‐out estimations. Results In the preferred CS‐ARDL specification, controlling for capital, labour, and structural breaks, gross fixed capital formation per inhabitant is positively and significantly associated with real GDP per capita. Tourism intensity exhibits a positive but only marginally significant association, while energy consumption and the implicit energy tax rate are statistically insignificant. Energy consumption is positively associated with GDP per capita only in specifications excluding capital and labour. Panel VAR results indicate that tourism Granger‐causes GDP per capita gr…

title: Development and validation of a social support scale of physical exercise for Chinese urban older adults in the context of sports-medicine integration
abstract: Abstract Objective The purpose was to develop and validate a scale based on the social support theory in the context of Sports-Medicine integration, assessing available social support for physical exercise among independent urban older adults in China. Methods The initial items were generated through semi-structured interviews, expert interviews, and the Delphi method. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) ( n = 266) was used to explore the factor structure, and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) ( n = 312) was employed to examine item reliability, composite reliability, and model fit. Finally, test‑retest reliability, external convergent validity, and discriminant validity were evaluated. Results EFA extracted four factors, which together accounted for 73.526% of the total variance. Cronbach’s α values ranged from 0.824 to 0.912, inter‑item correlations ranged from 0.342 to 0.868, and item‑total correlations ranged from 0.508 to 0.861. CFA showed that squared multiple correlations ranged from 0.382 to 0.922, CR and ICC ranged from 0.831 to 0.917, 0.763 to 0.903; respectively. RMSEA = 0.064, χ² = 122.384, χ²/df = 2.074, GFI = 0.974, AGFI = 0.901, CFI = 0.974, TLI = 0.995, NFI = 0.951, SRMR = 0.063, for the first‑order model; for the second‑order model: RMSEA = 0.063, χ² = 126.227, χ²/df = 2.069, GFI = 0.935, AGFI = 0.903, CFI = 0.973, TLI = 0.965, NFI = 0.949, SRMR = 0.063, and the…

title: Preparation of Novel Selenium-Enriched Antioxidant Peptide from Yellowfin Tuna Dark Meat Water-Soluble Protein Using Energy-Gathered Ultrasound-Assisted Enzymatic Hydrolysis
The Maxwell Mass Effect as a Model for the Venusian Atmosphere: Integrating the Dew-Point Anchor Hypothesis, Radiative Opacity Lapse Rate and Polar-Vortex Energy Pathway
abstract: The Maxwell Mass Effect treats the surface temperature of Venus as the dependent variable required to support atmospheric mass against gravity. Solar energy is captured in a shallow topside thermal heating pool, stored as potential energy, and returned to depth by organised descent in the polar vortices under conservation of angular momentum. The sulfuric-acid lifting condensation level acts as the thermodynamic anchor. A two-component radiative opacity lapse rate fixes the geometric separation between that level and the infrared emission altitude. Stochastic inverse modelling with a VIRA profile, hydrostatic integration and thermodynamic filters recovers a cloud base near 49.6 km, an emission level near 69.4 km at 229 K, and a surface pressure of 91.5 bar. An energy-budget test shows that the required polar mass flux lies within observed vortex descent speeds. Only this framework supplies a structural explanation for the polar vortices.

title: Draw-Ratio-Programmed Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fibers for Controllable Unidirectional Contraction and Intelligent Textile Integration
abstract: Abstract Liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) fibers are promising candidates for soft actuators. However, it remains difficult to combine a low-temperature actuation onset, room-temperature retention of a mechanically programmed length, and textile processability in a single LCE fiber. Inspired by the energy input, state retention, and triggered release sequence of biological latch-mediated spring actuation (LaMSA), this study combines continuous spinning with room-temperature post-curing draw-programming to fabricate a high-performance, unidirectionally contracting LCE fiber. UV curing establishes the permanent network and its reference length, whereas subsequent mechanical stretching writes a recoverable extended state without a second curing step. Wide-angle/small-angle X-ray scattering (WAXD/SAXS) measurements show increased axial orientation after programming, and tensile-mode DMA shows that the programmed state has a higher storage modulus E′ and undergoes gradual softening between 30 and 54 °C under fixed-length test conditions. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) identifies a thermal transition over approximately 25–54 °C, with a peak at 42.5 °C. When the fiber is free to move, photothermal heating releases the programmed deformation and drives contraction toward the cured reference length. Endpoint photographs show retention of the programmed length for more than one mo…

title: Relationship between anthropometric parameters and serum asprosine levels in non-diabetes mellitus adult subjects with a cross sectional study design
abstract: Anthropometry involves quantitative measurements of body dimensions and composition, including muscle, bone, and adipose tissue, and is used to assess body shape, health, and nutritional status. Anthropometric parameters can also help identify risk factors for diseases such as obesity. Obesity and overweight are associated with excessive body fat accumulation. Hormones involved in glucose metabolism and homeostasis may contribute to the development of obesity. Asprosin is a protein hormone secreted by white adipose tissue that promotes hepatic glucose release. This study aimed to determine the relationship between anthropometric parameters (height, weight, body mass index, waist circumference, pelvic circumference, mid-upper arm circumference, and skinfold thickness) and serum asprosin levels. An analytical observational study with a cross-sectional design was conducted involving 80 adults: 21 obese women, 20 non-obese women, 18 obese men, and 21 non-obese men. The results showed no significant correlations between serum asprosin levels and any of the anthropometric parameters examined in the adult participants (p > 0.05). The study concluded that anthropometric parameters were not significantly associated with serum asprosin levels in adults without diabetes mellitus.

title: Combining behaviour change theory and service design to develop household food waste intervention concepts with residents and public sector actors in Sweden
abstract: Abstract Households generate about 60% of consumer-level food waste globally. Interventions to reduce food waste often rely on awareness-raising, but everyday routines, not lack of awareness, mainly drive it. This study explores how combining the COM-B model of behaviour with service design methods can support the development of intervention concepts to reduce household food waste in Sweden. Thirty semi-structured interviews with household members across Sweden were conducted to map the household food journey and identify where participants described food being wasted and opportunities to reduce it. Concepts developed from this analysis were refined through two rounds of prototyping workshops with households and two focus groups with public-sector actors. Interviewees linked food waste mainly to routine-level challenges of planning, limited overview of stored food, household coordination and time, and half described their household as wasting little or no food. Two leverage points stood out: the organisation and visibility of stored food, and the link between what is at home and what is bought. Participants favoured simple, low-effort tools that fit existing routines, such as “eat soon” prompts and a shared photo of the fridge, and both household and public-sector participants saw potential in feedback that makes food waste visible. Two exploratory motivational orientations, ec…

title: Comparison of the LRFD Method and the Performance-Based Method in the Design of Mid-Rise Reinforced Concrete Moment Frames under Blast Loading
Training on the Design of the React-Based 'QueueGo' Digital Queue Management System for Multi-Counter Services at SMKN 24 East Jakarta
abstract: This community service program (PKM) was carried out at SMKN 24 Jakarta Timur on 7–18 September 2026 to improve students’ understanding and practical skills in designing and developing a digital queue management system for multi-counter services. The school partner previously relied on manual queue handling, which caused disorderly service sequences, limited visibility of queue positions for visitors, and difficulties for staff in monitoring multiple service counters simultaneously. To address these issues, the team conducted a structured training and workshop using QueueGo, a React-based queue management application, both as an interactive learning medium and as the prototype output. The implementation method comprised four stages: pretest, guided training and workshop, evaluation (posttest), and participant feedback. Meanwhile, the system prototype was developed using the Prototype model, establishing the system design and frontend interface as the activity checkpoint. The resulting outputs include a functional QueueGo prototype featuring separate customer and operator workflows (user registration and login, guest access, counter selection, digital queue tickets, real-time queue monitoring, operator control panel, automated voice announcements, and service history), comprehensive system design documentation (use case diagram and activity diagram, activity documentation, and a…

title: Design and initial psychometric evaluation of the multidimensional school social climate inventory for parents (MSSCI-P) in Chile
abstract: Introduction School social climate research has relied predominantly on students' and teachers' reports, whereas multidimensional measures designed for parents and guardians remain scarce, particularly in Latin America. This study developed and examined the initial psychometric properties of the Multidimensional School Social Climate Inventory for Parents (MSSCI-P). Methods An instrumental, cross-sectional study was conducted with a non-probability sample of 1,172 parents and guardians from 94 schools across Chile's 16 regions. The administered 107-item version was examined using Exploratory Graph Analysis (EGA), followed by a complementary Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) using WLSMV in the same sample. Internal consistency and Average Variance Extracted (AVE) were also assessed. Results Seventeen items that did not reach a network loading of .30 in any community were excluded, yielding a 90-item solution comprising ten dimensions: Integral Safety; Physical Safety and Respect for Diversity; Collaboration and Integration; Interpersonal Relationships; Sense of Belonging; Teaching-Learning and Inclusion; Educational Leadership; Physical Environment and Organizational Structure; Laboratory Resources; and Educational and Support Resources. The CFA model showed adequate fit (scaled CFI = .920; scaled TLI = .917; scaled RMSEA = .055, 90% CI [.054, .056]; SRMR = .061). Internal cons…

Displaced by Design: Environmental Injustice in the Placement of Subsidized Housing Near Contaminated Land
abstract: This case study explores the intersection of environmental justice and af-fordable housing by examining the 800 Middle Street property in Houston, Texas. Although the site previously received a state-issued No Further Ac-tion (NFA) determination, construction activities beginning in December 2022 revealed buried incinerator ash and hazardous materials outside earli-er sampling boundaries. This development raises serious concerns about the adequacy of prior environmental investigations and illustrates how newly constructed subsidized housing may be placed near historically contami-nated land or sites with unresolved environmental risks. Drawing on loca-tion-based document analysis, records obtained through public information requests, environmental regulatory filings, and demographic data, this study analyzes how regulatory clearance processes and redevelopment practices intersect within environmentally vulnerable communities. Find-ings indicate limited spatial sampling, reliance on state-level remediation determinations, and fragmented institutional oversight can normalize envi-ronmental uncertainty for low-income populations while formally comply-ing with regulatory standards. The property, now fully built, embodies a critical tension between the ur-gent need for affordable housing and the ethical imperative to ensure resi-dential safety. By situating this case within broader …

A pilot single-case experimental evaluation of virtual reality-integrated work-focused cognitive behavioural therapy for patients experiencing burnout
abstract: Abstract Background: Burnout is a major cause of long-term sickness absence. Work-focused cognitive behavioural therapy (W-CBT) is a promising approach, but in vivo workplace exposure is difficult to arrange during sick leave, leaving few preparatory options before gradual work resumption. Aims: This pilot study evaluated the preliminary effectiveness of a 9-session W-CBT protocol integrating graded virtual reality (VR) exposures to interpersonal return to work (RTW) challenges, for workers on sick leave due to burnout. Method: In a single-case experimental design (A–B–A), four participants (two women, two men; mean age = 49.5 years, range 40–56; mean sick-leave duration = 7.5 months) completed a 9-session intervention combining psychoeducation, cognitive restructuring, behavioural activation, and VR exposures (sessions 2–8) with in vivo assignments. Outcomes were assessed at 14 time points and analysed through visual inspection and non-overlap (Tau-U) indices benchmarked against Parker et al . (2011). Results: Responses were heterogeneous. Three participants showed visible improvements in RTW self-efficacy, expectations and confidence communicating with managers and colleagues during the intervention, with Tau-U values in the medium-to-strong range for most primary outcomes; gains were partially maintained at follow-up. RTW-related anxiety fluctuated and re-elevated in two par…

title: SvCmr1-mediated regulation of melanin and Altersolanol A biosynthesis governs virulence in Stemphylium vesicarium
abstract: Stemphylium vesicarium is a destructive necrotrophic pathogen that causes leaf blight and severe yield losses in multiple crops. The polyketide phytotoxin Altersolanol A acts as a key virulence factor of this fungus. Although the polyketide synthase SvPKS1 catalyzes Altersolanol A biosynthesis, the upstream regulatory mechanism governing Altersolanol A production remains poorly understood. Here, we functionally characterized SvCMR1, a conserved chimeric zinc-finger transcription factor harboring both Zn 2 Cys 6 and C 2 H 2 domains. This transcription factor localizes to the nucleus and exhibits transcriptional activation activity. Deletion of SvCmr1 markedly reduced the biosynthesis of melanin and Altersolanol A, and substantially attenuated fungal virulence. Transcriptomic and RT-qPCR analyses revealed that SvCMR1 positively regulates DHN-melanin biosynthetic genes but has no effect on SvPks1 . Tricyclazole inhibition and exogenous 1,8-DHN supplementation assays support a functional association between the DHN-melanin pathway and Altersolanol A biosynthesis. Collectively, SvCMR1 serves as a regulator coordinating melanin and Altersolanol A biosynthesis, together with fungal virulence. These findings deepen our mechanistic understanding of S. vesicarium pathogenicity and provide valuable insights for the sustainable control of Stemphylium leaf blight.

title: Experiences of virtual reality interventions among intensive care unit patients: a systematic review and qualitative meta-synthesis with supplementary family perspectives
abstract: Objective To systematically synthesize the experiences and perceptions of intensive care unit (ICU) patients receiving virtual reality (VR) interventions, supplemented by family members’ perspectives, and to provide evidence for developing patient-centred VR interventions in the ICU. Methods Nine databases were systematically searched: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CINAHL, SinoMed, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang, and VIP. The initial search was completed on May 30, 2026, and updated on October 25, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened the studies and assessed methodological quality using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Qualitative Research. Qualitative evidence was synthesized using the JBI meta-aggregation approach, and the confidence of the synthesized findings was assessed using the ConQual framework. Results Ten studies from China, the United States, Brazil, and Denmark were included. Forty-nine qualitative findings were aggregated into 13 categories and four synthesized findings: (1) patients’ perceived physical and psychological experiences and potential benefits; (2) factors facilitating VR engagement and implementation; (3) multidimensional implementation barriers and challenges; and (4) expectations and needs for VR optimization. ConQual assessment indicated moderate confidence for synthesized findings 1, 2…

title: Species-specific radial growth responses to climate change in Mount Qomolangma mixed forests
abstract: Climate warming and drought have affected radial growth across forest types on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau, but interspecific responses within mixed forests remain poorly understood. We compared Picea smithiana , Tsuga dumosa , and Pinus wallichiana in a primary mixed forest in Gyirong County, Mount Qomolangma National Nature Reserve. Standard (STD) and residual (RES) chronologies were related to CRU climate and scPDSI for 1950–2022 and the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) for 2000–2022. Five initially mean-fitted T. dumosa cores were refitted with 50-year splines. Temperatures increased during 1980–2022. After Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) correction of ordinary Pearson P values, P. smithiana growth was negatively associated with winter–spring and early-summer temperatures and positively associated with spring scPDSI; its STD index declined during 1980–2022. T. dumosa showed positive associations with winter–spring scPDSI and selected summer temperature indices in the adopted STD chronology, but none remained significant after BH correction under all-core 50-year splines. However, its association with June–September mean temperature weakened in RES, nearly disappeared after linear detrending of both series, and did not pass stationary-bootstrap/BH testing in STD. A persistent suppression–release pattern also suggested possible contributions from stand processes. No growt…

Analisis Pengaruh Kepemimpinan Transformasional, Komitmen Organisasi, dan Keterikatan Kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan PT Indocement Plant 11–14 dengan Iklim Organisasi sebagai Variabel Mediasi
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of transformational leadership, organizational commitment, and work engagement on employee performance at Plant 11–14 of PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa, with organizational climate serving as a mediating variable. Field observations indicate that employee performance has not yet been optimal, as reflected by less inspiring leadership, weak emotional commitment, and low work engagement. The study population consisted of 395 employees, with a sample of 199 respondents determined using the Slovin formula. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using SEM-PLS with SmartPLS 4.1. The main findings show that transformational leadership, organizational commitment, and work engagement have a positive effect on organizational climate. Work engagement and organizational climate have a positive and significant effect on employee performance, whereas transformational leadership and organizational commitment do not have a significant direct effect. Furthermore, the mediation analysis reveals that organizational climate mediates the influence of the three independent variables on employee performance. Practical implications emphasize the importance of building a conducive organizational climate through transformational leadership, strong commitment, and optimal work engagement to improve sustainable productivity.

title: Pb modulates adventitious root growth and ginsenoside accumulation in Panax ginseng through integrated physiological and transcriptional responses
abstract: Lead (Pb) pollution is one of the most widespread forms of heavy metal contamination in soils and represents an important factor affecting the quality of medicinal plants during cultivation. However, the integrated effects of different Pb levels on root development and ginsenoside accumulation in ginseng remain unclear. In this study, ginseng adventitious roots were exposed to different concentrations of Pb(CH 3 COO) 2 ·3H 2 O, and their responses were investigated by analyzing root morphological characteristics, cellular ultrastructure, antioxidant enzyme activities, transcriptomic profiles, and ginsenoside contents. The results revealed that P. ginseng adventitious roots exhibited clear concentration-dependent and stage-specific responses to Pb stress. As Pb concentrations increased, root growth was progressively inhibited, accompanied by extensive adjustments in processes associated with the cell wall, redox homeostasis, and metabolism. Quantitative analysis of the major medicinally active compounds revealed that, compared with the control, the contents of most detected ginsenosides per unit dry weight of root tissue decreased following lead acetate treatment, with the exception of a few oleanolic acid-type ginsenosides. These Pb-induced alterations in ginsenoside accumulation are likely attributable to the coordinated effects of multiple physiological and metabolic processe…

title: Morphological diversity dynamics and potential breeding selection signals in chrysanthemum varieties assessed by DUS testing characteristics
abstract: Introduction Chrysanthemum has a long cultivation history in China, with rich phenotypic diversity and considerable ornamental and economic value. Methods In this study, we observed and statistically analyzed 608 morphologically diverse chrysanthemum varieties tested in Yunnan over the past decade based on 31 characteristics (including multiple expression states) specified in GB/T 19557.19-2018, Guidelines for the conduct of tests for distinctness, uniformity and stability—Chrysanthemum. This study aimed to reveal the dynamics of morphological diversity, shifts in breeding-selection directions, trait stability, and varietal-succession patterns in chrysanthemum breeding over the past decade. Results Frequency distribution analysis showed that most qualitative traits remained stable across four time periods without strong directional selection, retaining abundant phenotypic variation among varieties. Quantitative-trait analysis indicated that leaf length and leaf width showed minimal inter-annual variation, making them the most reliable indicators for DUS testing; plant height fluctuated substantially, whereas ray-floret length and width declined continuously, suggesting a potential breeding selection signal toward compact plant architecture and smaller flower structures. Cluster analysis identified four successive temporal groups of chrysanthemum varieties reflecting breeding su…

title: Characterization of the trehalose-6-phosphate synthase gene family in teak and functional analysis of TgTPS1 in transgenic tobacco under drought and salt stress
abstract: Plants are continuously exposed to abiotic stresses, such as drought, extreme temperatures, and high salinity, which restrict growth and reduce crop yields. Plant adaptation to these conditions involves changes in gene expression and the accumulation of osmoprotective compounds, including trehalose, which contributes to the protection of cellular proteins and membranes under stress conditions. Previous studies showed that the expression of TgTPS1 (Teak Trehalose Phosphate Synthase) increased in teak seedlings subjected to moderate and severe water stress, suggesting a potential role in abiotic stress responses. However, the functional role of TgTPS1 and its contribution to plant tolerance to abiotic stress remain poorly understood. Therefore, this study aimed to characterize the TPS gene family in teak and investigate the functional role of TgTPS1 in plant responses to drought and salt stress. The TPS gene family was characterized through genome-wide analyses, including the identification of TPS family members, their evolutionary relationships with homologs from other plant species, gene structure, and relative transcript abundance. In addition, the full-length coding sequence (CDS) of TgTPS1 was isolated from teak and constitutively expressed in tobacco plants for functional characterization. TgTPS1 -overexpressing lines L3 and L4 showed no major phenotypic differences from wi…

title: Host plant-mediated variation in the biology, morphometric, and nutritional indices of fall armyworm, Spodoptera frugiperda (J.E. Smith) (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae)
abstract: Introduction Maize ( Zea mays L.) is one of the most important cereal crops worldwide because of its high productivity, adaptability, and diverse uses in food, feed, and industrial sectors. Among the insect pests attacking maize, the fall armyworm ( Spodoptera frugiperda J.E. Smith) (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) has emerged as one of the most destructive invasive species worldwide. Methods Evaluated the influence of five host plants, namely maize ( Zea mays ), pearl millet ( Pennisetum glaucum ), sorghum ( Sorghum bicolor ), sugarcane ( Saccharum officinarum ), and banana ( Musa spp.), on the biological performance, morphometric characteristics, and nutritional indices of S. frugiperda under laboratory conditions. The insects were maintained in plastic rearing containers under controlled environmental conditions of 27 ± 2 °C, 65 ± 5% relative humidity, and a 16:8 h (light:dark) photoperiod. Results and discussion Significant differences were observed among host plants for developmental, reproductive, morphometric, and nutritional parameters. The shortest larval duration (13.37 ± 0.36 days), pupal duration (8.00 ± 0.19 days), and total life cycle period (35.88 ± 1.00 days in females) were recorded on maize. In contrast, banana resulted in the longest larval (30.55 ± 0.25 days), pupal (11.08 ± 0.16 days), and total developmental periods (54.59 ± 0.31 days). Fecundity was highest on ma…

title: Plant and nutrient benefits remain despite declining root colonization: Funneliformis mosseae inoculation of perilla under cinnamic acid application
abstract: Introduction Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) can improve plant nutrient acquisition and stress responses, but their effects under allelopathic stress remain incompletely understood. Methods We conducted a pot experiment with perilla ( Perilla frutescens ) inoculated or not inoculated with Funneliformis mosseae and treated once with cinnamic acid solutions at nominal concentrations of 0, 1, or 4 mM. Three independent pots were used per treatment. At maturity, 75 days after a single application, we assessed plant growth, soil properties, enzyme activities, microbial communities, and soil metabolite profiles. Results In non-inoculated plants, cinnamic acid was associated with lower shoot and root dry weights and 100-seed weight, whereas plant height showed a nonmonotonic response. Inoculation was associated with higher shoot dry weight and 100-seed weight at 1 mM and with higher plant height, root dry weight, and 100-seed weight at 4 mM; the shoot dry weight difference at 4 mM was not significant. Available phosphorus and potassium were higher in inoculated than non-inoculated pots at both concentrations. Microbial profiles showed treatment-associated variation in relative abundance, but no genus-level comparison passed false-discovery-rate correction. Pot-level metabolomics retained 191 and 33 features in the 0 and 1 mM contrasts and none at 4 mM after Welch testing and Benjam…

title: Transcriptomic analysis of physiological responses and key metabolic pathways in maize seedlings under NaHCO3 stress
abstract: Introduction Soil salinization-alkalization severely threatens global agriculture. Alkaline salts such as NaHCO 3 inhibit crop growth, reduce yield, and degrade the quality of maize ( Zea mays L.). Most existing maize stress studies focus on salt stress, while the molecular mechanisms underlying alkali tolerance remain largely unclear. Methods Three alkali-tolerant and three alkali-sensitive maize varieties were selected based on prior screening. Seedlings were treated with 80 mM NaHCO 3 to simulate alkali stress. Growth and physiological traits were measured, and transcriptomic analysis was performed using the alkali-tolerant cultivar Liangyu 99 (A) and the alkali-sensitive cultivar Kenyu 90 (B). Results Alkali stress suppressed seedling height and leaf development and reduced biomass accumulation. hysiologically, total chlorophyll (a+b) content declined and relative electrolyte leakage increased. Antioxidant enzyme activities changed more dynamically and remained higher in the tolerant genotype. Transcriptome data showed that Liangyu 99 triggered broad transcriptional reprogramming at the early stage of alkali stress, whereas transcriptional activation was markedly delayed in Kenyu 90. Between the two genotypes, differentially expressed genes (DEGs) showed moderate changes, with more upregulated than downregulated transcripts. GO enrichment indicated that DEGs were enriched i…

title: Financial Inclusion, Peer-to-Peer Lending, and MSME Sustainability: Consumer Trust as a Potential Mediator
abstract: Purpose: This study examines the relationships among financial inclusion, Peer-to-Peer (P2P) lending, consumer trust, and the business sustainability of Micro, Small, And Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).Research Methodology: A descriptive qualitative approach was employed through a narrative literature review of five primary publications. The studies were compared in terms of their research objectives, variables, methods, populations, and findings.Results: The reviewed evidence indicates inconsistent relationships between financial inclusion and business sustainability. P2P lending appears to support business performance, although direct evidence concerning long-term sustainability remains limited. Trust is associated with the acceptance and intended use of digital lending services.Conclusion: Financial access and digital financing may support business continuity when accompanied by appropriate financial management. Consumer trust represents a plausible intervening mechanism, but its mediating role remains empirically unconfirmed.Limitations: The review relies on five purposively selected studies and does not estimate causal relationships or mediation effects.Contributions: The study integrates previously fragmented findings and proposes a conceptual direction for examining trust in financial service providers as a potential mediator of MSME sustainability.

title: Corona-Length Dependence of Equilibrium Fusion and Fragmentation Energy Barriers in Block Copolymer Micelles
abstract: Abstract Fusion and fragmentation are intrinsic dynamic pathways in block copolymer micelles, governing both structural transformations and the transport of solubilized molecules. Yet, how the macromolecular architecture controls their energetic barriers remains poorly understood. In particular, while the influence of the core-forming block has been investigated, the contribution of the corona remains less explored, especially for fusion under equilibrium conditions. Here, this contribution is examined by quantifying equilibrium fusion and fragmentation kinetics in aqueous Pluronic PEO–PPO–PEO micelles from the time-resolved intermicellar exchange of an extremely hydrophobic fluorescent probe. A systematic series of copolymers with comparable PPO block lengths and PEO blocks spanning approximately 17–140 EO units was examined in the spherical-micelle regime and combined with previously reported data for copolymers spanning a broader range of PPO block lengths. Increasing the corona length produces only weak changes in both fusion and fragmentation rates, in marked contrast to the much stronger dependence on core length. The apparent activation energies for fusion and fragmentation are remarkably similar in magnitude and exhibit closely related dependences on block architecture. For both processes, this dependence is described by a common scaling form, ΔEapp ∝ NcoreaNcoronab, wi…

Automated Credit Risk Assessment for Peer-to-Peer Lending Platforms Using Natural Language Processing on Textual Loan Application Data
abstract: Peer-to-Peer (P2P) lending platforms have disrupted traditional consumer credit markets by facilitating direct financial transactions between individual retail investors and borrowers. However, evaluating borrower creditworthiness in P2P lending presents severe information asymmetry challenges, as applicants often lack formal credit histories, audited financial statements, or collateral backing. While traditional credit scoring models rely strictly on quantitative financial metrics (e.g., debt-to-income ratio, FICO score, monthly income), they fail to capture qualitative behavioral signals embedded within borrower-authored loan application narratives. This paper presents an automated, multimodal credit risk assessment architecture that integrates Natural Language Processing (NLP) embeddings, psycholinguistic readability metrics, and sentiment analysis with tabular financial indicators to predict borrower default risk. Grounded in non-linear analytical parameterization paradigms and enterprise risk management frameworks, our methodology extracts semantic, emotional, and deception micro-signals from loan description texts using fine-tuned RoBERTa and TF-IDF representations. Evaluated on an empirical dataset of 320,000 P2P loan applications processed across major fintech lending platforms between 2020 and 2026, our multimodal NLP-enriched model achieved an Area Under the Receiver …

title: A transformer-configuration-aware incremental directional protection scheme for inverter-based resources
abstract: Inverter-based resources (IBRs) supply fault currents that differ fundamentally from those of synchronous generators, challenging conventional protective relays. While prior studies have focused on positive-sequence fault currents, the negative- and zero-sequence responses of IBRs under unsymmetrical faults, and their dependence on transformer winding connections and grounding, remain insufficiently understood. Using real-time electromagnetic transient simulations, we characterize the sequence currents during balanced and unbalanced faults under four transformer winding connections. The positive-sequence current remains below 1.1 p.u., the negative-sequence current stays below 0.07 p.u., and zero-sequence current appears only for ground faults with a grounded Y-connected transformer, leaving conventional protection with little to act on. Building on this analysis, we develop an incremental focused directional protection scheme that compares each voltage and current sample with its value one cycle earlier. Faults are detected from the change ratio of incremental quantities ( K R ) and the maximum absolute incremental angle ( | Δ θ | max ) , and the trip is supervised by a directional condition on the fault-period voltage-current angle, without requiring line impedance data or sequence currents. Simulation results across diverse fault types, transformer connections, and system co…

title: Energy and macronutrient intake and food provision among disaster responders and disaster-affected populations: a systematic review
abstract: Background Natural disasters pose distinct nutritional challenges for disaster responders and disaster-affected populations, underscoring the need for reliable evidence on dietary exposure during emergencies. This systematic review synthesized evidence on energy and macronutrient intake while distinguishing observed dietary intake from food provision. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, five bibliographic databases were searched from inception to September 1, 2026. Grey literature was additionally identified through WHO IRIS, the World Food Programme, ReliefWeb, and Google Scholar. Studies reporting quantitative energy or macronutrient intake or provision during natural disasters were eligible. Given the small number of studies and substantial differences in populations, disaster contexts, assessment periods, and dietary assessment methods, the findings were synthesized narratively. Results Seventeen reports from 11 countries were included. Four studies assessed observed dietary intake among disaster responders, all conducted in wildfire settings. Reported mean energy intake ranged from 2,945 to 3,814 kcal/day for full-day assessments and from 1,494 to 2,195 kcal/work shift for work-shift assessments. Three studies reported individual dietary intake among disaster-affected populations, with mean energy intake ranging from 1,274 to 3,611 kcal/day. Ten reports assessed food prov…

The reshaping effect of digital knowledge stock on corporate energy intensity from the perspective of knowledge governance
abstract: Purpose Drawing on knowledge management theory, this study aims to examine the impact of a firm’s stock of digital knowledge on its energy intensity. This study identifies a dual-pathway model involving realized absorptive capacity and digital-green knowledge integration and analyses the moderating roles of the foundation for objective absorption and the managerial green cognition. Design/methodology/approach Using data on Chinese A-share listed companies from 2012 to 2023, this paper conducts an empirical analysis from three dimensions: main effects, transmission channels and contextual constraints. Findings A company’s stock of digital knowledge can significantly reduce its energy intensity. Realized absorptive capacity and the digital-green knowledge integration act as independent and parallel mediating factors between the two. Both the foundation of objective absorption and the managerial green cognition positively reinforce the energy-saving effects of the stock of digital knowledge. Originality/value This paper extends knowledge management research into the domain of corporate energy use, elucidating the underlying mechanisms through which digital knowledge affects energy intensity and clarifying the contextual conditions that shape this relationship.

title: Quantification of nerve material-composition alterations in trigeminal neuralgia using a combination of dual-energy CT and MRI
abstract: Background To qualitatively assess material composition alterations of the trigeminal nerve in patients with trigeminal neuralgia (TN) using material decomposition techniques and energy spectrum curve slope (λ HU ) calculation in dual-energy CT (DECT), with the aim of advancing understanding of TN pathogenesis. Methods This single-center study enrolled both a control group and a group of patients with TN. DECT images were fused with MRI images for anatomical localization. Quantitative parameters [λ HU , relative water content (WC), and relative fat content (FC)] in DECT were compared between affected and unaffected nerves, and across subgroups (acute vs. chronic, medication only vs. mixed treatment, postoperative pain vs. pain-free). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess diagnostic performance. Results A total of 51 patients with TN (mean age, 65.13 ± 12.89 years; 17 male) and 28 control subjects (mean age, 65.14 ± 13.81 years; 14 male) were included. λ HU values on the affected side of TN patients were smaller than control group, and the WC and FC values were higher ( P < 0.05) in most subgroups. Except for acute and pain groups, WC and FC values of the unaffected side in all TN subgroup were larger than those in the control group ( P < 0.05). Conclusions It is feasible to quantitatively analyze the alterations of material components in…

title: Layer-wise hybrid binary–stochastic computing architecture for energy-efficient diabetes prediction on FPGA
abstract: Stochastic computing encodes numbers as probabilistic bit streams and reduces multiplication to a single logic gate, which makes it an appealing arithmetic substrate for always-on biomedical inference under severe energy constraints. Its accuracy is bounded by two effects usually treated as global properties of a design: the inverse square-root convergence of stream-based estimates, and the systematic bias introduced when operand streams are correlated. This article proceeds from a different observation, namely, that the accuracy cost of stochastic approximation is not distributed uniformly across the layers of a network, and that precision should be allocated where measurement shows it is required. We define a layer-wise stochastic sensitivity metric that isolates the accuracy attributable to mapping each individual layer into the stochastic domain, and develop a partitioning procedure that converts the resulting profile into a hybrid binary–stochastic assignment while reporting the retained fraction of stochastic computation as an explicit hardware-cost proxy. The methodology is demonstrated on an 8–12–8–4–1 fully connected classifier trained on the PIMA Indian Diabetes dataset under a leakage-free preprocessing protocol. Profiling reveals a strongly concentrated sensitivity distribution, the second hidden layer alone accounting for an 11.9 percentage-point accuracy loss whil…

title: Energy Storage Properties of Natural Clinoptilolite-Based Anodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries: Improved Capacity and Stability via Magnesiothermic Reduction
abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate the morphology, chemical composition, and electrochemical performance of natural clinoptilolite subjected to thermal and chemical treatment. Magnesiothermic reduction of this natural zeolite resulted in an increase in the Si/O ratio and the formation of a new crystalline silicon phase. SEM observations showed that the original particle morphology was largely preserved, whereas EDS and XRD confirmed changes in the elemental and phase composition, respectively. The suggested partial reduction of SiO2 was additionally confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), which revealed a substantial decrease in the surface aluminum content and densification of Si species on the modified surface. Electrochemical studies showed that the clinoptilolite-based materials can be used effectively as negative electrodes in lithium-ion batteries. Cyclic voltammetry indicated stable electrochemical properties, with a predominantly capacitive contribution at higher scan rates and a greater contribution from diffusion-controlled processes at lower scan rates. In turn, galvanostatic tests confirmed the high specific capacity, reaching 668 mAh/g for the material after magnesiothermic reduction, with a capacity retention of ∼94% after 1000 cycles. The results indicate the potential use of the tested materials as negative electrodes with high specific capacity …

title: Effects of Intradialytic Aerobic versus Active Range-of-Motion Exercises on Functional Capacity and Cognition in Hemodialysis patients: Randomized clinical Trial
abstract: Introduction: Chronic kidney disease is associated with high morbidity and mortality, and patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis often experience both physical decline and impaired cognitive performance. Because these limitations can affect independence and quality of life, rehabilitation strategies during dialysis are increasingly important. Material and methods: A randomized controlled trial was conducted on 69 patients with end-stage renal disease aged 5060 years. Participants were equally allocated into three groups (n=23 each): Group A performed aerobic exercise using a simple foot-pedal exerciser, selected because it is a practical and low-cost option in our setting, Group B followed an active free ROM program, and Group C received standard care only. Functional capacity was assessed using the 6-minute walk test, and cognitive function was evaluated using the Mini-Cog test. Outcomes were measured at baseline and after 8 weeks of intervention. Results: Both intervention groups experienced statistically significant improvements in 6MWT distance and Mini-Cog scores compared with baseline (p < 0.05), while the control group showed no significant change. Between-group comparisons favored Group A over Group B, with larger mean gains in both 6MWT and Mini-Cog (p < 0.05). Conclusion: Intradialytic aerobic exercise and active free range-of-motion exercises both improved funct…

title: Regional innovation capacity and marine green economic efficiency in China: an empirical analysis using double machine learning
abstract: Introduction The green transformation of the marine economy requires translating innovation resources into energy savings, emission reductions, and more efficient resource use. Whether regional innovation capacity generates such green benefits remains an important question for innovation-led development in coastal regions. This study examines the relationship between regional innovation capacity and marine green economic efficiency in China.​ Methods Using panel data for 11 coastal provincial-level regions in China from 2011 to 2022, this study employs double machine learning to examine the relationship between regional innovation capacity and marine green economic efficiency.​ Results The baseline results reveal a significant positive association between regional innovation capacity and marine green economic efficiency, which remains robust across multiple robustness checks. The mechanism analysis identifies digital talent accumulation, industrial collaboration, and digital technology application as three potential pathways through which regional innovation capacity contributes to marine green economic efficiency. The heterogeneity analysis reveals regional differences across the northern, eastern, and southern coastal regions, with the estimated effect for the eastern coastal region being statistically insignificant. Furthermore, the spatial analysis identifies a significantl…

Why agility is not enough: innovation capacity as the mechanism linking strategic agility to resilience under environmental turbulence
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how strategic agility shapes organisational resilience in the energy sector, focusing on the mediating role of innovation capacity and the moderating role of environmental turbulence within a dynamic capabilities framework. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 808 middle- and senior-level managers of energy organisations in Türkiye were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling. The indirect effect was assessed with bootstrapping and moderation was tested through multi-group analysis. Findings Strategic agility has no significant direct effect on organisational resilience; its influence operates almost entirely through innovation capacity, which strongly predicts resilience. Environmental turbulence weakly conditions the direct path, which is absent under low turbulence and only marginally positive under high turbulence. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional, single-source design limits causal inference and the findings reflect managerial perceptions in one sector and country. Practical implications Agility investments translate into resilience only when routed through innovation capacity, giving managers a basis for sequencing capability investments as environmental conditions change. Social implications Policy makers can strengthen energy organisations’ resilience by supporting innovation capacity,…

abstract: Мета дослідження – обґрунтувати можливість трактування риторичної фігури як механізму культурної пам’яті та простежити шлях від проториторичних моделей до їх барокової кодифікації. Методологічна основа. Застосовано культурологічний, семіотичний, компаративний та історико-типологічний підходи. Теоретичну основу становлять концепції культурної пам’яті Я. Ассмана та П. Коннертона, поняття “Nachleben” та “Pathosformel” А. Варбурга, а також теорія musica poetica, представлена працями Й. Бурмейстера, Й. Маттезона та сучасними дослідженнями Д. Бартеля та М. Е. Бондса. Біблійний сюжет про Вавилонську вежу розглядається як культурологічна модель переходу від уявної єдності мови до множинності способів сакрального вираження. Наукова новизна роботи полягає у трактуванні риторичної фігури як механізму культурної пам’яті, здатного зберігати й транслювати динамічну структуру переживання після зміни первісного контексту. Запропоновано поняття «проториторична структура» на позначення стійких моделей організації руху й переживання, що передують їх теоретичній кодифікації. title: Antithrombotic therapy for patent foramen ovale-associated migraine: mechanism, the COMPETE trial, and patient selection for closure
abstract: Migraine and patent foramen ovale (PFO) co-occur significantly more often than chance, with the strongest association observed in migraine with aura. This overlap has driven two decades of research on a simple question: does the interatrial shunt itself—or the material carried across it—cause the headache? Observational studies have consistently associated PFO closure with a reduced migraine burden. However, three randomized trials—the Migraine Intervention With STARFlex Technology (MIST), the Percutaneous Closure of PFO in Migraine With Aura (PRIMA), and the Prospective Randomized Investigation to Evaluate Incidence of Headache Reduction in Subjects With Migraine and PFO Using the Amplatzer PFO Occluder Compared to Medical Management (PREMIUM)—have all failed to meet their primary endpoints. As a result, PFO closure has received no guideline support for migraines, leaving a significant therapeutic gap and an unresolved mechanistic question: Could a drug, rather than a device, effectively target the same pathway with less risk? The multicenter, open-label Comparison of the Effect of Medication Therapy in Alleviating Migraine With Patent Foramen Ovale (COMPETE) trial has reshaped this debate. Among 1,000 adults with PFO and migraine, aspirin, clopidogrel, and rivaroxaban achieved headache response rates comparable to metoprolol. Rivaroxaban—a direct factor Xa inhibitor—had a res…

title: Modelling reversible sorption as a mechanism for contaminant release from resuspended sediment
abstract: The contamination of lake and river beds is partially driven by sorption, a process in which contaminants adhere to sediment. In this paper, a coupled sediment-contaminant transport model is developed in which sorption is modelled with a first-order kinetic reaction term. The model accounts for exchanges between surface water and an underlying sediment bed through turbulent diffusive fluxes and is validated against laboratory experiments. The model introduces two key dimensionless parameters: the ratio of sorption to sediment suspension time scales ( upper Gamma Γ $\operatorname {\varGamma }$ ), and the ratio of the contaminant and sediment diffusivities ( upper D D $\operatorname {\mathit{D}}$ ). One-dimensional numerical simulations of the erosion of a contaminated sediment layer are used to investigate the influence of the dimensionless parameters, the initial conditions and the volume of eroded sediment. The value of upper Gamma Γ $\operatorname {\varGamma }$ is found to determine the relative importance of desorption and fluxes across the sediment–water interface to increasing the dissolved contaminant concentration in the surface water. The proportion of the dissolved contaminant concentration released into the surface water via desorption is found to depend on the contaminant concentrations in the underlying sediment bed in addition to upper Gamma Γ $\operatorname {\varG…

title: Investigation into the generation and migration mechanism of calcium ions during acidic dissolution of rough-walled carbonate fracture
The “Work in Russia” Platform in the Public Oversight Mechanism For Employment
abstract: The article examines the role of the Unified Digital Platform “Work in Russia” for employment and labor rela-tions in the public oversight mechanism. It focuses on how a state information system can support oversight without acquiring independent public power. The article argues that the digital infrastructure may technological-ly mediate the exercise of public power by performing certain operations of recording, comparing and prelimi-narily analyzing legally relevant data, while legal qualification and authoritative decision-making remain the responsibility of the competent public authority. This approach provides the basis for the author’s concept of a digital oversight signal in the field of employment and explains its public-law nature. The article distinguishes an oversight signal from a statutory risk indicator and proposes a classification of signals according to the type of legal inference they can support. The paper recommends establishing regulatory rules for detecting, verifying, and referring signals to the competent authority, as well as notifying employers before a legally significant de-cision is made. The article emphasizes that the signal is a doctrinal category denoting a verifiable information message that produces no autonomous legal effects, and it also distinguishes aggregate labor-market monitor-ing indicators from oversight signals.

title: 民族地区职业教育与乡村振兴的联动机制构建——以广西职业师范学院为例
abstract: Technical and skilled talent, together with localized vocational teaching staff, constitute an important support for rural revitalization in ethnic regions. Drawing on the practice of Guangxi Vocational Normal University in serving rural revitalization, this paper identifies five forms of linkage: university–locality cooperation, teacher–student service, consumption-based assistance, vocational teacher empowerment, and industry–education integration. It then examines the practical dilemmas involved, including the mismatch between supply and demand, nominal collaboration, a weak teaching workforce, and insufficient local attachment. On this basis, the paper constructs a four-dimensional framework of "government–university–enterprise–village" linkage and proposes optimization paths along six dimensions: institutional supply, actor architecture, program alignment, workforce support, evaluation and incentives, and cultural cultivation. The study finds that the linkage between vocational education and rural revitalization in ethnic regions is moving from "activity-based assistance" toward "institutionalized linkage." Only when periodic assistance campaigns are replaced by routine institutional arrangements can vocational education become an endogenous driver of rural revitalization.

title: Selective Flotation Separation of Celestite from Quartz by a Gemini Anionic Surfactant: Interfacial Adsorption Behavior and Molecular Mechanism
abstract: Abstract Strontium carbonate for cathode-ray tube manufacture is widely produced from celestite. Celestite commonly occurs in association with quartz, while conventional collectors generally exhibit insufficient collecting capacity and selectivity toward celestite. Therefore, achieving efficient separation and purification of celestite and quartz by froth flotation remains challenging. We synthesized sodium bis(decylethoxy) disulfate (SDED), an anionic gemini surfactant. Microflotation tests compared SDED with sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) for the selective recovery of celestite from quartz. At pH = 7 and a collector concentration of 1.5 × 10–5 mol/L, SDED recovered 92.5% of the celestite, compared with 57.5% for SDS. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra indicated preferential adsorption of SDED on celestite. The accompanying increase in contact angle showed that SDED treatment made the celestite surface markedly more hydrophobic. Zeta potential measurements and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) suggested a possible cyclic chelation mechanism involving the −CHOSO3– groups of SDED and surface Sr sites. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations yielded a smaller frontier-orbital gap for SDED (0.158604 au) than for SDS (0.288699 au). The corresponding CLogP values were 7.579 and 4.995. These descriptors suggest greater chemical reactivity and hydrophobicity for SDED.

title: Risk management in times of geopoliticization. The use of mitigation measures in the Italian investment screening mechanism
abstract: Abstract Investment screening mechanisms have become central to economic security and de-risking strategies, yet existing research has largely focused on a limited set of explanatory variables, such as investor country of origin, geopolitical alignment, and sectoral exposure, and has analyzed outcomes through a binary veto versus non-veto lens. This article moves beyond these approaches by conceptualizing investment screening as a risk-management process structured along a continuum from avoidance to resilience. Focusing on Italy’s ISM, it combines an original dataset of 1,055 notified operations with quantitative screening analysis and litigation-based qualitative process tracing to explain how security concerns are translated into differentiated intervention outcomes. Operational configurations are the most consistent correlates of escalation, while geopolitical attributes are associated chiefly with outcomes at the upper end of the intervention spectrum. Moreover, sectoral domains operate as distinct regulatory regimes: 5G converges toward standardized hard-resilience prescriptions, defense displays calibrated escalation, and energy-related activities exhibit more heterogeneous patterns. By reframing investment screening as a form of risk governance rather than a binary security response, the article bridges macro-level de-risking narratives with the micro-architecture of po…

title: A conceptual framework for the application of expressive art therapy in drug regulatory crisis intervention: an exploration based on a goal mechanism
abstract: Drug regulatory crises represent a unique form of public health emergency that not only poses a direct threat to public health and safety but also generates widespread psychological distress, crises of trust, and disruptions to social order. Traditional approaches to crisis intervention primarily rely on the dissemination of authoritative information, medical treatment, and government administration, often paying insufficient attention to the psychological trauma and life challenges resulting from such events. Expressive arts therapy can provide non-verbal avenues for emotional expression and psychological healing for individuals affected by drug regulatory crises through artistic modalities such as music, visual art, dance, poetry, and drama. Accordingly, this study’s primary goal is examining the trauma reconstruction of the public, as well as that of supervision, duty, and other related personnel. Specifically, it considers the mechanisms of non-verbal agglomeration and phased equilibrium as its operating framework to build a three-stage model of drug regulatory crisis intervention. In doing so, it aims to clarify the complete action logic from non-verbal artistic expression to awakening the internal psychological pathway and transforming the expected effect. Through this, it develops a practical theoretical pathway from medical treatment and psychological intervention to so…

title: Drivers of electric vehicle adoption in Brazil
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a contextual extension of UTAUT2 to explain behavioral intention to adopt electric vehicles in Brazil, where institutional signals, economic constraints and psychological barriers influence sustainable consumption. Design/methodology/approach A survey of 660 Brazilian adults assessed UTAUT2 core drivers and additional constructs, including environmental consciousness, personal innovativeness, financial self-efficacy, perceived government incentives, resistance to change and price sensitivity. Covariance-based structural equation modeling estimated structural relationships, and multigroup analyses evaluated heterogeneity across generational cohorts and gender. Findings The proposed model accounted for 79.3% of the variance in behavioral intention. Government incentives served as signals that influenced multiple perceptions, while price sensitivity remained a persistent inhibitor. The significance of effects varied by generational cohort and gender, suggesting that policy and marketing interventions do not have uniform effects across demographic segments. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design and self-reported measures limit causal inference. Future research should use longitudinal and experimental designs and incorporate behavioral outcomes. Practical implications The findings offer insights for designing targeted policie…

title: Interface-Modified Second-Harmonic Generation under Electric and Magnetic Fields in WSe2/CuCrP2S6 Heterostructures
abstract: Abstract Multiferroic van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures provide a promising platform for tailoring the nonlinear optical responses of two-dimensional semiconductors through interfacial interactions. However, how electric and magnetic fields independently modulate second-harmonic generation (SHG) within the same heterostructure remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate electric- and magnetic-field modulation of SHG in monolayer WSe2 interfaced with multiferroic CuCrP2S6 (CCPS). Out of plane magnetic fields reconfigure the SHG intensity and principal polarization axis in Au-grating-supported WSe2/CCPS heterostructures below the Néel temperature of CCPS. Electrical bias modulates the SHG intensity and polarization anisotropy within the same WSe2/CCPS heterostructure. First-principles calculations reveal changes in the interfacial electronic structure of WSe2 between different CCPS polar configurations. These results highlight the potential of multiferroic vdW heterostructures for electric- and magnetic-field modulation of nonlinear optical responses, with implications for tunable frequency conversion and polarization control.

title: A lightweight adaptive dehazing method for unmanned aerial vehicle video
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to address haze-induced degradation in UAV visual perception, a critical risk to operational safety. The authors propose an engineering-aware, lightweight UAV video dehazing strategy. Design/methodology/approach The authors propose a lightweight strategy integrating OpenCL-accelerated CLAHE in the LAB color space to reduce redundancy. The authors further apply configurable spatial downscaling, frame skipping and asynchronous multithreading to balance visual enhancement and runtime. Findings The proposed lightweight method sustained the 30 fps source cadence in the supplied-video replay without queue drops or processing errors. The default configuration processed every second frame, corresponding to a processing completion rate of 15.00 fps, while the isolated offline timing test achieved 745.5 fps under the specified timing procedure. Practical implications In tested environments with Intel integrated graphics, this approach demonstrates high resource utilization while maintaining continuous processing of the input video. The potential advantages of this approach in physical drone control, obstacle avoidance and downstream decision-making still need to be validated through hardware deployment and task-specific benchmarking. Originality/value The authors conducted an experimental evaluation of the proposed method using a paired image quality assessment sc…

title: Electric networks of infection: a hypothesis linking extracellular electron transfer (EET) with bacterial virulence, biofilm resilience, and cross-species cooperation
abstract: EET enables microorganisms to transport electrons beyond the cell envelope through conductive proteins, redox mediators, extracellular DNA (eDNA), and biofilm-associated structures. Although EET was originally characterised in environmental electroactive bacteria, recent discoveries have identified flavin-dependent and other EET mechanisms in clinically relevant microorganisms, including Listeria monocytogenes , Staphylococcus aureus , and Enterococcus faecalis . These findings suggest that EET may contribute to microbial adaptation and survival in host-associated environments characterised by oxygen limitation, oxidative stress, and nutrient restriction. This study advances the hypothesis that chronic and polymicrobial infections function as partially electrically integrated microbial ecosystems in which EET serves as a community-level mechanism linking redox homeostasis, biofilm resilience, metabolic cooperation, and virulence-associated adaptation. Within this framework, direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET) is proposed to operate alongside quorum sensing (QS) and metabolite exchange, facilitating energetic interactions between microbial populations embedded within infection-associated biofilms. Support for this hypothesis derives from four converging lines of evidence: (i) increasing recognition of EET pathways in host-associated microorganisms, (ii) the central role…

ROHIS ULUL ALBAB: PEMBENTUKAN BUDAYA RELIGIUS MELALUI PROGRAM KEAGAMAAN BERKELANJUTAN DI MADRASAH
abstract: ABSTRACT Islamic student organizations (ROHIS) in madrasahs require not only scheduled religious activities but also effective management to maintain student involvement and ensure that evaluation findings lead to improvement. This study aims to analyze the implementation of the ROHIS Ulul Albab program at MAN 1 Gorontalo Regency in supporting the achievement of the madrasah's religious vision. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through non-participant observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation involving the head of the madrasah, ROHIS advisor, organization administrators, Islamic Religious Education teachers, and students who were not members of ROHIS. Data analysis involved data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification, while data trustworthiness was established through source, technique, and time triangulation. The findings indicate that ROHIS management encompasses four dimensions: planning, organizing, implementation, and supervision. Planning was aligned with the madrasah's vision and mission and supported by the formal appointment of advisors and administrators through an official decree. Routine activities were implemented relatively consistently; however, student participation in certain activities remained uneven, and some students lacked readiness to perform religious du…

title: A novel agreement-based pseudo-label filtering strategy for semi-supervised 3D liver segmentation
abstract: Background Liver segmentation from computed tomography (CT) images is crucial for clinical applications such as diagnosis and treatment planning. Manual annotation of large-scale datasets, however, is time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address this, we propose a semi-supervised liver segmentation framework that effectively leverages both labeled and unlabeled data. Methods As part of this framework, we introduce a novel agreement-based pseudo-label filtering mechanism that enhances segmentation performance. Unlike traditional teacher–student frameworks that directly use all teacher-generated pseudo-labels, which may contain noise due to uncertain predictions, our method selects only those predictions where the teacher and student models agree and the teacher's confidence exceeds a predefined threshold. This dual-consensus strategy is the key novelty of our approach and ensures that only highly reliable pseudo-labels contribute to the consistency loss, significantly improving segmentation accuracy and model robustness under limited supervision. We evaluate our method on the LiST and CURVAS datasets. Results Experiments on the LiTS dataset show that our method efficiently leverages unlabeled data and achieves better performance than several existing semi-supervised approaches from recent years. Using 16 labeled data, our method achieved a Dice score of 90.28%, a Jaccard index…

title: The impact of external CEO appointments on firm strategy and risk
abstract: Purpose This paper examines whether chief executive officer (CEO) origin is associated with risk-taking across innovation, financing, and organizational scope; how any difference changes over tenure; and whether the performance consequences differ by risk-taking channel. Design/methodology/approach We build a panel of 55,461 firm-year observations on US publicly traded firms from 2000 to 2024 by combining BoardEx executive histories with Compustat and Center for Research in Security Prices data. We measure risk-taking using three policy variables over which CEOs have substantial influence: research and development (R&D) intensity, leverage, and the number of business segments. We estimate industry- and year-fixed-effects models and supplement them with propensity-score matching and two instrumental variables based on the local supply of executive talent. Findings Firms led by external CEOs have higher R&D intensity, use more leverage, and operate fewer business segments. Matched-sample results are consistent with the baseline estimates, and the instrumental-variable analyses provide broadly similar evidence. The findings are not driven by the global financial crisis or COVID-19. The risk-taking difference generally weakens as external CEOs accumulate tenure. External CEO status is positively associated with Tobin's Q. Strategic refocusing is associated with stronger performance…

Germination as a Strategy to Enhance Functional and Nutraceutical Properties of Indonesian Pigmented Rice Inpari-24
abstract: This study investigated the effect of germination stage (0-48 h) on the morphological development, bioactive compounds, and nutritional quality of Indonesian pigmented rice Inpari-24. The root and shoot lengths of rice seeds increased progressively, with roots showing more rapid elongation, reaching ~30 mm at 48 h compared to ~12 mm for shoots. γ-Aminobutyric acid (GABA) content increased markedly from 8.29 to 90.28 mg/100 g dry basis (db), peaking at 48 h, while phytic acid decreased from 0.11 to 0.03 g/100g db. Antioxidant activity rose from 245.70 to 369.04 mg ascorbic acid equivalent (AAE)/100 g db at 36 h before declining sharply at 48 h, while total phenolic content increased modestly from 137.46 to 154.63 mg gallic acid equivalent (GAE)/100 g db within 12 h, remained stable until 36 h, and decreased to 105.64 mg at 48 h. In contrast, anthocyanin content declined continuously from 0.91 to 0.29 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside equivalents (C-3-GE)/100 g db. These results indicated that an optimal germination time of 12-36 h maximizes antioxidant activity, total phenolic content, and GABA accumulation, reduces phytic acid, and supports early seedling development while minimizing losses in anthocyanin content.

title: Intercalation Strategy of Macromolecular Conductive Agent for Constructing High-Performance V2O5·3H2O Cathode in Zinc Metal Batteries
abstract: Abstract As renewable energy technologies and energy storage systems advance, rechargeable zinc metal batteries are increasingly becoming a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries. However, the reported vanadium oxide cathodes of zinc metal batteries usually suffer from problems such as low intrinsic conductivity, sluggish diffusion kinetics of Zn2+, and susceptibility to structural collapse during cycling. To address these challenges, a macromolecular conductive agent has been introduced to enhance the interlayer spacing and electrical conductivity of vanadium oxide cathode materials. This work introduces modified poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene): poly(styrenesulfonate) into V2O5·3H2O interlayers via a hydrothermal method. Characterization results demonstrate that the intercalation of the macromolecular conductive agent effectively enlarges the interlayer spacing of V2O5·3H2O, thereby facilitating Zn2+ diffusion and enhancing electrochemical activity. The optimized composite cathode has preferable cycling performance. With a specific capacity of 112.1 mAh g–1 even at a high current density of 2.0 A g–1, it still exhibits excellent performance after 1200 cycles, achieving long cycle performance of vanadium-based cathode materials. Meanwhile, the ionic diffusion kinetics of the composite has also been improved, and the order of magnitude of DZn2+ can reach 10–6 to 10–5 cm…

title: ISNCC Palliative Care Position Statement
Professional and educational development for person-centred care and shared decision making in the integrated care system: the concept of power
abstract: Purpose Person-centred care is a crucial component of realising the aspirations of integrated care systems, ensuring service users receive interventions tailored to their needs and efficient utilisation of health and social care resource occurs. To effectively achieve person-centred care, practitioners and leaders within integrated care systems are recommended to engage in processes of shared decision making through individual and collective stakeholder engagement, maximising the opportunity afforded by the legislation of integrated care systems in England and the necessary redesign of services to align provision with the needs of local communities and care recipients. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper presents the principles of person-centred care, shared decision making and stakeholder engagement through an ethical and values-based practice lens, advocating for the recognition of and redistribution of professional power to recipients of care as a cornerstone for effective practice within integrated care systems and as a core component for the development and education of health and social care practitioners. Findings The discussion conceptualises person-centred care and shared decision making as stakeholder engagement processes within integrated care systems and advocates for user empowerment as an essential activity for improving outcomes for individuals, the…

Phenotype-blind by design: definition drift and power erosion in sepsis trials
abstract: Background Sepsis definitions evolved through Sepsis-2 and Sepsis-3, while subphenotyping research expanded and control mortality declined. Yet the sepsis trial ecosystem has not been examined as a system. Methods Registry-linked meta-research, frozen 15 September 2026, screened 5,397 ClinicalTrials.gov records from five condition queries, identifying 2,291 unique registrations and 868 adult sepsis trial families. Definitions, enrichment, endpoints and visibility were coded using prespecified rules. Wilson intervals, Cochran-Armitage tests, Kaplan–Meier methods and competing-risk (Aalen-Johansen) estimation were used, with termination and withdrawal modelled as competing events for disclosure. The corpus is limited to ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed, and power benchmarks are illustrative constants rather than trial-specific calculations. Results SIRS language declined from 17.9% (2001-2015) to 4.5% (2016+), while SOFA language increased from 2.1% to 20.5%; “severe sepsis” persisted in 7.2%. Only 6.8% specified a SOFA threshold under the prespecified rule (10.4% when Unicode ≥ forms were matched), indicating lexical change without operational convergence. Biological enrichment occurred in 5.5% of families versus 44.5% using clinical-severity enrichment, and was not associated with mortality-primary trials ( p = 0.44). Mortality was the primary endpoint in 35.9% of families (312/86…

title: Platform power, epistemic influence, and algorithmic meaning-making: a structural analysis of TikTok's communication effects in Indonesia
abstract: This study investigates how TikTok's recommendation algorithm operates as a structure of epistemic power in Indonesia—shaping not merely what users see, but what they come to believe and how they interpret social reality. Using structural equation modeling (SEM) with 300 Indonesian TikTok users (aged 18–35), the study tests a four-construct model—algorithmic exposure, engagement, meaning construction, and perception—that positions platform architecture as a constitutive force in public knowledge formation. Results confirm that algorithmic exposure strongly drives engagement ( β = 0.61, p < .001), engagement facilitates meaning construction ( β = 0.54, p < .001), and meaning construction exerts the most powerful effect on perception ( β = 0.67, p < .001). Critically, algorithmic exposure also directly shapes perception ( β = 0.22, p < .01), suggesting that platform-controlled repetition can bypass deliberative cognition—a finding with significant implications for epistemic autonomy in Indonesia's algorithm-saturated media landscape. Mediation analysis reveals that meaning construction accounts for 62.2% of the engagement–perception pathway, establishing it as the primary mechanism through which algorithmic platforms colonize audience cognition. Building on these empirical findings, the study proposes the Platform Epistemic Influence (PEI) Framework—a three-layered mo…
