Unlocking the Protective Power of Sinomenine: How It Alleviates LPS-Induced Cardiomyocyte Inflammatory Injury Partially Through an Nrf2-Dependent Pathway
abstract: Background: Myocarditis is an inflammatory cardiomyopathy characterized by cardiomyocyte injury, oxidative stress, and immune dysregulation. Sinomenine, a naturally occurring alkaloid with established anti-inflammatory properties, has been reported to have cardioprotective benefits. However, its underlying molecular mechanisms in myocarditis remain unclear. This study examined the effects and mechanisms of sinomenine in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced cardiomyocyte injury. Methods: An in vitro model of LPS-induced cardiomyocyte inflammatory injury was established using LPS treatment, with or without sinomenine pre-treatment. We evaluated the effects of sinomenine on cell viability, apoptosis, reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) pathway in this cellular model using cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8), flow cytometry, Western blotting, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and immunofluorescence. In addition, we investigated the role of the Nrf2 pathway in the protective effects of sinomenine against myocardial cell injury through Nrf2 silencing. Results: Sinomenine significantly alleviated the LPS-induced reduction in cell viability while suppressing apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses (p < 0.05). In particular, sinomenine reduced the…

title: Theory X in a High-Power Distance Culture: The Effect of Micromanagement on Workforce Productivity
abstract: Micromanagement is frequently used to maintain quality and reduce errors in Nigeria's volatile manufacturing sector, yet its long-term implications for employee productivity remain contested. Drawing on Theory X, Theory Y, and self-determination theory as the guiding theoretical lens, this study examined how excessive supervision, lack of autonomy, and detailed reporting affect employee productivity among permanent staff at Vitafoam Nigeria PLC, Ikeja. Whereas earlier Nigerian studies such as Iro et al. (2019) and Ndidi et al. (2021) examined micromanagement and performance in broad, aggregate terms without isolating specific control dimensions at the firm level, this study disaggregated micromanagement into three distinct dimensions within a single large manufacturing firm to provide a more focused explanation of how specific control practices shape workforce productivity in a high power distance setting. The study adopted a quantitative descriptive survey design. Data were collected from 230 permanent employees selected through stratified random sampling, with 219 usable responses, representing a response rate of 95.2 per cent. Multiple regression analysis showed that the three micromanagement dimensions jointly accounted for 61.2 per cent of the variation in employee productivity, and the overall regression model was statistically significant. Excessive supervision and lack …

title: AI-enabled HR practices and employee-perceived customer experience outcomes in retail services: the mediating role of frontline employee engagement
abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in human resource (HR) functions is transforming how retail service organizations manage frontline employees and deliver customer experiences. Although previous studies have examined AI in HR primarily in terms of efficiency and cost, limited research has explored its association with customer experience-related outcomes through employee processes. This study examines the relationship between AI-enabled HR practices and customer experience outcomes in retail services, focusing on the mediating role of frontline employee engagement. Drawing on social exchange theory, the study proposes that AI-enabled HR practices, including AI-based performance feedback, personalized training, and intelligent workforce scheduling, are associated with stronger frontline employee engagement. The proposed relationships were examined using cross-sectional survey data from 242 frontline retail employees through structural equation modeling. Customer service quality and customer satisfaction were assessed from employees’ perceptions of customer-facing service outcomes rather than direct customer responses. Results indicate positive associations between AI-enabled HR practices and frontline employee engagement, and between engagement and employee-perceived customer service quality and satisfaction. Bootstrapped mediation analysis further indicates s…

title: Financial Distress in Indonesian Retail Companies: Prediction Model Performance and Financial and Macroeconomic Determinants
abstract: Financial distress poses risks to Indonesian retail companies amid changing sales conditions and financial pressures, making early detection reliable and timely. This study compares the classification performance of the Altman Z-Score, Zmijewski X-Score, and Grover G-Score against a Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) benchmark and examines how fundamental and macroeconomic factors affect distress. A quantitative approach uses secondary quarterly data from 19 companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024, yielding 380 observations. Model performance is evaluated using confusion matrices and classification metrics, followed by random-effects panel regressions with robust standard errors using DSCR and the best-performing model’s score as dependent variables. Zmijewski performs best, with 81.3% accuracy, 78.4% balanced accuracy, and a 40.0% false negative rate. DAR is negatively associated with DSCR, while TATO is positively associated with DSCR; ROA is positive at the 10% significance level. Firm size is negatively associated with the Zmijewski score. CR, GDP, and the BI Rate are not significant in the respective models, while inflation is positively associated with DSCR only. The findings support combining model-based screening with financial and macroeconomic monitoring.

title: Enhancing Pricing Accuracy and Cost Efficiency Through Full Costing: Evidence from an Indonesian Culinary MSME
abstract: Reliable product-cost information is important for culinary micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), yet simplified costing records may omit shared manufacturing overhead and overstate the margin available for pricing decisions. Previous full-costing case studies primarily compare calculated production costs, leaving the distinction between more complete cost recognition and observed improvements in pricing or efficiency insufficiently established. This study reconstructs March 2025 manufacturing costs for three products at Pempek Feri Palembang using a descriptive documentary comparison of enterprise-reported costs and full-cost estimates. Company-method costs total IDR 14,456,000 across adaan, lenjer, and telur, compared with IDR 15,531,715 under full costing, an increase of IDR 1,075,715 (7.44%). The product-level increases are IDR 378,207 (7.57%), IDR 397,113 (8.37%), and IDR 300,395 (6.37%), respectively. Against reported revenue of IDR 46,550,000, illustrative gross margins decline from 68.95% to 66.63% if period production cost is assumed equal to cost of goods sold. These findings demonstrate a more inclusive accounting cost base, not observed changes in actual selling prices or physical production efficiency. The case contributes an evidence-bounded distinction between manufacturing-cost completeness, price-setting information, and realized operating outcomes.

title: Merchant live-streaming or influencer live-streaming? Pricing and strategic analysis of storable products
abstract: Purpose Storable products constitute a significant portion of live-streaming e-commerce. Consumers are enticed to stockpile such products during live-streaming, which boosts immediate volume but inevitably cannibalizes subsequent regular sales. Furthermore, the disparities in pricing power, traffic reach and cost structures between different live-streaming modes (i.e. influencer and merchant live-streaming) shape consumer stockpiling and retailers' profits, necessitating a rigorous exploration into the optimal strategy selection and pricing decisions. Design/methodology/approach A two-period game-theoretic model is developed to depict consumer stockpiling, consisting of a live-streaming period and a subsequent regular sales period. The optimal live-streaming strategy and pricing decisions is obtained by backward induction. Findings The results reveal that influencers may intentionally lower prices to induce stockpiling when storage costs are low, which can cannibalize the retailer's regular period sales to zero. In contrast, merchant live-streaming typically involves equivalent pricing across periods to deter stockpiling. Interestingly, the retailer may choose influencer collaboration even if it leads to negative profits during the live-streaming period, provided the influencer's traffic expansion significantly boosts the long-term market scale. Furthermore, the retailer's ince…

title: Development of Web-Based Learning Media for Teaching Trigonometric Ratios to Grade X Students
abstract: Teaching trigonometric ratios remains challenging because students often struggle with abstract concepts, conventional instruction predominates, and digital learning resources are underused. This study developed a Google Sites learning resource for teaching trigonometric ratios to tenth-grade students at MAS TI Batang Kabung and evaluated its validity and practicality. The study followed the 4D development model (Define, Design, Develop, and Disseminate) and involved one mathematics teacher and 25 tenth-grade students in a product trial. Data were collected through observations, interviews, documentation, and validation and practicality questionnaires, then analyzed using descriptive quantitative and qualitative techniques. Expert validation scores for content and media were 91.07% and 92.11%, respectively, both classified as highly valid. Practicality scores were 93.42% from the teacher and 86.26% from the students, yielding an overall mean of 89.84%, classified as highly practical. The resource brings together instructional materials, illustrations, videos, exercises, and assessments on a single website. The validity and practicality ratings support its use as a structured digital resource for teachers and students that offers flexible access to trigonometry materials and activities.

title: GrowGen: stable property-conditioned molecular generation using a decoder-only Transformer and reinforcement learning
abstract: Introduction Generative AI for molecule design has gained attention for its potential to create new scaffolds, but aligning stability optimization and property conditioning with chemical principles and drug-like properties remains challenging. Methods We present GrowGen, a decoder-only Transformer using rotary position embedding (RoPE) with property conditioning via descriptor embeddings and policy-gradient reinforcement learning. Physicochemical descriptors were computed with RDKit, normalized, and introduced as additive global conditioning embeddings. Supervised pretraining on SMILES was followed by Monte-Carlo REINFORCE fine-tuning, with reward scoring computed from molecular validity, global uniqueness and the quantitative estimate of drug-likeness (QED). Generation used temperature-based and nucleus sampling. The framework was evaluated on GDB13rand, MOSES and ZINC. Results Reinforcement learning increased average QED while maintaining chemical validity above 80%, uniqueness above 90% and novelty above 99%. Direct validation of property-conditioning accuracy against specific target values was dataset-dependent – strong on MOSES, moderate on ZINC, and a limitation on the smaller GDB13rand dataset. Controlled ablations showed that the discrete drug-like/non-drug-like token already captures most of the conditioning mechanism’s steering effect, with the continuous descriptor p…

title: Learning Flexible Correlations in Gaussian Processes for Structured Categorical Inputs
abstract: Abstract. Gaussian process (GP) models are widely used for prediction and uncertainty quantification in computer experiments and scientific applications. However, most mixed-input GP methods treat categorical variables as flat factors, ignoring the grouped or hierarchical organization that frequently arises in practice. We propose the Unrestrictive Correlation Gaussian Process Model for Grouped Factors (UC-Grouped), a flexible kernel construction for mixed inputs with structured categorical factors. UC-Grouped decomposes categorical dependence into two interpretable components: a correlation matrix across groups and block-diagonal correlation matrices for levels within groups. These components are combined through a positive semidefinite convex mixture with a learnable weight, allowing the model to adaptively balance cross-group similarity and within-group heterogeneity. Both correlation layers are parameterized using a hyperspherical construction that guarantees valid correlation matrices while enabling rich, nonexchangeable dependence patterns. Across controlled simulation studies, UC-Grouped often achieves the best predictive, interval, and scoring-rule performance, with its clearest gains when both group-level and within-group level effects are present. A real application to airfoil self-noise data shows that UC-Grouped gives the best average predictive and scoring-rule per…

title: Internet-based learning adaptability and dual-factor model of mental health in older adults: the mediating role of basic psychological need satisfaction
abstract: Older adults currently face the digital divide. To address this disparity, studies on older adults have gradually shifted from focusing on internet use behaviors to examining individual characteristics of internet-based learning. However, older adults’ adaptability to internet-based learning environments remains underexplored. This study examined the relationships among older adults’ internet-based learning adaptability, basic psychological need satisfaction, and dual-factor of mental health. A total of 1,069 older adults (692 females and 377 males) from China participated in the study. Questionnaires were used to assess older adults’ internet-based learning adaptability (internet use, attitudes toward internet-based learning, satisfaction with internet-based learning, self-efficacy in internet-based learning, and sense of control over internet-based learning), basic psychological need satisfaction, negative indicators of mental health (depression, anxiety, loneliness, and subjective cognitive decline) and positive indicators of mental health (social adaptation and attitudes toward aging). A path analysis indicated that internet-based learning adaptability was positively associated with basic psychological need satisfaction and positive mental health indicators, and negatively associated with negative mental health indicators. Additionally, basic psychological need satisfaction…

title: TL-PCNN: Transfer Learning-enabled Advanced Parallel CNN with score-level fusion for Parkinson's disease detection using MRI images
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative condition that demands early and accurate diagnosis to enhance patient care and treatment effectiveness. However, diagnosing the condition in its early stages is still tough as its symptoms often overlap with those of other neurological disorders. Hence, this study proposes a novel Transfer Learning-enabled Advanced Parallel CNN-based Parkinson's disease Detection (TL-APC-PD) framework that uses magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and combines advanced image processing and deep learning techniques. The framework begins with preprocessing MRI images through Gaussian filtering to suppress noise and improve overall image quality. Subsequently, both deep and texture features are extracted to capture a wide range of image characteristics. Deep features are learned using pre-trained convolutional neural network models such as Residual Network (ResNet) and Visual Geometry Group 16 (VGG16), while texture-based features are obtained using Local Ternary Tree Pattern (LTTP) and Log-Gabor Filter with Adaptive Threshold-based Median Ternary Pattern (LFAT-MTP) techniques. These features are then classified using the Top-k max average pooling-based parallel convolutional neural network (TkMAP-PCNN) and the ShuffleNet models. To further boost classification accuracy and robustness, an Adaptive Normalization-based Score Level Fusion (AN-S…

Functional hearing difficulty and digital-resource gradients in foundational learning across diverse MICS6 settings
abstract: Prior MICS6 research has documented hearing-related reading disadvantages and mixed numeracy findings, but existing analyses differ in outcome definitions and geographic coverage. We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of 17 MICS6 country-survey datasets identified by reference years 2017–2019 (some fieldwork extending into 2020), examining functional hearing difficulty and household digital resources in relation to directly assessed foundational reading and numeracy. Outcomes were independently reconstructed and compared with published official survey estimates using a prespecified 0.5-percentage-point validation gate; unresolved combinations were excluded without recalibration. Validated source samples comprised 15 reading surveys (84,975 children) and 15 numeracy surveys (78,311), with 13 validated for both. Weighted linear probability models with country fixed effects and PSU-clustered standard errors estimated adjusted probability differences. Higher-severity hearing difficulty was associated with lower reading (−10.68 percentage points; 95% CI −16.43–−4.92) and numeracy (−5.53; −9.95–−1.11). Internet access was associated with higher reading (+5.00; 3.82–6.19) and numeracy (+4.87; 3.68–6.06); computer/tablet associations were +8.37 and +6.73 points, respectively. Hearing–reading was comparatively stable, whereas hearing–numeracy was less precise in alternative …

title: Two-instrument da Vinci SP cholecystectomy through a 2-cm incision: learning curve in 193 consecutive cases by a surgeon experienced in reduced-port laparoscopy
abstract: Abstract Using three da Vinci SP (single port) instruments requires an umbilical incision of at least 2.5 cm, which reduces the SP cosmetic advantage. This study describes a two-instrument floating-docking technique that keeps the incision at 2 cm and assessed its learning curve. Consecutive SP cholecystectomies ( N = 193) by a single surgeon with prior experience of approximately 825 two-port cholecystectomies were reviewed. Only Cadiere forceps and monopolar cautery were used, with fundus-first dissection and confirmation that the cystic duct was the only tubular structure entering the gallbladder before clipping. Learning curves were plotted using cumulative sum analysis, and because the curves plateaued the change point was determined by least-squares partitioning. Mean total operative time was 34.9 ± 10.5 min, and console time was 15.8 ± 6.6 min. An additional 5-mm port was placed in 4 patients (2.1%), without open conversion. Complications occurred in 8 (4.1%), all ≤ Clavien–Dindo grade II, without bile duct injury, major complications, readmission to our institution, or death. Least-squares partitioning identified the same change point of 24 cases for both measures. Thereafter console time decreased by 38% and total operative time by 34% (both p < 0.001) and continued to decrease beyond case 100. Acute cholecystitis and wall thickening did not differ between phases, prev…

title: Precise deep-learning reconstruction of galaxy cluster mass maps and substructures from optical observations
abstract: Accurately mapping the total mass distribution within galaxy clusters, including dark matter, is fundamental to understanding structure formation and constraining cosmological parameters. Standard mass mapping relies almost exclusively on gravitational lensing, which often yields smooth distributions based on analytical profiles, thereby missing critical internal substructures. We introduce a complementary, simulation-based inference approach to reconstruct detailed galaxy cluster mass maps and resolve internal substructures directly from optical imaging. We trained deep learning models on realistic hydro-simulated galaxy clusters to interpret observed cluster images. This framework was then applied to observations of real galaxy clusters obtained by the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) as part of the Cluster Lensing And Supernova survey with Hubble (CLASH) program. The reconstructed mass maps successfully reproduce the overall shapes and radial mass profiles of the CLASH clusters, showing strong agreement with independent gravitational lensing measurements. Using the subhalos derived from these reconstructed maps, we find that their mass functions exhibit a power-law behavior broadly consistent with predictions from numerical simulations. Our results demonstrate that combining optical imaging with deep learning provides a scalable, physically meaningful approach to mapping cluster…

title: Internalizing Love-Based Curriculum Values in Akidah Akhlak Learning: Strategies and Challenges in Madrasah
abstract: This study aims to analyze the strategies used in internalizing Love-Based Curriculum values in Akidah Akhlak learning at MTs Cijawura Kota Bandung. A qualitative case study design was employed involving one Akidah Akhlak teacher, one madrasah leader, and five students from Grades VII and VIII. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, observation, and documentation and analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing or verification. The findings show that Love-Based Curriculum values were internalized through integrated pedagogical strategies combining value-based lesson planning, differentiated and joyful learning, dialogical interaction, teacher role modeling, habituation, reflection, and behavioral observation. The internalized values covered spiritual, personal, social, intellectual, environmental, and national dimensions. The process was strengthened by institutional support, religious habituation, positive madrasah culture, teacher exemplarity, and student participation. Inhibiting factors were related to limited learning time, student diversity and discipline, as well as external influences from peers, family backgrounds, and social media. These findings indicate that the internalization of Love-Based Curriculum values requires an integrated educational environment that co…

title: iFCM-FL: incremental fuzzy c-means clustering-based federated learning under intermittent client participation
abstract: Clustered federated learning provides each client with a model assembled from the same cluster it belongs to. In clustered federated learning, client participation is intermittent, and clients that do not participate in a communication round receive no updated cluster membership information and must rely on the membership values retained from their most recent participation. This study focuses on these outdated memberships. In hard clustering, an incorrect assignment causes the client to receive a model from an inappropriate cluster, whereas fuzzy memberships preserve partial association with the correct cluster, potentially reducing the impact of such misalignment. To address this challenge, we investigate incremental fuzzy c-means clustering-based federated learning (iFCM-FL), which clusters principal component analysis (PCA)-reduced client model updates and maintains temporal membership consistency by aligning clusters across consecutive rounds using the Hungarian matching algorithm, followed by temporal membership smoothing. Experiments on rotated Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology digit dataset (MNIST) with 20 clients across four rotation groups, 50% client participation, and five random seeds demonstrate that temporal membership smoothing improves training stability under intermittent participation. An ablation shows that smoothing reduces accuracy dr…

title: Glucose-to-albumin ratio predicts major adverse cardiovascular events after non-cardiac surgery: a two-cohort study with external validation of machine learning models
abstract: Background The glucose-to-albumin ratio (GAR) has emerged as a novel prognostic biomarker in various clinical settings, but its association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after non-cardiac surgery and its value in machine learning (ML) prediction have not been validated. Methods This retrospective study included patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery from the MOVER and INSPIRE cohort. The primary outcome was MACE occurring within 30 days after surgery during the index hospitalization. The association between GAR and MACE was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Six ML models were developed by 5-fold stratified cross-validation internally (MOVER) and subsequently validated externally (INSPIRE). SHAP analysis was applied to the best-performing model to interpret the contribution of each predictor to the outcome prediction. Results Among 8,098 patients in the MOVER cohort, MACE occurred in 394 (4.9%), while among 75,971 patients in the INSPIRE cohort, it occurred in 902 (1.2%). Multivariable analyses indicated that per SD increase in GAR significantly correlated with MACE in both MOVER (OR = 1.15, 95% CI = 1.06–1.25) and INSPIRE (OR = 1.12, 95% CI = 1.07–1.18) cohorts. As a categorical variable, high GAR level remained associated with MACE in both MOVER (OR = 1.69, 95% CI = 1.32–2.17) and INSPIRE (OR = 1.30, 95% CI = 1.08–1.56) cohorts. Among 6 ML m…

title: Potential under siege: palestinians faculty perspectives on underachievement, trauma, and AI-supported learning among high-potential students in Gaza
abstract: Introduction Underachievement has traditionally been examined through individual, familial, and school-based explanations, but less is known about how it emerges amid war, educational destruction, displacement, and digital disruption. This study explored Palestinian university faculty perspectives on underachievement among high-potential students during and following the 2023-2025 war on Gaza. Methods This qualitative exploratory study employed semi-structured interviews with nine Palestinian university faculty members. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Six themes were identified: (1) trauma, hardship, and disrupted learning capacity; (2) digital continuity with limited effectiveness; (3) AI as conditional support; (4) technology-supported recovery; (5) infrastructure and digital inequality; and (6) flexible models for recovery. Faculty interpreted declining academic performance as reflecting disrupted opportunities to develop and demonstrate potential rather than diminished ability. Digital platforms provided limited educational continuity, while infrastructural inequalities constrained participation. Participants distinguished existing AI applications, including explanation, summarization, and writing support, from proposed applications for educational recovery, such as adaptive feedback, progress monitoring, and mentoring. Discussion The findings …

title: Machine learning model predicting intracranial aneurysm rupture based on systemic immune-inflammation index: a retrospective development and validation study
abstract: Background and objective Early identification of ruptured intracranial aneurysms remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning (ML) model based on Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) for predicting aneurysm rupture. Methods A retrospective study enrolled 311 patients with intracranial aneurysms (194 unruptured, 117 ruptured). A three-tiered feature selection framework (univariate analysis, Boruta algorithm, LASSO regression) was employed. Four machine learning algorithms [Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVC), gradient boosting machine (GBM)] were trained on 70% of the data and validated on the remaining 30%. Model performance was evaluated by AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. SHAP analysis was used for interpretability. Results Univariate analysis identified SII, glucose (GLU), fibrinogen (FIB), creatinine (Cr), uric acid (UA), and aneurysm location as significant predictors ( P < 0.05). Among the four models, GBM exhibited optimal performance (AUC = 0.983, 95% CI 0.959–0.999), followed by RF (AUC = 0.967), LR (AUC = 0.947), and SVC (AUC = 0.939). SHAP analysis revealed SII as the most important predictor, with a non-linear positive correlation between SII and rupture risk. Conclusions The gradient boosting machine (GBM) model demonstrated superior predictive efficacy for intracranial an…

title: IMAP-FL: an intelligent multi-agent privacy-preserving framework for federated learning combining client-side differential privacy and secure aggregation
abstract: Federated learning (FL) allows hospitals to train a shared diagnostic model without pooling patient data, but client updates can still leak information through gradient inversion and membership inference, and adversarial clients can degrade the model through poisoning. Differential privacy (DP) and secure aggregation (SecAgg) address different aspects of this problem: DP limits what the trained model and transmitted updates reveal about any single training record, while SecAgg conceals each client's update from the server. We present IMAP-FL, an Intelligent Multi-Agent Privacy-Preserving framework for Federated Learning that integrates client-side DP-SGD, Bonawitz-inspired pairwise masking, and agent-level privacy-budget management in a zero-trust setting. The contribution is an architectural integration of established mechanisms rather than a new privacy primitive. We prove record-level (ε,δ)-DP for a fixed noise schedule using Rényi DP accounting; the adaptive, validation-loss-driven scheduler used in the main experiments is evaluated empirically and is not covered by this guarantee. Experiments use the three-class COVID-19 Radiography Dataset (15,153 chest X-rays) split across five simulated hospital clients with a Dirichlet non-IID partition. title: Deep learning–based ECG analysis for predicting heart failure with improved ejection fraction: a multimodal late fusion study
abstract: Background HFimpEF, defined as LVEF >40% with a ≥10-point increase from prior HFrEF, affects about 30% of patients but carries relapse risk. Baseline prediction could guide management, yet no validated ECG-based tool exists. We evaluated ECG–clinical prediction of LVEF improvement. Methods A retrospective two-center cohort of 819 patients (299 improved, 520 non-improved) with baseline 12-lead ECG waveforms and clinical variables was assembled. ECG features were extracted by a pretrained one-dimensional residual network encoder. Five models—clinical-only, ECG-only, early fusion, clinical–ECG late fusion, and clinical–ECG–measurement fusion—were compared under a shared five-fold out-of-fold prediction framework. Discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and center-stratified performance were evaluated. Results The ECG-only model (AUROC: 0.766, AUPRC: 0.660) outperformed the clinical-only model (AUROC: 0.656, AUPRC: 0.511). The clinical–ECG fusion model achieved the highest AUROC (0.800; 95% CI: 0.767–0.832), while the clinical–ECG–measurement model achieved the highest AUPRC (0.713; 95% CI: 0.668–0.758); adding ECG machine measurements yielded minimal incremental benefit. Calibration analysis revealed residual probability bias requiring recalibration. Decision curve analysis confirmed positive net benefit across a broad threshold range. Center-stratified performanc…

title: Peningkatan Kemampuan Menulis Puisi melalui Metode Quantum Learning pada Siswa Kelas XI C SMA Negeri 1 Tayan Hilir Tahun Ajaran 2025/2026
abstract: Abstrak: Menulis puisi menuntut siswa memadukan kompetensi kebahasaan, imajinasi, dan kepekaan estetis, sedangkan hasil pengamatan awal di kelas XI C SMA Negeri 1 Tayan Hilir menunjukkan bahwa banyak siswa masih kesulitan mengembangkan ide, memilih diksi, dan menggunakan gaya bahasa. Penelitian terdahulu telah membahas pembelajaran aktif dan kreatif, namun bukti berbasis tindakan kelas mengenai peningkatan bertahap kemampuan menulis puisi siswa sekolah menengah melalui Quantum Learning masih terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan penerapan metode tersebut dan menganalisis peningkatan kemampuan menulis puisi siswa. Penelitian menggunakan tindakan kelas model Kemmis dan McTaggart pada 33 siswa dalam tiga siklus. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, tes unjuk kerja, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis secara kuantitatif dan kualitatif. Nilai rata-rata meningkat dari 66,82 pada pra siklus menjadi 73,18, 80,18, dan 90,00, sedangkan ketuntasan klasikal meningkat dari 27,27% menjadi 54,55%, 69,70%, dan 90,91%. Kebaruan penelitian terletak pada integrasi siklik media gambar, musik instrumental, diskusi, umpan balik, dan presentasi karya untuk memperkuat latihan menulis puisi.

title: Green finance investments in the era of geopolitical uncertainty: moderation and mediation effects
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effects of environmental knowledge, corporate social responsibility (CSR) scepticism and media intervention on willingness to invest in green finance products (WGF) through the mediation of greenwashing perception. Furthermore, the study examines the moderating role of geopolitical uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 372 Islamic Bank customers via a questionnaire and evaluated using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings The study reported a positive relationship between environmental knowledge, CSR scepticism, media intervention and greenwashing perception. In addition, the results show a negative relationship between greenwashing perception and WGF. Furthermore, geopolitical uncertainty negatively moderated the relationship between greenwashing perception and WGF. Practical implications This study proposes pragmatic approaches for Islamic banks to enhance the adoption of green finance and effectively tackle greenwashing amid geopolitical uncertainty. By implementing focused sustainability education, individuals are empowered to make well-informed investment decisions and better understand greenwashing. Engaging in collaborative media initiatives and employing transparent marketing strategies can bolster trust among environmentally conscious customers, increasing their involvement in susta…

Firm-level economic policy uncertainty, corporate finance and bank intermediation
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how firm-level economic policy uncertainty (EPU) shapes corporate financial decisions and transmits to banks, quantifying how much of banks’ response runs indirectly – through borrowers’ and depositors’ balance sheets – rather than through banks’ own reaction. Design/methodology/approach Firm-level EPU is measured from the textual content of 10-K MD&A disclosures and instrumented, in an IV-GMM framework, using industry exposures to macroeconomic volatility factors together with a regulatory-intensity alternative. Log–log elasticities are estimated on a 1994–2023 panel of US firms (Compustat) and banks (Call Reports) with firm/bank and year fixed effects. A geographic mediation framework, built on a two-tier FDIC Summary of Deposits × QCEW weighting, links firms to regional banks; heterogeneity, robustness checks and a COVID-19 event study complement the analysis. Findings Higher firm-level EPU reduces investment and debt issuance and raises precautionary cash, most strongly for financially constrained and manufacturing firms. Banks exposed to more uncertain firms increase deposits, contract lending and accumulate liquid assets, with effects concentrated in community and regional institutions and attenuated by size and capital. The corporate channel accounts for 8–28% of the bank-level effect and banks’ direct response for the remainder; COVID-…

title: Navigating uncertainty: an interpretative phenomenological analysis informed qualitative study of parents' and caregivers' lived experiences and interpretations of childhood vaccination hesitancy in Delta State, Nigeria
abstract: Background Vaccine hesitancy remains a persistent global public health concern. In Nigeria, longstanding historical, cultural, and institutional dynamics continue to undermine childhood vaccination uptake. This study makes a novel contribution to the literature by applying a broader qualitative study adopting an Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) informed analytical approach to examine how parents and caregivers construct and interpret childhood vaccination hesitancy through their lived experiences. Methods Twenty parents and caregivers from Delta State, Nigeria, whose children aged 0–3 were unvaccinated or not up to date with routine immunizations, participated in the study. Data were collected through two focus groups ( n = 5 each) and 10 individual interviews. The data were analyzed using an IPA informed analytical approach. Findings The study reveals that childhood vaccine hesitancy is driven by the convergence of historical fears, uncertainty, cultural identity, and fear of external control. Caregivers perceived adverse reactions further intensify reluctance, reinforced by low trust in the healthcare system. These dynamics highlight the urgent need for strengthened media engagement and targeted public awareness efforts. Conclusions The study recommends interventions that emphasize transparent communication, professionalized vaccine delivery, culturally informed…

title: A BIM-based framework for reliability-constrained cost minimization of electromechanical systems under seismic uncertainty in early design
abstract: Purpose This study develops a proactive methodology that integrates probabilistic seismic assessment into building information modeling (BIM) during early design. While BIM is widely used for design management, its potential for component-level reliability-based seismic evaluation remains underexplored. Design/methodology/approach A BIM-based probabilistic framework was developed to support the reliability-constrained cost minimization (RCCM) of mechanical and electrical (M&E) component configurations under seismic uncertainty. The framework integrates fragility curves and seismic hazard characterization into a unified decision-support model to select the lowest-cost feasible M&E component configuration that satisfies user-defined reliability thresholds during early design. The framework is demonstrated through a case study of the early design of a backup power system in a sewage pumping station. The case study is followed by complementary sensitivity analyses that examine how variations in site-specific seismic hazards, reliability requirements and the median fragility parameter θ influence component selection. The implementation uses Python scripts within Dynamo to process location-specific hazard information and evaluate reliability-based alternatives directly within the BIM workflow. Findings Results indicate that embedding probabilistic seismic assessment in BIM enhances e…

title: Navigating uncertainty: changes in the occupational preferences of swiss apprenticeship seekers in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Abstract Transitions from school to vocational education and training are inherently characterised by uncertainty and shaped by young people’s preferences, perceptions of occupational opportunities, and broader labour market dynamics. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted working conditions and training opportunities, potentially reshaping how occupations were evaluated in terms of stability, accessibility, and risk. Building on perspectives from Subjective Expected Utility theory and research on occupational preference formation, this study examines how the pandemic was associated with changes in apprenticeship seekers’ occupational interests in Switzerland. The analysis draws on more than 22 million online search queries from a national apprenticeship platform (2018–2025), used as an indicator of occupational interest. Using Seasonal-Trend Decomposition to disentangle long-term trends, seasonal patterns, and short-term fluctuations in search interest, the study analyses monthly search activity at the training-occupation level. The analyses distinguish between occupations exposed to different forms of pandemic-related impacts: working from home, increased workload, short-time work, and marginally impacted occupations. Results reveal two temporally distinct patterns. During the initial months of the pandemic, volatility in search activity increased, consistent with a short-term disru…

title: Manufacturing Uncertainty Without Redistribution? Point-Halving and Championship Splits in Europe’s Smaller Football Leagues
Towards reliable IoT security: deterministic binarization in the arithmetic optimization algorithm for network-intrusion feature selection: controlled and cross-dataset validation
abstract: Introduction Wrapper-based feature selection can reduce dimensionality in network intrusion detection, but continuous-to-binary mapping may influence predictive performance and subset compactness. Methods The Deterministic Binarization Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm (DBAOA) preserves AOA's stochastic continuous search while replacing BAOA's probabilistic binary sampling with a deterministic midpoint threshold. Matched 30-run controlled evaluations on NF-UNSW-NB15-v2 were followed by independent validation on NF-ToN-IoT-v2, together with sensitivity, stability, convergence, and downstream-classifier analyses. Results On NF-UNSW-NB15-v2, weighted F1 was similar for DBAOA and BAOA (0.95291 vs. 0.95336), but DBAOA selected fewer features (12.07 vs. 14.90; 19.0% reduction; Holm-adjusted p = 0.028). On NF-ToN-IoT-v2, DBAOA achieved higher weighted F1 (0.94623 vs. 0.94347; difference 0.00276; bootstrap 95% CI 0.00139–0.00413; Holm-adjusted p = 0.00075) and fewer features on average (16.67 vs. 18.30; Holm-adjusted p = 0.063). On an untouched 100,000-flow NF-ToN-IoT-v2 holdout, the post hoc DBAOA medoid matched or exceeded all-feature accuracy for random forest and XGBoost, while RBF-SVM accuracy decreased. Discussion The feature-count change was in the same direction across datasets, but statistical-significance patterns differed, and downstream transfer was learner-dependent.

title: Discovery and Structure–Activity Relationship Optimization of a Novel Rv1625c Agonist Chemotype with Antitubercular Activity
abstract: Abstract Rv1625c/Cya has emerged as a promising target for the development of treatment-shortening therapies for tuberculosis. Screening of an Enamine compound library identified sBVQ004 as an initial hit, and rapid hit optimization led to compound 1, which was subsequently confirmed as an Rv1625c/Cya agonist. Structure–activity relationship studies identified lead compound 25 with potent activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv under cholesterol-dependent growth conditions (MIC = 0.27 μM) and strong intramacrophage activity (EC50 = 0.079 μM). Compounds 1 and 25 showed oral bioavailabilities of 84.5% and 51.9% in mice, respectively. Repeat twice daily (BID) oral dosing of compound 1 resulted in a dose- and time-dependent decrease in systemic exposure. Despite this pharmacokinetic limitation, the potency and overall profile of this chemotype encouraged continued optimization.

title: A Runge-Kutta-Type Parallel-Iterative Method for Preserving the Symplectic Structure of Stochastic Hamiltonian Systems
abstract: A parallel-iterative method for stochastic differential equations is proposed in this paper. The method is based on the stochastic Runge-Kutta method and applies the waveform relaxation technique to implement parallel computing. Furthermore, for the stochastic Hamiltonian system (SHS) with multiplicative noise, we study conditions under which the method conserves the symplectic structure of the SHS in the framework of parallel computing. The method not only improves the computational efficiency but also keeps the critical symplectic-preserving property of the SHS. We also consider the simulation process to give the concrete implementation, which is further simplified. Moreover, numerical examples validate the correctness and feasibility of the theory.

title: Optimization of Radio Frequency-Assisted Papain Treatments for Beef Tenderization: Effects on Texture, Water Distribution, and Muscle Microstructure
Multiphase capillary-driven tear transport and microchannel optimization for self-moisturizing contact lenses
abstract: Abstract Existing self-moisturizing contact lens studies rarely incorporate transient multiphase tear–air interactions together with quantitative microchannel geometry optimization, limiting predictive design of efficient hydration systems. In this work, the systematic parametric investigation of microchannel geometry embedded in the contact lens, along with the fluid flow through the channel, has been carried out. It follows the multiphase modeling framework, which properly accounts for tear-air capillary interactions that can facilitate self-regulated hydration in contact lenses during interblink periods. A 3-D microchannel architecture composed of biocompatible polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) was modeled and analyzed using the commercial finite element analysis (FEA) tool COMSOL Multiphysics. It establishes that microchannel length, width, and height quantitatively control transient tear penetration and filling efficiency, enabling geometry selection for rapid passive hydration. In particular, variation of the contact angle from 67.5° to 45° reduced the total channel filling time from approximately 13.15 ms to 11.13 ms, while a further reduction to 30° resulted in a slightly higher filling time of 11.43 ms, indicating a non-monotonic dependence of filling time on contact angle under the investigated conditions. The simulation model appropriately incorporated tear properties and …

title: A novel lightweight magnetic shielding cylinder of double-layer permalloy and residual field optimization experiment study
abstract: Abstract Magnetic shielding cylinder (MSC) serves as a foundational device by providing ultra-low magnetic environment for various frontier technologies. However, emerging application scenarios impose weight limitation that requires the reduction in shielding layer, which inherently compromises passive shielding efficiency. The MSC of fewer layers suffer from an elevated residual field limit under degaussing, whereas implementing a conventional external active compensation system to further suppress the residual field scales up the volume, thereby limiting its application scenarios. In this paper, a novel lightweight MSC is proposed, composing of a double-layer permalloy, an aluminum layer and a set of integrated external compensation coils. The residual field performance within internal cavity is optimized with pulsed magnetization regulation method based on the hysteresis characteristic of permalloy. To verify this scheme, both simulation and experiment are performed on a double-layer permalloy MSC ( ∅ 30 × 60 cm ), the average residual field in the target region is reduced from 6.56 nT post-degaussing to 2.31 nT and exhibits excellent temporal stability. This highly integrated, lightweight magnetic shield provides valuable guiding significance for the advancement of novel hybrid magnetic shielding structures.

title: Exact Internal Controllability and Synchronization for a System of Wave Equations with Coupled Robin Boundary Condition
abstract: Abstract. This paper shows the exact internal controllability and synchronization for a coupled system of wave equations with coupled Robin boundary condition. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Management: Current Therapeutic Approaches and Future Directions
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) negatively impacts both individual and social development, functional outcomes, and quality of life. Despite extensive research on the topic, this psychiatric disorder continues raising significant considerations regarding its optimal management. The present review provides an overview of recent evidence on standard clinical approaches, including pharmacological and behavioral interventions, as well as complementary approaches, including interventions based on physical activity, dietary modifications, microbiota-targeted treatments, digital tools, music therapy, and neurostimulation techniques. ADHD management might rely on a combination of pharmacological and non-pharmacological strategies, with standard treatments showing the most consistent clinical utility. Across therapeutic modalities, most interventions appear to show more consistent effects in pediatric populations, but remain limited regarding generalizability across developmentalstages. Moreover, the optimal integration and comparative effectiveness of different interventions remain insufficiently established. Given the multifactorial etiology of ADHD, current therapeutic options may therefore be considered within a personalized framework to better align interventions with individual patient profiles and needs.

title: Surgical management and short-term follow-up of left ventricular pseudoaneurysm rupture following acute myocardial infarction: a case report
abstract: Background Left ventricular pseudoaneurysm (LVPA) is a serious mechanical complication of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) with high mortality, independently predicted by total occlusion or proximal stenosis of the left anterior descending artery (LAD), and often requiring surgical intervention once developed. Case presentation A 69-year-old male presented with severe chest pain for half a month. Echocardiography revealed a LVPA with thrombus and a large pericardial effusion. Coronary angiography showed 100% occlusion of the proximal LAD, 50%–60% stenosis in the proximal and distal left circumflex artery. The patient underwent LVPA resection and left ventricular reconstruction using the Dor procedure, which effectively improved cardiac function and left ventricular remodeling. Conclusions We present a rare case of LVPA rupture complicated by massive blood clots in the pericardial cavity. Early surgical intervention is essential, as it improves cardiac function and promotes reverse left ventricular remodeling.

title: Enhancing Financial Literacy and Financial Management Capabilities of MSMEs for Sustainable Business Development in Ligarmukti Village, Klapanunggal District, Bogor Regency
abstract: This Community Service initiative aims to enhance financial literacy and financial management capabilities among Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to support long-term business sustainability in Ligarmukti Village, Klapanunggal District, Bogor Regency. This activity was motivated by the critical need for MSME entrepreneurs to manage business finances effectively, particularly regarding transaction recording, separating personal and business funds, capital management, profit calculations, and utilizing formal as well as digital financial services. The implementation methodology integrated educational lectures, participatory training, and community empowerment through financial literacy modules, practical simple bookkeeping, an introduction to banking products and services by Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) Klapanunggal Sub-branch, and the distribution of basic food supplies. Designed collaboratively by Perbanas Institute, the Ligarmukti Village Government, and BRI Klapanunggal, the evaluation focused on measuring participants' understanding of financial literacy and their capability to execute financial planning and transaction recording. This program is expected to foster orderly financial management habits, elevate business decision-making quality, and fortify MSME resilience against operational risks, serving as an initial step toward building self-reliant, adaptive, a…

title: Cloud Computing Adoption in Management of Educational Institutions: A Systematic Literature Review of Drivers, Implementation, Benefits, and Challenges
abstract: Purpose: Cloud computing has become an important component of digital transformation in educational institutions, supporting scalable digital learning environments and improved educational service delivery. However, evidence on cloud computing adoption remains fragmented across institutional contexts, theoretical perspectives, and technology applications. This systematic literature review synthesises research on cloud computing adoption by examining drivers, implementation approaches, benefits, and challenges.Methodology: Following the PRISMA framework, a structured search was conducted across Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore Digital Library, and ERIC. From 1,001 identified records, 46 studies met the eligibility criteria after screening and full-text assessment. The included studies were analysed using thematic synthesis.Results: Findings show that adoption is influenced by technological readiness, compatibility, security, organisational support, institutional resources, and environmental factors. Cloud computing supports learning management systems, digital learning platforms, administrative services, and smart campus initiatives. However, security, privacy, infrastructure limitations, cost, and institutional readiness remain major challenges.Novelty and Contribution: This review provides an integrated synthesis linking adoption determinants, implementation pathways, outco…

title: Investor sentiment, crash risk and accounting information quality
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether investor sentiment is associated with stock price crash risk in Latin American capital markets and whether lower accounting information quality strengthens this relationship. Design/methodology/approach This study analyzes an unbalanced panel of publicly traded firms from Brazil, Chile, Mexico and Peru over the period 2004–2024. The empirical analysis uses fixed effects (FE), two-stage least squares (2SLS) and System-GMM. Crash risk is measured using negative conditional skewness and down-to-up volatility. Investor sentiment is assessed at aggregate and firm-specific levels, while accounting information quality is proxied by absolute discretionary accruals. Findings The results indicate that firm-specific and aggregate investor sentiment are positively associated with stock price crash risk, with System-GMM supporting this relationship after accounting for endogeneity and dynamic effects. This study also finds partial evidence that lower accounting information quality strengthens this relationship: greater earnings management intensifies the association between firm-specific sentiment and crash risk when crash risk is measured by negative conditional skewness, but no comparable moderating relationship is observed for down-to-up volatility or aggregate sentiment. Research limitations/implications Future research could examine other inst…

title: Silent sustainability: understanding greenblushing among European tourism eco-entrepreneurs
abstract: Purpose This paper investigates the communicative dynamics of eco-entrepreneurs within the European accommodation sector, specifically exploring the gap between substantive sustainability practices and limited public communication. By examining the drivers of communicative reticence, the study seeks to explain why certified practices remain weakly visible (silent sustainability) and when this reflects deliberate restraint (greenblushing) rather than limited communication capability, thereby uncovering the tensions between entrepreneurial authenticity, resource constraints and the fear of external scrutiny. Design/methodology/approach We adopt a qualitative multiple-case study design based on 23 semi-structured interviews with owner-managers of environmentally certified accommodation SMEs across Europe, complemented with website, booking-platform and publicly available certification information. The material was analysed using a Gioia-informed procedure to develop first-order concepts, second-order themes and aggregate dimensions that explain sustainability communication (SC) practices and motivations (e.g. authenticity, scrutiny avoidance, credibility concerns and resource constraints). Findings Eco-entrepreneurs frequently reduced the specificity and prominence of public sustainability claims while retaining richer interpersonal and internal communication. Greenblushing, under…

title: Impact of Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) Practices on Economic Sustainability: The Mediating Role of Green Innovation (Special Reference to Katunayake Export Processing Zone)
abstract: Sustainability is one of the crucial factors in the modern world. Today world is facing lot of environmental problems like resource depletion, climate change, hazards and emissions etc. Sustainable solutions have become ‘the way ‘resolve these issues. Not only people also today businesses have responsibility to attempt to integrate sustainability into their processes. Therefore, this study is based on Green supply chain management practices and their impact on Economic sustainability with the mediating role of Green Innovation. This study presents a new approach to the Sri Lankan apparel industry and analyzes whether such practices have any impact of Economic sustainability. The lack of research attention has been given on the impact of GSCM practices on Economic Sustainability with the mediating effect of Green Innovation. Hence, the current research addresses the knowledge and empirical gap. Researcher used quantitative method in conducting this study. The data was collected from a sample of 208 respondents including the managerial and executive level of the Apparel Firms in the Katunayake Export Processing Zone. The collected data was analyzed by the Smart PLS software. According to the findings researcher drew a conclusion that there is a significant impact of GSCM Practices on Economic Sustainability. Meantime the results led to reveal that the relationship between GSCM pr…

title: School Management Readiness for Strengthening Specialized Science Instruction Under the MATATAG Curriculum: A Conceptual Framework and Action-Plan Model
abstract: The MATATAG Curriculum reforms basic education in the Philippines by decongesting learning competencies and strengthening foundational learning from Kindergarten to Grade 10. Translating these policy directions into meaningful Science instruction requires school-level capacity to align teachers, curriculum implementation, and learning resources. This conceptual paper examines school management readiness for specialized Science instruction in junior high schools through a narrative synthesis of relevant policy documents, theoretical literature, and Philippine education studies. Guided by Instructional Leadership Theory, General Systems Theory, and the Resource-Based View, the paper organizes readiness into three interrelated dimensions: Instructional Leadership, Curriculum Management, and Resource Management. The synthesis identifies issues that warrant attention, including teacher-subject specialization mismatch, access to relevant professional development, curriculum coordination, resource functionality and accessibility, and the administrative conditions surrounding procurement and resource support. In response, the paper proposes a four-pillar action-plan model focused on workforce alignment and mentoring, learning tools and equipment usability and maintenance, instructional coaching, and inter-institutional partnerships. The framework is presented as a conceptual guide for …

title: HOW THE CONSTRUCTION OF UNIVERSITY FINANCIAL INTELLIGENCE EMPOWERS FINANCIAL OPERATION MANAGEMENT UNDER THE ORIENTATION OF DEVELOPING NEW QUALITY PRODUCTIVE FORCES
abstract: Against the backdrop of the national strategic initiative to foster and develop new quality productive forces and advance digital and intelligent development, this paper reviews the evolutionary process of financial digital transformation in universities. Drawing on the current state of universities’ financial intelligent construction, it identifies practical dilemmas existing in such transformation. From the two dimensions of technical concepts and implementation paths, this study systematically analyzes and summarizes universities’ financial digital transformation. The findings provide practical references for universities to achieve full-scenario and comprehensive deployment of digital and intelligent financial management.

title: Earnings Management of Oil & Gas Firms After the Russian Invasion of Ukraine
abstract: Abstract Political crises often lead to sharp increases in energy prices and, consequently, in the profits of oil and gas companies. However, exceptionally high profits may be perceived as unethical, creating reputational and legitimacy concerns that can influence firms’ financial reporting behavior. Yet, there is no evidence whether European oil & gas firms manage earnings after sudden political crises, and whether their responses differ across countries. Using a difference-in-differences design, this study documents that European oil & gas firms engaged in significant income-decreasing earnings management—through both accrual-based and real activities—following the Russian invasion of Ukraine. This effect is particularly pronounced in the third quarter of 2022 and the first quarter of 2023. We further find that (real) earnings management by oil & gas firms is more pronounced in countries that implemented windfall profit taxes and in institutional environments characterized by stronger democratic governance. At the firm level, the effect is concentrated among oil & gas firms with relatively low sustainability scores, which exhibit significantly greater income-decreasing earnings management than control firms. These findings suggest that earnings management decisions were driven not only by tax considerations but also by legitimacy and reputational concerns. This study contribu…

title: Longitudinal Nutritional Management in Early Diffuse Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis With Severe Malnutrition: A 12-Month Case Report
abstract: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) is a multisystem autoimmune disease characterized by progressive fibrosis, vasculopathy, and immune dysregulation. ilk cümleyle oldukça benzer. Tekrara düşmemek için bu cümle silinebilir Nutritional deficiencies are also a component that needs to be treated in the management of the disease. A 39-year-old man with newly diagnosed dcSSc associated with interstitial lung disease received cyclophosphamide followed by mycophenolate mofetil and rituximab. During follow-up, he developed progressive anorexia and severe weight loss despite adequate immunosuppressive treatment. Serial nutritional assessments demonstrated a marked decline in body mass index, body composition, and phase angle, indicating progressive malnutrition. During the 12-month follow-up, progressive nutritional recovery was achieved with restoration of body weight, improvement in phase angle, normalization of inflammatory markers, and recovery of functional nutritional status. This case highlights that successful management of dcSSc extends beyond immunosuppressive therapy. Early recognition of malnutrition, serial nutritional monitoring, and individualized medical nutrition therapy may substantially improve clinical outcomes.

title: Analysing paradigmatic diversity in accounting research: a structured framework of education areas and critical-intensity
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine paradigmatic diversity within accounting education (AE) as a subfield of accounting research and map how different paradigmatic orientations are distributed across substantive areas of AE research. Design/methodology/approach This study develops and applies a structured analytical framework that classifies research across eight education domains and introduces a critical-intensity measure to assess the distribution of research paradigms. A systematic review of 4,148 peer-reviewed articles published between 1999 and 2025 is conducted, with each study coded as positivist, interpretive or critical. Findings The results of this study reveal a strong dominance of positivist approaches (70.6%), with interpretive (19.6%) and critical (9.8%) paradigms remaining underrepresented. The critical-intensity analysis shows that critical engagement is more pronounced in areas such as accounting information systems and technology, as well as assessment and student performance. In contrast, governance, auditing and professional practice, as well as international and comparative domains, are largely interpretive. Practical implications The findings of this study identify areas in which interpretive and critical inquiry is comparatively concentrated or underrepresented, providing an empirical basis for future research examining whether and how paradigmatic divers…

title: Improving Digital Literacy and Financial Transaction Efficiency Among Msmes in Kampung Parit, Melaka, Malaysia
abstract: This community service activity aims to improve digital literacy and financial transaction efficiency among MSMEs in Kampung Parit, Melaka, Malaysia, through the implementation of an e-wallet-based payment system. Implementation methods include outreach, training on how to use the e-wallet application, and direct assistance in implementing the system in daily buying and selling activities. The results of the activity showed that the majority of MSMEs were able to operate e-wallets independently, making transactions faster, more secure, and digitally recorded, increasing consumer trust. Furthermore, business owners began to experience efficiencies in financial management and sales recording. In conclusion, implementing an e-wallet payment system can be an effective strategy to support the digitalization of MSMEs, increase the competitiveness of small businesses, and expand market access through practical and modern cashless transactions.

title: DETERMINAN UNDERPRICING IPO: PENGARUH REPUTASI UNDERWRITER, LISTING DELAY, UMUR PERUSAHAAN, DAN FINANCIAL LEVERAGE DI BURSA EFEK INDONESIA
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effects of underwriter reputation, Listing Delay, firm age, and financial leverage on Underpricing among Islamic companies conducting Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. This study is motivated by the persistently high levels of Underpricing among Islamic companies and the inconsistencies in previous research findings regarding the factors influencing it. This study employs a quantitative approach with an associative research design. The sample consists of 34 companies. The sampling technique used is purposive sampling. The data utilized are secondary data obtained from company prospectuses, financial statements, and publications of the Indonesia Stock Exchange. Data analysis employed multiple linear regression preceded by classical assumption tests. Data processing and analysis were conducted using EViews 13. Hypothesis testing was performed via partial tests (t-tests), simultaneous testFs (F-tests), and the coefficient of determination (R²). The results of this study indicate that the underwriter’s reputation, Listing Delay, firm age, and financial leverage do not have a significant effect on the degree of Underpricing, either individually or collectively, as evidenced by the statistical tests conducted. This study is expected to contribute to the development of the Islamic finance literature and serve as a basis for…

title: The Impact of Fintech Technology on the Financial Statements of Financial Companies
abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of financial technology (fintech) on the financial statements of financial companies in 2026. The study employs a qualitative approach using a literature review method. Data were obtained from reputable academic journals, scholarly books, and relevant official regulatory sources addressing fintech, financial reporting, artificial intelligence, automation, blockchain, cloud accounting, big data analytics, and digital reporting. The analysis was conducted through thematic synthesis to identify the mechanisms through which fintech affects financial reporting quality. The findings indicate that fintech has a substantial potential to improve the quality of financial statements by enhancing accuracy, relevance, timeliness, transparency, efficiency, and verifiability. Artificial intelligence supports data analysis, anomaly detection, forecasting, and accounting process automation. Automation improves processing efficiency and can strengthen internal controls by reducing repetitive manual procedures. Blockchain enhances transaction traceability and data integrity, while cloud accounting facilitates data integration and accessibility. Digital reporting further improves reporting timeliness and supports regulatory compliance. However, the benefits of fintech depend on data quality, organizational readiness, human resource competence, cybersecurity, i…

title: A Technical Debt as Institutional Memory- A Narrative Review of Legacy Modernisation in Regulated Financial Systems
abstract: Technical debt is usually measured based on its impact on software quality, maintenance work and change. For regulated financial systems, however, a legacy implementation may also have business rules, the need for which may not be well documented. This is a narrative review that is a synthesis of literature on technical debt, software evolution, legacy modernisation and organisational memory, banking guidance and a documented operational incident, all of which are used to investigate that tension. It suggests the debt-as-memory hypothesis: there are technically undesirable artefacts that contain information that is needed to interpret and/or reproduce an institutional obligation. The synthesis identifies three markers of these artefacts: uncertain rationale, lack of independent evidence and consequences that occur beyond the immediate change process. A conceptual taxonomy is provided that links the candidate debt forms to the knowledge at risk and a comparison of six modernisation strategies is provided that outlines their potential for retaining the behaviours and the evidentiary requirements for each. Practical assessment is communicated through: Provenance review, examination of historical exception, self-documented proven rules, and test of planned behaviour. The analysis does not seek to measure the amount of memory bearing debt, nor to prioritise the modernisation strateg…
venue: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Financial Reporting Quality: The Mediating Role of Accounting Process Automation
abstract: AI is making a dent in the work that accountants do, and the link between AI and the quality of financial reporting stems in part on how organisations integrate AI into their daily routines. The purpose of this study is to investigate the correlation between adoption of artificial intelligence and financial reporting quality as well as the mediation effect of accounting process automation. The analysis sample consists of 360 respondents from professionals in the fields of accounting, financial reporting, financial management, internal audit and accounting systems oversight. Partial least squares structural equation modelling is used to analyze three reflective constructs with five indicators. Indicator reliability, internal consistency, convergent and discriminant validity are supported by measurement assessment. For structural inference 10,000 bootstrap resamples were used. Both artificial intelligence adoption and accounting process automation are positively associated with financial reporting quality, with an average beta value of 0.500, while artificial intelligence adoption is positively related to accounting process automation with an average beta value of 0.478. The direct link between the use of AI and Financial Reporting quality is also positive and significant (beta = 0.189). Regarding the specific indirect effect, it is found to be 0.239 (95% CI: 0.188 to 0.296), sho…

title: Wave overtopping load transmission and landward revetment stability on a sloping sea dike with varying crest widths
abstract: Introduction Wave overtopping threatens sea-dike landward slopes. Their stability depends on both load transmission across the crest and revetment resistance. Methods A calibrated 1:30 Froude-scaled model of a sloping sea dike in Zhejiang, China, was tested in a two-dimensional flume. A servo-controlled piston-type wavemaker generated shore-normal irregular waves using a JONSWAP spectrum. The tests covered four crest widths (8 -20 m), four wave -water-level conditions (100 -500-year return periods, 13% exceedance wave height H 13 % = 5.28 -5.66 m, and spectral mean period T = 15.5 -16.8 s), and four landward revetments. Overtopping pressure, flow velocity, discharge, and revetment response were quantified. Results Increasing crest width from 8 to 20 m reduced mean landward-slope velocity by 25.4 -30.5%. Widening from 16 to 20 m yielded a further reduction of 1.6 -5.8%. Pressures also decreased with crest widening. The 16 m crest under the 200-year condition had higher mean overtopping discharge than the 8 m crest under the 100-year condition (0.068 vs. 0.042 m³/(m·s)), but lower mean landward-slope velocity (approximately 2.3 vs. 2.6 m/s). Dry-stone damage progressed from stone loosening and local depression to stone loss and exposure of the dike body. Crest widening delayed clear instability until more severe conditions, although pronounced erosion persisted for the 16 and 20 …

title: Quality of financial information and access to bank financing: evidence from private Spanish firms
abstract: Purpose This study analyses how the quality of financial information affects bank borrowing, including access to credit and the amount of new debt. It uses a large sample of Spanish private firms from 2003–2019 and examines how firm size and bank regulations associated with the 2008 crisis and Basel II affect this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Using accruals quality measures as proxies for financial reporting quality, we employ logit models to analyse access to financing and Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regressions for the debt amount, applying Heckman's two-step selection correction. Findings The results indicate that higher financial reporting quality significantly increases the likelihood of obtaining bank financing. Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) benefit more than large firms, and access to financing declines following the financial crisis and the implementation of Basel II. Regarding the amount of new debt, although higher financial reporting quality is associated with larger amounts of new debt, the results do not confirm a differential role of quality either for SMEs or after 2008. Research limitations/implications The study uses an indirect proxy for new bank debt, which does not distinguish between new loans, extensions or renewals of credit lines. Social implications High-quality financial reporting is not only a regulatory requirement, but also…

title: More Is More, Less Is More, More Is Less: Choosing the Right Amount of Data to Show
abstract: How much data should a single figure show? Many researchers default to a ‘more is more’ approach and show every data series with equal visual weight. While authors may believe that showing everything signals transparency, data visualizations in scientific papers exist to argue a hypothesis or advance an argument, and dense, uniformly styled charts often obscure the very findings they are meant to communicate. This article examines three strategies for deciding how much data to display: ‘more is more’ (show everything), ‘less is more’ (show only the key result, at the cost of context), and ‘more is less’ (show everything but deliberately emphasize what matters). Using a line chart adapted from the chemistry literature, I demonstrate practical techniques such as direct labeling, sequential color palettes, the ‘start with gray’ approach, and small multiples that can help authors guide readers’ attention while preserving the fuller context of their results.

title: Description of the occurrence and possible transmission of potentially pathogenic E. coli between sows and pigs from fifteen U.S. midwestern breeding herds and their early downstream nursery phase
abstract: A better understanding of the dynamics of E. coli transmission among sows and pigs during the due-to-wean phase and the prevalence of potentially pathogenic virotypes and pathotypes post-weaning adds significant value to veterinarians, producers, and stakeholders. The objectives of this study were to evaluate the potential risk of sows in the transmission of E. coli to pigs before weaning, evaluate the prevalence of potentially pathogenic hemolytic E. coli at the due-to-wean and early nursery phase (10 days post-weaning), and determine the pigs’ F18 susceptibility 10 days post-weaning from different production systems in the US. Only farm 2 (out of 15 farms) had matching detection of EPEC in 2 out of 20 sows (10% - 95% CI = 0.2-31.7) and their respective 3-wk-old pigs (due-to-wean). Potentially pathogenic hemolytic E. coli frequency of detection in sows was positively correlated with detection in 3-wk-old pigs. For each 5-percentage-point increase in frequency of detection in sows, the prevalence risk ratio of detecting potentially pathogenic hemolytic E. coli in 3-wk-old pigs increased by 1.95 (95% CI 1.43-2.63). There was no significant association of sow-pig frequency of detection in 4-wk-old pigs. Enteropathogenic E. coli pathotype (EPEC) was more frequently detected (64%), followed by F4 enterotoxigenic E. coli (32%), and F18 enterotoxigenic E. coli and F18 hybrid enteroto…
