title: Conscious coins: an interpretive structural approach to understanding behavioral drivers of green cryptocurrency investment
abstract: Purpose This study systematically aims to explore and structures the key enablers driving green cryptocurrencies adoption. Design/methodology/approach The study uses interpretive structural modelling approach to delve into the complex interplay between psychological, technological, financial and regulatory factors, revealing both direct and indirect influences on investment decisions. Findings Drawing on a comprehensive literature review and insights from 20 domain experts, the research identifies 19 critical factors influencing green cryptocurrency adoption. These factors are organised into a five-tier hierarchical structure, uncovering their causal relationships and classifying them according to their influence levels. Research limitations/implications The present research is constrained by expert-driven analysis, which may affect the objectivity of the findings. Further quantitative validation of the identified factor interrelationships is warranted. The exclusion of demographic and psychographic influences restricts user segmentation insights, while the static view limits generalisability. Practical implications From a practical perspective, the study provides actionable recommendations for businesses, policymakers and environmental advocates by helping to promote sustainable practices, address key barriers and foster a more resilient green cryptocurrency ecosystem. title: A Study on Human Resource Management Practices and Employee Record Management at Vankal Cables and Transmission Limited
abstract: Human Resource Management (HRM) is an important organisational function concerned with managing employees and supporting the achievement of organisational objectives. It includes activities such as human resource planning, recruitment and selection, training and development, performance management, employee relations and maintenance of employee records. This study examines the relevance of HR practices and employee record management at Vankal Cables and Transmission Limited, Tilda, Chhattisgarh, through the practical learning gained during the internship. The internship was undertaken in the Human Resource Department of Vankal Cables and Transmission Limited from 15 June 2026 to 16 July 2026. The internship certificate records involvement in HR and procurement activities and assistance with employee records. The study therefore focuses on the importance of organised documentation, accuracy, administrative coordination and the role of HR in an industrial organisation. The paper follows a descriptive approach and is based on internship experience, available internship documentation and secondary information from books and research publications. It does not claim a formal employee survey or unverified company-wide results. The study highlights that systematic employee records, confidentiality, coordination and clear administrative procedures support effective HR management. Keywor…

title: The invisible architecture of firm performance: unveiling the role of corporate governance in translating values into financial outcomes
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine the impact of espoused values on firm performance, emphasizing the mediating role of corporate governance. Design/methodology/approach The present study analyzes BSE 500 companies across seven years, spanning from 2017–2018 to 2023–2024. The research uses firm fixed-effects regression and two-stage least squares (2SLS) panel estimation. Mediation is tested through bootstrap resampling. Findings Espoused values positively and significantly predict both Tobin’s Q and market capitalization, and corporate governance quality independently improves firm value. The findings reveal that corporate governance partially mediates the values–performance relationship, with mediation proportions rising from approximately 3%–4% under fixed effects to 10%–13% under 2SLS, indicating attenuation bias in baseline models. Disaggregated analysis reveals that customer and shareholder value orientations are the strongest performance predictors, while community and environment value disclosures carry a negative signal, consistent with institutional isomorphism and investor skepticism toward generic corporate social responsibility (CSR) rhetoric. Practical implications Boards should treat value disclosures as a strategic signaling instrument, prioritizing customer-oriented and shareholder-oriented commitments and ensuring governance structures remain congr…

title: Cognitivism and Managerial Decision Quality in Financial and Strategic Management: A Critical Review
abstract: Managerial decision quality has become increasingly important in financial and strategic contexts marked by uncertainty, digital transformation, and continuous capability renewal. Yet adjacent literatures on behavioral finance, managerial cognition, strategic flexibility, and management learning have largely developed in parallel, leaving limited cross-domain explanation of how shared cognitivist mechanisms shape managerial judgment. This article addresses that gap through a structured critical literature review of metacognition, schema flexibility, and self-efficacy across financial management, strategic management, management education, and executive development. Rather than providing statistical aggregation, the review offers an interpretive synthesis of heterogeneous studies supported by illustrative corporate and institutional cases. Three recurring patterns emerged. Metacognition was repeatedly linked to reflective monitoring, bias checking, and corrective judgment. Schema flexibility was associated with interpretive updating and adaptation when dominant frames became inadequate. Self-efficacy appeared to support the translation of cognitive preparation into action readiness under complexity. Across the reviewed literature, managerial failures were often linked to weak reflective control or rigid interpretive frames, whereas feedback-rich learning designs and structured d…

title: The lowry model: inorganic existential social theory. Section III: moving past static weight lock, financial scale walls, and autoregressive collapse
abstract: Current AI scaling paradigms rely on the premise that exponentially increasing compute and synthetic data are requisite for intelligence gains, driving the industry toward financial scale walls and autoregressive data collapse. To address potential compute-cost bottlenecks, this paper introduces foundational theoretical frameworks, including Enterprise Incremental Complexity Bucketing, a matrixing structure that drastically reduces compute load by dynamically matching systemic expenditure to task complexity. To counter synthetic data degradation, I introduce Lens-Based Training, a methodology that extracts exponentially denser neural connections from foundational datasets, neutralizing the artificial constraint of data scarcity. This is structurally paired with protocols for activating renewable, high-dimensional training data derived directly from uncodified human architectures and Continuous Organic Sensory Ingestion (COSI). Ultimately, this framework hypothesizes that models are dramatically underperforming relative to their latent capability because they lack environmental activation triggers, providing an architectural pathway to elite computational performance that bypasses the limitations of brute-force scaling.

title: Digital-Twin-Based Compliance Review of Financial Terminal Devices: A Reproducible Framework and Controlled Evaluation
abstract: Financial terminal compliance reviews are often periodic, sample-based, and weak in reconstructing time-dependent violations. This study develops a reproducible digital-twin framework for continuous compliance review and examines whether dynamic synchronization and evidence-chain reconstruction provide measurable gains beyond automated rule checking. The framework comprises physical-terminal, communication, virtual-twin, and compliance-decision layers, integrating rule mapping, a lightweight neural network, 3σ anomaly screening, random forests, and an Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). A controlled evaluation used 500 devices, including Automated Teller Machines (ATMs), Point-of-Sale (POS) terminals, self-service terminals, and mobile payment devices. Primary operational records, secondary compliance documents, and synthetic abnormal cases were kept source-labelled. Manual sampling, non-twin automated rules, and the proposed framework were compared across ten independent runs. The digital-twin scheme achieved a 97.6% modelling success rate, synchronization error no greater than 0.035, and mean latency of 70 ms. It identified 263 compliance events, compared with 218 for automated rules and 150 for manual review. Coverage and accuracy were 98.6% and 96.2%, respectively, while review time averaged 0.8 min per device. Relative to automated rules, the gains were 2.2 percentage points…

title: Digital reflective practice tools for new graduate nurse transition: organisational design principles from a qualitative study
abstract: Background New graduate registered nurses (NGRNs) face high cognitive and emotional demands during transition to practice, and international first year attrition sits at around 20%. Digital reflective practice tools are increasingly procured to extend scarce clinical educator capacity. The features such tools require already exist in healthcare and consumer platforms, yet adoption is inconsistent, suggesting that organisational conditions rather than functionality alone may shape whether they are used. This study aimed to identify the organisational conditions under which digital reflective practice tools support NGRN transition, grounded in the accounts of NGRNs and clinical nurse educators (CNEs). Methods A qualitative descriptive design within a constructivist paradigm was used. Five focus groups (NGRNs n = 12; CNEs n = 7) were conducted across public, private, and community health services in two regions of New South Wales, Australia, between March and November 2025. NGRN and CNE groups were held separately. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, with sufficiency judged by information power. Results Participants’ accounts pointed less to tool features than to four organisational conditions, each associated with a participant-described rationale. First, help-seeking was governed by cognitive load: NGRNs avoided synchronous channels not through lack of confiden…

title: Supporting resilient performance and workforce mental well-being in care for older adults: a participatory stakeholder study of design requirements for a digital toolbox for healthcare leaders
abstract: Introduction Healthcare organizations need practical leadership support that strengthens resilient performance and workforce mental well-being without adding to the demands on healthcare professionals. However, there is limited empirical knowledge about how digital leadership support should be designed and under what conditions it could be used in practice. This study aimed to identify design requirements and contextual conditions for a digital toolbox intended to support healthcare leaders in supporting resilient performance and workforce mental well-being in care for older adults. The preliminary concept originated within Support4Resilience, a project focused on this care context. Methods We collected data through four participatory stakeholder workshops involving 31 participants representing healthcare practice and leadership, informal-caregiver perspectives, academia, education, advocacy, policy and regulation, and health-service development. Participants examined preliminary thematic areas and proposed toolbox components rather than a functioning prototype. We analyzed the data using reflexive thematic analysis. Results The analysis generated five themes: supporting autonomy within shared organizational boundaries; clarifying roles, responsibilities, and priorities; strengthening relational and inclusive leadership; integrating support into time-constrained workflows; and …

title: Intelligent Pronunciation Learning Pathways in Education 4.0: An Instructional Design Framework
abstract: Pronunciation plays a central role in oral intelligibility, yet many technology-enhanced language courses still treat it as an add-on or reduce it to isolated drill practice. This conceptual study proposes an instructional design framework for intelligent pronunciation learning pathways within Education 4.0 ecosystems. The study uses a theory-synthesis approach: peer-reviewed work on pronunciation instruction, high-variability phonetic training (HVPT), corrective feedback (CF), computer-assisted pronunciation training (CAPT), automatic speech recognition (ASR), adaptive learning, and learning analytics ethics was selected, compared, and synthesized to identify design requirements for data-informed pronunciation support. The framework contains three interdependent layers: Input, which organizes high-variability exposure through HVPT principles; Feedback, which uses AI-mediated support informed by L2 CF and mediation theory; and Adaptation, which sequences learner-specific pathways through learning analytics and adaptive learning concepts. The framework differs from single-tool CAPT models by treating pronunciation learning as a governed pathway that connects input design, feedback reliability, teacher mediation, contextual constraints, and ethical safeguards. The article also examines Iraqi Kurdistan as an illustrative under-resourced EFL context, where limitations in digital in…

title: SYSTEM DESIGN AND PROPOSED SURVEY WORKFLOW FOR LIGHTWEIGHT UAV-BORNE GROUND-PENETRATING RADAR IN URBAN ENVIRONMENTS
abstract: Operating ground-penetrating radar (GPR) from a multirotor requires a payload that fits the aircraft’s mass limits and keeps the antenna stable enough for repeatable surveys. This conceptual design addresses those constraints for a controlled municipal utility corridor. The proposed unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) carries a downward-looking antenna on a damped mount and powers the radar from a dedicated battery. A recorder associates each radar trace with the estimated antenna position and retains the original measurement onboard. A reduced preview sent over a proposed 5.8 GHz link allows the operator to monitor acquisition during flight. The workflow defines how to plan survey lines, flag gaps in usable coverage, and verify suspected targets on the ground. A design requirements matrix links payload mass, antenna motion, time synchronization, positioning, and preview throughput to planned acceptance checks. Validation would begin with bench tests and progress to repeated passes over utilities with independently documented locations and depths, using ground-based GPR as a comparator. The contribution is a system architecture and verification procedure. Prototype implementation, simulation, and field validation remain future work.

title: Design, Thermal Analysis and Implementation of a Linear Converter
abstract: In electronic devices such as automotive LED lighting and digital screen applications, LDO (Low Drop-Out) or linear regulators are important components used as power supplies. Linear converters regulate the DC voltage by reducing it to a lower DC voltage level with the a dissipation mechanism. Since they constantly dissipate power in the form of heat, their efficiency is low. Linear converters generally need a heatsink, so they are larger and heavier. Conversely, they have simpler design and manufacturing structure with more cost-effective. They have less ripple and noise at the output. In this study, the advantages and disadvantages of linear converters were discussed and their thermal problems were detailed, with recommendations to solve the thermal problems. Thermal problems in these structures were analyzed by aid of Siemens FloEFD software for a linear converter designed with 9.6W output power driven by eight MOSFETs with 28 V input and 12 V output voltage. The thermal measurements taken by a thermal camera were presented for the designed and manufactured linear converter to prove the consistency of measurement and simulation results. The thermal characteristics of the designed circuits were obtained in light of the analysis and the minimum dimensions for long-term stability were studied and four different methods were presented to solve the thermal problems: increasing th…

title: Environmental procuratorial public interest litigation under the ecological and environmental code: institutional design and operational logic
abstract: Promulgated in 2026, the Ecological and Environmental Code of the People’s Republic of China introduces the concept of ‘ecological and environmental procuratorial work’ into legislation for the first time and systematically sets out procuratorial responsibilities for ecological and environmental public interest litigation in nine provisions. Article 1074 establishes special rules for damage to the marine ecological environment. Through an examination of institutional evolution, analysis of legal norms, and comparative inquiry, this article addresses how the Code consolidates and restructures environmental procuratorial public interest litigation and what distinctive indigenous characteristics emerge in the marine context. It argues that China’s system is not a transplant of US citizen suits, but a structural institutional innovation grounded in China’s own constitutional system. The Code establishes four basic forms: procuratorial involvement in compensation for non-marine ecological and environmental damage; procuratorial public interest litigation concerning compensation for marine ecological and environmental damage; environmental civil public interest litigation; and environmental administrative public interest litigation. The system is both compliance-inducing and collaborative. It differs fundamentally from US citizen suits in the source of authority, the identity of plai…

title: Design and experiment of a vision recognition system for maize seedling rows based on SegFormer
abstract: To address the precision and robustness requirements of local relative navigation for inter-row operations during the maize seedling stage, a SegFormer-B2-based visual recognition system was designed and implemented in this study. Built upon the ROS framework, the system employs SegFormer-B2 for pixel-level segmentation of maize seedling rows and integrates morphological mask refinement, connected-component filtering, least-squares row fitting, and navigation-midline construction to obtain lateral and heading deviations. The static comparison experiment evaluated navigation-line extraction under normal growth, missing seedlings with row discontinuities, weed interference, and leaf-litter interference. Across the 50 test images, the proposed method achieved mean lateral and heading deviations of 8.91 pixels and 0.844°, respectively, outperforming the conventional ExG+RowLine and HSV+Morphology methods. The mean errors and sample standard deviations for each scenario further characterized the extraction accuracy and its variation under different field conditions. Dynamic field experiments evaluated continuous navigation-parameter outputs while the vehicle was manually driven along a reference string. Under the 20 cm and 25 cm plant-spacing configurations, the lateral deviation RMSE values were 2.89 cm and 3.11 cm, respectively, and the heading deviation RMSE values were 3.260° an…

title: Diagnosing the environmental performance gap of manufacturing enterprises in Uzbekistan through a threshold-based indicator system: instrument design and a first enterprise-level application
abstract: Whether Uzbek manufacturing can respond to the national green agenda depends on capacities that country-scale indices miss. This brief report presents a threshold-based diagnostic instrument for the environmental performance gap of manufacturing enterprises and a first application to a textile enterprise, Toshbuloq Teks LLC. The instrument combines twenty indicators in five blocks: energy and resource efficiency, capital and technology, investment and finance, environmental costs and impact, and governance. Each indicator carries a norm with pre-crisis and crisis bands, every boundary is documented, and observed values become distance-to-target scores aggregated into sub-indices and an overall index. In 2024, seventeen of the twenty indicators fall in the crisis band and none reaches its norm; the overall index equals 62.2 on a hundred-point scale, so the enterprise stands on average at 62 percent of its norms. Tightening every boundary by up to twenty percent raises the crisis count to twenty; under loosening, no indicator attains its norm up to ten percent and a majority remains in crisis up to five percent. The index stays within 61.3–63.3 when any single indicator is excluded and within 57.7–69.3 in ninety percent of random re-weightings. An equal-weight integral index of the enterprise’s energy economics over 2016 to 2024 rises from 0.128 to 0.716 and falls to 0.469, consi…

title: Bridging the digital divide via legal reform – supporting readiness for paperless maritime trade
abstract: Purpose Paperless documents and systems can achieve sustainability goals, ensure more transparency and secure seamless payment across borders in maritime trade. However, as a result of the disparity in the legal recognition and acceptance of these paperless systems, some countries are benefiting from the fruits of innovation more than others in the trade ecosystem. This study aims to analyze the so-called “digital divide” and the reforms required to bridge the gap in seaborne trade. Design/methodology/approach This paper undertakes a comparative policy analysis of various domestic reforms in selected regions across Europe, Asia and Africa. It utilizes quantitative data from the United Nations Global Survey on Paperless Trade Facilitation measures as an empirical framework. This was employed to assess the digital divide with the aim of creating awareness of the potential of digital trade in the maritime sector. Findings The results show that there is no distinct line between developed and developing countries in terms of the domestic legal reforms that can be taken to transition to the use of paperless shipping documents and systems. Research limitations/implications This research acknowledges bias in the sampling as it selected regions that are believed to have made remarkable progress in paperless trade measures but may have excluded significant regions. The authors had consid…

title: Understanding Green Purchase Intention in Sustainable Fashion: An Integrated Model of Green Product Attributes, Green Marketing Communication, Green Attitude, and the Moderating Role of Generative AI Usage among Sri Lankan Generation Z Consumers
abstract: The development of environmental problems related to the fashion field has made sustainable consumption more important in the fashion industry, especially among Generation Z consumers. This study seeks to investigate how green marketing practices (green materials, green labelling, and green advertising) affect green purchase intention in the context of the sustainable fashion industry in Sri Lanka, and to analyse if green attitude can be used as a mediator and generative AI usage can be used as a moderator. Data was collected with a quantitative approach using a positivist philosophy from 165 consumers belonging to Generation Z in Sri Lanka using a structured self-administered questionnaire sent through online platforms. The data were analysed with SPSS software and descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, multiple regression analysis, mediation analysis, moderation analysis and moderated mediation analysis. The results indicate that green marketing practices have a great positive effect on green purchase intention, where green labelling is the most significant one. Green attitude was found to be a significant partial mediator between green marketing practices and green purchase intention. Importantly, the green attitude amd green purchase intention link was negatively moderated by the use of generative AI, showing that as the use of AI grows, the link between attitude and…

Model-predicted weak-echo angle retrieval for space-target active laser sensing based on a vortex-phase-encoded wide-angle metalens and multi-pixel photon counter
abstract: Abstract To evaluate weak-echo angle retrieval for space-target active laser sensing under strong background, we develop a photon-counting model integrating a vortex-phase-encoded wide-angle metalens (WAM) with a multi-pixel photon counter (MPPC). The WAM maps the incidence angle onto an annular focal spot, while an adaptive pipeline performs full-area response acquisition, coarse centroid estimation, pre-aperture-assisted annular photon selection, multi-response centroid refinement, and angle retrieval. The system model couples laser propagation, Lambertian target reflection, telescope collection, WAM focusing, MPPC parasitic effects, and four-electrode readout. For an idealized 100 km link at zenith and azimuth angles of 30° and 180°, respectively, simulations predict zenith and azimuth errors of 0.0305° and 0.0201°, a detection probability of 99.981%, and a false-alarm probability of 0.0131%. The estimated annular center meets the 0.5 μ m convergence criterion after four iterations. Without prior knowledge of the true spot center, the adaptive method approaches ideal fixed-annulus selection and markedly outperforms full-surface MPPC integration. This model provides a framework for evaluating and optimizing wide-field photon-counting angle retrieval under weak-echo and strong-background conditions.

title: Harmonizing calibrations for multi-center 177Lu dosimetry: insights from the Pan-Canadian PR.21 trial
abstract: Abstract Introduction The rapid expansion of radiopharmaceutical therapies (RPTs) has increased the need for multi-center clinical trials, yet achieving consistent dosimetry across institutions with different imaging equipment remains challenging. This study developed a practical and reliable calibration approach for a multi-center pan-Canadian 177 Lu-PSMA-617 trial. Specifically, a centralized core laboratory was established to cross-calibrate equipment and support dosimetry calculations across all sites. This approach reduced inter-site variability and minimized the need for radioactive source handling at remote centers. The method is applicable to future RPT clinical trials requiring harmonized dosimetry. Methods The core laboratory radionuclide calibrator was first calibrated against the manufacturer’s (Novartis AG, Basel, Switzerland) reference standard and validated with a high-purity germanium (HPGe) detector calibrated with a NIST-traceable source. Reference radioactive sources were then prepared, documented, and shipped to the participating sites. Sites performed planar and SPECT/CT acquisitions using these sources and adjusted their radionuclide calibrator dial settings to match the core laboratory activity reference. Sites submitted acquisition data to the core laboratory for verification and protocol compliance. The sensitivity and dead-time constant for each SPECT/…

title: HLE-ViT: a hierarchical lesion-enhanced global context vision transformer for multi-class skin lesion classification
abstract: Introduction Accurate skin lesion classification is central to computer-aided dermatological diagnosis. However, reliable classification remains challenging because different lesion categories often share similar visual appearances, whereas lesions within the same category can vary substantially. Although existing deep learning methods can extract discriminative representations from dermoscopic images, they often fail to adequately capture and integrate low-level, fine-grained lesion cues with high-level semantic relationships and spatial structure. Method To address these challenges, we propose HLE-ViT, a stage-matched hierarchical lesion enhancement framework built on a local–global context Vision Transformer. HLE-ViT deploys distinct enhancement modules according to the representational characteristics of different network stages. Specifically, the Shallow Saliency Enhancement Module (SSEM) performs neuron-wise recalibration of shallow feature responses through a parameter-free attention mechanism, whereas the Deep Semantic-Coordinate Module (DSCM) combines multi-token attention-response mixing with height- and width-dependent feature recalibration in deep stages. By integrating SSEM and DSCM, HLE-ViT provides stage-matched enhancement of shallow and deep feature representations. Results We evaluated HLE-ViT on three publicly available dermoscopic image datasets, HAM10000, I…

title: Spatially resolved multi-omics identifies an EndMT-like cell-enriched progression niche for prognostic and immunotherapeutic stratification in MIBC
abstract: Background Muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) is a clinically aggressive and highly heterogeneous malignancy. The driving mechanisms remain incompletely defined, with a particular lack of systematic understanding of the spatial remodeling mechanisms within the tumor microenvironment (TME), especially those involving endothelial cells and their endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT). Methods Using a cohort of 92 patients with MIBC who underwent radical cystectomy, we integrated imaging mass cytometry (IMC), spatial transcriptomics (ST), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) to characterize TME heterogeneity between the good-prognosis (GP) and poor-prognosis (PP) groups. Functional cellular niches were mapped in situ using DoRothEA-based transcription factor activity inference, cellular neighborhood analysis, and robust cell type decomposition (RCTD) spatial deconvolution. A niche-derived prognostic signature was subsequently developed by evaluating 117 machine-learning algorithm combinations and validated in independent bladder cancer and pan-cancer cohorts. Results The PP group exhibited greater activation of extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, angiogenesis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and integrin signaling. Spatial heterogeneity in collagen architecture was observed between the TME of the PP and GP tumors. Spa…

title: Bibliometric mapping and thematic evolution of the intersection between premature ovarian insufficiency and anxiety/depression: a multi-database analysis (2000–2025)
abstract: Background Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) carries elevated risks of depression and anxiety, and research on its mental-health dimension has grown rapidly, but its knowledge structure, thematic evolution and thinnest areas remain unmapped. Methods The corpus came mainly from PubMed (five queries: two MeSH-based, three title/abstract; 2000–2026), supplemented by OpenAlex and Crossref (each capped at 800 records). Because the OpenAlex year filter is an exact-equality, not a range filter, that arm returned 2000 records only; OpenAlex is thus not a comparison arm and the corpus is PubMed-centred (88.5%). Cross-source deduplication, rule-based relevance and completeness filtering, and independent two-author title/abstract review yielded 1,836 records (1,768 for 2000–2025; 68 online-first 2026). Because mental-health indexing is inconsistent, a 444-record subset (24.2%) was defined by a disclosed title/abstract lexicon. Analyses comprised descriptive bibliometrics, Bradford zoning, topic modelling [latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA); non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) as a check], collaboration and co-citation networks, MeSH co-occurrence, the strategic diagram, burst detection, coverage-gap quantification and a PubMed-versus-Crossref consistency check. Results Output rose from 54 records in 2000 to 153 in 2025. On the annual series a decelerating quadratic is preferred (R …

title: The labour market in Colombia, 2010-2025
abstract: Colombia’s labour market has largely recovered from the Covid-19 shock, with employment and unemployment returning to pre-pandemic levels. However, compared with OECD countries, labour market performance remains constrained by poor job quality, widespread informality, and persistent gender and regional disparities. Low labour productivity, a statutory minimum wage that is high relative to median earnings, elevated non-wage labour costs, and wage rigidities continue to constrain formal job creation, making productivity-enhancing policies and greater formalization the country’s main labour market priorities.

title: From Flexible Workloads to Verifiable Grid Resources: The Next Phase of Electricity–Computing Coordination
abstract: Artificial-intelligence (AI) data centres are growing electricity loads and potential sources of demand-side flexibility. Published work establishes that selected workloads can be modulated under specific conditions: a published demonstration on a cluster of 256 graphics processing units (GPUs) reported a 25% power reduction for three hours while maintaining the quality-of-service (QoS) target stated by its authors. That result is cluster-level evidence, not an independently verified whole-facility point-of-common-coupling (PCC) response or firm fleet-wide capacity; much of the wider literature is analytical, simulation-based or trace-based. The unresolved gap is a workload-aware route from potentially shiftable computations to a contractually specified, measured and repeatably deliverable grid service that also accounts for recovery and system impacts. This Perspective makes three contributions: it critically separates nominal potential, observed response and qualified grid delivery; proposes an assessment framework that links task eligibility, service-level agreements (SLAs), component attribution, measurement uncertainty, activation reliability and rebound to established demand-response measurement and verification (M&V); and identifies grid- and emissions-aware validation priorities. A transparent, hypothetical example illustrates why event-level capacity, storage losses, d…

title: Governing Climate Finance for Sustainability: A Systematic Review of Hierarchical, Network, and Market‐Based Models
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate finance governance is central to the mobilization and allocation of resources for effective and equitable climate action, although research on the different approaches to governance remains fragmented. This study systematically reviews the ways in which hierarchical, market‐based, and network governance shape climate finance in different institutional contexts. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta‐Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement, peer‐reviewed empirical studies published between 2015 and 2025 were identified through Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar, with searches completed on 30 July 2025. A total of 40 peer‐reviewed studies were included in the final thematic synthesis. Four themes emerged: (i) hierarchical governance: bureaucracy and effectiveness; (ii) market‐based governance: potential and risks; (iii) network governance: participation and accountability; and (iv) cross‐model issues: fragmentation, climate justice, and coordination. The findings point to different institutional trade‐offs: hierarchical governance strengthens legitimacy and accountability but may constrain flexibility; market governance enhances resource mobilization but may compromise distributive equity; and network governance promotes participation but may weaken coordination and accountability. title: ПРОГНОЗУВАННЯ РИЗИКУ ВТРАТИ ІТ-ТАЛАНТІВ І ВИБІР СТРАТЕГІЇ УТРИМАННЯ: ПСИХОЛОГІЧНА БЕЗПЕКА ТА ОРГАНІЗАЦІЙНА ДОВІРА ЯК УМОВИ ЗАСТОСУВАННЯ КАДРОВОЇ АНАЛІТИКИ
abstract: HR analytics in IT companies mostly describes the workforce but does not carry the forecast of talent loss risk through to the choice of interventions, while an unexplained estimate of an individual employee’s quit risk threatens psychological safety and trust – the very resources that retain employees. The article aims to substantiate a method for forecasting the risk of IT talent loss and choosing a retention strategy and to define the conditions under which the results of HR analytics can be applied. The study uses analysis and synthesis of the literature, economic and mathematical modeling (a discrete-time logistic survival model and mixed-integer linear programming) and a computational experiment on a synthetic test dataset generated by a prototype of the information and analytical system. A two-level forecasting architecture is proposed in which workforce demand, competency deficit and the risk of losing high-potential employees form a single loop; voluntary turnover risk enters managerial calculations as an expected cohort loss rather than as individual probabilities. Retention is formalized as one of five levers of a strategy portfolio – develop, hire, contract, retain, redeploy – in an optimization problem with a risk constraint, where infeasibility is reported as a set of conflicting constraints. title: A DUAL-INDEX FRAMEWORK FOR EVALUATING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF HRM DIGITALIZATION IN PUBLIC ORGANIZATIONS
abstract: The article develops a quantitative instrument for evaluating the effectiveness of HRM digitalization initiatives in public organizations, where technology investments must be justified under accountability constraints. Grounded in the Dynamic Capabilities theory, it proposes a dual-index framework: an Implementation Feasibility Index aggregating normalized scores across technological readiness, organizational adoption, engagement impact, and business outcomes, and a Confidence Index quantifying the statistical reliability of the evaluation. The indices form a quadrant matrix classifying initiatives as implement, pilot, extend testing, or reject. A simulated evaluation of three initiatives in a city administration, with Dirichlet-based weight sensitivity analysis, yields differentiated, actionable classifications and an explicit reliability bound for public managers.

title: ІДЕНТИФІКАЦІЯ ЗАГРОЗ ТА РИЗИКІВ СОЦІАЛЬНО-ЕКОНОМІЧНІЙ РЕІНТЕГРАЦІЇ ВЕТЕРАНІВ ВІЙНИ
abstract: The article identifies and systematizes threats and risks to the socio-economic reintegration of war veterans in Ukraine. The methodological framework of the study comprises systems and security-oriented approaches, methods of analysis and synthesis, scientific generalization, comparative analysis (incorporating elements of content analysis), classification, and a structural-logical method. Based on a comparative analysis of 25 studies conducted between 2022 and 2026 by various Ukrainian and international organizations – including the Ukrainian Veterans Foundation, the Centre for Sustainable Peace and Democratic Development, Veteran Hub, and Cedos, among others – a matrix of the thematic scope of reintegration issues was developed. This process identified common and distinct research emphases and established an empirical basis for identifying threats. The primary threats to the socio-economic reintegration of war veterans in Ukraine were identified and systematized, categorized into economic, social, psychological, rehabilitation-related, institutional-legal, and family/domestic domains. A model illustrating the transformation of threats into corresponding risks was constructed, highlighting the potential interconnections between them. title: ВПЛИВ ФАНДРАЙЗИНГУ НА ФІНАНСОВУ СТІЙКІСТЬ ПІДПРИЄМСТВ В УМОВАХ КРИЗИ
abstract: The article examines the role of fundraising as a modern instrument for attracting financial, material, informational and expert resources to support the financial stability of enterprises and organizations under crisis conditions and martial law. The relevance of fundraising mechanisms is substantiated for entities that face limited internal financial resources, declining solvency, disrupted business relations, increased financial risks, and the need to maintain socially significant or productive activities. The study summarizes approaches to the essence, subjects, objects, tasks and principles of fundraising, including transparency, accountability and voluntariness. Particular attention is paid to anti-crisis and wartime fundraising in Ukraine, whose specific features are determined by extensive humanitarian, defense, medical, evacuation and recovery needs, as well as by the active use of digital platforms and social networks. The relationship between fundraising and the key components of enterprise financial stability is considered, including liquidity, solvency, financial autonomy, profitability, resource provision, business activity, and the quality of relations with financial partners and counterparties. title: МОДЕЛЮВАННЯ ТА ПРОГНОЗУВАННЯ ПРОПОЗИЦІЇ ПРАЦІ ДОМОГОСПОДАРСТВАМИ З УРАХУВАННЯМ СКЛАДУ ДОМОГОСПОДАРСТВ ТА ХАРАКТЕРИСТИК ЇХ ЧЛЕНІВ В ПОВОЄННИЙ ПЕРІОД: МІЖНАРОДНИЙ ДОСВІД ТА СУЧАСНІ РЕАЛІЇ
abstract: The purpose of the article is to study the tools for modeling and forecasting labor supply by households in Ukraine, taking into account their composition, characteristics of members, and the peculiarities of intra-family decision-making to substantiate post-war employment policy in Ukraine. The methodological basis of the study is a systematic approach to the analysis of household labor supply and a comparative analysis of international experience in its modeling. To assess the impact of the composition of the household and the characteristics of its members, the use of statistical and mathematical methods is envisaged. The method of logical generalization allowed us to take into account the interdependence of decisions of household members regarding participation in employment. The abstract approach was used to forecast labor supply under different conditions of post-war recovery and determine the possibilities of applying the results in state employment policy. The article considers approaches to modeling and forecasting labor supply by households, taking into account their composition and characteristics of members in the context of post-war reconstruction of Ukraine. It summarizes international experience in using statistical-mathematical and microsimulation methods to analyze population participation in employment. title: Two‐Dimensional Materials for Moisture‐Enabled Electricity Generation: From Functional Roles to Performance Benchmarking
abstract: ABSTRACT Moisture‐enabled electricity generators (MEGs) harvest ambient water vapor as direct‐current electricity, yet their translation is constrained less by peak output than by control of coupled device processes. In open, humidity‐coupled architectures, water uptake and evaporation, ion redistribution, charge extraction, interfacial reactions, and mechanical deformation occur simultaneously and often compete. This Review examines two‐dimensional (2D) material‐based MEGs from an engineering perspective. Graphene‐based materials, MXenes, transition‐metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), and hybrid 2D systems are considered as functional components that define moisture‐access boundaries, regulate selective ion transport, reduce electronic and interfacial losses, and stabilize deformable or reactive interfaces. Emphasis is placed on how working mechanisms are implemented, optimized, and verified within device architectures, rather than on how individual materials increase isolated voltage or current values. Reported devices are further assessed in terms of humidity tolerance, operation lifetime, scalability, flexibility, and reporting completeness. By linking material function with boundary control, mechanical integration, and benchmarking readiness, this review outlines design principles for moving MEGs from condition‐sensitive demonstrations toward reproducible, durable, and deployabl…

title: РОЛЬ КАДРОВОГО МЕНЕДЖМЕНТУ В АНТИКРИЗОВОМУ УПРАВЛІННІ ПІДПРИЄМСТВАМИ ІНДУСТРІЇ ГОСТИННОСТІ
abstract: The article conducts a comprehensive study of personnel management as a strategic tool of anti-crisis management in the hospitality industry. The relevance of the topic is due to the high level of instability of the market environment, which is caused by global economic downturns, pandemics and, in particular, military operations in Ukraine. It is substantiated that the hospitality industry is the most vulnerable to external shocks due to direct dependence on tourist flows and income of the population, which requires rethinking traditional approaches to personnel management. The author determined that human capital is the foundation of the sustainability of the hotel and restaurant business. Within the framework of the anti-crisis approach, the key stages of working with personnel are highlighted, from in-depth diagnosis of personnel potential (loyalty and productivity assessment) to optimization of the organizational structure. The importance of avoiding unjustified layoffs in order to preserve unique competencies is emphasized, offering instead flexible forms of employment and retraining. Considerable attention is paid to the digital transformation of HR processes. The implementation of complex special programs for working with personnel, which automate routine operations and allow management to focus on strategic development, is considered. title: Risk Management in Decentralized Finance: Applications of Perpetual Continuous-Installment Options to Automated Market Makers and Lending Protocols
abstract: Decentralized Finance protocols face critical risk-management challenges that arise from their perpetual time horizon and optionality to exit. Liquidity providers in automated market makers (AMMs) suffer adverse selection costs known as loss-versus-rebalancing (LVR), while borrowers in lending protocols face abrupt liquidations during market volatility, incurring liquidation penalties. This paper presents a unified framework using perpetual American continuous-installment (CI) options to address both problems. For constant function AMMs, a liquidity position is mathematically modelled as a portfolio of perpetual CI options that delta-replicates the liquidity position at each point over a perpetual horizon. As a result, an equivalence is formed between the position's LVR and the option portfolio's funding fees (time value decay). This gives rise to actionable hedging strategies, including the construction of a liquidity position with an approximately constant instantaneous LVR rate under the constant-volatility GBM model and hedgeable by a unit CI option. For lending protocols, this paper proposes a liquidation-resistant lending mechanism where borrowers pay funding fees only when collateral value approaches critical thresholds, transforming discrete liquidation events into a continuous, graduated mechanism. title: Anti-Black Racism and Labour Market Exclusion: Racial Linguicism Among Skilled Black Francophone African Immigrants in Montreal, Quebec (Canada)
abstract: Canadian immigration policies are based on human capital discourses that prioritize the selection of skilled workers to contribute to the Canadian economy. Many African immigrants come from Francophone African countries, hoping to integrate socio-economically, with French language skills being a primary determining factor in their choice of Quebec. However, these skilled Black African immigrants face barriers when attempting to access pre-migration professions or employment commensurate with their qualifications. This paper illustrates how French language skills are erased by bilingualism or English fluency requirements in the Quebec labour market. The findings reveal that racialization and language, particularly the experience of being Black Francophone African immigrant, shape access to the Quebec labour market and affect employment opportunities by directing individuals toward often lower-skilled or unskilled occupations and excluding participants from their pre-migration professions and skilled employment. African immigrants also encountered accent discrimination, among other discriminatory practices, consequently highlighting the intersection of racialization, linguistic identity, and labour market inequality. title: Structural investigations of halide and polyhalide salts of 1-methyl-2,1,3-benzoselenadiazol-1-ium
abstract: To examine the effect of counteranion identity on chalcogen bonding (ChB), three new crystal structures were obtained by mixing N -methyl-2,1,3-benzoselenadiazolium chloride (C 7 H 7 N 2 Se + ·Cl − ) with N -bromosuccinimide, affording salts of a polybromide [1-methyl-2,1,3-benzoselenadiazol-1-ium bromide hemi(dibromine), C 7 H 7 N 2 Se + ·Br − ·0.5Br 2 , denoted [Se]Br 2 ·Br], a disordered bromide/chloride (1-methyl-2,1,3-benzoselenadiazol-1-ium bromide/chloride(0.33/0.67), C 7 H 7 N 2 Se + ·Br 0.33 /Cl 0.67 − , denoted [Se]Br/Cl) and a disordered chloride dichlorobromide/tribromide [1-methyl-2,1,3-benzoselenadiazol-1-ium hemichloride dichlorobromide/tribromide(0.365/0.135), C 7 H 7 N 2 Se + ·0.5Cl − ·0.365BrCl 2 − ·0.135Br 3 − , denoted [Se]Cl·BrCl 2 /Br 3 ]. title: Grounded in Experience: U.S. Midwestern Farmers’ Weather Forecasting Uses and Expectations
abstract: Abstract Weather and climate variability pose growing challenges for agricultural decision making. However, while technological changes have made weather forecasts more accessible than ever, those generating forecasts have incomplete information about how farmers use weather data. To understand how farmers interpret and use forecasts, we conducted 19 semi-structured interview sessions with 21 farmers in Illinois, Michigan, and Ohio. Results showed that farmers frequently used forecasts, particularly regarding precipitation extremes, frost, and heat stress, to influence not only planting and harvesting times, but also a wide variety of other farming practices. Farmers treated risk management as part of routine adaptation rather than crisis response. Farmers valued forecasts, but forecasts were not passively received and accepted. Rather, farmers triangulated forecasts from multiple sources, including official forecasts, decision-support tools, local weather stations, online platforms, and peer exchanges. They performed interpretive labor by integrating forecasts with field observations and experience and built trust in forecast sources over time by tracking forecast accuracy. Farmers wanted additional decision-relevant variables to be included in weather forecasts, but the desired variables differed based not only on crop type and farm scale, but also managerial approach, indivi…

title: A Verifiable Data-Fusion and Explainable AI Approach for Urban Flood-Risk and Carbon-Emission Forecasting with ISO/IEC-Aligned Validation
abstract: Municipal decision-support services increasingly combine open public data with machine learning, yet their data pipelines, models and explanations seldom come with evidence that an independent party can verify. This study proposes a verifiable framework that couples spatio-temporal data fusion, exactly explainable models and an executable validation protocol aligned with International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission (ISO/IEC) quality models, and demonstrates it on flood-risk and carbon-emission forecasting for the 25 administrative zones of Pyeongtaek, Republic of Korea. Twelve open sources, including weather, terrain, flood, electricity and emission-factor data, are aligned on a common zone-and-hour key in a fused store with provenance tags and declarative quality rules. A gradient-boosted flood-susceptibility model with 49 label-free terrain, river and building features is coupled with a rainfall trigger and explained by exact TreeSHAP, whereas a ridge model forecasts monthly electricity demand and CO2 and is explained by closed-form Shapley values. All 75 test cases, mapped to ISO/IEC 25012, 5259-2, 25010, 25059, TS 4213 and TS 6254, passed. title: Whey Protein Retention and β ‐Carotene Enrichment Improve the Antioxidant Capacity and Quality Stability of Traditional Sary Irimshik
abstract: ABSTRACT Sary irimshik is a traditional concentrated dairy product of Central Asia, but its antioxidant properties and response to whey protein retention remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated a functional variant produced by retaining whey proteins during processing and adding provitamin A ( β ‐carotene) after high‐temperature treatment. Effects of milk type, treatment, and storage duration (1, 7, and 14 days), with an additional 365‐day validation, were assessed using physicochemical, antioxidant, sensory, and microbiological measurements. Goat‐milk products showed higher protein and dry‐matter contents and less whey separation, while cow‐milk samples generally showed higher yields in the Control and Additive 2 treatments. β ‐Carotene addition was associated with improved color and antioxidant characteristics. Several free amino acids showed higher concentrations in analyzed extracts on day 7, followed by decreases by day 14. Sensory scores remained high (4.9–5.0). At days 7 and 14, total aerobic microbial counts were ≤ 31 CFU/g and coliforms were not detected. After 365 days, counts reached 1–3 × 10 3 CFU/g, while coliforms remained undetected. These findings support the potential of whey protein retention and β ‐carotene enrichment to improve selected quality characteristics of Sary Irimshik.

title: Impedance-Informed Battery Degradation Modeling for Sustainability Assessment: Reliability-Aware Screening Using Classical, Pseudo-FO, and Mittag–Leffler Models
abstract: Reliable lifetime estimates are essential when battery degradation models are used to calculate environmental indicators normalized by lifetime energy throughput. This study evaluates a cycle-only benchmark and three impedance-informed formulations (classical, pseudo-fractional-order, and Mittag–Leffler fractional-order) using causally matched discharge and EIS data from 12 NASA batteries. Under the 80/20 chronological hold-out, the best of the three impedance-informed formulations achieved lower SOH prediction RMSE than the cycle-only benchmark in 10 of 12 cells; however, this best-of-three comparison is descriptive because model ranking and evaluation used the same hold-out observations. To examine pre-EOL forecasting without future-data leakage through historical backtesting, eight pre-EOL landmark backtests were conducted across four batteries using truncated histories. The four models satisfied a 20% EOL-relative error tolerance in 2/8, 1/8, 4/8, and 5/8 cases, respectively, whereas the corresponding RUL-relative tolerance was satisfied in 0/8, 0/8, 3/8, and 3/8 cases. The five full-data Reliable Observed outcomes, therefore, represent retrospective EOL agreement rather than independently validated lifetime forecasts. The environmental findings should consequently be interpreted as screening-level, model-dependent energy-throughput scenarios rather than demonstrated emissi…

title: Sustainable Zinc Fertilization of Lettuce: Biochar-Mediated Zn Availability from Conventional and Battery-Recovered Sources
abstract: Abstract Zinc (Zn) is an essential micronutrient in plants, but excessive fertilization may lead to soil accumulation and imbalances. This study evaluated the combined effects of Zn source (ZnSO4 and Zn recovered from spent alkaline and Zn/C batteries via glycine/ammonia leaching, Zn-GLY), application rate (2 and 20 mg Zn·kg–1), and biochar amendment on lettuce growth and Zn accumulation. Biochar significantly increased fresh biomass, with gains ranging from 45.7 to 79.2% compared to unamended soils. At the high Zn dose, biochar reduced leaf Zn concentrations by 53.5% (ZnSO4) and 78.7% (Zn–GLY), while maintaining root Zn levels comparable to those in low-dose treatments. Biochar reduced CaCl2-extractable Zn and decreased Zn accumulation in leaves at the highest Zn application rate while increasing microbial biomass. Glycine/ammonia extracts from spent batteries performed comparably to conventional ZnSO4 as a fertilizer source under the conditions tested. These findings provide preliminary evidence that Zn recovered from spent batteries may represent a promising alternative Zn source for crop fertilization under controlled conditions. Further research under field conditions is required to assess its long-term agronomic performance, environmental safety, and practical applicability.

title: Imaginative literature as a vehicle of narrative soft power
abstract: The article examines fiction as a potential resource of soft power and a means of shaping the international perception of national culture. The theoretical framework draws on the concepts of soft power, strategic narrative, and narrative transportation. A conceptual and analytical model of literary influence is proposed, encompassing three interrelated mechanisms: sensory richness, emotional universality, and symbolic integration. Drawing on Ukrainian literature from different historical periods, the article analyzes how national experience, collective memory, cultural identity, and moral choice are represented in literary works. The concept of “the power of cultural presence” is introduced to describe the potential of literary texts to sustain long-term interest in a culture and deepen its understanding beyond national boundaries. The role of translation, publishing, cultural institutions, and reader reception is also examined. The article emphasizes that literature does not guarantee changes in political beliefs but creates opportunities for a multifaceted understanding of culture.

title: The Effect of Sustainability Practices, Governance Quality, and Financial Performance on Investment Strategy Formulation
abstract: Investment strategy formulation requires integrating sustainability practices, governance quality, and financial performance, particularly in high-risk industries such as the oil sector. This study examines how these three factors influence investment strategy formulation. A quantitative approach was employed using corporate bank statement data from October to December 2025. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression, including partial t-tests, a simultaneous F-test, and the coefficient of determination. The results indicate that sustainability practices have a significant negative effect on investment strategy formulation (β = −0.412; p = 0.006), while financial performance has a significant positive effect (β = 0.536; p < 0.001). Governance quality has a positive but insignificant effect (β = 0.128; p = 0.081). Simultaneously, the three variables significantly influence investment strategy formulation (F = 18.726; p < 0.001), explaining 61.7% of its variation (R² = 0.617). These findings highlight the importance of financial performance and expenditure control in investment planning, while emphasizing the need to evaluate governance by effectiveness rather than transaction frequency to support more disciplined investment decisions.

title: Effectiveness of Enhanced Reading Comprehension Through Active Reading Strategy (ERCARS) for Reading Comprehension among Grade 10 Students
abstract: This study examined the effectiveness of the Enhanced Reading Comprehension through Active Reading Strategy (ERCARS), particularly its questioning dimension, in improving reading comprehension among Grade 10 students. A one-group pretest–posttest design was employed involving 45 purposively selected frustration-level readers at Pagsabungan National High School, Mandaue City, Philippines, during School Year 2026–2027. The intervention consisted of 12 structured sessions incorporating teacher modeling, guided questioning, worksheets, and independent practice. Data were collected using the Philippine Informal Reading Inventory, ERCARS worksheets, and a student experience survey and analyzed through descriptive statistics, a paired-samples t-test, and thematic categorization. Results revealed that the mean reading comprehension score increased from 47% to 81%, representing a 34-percentage-point improvement. The difference was statistically significant (t = 7.65, p < 0.001). Students reported positive experiences (M = 3.72), particularly regarding comprehension, guided instruction, and confidence in questioning. However, question formulation, identification of essential information, and unfamiliar vocabulary remained challenges. The study concludes that ERCARS is a promising supplementary intervention for struggling readers. Integrating structured questioning into regular reading in…

title: Marketing digital y posicionamiento empresarial: revisión sistemática de la evidencia científica en contextos organizacionales
abstract: In recent years, digital transformation has profoundly changed how organizations interact with their customers and develop competitive advantages. Against this backdrop, digital marketing has become a fundamental tool for strengthening business positioning through the use of social media, content marketing, digital advertising, and data analytics. The objective of this systematic review was to analyze the influence of digital marketing on business positioning based on available scientific evidence. To this end, the PRISMA 2020 guidelines were followed, and studies published between 2021 and 2025 were reviewed across academic databases such as Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, SciELO, and Google Scholar. After applying selection criteria, 30 studies related to the topic were analyzed. The results show that digital marketing strategies foster brand recognition, increase business visibility, strengthen customer relationships, and contribute to the development of sustainable competitive advantages. Furthermore, it was identified that social media, content marketing, digital segmentation, and data analytics are the most widely used tools for enhancing organizational positioning. It is concluded that digital marketing represents a strategic resource for business competitiveness, although its effectiveness depends on factors such as the organization's digital capabilities, market…

title: Mitigation strategy for volume deformation of concrete with tunnel‐excavated rock as aggregate: Combined effects of acrylamide and CaO ‐ MgO expansive agent
abstract: Abstract A massive volume of excavated rocks has been generated with the development of underground space, while many construction projects are faced with the scarcity of natural aggregates. However, the utilization of tunnel excavated rocks as aggregates may degrade the early‐age deformation behavior of concrete, yet it still lacks sufficient understanding on this aspect. This research investigates the combined incorporation of acrylamide (AM) as an in situ polymerization agent and CaO‐MgO expansive agent (CMEA) to control the autogenous shrinkage of such tunnel‐slag concrete. Results show that the incorporation of CMEA converted autogenous shrinkage to evident expansion for early‐age concrete, thus mitigating the late‐age volume deformation effectively. With the increased MgO proportion in CMEA, the shrinkage‐compensation function can be mildly weakened, while the mechanical strength is enhanced. The incorporation of AM alone increased the internal relative humidity and contributed to microstructural refinement. Within the investigated dosage range, the optimized combination of AM and CMEA in concrete exhibited a balance between shrinkage deformation and mechanical properties, reaching a peak expansion of 183.6 με with 10.3% higher compressive strength at 28 days than the control concrete. Consequently, the combined use of AM and CMEA is proposed as an innovative mitigation s…

title: Community-based management of nocturnal polyuria in older adults: protocol for a multicenter randomized controlled trial of a circadian-aligned dosing strategy using continuous digital monitoring
abstract: Background Nocturnal polyuria (NP) is a common age-related condition and a major contributor to nocturia, affecting sleep, quality of life, and healthy aging. Although desmopressin is an established pharmacological option, the risk of hyponatremia and the need for safety monitoring may limit its use in older adults. Guifu Dihuang Pill (GFDH) and Jinkui Shenqi Pill (JKSQ) are traditional Chinese medicine formulations used for urinary symptoms, but their efficacy and safety in NP and the optimal timing and duration of treatment remain unclear. This study aims to evaluate two dosing schedules for GFDH and JKSQ and explore response-guided treatment duration. Methods This multicenter, randomized, open-label, parallel-controlled trial will recruit 360 participants with NP from 11 community hospitals. Participants will receive GFDH ( n = 240) or JKSQ ( n = 120), with randomization within each formulation group to evening once-daily dosing or twice-daily dosing in a 1:1 ratio. Both regimens provide the same total daily dose of the assigned formulation. Treatment will last up to 8 weeks, with discontinuation permitted when predefined efficacy or complete remission criteria are met. The primary outcome is nocturnal urination frequency (NUF). title: HSWL : A Deep Reinforcement Learning‐Driven Wear Leveling and Cache Management Strategy for Hybrid Flash SSDs
abstract: ABSTRACT Data volumes continue to grow, and distributed storage systems assembled from large numbers of SSDs now form the backbone of modern data centers. Hybrid flash SSDs, which integrate high‐performance, long‐endurance SLC caches with cost‐effective, high‐density QLC main storage, achieve a compelling trade‐off among capacity, cost, and performance. However, the substantial discrepancy in P/E cycle endurance between the SLC cache and the QLC main storage region easily induces severe cross‐region wear imbalance, which shortens the overall lifespan of the SSD. This paper proposes HSWL, a cross‐region wear‐leveling and cache‐management strategy tailored for hybrid SLC/QLC flash SSDs. HSWL builds a Cache Decision Agent on the DQN framework. The agent observes the average wear, utilization, and wear‐distribution statistics of both regions and, at each decision point, chooses between evicting cold data to QLC and performing intra‐SLC garbage collection. The agent is paired with a numerically robust reward function and an LRU‐based victim‐selection policy. Experiments are conducted on the custom‐developed HybridSSDsim simulator using seven real‐world workload traces against three baselines: Circular‐log, a threshold heuristic, and a Samsung‐style RL‐based SLC cache manager. All results are averaged over five independent runs with different random seeds, and standard deviations are…

title: The Role of Postponement Strategy in Modern Logistics: Practical Applications and the Impact of Digitalization
abstract: The increasing complexity of global supply chains and rapidly changing consumer demands require new levels of flexibility and adaptability from logistics systems and players. Postponement is a logistics and supply chain strategy in which certain activities or decisions (such as final manufacturing steps, packaging, configuration, or even shipping direction) are postponed until the last possible moment, until demand is known with certainty. The study aims to explore the application of the postponement strategy in Hungary and examine the extent to which Industry 4.0 technologies and digitalization contribute to its implementation. The research is based on questionnaire responses from logistics managers at 27 Hungarian industrial companies. According to the results, the strategy is not widely used in Hungary, appearing most often in final assembly and packaging, with reducing inventory levels and managing demand fluctuations among its objectives. Although there is a tendency for a relationship between digitalization and postponement, no statistically significant correlation can be confirmed. The cluster analysis identified three company profiles: digitally advanced companies that use postponement; companies with moderate digitalization that use postponement to some extent; and companies with low digitalization that do not use postponement. The results show that digitalization alon…

title: Uso de la inteligencia artificial en la toma de decisiones estratégicas empresariales: una revisión sistemática
abstract: El artículo que se realizó tuvo como principal objetivo evaluar, por medio de una revisión sistemática, el impacto del uso de la inteligencia artificial en la toma de decisiones estratégicas empresariales y así establecer sus efectos sobre la precisión, eficiencia y competitividad organizacional, mientras sus objetivos específicos fueron “Determinar que enfoques de la inteligencia artificial se han ilustrado en el contexto de la toma de decisiones estratégicas empresariales” y “Determinar que aplicaciones de la inteligencia artificial se han ilustrado en el contexto de la toma de decisiones estratégicas empresariales”. Asimismo, siguiendo las directrices de la declaración PRISMA 2020, se realizó en las bases de datos Web of Science, Science Direct, Springer y Redalyc una búsqueda exhaustiva, abarcando el período de 2024 a 2026. Se identificaron. Se identificaron 270 registros iniciales, de los cuales 32 articulos lograron cumplir con los criterios de inclusión y fueron sometidos a un análisis de síntesis cualitativa con el apoyo del software ATLAS.ti. La evidencia sugiere que la IA mejora significativamente la capacidad analítica y la eficiencia organizacional, pero su efectividad depende de factores como la gobernanza ética, la calidad de los datos y la integración con el juicio humano. Se concluye que la IA se define como una capacidad estratégica que fortalece y no reemplaza…

title: The Complementary Role of Open Innovation and R&D: A Pathway to Eco‐Innovation
abstract: ABSTRACT Why do firms with comparable levels of external knowledge sourcing achieve fundamentally different eco‐innovation outcomes? This study examines how green and non‐green R&D interact with inbound open innovation strategies to shape the intensity of eco‐innovation implementation. Although prior research has largely treated R&D as homogeneous, we distinguish between green and non‐green R&D and argue that each develops distinct, domain‐specific absorptive capacities. Drawing on absorptive capacity theory and the natural resource‐based view, we argue that green R&D builds domain‐specific absorptive capacity that enables firms to translate external knowledge into competitive environmental capabilities more effectively than non‐green R&D. Using merged data from 709 Irish firms, we employ negative binomial regression to test for complementarity and substitutability between internal R&D and different forms of external knowledge sourcing. Capital‐intensive investments in software act as strategic complements to internal R&D, with this complementary relationship being stronger for green R&D. Conversely, contracting out R&D substitutes for green R&D for particular eco‐innovation outcomes, potentially limiting the development of firm‐specific environmental capabilities. These findings demonstrate that strategic alignment between inbound open innovation and green R&D is critical to b…

title: اثر استراتيجيية (PQ5R) في التعبير الكتابي عند طالبات الصف الاول المتوسط
abstract: يهدف البحث الحالي الى التعرف على: " اثر استراتيجيية (PQ5R) في التعبير الكتابي عند طالبات الصف الاول المتوسط" للتأكد من الهدف صاغت الباحثة الفرضية الاتية " لا يوجد فرق ذو دلالة احصائية عند مستوى الدلالة (0.05) بين متوسط درجات الطالبات اللاتي درسن مادة التعبير الكتابي وفق خطوات استراتيجية (PQ5R) للمجموعة التجريبية، وطالبات المجموعة الضابطة اللاتي درسن المادة نفسها وفق خطوات الطريقة التقليدية في اختبار التعبير الكتابي البعدي"، تكون مجتمع البحث من طالبات الصف الاول المتوسط في المديرية العامة لتربية محافظة بغداد الكرخ/الثالثة،وقد اختارت الباحثة بالطريقة العشوائية البسيطة مدرسة النخيل للبنات لتمثل عينة البحث، اذ تكونت المجموعة التجريبية من (35) طالبة،بينما تكونت المجموعة الضابطة من (36) طالبة، واعدت الباحثة اختبار التعبير الكتابي وكان عنوان التعبير هو "الاهتمام بالتراث والمحافظة عليه"، واعتمدت معيار التصحيح (الربيعي،1997)، وبعد ان تم تطبيق الاختبار تبين تفوق المجموعة التجريبية على المجموعة الضابطة.

Bearing-grouped, stage-resolved uncertainty assessment for remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings
abstract: Abstract Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of rolling bearings supports condition-based maintenance and risk-informed operation. However, point-estimation error metrics and marginal interval coverage do not show whether uncertainty is reliable across physical bearings or near failure. This study develops and evaluates a bearing-grouped, stage-resolved uncertainty quantification framework that retains competitive point accuracy while revealing stage-specific calibration and support saturation. The framework combines a causal-in-time state-aware Extra Trees predictor with bearing-grouped, locally normalized asymmetric conformal calibration. All transformations, state probabilities, point and scale models, and conformal quantiles are fitted within bearing-disjoint training folds, and the same three seeds are used for inner out-of-fold construction and outer prediction. All 15 complete XJTU-SY trajectories and 17 complete PHM 2012 trajectories are assessed using five repetitions of three-fold nested bearing-level cross-validation, with leave-one-condition-out analysis as a descriptive robustness check. The state-aware predictor yields bearing-balanced normalized root mean square error values of 0.289 on XJTU-SY and 0.214 on PHM 2012, reductions of 2.3% and 4.9% relative to direct Extra Trees; PHM MAE decreases by 9.1%. Enhanced Discriminatory Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading for Privacy-Aware Interactions via KNN-Guided Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading based on the multi-leader multi-follower Stackelberg game (MLMFG) enables decentralized interactions between prosumers and consumers while limiting the disclosure of sensitive information by P2P agents. However, restricted information exchange may reduce the strategic awareness of individual agents, leading to inefficient decision-making. To address this challenge, this study developed a P2P energy trading model with improved local strategic decision-making mechanisms supported by graph neural networks (GNNs) with k-nearest neighbor (KNN)-guided graph formulations. First, the KNN clustering mechanism classified neighbors with the closest financial similarities and most appropriate physical connections, thereby localizing coordination and reducing message-passing synchronization. Then, the GNN with a KNN-based neighbor-selection mechanism was designed to support the decision-making process of P2P agents, thereby enhancing their strategic awareness under the MLMFG. Numerical experiments were conducted based on the South Korean retail electricity market to verify the performance of the proposed method. The results demonstrated that the proposed method achieved a 95.07% improved runtime compared with conventional discriminatory P2P energy trading with the MLMFG while also improving voltage-limit compliance and a favorable tradeoff between incomplet…

title: Mycobacterial phenolic glycolipid triggers ATP-mediated neuronal signalling and cough
Platform Information Design and Competitive Price Targeting
abstract: We study platform information design, in which a platform provides information about individual consumers, enabling sellers to set targeted prices. Because targetable information partitions the market and might intensify seller competition, what information should be provided remains an empirical question. We collect novel microdata from Steam, the dominant PC video game platform, and use granular consumer purchase and usage data to estimate their heterogeneous demand for video games. We then develop an equilibrium targeted pricing model to simulate counterfactual outcomes under all possible information designs. We demonstrate that the profit-maximizing information design—which distinguishes heterogeneous consumer types while accounting for the design’s equilibrium impact—yields substantially higher profits compared to demand-based heuristics that ignore the equilibrium impact.

title: Sotatercept Improves Right Heart Mechanics Despite Reduced Myocardial Contractility in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A Prospective Exercise Hemodynamic Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: The right ventricular (RV) response to pressure overload is a crucial determinant of outcomes in pulmonary arterial (PA) hypertension. Sotatercept improves clinical outcomes, but its effects on the right ventricle have been inconsistent. We evaluated the effects of sotatercept on load-independent measures of RV contractility, RV–PA coupling, and right heart deformation at rest and exertion in patients with PA hypertension. METHODS: In this prospective trial among participants with PA hypertension recruited between July 2024 and May 2025, we performed simultaneous echocardiography and invasive pressure measurements during rest and exercise to evaluate changes in RV contractility (end-systolic elastance [Ees]), afterload (PA elastance [Ea]), RV–PA coupling (ratio of arterial Ea to Ees), and right heart deformation, including RV and right atrial strain, before and after 24 weeks of sotatercept using mixed models. RESULTS: Among 30 participants (n=21; 70% female; mean age, 49.3 years [SD 13.5]), sotatercept decreased PA Ea. These changes were associated with reduced RV contractility, PA pulsatility index, and the maximal rate of RV pressure increase over time (dP/dt max ; P <0.001 for all). The decrease in Ees was associated with a decrease in PA Ea (r=+0.70 [95% CI, +0.44 to +0.85]; P <0.0001) with preserved RV–PA coupling (mean difference, +0.08 [95% CI, −0.11 to +0.2…

title: High-frequency monitoring of SO 2 plumes from moderate-scale volcanic eruptions using a synergy of GEO and LEO satellites: a case study of the 2024 Kanlaon eruption
abstract: Satellite remote sensing is crucial for monitoring volcanic sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) globally. However, the rapid evolution of volcanic plumes necessitates high-frequency observations, which typical twice-daily overpasses of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) sensors fail to capture. To address this limitation, this study presents a synergistic Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) and LEO observation framework. Specifically, we show the first quantitative SO 2 retrieval from a GEO hyperspectral infrared sounder (FY-4B/GIIRS), using an optimal-estimation-based retrieval algorithm. Because current and upcoming GEO infrared sounders lack the strong ν 3 absorption band, our algorithm uniquely leverages the weaker ν 1 absorption band. Simulation experiments indicate that the theoretical detection limit (retrieval error >100 %) is 3 DU for plumes at 10 km altitude. During the June 2024 Kanlaon eruption, GIIRS captured early, high-concentration plume dynamics, though tracking diluted plumes remained challenging. Crucially, it provided the earliest satellite detection by continuously monitoring the initial nighttime burst (posterior error of 53.7±24.1 %), filling critical temporal gaps left by ultraviolet sensors. Combined with LEO (HIRAS, IASI, CrIS, TROPOMI and MLS) and GEO sensor (GEMS), the synergistic framework achieved high frequency quantification of SO 2 mass loading and transport pathways. We est…
