Relationship between salvage strategy and outcomes in patients with CBF or NPM1 -mutated AML and first molecular relapse
abstract: Abstract Given the uncertainty regarding the optimal management of molecular relapse in patients with core-binding factor (CBF) or NPM1-mutated acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we retrospectively analyzed the outcome of 121 adults over 18 years old from 12 centers with CBF (n = 28) or NPM1-mutated (n = 93) AML and first molecular relapse according to the salvage strategy used (up-front allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation [allo-HCT; n = 19], intensive chemotherapy [IC; n = 21], and venetoclax and azacitidine [VEN-AZA; n = 70]) and other strategies (n = 11; including AZA, gemtuzumab ozogamicin, and selective inhibitors). At 3 years, overall survival (OS) was not statistically different among the 4 groups (84% for up-front allo-HCT vs 81% for IC vs 79% for VEN-AZA vs 64% for others; P = .31). Allo-HCT was received by 98 (81%) patients, with a cumulative incidence of allo-HCT at 12 weeks of 100% for up-front allo-HCT, 71% for IC, 73% for VEN-AZA, and 82% for others (P< .001), with better outcomes in patients who underwent transplantation. In patients who received allo-HCT, type of salvage therapy was not statistically associated with post-HCT relapse, relapse-free survival, or OS. Our data suggest that up-front allo-HCT is a valuable option, if feasible, whereas other salvage strategies are associated with favorable outcomes and relatively low nonrelapse mortality after a…

title: Right Ventricular Reverse Remodeling Without Pulmonary Vascular Unloading During Sotatercept Therapy: An Invasive Pressure–Volume Loop Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sotatercept improves hemodynamics and functional capacity in pulmonary arterial hypertension; however, its direct actions on the right ventricle (RV) remain poorly understood. We investigated whether sotatercept exerts intrinsic RV protective effects beyond pulmonary vascular unloading. METHODS: In this registry-based cohort study, 28 consecutive patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension between April 2024 and September 2025 underwent right-heart catheterization with conductance-catheter RV pressure–volume analysis and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging before sotatercept initiation and again after a median of 6.1 months of treatment. Hemodynamic nonresponse was defined as a decrease in mean pulmonary arterial pressure by <10%. Reproducibility was tested in 2 independent sotatercept-treated cohorts (SPECTRA [Sotatercept Phase 2 Exploratory Clinical Trial in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension], n=20, cardiac magnetic resonance; Cologne, n=20, echocardiography). RESULTS: Among 28 patients (17 [61%] female; median age, 48 [IQR, 34–67] years), 21 (75%) were responders and 7 (25%) nonresponders. In responders, sotatercept significantly decreased mean pulmonary arterial pressure (52.0 [IQR, 49.0–65.0] to 39.0 [IQR, 32.0–42.0] mm Hg; P <0.001) and pulmonary vascular resistance (10.7±3.9 to 6.7±2.3 Wood units; P <0.001) without changing cardiac output, reduced RV end-diast…

title: Germline Genetic Variants and Epilepsy Surgery Response
The Effectiveness of Price Anchors and Second-hand Luxury Products
abstract: This study examines the influence of heuristics within the consumption of second-hand luxury items. Prices on second-hand retail platforms were operationalized to test the anchoring heuristic. A mixed-methods design was employed. The quantitative part involved an online experiment utilizing a simulated second-hand luxury purchase scenario to assess the anchoring effect. The qualitative part consisted of semi-structured expert interviews. The data reveal the influence of the anchoring heuristic being attenuated within the luxury sector but significant and in part contingent upon consumers’ per-purchase internal state. The analysis further suggests that price is not the only critical determinant of consumer choice.

User experience of a custom augmented reality-based exergame for children with cerebral palsy and acquired brain injuries
abstract: Abstract Conventional pediatric rehabilitation for cerebral palsy (CP) or acquired brain injury (ABI) prioritizes motor outcomes, often neglecting cognitive deficits and their interplay. Sessions are often perceived as repetitive and demotivating, reducing engagement. Immersive exergaming, especially through augmented reality (AR), enables simultaneous cognitive-motor training in safe, interactive settings. There is little evidence on immersive exergames for these children, and no immersive AR exergames target cognitive-motor rehabilitation or report on user experience (UX). This study aims to assess the overall UX of a purpose-built immersive AR exergame for children with brain injuries. Twenty-nine children (11.8 ± 1.6 years; 12 CP/17 ABI) participated in two sessions using the Microsoft HoloLens2, each involving one cognitive-motor AR game (AR Corsi and AR Zoo). UX was assessed through standardized questionnaires: System Usability Scale (usability), Technology Acceptance Model (acceptance), AttrakDiff (perceived experience quality), MeCue (emotions), Intrinsic Motivation Inventory (motivation), and Rating scale of Perceived Exertion for Children (fatigue). The exergame was well accepted and perceived as easy to use. Scores for motivation, emotions, and perceived experience quality were high and positive. title: Joint Bayesian Inference of Parameter and Discretization Error Uncertainties in ODE Models
abstract: Abstract. We address the problem of Bayesian inference for parameters in ordinary differential equation (ODE) models based on observational data. Conventional approaches in this setting typically rely on numerical solvers such as the Euler or Runge–Kutta methods. However, these methods generally do not account for the discretization error induced by discretizing the ODE model. We propose a Bayesian inference framework for ODE models that explicitly quantifies discretization errors. Our method models discretization error as a random variable and performs Bayesian inference on both ODE parameters and variances of the randomized discretization errors, referred to as the discretization error variance. A key idea of our approach is the introduction of a Markov prior on the temporal evolution of the discretization error variances, enabling the inference problem to be formulated as a state-space model. Furthermore, we propose a specific form of the Markov prior that arises naturally from standard discretization error analysis. This prior depends on the step size [Formula: see text] in the numerical solver, and we discuss its asymptotic property as [Formula: see text]. Numerical experiments illustrate that the proposed method can simultaneously quantify uncertainties in both the ODE parameters and the discretization errors, and can produce posterior distributions over the parameters wi…

title: Comparing Calibration Windows for Conformal Prediction of Monthly US Electricity Retail Sales
abstract: This study compared calibration windows for prediction intervals of monthly United States electricity retail sales. Data from January 2001 to December 2025 were used to evaluate one- and three-month-ahead forecasts over 2016–2025. Exponential smoothing in state space form (ETS) was the main model, and seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (SARIMA) provided a robustness check. Native ETS intervals were compared with conformal intervals based on the latest 24 errors (CP24), the latest 60 errors (CP60) and an expanding window. Performance was measured by coverage, mean width, mean Winkler score and width stability at 80% and 95% nominal coverage. For one-month ETS forecasts at 80%, CP24 increased coverage from 71.67% to 80.00%, but mean width increased by 14.69% and the mean Winkler score increased. At 95%, CP24 reached 95.00% coverage, with a 32.76% increase in mean width. Native ETS intervals had the lowest mean Winkler score at three months at both levels. The expanding window had the most stable ETS widths. For SARIMA, CP60 increased coverage and mean width at both horizons and nominal levels, while its mean Winkler score changed little. Width stability improved in only one of the four settings. These results suggest that improved coverage needs to be considered together with the increase in width and the change in the mean Winkler score.

title: The Impact of U.S. Monetary Policy Shocks on Emerging Market Exchange Rates-The Buffering Effect of the Level of Foreign Exchange Reserves
abstract: Since 2022, the Federal Reserve has continuously raised interest rates significantly in response to inflation, triggering global capital flows and severe exchange rate fluctuations. Emerging market currencies are generally facing depreciation pressure, with significant differences in depreciation rates among countries. This paper investigates the direct effect of an unforeseen Federal Reserve monetary policy Shocks to Exchange Rates in Emerging Markets. Data from 12 places were collected.countries—including India, China, Singapore, Turkey, Argentina, and Thailand—utilizing data on exchange rates, GDP, CPI, and foreign-currency reserves from the IMF, and FOMC announcements. A model was built with the rate of local currency. Depreciation of US dollars is used as the dependent variable, and the ratio of Foreign-currency reserves-to-GDP ratio, GDP growth rate and inflation rate. Based on the above data, rom the first quarter of 2014 to the fourth quarter of 2024, a median The total depreciation rates of these countries were not the same; only China reached 14.1 percent. In addition, there is a positive correlation between the size of quarterly interest rate hikes and the median cumulative exchange rate depreciation.

title: From Pop‑Up to Permanent: Market Experimentation and the Experiential Turn in Chinese Consumption
abstract: China's consumer market is shifting from transaction‑oriented retail toward experiential consumption. Pop‑up retail has become mainstream commercial infrastructure, and the debut economy is now a national strategic priority that supports brands as they move from temporary market experiments to a lasting commercial presence. Existing research offers little process‑based analysis of this transition under debut‑economy policies. Research on consumer experience and management strategy also remains disconnected. Through a multiple‑case study of To Summer, On, and Photoism, this article examines how temporary experimentation leads to permanent retail. The analysis identifies feedback‑driven, staged progression as the central mechanism. Brands use pop‑ups or slow pop‑ups as low‑cost experiments, gather market signals in actual consumption settings, and assess whether those signals justify further investment in permanent operations. Debut‑economy policies lower transition costs and help brands near the investment threshold proceed, while market experimentation remains central to the decision. The article brings together the experience economy, pop‑up retail, and the debut economy in a single analytical framework. Its five interrelated theoretical propositions explain the retail innovation pathway from temporary experimentation to permanent stores.

title: "Melissopalynologyin India: Integrating Pollen Analysis, Honey Authentication, and Market Potential"
abstract: Melissopalynology, the study of pollen in honey, is an essential tool for assessing the botanical and geographical origins of honey, ensuring quality control, and combating adulteration. While extensively researched in Europe and the United States, India has made significant strides in melissopalynological studies, particularly in identifying key bee-foraging plants and understanding seasonal variations in pollen availability. India's rich floral biodiversity contributes to a diverse range of pollen types in honey, reflecting distinct regional and ecological influences from the Himalayan foothills to coastal zones. Despite advancements, standardized protocols for pollen identification, honey authentication, and quality control remain underdeveloped. This review consolidates historical and contemporary studies on melissopalynology in India, emphasizing its role in strengthening the apiculture industry, ensuring honey purity, and enhancing market value. By integrating traditional pollen analysis with modern techniques such as DNA barcoding, HPLC, and GIS-based floral mapping, India can further advance its honey industry to meet domestic and international quality standards.

title: A Study on the Short-Term Impact of Inflation Levels and Geopolitical Conflicts on International Spot Gold Prices
abstract: In the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, many countries have implemented accommodative monetary policies, and inflationary pressures have continued to emerge. With the successive outbreaks of the Russia–Ukraine conflict and the Israel–Palestine conflict, demand for safe-haven assets in the investment market has increased, leading to significant fluctuations in gold prices. Although gold serves as both an inflation hedge and a safeguard against geopolitical risks, most existing studies analyse only the impact of inflation or geopolitical tensions on gold prices in isolation, and few examine the distinct short-term impacts arising from their interplay. This paper takes gold as its subject and, by combining relevant literature with price movements during typical events, analyses how inflation and geopolitical conflicts influence gold prices. The findings indicate that inflation provides long-term support for gold prices, with a longer-lasting impact, geopolitical conflicts, by contrast, can only temporarily drive up gold prices, which tend to fall back once market sentiment stabilises. Should inflationary pressures and geopolitical risks occur simultaneously, fluctuations in gold prices are likely to intensify further. London spot gold offers comprehensive trading data, making it suitable for analysing short-term price movements caused by external risks, the findings of this study ma…

title: Impact of ESG Rating Disparities on Equity Financing Costs: An Empirical Analysis of the A-Share Market in China
abstract: This paper selects A-share listed companies in China from 2019 to 2023 as the research sample and constructs an ESG rating divergence indicator based on the ratings of three domestic agencies—Huasheng, Shangdao Ronglv, and Menglang—to empirically examine the impact of ESG rating divergence on the cost of equity capital. Using a panel fixed-effects model, the study finds that domestic ESG rating divergence significantly increases the cost of equity capital, with a coefficient of 0.0163 and a p-value of 0.022, confirming Hypothesis H1. Furthermore, the effect exhibits source heterogeneity: domestic divergence exerts a significant positive effect, whereas foreign divergence, constructed based on Bloomberg, FTSE Russell, and MSCI ratings, shows no significant impact (−0.0012, p=0.847). When both types of divergence are included simultaneously, domestic divergence remains significant (0.0180, p=0.028), while foreign divergence remains insignificant (−0.0019, p=0.757), confirming Hypothesis H2 and indicating that domestic divergence is the key factor affecting financing costs, while foreign rating information has limited transmission efficiency in the Chinese market. The main conclusions remain robust across multiple robustness tests, including sample screening relaxation and winsorization. This paper expands the existing literature on the economic consequences of ESG rating divergen…

title: Building productivity in culinary MSMEs through market orientation: the mediating role of value co-creation on marketing performance
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the impact of responsive and proactive market orientation on the marketing performance of culinary micro, small and medium-sized culinary enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia, positioning marketing performance as a proxy for productivity. Specifically, it explores the mediating role of value co-creation, a mechanism that has received limited empirical attention in prior research. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a quantitative survey approach involving 319 respondents, comprising managers or owners of MSMEs. To evaluate the proposed hypotheses and examine both direct and indirect (mediating) relationships, the data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4. All variables were measured using previously validated measurement scales. Findings Proactive market orientation (PMO) significantly enhances value co-creation but lacks a direct effect on marketing performance; its impact is fully mediated by co-creation. Responsive market orientation (RMO) directly improves performance, and this improvement is partially achieved through co-creation. The study confirms co-creation as a pivotal mechanism linking MO to outcomes, with PMO's influence being entirely indirect and RMO's hybrid (direct/indirect). Originality/value This study advances the literature by integrating responsive and…

title: A Review of the Applicability of the Capital Asset Pricing Model in the Brazilian Stock Market
abstract: The Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) is commonly used to calculate equity cost and assess investment performance, though its validity for Brazil's stock market is still debated. This paper conducts a narrative literature review to compare representative studies in terms of research goals, sample rules and model settings, identifying consensus and conflicts in existing empirical results. The market factor can partly explain stock returns, but solid evidence proving standard CAPM fully prices assets and forecasts returns is lacking. Conditional and multi-factor extensions perform better in certain scenarios, yet their advantages rely on evaluation targets and may not generate notably different equity cost estimates. Inconsistencies among researches mainly arise from sample bias, market proxy errors, varied model designs, estimation windows and time-varying market features. Therefore, CAPM assessments need to separate theoretical validity, statistical performance and practical value, and test result robustness via sample, proxy and parameter sensitivity checks. This study clarifies applicable conditions for CAPM as an equity-cost benchmark and offers guidance for model selection and use in Brazil's stock market.

title: Discrimination in the Labour Market: Causes and Remedies
abstract: Discrimination in the labor market is a pervasive issue that hampers equal opportunities and undermines social progress. This paper explores the causes and potential remedies for discrimination in the labor market. It begins by identifying various forms of discrimination, including those based on gender, race, ethnicity, age, and disability, and highlights their detrimental effects on individuals and society as a whole. The causes of discrimination in the labor market are multi-faceted and complex. They can be attributed to deep-rooted biases, stereotypes, and prejudices held by employers, as well as structural factors within organizations and societal norms. Moreover, unconscious biases and systemic inequalities further perpetuate discriminatory practices. Such discrimination not only deprives individuals of fair access to employment but also contributes to income disparities and exacerbates social inequality. The study concluded that discrimination is fueled by various causes, including prejudice, stereotypes, biases, and structural inequalities To address this issue, the study recommended that organizations should adopt inclusive policies and practices that actively promote diversity in their workforce. This includes implementing unbiased recruitment and hiring processes, establishing diversity targets, and creating inclusive work environments that value and respect individu…

title: Artificial intelligence and the future of youth employment in a developing economy: skills mismatch, early-career transitions and labour market vulnerability
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping youth employment in Morocco, focusing on labour market vulnerability, skills mismatch and early-career transitions. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a mixed-methods approach combining a task-based quantitative analysis of secondary labour market data with qualitative evidence from 12 semi-structured expert interviews. Findings The findings indicate that AI adoption in Morocco remains limited and uneven, with applications concentrated mainly on basic functions. The quantitative analysis highlights the structural characteristics of youth employment, while the interviews reveal concerns about skills mismatch, access to early-career opportunities and potential AI-related job displacement. A central finding is the youth paradox: young people are perceived as digitally adaptable but continue to face structural barriers to quality employment and AI-complementary opportunities. The findings also highlight the importance of education and skills development, stronger school-to-work transition mechanisms and institutional coordination in supporting inclusive adaptation to technological change. Originality/value Despite growing concern about AI’s labour-market implications, youth remain underrepresented in the literature, particularly in developing economies. Drawing on the routine-biased technolo…

title: Issue Construction and Value Oriented Guidance in People’s Daily Reports on “Synergy Between Compu-ting Power and Electricity”
abstract: Against the backdrop of mounting anxiety over computing power related energy consumption triggered by the expansion of generative artificial intelligence, syn-ergy between computing power and electricity has evolved into a major com-pound issue bearing on China’s layout of new quality productive forces and its green low carbon transition. Taking relevant news reports from the People’s Daily media matrix as research samples, this study integrates the is-sue construction theory and Gamson’s “interpretive package” theory to explore how mainstream media construct this issue. The analysis reveals that in theme selection, media coverage focuses on strategic coordination, spatial restructuring and technological rationality. In framing, media employ framing devices such as metaphors, illustrative cases and slogans, together with reasoning devices in-cluding causal attribution, consequence prediction and moral principles to form interpretive packages. These packages realize the figurative translation and le-gitimacy justification of sophisticated technical content. In terms of val-ue oriented guidance, media transcend social subsystems and build a four dimensional value guidance path targeting governments, enterprises, media outlets and individuals, facilitating the transformation of policy intentions into nationwide strategic consensus. This research provides academic references for jo…

Achieving Sustainable Success in Japan’s Mobile Gaming Market: Investigation by Mixed Methods
abstract: Japan’s mobile gaming market has some of the highest spending levels in the world, yet many apps are terminated early and corporate profits have stagnated. This study examined the conditions for sustainable success at three levels: players, apps, and companies. A mixed-methods design combined factor analysis of spending and spending-cessation motivations based on surveys of Japanese players, fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) of 104 apps and 18 companies, and case studies. High-revenue spending motivations such as character collection correlated positively with the risk of spending cessation, whereas motivations rooted in playing with friends, supporting the operating company, and leisure showed only weak correlations. Avoiding the hyper-casual genre was the only necessary condition for long-term app operation. Counterintuitively, a high app survival rate did not necessarily lead to the profit growth of the company that provided the apps.

Optimization of Cross-Border E-Commerce Marketing Strategies for Haoyue Feather Co., Ltd.'s Down Bedding in the U.S. Market: A 4P-Based Case Study
abstract: With the continuous growth of global cross-border online consumption, the United States, boasting a mature e-commerce ecosystem and strong consumer purchasing power, has become a core market for Chinese home textile and bedding enterprises to expand overseas. However, during the transformation to cross-border e-commerce, many domestic down manufacturing enterprises generally encounter development bottlenecks such as severe product homogenization, insufficient brand premium, and high customer acquisition costs (CAC). Based on the 4P marketing theory (product, price, place, and promotion), this paper analyzes the company's deficiencies in product grading, pricing mechanisms, omnichannel collaboration, and content marketing. The findings indicate that the enterprise's over-reliance on single platforms and low-price, high-volume strategies, coupled with insufficient local market insights and brand accumulation, restricts its development. Therefore, this paper proposes a systematic optimization plan covering differentiated product stratification, value-oriented pricing, omnichannel collaborative operation, and long-term brand marketing, and provides implementation guarantees from the aspects of organization, funds, supply chain, and compliance. This research offers a practical case reference for traditional foreign trade factories to transform into cross-border e-commerce brands.

title: Federal Reserve Monetary Policy Surprises and Stock Market Reactions: Evidence from the United States and China
abstract: Federal Reserve monetary policy can influence stock markets in other economies through channels such as exchange rates, financial conditions, and risk appetites. This study examines 67 scheduled Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announcements from 2017 to 2025 as events, using the S&P 500 and CSI 300 indices to represent the US and Chinese stock markets, respectively. This study employs the event study method to calculate the cumulative abnormal return (CAR) and uses "MPShock" to measure the unanticipated policy information contained in the announcements. Accounting for time zone differences, the first trading day following the announcement is designated as the event day for the Chinese market. The results indicate that the average CAR across the various windows were not statistically significant. Following the introduction of MPShock, the US market exhibited a significant negative reaction within the [-1,+1] window, while the Chinese market showed significant negative reactions within the [-3,+3] and [-5,+5] windows; however, the interaction term was not significant, indicating no statistical support for a difference in overall shock sensitivity between the two markets. The core findings remained robust after the sequential exclusion of individual events. After controlling for renminbi (RMB) exchange rate fluctuations, the negative relationship in the Chinese market remaine…

title: Global policy uncertainty and Islamic equity market dynamics: evidence from Indonesia’s Sharia Stock Index
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how external policy-related shocks shape Islamic equity market dynamics in an emerging economy. Using Indonesia as a case, it examines the effects of US and China trade policy uncertainty and geopolitical risk on the Indonesia Sharia Stock Index (ISSI), while accounting for global oil prices and US monetary policy. Design/methodology/approach The study uses monthly data from March 2020 to December 2024 and estimates an autoregressive distributed lag model to distinguish short-run responses from long-run relationships among the ISSI and global uncertainty indicators. Findings US trade policy uncertainty (and, with a lag, China trade policy uncertainty) and geopolitical risk are associated with statistically significant short-run declines in the ISSI, consistent with heightened risk aversion during global stress episodes. In the long run, US trade policy uncertainty, global oil prices and the US policy rate show positive long-run associations with the ISSI, whereas China’s trade policy uncertainty and geopolitical risk are not robustly significant in the long-run specification. Originality/value This study provides evidence of horizon-dependent effects of external policy uncertainty in an emerging Islamic equity market. The results inform investors about the behavior of Sharia-compliant equities under global stress and highlight the importan…

title: Construction and Evaluation of a Simplified Barra Multi-factor Risk Model for the Chinese A-Share Market
abstract: The Barra multi-factor risk model is a core tool in quantitative investing. First proposed by Barr Rosenberg, it has been widely applied to risk analysis, portfolio management, and performance attribution. The model decomposes stock returns into common risk factors and idiosyncratic components via style and industry factors, enabling investors to systematically identify the sources and structure of portfolio returns. Although MSCI has developed dedicated Barra models for the Chinese stock market, such as the CNE5, CNE6, and CNE7 series, these commercial frameworks generally operate as black-box tools with limited public disclosure of their specific construction details. Grounded in the principles of feasibility and transparency, this paper constructs a simplified Barra multi-factor risk model for the Chinese A-share market. Book equity is derived from raw financial data and strictly aligned with financial report announcement dates, and factor returns are estimated through monthly cross-sectional regressions. Finally, the model is evaluated across three dimensions: explanatory power measured by 12-month rolling adjusted R-squared, factor return volatility, and the performance of major style factors. The assessment verifies whether the model can capture core style and industry risk exposures in the Chinese A-share market and provide a reliable foundation for follow-up research.

title: Do sustainability disclosures attract analysts' attention? Evidence from an emerging market
abstract: Purpose This study investigates whether sustainability disclosure influences analysts' coverage in an African emerging market and examines whether analysts respond differently to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure pillars among firms listed on the Casablanca Stock Exchange. Design/methodology/approach The empirical analysis relies on panel-data regressions for Moroccan listed firms over the 2017–2022 period. Baseline pooled OLS specifications are complemented by fixed-effects models, while robustness is assessed using a principal component analysis (PCA)-based ESG disclosure index and fixed-effects Poisson estimations. Findings The findings show that sustainability disclosure is positively associated with analyst coverage. However, when ESG disclosure is decomposed, only governance disclosure remains positively and significantly related to analyst coverage, highlighting governance disclosure as the most informative ESG dimension for analysts. Research limitations/implications The evidence is drawn from a single, relatively small emerging market and a constrained analyst environment, and disclosure-based ESG measures. Moreover, its observational design does not fully rule out endogeneity and reverse causality; the findings should therefore be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. Practical implications For managers, improving the quality and…

Market Challenges and Strategic Responses of Costco in Mainland China
abstract: Costco has an annual membership fee and a small number of products that it sells at low margins. This paper discusses the appropriateness of the model in mainland China in the context of household needs and purchasing behaviors. The qualitative case study is based on published research, reports and prices gathered from Costco's flagship store on JD.com. As of 12 September 2026, every one of the 49 Kirkland Signature products sampled offered non-member prices exactly 1.20 times member prices, representing a member discount of approximately 16.7 percent. With this premium, the 299-yuan annual fee can be recovered through 1,495 yuan worth of purchases at member prices, assuming that the delivery fee and discount are not different between the two types of consumers. The Black Diamond charge is 688 yuan a year, with a 3 percent rebate on qualifying pre-tax purchases. The cost of upgrading could be canceled out if customers spend about 12,967 yuan on eligible purchases (assuming the reward is fully redeemed). The reported rate of renewals in the mainland, around 60 percent, is lower than the 70 percent management hoped to achieve, highlighting retention as an issue. Costco should experiment with smaller sizes of fresh foods and share basket price comparisons but continue to offer bulk packs of storable food items and maintain its limited variety and Kirkland Signature.

title: The 2018 Section 301 Tariff Announcement and Short-Term Market Reaction of U.S. Technology Stocks: An Event Study of 11 Listed Companies
abstract: This paper examines the short-term stock-market reaction of U.S. technology stocks to the 2018 Section 301 tariff announcement. A market-model event study is conducted for 11 large U.S.-listed technology firms, divided into hardware/semiconductor and software/platform/cloud groups, with March 22, 2018 as the event day. The estimation window contains 110 trading days, with [-1, 1] as the primary event window and [-3, 3] and [-5, 5] as robustness checks. The full-sample cumulative average abnormal return is small and insignificant in the primary window (0.43%, p = 0.65), but significantly negative in the widest window (-4.27%, p = 0.013), supporting the first hypothesis only over wider windows. Both groups experience declines, with a somewhat larger point estimate for the software group, but inter-group differences are insignificant, so the second hypothesis is not supported. Leave-one-out tests confirm that no single firm drives the result. Overall, the announcement coincided with a broad, delayed negative repricing of technology stocks, although the small sample and concurrent firm-specific news warrant interpreting the findings as association rather than causation.

title: Branding disconnection through nostalgia in digital detox tourism
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how digital detox tourism brands use nostalgia to construct the emotional appeal and communicated experiential value of disconnection, and how these meanings are received and negotiated by participants and consumers. Design/methodology/approach The study combines a qualitative thematic content analysis of 73 brand-produced and brand-attributable promotional items from The Offline Club, Camp Grounded and Unplugged with a supplementary qualitative analysis of 28 publicly available first-person participant and consumer accounts. The analysis focuses on nostalgic cues, analogue practices, emotional framing and the relationship between branded meanings and public reception. Findings Across the three cases, nostalgia operates as more than a decorative aesthetic device. It provides a symbolic and temporal frame through which technological absence is associated with simplicity, presence, play, sociability and self-reconnection, while analogisation materialises these meanings through tangible objects, practices, aesthetics and rituals. The findings suggest that nostalgia performs a value-conversion function by reframing technological absence from potential deprivation into experiential enrichment. The reception analysis further shows that these meanings are selectively reproduced, reinterpreted and sometimes challenged. Analogue engagement is widesprea…

title: Farmer Organisations in the Digital Economy: Platforms, Market Linkages, Advisory Services and Collective Bargaining
abstract: Farmer organisations, including cooperatives, producer companies, producer organisations and farmer groups, have long been promoted as means for smaller farmers to reduce transaction costs, achieve scale and countervail the market power of buyers and input suppliers. The spread of mobile telephony, electronic marketplaces, agricultural e-commerce, digital advisory services and data-driven platforms is now reshaping each of these functions, yet the literatures on farmer collective action and on digital agriculture have developed largely in isolation. This critical narrative review examines how digitalisation alters the economic rationale, functions and governance of farmer organisations across four domains: market linkages, advisory services, collective bargaining and the governance of agricultural data. Experimental, quasi-experimental and observational studies, case studies, legal and political-economy analyses and selected institutional reports were retrieved from multidisciplinary and economics databases, a regional Indian journal platform and citation tracking, and appraised qualitatively for design, identification, outcome measurement and transferability. The evidence indicates that price information delivered digitally reduces spatial price dispersion but rarely raises farm-gate prices on its own, and that public electronic marketplaces and private e-commerce platforms pr…

title: Truck Brand Positioning under the Decarbonisation of the European Market
abstract: Decarbonisation changes the information European fleet operators use to evaluate truck brands. This study examines the publicly documented value propositions of seven established truck brands and the limitations of assessing them against a common set of indicators. The research combines a critical marketing literature review, descriptive analysis of published heavy-truck registration statistics for 2022–2025, a cross-sectional audit of 19 manufacturer and partner documents available on 2 November 2026, and a sensitivity analysis of energy costs. The Decarbonisation Positioning Architecture (DPA) is operationalised through product offerings, economic arrangements, charging, digital fleet services and implementation support. A register of 35 brand–dimension observations records the source, indicator, coding decision and geographic limitation. Each observation identifies a named offer and receives the maximum score of 2 on the 0–2 specificity scale. This ceiling effect prevents the scale from distinguishing between brands: alternative common weights and removal of one dimension leave the profiles identical. The selected documents reveal similar categories of reported offers, without establishing convergence of strategies, buyer preferences or equivalent service performance. title: Volatility Spillovers in China's Financial Markets During the 2015 Stock Market Crash: Evidence From DCC-GARCH and the DY Approach
abstract: This paper examines volatility spillovers among the stock, foreign exchange, money, and bond markets of China during the 2015 stock market crash. Using daily series of the CSI 300 index, the USD/CNY central parity rate, the 7-day Shanghai Interbank Offered Rate, and the 10-year Chinese government bond yield from the Wind Financial Database over January 2014 to December 2016, conditional volatilities are extracted with univariate sGARCH(1,1) models, the dynamic correlations of returns and interest rate changes are captured by the DCC-GARCH model, and the directional predictive contributions among conditional volatilities are measured by the generalized Diebold-Yilmaz (DY) spillover index. To address stationarity concerns, the reported statistics rely only on rolling windows with a stable vector autoregression. In crisis-stable windows the stock market is a net receiver of volatility spillovers, whereas the exchange rate and the long-term interest rate are net senders, with average predictive contributions of 5.948 and 2.795 percentage points to stock volatility. The average total connectedness index during the crisis under a 200-day window is 4.260%, lower than 7.420% before the crisis, while shorter windows reverse this comparison, indicating that phase comparisons depend on the time scale. title: Implementasi E-commerce Mobile Menggunakan REST API dan Web Service pada Koperasi Jamu
abstract: The advancement of digital technology encourages businesses to adopt electronic commerce systems to expand market reach and improve transaction efficiency. Koperasi Jati Husada Mulya Mandiri, a cooperative specializing in traditional herbal drinks, still relies on conventional sales processes, limiting customers’ access to product information and ordering services. This study aims to develop a mobile-based e-commerce application utilizing Representational State Transfer Application Programming Interface (REST API) and web services to support the digitalization of the cooperative’s sales activities. The system was developed by building a customer-facing mobile application using Flutter and the Dart programming language, along with a backend system and web services using Laravel and PHP. MySQL was used to store and manage product, customer, and transaction data. The system also integrates the Midtrans payment gateway to facilitate digital payments. The results indicate that the application was successfully developed and can retrieve and exchange data between the mobile application and the server through REST API. The implementation provides customers with easier access to product information and digital ordering services while supporting integrated sales transaction management. An Empirical Examination of Stakeholder Factors and Value-for-Money Audit Effectiveness in the Nigerian Public Service
abstract: The systemic issues of poor stakeholder integration, low inclusiveness, and weak frameworks remain persistent and undermine the effectiveness of the VFM audit in Nigeria, raising serious concerns among scholars. This study examined how the application of stakeholder factors affects value-for-money (VFM) audit effectiveness within the Nigerian public service. This study used a quantitative cross-sectional design and a stratified random sample of 115 stakeholders (auditors, policymakers, civil servants, and representatives of civil society) from federal ministries, departments, and agencies (MDAs) in Nigeria, selected using the Yamane formula, with 106 responding. A structured questionnaire in Google Forms was used to obtain primary data. Analysis of quantitative data was done with SPSS v30 using descriptive statistics and regression analysis techniques. The results indicated that the effect of stakeholder influence (β = 0.356, p = 0.008) and auditors’ role (β = 0.421, p = 0.010) were significantly positive on VFM audit effectiveness. On the other hand, stakeholder engagement (β = -0.214, p = 0.132) inversely and insignificantly influenced the effectiveness of the VFM audit. The study established that stakeholder influence and auditors' roles are significant determinants of VFM audit effectiveness, while stakeholder engagement return is insignificant. title: Digital Banking Service Excellence and Its Impact on Customer Satisfaction and Customer Retention: A Structural Equation Modeling Approach
abstract: With the increasing number of digital banking platforms, how to deliver financial services has changed completely, requiring a greater understanding of service excellence and its effect on customer behavioral outcomes. This study aims to explore the impact of Digital Banking Service Excellence on customer satisfaction and customer retention in technology-based banking environment. Service excellence is manifested in several aspects such as, system reliability, information security and privacy, ease of use of the interface, responsiveness of the service, service personalization and service accessibility. The study also explores the mediation between S.E., C.S. and C.R. The approach used in the study is quantitative using a structured questionnaire with a five-point Likert scale and sample of active users of digital banking. The proposed conceptual framework is tested empirically using advanced statistical and machine learning-supported analytical techniques, such as Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) for dimensional validation, Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) for construct validation and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) for hypothesis testing and relationship assessment. Further, the reliability and validity are checked by Cronbach's alpha, Average Variance Extracted (AVE) and Composite Reliability (CR). Attitudes, self-efficacy, and behavioral readiness for inclusive practice among pre-service teacher-psychologists in Kazakhstan: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Introduction This study examined inclusive readiness among pre-service teacher-psychologists as a multidimensional construct comprising value-based attitudes, professional self-efficacy, and behavioral readiness for inclusive practice. Methods A comparative cross-sectional design was used with 176 second- to fourth-year students from two universities in Kazakhstan. Measurement quality was examined using reliability analysis and confirmatory factor analysis, followed by descriptive statistics, adjusted general linear models, correlation analysis, and hierarchical multiple regression. Results The three-factor measurement model provided supportive evidence that the three readiness dimensions were empirically distinguishable. Descriptively, value-based attitudes were more strongly expressed than self-efficacy and behavioral readiness, although differences in raw scale means were not interpreted as evidence of a psychological gap. Item-level results indicated comparatively lower readiness for complex case decisions, sensitive communication with families, and multidisciplinary support planning. Professional self-efficacy showed the strongest association with behavioral readiness ( r = .62) and remained its largest independent correlate in the fully adjusted model ( β = .44), whereas the corresponding association with value-based attitudes was smaller ( β = .16). title: Mentor teachers' understanding of their roles in mentoring pre-service teachers in Tanzania
abstract: Purpose This study investigated mentor teachers' understanding of their roles in mentoring pre-service teachers during teaching practicum in Tanzania. Design/methodology/approach This qualitative study was conducted in the Iringa and Mbeya regions of Tanzania and involved 8 secondary schools hosting pre-service teachers from three universities with the highest enrolments. A total of 30 mentor teachers with at least 2 years of mentoring experience were selected through purposive sampling. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions, which complemented each other, and analysed using thematic analysis to capture convergence, divergence, and complementarity. Findings The results indicated that most mentor teachers clearly understood their roles in supporting pre-service teachers' professional growth and building interpersonal skills. However, a few had a limited and poor understanding of their responsibilities, leaving pre-service teachers with little or no guidance. Originality/value The study provides context-specific evidence on mentor teachers' understanding of their roles, highlighting the need to strengthen standardised understanding to improve the quality of pre-service teacher education in Tanzania.

title: Brand Activism in Services: A Review and Future Research Directions
abstract: Researchers are increasingly examining brand activism (BA), through which companies embed explicit social, environmental, or political stances into their core strategies. This study focuses on BA within the service industry. A systematic literature review was conducted using a hybrid design that integrates bibliometric analysis with a structured qualitative review, following the SPAR-4-SLR (Scientific Procedures and Rationales for Systematic Literature Reviews) protocol. This hybrid design enabled both a broad mapping of publication trends and a deeper synthesis of findings specific to service contexts. A total of 48 publications were analyzed without temporal restrictions to identify dominant themes and research patterns related to BA in services. The study clarifies the role of BA in service-specific framework, outlines directions for future research, and offers practical guidance for designing context-sensitive BA strategies. By addressing this, this study provides a sector-specific synthesis for service industries and highlights underexplored sectors and forms of activism that warrant further scholarly attention.

title: Developing pre-service teachers’ AI competence: a quasi-experimental study of a TICII-based methodical system
abstract: Introduction The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into higher education requires the purposeful development of pre-service teachers’ pedagogically grounded, responsible, and effective competence in using these technologies. Existing international frameworks (TPACK, DigCompEdu, the UNESCO AI Competency Framework for Teachers) provide a general basis for technological-pedagogical integration but do not fully operationalize the diagnostic, individualization, and ethical dimensions of AI competence as an integrated instructional and assessment system for teacher education. Methods This article reports a multi-institutional quasi-experimental study of a methodical system informed by the TICII (Transformation-Individualization-Competence-Inclusivity-Integration) conceptual model, conducted with master's-degree pre-service teachers in AI-related and computer-science fields across six higher education institutions in Uzbekistan over the 2023-2024, 2024-2025, and 2025-2026 academic years. The study examined the effect of a TICII-informed methodical intervention, supported by the EduAI platform, on pre-service teachers’ AI competence. title: Inventory Productivity and Carbon Emissions in Retailing
abstract: Problem definition: Higher inventory productivity is thought to be associated with lower carbon emissions and waste. We test this conventional wisdom using granular emissions data from CDP. Methodology/results: Pairing emissions data with firms’ financials, we show that most of the emission reduction benefits emerge organically with the scale of operations. Using causal inference techniques, we show that, absent the scale, an external shock to inventory productivity results in higher emission intensity in aggregate across scopes, in Scope 3, and its category of purchased goods and services. The effect on Scope 2 emissions is negative and null in Scope 1. The effect is concentrated in the non-essential retail segments, excluding food and beverage, and health and personal care retailers. Managerial implications: All else kept equal, a higher inventory productivity trades off associated profitability benefits with upstream carbon emissions, particularly in the Scope 3 category of purchased goods and services, underscoring the need for holistic implementation of lean practices. We explore the feasibility of carbon pricing as a mechanism to shift the retailers’ calculus to the dual objective of profit maximization and minimization of environmental impact.

Supporting, not replacing: counsellors’ and service coordinators’ perspectives on the use of artificial intelligence in youth online chat counselling
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored to support youth online chat counselling services (OCCS). Understanding stakeholders’ perspectives is essential to guide its effective implementation. This study explored counsellors’ and service coordinators’ perspectives on the role of AI in youth online chat counselling. Methods Sixty-two semi-structured interviews were conducted with counsellors and service coordinators from 33 non-profit OCCS across Belgium, Finland, Hungary, and Spain. Interviews were recorded, transcribed verbatim, translated into English, and analysed using qualitative thematic analysis in NVivo. Results Four key themes emerged during interviews: (1) attitudes towards AI, (2) current and (3) future applications, and (4) requirements for responsible implementation. Participants opposed AI replacing human counsellors but considered its growing role as inevitable. 6 out of 33 (18.2%) OCCS reported having incorporated a chatbot (at the time of the interview, type not specified). Participant reported current use of AI in OCCS included automated responses, suicide risk identification, and data management functions. Proposed future uses comprised intelligent routing, multilingual support, transcription, resource and referral identification, counsellor training, real-time suggestions and feedback, and documentation and reporting support. title: Octahedral Co 3+ Spin‐State Regulation in W‐Doped Co 3 O 4 for Accelerated Sulfur Redox Kinetics
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) are promising high‐energy storage systems, but their practical application remains limited by the low electronic conductivity of sulfur, sluggish Li–S redox kinetics, and the lithium polysulfide (LiPS) shuttle effect. These challenges require the rational design of cathode catalysts with well‐regulated electronic structures and active sites. Herein, Cu 2+ and Al 3+ substitution in Co 3 O 4 was first used to identify the catalytic roles of Co sites with different coordination environments, forming CuCo 2 O 4 and CoAl 2 O 4 as model systems. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that octahedral Co 3+ sites play a key role in enhancing LiPS adsorption and Li–S reaction kinetics. Guided by this insight, tungsten species with different oxidation states were used to direct distinct local perturbations of tetrahedral‐ and octahedral‐Co‐site environments in Co 3 O 4 , yielding W Td ‐Co 3 O 4 @NC and W Oh ‐Co 3 O 4 @NC, respectively, where NC denotes nitrogen‐doped carbon. Magnetic measurements and DFT calculations demonstrate that W 6+ doping induces a low‐spin to high‐spin transition of Co 3+ , generating additional unpaired 3d electrons that strengthen LiPS adsorption and accelerate LiPS conversion. As a result, W Oh ‐Co 3 O 4 @NC/S delivers high capacity, excellent rate capability, and long‐term cycling stability, even under lea…

title: Mental Health in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: How AI Use Affects Individual Emotion Regulation and Psychological Autonomy
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used not only to obtain information or complete tasks, but also to interpret feelings and make sense of difficult experiences. This review considers how such use may relate to emotion regulation and psychological autonomy. Drawing on self-determination theory and process-based accounts of emotion regulation, it examines evidence of both support and risk. Conversational systems may help users name emotions, consider alternative interpretations, and practise coping strategies in settings that feel private and accessible. However, these benefits should not be assumed to persist: when users routinely hand over emotional interpretation or personal decisions to a system, they may have fewer opportunities to exercise their own judgement. The implications therefore depend on the purpose and pattern of use, users' psychological needs and developmental circumstances, and the design of the system. The review discusses implications for AI developers, mental-health practitioners, educators, and policymakers.

Mitigating Negative Cross-Border Monetary Spillovers: Capital-Account Regulation under International Monetary and Financial Law in the Context of the 2022 Energy Shock
abstract: The 2022 global energy shock set off inflationary pressures and pushed major central banks to tighten monetary policy quickly. Those policy moves created cross border spillovers that shifted exchange rates and changed financial conditions in other economies. This research looks at capital account regulation and blends analysis with quantitative data to see whether international monetary and financial law can slow the spread of such spillovers. It builds a Legal Constraint Index (LCI) that mixes FARI IMF capital flow management compliance and surveillance metrics for a panel of 50 non-reserve currency economies from 2019 to 2023. Using a two-way fixed effects least squares (OLS) model the study checks whether stronger pre shock legal constraints correlate with lower exchange rate pressure after the shock. The baseline regression shows a coefficient on the interaction term implying that stronger pre shock legal constraints link to lower post shock exchange rate pressure yet this link is not statistically significant. The results indicate that capital account regulation alone may not sufficiently control global monetary spillovers and suggest that stronger IMF surveillance, cross border consultation and multilateral policy coordination might ease this situation.

title: Alkali Metal Cation Regulation of the Interfacial Microenvironment for Selective Glycine Electrosynthesis from Nitrate and Glyoxylic Acid
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical C–N coupling offers a potentially sustainable approach to glycine synthesis from glyoxylic acid (GX) and nitrate (NO3–), but competing reactions limit the selectivity under high current densities. Alkali metal cations can influence glycine electrosynthesis through modulation of the electrode–electrolyte microenvironment. However, their role in glycine electrosynthesis has remained largely unexplored. Here, the effect of alkali metal cations was systematically investigated using oxide-derived Bi. Notably, glycine selectivity follows the order of Na+ > K+ > Li+ > Cs+ at 200 mA cm–2, with Na+ providing an optimal balance among the consecutive reaction steps and achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 61.1% and a partial current density of 122.2 mA cm–2. A preliminary technoeconomic analysis further suggests potential economic viability at high current densities. Control experiments show that Na+ favors both the formation of NH2OH and the reduction of oxime to glycine. Together with in situ spectroscopy, these results suggest that cation-dependent interfacial electrostatic and hydration environments contribute to glycine selectivity. This work identifies alkali metal cations as effective interfacial regulators for controlling complicated electrochemical C–N coupling and provides insights into the rational design of selective glycine electrosynthesis.

title: Securitising digital sovereignty in Vietnam: adaptive governance in an era of techno-geopolitical competition
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how Vietnam securitises digital sovereignty in the context of intensifying techno-geopolitical competition in Southeast Asia and what explains its divergence from Singapore and Indonesia. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Copenhagen School securitisation theory, the study uses a qualitative comparative design in which Vietnam is the focal case and Singapore and Indonesia are structured comparators. Legislative documents, national strategies and secondary literature were selected using explicit criteria and coded in two deductive rounds for four digital-sovereignty dimensions and six securitisation elements. Findings Vietnam pursues pragmatic securitisation, termed digital adaptive hedging, a path between Singapore’s institutionalist rule-setting and Indonesia’s defensive localisation. Core data is localised, while non-sensitive data flows across borders; infrastructure supply is diversified through multi-vendor deployment; external commitments balance the US-led Indo-Pacific Economic Framework against China-anchored regional comprehensive economic partnership (RCEP); and foreign direct investment (FDI) conditionality is channelled towards semiconductor capability-building. Research limitations/implications The study relies on publicly accessible documents and interpretive coding; findings are configurative rather than causally identified.…

title: Low-Carbohydrate Diets, Carbohydrate Quality, and Sleep Regulation after Menopause: A Narrative Review
abstract: Driven by hormonal fluctuations, vasomotor symptoms, metabolic disturbances, and systemic inflammation, sleep problems often arise during the menopausal transition and postmenopause. Nevertheless, dietary modification may help improve sleep, but the roles of carbohydrate quantity and quality in postmenopausal women remain unclear. This narrative review examines how low-carbohydrate diets (LCDs) and carbohydrate quality relate to sleep after menopause, drawing on observational studies, clinical trials, systematic reviews, and mechanistic research. Existing studies shows that greater adherence to LCDs and very low-carbohydrate ketogenic diets may improve subjective sleep quality, potentially through changes in adiposity, inflammation, and neurochemical pathways. Beyond carbohydrate quantity, carbohydrate quality also seems to affect sleep. In postmenopausal women, higher dietary glycemic index has been linked to higher odds of prevalent and incident insomnia, while higher intake of fiber-rich foods is linked to better sleep outcomes. However, findings vary by diet, study design, and population. Few studies have examined postmenopausal women, as most have focused on younger or different groups. As a result, long-term trials using objective sleep measures are needed to assess whether reducing carbohydrate intake improves sleep after menopause.

Patriarchy in the Pixel: Digital Harassment, Somatic Regulation, and Subaltern Female Resistance in Contemporary Nepal
abstract: In contemporary Nepal, the rapid expansion of digital communication platforms has created a new frontier for structural gender-based violence, shifting traditional mechanisms of patriarchal control from physical spaces into virtual domains. Gender Trouble, Judith Butler argues that “gender is performatively constituted through regulatory practices that discipline the body”. This concept extends to online spaces, where digital harassment functions to police and suppress women’s presence. While contemporary media critics often contend that virtual platforms democratize public discourse and afford marginalized groups unprecedented visibility, this optimistic reading frequently overlooks how online misogyny, cyberstalking, and non-consensual image sharing replicate deep-seated offline power hierarchies. Responding to such critiques, Butler’s framework clarifies that “technological visibility without structural protection merely intensifies somatic regulation, transforming the digital screen into a modern equivalent oftraditional spatial exclusion”.Grounded in radical feminist theory, drawing on Catharine MacKinnon and Shulamith Firestone, and on Gayatri Spivak’s concept of subaltern agency, this paper examines how digital harassment functions as an instrument of bodily surveillance against women, particularly in socio-culturally conservative provinces such as Sudurpashchim. title: Regulation and bibliometric analysis of natural alkaloids on angiogenesis in triple negative breast cancer
Mounted equine-assisted services as a bottom-up intervention for trust building and autonomic regulation
abstract: The majority of studies on equine-assisted services (EAS) adopt a predominantly top-down perspective and emphasize the cognitive understanding of human–animal interactions, as well as the hormonal and affective effects of these interactions on human functioning. The importance of trust building and autonomic regulation may be underestimated because research in this area does not distinguish between mounted and unmounted moments of interaction or consider their respective impacts on body awareness and sensory processing when presenting and discussing outcomes. In this study, we build on existing evidence from the perspectives of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and affective neuroscience to examine and discuss how mounted EAS, through bottom-up pathways, directly supports the development of interpersonal trust and the regulation of the autonomic nervous system. A tentative theoretical framework is presented, together with suggestions for future studies. We conclude that mounted EAS provides unique embodied, bottom-up experiences and treatment effects that distinguish it from ground-based EAS and that this clinically important distinction warrants further empirical investigation.

title: Hansen Solubility Parameter Analysis of Pore Structure Regulation in Porous Polystyrene Microspheres with Temperature-Dependent Adsorption after NIPAM Modification
abstract: Abstract The pore structure of porous polystyrene microspheres (PPS) influences mass transfer and functional applications, yet the relationship between swelling agent compatibility and pore formation remains to be clarified. In this study, PPS microspheres were prepared by two-step seed swelling polymerization, and the effects of single and mixed swelling agents on seed swelling and pore structure were investigated using Hansen solubility parameter (HSP) analysis. The total solubility parameter difference (Δδ) and Hansen distance (Ra) were used to assess parameter matching. Toluene (TL) showed favorable HSP matching with polystyrene, yielding microspheres with uniform surface pores and a specific surface area of 33.67 m2/g, the highest among the single swelling agent systems. Increasing the cyclohexane/1,2-dichloroethane (CYH/DCE) mass ratio from 10/90 to 50/50 altered the HSPs and pore structures. The 20/80 system exhibited the highest specific surface area and pore volume within this series, whereas the average pore diameter reached 47.52 nm in the 30/70 system. When TL was blended with dibutyl phthalate (DBP), the high boiling point of DBP favored liquid-phase retention, while its plasticizing effect facilitated seed swelling. The resulting microspheres retained their spherical morphology and exhibited relatively uniform surface pores. N-Isopropylacrylamide (NIPAM) was subse…

title: Design principles for financial intelligence governance: balancing secrecy, sovereignty and cooperation
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to derive a set of design principles for financial intelligence governance by analysing two enduring tensions: preserving operational secrecy while ensuring democratic accountability, and fostering international cooperation without eroding national sovereignty. The paper sets out how these tensions can be institutionalised as productive forces and translated into replicable design principles for the European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA). Design/methodology/approach The study combines documentary, doctrinal and interpretive analysis of primary normative sources, including the European Union (EU) Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Package, Regulation (EU) 2024/1620, Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 and Directive (EU) 2024/1640, previous AML Directives, Spanish Law 10/2010 and Law 2/2023. It also examines institutional reports, including annual reports of Spain’s financial intelligence unit (FIU), the Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias (SEPBLAC), Mutual Evaluation Reports of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), advisories of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and documents from the Egmont Group, the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. These sources are read through a qualitative case study of SEPBLAC and its coordination agreement with Spain’s National Securities Market Commis…

Commentary: a practical response to the challenge of GenAI-Implementation for small business
abstract: Purpose This study aims to provide a response from a practitioner perspective on the articles in the special issue and provide insights and recommendations for small businesses to translate research into practice. Design/methodology/approach A conceptual approach is used, drawing on practice-informed insights. Findings This commentary identifies three key insights based on the articles in this special issue: (1) treat Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) like a new team member, (2) start with the customer, not the tool and (3) build capability through small-scale trials. Practical implications This commentary assists business chambers and small business by synthesising the key practical insights from articles in this special issue for use by small business. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this commentary is one of the first in an academic business journal to be the voice of small business on the topic of GenAI and small business.

Hardness and Microstructure Response to Tempering Duration in Traditional Forged Knives from Recycled Spring Steel
abstract: Traditional blacksmiths in South Sumatra face socio-economic and technological constraints, often relying on trial-and-error heat treatments that lead to inconsistent product quality, material waste, and economic losses. This study implements a participatory technology transfer and community mentoring model to improve the manufacturing of traditional forged knives from recycled vehicle leaf-spring steel. A cohort of 15 local blacksmiths (n=15) participated in a structured mentoring program focused on standardized tempering and circular-economy practices. Four blade specimens were evaluated to provide a technical benchmark: an untreated baseline and blades tempered at 550°C for 1, 2, and 4 h. The quantitative evaluation showed that mean hardness decreased from a highly stressed baseline of 43.02 ± 3.43 HRC to a more stable 41.84 ± 0.63 HRC (1 h) and 41.66 ± 0.96 HRC (2 h), effectively optimizing the hardness-toughness balance. Post-intervention assessments revealed a 25% reduction in production rejects, an 85% material recovery rate in the waste-to-product mass balance, and a 15% increase in operational cost-efficiency among beneficiaries. The implemented Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for thermal processing and safety ensure institutional sustainability, directly advancing UN SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) through actionable waste valorisation and localis…

title: Prognostic factors and prognostic models for recovery and treatment response in patients with painful cervical radiculopathy: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract Purpose This systematic review aimed to critically appraise (1) prognostic factors and models for recovery, and (2) prognostic factors and models for conservative treatment response in patients with painful cervical radiculopathy. Method MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, APA PsycINFO, and Web of Science were searched. Two independent reviewers screened abstracts and full-text articles and extracted data independently. Data extraction was performed using the Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systematic Reviews checklist. The Quality in Prognostic Studies (QUIPS) and the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment (PROBAST) were used to assess risk of bias. Strength-of-evidence summaries were created in GRADEpro, using prognostic factors and models as outcome variables and evaluating the consistency of the research findings. Results The systematic search retrieved 8,661 records, and seven studies met the selection criteria. Four studies examined prognostic factors: two for recovery and two for response to conservative treatment. Two studies assessed prognostic models predicting recovery after conservative treatment, and one study assessed a prognostic model for treatment response to neural tissue management. All prognostic factors studies were rated high risk and had very low certainty of evidence. The type of health insurance might be a prognostic factor for workdays lost.…

Pathological complete response as a prognostic marker and potential trial-level surrogate endpoint after neoadjuvant immunotherapy for resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Pathological complete response (pCR) is associated with long-term outcomes in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, its prognostic value and validity as a trial-level surrogate endpoint after neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapy remain uncertain. Methods We searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for randomized trials and cohort studies published from January 1, 2000, to February 28, 2026. Prognostic analyses compared patients with and without pCR within PD-1/PD-L1-containing treatment groups. Published or reconstructed log HRs were pooled using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models, with one estimate per parent study and endpoint after within-trial aggregation where required. Trial-level analyses used sample-size-weighted regression of log survival HRs on log pCR ORs. Alternative weighting schemes and leave-one-trial-out analyses were examined. HR-anchored curves were retained as an exploratory illustration rather than a validation method. Results Nine source estimates from eight parent studies contributed to the EFS prognostic analysis, and four studies contributed to the OS analysis. Achievement of pCR was associated with longer EFS (HR, 0.27; 95% CI, 0.19–0.38) and OS (HR, 0.21; 95% CI, 0.09–0.48). Trial-level analyses included seven randomized comparisons for EFS and five for OS, with cumulative comparis…

title: Multi-objective optimization of pulsed tungsten inert gas welding process parameters for Ti-6Al-4 V alloy using response surface methodology, Rao-3 algorithm, and TOPSIS
abstract: Abstract Pulsed tungsten inert gas (TIG) welding is a variant of the TIG welding process and is widely employed in various industries for joining titanium alloys. Owing to its precise control over heat input and periodic variation in arc energy, pulsed TIG welding offers greater flexibility in controlling weld bead geometry. In the present study, 20 bead-on-plate weld experiments were conducted using Pulsed tungsten inert gas (TIG) welding process by varying its process parameters i.e. peak currents ranging from 100 to 160 A and pulse frequencies ranging from 1 to 50 Hz. From 20 bead-on-plate welds, second-order response surface models were developed for bead width, penetration depth and HAZ width, which were then optimized using the parameter-free multi-objective Rao-3 algorithm. Furthermore, TOPSIS was employed to select the best compromise solution from each Pareto front for ten weight sets. The results showed that peak current mainly governed bead width and penetration, whereas pulse frequency controlled the HAZ, and the models predicted the experiments with mean errors below 2.7%. After optimization, the minimum bead width and HAZ width reached 6.67 mm and 1.05 mm, which are 11% and 15% lower than the smallest measured values, respectively. Moreover, a pulse frequency of 28–33 Hz was selected under all weights, and full penetration was achieved at 110–121 A with bead and H…

title: Pathological response and survival outcomes of three neoadjuvant strategies for resectable EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer
abstract: Background The optimal neoadjuvant strategy for resectable epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains uncertain. We compared pathological response and survival outcomes across three neoadjuvant strategies. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 186 patients with resectable stage II–IIIB EGFR-mutant NSCLC who initiated neoadjuvant therapy between 2020 and 2024. The regimens were neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NCT), neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NICT), or neoadjuvant EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor plus chemotherapy (NTT). Of these patients, 166 underwent definitive resection. Major pathological response (MPR) served as the primary endpoint, whereas secondary outcomes comprised pathological complete response (pCR), recurrence-free survival (RFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. Analyses used propensity score matching (PSM), Kaplan–Meier estimation, and Cox regression. Results The resection rates were 83.0%, 90.9%, and 93.3% for NCT, NICT, and NTT, respectively ( P = 0.234). Among resected patients, the MPR rates were 6.8%, 27.5%, and 23.8%, and the pCR rates were 0%, 18.8%, and 14.3%, respectively. At a median follow-up of 35 months, the 3-year RFS estimates were 50.7%, 59.6%, and 87.8%, and the 3-year OS estimates were 71.1%, 90.0%, and 94.2%, respectively. After PSM, OS and RFS curves differed between NTT and NCT (log-rank P = 0.0359 a…

title: Altered prefrontal hemodynamic response during a working memory task in individuals with psychotic spectrum disorders and a history of aggression measured by functional near-infrared spectroscopy
abstract: Introduction Aggressive acts committed by individuals with psychotic spectrum disorders (PSD) account for a small proportion of societal violence but may contribute to stigma. We examined prefrontal hemodynamic responses during visuospatial working memory (WM) in individuals with PSD and a history of aggression (PSD+AGG; n = 76), individuals with PSD without such a history (PSD−AGG; n = 66), and healthy controls (HC; n = 85). Methods Oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO) responses were measured using 16-channel functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) during a Reverse Corsi Block-Tapping Test. Hemodynamic responses were analyzed using performance-modulated and non-amplitude-modulated (NA) generalized linear models. Performance-modulated models incorporated block-level WM performance into task regressors, whereas NA models estimated task-related responses without behavioral amplitude modulation. Multiple comparisons were controlled using cluster-based permutation family-wise error rate (FWER) correction. Results In the performance-modulated Corsi contrast (V.1), PSD+AGG showed a lower HbO response than PSD−AGG in right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) channels 15–16 (cluster p = 0.049), with no significant clusters relative to HC. No significant clusters were observed in the performance-modulated Hard-versus-Easy or NA Corsi contrasts. In the NA Hard-versus-Easy contrast (V.4),…

Agency or reselling: impact of demand information asymmetry on sales mode preferences
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore the selection of sales modes when the supplier partners with the e-commerce platform to establish an online distribution channel, considering the impact of demand information asymmetry. Design/methodology/approach A game-theoretic model is developed in a two-level supply chain with one supplier and one e-commerce platform. Two common sales modes can be chosen, i.e. reselling mode or agency mode. The e-commerce platform holds private demand information, and the supplier invests in demand-enhancement activities (DEA). We explore how the e-commerce platform’s information sharing and the supplier’s DEA investment decisions impact the members’ preferences for sales modes. Findings We identify key factors affecting the selection of sales modes, including revenue-sharing ratio, demand volatility and cost coefficient of DEA. The members’ preferences for sales modes follow threshold-based policies. Originality/value Our findings reveal the interplay between sales mode selection and demand information asymmetry and provide valuable managerial insights to build the collaborative channel partnership for the e-commerce platform supply chain.
