title: The response of smallmouth bass populations in inland lakes to recent invasion by round goby
abstract: The round goby, Neogobius melanostomus , a Ponto-Caspian invader of the Laurentian Great Lakes, is now one of the dominant nearshore prey species. Nearshore predators, such as smallmouth bass ( Micropterus dolomieu ), are benefitting from high round goby abundance and now attain larger body sizes and are generally in better condition. Round goby are beginning to spread to smaller inland lakes in North America, yet the potential impacts to native fishes in these systems are relatively unknown and difficult to predict based on studies from the Great Lakes. Here, we investigated the impact of the round goby on smallmouth bass condition (weight-at-length) and growth (length-at-age) in three invaded inland lakes using body size and age measurements collected by a standardized monitoring program, which we compared to a suite of similar, uninvaded lakes. The condition of smallmouth bass populations in the invaded lakes remained stable in the ~10 years following goby invasion. However, bass in invaded lakes generally exhibited larger asymptotic lengths ( L ∞ ) coupled with slower rates of approaching those lengths ( k ), although responses varied among populations and sampling periods. Reference populations showed the opposite pattern, suggesting the potential for larger maximum body size where round goby are available. Our study shows the potential for inter-lake variability in the re…

Catalytic Manganese Ferrite Nanoparticles Improve Therapeutic Response in Glioblastoma Spheroids through Hypoxia Mitigation
abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive primary brain tumor characterized by treatment resistance, high recurrence rate, and dismal survival, features influenced by tumor hypoxia, a clinically well-established driver of radio- and chemoresistance. Manganese ferrite nanoparticles possess catalase-like activity capable of generating oxygen from tumor-endogenous hydrogen peroxide, offering a strategy to alleviate tumor hypoxia and re-sensitize GBM cells to chemotherapy. In this study, two manganese ferrite compositions (Mn2FeO4 and MnFe2O4) were synthesized using flame spray pyrolysis, characterized, and evaluated for their ability to reduce hypoxia. Nanoparticle internalization and distribution were confirmed in both patient-derived ZH757 and commercial U87MG GBM spheroid models. Both ferrite formulations decreased the hypoxic cell fraction in GBM spheroids after 17 days, without inducing cytotoxicity in normal fibroblasts. Therapeutic in vitro efficacy was assessed on the previously established GliaMimic treatment evaluation platform, which longitudinally monitors tumor progression during a 17-day in vitro treatment regimen of single-fraction radiation (4 Gy) plus multicycle temozolamide (10, 50, 100 μM TMZ) followed by a treatment-free interval. Nanoparticle-treated tumor spheroids exhibited in combination with radio- and chemotherapy enhanced early cytotoxicity and reduce…

title: Structured Mixture Item Response Model (SMIRT) for structured DIF in HRQoL measurement
abstract: Abstract Background Differential item functioning (DIF) is commonly observed in patient-reported outcome (PRO) measures across diverse populations. However, DIF analyses are mainly conducted in a post-hoc fashion and the most common practice is to revise or remove the item, without considering the systematic reason behind the DIF. This study investigated the possibility of using the structured mixture item response model to mitigate the issue by creating a composite scale applicable to heterogeneous groups. Methodology The structured mixture item response model was applied to address latent DIF, where a discontinuity parameter indicates the magnitude of the systematic difference in latent group responding. The analysis used PROMIS legacy anxiety and depression scale as illustrative examples ( N = 740). In total, 27 items were classified into two groups: (a) 14 cognitive-affective items, reflecting affective, cognitive, and interpersonal appraisal symptoms; and (b) 13 somatic-physiological items, reflecting physiological, neurovegetative, behavioral, or bodily symptoms such as appetite changes, sleep disturbance, fatigue, gastrointestinal symptoms, muscle tension, and psychomotor slowing. Results The discontinuity parameter estimated for the anxiety subscale is 2.71 and 2.12 for the depression subscale, which is quite large. Given these estimates, a composite scale is created wh…

title: Micro-cultural activism in slow fashion: how influencers reframe sustainable consumption on Instagram
abstract: Purpose This study examines the activist roles of slow fashion influencers on Instagram, focusing on how they construct and circulate sustainability narratives and reframe sustainable consumption into daily achievable practices. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a qualitative research design, analysing both visual and textual materials from the Instagram posts of slow fashion influencers. Findings The findings reveal that slow fashion influencers operate as micro-cultural activists who perform as educators, advocates and facilitators of ethical consumer practices. By voicing their concerns about workers' rights, animal welfare and textile waste, influencers make complex sustainability issues accessible while encouraging reflection on daily practices such as second-hand shopping, upcycling and recycling. Through their digital narratives, these influencers frame sustainability as an individualized moral identity project, thereby linking their personal consumption choices to lifestyle-oriented ethical advocacy. Research limitations/implications This article contributes to the literature on influencer culture and digital activism by shifting the focus away from short-term behavioural metrics towards cultural meaning-making and demonstrating how influencers use Instagram as a dynamic space for cultural activism. Social implications This paper shows how slow fashion influ…

title: High-power diode laser-assisted reintervention for recurrent fibrotic ankyloglossia following two scalpel frenectomies: a case report with 23​-month follow-up
abstract: Abstract Background Recurrent functional tongue restriction after previous lingual frenectomies presents a clinical challenge, particularly when earlier surgical records are unavailable. Case presentation A 22-year-old woman reported two previous scalpel frenectomies followed by recurrent restriction of tongue mobility. Before reintervention, maximum mouth opening was 51 mm, whereas opening with the tongue tip touching the incisive papilla was 16 mm (31.37%). Management comprised surgical release with a 980-nm high-power diode laser, histopathological examination of the excised tissue, perioperative photobiomodulation (808 nm before surgery and 660 nm afterward), and postoperative orofacial myofunctional therapy. Histopathology showed collagen-rich tissue consistent with fibrosis but could not establish its cause. Tongue-to-papilla opening increased to 29 mm immediately after surgery and measured 27 mm at eight months, an 11-mm improvement relative to baseline. At approximately 23 months, clinical examination showed a healed surgical site without clinically evident anterior frenulum reattachment; the patient reported satisfactory oral function without perceived recurrent tongue restriction. No standardized quantitative tongue-mobility measurement was obtained at this later visit. Conclusion This case documents favorable clinical and patient-reported findings after a multimodal …

title: Trade-offs in the Energy Transition: Local Public Health Gains and Socioeconomic Costs of U.S. Coal Facility Retirements
abstract: Retirement of coal-fired power stations and industrial coal plants is a crucial characteristic of the US energy transition process. While reduction in fossil fuel consumption provides climate and air-quality benefits nationwide, local communities hosting these facilities face uneven socio-economic, fiscal and public health outcomes. This paper analyses local socio-economic and public-health consequences of US coal-related facility shutdowns from the perspective of negative externality environmental economic theory and with the help of comparative case studies of Huntley Coal-Generating Station and Shenango Coke Works. By using peer-reviewed scholarly literature and secondary empirical evidence published in governmental reports, the paper aims to address two main research questions. First, what is the mixture of benefits and concentrated local costs of coal infrastructure shutdown? Secondly, what makes it so hard to prove the empirical link between environment policy, environmental conditions in the locality and health results and what case study evidence can be gained from a natural experiment?

title: Beyond “No Bed Syndrome”: reframing hospital bed shortages as a patient-flow and health-system coordination problem in Ghana
abstract: Ghana's “No Bed Syndrome” describes a recurring pattern in which patients seeking emergency or referred care are reportedly turned away because a receiving facility is said to have no bed. Existing evidence suggests the problem cannot be reduced to a simple count of physical beds. This Perspective develops a clinically and operationally grounded interpretation of No Bed Syndrome and proposes a feasible pathway for testing the mechanisms that may produce admission failure. Drawing on a targeted, non-systematic synthesis of Ghana-specific literature, patient flow is used as the primary organising framework, with the WHO health-system building blocks locating upstream system constraints and governance and the legal-institutional environment treated as contextual determinants rather than separate causal models. We argue that No Bed Syndrome is best understood as a multidimensional patient-flow problem involving genuine bed scarcity, staffed or functional-capacity shortages, delayed discharge, referral failure, poor visibility of available capacity, and potentially discretionary admission decisions; the last of these remains an untested hypothesis in Ghana. We further show that the primary text of Ghana's Health Institutions and Facilities Act, 2011 (Act 829) does not support the frequently repeated attribution of a vicarious-liability rule to section 25, which is in fact an interpr…

title: ANALYSIS OF GOVERNMENT MANAGEMENT IN VILLAGE DEVELOPMENT
abstract: This study aims to analyze government management in village development, based on management functions that encompass planning, organizing, implementation and supervision. Village development serves as a strategic effort to enhance community welfare through resource management, institutional strengthening, and increased public participation. The study applies government management theory, specifically focusing on planning, organizing, mobilizing, and supervising (POAC). A purposive sampling technique was employed to select informants, including the Village Head, Village Secretary, Head of the Economic and Development Division, Hamlet Heads, and community members. The findings regarding government management in the village development of Lebakmuncang reveal that the planning phase is not yet effective due to a lack of public dissemination regarding village development plans. Organizing remains ineffective, as evidenced by the misalignment between the competencies of government personnel and their assigned roles, which hinders the optimal distribution of work during development execution. Mobilization is also ineffective due to a lack of clarity regarding technical development specifications and project duration. Furthermore, supervision remains ineffective, as demonstrated by the absence of follow-up on both internal and external oversight findings, leaving the final outcomes of…

title: When newcomer influx becomes a retention risk: The moderating role of entry-level benefits
abstract: Early newcomer turnover is a persistent challenge for organizations, yet little is known about whether the scale of newcomer entry itself is associated with newcomer retention. Drawing on research on human capital flows and newcomer retention, we examine newcomer influx, defined as the number of newcomers entering an organization relative to its regular workforce, and test whether entry-level benefits condition its association with early turnover. Using five waves of Human Capital Corporate Panel II data from South Korea, we analyze 2,039 firm-year observations from 510 firms. Firm and year fixed-effects models show that within-firm increases in newcomer influx are associated with higher same-year newcomer turnover. This association is weaker when entry-level benefits are more favorable than the firm’s typical level. Count-based and other sensitivity analyses provide additional, although specification-sensitive, evidence for this pattern. The findings are interpreted as contemporaneous within-firm associations rather than causal effects.

title: Impact pathways: flexibility on the factory floor – expanding gig labor research into the manufacturing context
abstract: Purpose Manufacturers have begun to experiment with gig labor due to persistent workforce shortages. This article develops impact pathways that specify what manufacturers must resolve for gig labor to function as an effective flexibility lever, and where operations and supply chain management (OSCM) research can advance implementation. Design/methodology/approach We conducted 13 semi-structured interviews, 11 with manufacturing executives and two with CEOs of manufacturing-focused gig labor platforms. Transcripts were analyzed with a Gioia-style coding process. Findings We identify four impact pathways shaping whether gig labor can work in manufacturing: (1) designing flexible workflows for gig labor integration; (2) building plant-level legitimacy for hybrid core–gig workforces; (3) enablement of gig labor through platform mediation; and (4) governing the manufacturing gig labor supply chain. The pathways highlight implications for managers, platform designers, and policymakers. Managers should modularize suitable tasks, design quality into processes, and make the benefits of gig labor visible to incumbent workers. Platforms should embed skills-based matching without increasing income instability, and policymakers should assess whether safety, liability, and worker-classification rules fit flexible arrangements. Originality/value Gig labor research, developed mainly in consume…

title: AI words, AI deeds, and environmental assessment: the role of managerial ability
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how managerial ability (MA), AI-related disclosure (AI Words) and AI-related investment intensity (AI Deeds), a CSMAR-based proxy covering enabling digital assets, relate to composite environmental performance (EP) and external environmental ratings and whether the two AI measures are assessed differently. Design/methodology/approach Using data from Chinese non-financial A-share listed firms for 2010–2023, the study estimates models with firm and year fixed effects to examine the associations of MA, AI Words and AI Deeds with EP and external environmental ratings. Findings MA has a modest positive association with EP and a consistent negative association with AI Deeds, although the corresponding indirect association remains exploratory. In the contemporaneous model for the full rated sample, AI Words is associated with higher external ratings and AI Deeds with lower ratings, while neither is associated with rating-excluded EP. This pattern indicates a potential environmental assessment gap. Practical implications Regulators, rating providers and boards may benefit from distinguishing visible AI narratives from verifiable implementation and outcomes. Assessment and oversight frameworks for climate-transition governance could consider disclosure, resource allocation and energy implications rather than treating AI adoption as uniformly beneficial…

title: Multidisciplinary management of inoperable stage III nonsmall-cell lung cancer
abstract: Purpose of review Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized modern treatment of nonsmall-cell lung cancer in recent years. This review tries to describe the important changes that the Pacific trial has implemented into the treatment of locally advanced nonsmall-cell lung cancer with chemoradiotherapy as its former major locoregional management and intends to outline possible ways in the future to further improve long-term results. Recent findings One large randomized phase-III trial has completely changed our standard of care for stage III nonsmall-cell lung cancer. In patients without progression following definitive chemoradiation protocols, one year of consolidation therapy with durvalumab has become the treatment of choice. The FDA granted approval for durvalumab in February 2018 while the EMA selected patients with immunohistochemical PD-L1 positivity for approval in Europe during September 2018. The landmark results of this clinical trial and administration regimen have been supported by several extended access and real world investigations including long-term overall survival results of such a therapeutic design within the last years. Further insights have been gained on the management with this treatment strategy for patient populations confined to sequential administration of chemotherapy and radiation due to underlying comorbidities. Mechanistically …

title: Expert consensus on the management of hematologic adverse reactions related to pegylated interferon-alpha therapy for chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Abstract To assist clinicians in making rational decisions regarding the management of hematologic adverse reactions during pegylated interferon-alpha (PEG-IFN-α) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB), the National Medical Center for Infectious Diseases organized a panel of experts in infectious diseases, hepatology, hematology, and clinical pharmacy to develop this consensus based on current evidence and clinical practice. The consensus systematically describes the incidence, clinical characteristics, and mechanisms of neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, and anemia during PEG-IFN-α treatment for CHB; analyzes the association between cytopenias and antiviral efficacy; and proposes pretreatment risk stratification, standardized monitoring strategies, graded management protocols (including oral leukocyte-raising agents, recombinant human granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, recombinant human interleukin-11, recombinant human thrombopoietin, and other supportive therapies), as well as management recommendations for special populations, including patients with liver cirrhosis, older adults, children, and patients with renal insufficiency. It emphasizes that mild-to-moderate cytopenias should not be used as the sole reason for dose reduction or treatment discontinuation but should be assessed in conjunction with on-treatment efficacy indicators. This consensus aims to provide a referen…

Research on the Impact of Digital Inclusive Finance on Corporate Financing Costs: Theoretical Mechanisms and Empirical Tests
abstract: This paper takes Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share non-financial listed companies from 2012 to 2023 as the sample, matches city-level digital inclusive finance indexes of firms' registered places with corporate financial data, and examines the relationship between regional digital finance development and corporate financing costs. The empirical part uses the natural logarithm of financing costs as the dependent variable and the prefecture-level city digital inclusive finance aggregate index as the core explanatory variable; after adding control variables such as firm size, leverage, profitability, growth and firm age, industry and year fixed effects are controlled, and standard errors are clustered at the firm level. The results show that the estimated coefficient of the digital inclusive finance index is −0.1757 and is significant at the 1% level, indicating that regions with higher digital finance development correspond to lower corporate financing costs. Further analysis finds that digital inclusive finance is significantly positively correlated with both analyst attention and research report coverage, which supports the explanatory channel of external information environment improvement. Grouping results show that this negative relationship is more obvious in the samples of non-state-owned enterprises, larger enterprises and the eastern region. After adopting an alternative fin…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: System Dynamics Based Decision Support Model for Assessing Urban Water Availability: A Case Study of Bogor City
abstract: Background: Urban water availability is increasingly challenged by population growth, land-use changes, and rising water demand, necessitating integrated approaches to sustainable water-resource management. Objective: This study aims to develop a system dynamics-based decision-support framework for assessing long-term urban water availability in Bogor City, Indonesia. Methods: System dynamics modeling was conducted using Vensim, incorporating causal loop diagrams (CLDs), stock-and-flow diagrams (SFDs), and sensitivity analysis over a 100-year simulation period. Two scenarios were evaluated: a baseline model representing primary water supply and demand components (Scenario 1) and an expanded model incorporating green open space, rainfall, tourism, nonresident workers, water pricing, and household groundwater consumption (Scenario 2). Results: Both scenarios demonstrated declining trends in water availability and water balance. At Year 100, the high-case water balance reached approximately −1.40 billion m³/year in Scenario 1 and −1.01 billion m³/year in Scenario 2, reflecting structural model differences rather than demonstrable improvements in water availability. Sensitivity analysis identified the new subscriber rate and green open space ratio as the most influential parameters. In Scenario 2, variations in the new subscriber rate generated differences of approximately 33 billi…

title: Restorative Spaces, Privacy and Environmental Comfort in Hospital Wards: Architectural Requirements for Informal Caregiver Well Being
abstract: Informal caregivers provide essential support to hospitalised patients in Nigeria, yet hospital wards rarely accommodate their need for rest, privacy and environmental comfort. This article examines the architectural conditions affecting caregiver well-being in three tertiary hospitals in Jos, Nigeria, and identifies priorities for more supportive ward design. Drawing on a convergent mixed-methods study, it analyses questionnaires from 196 informal caregivers, interviews with 12 healthcare professionals, focus group discussions and structured observations at Jos University Teaching Hospital, Bingham University Teaching Hospital and Plateau State Specialist Hospital. 95.9% of respondents reported inadequate sleeping facilities, 88.8% reported privacy deficiencies, 80.6% reported thermal discomfort, 72.4% reported noise exposure, and 66.3% reported inadequate lighting. Sleeping provision was the strongest predictor of caregiver satisfaction (β = .45, p < .001), followed by privacy (β = .32, p < .01) and sanitation (β = .28, p < .05). Overcrowding was associated with emotional stress (r = .71, p < .001). Findings indicate that caregiver accommodation and environmental quality warrant explicit consideration in healthcare planning. The article recommends accessible rest facilities, adaptable furniture, privacy-sensitive arrangements and climate-responsive environmental improvements,…
venue: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT

title: Digital Sports Diplomacy as a Soft Power Instrument: An Assessment in Light of Global Indices and Social Media Data
abstract: Digital platforms have transformed diplomatic communication and expanded the areas in which sports diplomacy is carried out. This study examines the role of digital sports diplomacy in soft power production by using BCW Sports Practice's International Sports Federations Social Media Report (2020), the International Olympic Committee's digital engagement data regarding the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Olympic Games, and the Brand Finance Global Soft Power Index (2024). The study adopted a secondary data-based convergent parallel mixed-methods design. Here, qualitative documentary data and quantitative data, including social media metrics, digital engagement indicators, and soft power scores, were analyzed together. Document analysis, descriptive content analysis, descriptive thematic synthesis, and pattern matching techniques were used in the analysis process. The theoretical framework of the study was based on Corneliu Bjola's digital diplomacy model, Manuel Castells's network society theory, and Joseph Nye's concept of soft power. The findings showed that there is no direct causal relationship between international sports federations' digital presence and countries' soft power indicators. However, certain similarities and structural parallels were observed between them. The Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 data also revealed that digital engagement became more visible in sports diplomac…

title: Robot-Assisted 3D Metallography: System Development, Methodology, and Applications
abstract: Classical metallography using 2D sections provides reliable information on phase fractions but is limited for the quantitative determination of spatial geometries such as pore shapes, graphite morphology, conductor track geometries, or dendrite structures. Automated serial sectioning systems, known as 3D metallography, enable the generation of large-volume image stacks with high lateral resolution and controlled contrast through chemical etching, followed by digital reconstruction as 3D digital twins. This work integrates the methodological foundations and system architecture of the RASI system (Robot-Assisted Automated Serial-Sectioning and Imaging) developed at BAM with application examples, e.g. pore structures in sintered steel (Astaloy CrA). The emphasis lies on a detailed, reproducible methodology covering preparation, imaging, alignment, interpolation, and segmentation, along with quantitative presentation of results regarding shape, size, and distribution, and an in-depth discussion of the informational superiority of 3D over 2D analysis, system performance, limitations, and extension potential.

title: Performance investigation of a newly designed ventilative cooling garment for thermal management in hot environments
abstract: Purpose This study aims to address the occupational hazard of heat stress among outdoor workers by developing and evaluating a novel, lightweight ventilative cooling garment (VCG) for effective personal thermal management in hot environments. Design/methodology/approach The VCG adopts a separated heat transfer design and a two-stage air-blowing system. Its cooling performance was evaluated through thermal manikin and human subject tests under simulated hot and humid conditions (35°C, 50% RH). Findings The newly developed VCG is the lightest among comparable garments, delivering 39 W of cooling power with low energy consumption (7.5 W) and maintaining effective cooling for over five hours with 500 g of ice. The garment significantly reduced core and skin temperatures and heart rate, and improved thermal comfort and perceived exertion (p < 0.05) compared to controls. Thermal manikin tests confirmed reduced evaporative resistance and enhanced moisture permeability, while the garment maintained a safe cooling temperature of 32°C, avoiding skin erythema. Practical implications The VCG offers a promising solution for mitigating heat stress and improving safety and comfort for individuals working or exercising in hot environments. Originality/value This study introduces a novel, lightweight VCG that not only enhances cooling performance and user comfort, but also addresses key limi…
venue: International Journal of Clothing Science and Technology

title: First Results of a Radioxenon Detection System in Lithuania Capable of Tracing Radioxenon Releases from Different Sources
Beyond Participation: Indigenous Peoples’ Rights through Free, Prior and Informed Consent in Natural Resource Management
abstract: The protection of Indigenous peoples’ rights in natural resource management in Indonesia continues to face a gap between normative recognition and implementation, particularly due to the absence of comprehensive Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) standards. This research aims to analyze the philosophical foundations and implementation of FPIC and formulate a model for strengthening the protection of Indigenous peoples’ rights in natural resource management. The research employs normative legal research with statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches involving Canada and Peru through a literature review of primary and secondary legal materials. The findings show that FPIC positions Indigenous peoples as rights-holding subjects entitled to determine their position freely, prior to the implementation of activities, based on adequate information, and through genuine consent. Although Indonesia’s legal framework recognizes Indigenous peoples’ rights, FPIC regulation remains fragmented, insufficiently harmonized, and unsupported by adequate verification mechanisms, thereby risking its application being limited to formal consultation. Comparative analysis indicates the need to establish FPIC as a condition for the validity of decisions, with consent standards adjusted to the level of impact of the activity. The proposed model rests on three pillars: an overarching FPIC nor…
venue: Journal of Law, Environmental and Justice

title: Case Report: Indolent T-cell lymphoma of the gastrointestinal tract with central nervous system and bone marrow involvement
abstract: Indolent T-cell lymphoma of the gastrointestinal tract (ITCL-GI) is a rare mature T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder that usually follows a chronic clinical course; however, dissemination to high-risk sites, including the central nervous system (CNS) and bone marrow, may occur and substantially complicate diagnosis and management. We report a 42-year-old man who presented with progressive limb numbness for 2 years and gait instability for 2 months. Small-bowel endoscopy revealed multiple erosions, shallow ulcers, and luminal narrowing in the proximal jejunum. Biopsy demonstrated diffuse infiltration of small- to medium-sized lymphocytes with a CD2+/CD3+/CD5+/CD7+/CD8+/TIA-1+ phenotype, a low Ki-67 index, and monoclonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement. Review of prior gastric biopsies showed similar features. Bone marrow biopsy and cerebrospinal fluid cytology and flow immunophenotyping identified phenotypically concordant atypical T-cell populations, supporting a diagnosis of ITCL-GI with secondary involvement of the bone marrow and CNS. The patient received intrathecal methotrexate and cytarabine, together with antiviral therapy and subsequent systemic treatment. At approximately 2 years of follow-up, the patient maintained overall clinical stability with improved gastrointestinal symptoms, albeit with persistent neurological deficits and no documented complete remission. …

A Consumption-Based Forecasting Framework for Automotive Spare Parts Inventory Optimization: A Case Study of CFAO Mobility Nigeria
abstract: Effective spare-parts inventory management requires balancing parts availability with the financial risks of excess and obsolete stock. This study develops a Consumption-Based Forecasting (CBF) framework for optimizing Suzuki spare-parts inventory at CFAO Mobility Nigeria. Using after sales inventory and consumption records covering August 2025 to April 2026, the study applies a quantitative case-study approach integrating average monthly consumption, demand-velocity classification, stock inactivity assessment, usable inventory estimation and forecast-based replenishment decisions. The results show that total inventory value declined by 8.5%, from NGN 444.32 million to NGN 406.39 million, while the reported provision-stock ratio increased from 51% to 60%. SKU-level analysis further revealed contrasting inventory positions: an oil filter recorded average monthly consumption of 95.3 units and a forecast stock requirement of +665 units, indicating a replenishment need, whereas a fuel filter recorded average monthly consumption of 1.7 units and a surplus of 232 units. These findings demonstrate the coexistence of replenishment needs and excess stock within the same after sales inventory system. The proposed framework provides a structured basis for differentiated procurement, surplus-stock control and inventory-risk monitoring. Its predictive performance and operational effectivene…

title: Linear-information-flow price models: bilateral inverse-Gaussian option pricing and directional information rates
Out-of-Sample Volatility Forecasting for the SPDR S&P Retail ETF: A Comparison of GARCH and GJR-GARCH Models
abstract: This paper compares the out-of-sample volatility forecasting performance of several GARCH-family specifications for the SPDR S&P Retail ETF (XRT). The analysis uses daily adjusted closing prices from June 2006 to September 2026 to construct percentage log returns. Observations through December 2022 form the training sample, leaving 939 trading days for out-of-sample evaluation. The comparison covers GARCH(1,1) and GJR-GARCH(1,1) models under both normal and standardized Student-t innovations. One-step-ahead variance forecasts are produced with an expanding estimation window, with parameters re-estimated every 20 trading days. A 22-day historical-volatility measure serves as the benchmark. Forecast performance is evaluated mainly by QLIKE, RMSE and MAE, with QLIKE-based Diebold–Mariano tests used as supplementary evidence. GJR-GARCH with Student-t innovations records the lowest forecast loss across QLIKE, RMSE and MAE. The positive asymmetric coefficient also indicates a stronger conditional-variance response to negative innovations than to positive innovations of the same magnitude. These gains are small, however, and none of the pairwise QLIKE differences remains significant after Holm adjustment. Replacing the ARMA(0,1) mean specification with ARMA(0,0) does not change the model ranking. Overall, the evidence points to some benefit from allowing for asymmetry and heavy tails,…
