title: The Influence of Product Quality, Price Perception, and eWOM on Purchasing Decisions for “NS Fresh” Brand Strawberries
abstract: The background of this research is based on the fierce competition in the fresh fruit market and the fluctuations in sales prices such as NS Fresh brand strawberries which are required to implement an effective marketing strategy. This condition is strengthened by the rise of digital reviews (EWOM) on social media which is now the main reference for consumers before deciding to buy. The purpose of this study is to analyze the influence of product quality, price perception and EWOM on the purchase decision of NS Fresh strawberries. This study uses a qualitative method with ordinal data and is measured using a likert scale as an attitude measurement scale. Data collection was carried out by distributing questionnaires to 97 respondents that had been determined according to the Lemeshow formula. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression analysis. The results of the analysis of the F Test showed that Product Quality (X1), Price Perception (X2), and EWOM (X3) together had a significant effect on the purchase decision with a significance value of 0.000 < 0.005, and the results of the T Test analysis partially affected the purchase decision, with a significance value of Product Quality (X1) of 0.008 < 0.05, a significance value of Price Perception (X2) of 0.000 < 0.05, and EWOM (X3) of 0.037 < 0.05. This shows that the better the Product Quality, Price Perception, and EW…

title: Weather-Related Crash Risk Forecasting: A Forecast-Conditioned Deep Learning Framework for Heterogeneous Spatiotemporal Data
abstract: Abstract This study develops and evaluates a deep learning framework for forecasting weather-related statewide traffic crash risk. Using North Carolina crash records (2015–2018) aggregated to an equivalent-property-damage-only (EPDO) severity index on a 5-mi grid at weekly resolution, we train Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) networks under training-only normalization and climatology and combine independently initialized networks through deep-ensemble averaging. The framework is benchmarked against persistence, seasonal, climatological, linear, ARIMA, and gradient-boosting baselines with Diebold-Mariano and Wilcoxon significance tests over repeated random seeds. Two findings emerge. First, when models are restricted to crash-history inputs alone, the cell-level climatological mean proves to be a stringent benchmark that no method, including the deep ensemble, surpasses: at this resolution, weekly crash-risk anomalies carry little signal that crash history alone can recover, which establishes climatology as the reference against which weather-related crash forecasts should be judged. Second, conditioning on the target week’s meteorology restores predictability: a climatology-anchored residual model with weather features improves mean squared error over climatology by 6.8% ( $$p<0.01$$ p < 0.01 ), and by about 10% on cell-weeks with crashes, with gains concentrated…

title: Forecasting the Baltic Dry Index with Classical Time Series Models: A Rolling Out-of-Sample Evaluation
abstract: Predicting short-horizon movements in dry bulk freight rates matters for shipping operators and commodity desks. The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) summarises assessment-based rates across major dry bulk routes and is treated as an important market indicator. This paper addresses a focused question: among four classical univariate models, which produces the most accurate one-day-ahead forecasts of the daily BDI level on a recent sample? A naïve random walk, simple exponential smoothing, the Holt linear trend method and ARIMA are compared under a fixed 500-day rolling window from January 2018 to October 2026. Model parameters and states are updated so that each out-of-sample forecast uses only information available up to the previous trading day. Accuracy is measured by RMSE, MAE and MAPE; pairwise differences are tested with the Diebold–Mariano statistic under squared-error loss. Daily log returns are examined only through ARCH-LM tests and a short volatility sketch, and do not enter the level ranking. On this sample the Holt method records the lowest errors and significantly outperforms the random walk, whereas ARIMA ranks last. The results suggest that a parsimonious trend-aware smoother can be competitive for next-day BDI levels, and that volatility models should not share the same ranking as level forecasts.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: AutoML forecasting and internet-based political attention: a foresight perspective on PoW versus PoS cryptocurrencies
abstract: Purpose This study aims to assess whether macro-financial conditions and Trump-related political attention (TPA) provide useful information for one-hour-ahead cryptocurrency forecasting. It retains the comparative perspective between proof-of-work (PoW) and proof-of-stake (PoS) cryptocurrencies, while treating the PoW–PoS comparison as exploratory rather than causal. Design/methodology/approach Using H2O AutoML and hourly data from January to July 2025 for Bitcoin, Bitcoin Cash, Litecoin, Ethereum, Algorand and Cardano, the revised forecasting design predicts exact one-hour-ahead log returns and reconstructs prices from the return forecasts. All predictors are aligned to information available no later than time t. AutoML is compared with Random Walk, ARIMA, ARIMAX, Ridge and XGBoost under a three-block expanding-window out-of-sample design. Forecast differences are evaluated using Diebold–Mariano tests, and the incremental contribution of TPA is assessed by comparing otherwise identical AutoML specifications with and without TPA. Findings The revised results show that short-horizon cryptocurrency forecasting is dominated by strong persistence: Random Walk and ARIMA remain difficult benchmarks to outperform. H2O AutoML is competitive for several assets but does not systematically dominate simple benchmarks. Adding TPA produces heterogeneous rather than universal gains; the clear…

title: Sales Forecasting and Inventory Control of Turbean Coffee Raw Materials Using the Moving Average and EOQ Methods
abstract: Turbean Coffee produces coffee beverages before customers place their orders, so production volumes must be adjusted according to changes in sales and the availability of raw materials. This study aims to select the forecasting method with the lowest error, calculate material requirements, determine ordering policies, and compare inventory costs. Sales data from January–December 2025, recipe compositions, inventory costs, and supplier lead times were used in this case study. Three variations of the Moving Average MA2, MA3, and MA4 as well as the naïve method were tested over the period May–December 2025 using MAD, MSE, and MAPE. Material requirements were calculated based on sales and recipe proportions. Order quantities, safety stock, and reorder points were calculated using Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), Safety Stock, and Reorder Point. MA2 produced the lowest MAPE of 8.44% and a steady projection of 330.50 cups per month, or 3,966 cups in 2026. Actual sales of 3,410 cups in 2025 are equivalent to a demand of 85,250 g of coffee beans, 443.30 L of milk, 17,050 g of creamer, and 34,100 mL of each type of syrup. Based on the 2026 projection, the economic order quantity for coffee beans is 23,349.07 g, with a safety stock of 188 g and a reorder point of 1,752 g. The milk order quantity of 102.91 L is equivalent to approximately 63 days of operations. In a simulation using 2025 de…

title: H-IBTT: a multi-module integrated model based on hybrid WOA algorithm for short-term flow forecasting of sewage
Forward model of the Gaia DR3 selection function
abstract: The completeness of an astronomical catalogue depends on its selection function, which is a combination of the observing strategy, instrumental characteristics, and intrinsic properties of the sources being observed. This is particularly complex for Gaia, whose non-uniform scanning law and onboard prioritisation of bright sources in dense areas make its selection function vary strongly with celestial position and source brightness. We estimate the source catalogue selection function across the whole sky and over the full magnitude range, using only data from the Gaia catalogue and knowledge of the nominal scanning law as provided by the Gaia Observation Forecast Tool. 3 We developed a hierarchical Bayesian model that estimates the number of times Gaia scanned each celestial position jointly with the source detection efficiency, and fitted it via Markov chain Monte Carlo to the 1,806,196,447 sources in 3 with reported celestial positions, G magnitudes, and astrometric matched transit counts. 3 is essentially complete for G ∈ (5,19.5) in the on-sky median. After that, the completeness decreases with magnitude according to the scanning law pattern combined with the imprint of crowded regions. The completeness is also lower at the very bright end of the survey, consistent with the known limitations on Gaia observations of bright stars. We find an unexpected completeness increase be…

title: Area-Level Market, Neighbourhood and Socioeconomic Indicators for Housing Price Estimation
abstract: Reliable housing price estimation supports investment, development and planning decisions, yet many machine learning studies depend on property attributes such as floor area and number of bedrooms that open datasets often lack. This study examined whether area-level market, neighbourhood and socioeconomic indicators can predict housing prices, compared six regression algorithms, and deployed the best model as a web decision support system. A random sample of 200,000 records from the HouseTS dataset was split 80:20 into training and testing sets.
venue: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology

title: Price sensitivity and impulsive consumption in all-you-can-eat buffets: a moderated mediation perspective
abstract: Introduction This study examines the association between price sensitivity and impulsive consumption intention in all-you-can-eat buffet dining. Using Prospect Theory as the overall theoretical perspective and drawing on mental accounting and compensatory-consumption reasoning, it proposes a moderated mediation model involving Fear of Missing Out (FoMO), Psychological Ownership (PO), and Health Consciousness (HC). Methods A cross-sectional survey of 485 adults in China was used to test the model. FoMO and PO were specified as mediators, and HC was examined as a moderator of the associations between price sensitivity and FoMO, PO, and impulsive consumption intention. Results Price sensitivity was positively associated with impulsive consumption intention. The indirect association through PO was significant, whereas the indirect association through FoMO alone was not. The serial indirect path from price sensitivity through FoMO and PO to impulsive consumption intention was significant. The interactions between price sensitivity and HC were negative in the impulsive consumption intention, FoMO, and PO equations, indicating weaker associations with price sensitivity at higher levels of HC. Discussion The findings identify PO as the most proximal psychological correlate of impulsive consumption intention in the proposed model and highlight HC as a boundary condition for the associat…

title: Financing constraints and energy-price incentives shape community-heating investment and domestic carbon accounts: a synthetic-community analysis for Jinan, China
abstract: Public money for community heating is limited, and its carbon effect depends on how it is paid, not only how much. Support can relax initial financing, change marginal energy prices or merely move payments, yet evaluations rarely separate these channels, and carbon accounts can mistake a change of payer for a change of demand. This modelling study separates them: capital support of equal public present value tests the financing channel, annual support of the same present value, which pays 34% more undiscounted, serves as an accounting check of the payer channel, and a current-rule energy reimbursement tests the marginal-price channel; each is followed into dated domestic supply-chain carbon accounts (domestic fossil CO 2 plus on-site gas combustion, undiscounted). The experiment uses a financing-constrained investment model of a synthetic, uncalibrated 17-building community in Jinan, China, checked by 10-min redispatch, so its numbers illustrate mechanisms rather than estimate the effects of Jinan’s policies. Fixed support changed the heating system only when it relaxed a binding limit on initial finance. With private finance hard-capped at half the reference investment, all-capital support reduced the 20-year carbon account by 1.9–2.5 kt across ±30% installed costs and ±20% retail prices, and by about 2,550 t in the reference case. Under the same cap, a fully repaid interest-f…

title: The Interaction Between Managerial Tone and Investor Sentiment in Shaping Stock Price Informativeness: Evidence from China's A-Share Market
abstract: Managerial tone and investor sentiment are two informational forces that may reinforce or offset each other in capital markets. Signaling theory suggests that managerial tone conveys firm-specific information as a textual soft signal, while behavioral finance suggests that investor sentiment affects the information content of stock prices by shaping how efficiently investors process information. Whether these two forces are complementary or substitutive in determining stock price informativeness, however, remains unclear. Using a sample of 30 Chinese A-share listed firms from 2018 to 2025, this study constructs a managerial tone measure from annual reports and uses turnover rate as a proxy for investor sentiment. Panel fixed-effects models are used to estimate their individual and interactive associations with stock price synchronicity. Managerial tone is negatively but not significantly associated with synchronicity when examined separately, whereas the interaction between tone and sentiment is significantly positive. This result suggests a substitutive relationship: the synchronicity-reducing association of tone weakens in high-attention environments. The findings indicate that the information conveyed by managerial tone depends on market attention and provide evidence on asset pricing in environments with multiple information sources.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Mismatch between original and promotional price colors does not inhibit purchase intention
abstract: Purpose The primary objective of this study was to investigate whether incongruence between original and promotional price colors in the context of sales promotion would diminish purchase intention. Additionally, the study sought to examine whether this effect depends on product type and elaboration. Design/methodology/approach Five experiments examined the effects of color incongruence between original and promotional prices. Experiments 1 and 2 used a between-subjects design in which original and promotional prices appeared in different color combinations (red, blue, green or black), creating match versus mismatch conditions. Experiments 3 and 4A extended this approach by restricting colors to red and black and adding product type (utilitarian vs. hedonic) or elaboration level (low vs. high), respectively. Experiment 4 B further simplified the design to a two-level color condition (consistent vs. inconsistent) crossed with elaboration. Purchase intention was the primary dependent variable, with attitude towards the ad and willingness to pay also measured. Findings Experiment 1 showed no interaction between original and promotional price colors. Experiment 2 replicated the results. Experiment 3 showed the null effects regardless of product type. Experiment 4A further verified that the null effects still held regardless of elaboration. Notably, in line with the previous experim…

title: Earnings Preannouncement Quality and Analyst Forecasting Behavior: A Two-Dimensional Examination of Accuracy and Precision
abstract: Earnings preannouncements are important forward-looking information that listed companies use to convey their expected operating performance to the market before the formal release of periodic reports. They also serve as a key anchoring basis for analysts when forming earnings forecasts. High-quality performance forecast can reduce information asymmetry in the capital market and help external investors and analysts reasonably judge the operating conditions of enterprises. However, earnings preannouncement quality differs greatly across firms, and its influence on analyst forecasting behavior deserves further examination. Using a sample of non-financial A-share listed companies from 2017 to 2024, this paper examines how earnings preannouncement quality affects analyst forecasts. The results show that the accuracy error of earnings preannouncements significantly affects both analyst forecast bias and forecast dispersion. In contrast, the precision error increases forecast dispersion at the 5% level, while its effect on forecast bias is not significant. Further tests indicate that the degree of earnings management weakens the above transmission paths, providing empirical evidence for the "noise interference" theory.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Forecasting US Recessions with the Treasury Yield Curve
abstract: This paper examines the predictive power of the US Treasury yield curve for economic recessions using monthly data from September 1981 to September 2025. Two term spreads — the 10-year minus 3-month and the 10-year minus 2-year spreads — are compared within a binary Logit framework across forecast horizons of 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months. The results confirm that a lower term spread is associated with a higher recession probability, with the relationship strengthening at longer horizons. The 10-year minus 3-month spread retains statistical significance after controlling for the federal funds rate, unemployment, and CPI inflation, whereas the 10-year minus 2-year spread does not. In-sample fit improves from near zero at the 3-month horizon to a pseudo-R² of 0.126 at 24 months. Both spreads produce elevated recession probabilities before the 1990–91, 2001, 2007–09, and 2020 recessions, though the 2022–24 inversion has not yet been followed by a downturn. Out-of-sample tests using an expanding window confirm the in-sample pattern. The findings support the yield curve as a useful but imperfect leading indicator, while direct testing of transmission channels such as bank lending remains a direction for future research.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Nonlinear trajectories and individualized risk prediction of Xiyanping injection adverse drug reactions in children
abstract: Background Managing adverse drug reactions (ADRs) associated with Xiyanping injection remains a clinical challenge. This study aimed to identify potential risk factors, explore non-linear trajectories, and develop an individualized risk score for pediatric ADRs. Methods In this prospective cohort, 650 pediatric patients receiving Xiyanping were enrolled. LASSO regression and Cox proportional hazards models were utilized for feature selection. Potential non-linearities and interactive associations were evaluated using restricted cubic splines (RCS). An integer risk score was constructed and internally validated via bootstrap resampling and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results The overall ADR incidence was 4.15%. Absence of syndrome differentiation-guided treatment and polypharmacy were identified as primary risk-associated factors. Exploratory RCS analysis suggested a borderline, non-significant J-shaped dosage pattern (P for non-linearity = 0.079; exploratory inflection point at 7.6 mg/kg), which showed a hypothesis-generating positive additive interaction with allergy history. Subgroup analyses indicated that syndrome differentiation-guided treatment was consistently associated with lower ADR occurrence. The exploratory integer risk score demonstrated acceptable optimism-corrected discrimination (C-index=0.881) and calibration in internal bootstrap validation. Conclusion Syn…

title: The pre-leukemic clock: mutational dynamics, Inflammaging, and AI-driven risk prediction in clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP)
Statistical Methods for Assessment and Prediction of Cutting Tool Life
abstract: The stability of a cutting tool and its wear patterns are key factors determining the formation of systematic and random errors during machining. Improving tool stability reduces wear rates, which contributes to maintaining machining accuracy parameters within tolerances for a long time and reduces equipment downtime associated with tool readjustment and resharpening. This paper examines a methodology for assessing the stability and wear resistance of P6M5 high-speed steel drills based on the theory of random functions. The use of linear random processes to describe cutting edge wear patterns is substantiated, which allows for a reduction in the amount of experimental data while maintaining the required prediction accuracy. The study employs a combination of statistical methods, including testing the homogeneity of the initial tool quality using Bartlett’s test and evaluating the significance of wear factors using ANOVA and Fisher’s criterion.. The study's results allowed for the establishment of tool life distribution parameters, which allows for a quantitative assessment of the process reliability and the substantiation of maximum permissible wear values ​​for improving the efficiency of machining.

title: Machine learning prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma informed by 3D-genome selected circRNAs
abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) remains a major contributor to cancer mortality, with poor prognosis driven by limited options for early detection and intervention. Circular RNAs (circRNAs), a class of non-coding RNAs with tissue-specific expression and regulatory functions, have emerged as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In this work, we investigate the predictive value of circRNAs in HCC using public datasets GSE155949 (49 HCC + 49 normal samples) and GSE121714 (20 HCC + 10 normal samples), and a suite of machine learning approaches, including logistic regression, support vector machines, Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and deep neural networks. To capture circRNA contributions from multiple perspectives, we construct six distinct feature panels, one of which incorporates their spatial distribution within the Three-Dimensional (3D) genome. Our results show that circRNAs selected according to 3D genome loci improves prediction accuracy and enhances generalization by mitigating feature collinearity in small-sample settings. These findings highlight the advantages of integrating 3D genome information into circRNA-based predictive modeling and offer a scalable framework for biomarker discovery and precision medicine in HCC.

title: Spatiotemporal crowd behavior modeling through adaptive whale optimized hybrid AI networks for campus length of stay prediction
A data-driven framework for encrustation prediction and risk-based inspection of urban sewer networks
abstract: Purpose Ageing urban sewer networks face increasing deterioration under population growth, climate variability and deferred maintenance. Encrustation is a prevalent, operationally burdensome defect that progressively reduces hydraulic capacity and demands repeated cleaning. This study develops a machine learning framework for binary encrustation risk classification using Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) inspection records (2007–2021) integrated with infrastructure, environmental and demographic data from Hong Kong's drainage network. Design/methodology/approach Ten candidate classifiers were evaluated under stratified 5-fold cross-validation, with performance assessed on a held-out test set. Calibration was compared across raw outputs, Platt scaling and isotonic regression, and SHAP analysis was applied to interpret feature contributions. A three-tier risk stratification framework (Low, Moderate and High) was constructed from the best-performing classifier's retained raw predicted probabilities. Findings Random Forest achieved the best test performance (AUC-ROC = 0.8728; F1-score = 0.6343), statistically indistinguishable from Extra Trees in paired bootstrap comparison. Raw Random Forest probabilities outperformed Platt scaling and isotonic regression. The three-tier risk framework yielded encrustation rates of 11.5%, 55.4% and 80.4% for Low-, Moderate- and High-risk tiers, wit…

title: Integrating MeSH semantics and knowledge graph topology for structure-agnostic drug-drug interaction prediction
abstract: Abstract Background Adverse drug–drug interactions (DDIs) cause preventable hospitalizations, but exhaustive experimental screening of all drug pairs is infeasible. Many computational predictors rely on small-molecule structural representations, limiting their direct applicability to biologic therapeutics. We present a structure-agnostic framework that combines semantic representations derived from Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) with graph-derived topology from a Drug–Target–Protein knowledge graph constructed from DrugBank and UniProt. We further examine how MeSH annotation depth is associated with predictive performance. Results In transductive evaluation, latent gated fusion achieved an overall AUROC of 0.988 and improved mean AUROC and F1 over MeSH-only across all six interaction categories. Improvements in AUROC, F1, and precision remained significant after Holm correction for Low-Mid, Mid-Mid, and Mid-Deep interactions, with the largest mean AUROC gain in Low-Mid (+0.0304). In seen–unseen inductive evaluation, each test pair contained one held-out drug and one seen drug, and all DDI edges were excluded from the feature graphs. Fusion achieved an overall AUROC of 0.937, exceeding MeSH-only by 0.045; this improvement remained significant after Holm correction. Mean AUROC gains occurred across all six categories, with recurring improvements in Low–Mid ( + 0.063) and Mid–Mid…

title: Machine learning based prediction of tensile strength properties of fused filament fabricated PA-CFRP composites
abstract: Purpose Fused filament fabrication (FFF) has gained substantial attention in additive manufacturing for making lightweight functional structural components. However, the mechanical performance of FFF-fabricated parts is heavily impacted by several interdependent processing parameters, making accurate prediction challenging. This study aims to establish a precise machine learning-based framework to forecast the tensile characteristics of polyamide–carbon fiber reinforced polymer composites made using the FFF technique. Design/methodology/approach A thorough experimental data set was developed by systematically adjusting key FFF processing parameters, including nozzle temperature, layer height, infill density, printing speed and infill pattern. Machine learning models, particularly random forest, Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and Light gradient boosting machine (GBM), were created to predict tensile strength, Young’s modulus and elongation at break. Model performance was evaluated using the coefficient of determination (R2), and feature importance analysis was conducted to determine the most relevant process parameters. Findings Among the examined models, XGBoost had the highest predictive accuracy, reaching R2 values of 0.998 for the training data set and 0.956 for the test data set. LightGBM displayed greater generalization ability for all three mechanical properties. The…

title: Improved EfficientNet Lingnan ancient village micro-space design style prediction model integrating multi-scale features
Applications of Explainable Machine Learning to Casualty Risk Prediction in Residential Building Fires: Current Status, Roles of Fire Protection Systems, and Future Directions
abstract: The conditions that lead to casualties in residential building fires are a combination of several factors: vulnerability of the occupants, fire origin and spread, response to fire alarms, fire-service response and the effectiveness of protection systems. In this paper, explainable machine learning for casualty and loss prediction, interpretation of predictions, and active fire protection are discussed. The mixed variables and nonlinear relationships of the incident records can be addressed by tree models and ensembles. Training data distribution may change with resampling, which may help determine minority casualty classes. Neural networks are able to learn and model spatio-temporal patterns, but require larger datasets and more rigorous external validation. Nor do feature importance, nor SHAP, give causality. Another study has also been linked to a reduction in the risk of deaths when smoke alarms are present. Occupants with limited mobility may be protected through automatic suppression such as detector activated systems that do not need an occupant's response. However, research is hampered by class imbalance, regional variation, limited information on the status of the system and reliance on counterfactual estimates. Issues that need attention are consistent casualty categories, consistent evaluation metrics, validation across regions, use of model explanations in fire-safet…

title: An accuracy prediction method based on Monte Carlo simulation for inertial integrated structure alignment measurement in confined spaces
abstract: Abstract Inertial integration is an effective method for alignment measurement in confined spaces. Due to factors such as the large volume of data and the complexity of the calculations, there is currently no effective quantitative accuracy prediction method for inertial integrated alignment measurement in confined spaces in advance. This paper proposes an accuracy prediction method for the inertial/odometer/control point integrated measurement method. This method is based on Monte Carlo simulation. It generates true sensor measurements according to the designed alignment and generates error values based on the sensor error model. After introducing the error values into the true measurements, the simulated trajectory is solved. By repeating this process and conducting statistical analysis, the prediction accuracy of the alignment can be obtained. The experimental results indicate that this method achieves a resolution accuracy of better than 5 ppm, with an average relative accuracy of over 80% in real-world scenarios, demonstrating good validity and practicality.

title: Student Performance Prediction Using Machine Learning
abstract: Predicting academic performance before final examinations can help educators direct support towards students who need it most. This paper presents a research framework for student performance prediction using machine learning, developed from a postgraduate research proposal. The framework combines academic indicators, including previous examination marks, internal assessments, attendance, assignments and study habits, to classify academic risk. It describes data preparation, a comparison of interpretable and ensemble classification methods, and an evaluation plan that emphasizes recall for at-risk students rather than accuracy alone. A teacher-facing reporting interface is proposed to convert predictions into actionable academic support. As model training and institutional validation have not yet been completed, this paper reports a proposed methodology and anticipated contributions, not measured performance.
authors: Singaldip Pranali Sanjay and Prof. S. J. Ghorpade
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

title: A Novel Framework for Permeability Prediction of 3D Digital Rock Based on Action Recognition Methods
RIMU-SpecMamba: replicate-aware state space modeling for robust cross-scanner soil spectral prediction
abstract: Introduction Portable near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy enables rapid, non-destructive soil analysis, but spectral variations across instruments limit cross-scanner generalization. Repeated measurements contain valuable information about within-scanner variability and between-scanner spectral differences. Methods We propose RIMU-SpecMamba, a replicate-aware framework combining Real Residual Spectrum Augmentation (RRSA), replicate-consistency supervision, source-scanner alignment, and multi-resolution bidirectional state-space modeling. The framework is evaluated under a strict leave-one-scanner-out protocol involving nine held-out scanners, three source-data splits, and three random seeds, without using target-scanner data during training. Results Across 81 evaluations, summarized as 27 seed-aggregated scanner–split units, RIMU-SpecMamba achieves a mean Macro-R² of 0.8703 (descriptive SD = 0.0538). This is 0.0477 higher than the best-performing Mamba-family baseline, VanillaMamba (0.8226), corresponding to an approximately 5.8% relative improvement. Performance ranges from 0.8092 to 0.9459 across the nine scanner means. Discussion The results demonstrate the potential of exploiting real repeated measurements to improve zero-shot cross-scanner soil-property prediction within the evaluated Neospectra portable FT-NIR ecosystem and WoodyWellKSSL data release. Transfer to other instr…

title: Calibrating Large Language Model Agents for Cross-Experiment Prediction Through Preference-Weighted Sampling
abstract: Using DeepSeek-v4-flash, this study replicates social-preference calibration in the single-stage allocation games examined by Horton and colleagues. The paper estimates sampling weights for three social-preference agent types by constrained least squares and randomly draws agents one by one according to those weights. The paper additionally estimates weights by binomial maximum likelihood using the original human choice counts, and compares the cross-experiment predictions of human choices in two-stage games produced by agents sampled under the two weighting methods. Relative to an unprompted sample, the constrained least-squares calibrated sample reduces prediction mean squared error (MSE) by 51.1% and lowers mean absolute error (MAE) to 0.142833. The binomial-likelihood sample reduces MSE by 51.2%, but its MAE rises to 0.160000, showing no consistent cross-experiment improvement. The error in Berk18 suggests that fixed-preference agents may fail to distinguish game outcomes with equal total payoffs. The results indicate that theory-based social-preference-weighted sampling improves cross-experiment prediction, whereas changing the weight-estimation method alone may be insufficient to resolve errors in agent-behavior prediction.

title: Mechanical and thermo-structural characterization of roselle–ramie–pineapple leaf fibre hybrid epoxy composites with machine learning-based tensile strength prediction
A framework for outpatient CAR-T monitoring to support Canadian CAR-T capacity building
abstract: Introduction: why outpatient CAR-T therapy now in Canada? Chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR-T) therapy has significantly improved outcomes, including sustained remissions and even cures, for patients with refractory or relapsed B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL), B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), and multiple myeloma (MM).1-8 CAR-T products differ by antigen target, such as CD19 and B cell maturation antigen (BCMA); and by co-stimulatory domain, which is either CD28 (e.g., axicabtagene ciloleucel, brexucabtagene autoleucel) or 4-1BB (e.g., tisagenlecleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, idecabtagene vicleucel). Prior to CAR-T availability, patients with relapsed hematologic malignancies experienced poor outcomes. For example, in patients with relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphomas, the median overall survival was 6.2 months. prior to access to CAR-T therapy.9 These outcomes are balanced by CAR-T therapy-associated toxicities, including cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS). Despite the substantial clinical benefits observed with CAR T-cell therapy, treatment is associated with distinct immune-mediated toxicities, including cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity (ICANs). Although these adverse events are generally manageable with established treatment algorithms an…

title: Coupling network reconstruction-driven charge transport transition: Capacity breakthrough and wide-temperature sodium storage in Na 3 VCr(PO 4 ) 3 cathodes
abstract: Abstract NASICON-type sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) cathode material Na3VCr(PO4)3 (NVCP) theoretically offers the advantage of high energy density. However, its practical capacity is severely restricted, rendering the theoretical potential unrealized. The root cause underlying this capacity limitation remains unclear to date, posing a fundamental obstacle to the material's practical application. Through the deep synergy of theoretical calculations and experiments, this study reveals that the electron state localization induced by insufficient V–Cr d–d orbital hybridization in NVCP is the core bottleneck constraining the intrinsic kinetics of charge transfer. To address this, we propose a "coupling network modulation" strategy, employing Mo6+ with a 4d0 empty orbital as a probe to implement precise intervention in the local bonding environment. The preferential occupation of Mo6+ at the Cr site efficiently reconstructs the Cr–O–V bonding topology and enhances V–Cr orbital overlap, boosting the bulk electronic conductivity by two orders of magnitude. Simultaneously, the strong covalent Mo–O bonds pin the lattice framework, significantly improving strain resistance and effectively suppressing structural degradation during long-term cycling. Consequently, the optimized Na2.91VCr0.97Mo0.03(PO4)3 delivers an initial specific capacity of 105.2 mAh·g−1, achieving a 21.1% gain in specific…

title: Improving fiscal capacity through digital public infrastructure: evidence from India's GST collection
abstract: Purpose The main purpose of the present study is to assess the impact of digital public infrastructure (DPI) on goods and services tax (GST) collection in 28 different states of India, including the policy shock of 2022 related to the termination of the GST compensation regime. Design/methodology/approach The study constructs a DPI index using principal component analysis based on the panel dataset covering the period 2017 to 2024 and estimates the relationship between DPI and GST using the Arellano–Bover/Blundell–Bond estimator to address endogeneity and dynamic effects. Panel quantile regression is applied to capture heterogeneous effects of DPI, economic activity, labor market conditions and exports on GST revenue. Findings An inverted U-shaped nonlinear relation between GST revenue and DPI expansion is observed in India with heterogeneous impact across different states. High-performing states in DPI ecosystem implementation benefit more in GST collection with diminishing gains beyond a certain threshold of DPI development. In contrast, digitally lagging states exhibit weaker GST responsiveness, indicating that DPI alone is insufficient without complementary institutional capacity and economic formalization. Thus, DPI acts as a catalyst that strengthens existing economic and administrative capacity, which in turn increases GST growth. Exports and financial credit significant…
venue: Journal of Economic and Administrative Sciences

title: Grid-forming SVG DC-side hybrid capacitor series topology and capacity design method
abstract: Introduction Grid-forming (GFM) static var generators (SVGs) require adequate DC-side energy storage to provide transient active-power support during grid-frequency disturbances. This study aims to reduce supercapacitor requirements while maintaining the transient support capability of GFM SVGs. Methods A series hybrid DC-side topology combining supercapacitors and electrolytic capacitors with a bidirectional partial-power DC/DC converter is proposed. An 800 V direct-connected all-supercapacitor system serves as the benchmark. An energy-equivalent synchronization method and a coordinated engineering sizing procedure are developed for realizable commercial-cell banks and the partial-power converter. Results Using identical 3.0 V/50 F cells, the benchmark and proposed systems require 297s1p and 75s1p supercapacitor banks, respectively. This represents a 74.75% reduction in supercapacitor cell count and the corresponding aggregate cell mass and geometrical volume relative to the specified benchmark. The selected DC/DC converter is rated at 2.114 kW, equivalent to 21.14% of the 10 kW SVG rating. Under the investigated consecutive disturbances with finite rates of change of frequency (RoCoF), the proposed system’s individual decline-stage peak support is approximately 1.52% lower than that of the benchmark. At the time of the benchmark system’s peak, the proposed system’s support is…

title: Synthesis and characterization of a CPVC-based anion exchange adsorbent with enhanced capacity via hexamethylenediamine modification
From threat to adaptation: the psychological mechanism of AI-related cognition and experience on law students’ career indecision—an empirical test based on a moderated parallel mediation model
abstract: Introduction Career indecision has become a major challenge to individuals’ vocational psychological adaptation amid technological transformation. Drawing on the cognitive appraisal theory of stress and career construction theory, this study investigates the psychological mechanisms underlying law students’ career indecision. Methods We developed and tested a moderated parallel mediation model using a sample of 1,128 students from Chinese law schools. Results The results show that the psychometric structure of the four-dimensional AI career anxiety scale is stable among Chinese law students. AI literacy/exposure experience, perceived AI substitution in the legal profession, and perceived limitations of AI legal services are the three factors that are significantly associated with career indecision. These associations are fully or partially mediated through parallel pathways involving four types of career anxiety, among which socio-technical blind-spot anxiety exhibits a particularly prominent mediating effect (with the total indirect effect accounting for 65.4% of the total effect in the “perceived limitations of AI legal services → career indecision” pathway). This finding highlights the special role that macro-level risks, such as those involving algorithmic ethics, play in the psychology of the legal profession. The results showed that there was a direct positive relationshi…

title: Nanocopper Oxide Exacerbates Lead-Induced Impairment of Renal Repair Mechanism via Renal Clock Gene Dysregulation-Oxidative Stress Crosstalk, and a Mechanism-Guided Intervention Strategy Using Liposome-Encapsulated Curcumin
abstract: Abstract Nanocopper oxide (nano-CuO) is widely used in agriculture, while lead (Pb) persists as a soil and crop contaminant, raising concerns about combined exposure. However, their combined nephrotoxicity and mechanism-guided interventions have remained unexplored. Here, we show that nano-CuO aggravates the Pb-damaged renal repair mechanism via clock gene dysregulation-oxidative stress crosstalk, with arachidonic acid (AA) as a potential metabolic hub. Using mouse models and HK-2 cells, coexposure disrupted core circadian genes, exacerbated oxidative stress, and suppressed Wnt signal-involved renal repair mechanism, causing cell cycle arrest. Rescue experiments indicated a crosstalk between clock dysregulation and oxidative stress. We constructed liposome-encapsulated curcumin (Lipo-Cur), which normalized circadian genes, quenched oxidative damage, replenished AA, reactivated Wnt signaling, and reversed kidney injury in vitro and in vivo. This study unveils a clock gene/oxidative stress-repair mechanism axis underlying nano-CuO and Pb coexposure toxicity and highlights Lipo-Cur as a mechanism-guided intervention strategy.
venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

title: Unveiling the H2S Sensing Mechanism of CeO2/Bi2S3 Heterostructure Sensors Under High-Vacuum Conditions
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) detection under low-pressure and oxygen-deficient conditions is important for space-relevant gas analysis, yet semiconductor sensing mechanisms under vacuum remain poorly understood. Here, we report a CeO2/Bi2S3 heterostructure sensor exhibiting two-stage H2S sensing at a baseline pressure of 10–3 Pa. Initially, strong adsorption at active Bi2S3 sites produces a response of 17.03 to 0.1 Pa H2S. Repeated exposure–evacuation cycles induce surface self-conditioning, establishing a stable reversible stage consistent with weaker adsorption and enabling selective H2S detection at partial pressures as low as 0.002 Pa. Experimental analysis and density functional theory calculations support Bi2S3 as the primary adsorption and charge-transfer platform, while the interfacial internal electric field (IEF) and Ce3+/Ce4+ redox couple facilitate charge transport. This work clarifies the surface kinetic evolution of H2S sensing under vacuum and provides a material design strategy for reliable gas sensors used in future deep-space exploration.

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals the rules of component transformation and the mechanism of quality formation of Phyllanthi Fructus during natural sun-drying process
abstract: Abstract Natural sun-drying facilitates quality formation of Phyllanthi Fructus (PF) via enhanced accumulation of bioactive constituents. Nevertheless, its underlying molecular regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood, which impedes standardized quality control for this medicinal herb. In this study, transcriptomic and metabolomic approaches were integrated to systematically investigate time-course alterations in gene expression and metabolite abundance throughout an 11-day natural sun-drying process. Microstructural observations demonstrated that PF fruit cells retained intact morphological structures during the first four drying days, suggesting potential stress-triggered physiological responses. Key bioactive compounds such as gallic acid, chebulagic acid, ellagic acid and punicalagin gradually accumulated and peaked on day 8 of sun-drying. Transcriptome analysis identified 2,515 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with 1,261 up-regulated and 1,254 down-regulated transcripts. Functional enrichment showed these DEGs were principally enriched in three secondary-metabolism-related pathways: Phenylpropanoid biosynthesis (53 DEGs), flavone and flavonol biosynthesis (8 DEGs), and terpenoid backbone biosynthesis (23 DEGs). Metabolomics further annotated 58 differential metabolites largely involved in unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, …

title: Quantitative assessment of sheath blight on rice stems based on lightweight hierarchical segmentation head and soft gating mechanism
abstract: Introduction Accurate quantitative assessment of rice sheath blight is critical for disease monitoring and precise crop management. However, accurate quantification remains challenging because lesions are often small and subtle, with ambiguous boundaries against healthy stem tissue, and background interference may introduce false positives. To address these issues, this study aims to develop a lightweight segmentation framework for stem-focused sheath blight quantification. Methods A custom rice‑stem sheath‑blight image dataset was constructed. We proposed HSG-SegFormer, which integrates a hierarchical segmentation head and soft gating mechanism upon SegFormer-b0 backbone. Variety-grouped five-fold cross-validation was adopted to compare segmentation performance and lesion-severity quantification against manual reference annotations. Results HSG-SegFormer increased mIoU from 86.37% to 87.79% and lesion IoU from 77.81% to 80.36%. It obtained consistent improvements across small-, medium- and large-lesion groups and notably suppressed background false-positive activations. Compared with manual severity references, it yielded a higher coefficient of determination (R2=0.955) and lower prediction error, with only minor growth in model parameters and computational cost. Discussion The hierarchical head and soft-gating design enhance fine-grained lesion discrimination while preserving…

Influence Mechanism of Primary Fractures on Rock Breakage by Blasting in Deep Rock Masses: Experiments and Simulations
Removal performance and mechanism of incredibly low carbon/nitrogen ratio wastewater via anammox-enhanced anoxic/oxic/oxic/anoxic process under different temperatures
abstract: Temperature visibly affects microbial community structure and activity in bioreactors, thereby affecting the removal of pollutants; therefore, the adaptability to temperature is a crucial indicator for evaluating the application prospects of a new process. In this study, a lab-scale anammox-enhanced anoxic/oxic/oxic/anoxic process was developed to treat wastewater severely deficient in carbon sources under different test water temperatures (TWTs), whose C/N (COD/total nitrogen (TN)) ratio was only 1.66–1.70. The effluent TN, total phosphorus, and COD could still meet the specific discharge standards as TWT decreased (25 ± 1 °C to 15 ± 1 °C), and their removal rates slightly decreased from 97.77 ± 0.076%, 94.23 ± 2.72% and 96.43 ± 0.36% to 92.14 ± 0.13%, 93.73 ± 0.40% and 95.13 ± 0.078%, respectively, indicating a high adaptability to TWTs. Hydrolyzed microorganisms and refractory organic matter (ROM) provided a carbon source for denitrification, resulting in efficient COD removal and an incredibly low sludge yield coefficient (0.025–0.027 kg MLSS/kg COD) under different TWTs. Multiple N removal pathways were achieved in the bioreactor, including partial nitrification–denitrification, partial nitrification–anammox, and partial denitrification–anammox, which remarkably improved the N removal efficiency and adaptability under different TWTs. Phosphorus was removed via precipitatio…

title: Research on AI Driven Investor Sentiment Recognition Mechanism and Dynamic Impact on Asset Pricing Bias
abstract: In tandem with the rise of platform-based financial communication, investor sentiment is now measurable as a behavioral factor affecting the behavior of equity markets. In social media messages and corporate news, there is information dispersion regarding investors' expectation of firm value, risk events, and policy uncertainty, whereas machine learning offers computable methods to capture the signals from text data. On the basis of 486,217 messages by investors, 18,604 announcements of listed companies, and 412,380 firm-level daily trading records in the years between 2021 and 2025, an investor sentiment recognition approach based on artificial intelligence is designed in order to detect sentiment polarity, strength, and uncertainty. FinBERT-Transformer fusion model exhibits optimal classification results with accuracy of 0.887±0.011, macro-F1 of 0.872±0.014, and AUC of 0.931±0.009. Through dynamic panel regression, it was found that one-standard deviation increase in positive sentiment leads to overpricing at day one by 12.6±2.1 basis points, while negative sentiment increases underpricing by 16.8±2.4 basis points. These effects diminish after five trading days and reverse somewhat at day ten in the two groups of size and liquidity. The results suggest that AI recognition of investor sentiment helps interpret asset pricing bias in terms of expectation adjustment, attention co…

title: THE THREE-DIMENSIONAL GENERATION MECHANISM OF DIGITAL TEXTBOOKS FOR VOCATIONAL EDUCATION FROM THE PERSPECTIVE OF EMBODIED COGNITION
abstract: The building of digital textbooks for vocational education focuses on the technical presentation currently, while limited attention is paid to bodily engagement in skill acquisition. Based on embodied cognition theory, this paper treats the digital textbooks as an environment that provides perception and interaction, and this paper proposes a three-dimensional generation mechanism: perceptual situation, cognitive transformation, and motivational regulation. Perceptual situation focuses on whether the environment can respond to the learner immediately and forms a cycle of exploration and feedback; cognitive transformation promotes situated ability through safe trial and error and self-reflection, while motivational regulation offers suggestions according to the learner’s state and allows the learner to make decisions. The three-dimensional mechanisms interact with each other, forming the cycle of perception → cognition → motivation → perception. This paper also takes safety wiring as an example and demonstrates how the three-dimensional mechanism works, offering a theoretical basis for the transformation of digital textbooks into cognitive ecosystems.

Supramolecularly Assembled Conjugated Polymer for High-Capacity, Fast, and Durable Potassium Storage
abstract: Abstract Potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) are considered promising candidates for large-scale energy storage owing to the abundance and low cost of potassium resources. Organic anodes, with their flexible molecular frameworks and abundant redox-active sites, are well suited for the reversible storage of relatively large K+. However, achieving high capacity, fast charge transfer, and long-term stability simultaneously remains challenging. Here, we report a supramolecularly assembled crystalline conjugated polymer, poly(tetraaminobenzoquinone) (pTABQ), as an anode material for PIBs. By incorporating abundant carbonyl sites into an extended C–N conjugated framework and forming an ordered layered supramolecular structure through in-plane hydrogen bonding and out-of-plane π–π stacking, pTABQ undergoes charge redistribution within the framework and local rearrangement of the stacking structure during potassiation, enabling high capacity, fast charge transfer, and long-term cycling stability. Benefiting from the synergy between its structural and electronic properties, pTABQ delivers a high reversible capacity of 460 mAh g–1 at 100 mA g–1 and an ultralong cycle life of more than 8600 cycles at 2000 mA g–1. Furthermore, a pTABQ//KMnF full cell achieves a high energy density of 284 Wh kg–1. This work provides a design strategy for high-performance organic materials for electrochemical ene…

title: Synthesis of CuO/SiC composite with tailored microstructure for rapid cefaclor adsorption: Performance mechanism insight
abstract: Abstract To address the dual challenges of resource waste from decommissioned photovoltaic panels and antibiotic contamination in aquatic environments, this study developed a facile waste-to-resource strategy to convert retired photovoltaic silicon into a high-performance adsorbent. A CuO/SiC composite was synthesized via facile mechanical ball milling using SiC derived from retired photovoltaic silicon and commercial CuO. The composite was designed for efficient cefaclor (CEC) removal and characterized by XRD, XPS, SEM/TEM, BET, Zeta potential analysis and FTIR spectroscopy. The effects of CuO mass fraction, solution pH, and pollutant type systematically evaluated, along with reusability and adsorption mechanism. The 25% CuO/SiC composite exhibited optimal adsorption performance, achieving 98.83% removal of CEC (5 mg/L) within 10 minutes and retaining 99.34% efficiency after five adsorption-desorption cycles, with the highest removal at pH 6. Adsorption isotherms followed the Langmuir model, indicating monolayer adsorption on homogeneous sites, while kinetic fitted pseudo-first-order and pseudo-second-order models, suggesting coexistence of physical and chemical adsorption. The adsorption mechanism was primarily attributed to the synergistic effects of oxygen vacancy-induced active sites, electrostatic interactions, and hydrogen bonding between the composite and CEC molecules,…

title: Pattern dynamics in a vegetation-water model with nonlocal delay and finite soil carrying capacity
abstract: In arid ecosystems, limited water constrains not only vegetation biomass but also its spatial organization, yet it remains unclear how root-mediated water redistribution, delayed plant response, and finite soil resource limits jointly drive vegetation pattern transitions. To solve this problem, we develop a vegetation-water model incorporating cross-diffusion, nonlocal delay, and finite soil carrying capacity. Linear stability analysis identifies Turing instability conditions, and weakly nonlinear analysis yields amplitude equations that analytically determine the stability boundaries among uniform, stripe, and spot states. Our results reveal the distinct roles of three coupled mechanisms. Cross-diffusion is the primary driver of spatial heterogeneity and drives phase transitions from cold spots to stripes and then to isolated hot spots as feedback strength increases. Nonlocal delay shifts the Turing threshold and modulates the bifurcation boundary while exerting limited influence on the final selected pattern. Declining soil carrying capacity acts as a strict physical constraint that promotes cold spot patterns while substantially reducing overall vegetation density. These findings clarify how spatio-temporal feedbacks and soil limitations reshape dryland landscapes and suggest pattern-type transitions alongside declining density as potential early-warning indicators of desert…

title: Optimal Dietary Docosahexaenoic Acid Levels for Growth Performance, Innate Immune Function, Antioxidant Capacity and Gene Expression in Juvenile Small Yellow Croaker (Larimichthys polyactis)
Full integrity as a mediating mechanism associated with police officers’ reported misconduct orientation in the Indonesian National Police
abstract: This study tests whether full integrity mediates the effects of organizational culture, ethical leadership, and the reward system on Zero Oknum, the Indonesian National Police (POLRI) objective of eliminating deviant officer behavior. The term “oknum” denotes a rogue member of an institution. Survey data from 275 officers across ranks and divisions were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM): the measurement model satisfied reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity criteria. Structural and mediation effects were estimated by bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples. Full integrity fully accounted for the culture–Zero Oknum association and partially accounted for the reward-system association. Ethical leadership showed a strong direct association with Zero Oknum. The model explained 82.3% of the variance in Zero Oknum (R² = 0.823) and showed in-sample predictive relevance (Q² = 0.606). The findings extend Huberts’ full integrity framework to a hierarchical police organization in a developing democracy and indicate that reported misconduct orientation is associated with aligned culture, leadership, and incentives, not with structural reform alone.

title: Single/Double Degree-of-Freedom Switching Mechanism and Performance Verification of a Reconfigurable Quadruped Wheeled Robot
abstract: In this paper, a quadrupedal wheeled robot with reconfigurable single- and double-degree-of-freedom (DOF) modes is proposed, which is accomplished by knee joint folding and the use of mechanical limiters, without requiring any additional locking components. The lower leg is folded against a mechanical stop and a holding torque is applied to restrict the leg to a single degree of freedom for flat ground wheeling, while the stop is released to allow the leg to move with two degrees of freedom in the hip and knee for legged obstacle traversal. Kinematic and finite element models are created, and MuJoCo simulations are performed using a unified robot description format (URDF) model, which uses reinforcement learning to generate walking gaits. The double-DOF mode increases the maximum foot span by 24% (to 0.411 m) and provides 41% more clearance in the vertical direction, and the workspace changes from a one-dimensional arc to a two-dimensional (2D) area. The chassis, joint output shafts and limiters are not stressed beyond their material yield strengths with rated payloads of 20 kg and safety factors of 2.7–4.0. The robot was able to complete the five 20 s trials without falling, making a journey of approximately 1.94 m with an average speed of 0.098 m/s, and peak joint torques that were within the 25 N·m limit. These results confirm the kinematic and simulation feasibility of the …

title: Chemical Profiling and Potential Anti‐Inflammatory Mechanism of Gentiana scabra Bunge by UPLC‐Q/TOF MS/MS and Network Pharmacology
abstract: ABSTRACT Rationale As a commonly used Tibetan medicine, Gentiana scabra Bunge (GSB) is generally used to clear heat, detoxify the body, and soothe the throat and is indicated for epidemic febrile diseases, cough, laryngitis, pharyngitis, and other symptoms. However, its chemical profiling and mechanism in treating inflammation were not conducted, restricting its clinical applications. This work aimed to reveal the chemical profile and explore the anti‐inflammatory mechanism of GSB. Methods UPLC‐Q/TOF MS/MS was employed to analyze the chemical constituents in GSB. Network pharmacology was used to predict its anti‐inflammatory mechanism. The anti‐inflammatory activity of GSB was further evaluated in LPS‐stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages by MTT, NO, and Western blot assays. Results UPLC‐Q/TOF MS/MS identified 99 chemical constituents in GSB, mainly 40 iridoids, 36 flavonoids, 11 organic acids, 2 lignans, 5 alkaloids, 3 xanthones, and 2 others, including one potential novel compound and five compounds reported in GSB for the first time. Network pharmacology analysis revealed 355 inflammation‐related targets of GSB, with AKT1, TP53, TNF, IL‐2, and MAPK as core anti‐inflammatory targets, mainly involving the PI3K/Akt, TNF, IL‐17, and MAPK signaling pathways. At the cellular level, GSB (0.5–4 mg mL −1 ) showed no obvious cytotoxicity and significantly inhibited LPS‐induced NO production…

title: The Role of Shame in Leader Identity, Capacity, and Efficacy Development Among College Students
abstract: ABSTRACT While the field of leadership development has disproportionately emphasized positive leadership experiences, negative experiences and emotions consequentially shape leadership trajectories. Shame, an identity‐embedded emotion characterized as a negative evaluation of oneself as flawed or “less than,” hinders psychosocial wellbeing and meaning‐making capacity. Leadership development relies upon individuals’ socialization and enhanced meaning‐making structures; yet scant scholarship has intersected shame and leadership development, particularly among college students, which threatens to undermine meaning‐making capacity and leadership development. Therefore, the current empirical paper applies shame to three facets of leadership development: Leader identity, capacity, and efficacy. Ultimately, we propose a conceptual model that frames leadership development as a non‐linear, emotionally contingent cycle shaped by the resolution of shame through meaning making and support networks.

title: Recent Progress in the Structural Design of Silicon/Carbon Composite Anodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Silicon is considered to be a promising anode material for the next generation of lithium-ion batteries due to its high theoretical specific capacity. However, it will produce significant volume changes during the lithium insertion and delithiation processes, which further cause problems such as particle cracking, repeated rupture and formation of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), and loss of electrical contact. Silicon/carbon (Si/C) composite materials provide an effective way to alleviate the above problems by combining the high capacity of silicon with the good electrical conductivity, mechanical support capability and interface stabilisation of carbon materials. This article reviews the structural design of Si/C composite anodes, focusing on three typical structures (carbon-coated, embedded and hollow/porous), and compares their roles and limitations in interface protection, electron transmission, mechanical buffering and volume expansion control. Further analysis revealed that there are trade-offs between different structures in terms of performance, energy density, preparation complexity and scaled application. The future development of Si/C anodes requires further optimisation of the Si/C ratio, interface bonding, pore structure and multiscale structural design, while taking into account high performance, low cost and scalable manufacturing.

Emotional framing and visual image in carbon pricing persuasion: the mediating role of message elaboration
abstract: Purpose Drawing on the emotions-as-frames model (EFM), this study aims to examine the interaction between emotional framing and visual imagery in carbon pricing persuasion, focusing on the mediating role of message elaboration. Design/methodology/approach This study used a 2 × 2 between-subjects experimental design (emotion: hope vs fear; visual image: present vs absent) with a sample of 300 participants. Data were analyzed using analysis of variance (ANOVA) and analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) to test for main and interaction effects while controlling for climate change knowledge. The PROCESS macro was used to test for mediation. Findings The results indicated that fear framing was more persuasive than hope framing for behavioral intentions. The presence of a visual image in a fear-framed message showed a significant main effect on attitudes toward the climate change message. Furthermore, significant interaction was found between hope-framed messaging and visual imagery for attitudes toward the climate change message. Message elaboration, through evaluative processing, mediated the relationship between the emotional frames and the outcome variables. These effects remained robust after controlling for climate change knowledge. Practical implications This study offers important contributions and provides a messaging framework for policy practitioners and communication specialists…
