title: Size-Regulated Cobalt Nanoparticles in Nitrogen-Doped Carbon for Heterogeneous Markovnikov Hydroazidation of Alkenes
abstract: Abstract The development of efficient, recyclable, and structurally tunable catalysts is crucial for sustainable alkene functionalization. Herein, we report a nanoparticle size-engineering strategy for constructing metal−organic framework (MOF)-derived cobalt catalysts for the Markovnikov hydroazidation of alkenes. By modulating the Co/Zn ratio in bimetallic MOF precursors, the apparent particle size of cobalt nanoparticles (Co NPs) can be precisely controlled during pyrolysis. Among the prepared catalysts, Co1Zn4−NC exhibited the best catalytic performance, which is attributed to the synergistic effect of smaller apparent particle size, higher dispersion, and stronger metal−support interactions. Under mild conditions, Co1Zn4−NC enabled the hydroazidation of a broad range of aryl alkenes with good functional group tolerance. Mechanistic investigations indicate that a Co−H species, likely generated from the interaction between the cobalt site and silane, acts as a key intermediate in the hydrogen atom transfer step. Radical trapping experiments further support the involvement of radical intermediates in the catalytic process. Importantly, Co1Zn4−NC could be reused for at least five cycles with high catalytic activity and structural stability, and the system is readily scalable to the gram scale. This work not only provides a sustainable heterogeneous catalytic system for synthes…

title: Effects of stand types on soil active organic carbon pool and driving factors in the dry-hot valley region of Sichuan Province, China
abstract: Active organic carbon, as the core driver of soil nutrient cycling, is vital for enhancing soil carbon sequestration by directly participating in soil biochemical processes and transforming into stable organic carbon. Increasing soil carbon storage (SCS) promotes forest growth and ecosystem health by enhancing soil fer tility, water-holding capacity, and nutrients. To clarify the specific effects of different stand types on the soil active organic carbon pool in the dry-hot valley region, this study examined three typical forests: Pinus yunnanensis pure forest (YC), Pinus yunnanensis–Alnus cremastogyne mixed forest (YQ), and Camellia sinensis–Alnus cremastogyne mixed forest (CQ). We analyzed the soil active organic carbon pool, SCS and physicochemical properties at 0–20 cm depth and used redundancy analysis to identify key driving factors. Results showed that active organic carbon content and SCS decreased with soil depth across all stands, with the order CQ > YQ > YC, and significant differences were observed among stands and layers ( p < 0.05). Soil organic carbon (SOC) and SCS was highest in the CQ, with significant differences between the 0–10 cm and 10–20 cm layers ( p < 0.05). Easily oxidizable organic carbon and dissolved organic carbon also varied significantly among stands ( p < 0.05), with differences diminishing with depth, while light fraction organic carbon and mic…

title: Evaluating the role of embodied carbon transfer and its network in achieving carbon neutrality: insights from Chinese provinces
abstract: Abstract Background Against the backdrop of global climate change and carbon neutrality goals, clarifying the patterns and driving mechanisms of interregional embodied carbon transfer (ECT) is crucial for defining emission reduction responsibilities. However, existing assessments of provincial carbon neutrality levels (CNLs) often rely solely on production-side accounting, overlooking the implications of interprovincial trade. This study aims to assess the asymmetric effects of ECT on provincial CNLs and to provide insights for equitable carbon responsibility allocation and carbon balance management. Results Using multi-regional input–output (MRIO) tables for 30 Chinese provinces from 2012 to 2020, this study measures the scale and direction of interprovincial ECT, identifies its drivers via structural decomposition analysis, and characterizes the network using social network analysis. To evaluate carbon neutrality effects, we construct three indicators: net embodied carbon transfer (NECT), carbon transfer intensity (CTI), and carbon imbalance degree (CID). The results indicate that China’s interprovincial ECTs continued to expand, exhibiting a stable pattern of “eastern outflow and central-western absorption.” The scale effect remained the primary driver of ECT growth, while the technology effect shifted toward emission reduction. The ECT network became increasingly interconne…

title: Primary sources and secondary formation of brown carbon in urban Shanghai: insights from bihourly measurements of brown carbon and organic tracers
abstract: Brown carbon (BrC) is a significant component of atmospheric carbonaceous aerosols and has important influence on climate, atmospheric chemistry, and air quality. Our knowledge about its sources and atmospheric evolution is limited due to the challenges of accurate estimation of its mass concentrations. To address this gap, we examined concurrent measurements of bihourly BrC and a suite of organic molecular and elemental tracers in urban Shanghai from March to August 2020. BrC was determined by synergistically applying the Bayesian inference (BI) model to multi-wavelength aethalometer and total carbon (TC) measurements. BrC constituted 38 %–40 % of TC, with pronounced seasonal differences in diurnal evolution. The source apportionment analysis resolved 15 source factors and among them 7 were secondary sources, namely, secondary nitrate and sulfate formation processes, aromatic secondary organic aerosol (SOA), α -pinene SOA, β -caryophyllene SOA, isoprene SOA, oxygenated cooking OA, and secondary biomass burning. Secondary BrC accounted for 42 % and 49 % of total BrC in spring and summer, respectively. Seasonal contrast of the BrC contributions from primary and secondary sources were noticed. The formation mechanisms of secondary BrC were investigated by isolating events with continuous increment in secondary BrC concentrations, and the analysis suggested the diversity of oxidat…

title: Flood invasion evolution and sustainability‑oriented risk assessment of metro-led underground spaces under extreme rainfall scenarios
abstract: Abstract Climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall, posing growing flood intrusion risks to urban underground spaces and challenging the resilience and flood protection performance of existing metro station designs, which is critical for sustainable transportation infrastructure development. Taking Changban Metro Station in Guangzhou, China, as a case study, this study combined a coupled 1D–2D surface flood model with a 3D numerical model of flood propagation inside the station to investigate flood intrusion under rainfall events with different return periods. The spatiotemporal characteristics of flood propagation, including flow paths, arrival time, inundation depth, discharge, and velocity, were analyzed to assess the flood risk of the existing station design under intensifying rainfall conditions. Results show that both peak inflow and intrusion duration increase markedly with rainfall return period. Under the 100‑year rainfall scenario, peak inflow is 35 times that under the 5‑year scenario, while intrusion duration is 3.4 times longer. Flood propagation exhibits clear vertical and horizontal patterns, with faster spread on upper levels and in near‑field areas, and slower spread on lower levels and in far‑field areas. The platform level is identified as the most vulnerable zone and may experience substantial inundation even under low‑retu…

title: Effect of Cycling Protocol on the Stress and Mechanical Degradation of Hard Carbon Electrodes
abstract: Maximum stress experienced by an electrode during cycling is shown to cause mechanical degradation and capacity fade, but the effect of potential window and stress range (Δ σ ) on cycling behavior was not investigated. Here, stresses generated in hard carbon (HC)-based porous composite electrodes were measured in situ while cycling under three different potential windows: (i) full window (2–0.0005 V vs Na/Na + ), (ii) sloping (2–0.1 V vs Na/Na + ), and plateau (0.1–0.0005 V vs Na/Na + ) regions and three different C-rates. The stress range (Δ σ ), capacity, and mechanical hysteresis during sloping region were nearly rate-independent, while they showed significant rate dependence in the plateau region, suggesting two different ion-storage mechanisms. Both the stress range and mechanical hysteresis (indicator of irreversible deformation) increased at lower current densities during the plateau region, indicating higher irreversible mechanical work and degradation. During extended cycling, capacity continued to decrease even after the maximum stress saturated, indicating that Δ σ and hysteresis are important to explain electrode degradation. Based on these observations, an optimized cycling protocol was used which reduced stress range and mechanical hysteresis while increasing specific capacity at faster rate, demonstrating the importance of coupled electro-chemomechanical response…

title: Coordination‐Driven Spiral Self‐Assembly of Helical Mesoporous Polymer Nanospheres and Derived MoS 2 /Carbon Colloidal Nanospheres for Fast Lithium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Helical mesoporous architectures are attractive for electrochemical energy storage because their curved channels and spiral surfaces facilitate ion transport and interfacial charge transfer. However, their synthesis has traditionally relied on chiral templates or complex assembly procedures, limiting structural tunability and compositional flexibility. Herein, we develop a coordination‐driven spiral self‐assembly (CSS) strategy that converts achiral building blocks into helical mesoporous polymer nanospheres (HMPSs) with continuous spiral surface textures and internal helical mesopores. Interfacial Mo–S coordination drives micellar spiral organization without chiral additives, enabling systematic regulation of pore size, morphology, and composition. Subsequent carbonization transforms HMPSs into helical mesoporous MoS 2 /C nanospheres (HMMoS 2 /C) containing uniformly dispersed monolayer MoS 2 while retaining the helical mesostructure. Finite‐element simulations and density functional theory calculations reveal that the helical mesoporous architecture facilitates rapid Li + diffusion, local ion enrichment, and interfacial charge transfer, thereby improving Li‐storage kinetics. Consequently, HMMoS 2 /C delivers a reversible capacity of 1776.3 mAh g − 1 at 0.3 A g − 1 after 150 cycles, a high‐rate capacity of 752.7 mAh g − 1 at 10 A g − 1 , and outstanding long‐term cycl…

title: Dynamic Reconstruction of Ruthenium Carbides Into Carbon‐Encapsulated Ruthenium for Active and Durable Hydrogen Evolution in Acids
abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a self‐protective catalyst design strategy based on the electrochemical phase transition of ruthenium carbide (RuC), demonstrating that a catalyst possessing both protective functionality and catalytic activity can be formed in situ during a reaction. Under reductive conditions, RuC undergoes a dynamic reconstruction process wherein carbon atoms within the carbide lattice migrate to the surface, resulting in the formation of a Ru@C core–shell structure. Comprehensive spectroscopic analyses, including high‐resolution photoemission spectroscopy, hard X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and X‐ray absorption spectroscopy, validate the migration of carbon and the formation of the encapsulation layer. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the newly formed carbon shell serves as an active interface by inducing interfacial electron transfer from the Ru core to the carbon overlayer, thereby optimizing the binding energies of reaction intermediates. Consequently, the Ru@C catalyst achieves excellent hydrogen evolution reaction activity in acidic media comparable to that of commercial Pt/C. Furthermore, despite being operated for 600 h under a high current density of 1.0 A cm −2 and high temperature of 80°C that simulate a practical PEMWE system environment, the system demonstrated remarkable durability, exhibiting a negligible voltage degradation r…

title: Training future sustainable culinary professionals through game-based learning: development and preliminary evaluation of a carbon-reducing culinary board game
abstract: Introduction This study aimed to develop an educational board game that integrates carbon-reducing culinary competence and to evaluate its content validity and students’ self-reported player experiences in foodservice education. Methods Using the ADDIE instructional design model, we translated competency indicators across three dimensions (knowledge, attitudes, and skills) into game mechanics for Carbon-Reducing Culinary Helper. Experts in sustainable foodservice education, culinary instruction, board game design, and industry practice reviewed the game’s content. During playtesting, 82 undergraduate students in hospitality and culinary-related programs completed the Player Experience Inventory (PXI). PXI scores were compared between students with and without prior knowledge of sustainability. Results Item-level content validity indices ranged from 0.80 to 1.00, indicating satisfactory content validity. The ten PXI dimensions showed high internal consistency, with Cronbach’s alpha values ranging from 0.893 to 0.960. Students generally reported positive player experiences. No statistically significant differences in player experience were found between students with and without prior knowledge of sustainability. Discussion The expert ratings and positive player experiences support the game’s potential as a supplementary tool for foodservice education, education on sustainable fo…

title: Lone-Pair Stereochemical Expression and Its Relationship to Electron–Phonon Coupling and Excited-State Relaxation in Sb(III)-Based Hybrid Metal Halides
abstract: Abstract Metal halide scintillators with efficient emission and tunable thermal response are highly desirable for sensitive X-ray detection. Herein, three zero-dimensional (0D) Sb3+-based organic–inorganic hybrid metal halides, (ttp)2SbCl5 (Sb-1), (tottp)2Sb2Cl8 (Sb-2), and (tompp)2SbCl5 (Sb-3), were synthesized by modulating the steric environment of corresponding organic cations. The different stereochemical expressions of the Sb3+ 5s2 lone pair, with active lone pairs in Sb-1 and Sb-3 and a more localized lone-pair electron density in the dimeric Sb-2, contribute to their different radioluminescence (RL) properties. These compounds exhibit intense red–orange RL associated with Sb3+-related self-trapped excitons (STEs). Temperature-dependent photoluminescence (TDPL) measurements have revealed unconventional thermal responses, where Sb-1 exhibits kind of typical monotonic thermal quenching, whereas Sb-2 and Sb-3 display nonmonotonic temperature dependence, characterized by an enhancement at intermediate temperatures. Analysis of TDPL results have demonstrated that these anomalous responses possibly arise from the competition between thermally activated carrier detrapping and nonradiative relaxation. Electronic band structure calculations and in situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) results have further revealed the involvement of Sb–Cl electronic states and photoinduced …

title: Recognition–Transduction Coupling in Noble-Metal-Modified WO3 for Selective BTEX Sensing
abstract: Abstract Noble-metal decoration is widely used to enhance gas sensing, yet how modifier identity governs BTEX sensing remains insufficiently understood. Molecular recognition and signal transduction functions are usually modified simultaneously, obscuring their respective contributions to sensing response and selectivity. Here, WO3 nanofibers modified with Au, Pt, or Pd are used to examine how noble-metal identity modulates the coupled receptor and transducer functions across structurally similar BTEX analytes. Au-WO3 combines strong molecular interactions with substantial barrier modulation, enabling efficient conversion of molecular recognition into resistance changes. It enhances all four BTEX responses with calculated lower limit of detection of 15 to 97 ppb. Ethylbenzene adsorption on Au transfers 0.18 e and shifts the Au 5d band center downward by 0.70 eV, therefore Au-WO3 achieves pronounced response of 15.68 to 5 ppm ethylbenzene. Pd-WO3 receives 0.13 to 0.16 e from toluene and p-xylene but modulates the energy barrier by only 0.06 eV, so even strongly adsorbed p-xylene does not yield a correspondingly large response. However, Pt-WO3 shows the opposite imbalance, with the largest energy barrier modulation of 0.50 eV but charge transfer below 0.10 e from every analyte. Therefore, it responds weakly to all BTEX analytes in general. Meanwhile, fingerprints from the sensors…

Experimental and Numerical Studies of the Ratcheting/Creep Coupling Effect on the Behavior of 304L Austenitic Stainless Steel
abstract: This work examines the effects of the ratcheting/creep coupling phenomenon on the behavior of 304L austenitic stainless steel. In this situation, the performed tests are carried out considering different stress amplitudes and the same mean stresses in a circular path under axial-torsional stress control. This cyclic loading was preceded by inelastic pre-straining in which the maximum stress of the first cycle is kept constant for a given period, during this time creep may develop. In subsequent classical ratcheting cycles, they do not involve any hold time. Firstly, the obtained results indicate that, at room temperature, the nonlinear behavior of the 304L austenitic stainless steel is substantially rate-dependent. Additionally, no noticeable cyclic accumulation of plastic strain was detected after the creep phase completion, suggesting that creep is primarily responsible for the majority of the cyclic accumulation of inelastic strain observed in conventional ratcheting tests. The Multi-Mechanism model simulation of the ratcheting/creep coupling phenomenon exhibits a satisfactory qualitative concordance with the experimental data. However, the Multi-Mechanism model is less robust from a quantitative point of view in the simulation of the experimental strain evolutions. To enhance the prediction capabilities of the stress and/or strain levels response, further study is required,…

title: Sex-specific serum phosphate–parathyroid hormone coupling across a Qinghai clinical cohort and U.S. NHANES: dietary sensitivity and genetic triangulation
abstract: Background Serum phosphate and parathyroid hormone (PTH) are linked through tightly regulated mineral homeostasis, but whether their continuous association differs by sex across populations remains uncertain. We investigated whether sex modifies the serum phosphate–PTH association, whether short-term dietary phosphorus accounts for this pattern, and whether forward and targeted reverse Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses provide evidence for a stable causal direction. Methods Cross-sectional analyses included 1,613 complete cases from a clinical cohort in Qinghai, China, and 4,358 and 4,394 adults from NHANES 2003–2004 and 2005–2006, respectively. PTH was natural-log transformed, serum phosphate was scaled per 0.1 mmol/L, and the primary parameter was the sex-by-phosphate interaction. Dietary sensitivity analyses in NHANES incorporated reliable day-1 dietary recalls and repeated two-day mean intakes. Forward MR selected 181 independent phosphate-associated variants to evaluate PTH, 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], and lumbar-spine bone mineral density, with 151–160 variants retained per outcome after harmonization. Targeted reverse MR used two independent genome-wide significant clinical intact-PTH instruments. Results Positive sex-by-phosphate interactions were observed in Qinghai ( β = 0.032, 95% CI 0.008–0.057), NHANES 2003–2004 ( β = 0.047, 95% CI 0.030–0.063), and NHANES 2…

A multi-indicator and multi-device coordinated siting strategy for enhancing transient safety support capability in weak sending-end grids with renewable energy stations
abstract: Large-scale long-distance transmission of renewable energy leads to typical weak sending-end characteristics in power grids, where transient disturbances easily cause voltage instability and large-scale tripping of renewable energy units. To address the defects of one-sided indicators and insufficient multi-dimensional collaborative frameworks in conventional siting methods, this paper proposes a coordinated siting strategy for multiple reactive power support devices. Firstly, a multi-dimensional voltage safety evaluation system is established, including the multiple renewable energy stations short circuit ratio, transient voltage fluctuation index and reactive power compensation trajectory sensitivity index. Secondly, considering device characteristics and grid hierarchy, a differentiated deployment scheme for synchronous condensers and static synchronous compensators (STATCOM) is formulated. Furthermore, the entropy weight method and Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) method are integrated to build a siting decision model to resolve conflicts among multiple indicators. Multi-scenario time-domain simulations are carried out based on an actual renewable energy base model. The results show that the proposed strategy can effectively improve the steady-state performance and suppress transient voltage fluctuations of the power grid. It outperfor…

title: Agentic AI for Salesforce Ecosystems with DevOps Integration
abstract: Salesforce platforms power customer service and sales process and require continuous customizations to be performed with code, flows, and metadata, which need to be developed, tested and released safely. This paper introduces an architecture of agentic artificial intelligence featuring two complementary group of agents – business agents that triage cases and qualify leads and DevOps agents that develop, review and release changes through Salesforce DX, scratch orgs and continuous integration. Testing on 1,500 historical cases showed that agentic router classified the case to the appropriate queue in 90.1% cases, compared to 80.2% for a machine-learning classifier (p < 0.001) and 71.4% for rule-based router. Participation of agents shortened case handling time from 14.6 to 8.1 minutes (p < 0.001). Testing on 80 changes showed that a developer agent with a validation loop succeeded to deliver a change on the first try in 90.0% of cases, compared to 76.2% for manual development and 65.0% for a developer agent without validation with lead time shortened from 6.8 to 2.1 days (p < 0.001). Violations of governance limit were found in 2 of 80 validated changes. The findings suggest that agentic agents perform effectively on Salesforce when they are grounded in metadata of the platform and validated with automated tests.

Marketing considerations for translating environmental concern into purchase behavior towards energy efficient air conditioners: a serial mediation analysis
abstract: Purpose This study examines the relationship between environmental concern and the purchase behavior of energy efficient air conditioners (EEACs) among consumers. The study further investigates the theoretical mechanisms linking environmental concern with the purchase behavior of energy efficient air conditioners. Design/methodology/approach The study is largely quantitative with some qualitative inputs of information. Data from 424 households across Delhi and National Capital Region (NCR), Punjab and Tri-city were analyzed using bias-corrected bootstrapping analysis. Findings The study reveals that subjective norms exhibit the positive mediating effect between environmental concern and purchase intention. The study also finds the positive influence of personal norms in influencing behavior through intention. Moreover, the study finds the most robust serial mediation pathway through subjective norms and purchase intention between environmental concern and purchase behavior. These findings suggest that marketing interventions grounded in norm activation may be effective in encouraging EEAC adoption. Research limitations/implications The study relies on self-reported purchase behavior. Future research may examine actual purchase behavior using longitudinal data. Marketers may consider incorporating subjective and personal norms into communication strategies to encourage EEAC adop…

Three-dimensional random field generation and ABAQUS integration for tunnelling-induced sinkhole risk
abstract: This paper presents a robust methodology for generating spatially correlated three-dimensional random fields and integrating them into the Abaqus software program. The proposed algorithm is verified for both regular and irregular meshes. To enhance applicability, an alternative approach is also presented that generates random fields on regular mesh and maps them onto irregular mesh using Abaqus’s mesh-to-mesh solution mapping. The study identifies a critical relationship between mesh resolution and the scale of fluctuation (L): for hypoplastic soil with spatially varying friction angles, the mesh size must be less than L/3 to ensure modelling accuracy. This methodology is applied to assess the risk of tunnelling-induced sinkholes by analysing cutterhead–soil interaction. Numerical results demonstrate that spatial variability significantly alters support pressure–displacement responses. While homogeneous soil exhibits maximum displacement near the invert, spatially variable soil leads to maximum displacements in localised weak zones with low friction angles. By defining the onset of instability as the point of maximum curvature on the support pressure–displacement curve, the study establishes fifth- and 95th-percentile envelopes. The maximum curvature for these bounds occurs at normalised support pressures of 0.11 and 0.20, respectively. To minimise the risk of tunnelling-induce…

title: A fixed-feature perturbation benchmark of unsupervised multi-omics integration in gastric cancer
abstract: Background Unsupervised multi-omics workflows can yield stable partitions within one analytical framework while assigning patients differently across frameworks. We benchmarked this distinction in gastric cancer under shared feature identities and matched patient perturbations. Results Five protocol-frozen primary integration tracks were benchmarked in 352 TCGA-STAD primary gastric cancers with matched mRNA, microRNA, copy-number variation, non-silent mutation, and DNA methylation data; a second Cancer Integration via Multikernel Learning (CIMLR) preprocessing scheme was examined post hoc . Patient-dependent scaling, integration, and clustering were refitted in the same 100 prespecified 80% patient perturbations at K = 2–6. K = 2 was the only resolution without a cluster containing <10% of patients in any primary track or perturbation. Mean within-track pairwise adjusted Rand indices ranged from 0.078 to 0.955, whereas mean agreement among primary tracks within the same perturbation was 0.175. K = 3 increased mean cross-track agreement to 0.263 but produced two small-cluster perturbations in primary CIMLR. Thus, no tested K yielded a universally stable discrete patient partition. Reference microsatellite instability (MSI) status was associated with four of five K = 2 primary partitions and all five primary partitions at K = 3. MLH1 promoter methylation and cytolytic activity…

title: Challenges in Achieving High Energy Density in Lithium-Ion Batteries: Anode Materials and Silicon Modification Strategies
abstract: Due to the development of electric cars, portable electronic devices, and energy storage, lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have experienced an increase in energy density demand. However, restrictions associated with the design of classical electrodes hinder the improvement of batteries' characteristics. The present review article examines three types of anode materials, namely, graphite, graphene, and silicon, as well as their distinct features. First, despite low cost and reliable cycling ability, the capacity of graphite is limited by 372 mAh g⁻¹. Second, high conductivity and lithium storage capacities are provided by graphene, but there is a possibility of aggregation of its sheets that can cause instability. Last but not least, silicon attracts special attention owing to its potential capacity of 3579 mAh g⁻¹. But the constant expansion of silicon makes it harmful for the structure of the electrode and solid electrolyte interphase. In order to resolve these issues, three modification approaches, i.e., structural engineering, composite with carbon materials, and modification of the interface, are proposed. Experimental data support positive outcomes related to the use of such modifications and improvement of the electrode capacity and performance. At last, the drawbacks of silicon-containing anodes, namely production difficulties, electrode swelling, and gap between the experim…

title: Metal Sulfide-Based S-Scheme Heterojunctions for Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction: A Product-Oriented Review
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic CO2 reduction converts solar energy into chemical products, but inefficient use of photogenerated charge and competing surface pathways limit both activity and selectivity. Metal sulfides absorb visible light and often have sufficiently negative conduction-band potentials, yet rapid electron–hole recombination and photocorrosion restrict their performance. S-scheme heterojunctions can promote interfacial charge separation while retaining strongly reducing electrons and strongly oxidizing holes. This review organizes metal-sulfide-based S-scheme systems by target product: carbon monoxide (CO), methane (CH4), methanol (CH3OH), formic acid (HCOOH), and multicarbon (C2+) products. We first compare the S-scheme with Type-II and Z-scheme models and outline how complementary measurements identify the charge-transfer route. We then discuss how interfacial charge transfer and surface sites together determine the product, through the electron supply and charge state of active sites, bonded interfaces that also act as active sites, separated redox sites, and defects created during interface formation. For each product, reported performance is compared together with the reaction conditions and the selectivity definition used in the original study. Dedicated examples exist for CO, CH4, CH3OH, and ethylene (C2H4); we did not find an HCOOH-selective metal-sulfide S-sch…

title: Exploring wormholes in nonlinear $$f(Q, {\mathcal {B}})$$ gravity: energy conditions
Effect of operation condition on thermal analysis of typical energy diaphragm walls in cooling mode
abstract: To provide an accurate assessment of the energy potential to support decisions regarding implementing energy wall technologies and the effective utilisation of underground space and shallow geothermal energy, the effect of operation conditions on thermal analysis of energy diaphragm walls (EDWs) under the combined influences of wall depth (WD) and ground surface temperature fluctuations (GSTFs) in cooling mode is comprehensively studied. The potential influence of the operation condition is first compared through an EDW model test. Then two 3D heat transfer numerical models are built and verified. The findings from a full-scale model based on the climatic and geological conditions in the Chongqing area indicate that the thermal analysis under different operation conditions needs further consideration of WD and GSTFs, or may lead to an overestimation of the energy efficiency. A maximum value of the difference in the thermal efficiencies ranging from 6.4% to 14.4% is obtained for the WD at 10 m between those with and without GSTFs, for intermittent ratio (IR) values from 0 to 3; a maximum difference of 25.4% in the increase of the average daily heat release rate per unit wall area is also observed for the 10 m wall with IR = 3. The results highlight the consideration of GSTFs in the short-term thermal analysis of shallow-depth EDWs under intermittent operation for the accurate th…

title: The Influence of Nurse Knowledge and Clinical Leadership on Patient Safety Incident Reporting with Patient Safety Culture as a Mediation Variable at Abdi Waluyo Hospital
abstract: Patient safety incident reporting is essential for identifying potential risks, preventing adverse events, and improving the quality of hospital care. At Abdi Waluyo Hospital, limitations in nurses' understanding of incident reporting procedures and access to feedback have presented challenges to effective patient safety management. This study examined the relationships between nurses' knowledge, clinical leadership, and patient safety incident reporting, with patient safety culture serving as a mediating variable. A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted from May to June 2026, involving 150 nurses providing direct patient care at Abdi Waluyo Hospital in Central Jakarta, Indonesia. Participants were recruited using total population sampling, and data were collected through a structured questionnaire employing a four-point Likert scale. Data were analyzed using the Three-Box Method for descriptive analysis and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings revealed that nurses' knowledge and clinical leadership were positively and significantly associated with both patient safety culture and incident reporting. Patient safety culture demonstrated the strongest direct association with incident reporting (? = 0.511, p < 0.001) and partially mediated the relationships between nurses' knowledge, clinical leadership, and incident …

title: The Visual Afterlife of a Sports Mega-Event: Reinterpreting the Maccabiah Through Contemporary Poster Design
abstract: Abstract While scholarship on sports mega-events largely conceptualizes them as instruments of soft power, public diplomacy, and nation branding, it has paid less attention to their symbolic afterlife and to how visual legacies can be reinterpreted. Using the Maccabiah Games —the Jewish Olympics—as a case study, this article examines how the visual archive of a sports mega-event can become a site of political contestation by analyzing 12 contemporary artistic reinterpretations of historical Maccabiah posters (1932–1985) exhibited during the 2026 Maccabiah Games. The analysis focuses on new designs as secondary cultural productions that offer counter-narratives which revisit, challenge, and re-signify earlier representations of sport, Jewish identity, and statehood. Through qualitative thematic analysis of visual artifacts, five dominant topics of sport, nationality and history, security and militarism, gender, and socioeconomics were found to be at the heart of the new posters’ critique. The findings suggest that contemporary interpretations of the Maccabiah are shaped primarily by questions of nationalism, security, collective memory, and political responsibility. The article develops the concept of symbolic ownership of mega-events to explain how political accountability and state-centered criticism emerge even when non-state actors, in this case the Maccabi World Union, serv…
venue: International Journal of the Sociology of Leisure

title: From "Assistant" to "Companion": Digital Character Design for Psychological Support among University Students
abstract: Digital characters are becoming increasingly human-like and responsive, and people's expectations for them are gradually shifting from "assistants" to "companions". Targeting daily psychological support for university students, this paper addresses a straightforward design question: in what identity should a digital character appear, and how should the scope of companionship be controlled? Grounded in emotional design theory, this study selects four products, namely Doubao, Replika, Character.AI and Xingye, for comparison from three dimensions: character positioning, visual representation and emotional interaction. Design practice is carried out on this basis. The resulting design features an approachable and natural youthful figure, moderate emotional responses and lightweight desktop companionship, striking a balance among listening, responding and basic assistance. This study argues that the core value of digital companionship lies in encouraging users to communicate while making them aware of the boundaries of such companionship.

title: Advancing inclusive research through clinical trial design
abstract: Abstract Background There is a lack of standardized processes and frameworks, both in the US and globally, to advance representative and inclusive research in clinical trial enrollment. This imperative is needed to draw scientifically accurate conclusions from data and to ensure data collected are applicable to the populations most affected by the disease in question. Main text This commentary aims to describe the practices of developing inclusive clinical trial research using data-informed approaches that build upon available tools, modeling the previous US Food and Drug Administration drafts of diversity action plans (DAPs), including the establishment of, rationale for, and measures needed to meet inclusive enrollment goals. DAPs include the following sections: enrollment goals (disaggregated by race, ethnicity, sex, and age of clinically relevant study populations), rationale for enrollment goals, and measures to meet the enrollment goals. The 5 principles, a conceptual framework to ensure that a trial is as representative as possible using data-informed practices, can be incorporated into each of the sections, which leads to more representative trials for patients who have a particular disease and ultimately to improved patient outcomes. Conclusions The content of the DAP is iterative, as the Phase 3 clinical development plan evolves to ensure the learnings, information, a…

title: Hill Dickinson Stadium: modern construction through design for manufacture and assembly
abstract: The construction of Everton Football Club’s new stadium at Bramley-Moore Dock in Liverpool represents one of the most significant applications of modern methods of construction in the UK. Delivered within a constrained heritage dockland environment, the project demonstrates the integration of design for manufacture and assembly (DfMA), digital engineering and industrialised construction to achieve improvements in productivity, safety, sustainability and programme certainty. This paper examines how DfMA was embedded across the structural, architectural and building services design, and how it enabled a fundamentally different approach to construction delivery. Particular focus is placed on the prefabrication of structural components, the adoption of modular mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems, the use of schedule-linked three-dimensional (3D) digital simulation (known as 4D) and the development of innovative precast solutions such as double-stepped terracing units. The paper argues that the Hill Dickinson Stadium project illustrates a transition from traditional construction to a manufacturing-led paradigm, offering a replicable model for future complex infrastructure projects.
venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Civil Engineering

title: Back to the future: orchestrating dynamic capabilities for AI-enabled supply chain design
abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly promoted in supply chain (SC) design, but guidance on its adoption in the literature is fragmented and often overlooks empirical insights based on established digital technologies. As a result, cumulative theory building is hindered, and there is little clarity on recurring adoption issues and organizational challenges. This study explores how factors that affect the adoption of established digital technologies – such as the Internet of Things and radio-frequency identification – apply to the incorporation of AI into SC design from the orchestrator’s perspective. Design/methodology/approach This study employs a sequential mixed-methods approach. It begins with ten expert interviews to identify key reference technologies and core SC processes, which were then validated through a systematic review of 47 studies. Conditions for adoption were assessed using the technology–organization–environment and dynamic capabilities frameworks and applied to AI implementation in SCs. Findings We distill recurring AI adoption conditions into six dynamic implementation domains. We show that orchestrators address these through a recursive cycle of sensing, seizing and reconfiguring, in which reconfiguring resets the conditions sensed in the next iteration. This approach frames AI implementation as continuous capability renewal and foregrounds t…
venue: International Journal of Physical Distribution & Logistics Management

title: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan: Molecular Design, Clinical Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) dysregulation contributes to the progression of breast, gastric, lung, and other solid tumors, yet conventional HER2-targeted therapies remain limited by tumor heterogeneity and acquired resistance. Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), a HER2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), combines trastuzumab with a cleavable tetrapeptide linker and the topoisomerase I inhibitor DXd. Its high drug-to-antibody ratio and membrane-permeable payload support potent cytotoxicity and a bystander effect in tumors with heterogeneous HER2 expression. Clinical trials have demonstrated benefit in HER2-positive and HER2-low breast cancer, HER2-positive gastric cancer, and selected HER2-altered non-small cell lung cancers, although evidence maturity and biomarker criteria vary among tumor types. Interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, systemic toxicity, spatial and temporal HER2 heterogeneity, and multifactorial resistance continue to constrain the therapeutic index. This review examines the molecular design, mechanism of action, clinical applications, and limitations of T-DXd and evaluates antibody engineering, site-specific conjugation, linker and payload optimization, biomarker-guided selection, and mechanism-informed treatment strategies for next-generation HER2-targeted ADCs.

title: Teachers’ universal design for learning competence and inclusive mathematics teaching practices: the mediating role of universal design for learning implementation
abstract: Despite the growing recognition of Universal Designfor Learning (UDL) as a framework for promoting inclusive education, limited attention has been paid to the simultaneous roles of teachers’ UDL competence, UDL implementation, and inclusive mathematics teaching practices. This study, therefore, examined the mediating role of UDL implementation in the relationship between teachers’ UDL competence and inclusive mathematics teaching practices. The study adopted a quantitative survey design. An online questionnaire was used to collect data from 350 Senior High School mathematics teachers in Kumasi, Ghana. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was employed to analyse the relationships among the variables. The findings revealed that teachers’ UDL competence was positively associated with UDL implementation ( β = .608) and with inclusive mathematics teaching practices ( β = .435), and that UDL implementation was also positively associated with inclusive mathematics teaching practices ( β = .246). UDL implementation partially mediated the relationship between teachers’ UDL competence and inclusive mathematics teaching practices [indirect effect = .166, 95% CI (.052, .269)], accounting for 25.6% of the total effect, while the remaining 74.4% was direct. The study concludes that teachers’ UDL competence is associated with inclusive mathematics teaching both directly and through the classroo…

title: A Molecular Design Strategy for Biobased, Fluorine-Free, Aqueous-Developable, and Positive-Type Photosensitive Polyimides with Low Dielectric Loss at High Frequencies of 10–40 GHz
abstract: Abstract Photosensitive polyimides (PSPIs) are widely used as dielectric and passivation materials in semiconductor packaging because of their excellent thermal stability, mechanical strength, chemical resistance, and photopatternability. However, fluorinated building blocks are still widely employed in conventional PSPIs to achieve desirable material performance, raising increasing concerns regarding their sustainability and environmental impact. In this study, a series of fluorine-free, partially biobased polyimides (PIs) is synthesized from structurally diverse aromatic diamines containing bulky pendant groups and ester linkages in combination with three dianhydride systems, including an isosorbide-derived dianhydride and two aromatic dianhydrides. The resulting PIs exhibit tunable dielectric and thermomechanical properties and incorporate a renewable biomass-derived component; among them, IB-NB, with a benzonorbornane moiety, shows the most balanced performance and is selected as the polymer matrix for developing an aqueous-developable, positive-type PSPI. The type and content of the sulfonated diazonaphthoquinone as a dissolution inhibitor, the diamine-to-dianhydride ratio, and processing conditions are subsequently optimized. The optimized PSPI exhibits a sensitivity of 200 mJ cm–2, a contrast of 4.58, and successfully resolved 40 μm line-and-space patterns with a thickne…

title: AI and Digital Media Interaction Design: Technology, Experience, and Future Prospects
abstract: With the rapid development of digital media, artificial intelligence has become a core driving force of industrial innovation, while traditional interactive design relying on manual experience cannot meet users' personalized and immersive demands.This paper takes the integration of artificial intelligence and digital media interaction design as the research theme.It sorts out core AI technologies... analyzes their practical applications... discusses prominent challenges in practice, such as user privacy leakage, algorithm bias, insufficient designer creativityThe research concludes that AI can intelligently upgrade the whole design workflow... yet ethical and collaborative obstacles remain unsolved. In the future, human-AI collaboration will become the mainstream design paradigm... provide theoretical guidance for digital media design practice.

title: Effect of Micronutrient and Plant Extract on Growth Parameters of Oat (Avena sativa L.)
abstract: Background: Oat (Avena sativa L.) is a nutritionally superior cool-season cereal with growing importance in Punjab’s rabi cropping system. Micronutrient deficiencies, especially zinc and suboptimal use of biostimulants remain major constraints to oat productivity in Indian soils. Methods: A field experiment was conducted during the Rabi season 2025-26 at the Agricultural Research Farm, Lovely Professional University, Phagwara, Punjab. A randomised block design (RBD) with 13 treatments and 3 replications was used. Treatments comprised graded levels of ZnSO4 (0.2%, 0.4%, 0.8%), seaweed extract (2, 4, 8 mL), moringa leaf extract (2, 4, 8 mL) and their combinations with 50%, 75% and 100% RDF, applied as two foliar sprays at 30 and 60 DAS. Results: Treatment T13 (100% RDF + 0.2% ZnSO4 + 2 mL seaweed extract + 2 mL moringa extract) showed the highest reported plant height (126.7 cm), dry matter accumulation (120.9 g plant-1), leaf area index (6.2), effective tillers (304 m-2) and reported chlorophyll-meter reading (58.7) at the final observation. These are growth responses; yield and economic returns were not evaluated.

title: Virtual Experimentation of Tensile Reinforcement in Cellulose Nanofiber-Reinforced Rubber Composites through Integrated Multimodal Characterization and Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Machine-learning-based virtual experimentation is promising for accelerating materials development, but its application is often limited by small experimental data sets. In this study, a multimodal virtual experimentation framework was developed for cellulose nanofiber (CNF)-reinforced natural rubber (NR) composites (NR/CNF) using an approximately 100-sample data characterized by sedimentation (SED), X-ray diffraction (XRD), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), and time-domain nuclear magnetic resonance (TD-NMR). The characterization data were converted into latent descriptors and used to predict tensile properties. The reinforcement indices M300/M100 and M400/M100 showed the highest prediction accuracy, with holdout R2 values of 0.68 and 0.79, respectively. Hierarchical generative models reproduced the overall characteristics of the experimental profiles to generate and screen 500 virtual data. The generated descriptors retained moderate predictive capability for reinforcement indices (R2 = 0.45–0.54), supporting trend-level virtual screening. Feature-importance analysis showed that the primary sedimentation-derived descriptor (SED_PC1) accounted for approximately 60% of the total importance, and high-performing virtual candidates were concentrated toward the SED_PC1-rich region of the design maps. These findings identify SED_PC1 as the dominant predictive indicator f…

title: Exploring the barriers and pathways to sustainable adoption of virtual reality in architecture: a pilot study comparing industry and academic perspectives
abstract: Purpose A central concern in the sustainable adoption of digital technologies is that, despite demonstrated technical benefits, their integration across the architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) sector remains uneven. Virtual reality (VR) exemplifies this challenge: although it has the potential to transform architectural communication, collaboration and design education, uptake is fragmented by competing institutional priorities and by users’ cognitive and affective experiences. This study aims to investigate how VR is perceived and applied in academia and practice. Design/methodology/approach The authors conducted focus group interviews analysed using causal layered analysis (CLA). During these sessions, academics and industry experts used VR headsets, and their experiences and reflections were transcribed and systematically coded for analysis. Findings Beyond surface observations, CLA reveals how psychological factors (e.g. presence, immersion, agency) interact with technical and organisational barriers. Six themes emerged across both groups: collaboration, immersion, immersivity, embodiment, accessibility and cultural resistance, highlighting areas of alignment and divergence. The findings demonstrate that VR adoption is not simply a technical process but a cultural and organisational negotiation, and they propose pathways for effectively embedding immersive tech…

title: Partially biodegradable phosphorylated sugarcane bagasse based poly (AA-co-AM) hydrogel as a soil conditioner for drought stress mitigation and supplementary nitrogen delivery in lupine (Lupinus termis L.)
abstract: Abstract Background The excessive application of conventional mineral NPK fertilizers has led to severe environmental and agricultural challenges, including nutrient leaching, soil degradation, and ecological risks. Addressing these challenges requires sustainable alternatives that efficiently regulate soil moisture and nutrient availability. This study developed a partially biodegradable hydrogel composite derived from agricultural waste (sugarcane bagasse) to serve the dual purpose of water retention and improved nutrient retention. The hydrogel was synthesized by functionalizing sugarcane bagasse via phosphoric acid phosphorylation, followed by free-radical graft copolymerization with acrylamide (AM) and acrylic acid (AA). Subsequently, pot experiments were conducted to evaluate the efficacy of Phosphorylated Sugarcane Bagasse Based Poly (AA- co -AM) hydrogel on lupine grown under drought conditions. The hydrogel was applied at 0, 0.1% and 0.2% (W/W) in pots subjected to either well-water conditions (100% field capacity, FC) or water deficit (50% FC). Results FTIR and SEM analyses confirmed the successful grafting of monomers onto the bagasse and the formation of an interconnected porous network. The incorporation of acrylic acid (AA) significantly enhanced the material’s water swelling capacity, reaching up to 2900%. A specific hydrogel formulation with an AM: AA ratio of 1…

title: Coverage path planning of heterogeneous UAVs for crop remote sensing monitoring in irregular farmlands
abstract: Multirotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with gimbal imaging systems can acquire multi-angle and high-resolution farmland imagery, thereby providing essential data for precision crop monitoring. Single UAV is limited by endurance and imaging swath width, cooperative operation with heterogeneous UAVs has become an important solution for improving the remote-sensing data acquisition efficiency over large and complex farmland. This study addresses the problems of unbalanced workload and coverage path planning in cooperative data acquisition by heterogeneous UAVs over complex concave farmland. A two-step coverage path-planning method based on width-sum-guided convex decomposition and adaptive neighborhood assignment is proposed. Firstly, a bi-level optimization model is established, where heterogeneous UAV fleet makespan minimization is used as the global objective and single-sortie full-route distance minimization is used as the local objective. For irregular farmland boundaries, a width-sum-guided and direction-oriented convex decomposition strategy is then developed to divide complex regions into convex subregions suitable for boustrophedon image acquisition. On this basis, heterogeneous UAVs region assignment, multi-sortie splitting, and imaging-swath-matched path generation are performed by jointly considering the imaging acquisition performance index, task-duration…

title: The microbiome of controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) leafy greens: cleaner leaves with lower microbial richness but highly dynamic microbial communities
abstract: Introduction Controlled-Environment Agriculture (CEA) is an advanced form of agriculture where crops are grown under strict environmental conditions to optimize quality and yield. Little is known about whether this strict control affects crop microbial dynamics during a crop’s growing season. Methods Here, the bacterial and fungal communities were profiled using metagenomic barcoding throughout a growing season for two leafy greens: lettuce ( Lactuca sativa L.) and arugula ( Eruca sativa , L.). Both were grown in an indoor-grown, vertical farm at a commercial scale. We monitored microbial diversity and turnover rates across pre-harvest and post-harvest time points. Results Our findings indicated a microbial community that was surprisingly unstable, considering the controlled nature of the environment and differed significantly to that reported for field-grown outdoor leafy greens. While the microbiomes of lettuce and arugula were highly structured by phenology and the tissue sampled, we observed significant successional cycling. Also, the fertigation microbiome shared significant community structure with crop microbiomes. Discussion Taken together, this study provides an insight into the microbial dynamics at play within controlled-environment agricultural (CEA) systems, providing a route for precision microbial management in these agricultural systems, minimizing the potential…

title: Narrative Hedging and Identity Displacement: On the Instrumental Transformation of Soft Power in Japan's Diplomacy
abstract: As Japan accelerates its pursuit of "normal statehood" and expands its defence functions, vigilance within the international community, especially the Western bloc, against its historical revisionism has continued to weaken. Existing studies have paid insufficient attention to how Japan reconstructs its role identity to address diplomatic dilemmas under the dual burdens of geopolitical pressure and historical issues. This paper proposes the theoretical mechanism of "identity hedging". It argues that when a state faces geopolitical pressure and its inherent historical identity becomes a diplomatic burden, ontological security anxiety emerges. The state then proactively constructs high-order, universal role identities and exports soft power of political values through such identities, so as to conceal or offset diplomatic obstacles brought by negative historical labels. This paper comparatively analyses the evolution of Japan's identity construction and foreign policies in two phases: "apology and passive hedging" from the 1990s to the early 2000s, and "values and active hedging" from 2012 to the present. By reconstructing its national identity from a "post-war beneficiary of peace" to a "defender of the rules-based order", Japan turns this instrumental identity displacement into value-based soft power. Such soft power effectively reduces the vigilance of the international commun…

title: Effects of poultry manure and seaweed extract on growth and yield of wheat (Triticum aestivum L.)
abstract: The continuous use of chemical fertilisers has adversely affected soil condition and reduced the efficiency of nutrient use, resulting in lower wheat yields over time. A field study was performed during the rabi season of 2024–25 at the Agricultural Research Farm, Lovely Professional University, Punjab, using a split-plot design, with four levels of poultry manure (PM) (0, 5, 10 and 15 tonnes per hectare (t ha-1)) as main plot treatments and four levels of seaweed extract (SE) (0, 0.25 %, 0.75 % and 1 %) as subplot treatments, forming 16 treatment combinations with 3 replications. The study showed that applying PM at 15 t ha-1 significantly enhanced growth parameters including plant height, number of tillers and dry matter accumulation, while seaweed extract at 1 % enhanced crop vigour. The integrated application of 15 t ha-1 poultry manure and 1 % SE recorded the highest grain yield (61.21 quintals per hectare (q ha-1)), straw yield (56.09 q ha-1) and harvest index (52.21 %), with a significant interaction between poultry manure and SE (p < 0.05). These findings indicate a synergistic effect between PM and SE. The use of organic manure combined with biostimulants significantly enhanced yield attributes such as spike length and grain formation, leading to higher wheat productivity. This study indicates that the use of PM along with SE can be considered as an environmentally fri…

Pruning Severity Impact on Morpho-biochemical and Yield Characters of Pomegranate Cultivar Pearl Under Semi-Arid Conditions of Central Punjab, Pakistan
abstract: Pruning is a crucial horticultural technique that considerably affects plant growth, quality and yield of pomegranate (Punica granatum L.). This study was conducted to evaluate the effect of four different pruning intensities comprising control (zero pruning) C0, water shoot removal (WSR), sucker removal (SR), dead wood removal (DWR) and WSR+SR+DWR with four replications on fruit quality attributes including fruit weight, fruit size, color of arils, total soluble solids, titratable acidity, juice content and overall sensory acceptability. Experiment was carried out at Horticultural Research Institute, Faisalabad, Pakistan and laid out according to Randomized Complete Block Design comprised of four replications. Physical (Fruit size, fruit weight, No. of arils, juice percentage) and biochemical (total soluble solids, titratable acidity, vitamin C contents etc.) Treatment comprising suckers, dead wood and water shoots removal enhanced fruit size and increased total soluble solids levels leading to superior sweetness and marketability, excessive pruning, however, reduced fruit yield and promoted excessive vegetative growth. Disease incidence was maximum (19%) in control treatment (zero pruning) whereas, it recorded minimum (11.6%) in plants subjected to severe pruning (T4). Fruit set percentage was recorded maximum (30%) in plants that undergone severe pruning (Sucker, dead wood a…

title: Genome-wide identification of the AkCRK gene family and functional characterization of AkCRK5 in resistance to soft rot in Amorphophallus konjac
abstract: Cysteine-rich receptor-like kinases (CRKs) are an important class of plant receptor-like kinases that play key roles in immune responses, stress adaptation, and developmental regulation. However, the CRK gene family in Amorphophallus konjac has not been systematically characterized. In this study, a hidden Markov model was constructed based on conserved CRK protein domains to systematically identify and characterize AkCRK gene family members in A. konjac using TBtools software. The expression profiles of these genes were examined using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction under mannitol treatment, low temperature, methyl jasmonate (MeJA) treatment, and inoculation with the soft rot pathogen Pectobacterium carotovorum subsp. carotovorum ( Pcc ). For functional characterization, AkCRK5 was overexpressed in Nicotiana benthamiana , and transient overexpression was performed in A. konjac ; disease severity and lesion development were assessed after Pcc inoculation. A total of 19 AkCRK genes were identified in the whole genome of A. konjac , of which 17 were localized to seven chromosomes, while the remaining 2 could not be mapped to any chromosome. The predicted proteins ranged from 445 to 1,020 amino acids in length, with corresponding molecular weights spanning 49,137.82 -112,870.09 Da. Based on their physicochemical properties, the encoded proteins were predominantly …

title: Traditional agri-food products (TAPs) of plant origin in the Italian region Campania as cultural heritage and sources of nutritional value
Emerging Opportunities in Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Phenotyping for Insect‐Resistance Crop Breeding
abstract: ABSTRACT Breeding insect‐resistant cultivars depends on phenotypes precise and heritable enough to resolve the genetic variation underlying resistance. The ordinal damage score, recorded at a single timepoint, compresses antixenosis, antibiosis and tolerance into one number and may therefore limit the resolution of QTL mapping and GWAS. This review evaluates multimodal artificial intelligence (AI), the joint analysis of imaging, behavioural and physiological data streams, as a route to mechanism‐resolved resistance phenotypes. Three questions frame the synthesis: whether multimodal AI can generate more precise insect‐resistance phenotypes; whether such phenotypes are heritable, repeatable and suitable for genetic mapping; and how they could be integrated into breeding decisions. The evidence to date is largely unimodal, coming from damage segmentation, electrical penetration graph (EPG) waveform classification and physiological imaging studied separately, and no study has yet compared multimodal and conventional phenotypes in the same insect‐resistance mapping population. Improved mapping resolution is therefore treated as a testable hypothesis rather than an established result. To make it testable, we outline a validation design for a defined crop–pest system, a worked intermediate‐fusion case study, a phased roadmap from two‐modality experiments to genomic integration, and co…

title: Chorismate mutase inhibitors reduce the pathogenicity of the plant-parasitic nematode Meloidogyne incognita
abstract: Abstract As the plant-parasitic nematode Meloidogyne incognita is among the most notorious threats to food security and plant health, there is a demand for products that are more efficient for its control and less aggressive toward non-target organisms. M. incognita creates feeding sites on its hosts through the use of several proteins, among which chorismate mutase (CM) stands out. Consequently, the present study had the general objective of investigating the use of CM inhibitors/ligands to control M. incognita . Initially, an experiment with tomato plants inoculated with the nematode and treated with the inhibitors isatin and carvacrol was carried out, resulting in a reduced number of galls in tomato roots, which confirmed the potential of CM inhibitors to control this nematode. Then, the three-dimensional structure of the amino acid sequence of the CM produced by M. incognita was modeled using several computational programs/methods to obtain a homodimer. More than 230 million organic substances were used to select the most efficient ligands of CM through molecular docking. The selected substances underwent tests with M. incognita and showed that five substances reduced the number of root galls on plants to levels statistically equal to those observed using a commercial nematicide. Therefore, both CM and the selected substances have the potential to be used as a starting poin…

title: Protandrous dichogamy and chances of geitonogamy in the hermaphrodite East Indian glory bower (Clerodendrum glandulosum)
Genome‐wide identification of carboxylesterase gene family in tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum )
abstract: Abstract Carboxylesterases (CXEs) catalyze the hydrolysis of a wide range of ester compounds and play pivotal roles in plant hormone metabolism, volatile compound regulation, and stress responses. Despite their functional significance, a comprehensive characterization of CXEs in tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum ) remains lacking. In this study, a total of 24 SlCXE genes were identified through genome‐wide analysis, and their phylogenetic relationships, gene structures, and chromosomal distributions were systematically characterized. Collinearity analysis revealed that SlCXEs exhibit closer evolutionary relationships with homologs in dicotyledonous species. Transcriptome profiling indicated that several SlCXE genes are highly expressed during fruit ripening. Among these, Solyc01g108540 ( SlCXE6 ) was selected for further analysis due to its representative expression pattern, conserved structural features, and relatively diverse cis‐ regulatory elements. Subsequent expression analyses demonstrated that SlCXE6 displays tissue‐specific expression patterns, is dynamically regulated during fruit development, and responds differentially to pathogen infection, low‐temperature stress, and hormone treatments. These findings provide a comprehensive overview of the SlCXE gene family in tomato and offer novel insights into their evolutionary diversification and functional involvement in fruit …

title: Contrasting maize straw pre-decomposition strategies alter soil nutrient status, root metabolism, and rhizosphere microbial communities in an acidic red soil
abstract: Introduction Straw decomposition products may serve as organic amendments for acidic soils, but their effects depend on the decomposition strategy. Methods Maize straw was pre-decomposed for 150 d with either effective microorganisms (EM) or lime, and the resulting products were applied to an acidic red soil planted with maize. The pot experiment comprised three treatments: unamended control (CK), the EM-mediated straw decomposition product (EM-SDP), and the lime-mediated straw decomposition product (Lime-SDP). We assessed maize growth, soil properties, root metabolomic profiles, and rhizosphere bacterial and fungal communities. Results Both amendments promoted maize growth and altered root metabolic and rhizosphere microbial profiles. Lime-SDP treatment primarily alleviated soil acidity and increased total K, whereas EM-SDP treatment was associated with higher soil organic matter and greater N, P, and K availability. Root metabolic profiles were also strongly reconfigured, with treatment explaining 46.7% of the total metabolomic variation ( R 2 = 0.467, exact P = 0.0036), with the dominant response shared by both amendments. Treatment explained 30.5% of bacterial and 34.3% of fungal community variation based on Aitchison distances (both P = 0.0036). Terpenoid-related features were the only chemical class significantly enriched among the shared metabolic responses. Exploratory …

Knowledge-guided supervisory architecture with an LLM-compatible interface for robust energy management of integrated storage under renewable uncertainty
abstract: Introduction High renewable penetration couples forecast errors, storage dynamics, and grid constraints. We study a knowledge-guided supervisory architecture that maps operational context to bounded uncertainty margins, carbon and peak weights, degradation multipliers, and reserve targets. Methods A worst-corner rolling linear program coordinates battery, hydrogen, and thermal storage, followed by deterministic realized-balance repair. A large language model (LLM)-compatible interface is proposed, but the experiments use deterministic numeric context rules and do not execute retrieval, language-model inference, or a text parser. The synthetic 7-day comparison gives all model predictive control (MPC) controllers the same issued grid-event notices and emergency recourse. Results Each MPC controller achieves numerical zero unserved energy. Relative to fixed robust MPC, the adaptive supervisor decreases nominal peak import from 439.86 to 414.81 kW but increases evaluation cost from 3,160.73 to 3,337.12 USD and service-normalized emissions from 145.28 to 148.01 kg CO 2 /MWh. Four additional randomized scenarios show the same mean cost-peak trade-off, without establishing universal superiority. Isolated ablations and notice-recourse controls show that zero shortage is not unique to adaptive reasoning. All 57 released trajectories pass physical and accounting checks. Discussion Exact-…

Standardization landscape for positive energy districts: mapping SDOs, gaps, and recommendations for interoperability
abstract: Positive Energy Districts (PEDs) have emerged as a transformative paradigm for urban decarbonization, yet their implementation requires integration across energy systems, buildings, mobility, and information and communication technologies, for which no coherent international standardization framework currently exists. This conceptual analysis examines the PED standardization landscape using a three-layer interoperability model encompassing technical, governance, and social dimensions. The initial standard inventory was primarily sourced from the IEC Technology Report Positive Energy Districts, supplemented by documents from SET Plan IWG 3.2, JPI Urban Europe, and IEA framework definitions. PED-relevant standards were defined as documents addressing energy, the built environment, mobility, digital infrastructure, or urban governance within district-scale decarbonisation. The analysis drew on the inventory documented in the IEC Technology Report, supplemented by the framework documents noted above. Standards were coded against the three-layer interoperability framework using the definitions and decision rules described in the Methods. Because the analysis is based on a documented inventory rather than an independent systematic search, statements about coverage and absence refer to that inventory. The findings reveal a pronounced asymmetry: technical interoperability is extensivel…

title: Peer review of review articles: matching evaluation criteria to review type
abstract: Peer review of review articles is often conducted as though ‘review’ were a single genre. Narrative, critical and scoping reviews are assessed against criteria designed for systematic reviews, with requests for protocol registration, exhaustive searches or preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses flow diagrams that the chosen design never required. Drawing on more than two decades of editorial experience across toxicology, environmental health, and food safety journals, this viewpoint argues that the problem lies largely within editorial control and proposes three inexpensive remedies: journals should state which review types they accept, authors should declare their review methodology at submission, and reviewers should receive review-type-specific guidance.

title: Metal-Center-Regulated Charge-Storage Kinetics and Mechanisms in Co- and Ni-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks Anodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Metal–ligand chemistry, crystal structure, and morphology can influence sodium storage in BTC-based anodes. Examining these characteristics alongside electrochemical performance provides a basis for interpreting differences in charge-storage kinetics and cycling behavior. In this work, Co-BTC and Ni-BTC were synthesized from 1,3,5-benzenetricarboxylic acid under similar solvothermal conditions using cobalt acetate and nickel nitrate, respectively, and evaluated as sodium-ion battery anodes. Co-BTC forms relatively open, flower-like microspheres assembled from nanosheets with a specific surface area of 128.0 m2 g–1, whereas Ni-BTC develops denser interconnected nanosheet assemblies with a surface area of 80.8 m2 g–1. At 50 mA g–1, Co-BTC and Ni-BTC composite electrodes delivered second-cycle capacities of 402 and 102 mAh g–1, respectively, normalized to the corresponding MOF mass. Thus, Co-BTC provides higher specific capacity than that of Ni-BTC, although it has relatively lower capacity retention. Kinetic analyses reveal a larger diffusion-associated contribution, a lower apparent interfacial activation energy of 27.24 kJ mol–1, and generally higher apparent Na+ transport coefficients for Co-BTC, whereas Ni-BTC exhibits a predominantly surface-controlled response and a higher apparent activation energy of 35.74 kJ mol–1. Ex situ XPS and FTIR reveal cycling-dependent c…

title: Synergistic Integration for Energy Sector Decarbonization: Leveraging Solar, Storage, Power Systems, and Carbon Capture
abstract: The energy transition towards low carbon energy systems is an essential step in achieving the climate targets of the world and sustaining the future of the energy system. This narrative review is aimed at evaluating the synergies between four components of the energy transition: solar energy, energy storage, power‑system modernization, and carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS). The review will focus on advancements in energy storage technologies such as lithium‑ion batteries, flow batteries, and green hydrogen as they complement each other in solving the issue of the intermittency of renewables, balancing supply and demand of energy, and long duration storage of energy. In addition, the review will explore how smart grid technologies make it possible to monitor the power system and increase its flexibility and resilience. Though CCUS can have the potential to reduce emissions of the appropriate processes and energy sources, it still does not receive much attention and its usage level is relatively low compared to what is needed to achieve the global decarbonization. According to the estimates of the International Energy Agency, in the early 2025 the operational carbon capture capacity worldwide had already exceeded 50 million t of CO2 annually.

title: Metabolic Implications of Metal Toxicity: The Omics Paradigm Approach
abstract: Metal toxicity poses significant risks to human health and the environment, with far-reaching implications for metabolic processes. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying metal-induced metabolic disturbances is crucial for developing effective interventions and therapeutic strategies. Omics approaches, including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, offer comprehensive insights into the metabolic implications of metal toxicity. This review paper highlights the importance of omics techniques in elucidating how metals disrupt cellular pathways and processes, leading to metabolic alterations. By identifying biomarkers of metal exposure and toxicity, omics studies contribute to the early detection and assessment of metal-induced metabolic disturbances. Furthermore, these approaches facilitate the discovery of potential therapeutic targets for mitigating the adverse effects of metal toxicity on metabolism. Through a review of relevant literature, this paper provides insight into the metabolic pathways affected by metal toxicity, its impacts on metabolism, and the role of omics approaches in studying metal-induced metabolic disturbances. It further emphasizes the significance of integrating omics technologies into research on metal toxicity to advance our understanding of its metabolic implications and inform strategies for protecting human health and th…

title: Global dynamics and performance evaluation of a linkage-based geometrically nonlinear energy harvester: quasi-symmetric versus asymmetric bistable configurations
An Assessment of Residential Solar Energy Access and Consumption Patterns in Adamawa State
abstract: This study conducts a comprehensive assessment of residential solar energy access and consumption patterns in Adamawa State, emphasizing the relationship between Access to Solar Energy Consumption and key independent variables. Through rigorous regression estimation, Solar Energy Awareness, Community-Based Programs, Households Monthly Income, and Primary Use and Consumption of Solar Energy emerge as influential predictors. The model, with an impressive R-squared value of 0.769184, effectively elucidates 76.9% of the variability in Access to Solar Energy Consumption, providing nuanced insights into the strength and direction of these relationships. The assessment sheds light on the intricate dynamics of solar energy dynamics in Adamawa State, offering valuable insights for policymakers, researchers, and stakeholders keen on promoting sustainable energy practices. The study proposes targeted policy recommendations, including the promotion of solar energy awareness, strengthening communitybased programs, addressing income disparities for equitable access, encouraging sustainable consumption patterns, supporting research and development for innovation, and emphasizing ongoing monitoring and evaluation of policy impact. These recommendations aim to guide strategic initiatives that foster sustainable energy practices, ensuring informed decision-making and fostering a greener, more eq…
