title: Coordinated crack-dendrite evolution and directional regulation mechanisms in solid state lithium-metal batteries
abstract: Abstract Addressing safety issues such as internal short circuits and thermal runaway caused by crack-dendrite co-evolution induced by defects in solid state lithium-metal batteries (SSLMBs), an electro-chemo-thermal-mechanical coupled phase-field model is developed. Impacts of initial crack geometric characteristics, crack number, and intercell temperature gradients on crack propagation and dendrite growth behavior are systematically investigated to reveal the underlying regulatory mechanisms. Results show that effects of initial crack shape on crack propagation and dendrite growth depend on crack size. Among the configurations investigated, the two-crack configuration exhibits the smallest maximum growth distance and pronounced outward crack deflection. At 200 s, its combined crack and dendrite area is approximately 32% smaller than that of the single-crack configuration, while its maximum crack propagation distance decreases from 225.4 to 69.4 μm, a reduction of approximately 69.2%. Interactions between the stress fields of adjacent cracks contribute to this suppression and crack deflection, reducing the risk of short circuits. Temperature heterogeneity across the cell also alters crack propagation paths and dendrite growth patterns. Under large intercell temperature heterogeneities, pronounced crack deflection is accompanied by suppressed dendrite growth. The findings of th…

title: Determination of Kerogen Maturation by 1H NMR Relaxation in the Rotating Frame and Dynamic Decoupling
abstract: Abstract Kerogen is the primary organic constituent of petroleum source rocks and plays a crucial role in the generation and storage of hydrocarbons in unconventional reservoirs. The thermal maturity of kerogen is one of the key parameters controlling hydrocarbon generation and defining the oil and gas windows. Solid-state 13C nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is widely used for kerogen characterization because, as a non-destructive technique, it provides detailed information on molecular structure and maturity while allowing complementary analyses to be performed on the same sample. In this work, we evaluate the potential of 1H longitudinal relaxation in the rotating frame and the use of dipolar-decoupled evolutions as rapid indicators of maturity in a series of laboratory-matured kerogen samples. The results show a strong correlation with conventional 13C NMR-derived maturity parameters, while requiring significantly simpler instrumentation and substantially shorter experimental times.

title: Nutrition Outcomes and Participation Determinants Among Older Adults in Congregate Meal Programs
abstract: Purpose: Congregate meal programs (CMPs), supported by the Older Americans Act, serve as a key strategy to address food insecurity and loneliness among the aging population in the United States. However, despite their significance, the existing research concerning their nutritional effect, accessibility, and implementation is fragmented, limiting the ability to understand the effectiveness and reach of these programs. Method: The current narrative review explored findings from 32 studies based in the United States published between 2015 and 2025, identified through search terms (“congregate meal*” OR “senior nutrition program*” OR “Elderly Nutrition Program”) AND (nutrition OR dietary intake OR diet quality) in three different databases (PubMed, Web of Science, and EBSCO). Results: Three major domains emerged from the literature: (1) nutrition and food insecurity outcomes, (2) nutrition- and disease-related outcomes, and (3) factors influencing participation. Overall, the reviewed literature primarily, through observational studies, highlights the positive contributions of CMPs to improve diet quality, address food insecurity, and loneliness, while also identifying persistent challenges related to access, limited menu flexibility, and limited evidence on long-term health outcomes. Conclusion: Future work should prioritize the inclusion of longitudinal studies and equity-focused…

title: Seed Storage Studies in Selected Himalayan Montane Tree Species: Implications for Seed Banking and ex-situ Conservation
abstract: Background: Effective seed storage is essential for the Ex situ conservation of Himalayan montane tree species, which face climatic extremes, habitat degradation and regeneration constraints. Objective: The present study evaluated the effects of storage temperature and duration on the seed germination behaviour of three ecologically important Himalayan tree species, namely Alnus nitida, Quercus glauca and Tsuga dumosa. Methodology: Seeds were stored at ambient room temperature, 5°C or 15°C, and germination attributes were assessed at three-month intervals. Germination percentage, mean germination time and germination value were measured periodically using a completely randomised design. The effects of temperature and storage duration were examined using factorial analysis of variance. Cumulative germination retention was quantified using the area under the germination-retention curve (AUGRC), while post-peak exponential deterioration models were used to estimate deterioration-rate constants and modelled half-germinability periods. Results: Storage temperature, storage duration and their interaction significantly influenced most germination attributes. Seeds stored at ambient room temperature deteriorated rapidly, with complete loss of germinability after six months in A. nitida and Q. glauca and after nine months in T. dumosa. Storage at 5°C resulted in the greatest cumulative …

title: The association between aesthetic ability and physical exercise participation among Chinese college students: a cross-sectional moderated mediation analysis
abstract: Introduction This cross-sectional study examined associations between aesthetic ability and physical exercise participation by testing a moderated mediation model. Specifically, the model examined whether body image statistically accounted for part of this association and whether gender moderated the indirect pathway. Methods A total of 1,083 responses were collected from university students at eight institutions across Shanxi, Sichuan, Chongqing, and Guangdong, China, after data screening, 1,034 valid questionnaires were retained for analysis. Descriptive statistics, correlation analyses, regression analysis, and a moderated mediation model were conducted using SPSS 19.0 and PROCESS 3.5. Results Aesthetic ability was directly associated with physical exercise participation (b = 0.17, p < 0.001) and was indirectly associated with physical exercise participation through body image (indirect association = 0.07, 95% CI [0.046, 0.098]). Moderation analysis showed that the association between aesthetic ability and body image was stronger for males (b = 0.42, p < 0.001) than for females (b = 0.27, p < 0.001), and the association between body image and physical exercise participation was stronger in males (b = 0.40, p < 0.001) than in females (b = 0.07, p < 0.05). Discussion These cross-sectional findings identify aesthetic ability and body image as promising correlates…

title: Thermodynamic Modelling and Efficiency Evaluation of Thermal Storage Technologies: An Overview of Progress in the Last Three Years and Future Directions
abstract: Thermal energy storage (TES) technology appears to be increasingly important in the current energy transition process. This technology seems to offer a potential solution for balancing the unstable output of renewable energy and recovering thermal energy that can be considered industrial waste heat. This paper aims to review the modelling methods and efficiency of several thermal energy storage technologies. The content appears to cover sensible heat, latent heat, thermochemistry, and technologies that seem to constitute liquid or gas thermal energy storage. We also explain certain key metrics and compare single-phase models, two-phase models, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and dynamic models, each of which appears to have its relative advantages and disadvantages. In this context, a summary of key optimisation studies is particularly important. Under these evolving conceptual parameters, dynamic models and multi-field methods tend to more accurately describe actual operating conditions. This review ultimately aims to compare the efficiency of different thermal energy storage types and identify significant research gaps that appear to exist.

title: Public assistance program participation and overweight and obesity among low-income California adults: a repeated cross-sectional analysis of the California Health Interview Survey, 2019–2024
abstract: Abstract Background Participation in public assistance programs may be associated with weight outcomes among low-income adults, but associations may differ by program type and sex. We examined associations of participation in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), and California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs) with overweight and obesity among low-income California adults and evaluated differences by sex. Methods We analyzed 2019–2024 California Health Interview Survey (CHIS) data among adults with household income at or below 130% of the federal poverty level ( n = 16,918). Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (AORs) for overweight (BMI 25.0–29.9 kg/m²) and obesity (BMI ≥ 30.0 kg/m²), each compared with BMI < 25.0 kg/m², adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, smoking, insurance, and food insecurity, with sex-stratified models and formal interaction tests. Results SNAP participation was associated with higher odds of obesity (AOR = 1.23; 95% CI = 1.07–1.42) but not overweight; the association was concentrated among females (AOR = 1.37; 95% CI = 1.15–1.64; P for interaction = 0.04). CalWORKs participation was associated with higher odds of overweight (AOR = 1.29; 95% CI = 1.05–1.59) but not obesity, and this association did not differ significantly by sex. SSI was not …

title: Privatization and The Widening Tax Net: Revenue Loss and Rising Taxation in Nigeria
abstract: This paper examines privatization and the taxation regime in Nigeria. Its objective is to relate the current scope of taxation to the narrowing of government revenue sources that followed privatization. The study takes an explanatory approach and draws on secondary sources. It argues that the present scope of taxation results from the loss of revenue sources through the sale of public enterprises. It recommends that government reverse the privatization option and recreate government-owned capital, so that government can derive revenue from a wider range of sources.

title: Policy incentives for spent lithium-ion battery recycling: A calibrated tripartite evolutionary game analysis based on a Shanghai case study
abstract: Abstract China has become the world’s largest market for new energy vehicles, accompanied by a surge in spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, the low formal recycling rate of spent LIBs poses both environmental risk and resource inefficiency. Given China’s high import dependence on critical materials such as lithium, nickel, and cobalt, it is urgent to enhance formal recycling to mitigate ecological threats and ensure sustainable resource supply. This work evaluates the optimal strategy for the participation of three stakeholders: government, electric vehicle (EV) manufacturer, and consumer, in the recycling of spent LIBs by evolutionary game theory (EGT). Prior to empirical validation, the model is examined through evolutionary stability and sensitivity analysis to ensure robustness. The applicability of the proposed framework is demonstrated through a calibrated case study using Shanghai data from 2023. It is indicated that EV manufacturers are incentivized to establish recycling networks when subsidies or fines reach a threshold equivalent to approximately 0.82 million RMB per manufacturer under the Shanghai-specific parameter settings. Similarly, consumer participation can be promoted when penalties exceed approximately 315 RMB per vehicle. These thresholds should not be regarded as fixed policy standards, but rather as reference values that may vary with changes in …

title: Can Word-of-Mouth Translate into Box Office Revenue? — An Analysis of the Factors Influencing the Impact of Online Ratings on Movie Box Office Performance
abstract: Online ratings and word-of-mouth play an important role in the film market. This paper uses the literature analysis method to examine the relationship between online word-of-mouth and box office performance. It focuses on the effects of ratings, review sources, review formats, and emotional content on audience viewing decisions and film commercial performance. It also considers the effects of cultural, market, and platform differences. The results show that online word-of-mouth can influence audience perceptions, attract attention, and affect viewing decisions and box office performance to some extent. Online word-of-mouth is able to change how people see films and can make more audiences notice certain movies in the market. However, ratings and the number of reviews cannot explain commercial performance on their own. Their effects are also influenced by film characteristics, audience preferences, cultural background, market environment, and platform features. These different factors can work together and make the influence of online word-of-mouth become more complicated in various situations. This paper provides a reference for understanding the relationship between online word-of-mouth and film commercial performance.

title: A neuropsychological battery for use in sleep disorders: establishment of normative data and potential clinical thresholds
abstract: Objective Cognitive symptoms, particularly in attention, are a common but under-recognized clinical feature of sleep disorders. This observational study aimed to establish normative benchmarks for cognitive tests assessing neuropsychological constructs of attention, memory, and executive function and derive impairment thresholds for clinical and research applications. Methods A total of 127 cognitively unimpaired adults (age 18–75 years, 54% female) without excessive daytime sleepiness, marked self-reported cognitive difficulties, mood or neurological disorders, or untreated medical conditions affecting cognition completed the Psychomotor Vigilance Test, Sustained Attention to Response Test, Continuous Paired Associate Learning test, One-Back Test, and the International Digit Symbol Substitution Test-Symbols. Associations with demographic characteristics were examined using negative binomial models for count outcomes and Gaussian linear models for continuous outcomes. Primary abnormality thresholds were defined from age-adjusted standardized residuals using empirical 90th, 95th, and 98th percentile criteria in the direction of worse performance. Battery-level false-positive rates were calculated directly from the observed joint distribution of abnormal scores. Results In the healthy adults, increasing age was associated with poorer performance on the Continuous Paired Associate…

title: Overview of the Current Status and Trends in the Revenue Structure of NBA Clubs
abstract: The NBA is the world's top professional basketball league, and its clubs' revenue structure has evolved greatly since its founding. Drawing on materials, data analysis, and comparisons, this paper studies this evolution, divides the NBA's development from 1946 to 2026 into four stages, and compares the revenue systems of the NBA, CBA, and European basketball leagues. The findings show that media development, internal league rules, and global commerce were the main drivers of these changes. Ticket revenue is an important indicator of the quality of professional sports operations, while the centralized sale of TV broadcasting rights uses its monopoly position to secure higher revenue. Analysis of the NBA's latest reforms shows that playoff prize money has continued to rise with league revenue, offering a reference for the CBA's innovative development and revenue distribution. Today, digital media broadcasting rights have become the largest revenue source, while ticket revenue's share has dropped significantly. In the future, the NBA will rely more on streaming rights, deeper global markets, and monetization of digital content. This paper can help the CBA optimize its revenue structure and improve distribution, and it fills gaps in research on stage division and comparisons between Chinese and foreign leagues.

Ag 2 Te interfacial diffusion and phase transition induced built-in electric field evolution for synergistically enhanced thermoelectric performance of Bi 2 Te 2.5 Se 0.5
abstract: Abstract N-type Bi2Te2.5Se0.5 alloys exhibit a severe donor-like effect during powder metallurgy fabrication, which gives rise to excessively carrier concentration and degraded near-room-temperature thermoelectric performance. Suppressing the donor-like effect while preserving high carrier mobility remains a major bottleneck. Herein, Ag2Te/Bi2Te2.5Se0.5 composites are fabricated via mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering. Owing to interfacial diffusion between superionic Ag2Te and the Bi2Te2.5Se0.5 matrix, some Ag atoms occupy dual crystallographic sites by substituting at Bi lattice sites and intercalating into van der Waals gaps, which suppresses the donor-like effect and lowers the carrier concentration. At the phase-transition point of Ag2Te at ~420 K, reversal of the built-in electric field at the heterogeneous-interface enables enhanced carrier mobility below the transition temperature. Total thermal conductivity reduction originates from both decreased carrier thermal conductivity and suppressed lattice thermal conductivity induced by multiscale defects. The AT04 composite delivers a peak ZT of 1.23 at 410 K. At room temperature, the ZT of AT04 is 0.98, corresponding to an 80% enhancement relative to pristine Bi2Te2.5Se0.5 (ZT = 0.54). This work provides new mechanistic insights and an effective strategy for utilizing phase-transition-tunable hetero-interfaces to…

title: RA-MDST: correcting neighborhood redundancy in multi-distance oversampling of autonomous-vehicle crash data
abstract: Background Autonomous vehicle (AV) crash-severity data are small, high-dimensional and imbalanced. The Multi-Distance Synthetic Technique (MDST) generates minority samples from Euclidean and Manhattan nearest-neighbor sets, but the two metrics often select the same neighbors. Methods We propose the Redundancy-Aware MDST (RA-MDST), which takes three Euclidean neighbors and three Manhattan neighbors that exclude them, and generates samples by bounded pairwise interpolation. A type-preserving variant, RA-MDST-TP, keeps binary, categorical, and ordinal variables valid. Methods were evaluated on 324 California AV collision reports with 189 predictors and three severity classes, using a leakage-controlled protocol in which scaling, feature selection and oversampling are fitted inside each training fold (10 × 5-fold cross-validation, 10 classifiers), against random oversampling, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and SMOTE-NC. Results Euclidean and Manhattan top-three neighborhoods overlapped by 76.2% on average, and only 29.3% of MDST synthetic samples were unique. RA-MDST produced 100% unique samples and reduced near-duplicates from 93.5 to 35.7%; RA-MDST-TP produced no invalid values, compared with 17%–24% for interpolation-based methods; type-preserving variants of SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN also produced none and matched RA-MDST-TP in macro-F1, so its predictive gains over M…

title: Environmentally Friendly Structures and Promising Technologies in Hybrid Electric Aircraft
abstract: With the development of aircraft, the demand for energy-efficient and environmentally friendly aircraft is increasing. In this work, environmentally friendly structures and promising technologies in hybrid electric aircraft will be discussed, which include power system, thermal management, weight and structural design, ecology and environment and business model. To deal with the primary limitation----mass, some new components fabricated in composite materials can be considered to for use the body of the aircraft. Also, details such as the battery's model, material, lifespan, safety and endurance will be mentioned in this paper. As a result, carbon emissions and resource consumption are reduced significantly. However, basic infrastructures like maintenance and support measures still need to be improved.

title: Robust insensitivity of heterogeneous charge distribution and interlayer friction to strong external electric fields in twisted graphene bilayers
abstract: Abstract Twisted graphene bilayers exhibit rich physical phenomena under external fields, yet the coupled effect of electric fields and interlayer sliding on their charge distribution remains elusive. By combining first-principles calculations with a machine learning technique, we systematically investigate interlayer sliding-induced charge transfer and redistribution in both twisted and AB-stacked graphene bilayers under vertical electric fields. Unlike the homogeneous charge distribution observed in AB-stacked bilayers, the heterogeneous charge distribution in certain twisted graphene bilayers exhibits robust insensitivity to applied electric fields, even under strong fields up to 2 V/nm. This field insensitivity enables such twisted bilayers to maintain ultralow interlayer friction under extreme bias conditions. To quantitatively describe the coupled effect of interlayer sliding and electric fields on interlayer charge transfer and friction, we develop a charge-modified registry index (RICM) model for graphene bilayers. The revealed electric-field insensitivity in specific twisted configurations can be mainly attributed to the inherently small variation in the maximum registry index change (∆RICM) under bias, providing a simple descriptor for designing low-friction interfaces in electrically gated graphene devices.

title: A stochastic optimization method and its application for typical electric vehicle spare parts
abstract: Abstract Against the background of rapid electrification of the global automotive industry, the scale of electric vehicle ownership continues to expand. The after-sales maintenance spare-parts system faces prominent practical pain-points: high unit component value, low turnover frequency, long and uncertain procurement lead-time, and stochastic spare-parts demand. Historical operational data show that high-voltage battery modules exhibit a 60% stock-out rate and 7.2-day average customer waiting time under conventional management. Traditional empirical inventory strategies relying on historical averages or static safety stock cannot adapt to stochastic fault arrival and supply-chain delay risks, resulting in the structural co-existence of spare-parts shortage and inventory overstock. This paper adopts the Poisson distribution to characterize random low-frequency spare-parts demand, and employs the two-parameter Weibull distribution to model asymmetric long-tail stochastic procurement lead-time. On this basis, a bi-objective stochastic simulation-embedded optimization model is constructed, minimizing expected total cost and maximizing composite service level. Multiple practical constraints are integrated, including warehouse capacity upper bound, total budget limit, minimum service-level requirement, and lead-time probabilistic coverage constraint. Verified by historical operatio…

title: A CFD-based parameterization approach for correcting vehicle-mounted three-dimensional instantaneous wind measurements
abstract: Near-surface three-dimensional (3-D) wind vectors are essential meteorological variables in atmospheric boundary layer research and environmental monitoring. Vehicle-mounted mobile wind measurement platforms enable observations of near-surface wind fields with high spatial resolutions over relatively large spatial domains. However, vehicle-induced flow distortion, platform motion, and attitude variations introduce substantial interference into vehicle-mounted wind measurements, resulting in systematic biases in the measured wind vectors relative to the true ambient wind field. To obtain accurate 3-D wind measurements, this study proposes and validates a vehicle-mounted instantaneous wind correction method based on a CFD-derived parameterization scheme. A set of parameterized CFD simulations is conducted within a unified computational domain under multiple wind speeds and directions to establish a mapping between the true inflow wind and the flow-distorted wind measured by a vehicle-mounted anemometer. The correction framework further accounts for the effects of vehicle attitude variations and vehicle translation. Based on field validation experiments, under headwind conditions, the overall mean bias error (MBE) of horizontal wind speed decreased from 0.31 to 0.09 m s −1 (approximately 72 %), while the MBE of vertical wind speed changed from 0.82 to −0.26 m s −1 , corresponding …

title: Episode calibrated thermal residual monitoring for battery fast charging protection
abstract: Temperature-sensor faults can delay protective current reduction during battery fast charging, while unnecessary alarms reduce charge delivery. This study evaluates whole-episode calibration of thermal residual monitors in a reproducible Python simulation. A two-node virtual cell represents a 50 A h battery during a 1200s charging opportunity. Training, calibration, and testing use separate virtual cells. Raw, mean-centered, linear, and quadratic predictors are compared with an identified physical model, repeated calibration draws, alternative fallback policies, and independent parameter shifts. In the original nominal test, quadratic correction achieved a healthy filtered residual root mean square error of 0.396 °C. An identified physical predictor achieved 0.441 °C, with a gradual-bias detection delay of 73.61 s compared with 67.44 s for the original quadratic monitor. Across 20 independent training and calibration repetitions, quadratic healthy-episode alarms averaged 4.84% and ranged from 3.00% to 7.50%. Under simultaneous negative sensor bias and cooling loss, a prediction-independent 75 A fallback increased mean delivered charge from 22.960 to 33.049 A h relative to a 25 A cap, with zero observed 45 °C exceedances in both 400-cell comparisons. Under the combined parameter shift, recalibration reduced the healthy-episode false-alarm rate from 100% (400/400) to 4.75% (19/40…

title: AHO-deep BiLSTM: optimized deep learning model for maximum power generation in solar maximum power point tracking system
abstract: Abstract In renewable energy resources (RESs), Photovoltaic (PV) generation is considered as the main aspect for power generation, due to its inexhaustible supply and significant health and economic benefits. However, absolute temperature, solar irradiance, photovoltaic factors and climatic conditions reduce the maximum power extraction process and lead to degraded system reliability performance. Hence, handling of Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) is mandatory to extract high power, match impedance, and protect batteries significantly. Therefore, the research work employs the Aggressive Hunting Optimization-based Deep Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (AHO-Deep BiLSTM) technique to track the MPP and predict the switching conditions to adjust the switching matrix of the reconfigurable PV array. Additionally, the Single-Ended Primary Inductor Converter (SEPIC)/ZETA converter offers continuous input voltage and current, and mitigates the harmonic ripples and distortion, thereby reducing the power losses. The developed AHO algorithm ensures the optimal tuning of MPPT parameters to extract maximum power. Specifically, the AHO-Deep BiLSTM model exhibits the power, current and voltage values of 2,622.70 W, 96.81 A and 27.09 V in parallel connection, and also outperforms the voltage, current and power values of 152.08 V, 51.28 A, and 7,798.34 W attained under shading conditions. …

title: Polydopamine-Mediated Hierarchical Assembly Strategy for Multifunctional Poly(dimethylsiloxane) Composite Films
abstract: Abstract The development of flexible multifunctional materials capable of simultaneously providing thermal dissipation, electromagnetic interference (EMI) attenuation, and mechanical robustness remains highly challenging for advanced electronic applications. Herein, polydopamine (PDA)-assisted hierarchical assembly of MXene-Joule-heated nanocarbon (JHNC) nanohybrids (PMJC) is proposed to fabricate multifunctional composite films (PPC) based on poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) to meet the aforementioned requirements. The results showed that PDA-mediated hydrogen bonding, coordination interactions, and π–π stacking facilitate the layered assembly of JHNC and MXene. Strong interfacial adhesion between PMJC and PDMS was established through physical adsorption, van der Waals forces (VDW), and mechanical interlocking. The interconnected PMJC network enabled efficient stress transfer and continuous electrically and thermally conductive pathways, thereby enhancing the mechanical properties, EMI shielding effectiveness, and thermal conductivity of the PPC. The optimized PPC containing 0.5 g JHNC, 0.5 g MXene, and 5 g PDMS delivered a tensile strength of 1.57 MPa, a tensile modulus of 2.52 MPa, an elongation at break of 46.69%, an EMI shielding effectiveness of 35.95 dB, in-plane and out-of-plane thermal conductivities of 0.322 W·m–1·K–1 and 0.120 W·m–1·K–1. This study provides an effective…

Digital strategy-driven supply chain resilience for enhancing competitive advantage: a deep-learning-based dual-stage PLS-SEM-ANN analysis
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how digital strategies enhance firms' competitive advantage by improving supply chain (SC) resilience. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in the dynamic resource-based view, this research conceptualizes digital strategy as a mechanism for strengthening a firm's capabilities in digital products and services. SC resilience is defined as the capability to respond effectively and recover rapidly from disruptions. The study employs partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and artificial neural networks (ANNs) to investigate the relationships among digital strategy, SC resilience, and competitive advantage. Findings The PLS-SEM results show that SC resilience partially mediates the relationship between digital strategy and competitive advantage. Specifically, SC responsiveness and SC recovery transmit the effect of digital strategy on competitive advantage, whereas SC readiness contributes indirectly by strengthening subsequent resilience capabilities. The ANN results broadly corroborate these relationships and provide a modest complementary predictive perspective, with the clearest incremental insight observed in Model C, where SC readiness emerged as especially important for SC recovery. Originality/value This study extends the theoretical scope of the dynamic resource-based view by integrating digital strategy with SC resilienc…

title: Business Development Strategy Of Opak Cikuda In Setiawargi Village, Tamansari District, Tasikmalaya City
abstract: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play an important role in supporting economic growth, although they continue to face various challenges in their development. One MSME with considerable potential is Opak Cikuda, located in Setiawargi Village, Tamansari District, Tasikmalaya City. This study aims to analyze the internal and external factors influencing business development and to formulate an appropriate development strategy using the Internal Factors Analysis Summary (IFAS), External Factors Analysis Summary (EFAS), Internal–External (IE) Matrix, SWOT analysis, and the Quantitative Strategic Planning Matrix (QSPM). A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, with data collected through observations, interviews, documentation, and questionnaires involving ten respondents selected through purposive sampling. The findings show that Opak Cikuda achieved an IFAS score of 3.28 and an EFAS score of 3.20, placing the business in Cell I (Grow and Build) of the IE Matrix, which indicates strong potential for growth. SWOT analysis generated several strategic alternatives, while the QSPM identified the Strength–Opportunity (SO) strategy as the highest priority, with a Total Attractiveness Score (TAS) of 2.91. This strategy emphasizes leveraging product quality and uniqueness, strengthening digital marketing, improving production technology, and maintaining competitive pric…

title: From strategy to performance: how green supply chain management practices and intellectual capital enhance sustainability outcomes
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how environmental orientation (EO) enhances sustainability performance (SP) in manufacturing firms by integrating the roles of green supply chain management (GSCM) practices and green intellectual capital (GIC). It aims to reveal the synergistic effects of strategic orientation, operational practices and knowledge resources. Design/methodology/approach A conceptual framework was developed and tested using survey data collected from 386 middle and senior managers of manufacturing firms in Jiangxi Province, China. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was applied to assess the direct, mediating and moderating effects among EO, GSCM practices, GIC and SP. Findings The results indicate that EO and GSCM practices have significant positive effects on SP. In addition, GSCM practices mediate the relationship between EO and SP. Furthermore, GIC moderates the effects of both EO and GSCM practices on SP. Research limitations/implications This study provides practical implications for managers in enhancing SP by aligning EO with GSCM practices and leveraging GIC. However, the findings are based on data from a specific manufacturing context, which may limit generalisability. Future research could extend the model across different industries, regions and institutional environments to enhance external validity. Originality/value This stu…

title: Research on Optimization Strategy of Enterprise Cost Management under Digital Transformation
abstract: With the rapid iteration of big data, machine learning, and generative artificial intelligence technologies, traditional enterprise management models, which rely on manual experience, hierarchical supervision, and static data analysis, are gradually unable to adapt to the dynamic, personalized, and high-efficiency market competition environment. AI technology, with its advantages of autonomous learning, intelligent prediction, high-speed computing, and scenario-based decision-making, comprehensively penetrates enterprise organizational management, human resource management, financial management, operational management, and strategic management. It fundamentally optimizes enterprise resource allocation, improves operational efficiency, and promotes the innovative upgrading of management logic. However, while AI empowers enterprise management, it also creates practical challenges, including pressure for organizational restructuring, mismatches in employee competencies, data security risks, and ethical dilemmas in management. Drawing on authoritative research in China and abroad as well as enterprise digital transformation case studies, this paper systematically analyzes the positive impact of AI on modern enterprise management, sorts out the key difficulties in the current intelligent management transformation process, and proposes targeted optimization strategies. title: “Paths Projections” of International Power Rivalries: Bringing Process‐Tracing to Scenario‐Building
abstract: ABSTRACT We propose a new method of foresight that is theoretically grounded, analytically robust, and practically actionable. We argue that qualitative foresight can be advanced by bringing process‐tracing to scenario‐building. The resulting “paths projections” approach reinforces the strengths of existing IR theory–based foresight and applied scenario‐building, while addressing their respective weaknesses. Paths projections are conditional, process‐centered scenarios—modeled as theoretically informed causal mechanisms—that enable continuous assessment and updating of evolving international developments to inform political intervention. In this article, we introduce our paths projections approach and provide detailed step‐by‐step guidance on how to construct paths projections. We illustrate the approach with brief applications to US–China geopolitical rivalries, including both security rivalries over Taiwan and economic competition over interbank telecommunications. We thereby demonstrate the practical utility and analytical potential of the paths projections approach across “traditional” and “new” types of power rivalries.

title: Comparative Study of Controllers Using Grey Wolf Optimisation and Genetic Algorithm for Power Stabilization of Hybrid Nano Grid System
abstract: Our country, Pakistan, is now coping with several challenges. Electric power is one of them. Therefore, it is necessary to provide these resources to address power problems. To continuously supply electricity to a load, a hybrid nano grid integrates renewable and non-renewable energy sources in an eco-friendly, self-sufficient manner. The rising complexity of the power system necessitates the design of an appropriate controller. This work introduces various controllers, such as Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID), Fractional-Order Proportional-Integral-Derivative (FOPID) and Sliding Mode Control (SMC), to minimize power oscillations caused by generation sources and load disturbances and maintain the stability of the nano-grid system. The Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) and genetic algorithm (GA) techniques are used to determine the PID, FOPID, and SMC controllers’ optimal gains using MATLAB software. The integral square error serves as the objective function in both optimization techniques. In terms of power stability, SMC has done better than any other optimized controller. When applied to every controller, the GWO method has proven to be more effective than the Genetic Algorithm (GA) technique.

title: Immersive technologies and the mindful luxury experience: examining how augmented reality transforms fashion retail services for sustainable consumption
abstract: Purpose Drawing upon transformative service research (TSR) principles, this study aims to examine how augmented reality (AR) influences sustainable consumption behavior within luxury cosmetics retail services to enhance customer well-being. It explores whether AR-enabled service encounters can simultaneously encourage sustainable luxury consumption while mitigating impulsive buying through environmental knowledge. Design/methodology/approach This study employs a quantitative survey design using two independent samples of Chinese female retail customers (n = 341, n = 368) and the data has been analyzed through structural equation modeling. Findings Empirical findings have shown that a good AR service experience can lead to increased immersion, enjoyment and satisfaction, driving sustainable consumption of luxury. Nonetheless, first-time AR users exhibit stronger impulsive buying tendencies and thus the authors see a contradiction between experiential stimulation and responsible consumption. However, transparent and informative AR experiences may mitigate this risk. Practical implications Applying TSR principles, retail services should be redesigned based on AR services emphasizing information transparency, sustainability cues and customer delight to promote responsible consumption while limiting impulse-driven overuse. Originality/value This study contributes to Sustainable Deve…

title: Trading immediacy for control: consumer acceptance of deterministic delayed delivery in instant retail
abstract: Purpose This study investigated the psychological mechanisms behind consumer acceptance of deterministic delayed delivery in instant retail, moving beyond the conventional speed-price paradigm. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in expectation confirmation theory (ECT) and transaction utility theory, a first-stage moderated serial mediation model was proposed and tested using a scenario-based survey (398 valid responses) simulating peak-hour instant retail decisions, with partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and bias-corrected bootstrapping analyses. Findings The PLS-SEM results indicated significant associations among platform-related evaluations, perceived quality, expected confirmation degree, satisfaction with performance commitments, and self-reported willingness to choose deterministic delayed delivery. Price sensitivity positively moderated the association between the expectant effect and perceived quality. The findings suggest that, within the simulated decision context, consumers' stated willingness to accept delayed delivery was associated with perceived control, delivery certainty, and compensatory value. Originality/value This research extends ECT to online-to-offline (O2O) fulfillment, enriches transaction utility theory in micro-contract exchanges, and offers novel insights into delayed service design.

title: Repetition, Weighting, and the Pricing of Technical Event Risk: Evidence from Commercial Space Options
abstract: A failed space mission can wipe out much of the issuer's market value within two trading days. After removing independent news, the absolute abnormal return is 13.2% for failures and 5.9% for successes. Pre-mission implied volatility, or AIV, uses days (-10, -1) for the disclosure screen and (0, +1) for the actual stock reaction. Missions of the same issuer within 20 trading days is treated separately. Under the AIV-aligned screen, the standardized task-weighted AIV is +0.040, and an independent reconstruction with a maximum δ error of 0.10 gives +0.028. Across four issuers, the smallest exact sign p-value is 0.125, and no main test family passes the Holm correction. Schedule-verified non-overlapping missions show a higher premium, +0.123 standardized and +0.188 raw, but this fades under the disclosure screen. The evidence support a conditional, not universal, pre-mission pricing mechanism. Launch cycles and overlaps matter.

title: Big 4 office agglomeration and asymmetric pricing dynamics in local audit markets
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how the geographic agglomeration of Big 4 audit offices within metropolitan areas influences audit pricing across auditor tiers. The authors conceptualize Big 4 agglomeration, measured as the ratio of Big 4 to total audit offices within a market, as a spatial dimension of audit market structure that captures both competitive intensity and knowledge spillovers. The study investigates whether this agglomeration affects audit fees differently for clients of Big 4 and non-Big 4 auditors. Design/methodology/approach Using US public company data from 2004 to 2017, the authors estimate audit fee regressions incorporating a measure of Big 4 office agglomeration within each metropolitan statistical area. The analysis distinguishes between Big 4 and non-Big 4 clients, includes extensive controls and uses entropy balancing to assess the robustness of the findings. Additional analyses examine changes in Big 4 office agglomeration, exclude the financial crisis period and consider alternative geographic market definitions to assess the sensitivity of the results. The authors also interact Big 4 office agglomeration with spatial market-share distance measures to explore the mechanisms underlying the asymmetric pricing effects. Findings The authors find that greater Big 4 agglomeration is associated with lower audit fees for Big 4 clients but higher fees for …

title: Efficiency Comparison and Interaction Effects of Variance Reduction Methods in Monte Carlo Option Pricing: An Empirical Analysis Based on SHFE Copper Options
abstract: Monte Carlo (MC) simulation is a core numerical method for pricing financial derivatives, but its slow convergence can impose substantial computational costs when high precision is required. Variance reduction techniques, including antithetic variates (AV), control variates (CV), and quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC), have therefore been developed to improve computational efficiency. But these methods have been mainly analyzed individually or in simple combination in previous studies. It is not clear whether QMC and CV have complementary, overlapping or offsetting effects, especially in the Chinese commodity options. This paper systematically compares the standard MC, AV, CV, QMC and QMC+CV for pricing European and arithmetic-average Asian options by using the copper options traded on the Shanghai Futures Exchange. The variance reduction ratio, root mean squared error, and computation time are used to evaluate performance. The results indicate that QMC is much faster than MC and AV when pricing low dimensional European options while CV provides maximum variance reduction for Asian options. The efficiency gain due to QMC+CV is not just the sum of the two constituent methods: the interaction is positive at small numbers of time steps, but decreases and could be negative at high numbers of time steps. This research changes the debate from which is the best method to the interaction between …

Subjective expectations in asset pricing and household finance: evidence from inflation, trading, and wealth effects
abstract: Abstract Expectations are central objects in asset pricing and household finance. Asset prices depend on beliefs about future cash flows an​d discount rates, while portfolios, debt choices, and spending depend on subjective beliefs about returns, inflation, income, and interest rates. Yet finance and macroeconomics long studied these decisions without observing the beliefs of the agents making them. This article summarizes an age​nda that puts subjective expectations at the center of empirical finance. I first discuss why survey-based expectations are informative economic objects and how inflation expectations are formed. I then show why expectations are especially relevant during inflationary periods, when investors must assess real payoffs, nominal contracts, monetary policy, and valuation effects. The article focuses on evidence from linked surveys, experiments, and administrative financial records, showing that beliefs are heterogeneous, move with information and mental models, and affect trading, spending, debt, and portfolio choices in high-stakes real-world financial decisions.

title: Optimal dynamic pricing under authentic promotion and greenwashing in green consumer markets with endogenous environmental awareness
abstract: Abstract This paper studies firms’ dynamic pricing and marketing decisions under authentic promotion and greenwashing strategies in green consumer markets. Building on the Bass diffusion model, we develop a continuous-time optimal control model in which cumulative sales and market environmental awareness serve as state variables and price and green marketing effort serve as control variables, incorporating positive and negative word of mouth (WOM), a state-dependent perceived gain from greenwashing, and an expected penalty cost generated by external detection. The analytical results show that rising environmental awareness weakens the direct sales stimulus of greenwashing, whereas stronger negative WOM suppresses the subsequent diffusion of greenwashed products. The numerical results indicate that greenwashing may stimulate sales in the early market stage, but authentic promotion generally favors cumulative sales and awareness accumulation over longer horizons; even with lower sales, greenwashing can still extract private profit through higher prices. Short product lifecycles, slow market learning, low detection coverage, and weak penalties enlarge the profitable region of greenwashing, whereas jointly raising detection coverage and the unit penalty compresses it. Customized GenAI tutors in education: complexity, human interaction, and learning value
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how learning value and usage intentions emerge in artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled educational services when generative AI (GenAI) tutors are customized for specific pedagogical roles. Drawing on a service-dominant logic perspective, it investigates how perceived topic complexity and learners’ need for human interaction shape learning outcomes, value creation and continued usage intentions. Design/methodology/approach Two field studies are conducted, with customization operationalized as an ex-ante pedagogical role configuration. Study 1, a hybrid professor-supported course, uses thematic analysis guided by Bloom’s Taxonomy to examine perceptions of a customized GPT-based tutor. Study 2, a fully autonomous online module, applies pre/post-tests and moderated mediation analysis. Findings GenAI tutors configured for lower-order cognitive support (memorization and comprehension) are perceived as valuable. However, effectiveness depends on contextual conditions. In fully AI-mediated learning, perceived topic complexity negatively affects memorization, comprehension and perceived value. Under higher topic complexity, learners with stronger needs for human interaction perceive greater pedagogical value in the GenAI tutor. Continued usage intentions are driven by comprehension and perceived value rather than memorization. Practical implications Fi…

title: Penerapan Model Problem Based Learning dalam Meningkatkan Hasil Belajar Siswa pada Mata Pelajaran Matematika di Kelas V SD
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan penerapan model Problem Based Learning (PBL) dalam meningkatkan hasil belajar Matematika siswa kelas V SD Katolik Pangolombian pada materi penjumlahan pecahan. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) yang dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus. Setiap siklus terdiri atas tahap perencanaan, pelaksanaan tindakan, observasi, dan refleksi. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 15 siswa, yang terdiri atas 11 siswa laki-laki dan 4 siswa perempuan. Teknik pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui tes hasil belajar dan lembar observasi, sedangkan analisis data menggunakan analisis ketuntasan belajar secara klasikal. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penerapan model Problem Based Learning (PBL) mampu meningkatkan hasil belajar Matematika siswa. Persentase ketuntasan belajar pada siklus I mencapai 73% dan meningkat menjadi 90% pada siklus II. Peningkatan tersebut menunjukkan bahwa penerapan model Problem Based Learning (PBL) tidak hanya meningkatkan hasil belajar siswa, tetapi juga mendorong keaktifan siswa dalam mengikuti proses pembelajaran. Dengan demikian, dapat disimpulkan bahwa model Problem Based Learning (PBL) efektif diterapkan untuk meningkatkan hasil belajar Matematika siswa kelas V SD Katolik Pangolombian pada materi penjumlahan pecahan.

THE EFFECT OF THE DEEP LEARNING APPROACH ON STUDENTS' CRITICAL THINKING AND PROBLEM-SOLVING SKILLS IN MATHEMATICS SUBJECTS AMONG FIFTH-GRADE STUDENTS OF PUBLIC ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS IN PRAYA TENGAH DISTRICT
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of the deep learning approach on students’ critical thinking and problem-solving skills in Grade V mathematics at public elementary schools in Praya Tengah District. Specifically, the investigation examines the partial effect of the deep learning approach on critical thinking skills, its partial effect on problem-solving skills, and its simultaneous effect on both cognitive skills. The study employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental method using a nonequivalent control group design involving 114 Grade V students divided into experimental and control groups. The experimental group received instruction using the deep learning approach while the control group received conventional instruction, with data collected through critical thinking and problem-solving tests and analyzed using independent-samples t-tests and multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) via IBM SPSS Statistics. The results demonstrate that the deep learning approach exerts a significant partial effect on critical thinking skills (F=65.340,p<0.001) and problem-solving skills (F=58.236,p<0.001), as well as a significant simultaneous effect on both skills (Wilks’ lambda = 0.496, F=56.485,p<0.001). title: Perceived difficulty determines motor learning during postural control tasks with auditory feedback
abstract: Background Postural control is fundamental for everyday motor activities. However, the impact of perceived difficulty levels in postural control learning is poorly understood. This study aims to examine the effects of perceived difficulty on motor learning performance during static postural control training with auditory feedback in inactive adults. Methods Thirty-two subjects participated in the study and were randomly assigned to control (no feedback), easy, medium, or hard difficulty groups. A mobile application was developed to provide auditory feedback, signaling when postural corrections were necessary if the subjects exceeded a training threshold based on the rate of change of acceleration (jerk). Participants completed seven training sessions and one retention session 24 hours apart. The error was quantified as the number of times outside the threshold while receiving auditory feedback. A significant decrease in error and jerk indicated meaningful motor learning. Results Between the first day of training and the retention day, significant differences were only observed in the medium difficulty group in error (the number of times out of threshold reduced by 91.97%) and improvement of postural control as assessed by jerk (reduced by 31.75%). title: Coding Confidence Boosted: How Micro:bit Training Transforms Motivation and Programming Attitudes among Future Teachers
abstract: Abstract The dynamic development of educational digital technologies (edtech) requires contemporary teachers to have competences that go beyond traditional pedagogical training. The ability to programme and consciously use edtech in teaching activities is becoming particularly important in contemporary education. This poses serious challenges in the preparation of teaching staff in the context of the modernisation of education programmes. The aim of the study was to determine the level of acceptance of edtech and to identify the factors determining the readiness to use the Micro:bit environment in the education of future teachers, with particular emphasis on changes in attitudes towards digital competences in the field of programming. The study involved students of pedagogy from Poland (2025) who completed a 20-h programming course in the MakeCode and Micro:bit environments. The implementation used a pre-test/post-test procedure with a questionnaire covering six scales: perceived usefulness, ease of use, control of edtech, motivation, social acceptance of edtech, perceived barriers to edtech implementation, and attitudes towards programming. The results indicated that perceived subjective barriers significantly reduce the perceived ease of use of edtech. title: PENGARUH MODEL PROBLEM-BASED LEARNING DAN KEARIFAN LOKAL TERHADAP KESADARAN SOSIAL PADA SISWA KELAS V
abstract: This study was motivated by the need to improve students’ social awareness in Social Studies learning, particularly in terms of caring for peers, cooperation, responsibility, and the ability to understand social and environmental issues. The application of local wisdom values related to mutual cooperation, caring, and environmental responsibility also remains suboptimal. This study aimed to analyze the effect of the Problem-Based Learning model on students’ social awareness and examine differences in social awareness based on high and low levels of local wisdom. A quantitative approach was employed using a quasi-experimental method with a 2 × 2 factorial design. The research subjects were 45 fifth-grade students at SDN 05 Lembah Melintang. The experimental class received instruction using the Problem-Based Learning model, while the control class received conventional instruction. Data were collected using social awareness and local wisdom questionnaires and analyzed using two-way ANOVA and independent-samples t-tests. The results showed that the mean social awareness score of the experimental group was 91.65, higher than that of the control group, which was 69.55. The two-way ANOVA results indicated that the Problem-Based Learning model had a significant effect on students’ social awareness (F = 11.199; p = 0.002), with a partial eta squared value of 0.215. title: Examining the Effect of GeoGebra-Supported Teaching on Conceptual Learning of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
abstract: Research shows that students have conceptual difficulties with the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (FTC). This study aims to examine the effect of GeoGebra-supported teaching on conceptual understanding of the FTC. A mixed-method approach was utilized, employing experimental design with a pretest-posttest control group for the quantitative part and students’ written opinions about the process analyzed for the qualitative part. The study involved 35 (experimental group = 21 and control group = 14) second-year mathematics and computer science department students from a state university in Türkiye. Data was collected with a conceptual test consisting of open-ended questions and an opinion form. In the experimental group, GeoGebra was used exclusively through lecturer-led demonstrations, and in the control group, conventional teaching methods were used. Quantitative results indicated significant improvements in conceptual understanding of the theorem for the experimental group. However, the difference in posttest scores between the two groups was not statistically significant. In contrast, qualitative findings showed that the experimental group strongly endorsed GeoGebra's dynamic and visual features as beneficial for enhancing conceptual learning. title: Development and validation of machine learning models for predicting extrauterine growth restriction in preterm infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia born at <32 weeks of gestation
abstract: Objective To develop and validate machine learning (ML) models that use data available on postnatal day 28 to predict extrauterine growth restriction (EUGR) at 36 weeks’ postmenstrual age (PMA) in infants born at <32 weeks of gestation who survived to 36 weeks’ PMA and were diagnosed with bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD). Methods We retrospective included preterm infants with BPD (2018 NICHD criteria) admitted to the two campuses of Shanghai First Maternity and Infant Hospital in 2015–2025. East Campus infants ( n = 420) were randomly divided 7:3 into a training set ( n = 294) and an internal validation set ( n = 126); West Campus infants ( n = 108) formed a cross-campus validation set. LASSO selected predictors from 12 candidates, and 7 ML models were developed and compared with logistic regression (LR) and growth-only benchmarks. We evaluated discrimination, calibration, and net benefit were and interpreted selected model with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results EUGR occurred in 52.4% of the development cohort. LASSO selected 8 predictors: birth weight, small for gestational age (SGA), invasive mechanical ventilation ≥7 days, weight gain velocity, feeding intolerance, enteral feeding initiated within 24 h, fluid intake reaching 150 mL/(kg·d) by 1 week, and exclusive breast milk feeding. Two-Stage Machine Learning-Assisted Multiplex Catecholamine Quantification in Artificial Urine on a Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Paper
abstract: Abstract Catecholamines, including dopamine, epinephrine, and norepinephrine, are important biomarkers of neurological and neuroendocrine disorders. However, their simultaneous quantification in body fluids remains challenging because of their similar molecular structures, which produce highly overlapping Raman spectroscopic signatures. Here, we develop an integrated platform combining an iron-nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA-Fe)-functionalized surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) paper with a two-stage machine learning pipeline for catecholamine quantification in artificial urine. The SERS paper enables rapid drop-and-measure detection, achieving limits of detection of 7.18, 9.01, and 6.80 μM for dopamine, epinephrine, and norepinephrine in artificial urine, respectively. For samples with unknown compositions, the pipeline first classifies the catecholamines present (92.19% group-level accuracy) and then quantifies single-component samples via intensity-ratio calibration and mixtures via trained partial least squares regression models (global root-mean-square error: 2.27 μM). This work establishes a functionalized SERS paper platform coupled with machine learning as a proof of concept for the identification and quantitative analysis of structurally similar metabolites in complex mixtures.

Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is the mainstream technology to improve the mathematical reasoning ability of large language models, but evaluation protocols across papers are not unified, and low-sampling and high-sampling pass@k metrics often yield inconsistent conclusions, and there is a lack of systematic review of the evaluation practice. Focusing on the core issue of evaluation completeness, this paper systematically combs three RLVR technical routes: outcome supervision, process supervision, and verifier-free, analyzes the principles of representative algorithms, summarizes the experimental results of public papers, and designs a structured coding scheme covering 9 fields. The 9 representative papers are coded one by one from the aspects of technical route, base model, sampling scale, and training configuration. Statistics show that the current RLVR field is deeply in the dilemma of fragmentation of evaluation protocols: the caliber of evaluation indicators is incompatible with each other, high-sampling evaluation data are scarce, and there are obvious differences on whether low sampling can expand the reasoning boundary. The disclosure of key hyperparameters such as temperature and KL coefficient is scattered and unsystematic, and the horizontal comparison lacks a common foundation. title: Embedded Sensing and Machine Learning-Based Interactive Experience Evaluation of Contemporary Jewelry from a Wearable Art Perspective
abstract: Wearable computers and embedded interaction systems have changed contemporary jewelry into interactive systems that can sense users' actions and provide them with a feedback. In this research, a computational analysis system is designed by combining embedded interaction system for touch sensing, wireless sensor network for data collection, and machine learning to study interactive experiences in contemporary jewelry from wearable art point of view. An interactive brooch based on ESP32 microcontroller board with embedded touch sensing by MPR121, feedback provided by RGB LED, and wireless communication by Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) is proposed. In order to implement interactive actions in this prototype and collect behavior data related to task completion time, touch frequency, response latency, and error rate, a within-subject experiment with 48 participants is conducted to compare static brooch with interactive one in terms of usability, immersion, emotional expression, and wearing comfort. Random forest classification model with 300 decision trees is trained to classify high immersion and low immersion cases according to collected behavioral and experience features with five-fold cross validation. title: Deep feature extraction approach for enhancing global NO2 low-cost sensor calibration models
abstract: Abstract Accurate monitoring of air pollution is essential for developing effective mitigation strategies. While traditional monitoring methods have limitations, high-density low-cost sensor networks provide a promising alternative. However, concerns about their accuracy and stability remain. Machine learning offers strong potential to improve calibration, enhancing reliability while reducing costs. In this study, we present a deep-feature extraction approach to enhance machine-learning-based global calibration models for NO 2 low-cost sensors. Our method extends existing frameworks by leveraging a CNN-LSTM architecture for automatic feature extraction. Activation maps (AMs) from the one-dimensional CNN layers capture key patterns in sensor behavior and environmental variability. These features are then pruned using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to reduce redundancy and retain the most informative components. The selected features are combined with the original inputs to train the calibration models, aiming to improve model accuracy and generalization across diverse conditions. We evaluated the method using datasets from Switzerland and the USA. Results demonstrate noticeable improvements over baseline models. For example, the root mean square error (RMSE) decreased by an average of 7% ± 3% for the Switzerland dataset and 10% ± 4% for the USA (ElCajon) dataset. This study …

Uni-nullnorms and Null-uninorms on bounded trellises
abstract: In 2024, L. Zedam et al. pointed out that the meet operation is not a t-norm on a proper bounded trellis. This finding highlights the differences between aggregation operators on bounded trellises and those on bounded lattices, thereby inspiring our research into aggregation functions on bounded trellises. In this paper, uni-nullnorms and null-uninorms of the bounded trellises are first defined. Then, uni-nullnorms and null-uninorms on bounded trellises are constructed by employing interior and closure operators, along with t-(sub)norms and t-(super)conorms. Especially, if [Formula: see text] (resp. [Formula: see text]), a new method of constructing uninorms (resp. nullnorms) on bounded trellises is obtained. Differences between our work and existing literature are also illustrated through comparative examples. Additionally, new methods for constructing nullnorms and uninorms on bounded lattices are naturally presented.

title: Uncertain Performance: How to Quantify Uncertainty and Draw Test Sets When Evaluating Classifiers
abstract: Abstract Supervised machine learning has become increasingly popular in social science research, often employing classifiers to measure political constructs. Although evaluating classifiers on a test set is critical for establishing their validity, guidance on how to conduct such evaluation is limited. In particular, researchers have paid insufficient attention to the variance of performance metrics estimated on test sets. This article demonstrates that typically sized test sets yield highly noisy and often uninformative estimates of classifier performance, particularly for imbalanced tasks—common in social science applications like identifying hateful or emotional speech—where one outcome class is rare. To address this issue, this article introduces methods to quantify uncertainty in performance estimates based on their sampling distribution and validated with simulations. It also introduces a design-based approach in political science to enhance statistical precision when evaluating classifiers: efficient stratified sampling based on the outcome’s predicted probability. Simulations using synthetic and real data show that this strategy meaningfully reduces the variance of performance estimates, especially in imbalanced tasks, while ensuring that they remain consistent. Finally, the article illustrates how to calculate the test set size required to achieve a desired level of st…

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Error-Gated $$\sigma $$-Modification Adaptive Control for Cascade Missile Longitudinal Autopilots Under Aerodynamic Uncertainty
abstract: Abstract An error-gated $$\sigma $$ σ -modification adaptive law is proposed for the inner loop of a cascade feedback-linearized missile longitudinal autopilot. A Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) policy jointly schedules the adaptation gain and the leakage coefficient of the disturbance estimator, while a smooth error gate activates the $$\sigma $$ σ -modification only when the filtered tracking error is large, so that the law behaves as a pure integral estimator near equilibrium and as a $$\sigma $$ σ -modified law during onset transients. A projection on the estimate combined with the bounded scheduled coefficients gives uniform ultimate boundedness of the inner-loop error under a bounded disturbance, with no required bound on the policy output rate. Simulation studies separate mechanism validation from controller positioning through constant-disturbance, disturbance-transition, ablation, Monte Carlo, and flight-envelope stress-grid tests. Within the adaptive-controller family, the proposed law reduces the mean integral of time-weighted absolute pitch-rate error and the fin-command total variation relative to a fixed gated adaptive baseline. Against a nonlinear disturbance observer (NDO), time-delay control (TDC), sliding mode control (SMC), and $$\mathcal {L}_1$$ L 1 adaptive control, it occupies a competitive Pareto position with strong pitch-rate recovery and smooth command activit…
venue: International Journal of Control, Automation, and Systems

title: Some Methods to Construct Uninorms on Bounded Lattices by Closure Operators or (and) Interior Operators
abstract: The main objective of this article is to propose novel constructions of uninorms on bounded lattices by closure operators or (and) interior operators. Firstly, new constructions of uninorms on bounded lattices via three closure operators are presented. Secondly, new constructions of uninorms on bounded lattices via three interior operators are proposed. This work establishes the conditions for a binary operation to be a uninorm on bounded lattices. We compare the generalized structures presented in this paper with the existing ones and provide some examples to highlight the differences. Finally, additional new constructions of uninorms on bounded lattices are proposed based on closure operators and interior operators.
