title: Monetary policy, uncertainty and the dynamics of bank credit risk in a bank-dependent frontier economy
abstract: Purpose The research examines how changes in the policy rate and monetary-policy uncertainty are associated with the credit risk of commercial banks in Vietnam, a bank-dependent frontier economy. Design/methodology/approach A balanced quarterly panel of 27 banks over 2018Q1–2024Q4 is combined with the State Bank of Vietnam refinancing rate and a news-based index of monetary-policy uncertainty. Bank fixed-effects models and panel local projections are estimated with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and wild cluster bootstrap inference. The analysis examines loan-restructuring programmes, the direction of rate changes and the central bank's reaction to domestic and external conditions. Findings Policy-rate changes are positively associated with non-performing-loan (NPL) ratios with a delay. The association appears in the second quarter at 0.35 percentage points per percentage point of rate change and rises to 0.45 percentage points after five quarters. At longer horizons, it is associated mainly with the 2019–2020 rate cuts, which were followed by lower reported NPL ratios while a loan-restructuring programme was in force. The response is similar for weakly and well-capitalised banks. Monetary-policy uncertainty is associated with higher NPL ratios on impact, in a period when uncertainty and banking stress rose together. Research limitations/implications The policy variables are ag…

title: Digital Twin Modeling for Wholesale Telecom Infrastructure Optimization
abstract: Wholesale telecom carriers provide capacity and voice termination services to other operators; they work with tight margins and service-level commitments; mistakes in capacity planning or routing may cost dearly. This paper develops a digital twin of a wholesale carrier network with a topology and routing model, traffic matrix forecast trained on telemetry data, a failure model, and a commercial model of rates and route costs. The twin is used for what-if analysis and optimization. On 120 backbone and interconnect links, the twin makes 24-hour link utilization forecasts with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 9.7%, compared with 16.2% of seasonal naive (p < 0.001) and 11.8% of LSTM alone (p = 0.005). There is a correlation between predicted and observed utilization of r = 0.96 (p < 0.001). During 24 maintenance events, the twin detects congestion with sensitivity 0.889 and specificity 0.867. With the help of the twin, planning achieves reducing monthly congested link-hours from 412 to 143 (p < 0.001), planned capital expenditures are cut down by 22%, and cost of voice routes per 1,000 minutes is reduced from $8.62 to $7.41.
venue: Journal of Intelligent Internet of Things Systems

title: Non-uniqueness of Leray-Hopf Solutions to Forced Stochastic Hyperdissipative Navier-Stokes Equations up to Lions Index
abstract: Abstract. For the hyperdissipative Navier–Stokes equations (up to Lions index) driven by a linear multiplicative noise and a specific random force term, we prove nonuniqueness of global in time probabilistically strong Leray–Hopf solutions by a straightforward construction without stopping time technique. As a second result, we derive local nonuniqueness of the system driven by a linear multiplicative noise and a specific DETERMINISTIC force term. Such nonuniqueness is robust in the sense that we are allowed to perturb the deterministic force term in an appropriate way. This is closely related to a critical condition on the force term under which the system is locally well-posed.

title: Synergistic optimization of sensitivity and point-of-care performance: orthogonal readout SERS-LFA for multiplexed precise detection
Rewiring versus optimization: how to connect the two philosophies of improving photorespiration?
abstract: Abstract Main conclusion Synthetic bypasses as well as optimized expression of native photorespiratory enzymes improve plant performance through overlapping mechanistic principles, yet their full benefits emerge from similar and distinct features such as relief of metabolic constraints and energetic savings. Abstract The long-standing view on photorespiration as a wasteful and dispensable evolutionary relic has shifted substantially in recent years. Photorespiration is now recognized as an essential metabolic process that not only recycles 2-phosphoglycolate (2PG) to sustain oxygenic photosynthesis, but also impacts on metabolic homeostasis, redox balance, environmental acclimation, and stomatal regulation. Nevertheless, its associated CO2 loss, energetic costs, and metabolic constraints have motivated extensive efforts to improve plant productivity through genetic engineering of photorespiration. Two principal strategies have emerged: (i) introducing synthetic bypasses that reroute photorespiratory flux, particularly inside the chloroplast, and (ii) optimizing the native pathway by engineering expression of key enzymes such as 2PG phosphatase (PGLP1) and glycine decarboxylase (GDC). Although these approaches differ fundamentally in design, they produce overlapping physiological and metabolic outcomes, suggesting a partially shared mechanistic basis. One possibility is that bot…

title: Mobile low-dose computed tomography lung cancer screening within an integrated thoracic oncology network: a real-world implementation and provider-cost evaluation
abstract: To evaluate the clinical, operational, and economic performance of a community-based mobile low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) lung cancer screening program integrated with a tertiary thoracic oncology network. This retrospective implementation study included 1279 individuals screened in Milan, Italy, during November and December 2024. Among 250 screen-positive participants, initial management comprised immediate diagnostic evaluation or planned imaging surveillance – an exploratory logistic regression examined factors associated with immediate diagnostic allocation. A provider-cost scenario model applied assumed annual fixed costs and a constant variable cost per scan to alternative annual screening volumes. Overall, 250 participants (19.5%) had at least one nodule measuring 6 mm or more, and 52 (4.1%) entered the immediate diagnostic pathway. Five lung cancers were detected, corresponding to a cancer detection rate of 0.39% [95% exact confidence interval (CI) = 0.13–0.91]. Nodule diameter and solid morphology were independently associated with diagnostic allocation; apparent model discrimination was 0.84 (95% CI = 0.80–0.88). The median interval from screening LDCT to the first recorded diagnostic assessment was 18 days. Modeled provider cost was approximately €391 per scan at an assumed annual volume of 1279 examinations and decreased in higher-volume scenarios. Mobile lung…

title: An Integrated Tick Management (ITM) protocol combining strategic acaricide treatments and pasture management for cattle tick control
abstract: Abstract The cattle tick Rhipicephalus microplus remains as a challenge for cattle production in tropical and subtropical regions. To date, R. microplus control has relied mainly on chemical acaricides. However, the widespread acaricide resistance has highlighted the need for alternative approaches for sustainable tick control. In this sense, Integrated Tick Management (ITM) is an approach that combines more than one strategy, aiming at long-term control with delayed resistance selection. Here, we evaluated, under field conditions, management practices that combine strategic acaricide treatments with pasture spelling. The approach was based on alternating cattle between infested and presumed tick-free (non-cattle-grazed) paddocks after defined strategic acaricide treatments, thereby allowing a pasture spelling period. Four groups of 20 animals were formed: two managed under ITM conditions, one using only chemical acaricides, and an untreated control group. At the beginning of the spring, the two groups selected for ITM received two successive acaricide treatments. After that, two groups were temporarily moved during summer to presumed tick-free paddocks for 49 days, allowing this time of pasture spelling. One of these paddocks had been previously used for rice cultivation, and the other one for sheep grazing. After this period, cattle returned to the original paddocks. The grou…

title: Integrated Gravimetric, Electrochemical, Kinetic, and Thermodynamic Evaluation of Dioscorea bulbifera (Bitter Yam) Leaf Extract as a Green Corrosion Inhibitor for Mild Steel in Hydrochloric Acid
abstract: Corrosion of mild steel in acidic media remains a major challenge in industrial operations, necessitating the development of environmentally sustainable corrosion inhibitors. This study investigated the corrosion inhibition performance of Dioscorea bulbifera leaf extract on mild steel in hydrochloric acid using complementary phytochemical, gravimetric, electrochemical, kinetic, and thermodynamic analyses. Phytochemical screening confirmed the presence of bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, tannins, alkaloids, saponins, phenolics, and terpenoids, which are responsible for the adsorption and protective properties of the extract. Gravimetric measurements revealed a concentration-dependent reduction in weight loss and corrosion rate, while the inhibition efficiency increased from 19.17% at 0.5 g L⁻¹ to 83.48% at 2.5 g L⁻¹, accompanied by a maximum surface coverage (θ) of 0.8348. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) showed a significant increase in charge transfer resistance from 32.1 to 253.8 Ω cm⁻² and a decrease in double-layer capacitance from 103.5 to 8.5 μF cm⁻², confirming the formation of a protective adsorbed film. Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) measurements further demonstrated a reduction in corrosion current density from 847.5 to 69.7 μA cm⁻², achieving a maximum inhibition efficiency of 91.8%. Kinetic analysis revealed a progressive decrease in the…

title: Mechanistic insights into the chemo- and regioselectivity of the 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition between 5,5-Dimethyl-3-methylenepyrrolidin-2-one and Phenyl(phenyldiazen-1-ium-1-ylidene)methanide: An integrated DFT, ADMET, and molecular docking study
abstract: The chemo- and regioselectivity of the 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition between 5,5-dimethyl-3-methylenepyrrolidin-2-one (R1) and phenyl(phenyldiazen-1-ium-1-ylidene)methanide (R2) was investigated using Density Functional Theory (DFT) at the B3LYP/6-311G(d,p) level with the CPCM solvation model in ethanol. Four competitive reaction pathways were examined to distinguish cycloaddition at the exocyclic C=C bond from the alternative pathway involving the carbonyl C=O group. The pathways leading to P1 and P2 are strongly exergonic, with reaction Gibbs free energies of −26.34 and −26.19 kcal mol⁻ 1 , respectively, indicating that these two cycloadducts are nearly isoenergetic thermodynamically. Their corresponding activation barriers are 13.42 and 17.47 kcal mol⁻ 1 , giving a ΔΔG ‡ of 4.05 kcal mol⁻ 1 in favor of the TS1 → P1 pathway within this regioisomeric pair. Among all four pathways, TS3 exhibits the lowest calculated activation barrier (8.65 kcal mol⁻ 1 ). In contrast, the corresponding product P3 is only weakly stabilized (ΔG = −2.90 kcal mol⁻ 1 ), revealing a clear distinction between kinetic accessibility and thermodynamic product stability. Global and local conceptual-DFT descriptors, Parr functions, and ELF/BET analyses provide complementary insight into the electronic factors controlling the reaction and support a concerted but asynchronous bond-forming process along the pathw…

title: Predicting the Status of Overdue Loans in the US Banking System: Evidence from the US Banking System's Call Reports
abstract: The quarterly Call Reports of FFIEC will be used in this paper to forecast the two-quarter-later delinquency status of commercial and industrial loans, agricultural loans, multi-family residential loans, and credit card loan portfolios. There are 288,396 observations of test data from all loan types at 288 banks, and the sample event rate is 2.43%. LightGBM model AP is 0.13, which has exceeded both the original delinquency rate of 0.0759 and the logistic regression model's 0.10. The 95% confidence intervals for the AP relative to the two initial benchmarks are [0.04, 0.07] and [0.03, 0.04]. Modify the delinquency threshold and change the reporting deadline, and then LightGBM's AP consistently leads the ranking of the initial rate in all four loan sectors and different bank-size groups under ten random seeds. Weighting by loan balance increased the AP of LightGBM, and the ranking of the initial delinquency rate can help to identify more loans in the top ten percentile groups of the target event earlier. The last submission time in the FFIEC database was used to find the old data.

title: Preparation and radiation resistance of a rigid-flexible epoxy resin co-curing system
From reactive care to predictive wellness: AI-integrated preventive medicine and holistic health in the era of precision healthcare
abstract: As chronic disease, mental illness, metabolic disease, and aging populations rise in prevalence, there has been a shift from reactive healthcare to predictive and preventive medicine. The healthcare system has experienced radical changes in technology with the introduction of artificial intelligence (AI), precision medicine, wearable devices, digital biomarkers, genomics, and microbiome analysis, which can provide individualized risk assessments, continuous monitoring, and adaptive preventive measures. In addition, a holistic approach to health, including nutrition, exercise, sleep, mental wellness and lifestyle medicine, can help individuals sustainably optimize their health. This article will review how AI can be integrated into the field of preventive healthcare, including applications of digital therapeutics, personalized nutrition, remote monitoring, cancer prevention, cardiovascular prevention, and longevity medicine. While there are still many challenges surrounding bias, privacy and data security, equity, and ethical considerations, addressing these issues will be critical. Ultimately, combining AI-based predictive wellness with holistic healthcare will create new possibilities for future precision healthcare systems that emphasize personalized prevention and have a positive impact on the overall health of communities.
venue: Journal of Preventive Medicine and Holistic Health

title: Research on Mechatronic Control System Theory: Application Analysis of Electronic Circuits and Digital Encoders in Precision Motion Control of Industrial Robotic Arms
abstract: Mechatronic control systems serve as the core support for realizing precision motion control of industrial robotic arms. Adopting the literature analysis method, this paper conducts research from three dimensions namely electronic circuits, digital encoders and control circuit systems, sorts out the basic principles of each module, analyzes the cooperative operation mechanism of electronic control components, and clarifies the critical effect of closed-loop architecture on the positioning accuracy of robotic arms. The study reveals that traditional basic control schemes are restricted by measurement noise, dynamic coupling and hardware time delay, making it difficult to balance motion speed and trajectory tracking accuracy simultaneously. Based on theoretical sorting and literature review, this study clarifies the internal logic of how electronic control systems affect the operational accuracy of robotic arms, and can provide theoretical references for subsequent research such as optimization of error compensation algorithms and anti-interference hardware design.

title: Position-conditioned multi-target backdoor attacks on decoder-only code language models
Detection rate and clinical relevance of cerebral microbleeds in early detection of cerebral small vessel disease: 3.0T MRI versus multi-detector CT
abstract: Background and purpose Cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) are a core imaging marker of cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD). Early recognition of CMBs is important for delaying the progression of cognitive impairment. Although multi-detector computed tomography (MDCT) is widely used for initial brain screening, its performance in detecting CMBs has not been fully validated. Using 3.0T MRI susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) as the reference standard, this study aimed to systematically evaluate the detection capability and missed-diagnosis factors of MDCT for CMBs, analyze the relationship between CMBs and cognitive function, and construct a CT-based prediction model for MRI-detected microbleeds. Methods A total of 486 patients who underwent both cranial MDCT and 3.0T MRI (including SWI) during the same period were retrospectively enrolled. Two radiologists independently and blindly assessed CMBs, and the sensitivity, specificity and miss-rate of CT were calculated. Independent risk factors for CT missed diagnosis were identified by multivariate logistic regression among MRI-positive patients. Spearman correlation and multivariate linear regression were used to analyze the associations of CMB count and distribution with Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores. A prediction model consisting of age, CT white matter hypodensity score and number of lacunar infarcts was developed in a…

title: A cross-sectional analysis of objectively recorded moderate-to-vigorous physical activity levels in a multi-ethnic sample of middle-aged women in Norway (2019–2022): exploring the role of one-versus three-dimensional accelerometer data and criteria for number of valid days
abstract: Abstract Background We aimed to compare total and bouted moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) (min/day) derived from one- and three-dimensional accelerometer data and to examine how applying different valid-day eligibility criteria affected the composition of the analytical sample and population-level MVPA estimates among women in a multiethnic population. Methods We used accelerometer data collected at the 11-year follow-up of women originally enrolled in the STOR-Groruddalen study. Ethnicity was self-reported. Generalized Linear Models (GLMs) with gamma and Tweedie distributions were used to estimate marginal means for total and bouted MVPA (≥ 10) consecutive) min/day respectively from Actigraph wGT3X-BT data, using one- and three-dimensional accelerometry data and ≥ 1 or ≥ 4 days as criteria for valid number of days, controlling for age, education, and parity. Estimates of mean MVPA ratio representing percentage change in expected physical activity (PA) minutes relative to the reference group, Western women were obtained from the statistical models. Results Of the 385 women who met at the 11-year follow-up, 280 had ≥ 1 valid physical activity monitoring day. Among these, mean (SD) age was 42.0 (4.6) years, 48% were ethnic minorities, and 19% women had < 4 valid PA monitoring days. Estimated marginal means (95% confidence intervals) based on ≥ 1 valid day for Western…

title: MGAFN: Multi-Granularity Alignment and Fusion Network Based on MultiModal Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Multimodal aspect-based sentiment analysis (MABSA) aims to identify the sentiment polarity toward a target aspect using textual and visual information. Existing methods often perform cross-modal interaction at a single semantic granularity, making it difficult to capture both aspect-level details and global context. Moreover, visual content may be irrelevant to the target aspect, and static fusion can introduce noise into sentiment prediction. To address these challenges, we propose a Multi-Granularity Alignment and Fusion Network (MGAFN). MGAFN constructs fine- and coarse-grained representations of text and images, then aligns them at the token–patch and sentence–scene levels, respectively. An adaptive gating mechanism regulates the contribution of visual features according to their relevance to the target aspect. A coarse-grained semantic distribution constraint further encourages consistency between paired text and image representations. Experiments on the Twitter-2015 and Twitter-2017 datasets show that MGAFN achieves competitive performance against representative MABSA baselines. These results suggest that multi-granularity alignment and adaptive visual fusion can improve aspect-level sentiment prediction while reducing interference from irrelevant visual information.

title: Volumetric-aware AI framework for food classification and size-conditioned nutritional quality estimation using multi-task vision transformers
abstract: Abstract Image-based dietary assessment faces a fundamental challenge: nutritional content varies significantly based on physical properties like portion size, food variety, and growing conditions factors, often not directly observable from images alone. Existing vision-based nutrition systems typically output deterministic values without acknowledging this inherent variability, limiting their scientific validity and practical utility. We present a novel volumetric-aware multi-task framework that addresses this gap by explicitly modeling portion size as an intermediate physical property before nutritional estimation. Our approach leverages the EVA-02 Vision Transformer as a backbone feature extractor with three parallel prediction heads: (1) food classification identifying 33 antioxidant-rich food categories, (2) volume/size estimation predicting relative portion dimensions, and (3) size-conditioned nutrition estimation that scales predictions based on estimated portions. The model was trained end-to-end with multi-task optimization, balancing classification accuracy, size estimation precision, and nutritional prediction error. Experimental results demonstrated superior performance with 99.76% classification accuracy on the curated dataset (95.67–97.83% on external datasets), overall nutritional MSE of 0.0048 with R 2 of 0.993 (average per-attribute MSE: 0.0045), and size estim…

title: Comparative multi-omics reveals pathogen-specific defense responses and candidate volatile markers in grape berries infected by Aspergillus carbonarius and Alternaria alternata
abstract: Abstract Postharvest grape berries are highly susceptible to infection by Aspergillus carbonarius and Alternaria alternata, two important decay pathogens that produce ochratoxin A and alternariol, respectively, thereby posing substantial food safety risks. However, pathogen-specific defense responses in grape berries and their associated volatile signatures remain poorly understood. This study compared the responses of ‘Muscat Hamburg’ grape berries (Vitis vinifera L.) to A. carbonarius and A. alternata using phenotypic, physiological, transcriptomic, untargeted metabolomic, and volatile metabolomic analyses. Both pathogens activated the phenylpropanoid–stilbene pathway and increased resveratrol accumulation, indicating a conserved defense baseline. However, A. carbonarius caused rapid lesion expansion accompanied by extensive membrane lipid remodeling, lipoxygenase cascade activation, and broad metabolic reprogramming. In contrast, A. alternata induced localized lesions and selective shifts in stilbene-, flavonoid-, and physical barrier-related pathways while maintaining membrane lipid homeostasis. Volatile profiling at 2 d post-inoculation identified 40 differentially accumulated volatile organic compounds (15 shared, 25 pathogen-specific). Based on these signatures, a hierarchical early warning platform was established: a marked increase in 1-hexanol served as a shared marke…

title: Multi-source, multi-level, graph-based institutional collaboration indicators for research assessment with Ricgraph
abstract: Abstract Researchers rarely work alone: they work with colleagues within and between organizations on all organizational levels. They collaborate on a variety of research results beyond traditional publications. However, collaboration indicators in research assessment usually rely on a single source, focus on top-level institutions, and may focus on journal articles only. This limits what can be seen about collaborations within organizations, and for results such as data sets and software. This article introduces a multi-source, multi-level, graph-based approach to collaboration indicators using Ricgraph (Research in context graph). Publications, data sets, software, persons, and organizational information from multiple systems are integrated into a single graph. Collaborations are defined as shared research results connecting organizations via persons. They are quantified on top-level organization, as well as on faculty and departmental level, providing a concrete operationalization of multi-source, multi-level collaboration indicators for science-of-science research. Combining multiple sources substantially increases the observed coverage of collaborations, especially for data set and software collaborations (>400% for sources in this article, compared to a single source). Multi-level collaborations overviews reveal patterns that are invisible at the top-level alone. These…

title: Automated Wildlife Monitoring using a YOLOv8-based Object Detection Model for Conservation and Ecological Management Applications
abstract: Background: Wildlife detection is an important component of biodiversity monitoring and conservation research. Conventional wildlife surveys and manual inspection of camera-trap imagery are labor-intensive and difficult to scale. Deep learning- based object detection provides an opportunity to automate the identification and localization of wildlife in digital images. However, the effectiveness of such models must be evaluated using clearly separated training, validation and independent test data. Methods: This study evaluates a YOLOv8-based object detection model for four African wildlife species: buffalo, elephant, rhino and zebra. The model was trained using the publicly available African wildlife dataset containing 1,504 annotated images. The dataset was divided into training (1,052 images), validation (225 images) and independent test (227 images) subsets. Data augmentation was applied only to the training subset to improve model generalization. The model was evaluated using precision, recall, mAP@50 and mAP@50-95, together with class-wise analysis, confusion-matrix assessment and qualitative visualization of detection results. Result: The final evaluation on the held-out test set demonstrated an overall mAP @ 50 of 0.83 and mAP@50-95 of 0.61, with overall precision and recall of 0.80 and 0.75, respectively. Class-wise evaluation showed precision values ranging from 0.780 …

title: Digital Inclusive Finance and Urban Innovation Ratio Upgrading
abstract: Private firms in China often struggle to obtain bank credit, especially for research and development projects that offer little tangible collateral. Digital inclusive finance may ease these constraints. This paper examines whether the development of digital inclusive finance is associated with a higher share of invention patents in Chinese cities. The analysis focuses on changes in patent composition rather than changes in the total number of patents. It combines the Peking University Digital Financial Inclusion Index, patent data, and city-level economic statistics for the period from 2011 to 2022. The data are matched by city and year. The results show a positive relationship, with a baseline coefficient of 0.2741 that is significant at the 1 percent level. This relationship is also stronger in cities with better protection of intellectual property rights. These findings suggest that digital finance and intellectual property protection may play complementary roles in supporting invention-oriented innovation at the city level.

title: Effectiveness of Nurse-Led Self-Management Interventions in Improving Disease Control, Treatment Adherence, and Quality of Life Among Adults with Chronic Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
abstract: Background: Nurse-led self-management interventions are increasingly used to support adults living with chronic diseases, but cross-disease evidence remains fragmented. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their effectiveness for disease control, treatment adherence, and quality of life. Methods: PubMed and Scopus were searched for peer-reviewed randomized controlled trials published from 2016 to 2026. Eligible studies enrolled adults with chronic diseases and compared a clearly nurse-led self-management intervention with usual care or another eligible comparator. Random-effects meta-analysis was conducted only for clinically compatible outcomes. Results: Of 393 records identified, 121 duplicates were removed and 69 randomized controlled trials were included in the qualitative synthesis. Disease control was reported in 43 trials, quality of life in 32, and treatment adherence in 15. Nine trials contributed to the HbA1c meta-analysis, showing a significant reduction favoring nurse-led intervention (MD = -0.53 percentage points, 95% CI -0.85 to -0.21; p = .001; I2 = 88.2%). Five trials contributed to the systolic blood pressure meta-analysis (MD = -4.20 mm Hg, 95% CI -7.18 to -1.22; p = .006; I2 = 53.4%), although the HartungKnapp interval was wider because of the small number of studies. Adherence and quality-of-life findings were generally favorable but too hetero…

title: Guest editorial: Early career academics’ identity development in a changing era: challenges, strategies and institutional management
The Impact of Digital Inclusive Finance on Enterprise Innovation Output
abstract: This paper matches data on Chinese A-share listed companies from 2011 to 2022 with city-level digital inclusive finance indices to obtain a panel sample covering 36,599 firm-year observations, 4,699 firms, and 282 cities, and tests the relationship between digital inclusive finance and enterprise innovation output. The baseline model includes city and year fixed effects, with standard errors clustered at the city level. The results show that the development of city-level digital inclusive finance is significantly positively correlated with both invention patent applications and total patent applications. Further analysis finds that digital inclusive finance is significantly correlated with lower financing constraints, and that stronger financing constraints are associated with lower invention patent output by firms, a result consistent with the theoretical expectation of the financing constraints channel. Grouped regressions show that the positive relationship mainly appears in non-state-owned and private enterprises, and is more prominent in the central and western regions. After replacing the innovation measures, winsorizing, using the one-period lagged digital inclusive finance index, and excluding the financial industry, the core conclusions do not change substantially. Overall, the development of digital inclusive finance is significantly associated with improved enterpris…

title: Human Oversight in AI-Assisted Financial Record-Keeping: A Study of Error Detection and Accountability
Financial Shocks and the Allocation of Decision Rights: A Property-Rights Framework for Healthcare Investment
abstract: We develop a property-rights framework for healthcare investment under financial shocks. Financing-cost shocks reduce perceived project value in proportion to the costs internalized by the effective decision maker (Proposition 3). Observed investment changes depend on projects’ proximity to approval thresholds (Proposition 5). Separated rights can introduce approval frictions; credible financing support combined with capital ceilings can shift adjustment toward administrative rationing. Five European health systems illustrate institutional configurations without providing a causal test. The contribution is a set of conditional, empirically distinguishable predictions about governance-mediated investment responses.
venue: British Journal of Healthcare and Medical Research

title: The impact of circular economy disclosure on corporate performance: the moderating role of board gender diversity
abstract: Purpose The authors investigate the impact of circular economy disclosure (CED) on firm performance (FP), furthermore, to investigate the potential moderating role of gender diversity on this relationship. Design/methodology/approach The study sample consisted of 46 French nonfinancial-listed firms on the SBF 120 index from 2014 to 2024. An automated content analysis approach was used to measure the CED. The authors used both the return on assets (ROA) and the return on equity (ROE) to measure the firm’s performance. The feasible generalized least squares (FGLS) were estimated for the panel data models. This study was supplemented by applying the generalized method of moments (GMM) to address any suspected endogeneity problem and to check the robustness of the findings. Findings The results of the study indicate a positive impact of CED on FP. Nevertheless, the impact of gender diversity on FP was found to be insignificant. In addition, a negative moderating influence is revealed of gender diversity between the relationship between CED and FP. Originality/value This study contributes to the growing and limited research on CED and FP. The authors provide the first empirical evidence on the impact of CED on FP in the French context. In addition, a list of circular economy keywords was adapted to the French context. Moreover, to the best of our knowledge, it is the first study inv…
venue: Journal of Financial Reporting and Accounting

title: The human right to drinking water and environmental impact assessment in the Kyrgyz Republic: SDG 6
abstract: ABSTRACT Although the Kyrgyz Republic generates much of Central Asia's freshwater runoff, only 74% of its population used safely managed drinking water services in 2024, and access remains unequal across rural areas and regions. This article examines whether the 2025 reforms, namely the new Water Code and the World Bank–led Universal Access Program, advance the human right to drinking water and Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6), with particular attention to environmental impact assessment (EIA), which international courts have recognized as an obligation under customary international law. Combining doctrinal and comparative legal analysis with secondary SDG 6, MICS 2023, and village-level data, the study assesses national law against CESCR General Comment No. 15, the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions, and the case law of the International Court of Justice. The 2025 Code prioritizes drinking water use but excludes drinking water services from its scope and creates no enforceable individual right. EIA is required for water-use permits only in listed cases, and the system lacks screening, binding public participation, strategic assessment, and a transboundary procedure. The Program addresses past failures but defers the least-served oblasts. The article recommends a drinking water law, an EIA law aligned with international standards, and needs-based investment.

title: The Intergenerational Transmission of Disadvantage in Euro​pe: A Latent Class Analysis
abstract: Abstract Comparative research on the intergenerational transmission of socioeconomic disadvantage remains limited, largely due to a lack of harmonised information on parental circumstances. To address this limitation, we propose using latent class analysis to identify disadvantaged groups by incorporating measures of education, social class, financial hardship and material deprivation. We draw on the 2019 EU-SILC ad​-hoc retrospective module, which provides information on respondents and their parents to provide transition matrices and summary mobility indices across thirty European countries. Our results show substantial variation in disadvantage persistence and provide a robust ranking of countries. These findings contribute to comparative research by showing how disadvantage is reproduced across generations in Europe.

title: Taxation Dynamics and Economic Performance in Nigeria: Evidence from The Revised Tax-To-GDP Series, 2010–2021
abstract: This study examines how taxation dynamics relate to economic performance in Nigeria between 2010 and 2021, using the revised official tax-to-GDP series of the National Bureau of Statistics alongside real GDP and inflation data. Descriptive, correlation, regression and lead–lag analyses are applied to the annual series and interpreted against recent peer-reviewed evidence. Three findings stand out. First, the tax-to-GDP ratio fell from 15.3% in 2010 to 8.3% in 2016 and recovered only to 10.9% by 2021; in 2010 prices, total tax revenue was about 6% lower in 2021 than in 2010 while real GDP rose by about 32%. Second, the rising non-oil share of tax revenue (82.3% to 88.6%) reflects the collapse of oil taxes rather than a deepening of the non-oil base, whose ratio to GDP fell from 12.6% to 9.6%. Third, the tax ratio is positively associated with growth (0.56 percentage points of growth per percentage point of tax-to-GDP), but the association weakens once inflation and the oil component are considered, and lead–lag tests suggest, weakly, that growth leads tax revenue rather than the reverse. Taxation in Nigeria is therefore largely procyclical and commodity-driven. The paper argues for real base-broadening, counter-cyclical fiscal buffers, macroeconomic stability and stronger institutions as the conditions for the 2025 tax reforms to raise economic performance.

Accounting Anomaly Detection Using Relational Graph Convolutional Networks over Heterogeneous Financial Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Accounting anomalies can occur because of relational dependencies which can be missed by independent firm-year feature vectors. In this research, the use of a heterogeneous financial knowledge graph along with R-GCN for anomaly detection is considered. Financial data is retrieved from SEC EDGAR filings and US-GAAP XBRL facts in the period 2010–2024. Enforcement releases are used to indicate the periods of misconduct. Graph nodes correspond to firm-years, accounting accounts, executives, auditors, and industries and edges of five relation types connect them. The inputs include thirty-seven financial features and entity embeddings, which are processed with the help of three-layer R-GCN with relation-specific aggregation of messages and then classified with a multi-layer perceptron classifier. Weighted binary cross-entropy is used as the loss function to handle the problem of imbalanced classes. Time-aware graph snapshots and chronological splitting are performed to avoid information leakage. GNNExplainer is utilized to produce explanatory subgraphs which undergo perturbation-based stability assessment. With ten random seeds, the obtained results are as follows: AUPRC – 0.486 ± 0.021, AUROC – 0.913 ± 0.009, F1-score – 0.571 ± 0.018. The performance is better than that of graph-feature XGBoost by 0.065 ± 0.014 in AUPRC. Ablation studies show that removal of auditor relations leads …

abstract: Digital change is sweeping across the banking industry, and at the same time society is pressing firms to operate more sustainably. Against this backdrop, fintech adoption, social responsibility programs, and the way lenders manage default exposure have become decisive for how much profit a bank earns. Our objective is to determine how far Financial Technology (Fintech), Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), and Credit Risk explain the profitability of banks traded on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) from 2021 to 2024. We applied an associative quantitative method, and purposive selection produced 38 banks observed for four consecutive years, giving 152 bank-year data points analyzed through multiple linear regression (pooled data structure). Two of the three predictors, Fintech and CSR, lift Return on Assets, and both effects reach statistical significance. Credit Risk, proxied by the Non-Performing Loan (NPL) ratio, pulls Return on Assets down, and this negative effect is likewise significant. Given an Adjusted R2 of 0.190, the model captures a specific portion of financial performance variance, implying that statistical findings reflect associative relationships rather than direct absolute causality. title: Free trade agreements and foreign direct investment in ASEAN-5 economies: Panel evidence using country-specific FTA counts, 2000-2024
abstract: Type of the article: Theoretical ArticleDang Minh Le - Corresponding author, email: minh.ledang@stu.edu.vnAbstractWhether free trade agreements (FTAs) raise foreign direct investment (FDI) in developing economies remains empirically unresolved, partly because FTA exposure is often measured with a coarse binary indicator. This study rebuilds the FTA measure from agreement-level data and examines its association with FDI inflows in five ASEAN economies (Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines) over 2000–2024. FTAcount, the number of goods FTA families in force at year-end in each country, is constructed from the WTO Regional Trade Agreements Information System and the ADB Asia Regional Integration Center database, and the country-year chronology is reported in the Appendix. Using a balanced panel of 125 observations, the study estimates pooled OLS, fixed-effects (FE), random-effects, FGLS, panel-corrected, and Driscoll-Kraay specifications, with and without year effects, and assesses inference with a wild cluster bootstrap because the panel has only five clusters. FTAcount is positively associated with FDI in estimators that ignore country heterogeneity (0.093-0.128 percentage points of GDP per additional agreement), but the sign reverses once country effects are included (FE: –0.184; with year effects: –0.200). Inference for these within-country estimates is …

title: Financial Feasibility Analysis of Smallholder Oil Palm in Tasikmalaya Regency
abstract: Oil palm is a high-value plantation commodity that plays a crucial role in boosting community income. However, smallholder oil palm farming faces risks associated with fluctuations in Fresh Fruit Bunch (FFB) prices and rising production costs, particularly for fertilizer. This study aims to analyze the financial feasibility of smallholder oil palm farming in Ciheras Village, Cipatujah District, Tasikmalaya Regency, as well as the business's sensitivity to changes in FFB prices and fertilizer costs. A case study method utilizing both primary and secondary data was employed. The analysis was conducted using Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), Net Benefit-Cost Ratio (Net B/C), Payback Period (PP), and sensitivity analysis. The results indicate that the oil palm farming venture is financially feasible, with an NPV of Rp332,371.55, an IRR of 15%, a Net B/C of 1.01, and a payback period of 7 years. These findings demonstrate that the business is capable of generating profit and recouping investment capital in accordance with feasibility criteria. However, the sensitivity analysis reveals that the business is quite vulnerable to changes in prices and production costs. A 10% decrease in FFB prices causes the NPV to drop to zero, while a 14.6692% increase in fertilizer costs brings the business to the break-even point. Thus, while smallholder oil palm farming in Cihe…

abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the relationship between Islamic financial literacy, Islamic financial inclusion and government support towards behavioural intention in adopting Islamic banking services. This study also investigates the influence of actual usage on achieving the objectives of maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah, particularly in the dimensions of education, justice and well-being. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative approach was used with the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling method to test the proposed conceptual model. Data were collected through structured questionnaires distributed to 749 respondents with access to Islamic financial services. Findings The results indicated that Islamic financial literacy and Islamic financial inclusion significantly influenced users’ behavioural intention to adopt Islamic banking services. Furthermore, behavioural intention strongly affected actual use, which in turn positively contributed to the three dimensions of maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah, namely, education, justice and wealth distribution. However, government support did not exhibit a significant relationship with behavioural intention, suggesting a gap between public policy and public perception. abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify, prioritize and map the causal interrelationships among word-of-mouth (WOM)-related factors shaping investors’ financial behavior from an Islamic financial marketing perspective. It examines how trust, social interaction, shared vision, family and friends, expert knowledge, risk-taking, past stock performance, financial advertising and investment experience jointly shape investors’ financial decisions. Design/methodology/approach A structured literature-based factor identification process and expert validation were used to identify the relevant WOM-related factors. The Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) method was then applied to analyze their direct and indirect interrelationships. Judgments from 15 academic and financial-market experts were aggregated to classify the factors into cause and effect groups and construct a causal map. Findings Relational trust, investment experience, risk-taking and social interaction are the most prominent factors in the WOM network. Relational trust, social interaction, shared vision, past stock performance and expert knowledge operate as causal drivers, whereas financial advertising, risk-taking, family and friends and investment experience are mainly influenced by other factors. The results indicate that trust-based communication and credible knowledge sources are central to investors…

title: AI-assisted siRNA drug design: potential applications in PCSK9-targeted lipid-lowering therapy
abstract: Some patients do not reach their low-density lipoprotein cholesterol targets despite existing lipid-lowering treatment. Small interfering RNA drugs targeting PCSK9 offer an additional treatment option. However, silencing activity varies among candidate sequences, and chemical modifications and delivery conditions also affect their therapeutic potential. This review evaluates the evidence supporting AI-assisted early screening of PCSK9-targeting siRNAs and the limits of its application. This paper examines studies of activity prediction for chemically modified siRNAs, computational evaluation using AttSiOff, clinical trials of inclisiran, and research on modification optimization and GalNAc-mediated liver-targeted delivery. Current evidence indicates that machine learning can use sequence information and selected modification features to help prioritize candidates, while inclisiran trials support the lipid-lowering effects of PCSK9-targeting siRNAs. These findings are not yet sufficient to establish that integrating AI tools improves actual screening efficiency or therapeutic efficacy. Future studies should first standardize modification and delivery conditions, then conduct prospective controlled screening using hit rate and experimental resources as evaluation measures, followed by validation of candidate efficacy and safety in vivo.

abstract: Background Cataract remains the leading cause of vision impairment among older adults worldwide, and hospitalization expenditure for cataract surgery may be influenced by both the care pathway and consumable pricing policies. Objective It remains unclear how much of the recent decline in cataract surgery expenditure in Chinese hospitals is associated with the shift from inpatient to day-case management, as distinct from intraocular lens (IOL) price reform through volume-based procurement (VBP). Methods This retrospective study used monthly records of 19,112 age-related cataract admissions (2014–2026) at a county-level hospital in Zhejiang Province, China. A two-breakpoint segmented regression (interrupted time series) was applied, with breakpoints at the formalization of the day-case pathway (July 2020) and the implementation of regional IOL volume-based procurement (January 2022). Costs were expressed in 2014 constant prices. Monthly outcomes were modeled with ordinary least squares and Newey–West standard errors (original model) and with month-of-year indicators and autoregressive errors (final model), supplemented by binomial and Poisson models. Sensitivity analyses addressed transition handling, concurrent DRG payment (January 2020), and case mix. Occupational Safety and Health Management Systems as a Legal Obligation of Electricity Companies in Indonesia
abstract: Workers in Indonesia's electricity sector face significant occupational hazards, while workplace safety enforcement remains fragmented across labor, electricity, and social security regulations. This study examined the legal enforceability of Occupational Safety and Health Management System (OSHMS) requirements for electricity companies and evaluated legal remedies available through the Industrial Relations Court. This research employed doctrinal legal methods using statutory and conceptual approaches, supported by legislation, legal scholarship, international standards, and established legal principles. The findings showed that OSHMS implementation constitutes a legally binding obligation for companies meeting applicable statutory criteria. However, enforcement remains constrained by fragmented regulatory oversight, ineffective sanctions, and legal uncertainty concerning the responsibilities of companies controlling worksites where contractor employees face occupational hazards. Furthermore, the Industrial Relations Court has the authority to adjudicate employment disputes involving statutory occupational safety and health rights and provide appropriate individual remedies. Nevertheless, broader structural remedies remain limited by procedural uncertainties regarding collective claims, access to employer-held safety records, and mechanisms for monitoring compliance with judici…

title: Leverage-Based Solvency Risk as a Moderator of the ESG–Financial Performance Link: Evidence from the Iraqi Frontier Market
abstract: This study examines whether leverage-based solvency risk moderates the association between ESG disclosure and financial performance among 28 non-financial firms listed on the Iraq Stock Exchange over 2015–2024. Relative solvency risk is operationalised through a synthetic, rate-scaled cost-of-debt (COD) proxy constructed from a standardised-leverage index, a sovereign spread, and a tax shield; COD is a model-implied measure rather than an observed borrowing rate. ESG disclosure is measured using a 15-item checklist. While the direct effect of COD on financial performance is not statistically robust once the tax component is removed, panel regressions with firm-level wild cluster bootstrap-t inference indicate that the ESG–ROA association becomes more positive as relative solvency risk increases. The aggregate ESG × COD interaction (β = 15.630, p = 0.011) and the governance interaction (β = 17.798, p = 0.013) are significant at the 5% level, whereas the social interaction is not significant (p = 0.102). No statistically significant interaction is found for cash-flow ROA (CFROA). Alternative leverage-based moderators yield comparable interaction patterns, indicating that COD provides no additional moderating information beyond its leverage component. Although the ROA interaction survives year fixed effects, it becomes insignificant when firms with persistently negative equity are…

title: First Report of Curvularia Leaf Spot ( Curvularia lunata ) on Corn ( Zea mays L.) in Michigan
abstract: In September of 2025, corn leaf samples exhibiting symptoms typical of infection by Curvularia lunata were collected from field trials consisting of various hybrids at the Michigan State University Plant Pathology Farm, Ingham County, Lansing, Michigan (42.70°N, 84.47°W). Small tan lesions measuring roughly 1 mm in diameter with a brown circular margin were observed in the middle to upper canopy of the plants ranging from 1-5% severity of leaf coverage. Symptomatic leaves were taken from the field back to the lab, surface disinfested with 70% ethanol for 10 s, wiped dry and placed into a humidity chamber for 24 h at ambient room temperature (~22°C). Melanized spores were observed in the lesions and were single spored and plated onto water agar. Pure cultures were obtained after 24 h and transferred to potato dextrose agar (PDA) amended with 50 mg/L chloramphenicol. Culture morphology on PDA appeared a tan-brown color with concentric rings that later darkened in appearance and formed contrasting star shaped angles of light and dark after 3 days. Conidia grown on PDA measured 16.7–26.5 µm in length (mean: 21.7 µm) and 6.66–14.8 µm in width (mean: 10.6 µm); n = 50 and appeared curved with three septa. Genomic DNA was extracted from isolate CL25-1 using the MP Bio FastSpin Kit (MP Bio) and was used for multi-locus sequencing. Loci used in identification and sequencing consisted of …

title: Shouting for sale: The systematic multimodal interactional order of market activities
abstract: Shoutouts are a familiar characteristic of the sounding ecology of open-air markets. While their format has been studied as a lively example of verbal virtuosity, their precise organisation within the rich unfolding activities of the market remains largely understudied. Grounded in multimodal Conversation Analysis, this study addresses the situated, praxeological and interactional order of shoutouts in markets, showing how they are skilfully and methodically positioned within the sellers’ work and transactions. In particular, the analyses detail three sequential environments in which sellers systematically perform shouting out, and how they are located within current transactions. This enables us to discuss shoutouts as particular actions, designed to the overheard by anybody, and thus only diffusedly and generically addressed to possible overhearing co-present people, who might (or might not) respond to them in the (re)orientation of their ongoing trajectories and conducts.

title: Pandemic Panic or Structural Change? Herding Intensity and Market Efficiency in Crypto Markets
abstract: This study examines market efficiency and herd-related dynamics in seven major crypto assets—Bitcoin, Ethereum, Cardano, Chainlink, Litecoin, Dogecoin and Monero—from 27 December 2019 to 7 January 2025. Daily observations are analysed using multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MF-DFA) to investigate whether the informational and behavioural properties of cryptocurrency markets changed across the COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 periods. The analysis distinguishes the COVID-19 period (27 December 2019—5 May 2023) from the subsequent post-COVID-19 period (6 May 2023—7 January 2025). The findings indicate that all selected crypto assets display multifractal characteristics, although the intensity and direction of the changes differ across assets. Changes in the average multifractal spectrum indicate that multifractality increased for Cardano, Chainlink, Dogecoin and Monero after the COVID-19 period. In contrast, Bitcoin, Ethereum and Litecoin exhibited lower average multifractal characteristics in the later period. The magnitude of long memory index further indicates changes in market inefficiency across the two periods, with higher inefficiency observed for Bitcoin, Cardano, Chainlink and Monero in the post-COVID-19 period. These results highlight substantial heterogeneity in the evolution of dependence structures and market efficiency across cryptocurrency markets.

title: Earnings management and ESG: The impact of board gender diversity in an emerging market
abstract: This paper examines whether firms’ corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosures are affected by earnings management. It also examines whether board gender diversity may exert a positive or negative influence. Data were collected from an unbalanced panel of 363 firm-years. These firms were listed on the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul) between 2021 and 2024. A baseline panel regression and a dynamic two-step system generalized method of moments (GMM) are used to overcome endogeneity issues. Findings show that earnings management, measured by discretionary accruals using the performance-adjusted modified Jones model, has a negative impact on firms’ ability to disclose non-financial information. It was also found that board gender diversity can improve a firm’s ESG disclosure; however, the interaction term was found to be negative. This shows that if a firm is manipulating its financial statements, this creates an obstacle to disclosing sustainability information. Supporting the tokenism theory, the findings indicate that female directors do not help in disclosing sustainability information if financial statements are being manipulated. This paper uses the agency, stakeholder, and resource dependence theories to help support the findings, showing that there needs to be more enforcement to stop earnings management.

abstract: This study assesses electricity-related greenhouse gas emissions from aluminum alloy wheel manufacturing at Jajce Alloy Wheels d.o.o., Bosnia and Herzegovina, within a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment covering raw materials, inbound transport and manufacturing. Plant-level data and Ecoinvent datasets were used, with results expressed per kilogram of finished product. A descriptive comparison of the 2023 residual-mix and 2024 market-based hydro–wind inventories was complemented by a solar photovoltaic sensitivity analysis holding the 2024 electricity demand and non-electricity inputs constant. Reported electricity-related emissions decreased from 1.864 to 0.030 kg CO2e/kg between the annual inventories, a reduction of about 98.4%, despite higher electricity demand per kilogram. However, differences in annual activity data and background database versions prevent attribution of this change solely to electricity procurement. Total manufacturing emissions decreased from 2.81 to 1.27 kg CO2e/kg, whereas the cradle-to-gate footprint increased from 7.88 to 10.3 kg CO2e/kg alongside a higher raw-material contribution. Under the selected photovoltaic factor, electricity-related emissions were 0.189 kg CO2e/kg, yielding indicative total manufacturing emissions of approximately 1.43 kg CO2e/kg. This sensitivity result is conditional on equivalent electricity delivery boundaries and do…

title: A harmonic–economic optimization framework for filter design and placement in active distribution systems
abstract: The paper introduces a harmonic filter design subject to engineering constraints and a techno-economic optimization model of active distribution systems. The augmentation of nonlinear loads, as well as inverter-based DERs, worsens locational marginal pricing (LMP) and copper losses and harmonic distortion. In contrast to traditional methods that aim at minimizing the total harmonic distortion (THD), the proposed methodology combines harmonic-sensitive multi-period power flow analysis, frequency-sensitive network modeling, IEEE-1531-compliant passive filter parameterization, and explicit internalization of losses in the economy. Filter inductance and resistance are calculated based on reactive power rating, tuning frequency, and quality factor requirements so that resonance is possible and unrealistic combinations of parameters are avoided. An explicit index of filter-design performance is added to restrict the inductor current stress and capacitor voltage stress and place the engineering feasibility as part of the optimization procedure. The quantification of harmonic losses as a function of frequency order is included in the marginal loss element of nodal pricing and allows harmonic mitigation costs to be reflected in the price. The resultant nonlinear multi-period optimization has the simultaneous minimization of voltage THD, harmonic losses, system loss, economic cost, and c…

The Price of Removing Fuel Subsidy: Renewed Hope or Renewed Hardship? Tinubu's Economic Reforms and The Suffering of Ordinary Nigerians
abstract: The removal of Nigeria's petrol subsidy in May 2023 marked a major turning point in the country's economic policy and renewed the longstanding debate over the relationship between fiscal reform, economic stability and social welfare. Announced by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as part of a broader programme of economic restructuring, the policy was justified on the grounds of reducing government expenditure, eliminating fiscal distortions, improving public revenue and creating opportunities for productive investment. However, the immediate adjustment generated significant economic pressures, including increased petrol prices, rising transportation costs, inflationary pressures, declining household purchasing power and growing difficulties for small businesses and low-income households. This paper examines the historical background, economic justification, implementation and socioeconomic consequences of fuel subsidy removal under the Tinubu administration. Using a qualitative historical anddocumentary methodology, it draws on government publications, economic reports, newspaper investigations, journal articles, institutional assessments and relevant scholarly literature. The paper argues that although subsidy reform addresses genuine structural weaknesses in Nigeria's public finances, its developmental value must ultimately be assessed by the extent to which fiscal savings transla…

title: A Transition-Aware Power Discriminative Network for Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for grid dispatching, electricity market trading, energy storage configuration, and microgrid energy management. However, transition events and nonlinear meteorological-power trajectory patterns make accurate multi-step forecasting challenging. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to improve short-term PV power forecasting by enhancing sparse transition periods without manual weather labels and by constraining the global shape of future power trajectories. METHODS: A transition-aware power discriminative network (TAPD) is proposed. TAPD consists of a transition-aware enhancement module (TAE) and a predictor-discriminator joint modeling module (PDJM). TAE estimates time-wise transition scores from power-irradiance response features and adaptively enhances encoded representations. PDJM combines a coarse-to-fine horizon-aware predictor with a conditional power-sequence discriminator to jointly constrain point-wise accuracy, frequency-domain structure, adjacent-step relations, and overall trajectory shape. RESULTS: Experiments on three real PV station datasets released by the State Grid show that TAPD outperforms state-of-the-art forecasting models. Averaged across 1 h, 3 h, 6 h, and 12 h prediction horizons, TAPD reduces mean absolute error (MAE) by 10.09%, 6.74%, and 10.31%on Stations A, B, and C, respectively. CONC…

title: New Graduate Nurses in Charge Nurse Roles: A Narrative Inquiry
abstract: Background The charge nurse role is a complex leadership position that was historically reserved for experienced nurses. Due to high staff turnover and staff shortages in acute care, new nurses are being assigned to leadership roles such as the charge nurse role within their first year of practice. Purpose This study explored the experiences of ten new graduate nurses assigned to the charge nurse role in acute care settings. Methods A narrative inquiry design was used to guide this study. The data were collected in two semi-structured interviews, four weeks apart. Results Three themes were identified: The Charge Nurse Context and Timing, Leadership Preparedness, and Professional Growth: Becoming a Leader. Participants reported that they often felt unprepared due to minimal training and/or resources. Over time and through experience, they reported experiencing professional growth and an understanding of their preferences towards leadership. Conclusion/Implications This study revealed that new nurses can be capable leaders; however, their readiness for leadership may occur at different points within their transition to practice. The findings of this study can help inform the development of resources and practice changes to better support new nurses assigned to clinical leadership roles.

title: Comprehensive Analysis of the Efficient Use of Rolling Stock of Operating Companies: Modeling and Forecasting
abstract: The focus of this study is on the analysis and approaches to forecasting the efficient use of rolling stock of operating companies, including an integrated approach in terms of financial utility of transport space and tariff forecasting. The study uses modeling and forecasting methods, including neural network methods, to forecast the use and pricing of railway cars, as well as a previously developed method for economic and geographical definition of «areas of influence» involved in the process of transporting stations. A new approach is the inclusion of a railway non-linearity coefficient for designated port stations where empty car flows originate. This coefficient is crucial to account for the unique geographic characteristics of the transport network relative to potential destination stations. The result of the study is a geometric routing model that characterizes the competitive market for transportation of empty cars initiated from selected departure stations. This model has been successfully integrated into the Maxima computer mathematics system, demonstrating its practical applicability in real-life scenarios.

title: Predictors of Recovery From Aphasia After Stroke
abstract: Predicting recovery from aphasia after stroke is challenging, yet essential. Accurate prognoses would enable stroke survivors and families to establish realistic expectations and make informed decisions, allow clinicians to plan rehabilitation, and inform the development and implementation of interventions. This review synthesizes current evidence on predictors of aphasia recovery, integrating diverse biological, behavioral, environmental, and temporal determinants into a unified conceptual framework organized around 3 fundamental determinants: the integrity of the language network, neuroplasticity throughout the remaining brain, and the passage of time. Lesion location and extent are powerful predictors, accounting for more than half of the variance in aphasia outcomes, but other interacting factors contribute to heterogeneous recovery trajectories, including variability in language network organization and effects of diaschisis. The capacity for neuroplasticity depends on the brain health and functionality of surviving tissue, but the realization of this potential depends critically on engagement in language use, which can be promoted by intensive speech-language therapy, social participation and supportive communication environments. Recovery follows a predictable decelerating time course, with rapid early gains driven primarily by reperfusion and resolution of dysfunction i…

title: Modeling Hedging of Renewable Energy Price Fluctuations: Risk Management Strategies with Forward Contracts, Futures Contracts, Options, and Energy Swaps
abstract: This paper explores a scientific approach using the technology of modelling and analysis of risk management strategies for renewable energy price fluctuations to achieve economic growth. It investigates the application of forward contracts, futures contracts, options, and energy swaps in mitigating the financial risks associated with price volatility in renewable energy markets. The paper presents mathematical formulations for each of these instruments, provides solutions, and offers a comprehensive analysis of their effectiveness in hedging risk. Numerical simulations demonstrate the application of these models in real-world scenarios, highlighting their role in stabilising energy markets with positive consequential economic growth.

title: A comprehensive analysis of the implementation of socially-adaptive demand response programs in Japan’s electricity market
abstract: Abstract Background Previous studies often overlook the impact of complex socio-demographic factors on consumerresponses to Demand Response Programs (DRPs) in electricity markets. This study addresses this gap by developinga comprehensive socially adaptive modeling framework to analyze the successful implementation of Price-basedDemand Response Programs (PBDRPs) in Japan's unique electricity market.The modeling framework developed in this study integrates a Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS) econometric modelwith a multi-objective optimization model designed to maximize the welfare of both service providers and consumers participating in PBDRPs in the Japan Electric Power Exchange (JEPX) market. The econometric model in corporatesa wide array of variables, including gender, education, lifestyle, and household composition, to reflect how social factors affect consumers’ electricity consumption patterns and their responses to DRPs. Results The findings demonstrate that dynamic pricing strategies tailored to peak, valley, and off-peak hours can effectively manage demand fluctuations by encouraging consumer participation in PBDRPs. A sensitivity analysis ofthe influence of various social factors on consumer demand highlights the importance of gender-specific dynamics inenergy consumption patterns among the elderly Japanese adults, emphasizing the differences between male and femaleseni…

title: Evaluation of Antioxidant Capacity (FRAP) and Antimicrobial Efficacy (ZOI and MIC) of Polyherbal Immunomodulatory Formulations
abstract: Objective: The present study aimed to evaluate and compare the in vitro total antioxidant capacity and antimicrobial efficacy of individual natural extracts (Amla, Chyavanprash, Marking Nut tree, and Gorakhmundi) alongside their optimized polyherbal dosage forms—Tablet Formulation F05 and Granules Formulation F06. Methods: Total antioxidant capacity was assessed via the Ferric Reducing Antioxidant Power (FRAP) assay using Trolox as a reference standard across 10–100 µM. Antimicrobial efficacy against pathogenic Gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Enterobacteriaceae was evaluated using the Zone of Inhibition (ZOI) agar disc diffusion method and the Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) broth macrodilution assay. Statistical analysis was performed using One-Way ANOVA to verify concentration-dependent antibacterial effects. Results: The FRAP assay demonstrated superior ferric reducing power for the combined dosage forms—Tablet Formulation F05 (60.67 µmol TE/g) and Granules Formulation F06 (60.00 µmol TE/g)—compared to individual extracts (25.33–54.00 µmol TE/g). In the ZOI assay, at 0.10 mL application volume, Granules Formulation F06 (27 mm) and Tablet Formulation F05 (25 mm) exhibited significantly larger inhibition zones than single Amla (20 mm) and Chyavanprash (18 mm) extracts. One-Way ANOVA confirmed a statistically significant concentrationdependent antibacteria…

title: Decoupling the Steric Influence: Unveiling the Coupling Mechanism of Internal and External Steric in Phosphoryl Carboxylic Acid Extractants
abstract: Abstract The separation of rare earth elements (REEs) remains a challenge due to their nearly identical ionic radii and chemical properties. Molecular engineering of extractants through the modulation of substituents and alkoxy carbon chains is essential for enhancing selectivity. The rational design of next-generation rare-earth extractants relies on understanding the interplay between structural modules and separation performance. This study successfully decouples the steric contributions of internal α-methyl substitution and external long carbon chains using computational methods. The two contributions are found to be coupled rather than strictly additive, with the external carbon chains dominating the thermodynamic cost of complexation and partially masking the effect of the internal α-methyl substituent. The internal substituent provides a small, ion-dependent modulation of the ligand’s intrinsic binding preference. This research indicates that ligand optimization requires the internal and external steric modules to be treated as coupled, and provides a quantitative basis for targeting extractant performance.

title: A Coupled Critical Shear Crack and Local Bond–Slip Model for Predicting the Shear Capacity of CFRP-Strengthened Reinforced Concrete Beams
abstract: Externally bonded carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) sheets are widely used to strengthen reinforced concrete (RC) beams in shear. However, predicting the CFRP contribution is difficult, since concrete cracking, stirrup action, and CFRP debonding interact at the critical crack. This study presents a mechanics-based model for slender U-wrapped beams with a/d ≥ 2.5. The concrete contribution follows a critical shear crack theory (CSCT)-type criterion, and the crack angle follows the AASHTO strain relation. The CFRP is modeled as discrete crack bridges with a Lu-type bond–slip law, and its contribution is the peak of the summed bridge response, without an assumed effective strain. For 31 external rectangular beams, obtained by screening a published 172-beam database, the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was 12.01%, compared with 21.31% for ACI 440.2 and 16.07% for fib Bulletin 14, and it remained between 9.9% and 14.0% when each program was removed in turn. For an independent six-beam series, the MAPE was 3.71% for the total capacity and 14.78% for the CFRP contribution. The main limitation is that the concrete and CFRP terms are not evaluated at the same crack opening, and enforcing this compatibility would reduce the predictions by 27–33% on average. T-beams, anchored beams, and other configurations are reported separately.

title: Network pharmacology and bioinformatics analysis of the potential mechanism of morin against myocardial infarction
abstract: Background As a typical natural flavonoid compound, morin exerts definite cardioprotective effects. Nevertheless, its specific molecular regulatory mechanisms in the treatment of myocardial infarction have not been fully elucidated. Methods This study combined network pharmacology and bioinformatic strategies to screen candidate targets of morin as well as genes closely associated with myocardial infarction across diverse databases. Further validations were implemented via functional enrichment analysis, three machine learning models including LASSO regression, SVM-RFE and random forest algorithm, immune infiltration assessment and molecular docking verification. Results Through a multi-step screening process, six candidate genes were identified, including ARG1, CDK6, CXCR1, CYP1B1, MMP9, and PFKFB3. These candidate genes are enriched in inflammation- and metabolism-related signaling pathways, including the TNF, AMPK, HIF-1, and IL-17 pathways, as well as pathways involved in arachidonic acid metabolism and phagocytosis. Immune association analysis suggests that these genes are associated with neutrophils, macrophages, and mast cells. Molecular docking simulations predict a potential binding interaction between mulberry pigment and these target proteins. Conclusions Morin may alleviate damage caused by myocardial infarction by regulating immune and inflammatory responses, metab…

title: Cost-aware adaptive energy management system with frequency decoupling for fuel cell hybrid electric vehicles
abstract: Recent advancements in Energy Management Systems (EMS) for Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicles (FCHEVs) have significantly improved power allocation and component lifespan through intelligent optimization methods. The literature has been reported with diverse EMS, but they rely on frequency-based switching between Energy Storage System (ESS) such as fuel cell, battery, and super capacitor. This paper proposes an adaptive EMS, that allocates the power among the fuel cell power, battery power, and super capacitor power based on the power demand transitions. Inspired by the frequency-decoupling method, this paper employs Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to separate the demand power into low-frequency and high-frequency component. In addition, this paper proposes multiple objectives that deal with stable and maximum power output from the energy sources, minimizing fuel consumption and cost associated with the energy sources. These multi-objectives are formulated as an optimization problem, which is solved using Adaptive Population-based Genetic Algorithm (APOGA). The performance of the proposed algorithm is compared against conventional frequency-aware and frequency-unaware EMS for three benchmark drive cycles. The proposed method is found to be better at minimizing fuel consumption and energy storage costs while improving the stability of battery power, fuel cell power and superc…
