title: P14.10.B CDKN2A homozygous deletion defines a distinct treatment response pattern and therapeutic vulnerability in IDH-mutant astrocytoma
abstract: Abstract Background CDKN2A homozygous deletion (HoD) is associated with poor prognosis in IDH-mutant astrocytomas, but its treatment implications remain incompletely understood. Material and Methods We applied machine learning-based contouring of serial peri-cavity MRI FLAIR volumes from post-resection, pre-radiotherapy baseline through early post-treatment intervals, alongside MR spectroscopy. Underlying biology was investigated using transcriptomic analyses of TCGA IDH-mutant gliomas and single-cell RNA sequencing. Functional validation was performed in CDKN2A knock-in models of CDKN2A-null IDH-mutant glioma cell lines. In parallel, in silico screening of cell cycle-targeting compounds, prioritised by neural network-based predictions of blood-brain barrier permeability and clinical feasibility, was followed by in vitro evaluation. Results CDKN2A HoD tumours demonstrated an initial reduction in FLAIR, whereas non-deleted tumours showed gradual reduction or stability. MR spectroscopy suggested elevated 2-hydroxyglutarate (2HG) levels in CDKN2A HoD tumours, consistent with altered metabolism. Transcriptomic analyses revealed enrichment of cell cycle dysregulation, neuronal stemness programs, and increased IDH1 expression, supported by single-cell RNA sequencing and a morphology grade-matched cohort, indicating effects independent of histological grade. Functional validation conf…

title: Perceived contributions of malaria mass drug administration to the 2022 Ebola virus disease response in Uganda: a qualitative study of implementation experiences and lessons learned
Case Report: Complete histopathological response in a patient with pleural mesothelioma
abstract: Introduction We present a patient with pleural mesothelioma (PM), epithelioid subtype, who achieved a complete histopathological response following second-line treatment with the immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) pembrolizumab in combination with lenvatinib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor that targets multiple anti-angiogenic pathways. Case Following first-line chemotherapy, disease progression was observed, and the patient started second-line treatment with pembrolizumab and lenvatinib. After the fourth cycle, a near-complete radiologic response was achieved. The near-complete response persisted until the 22 nd cycle, when the patient unfortunately died. The patient had an overall survival of 16.8 months from the start of second-line treatment and 27.9 months from initial diagnosis. Autopsy revealed that the cause of death was a myocardial infarction, possibly related to the treatment, although the definitive cause could not be established. Furthermore, the autopsy did not identify viable mesothelioma cells in any of the examined tissues, demonstrating a complete histopathological response. Discussion This is the first reported complete histopathological response in PM achieved without prior surgical intervention. Complete responses in PM remain exceptionally rare, with only two previously reported, both following surgical resection and treatment with ICIs. Together, these cases …

title: Synchronous Thermochromic and Heat-Response-Enhanced Anisotropic Conductive Janus Film Functionalized by Upconverting Luminescence for Multi-Scenario Applications
abstract: Abstract Developing stimulus-responsive multifunctional materials for multi-scenarios is meaningful. Herein, synchronous thermochromic and heat-response-enhanced anisotropic conductive Janus films (STHACJFs) are first designed and fabricated by respectively utilizing Janus-nanofiber and composite-nanofiber as microscopic building units to form the down-layer heat-response-enhanced anisotropic conductive Janus-nanofibers array membranes (HACJAMs) and up-layer thermochromic composite-nanofibers array membranes (TCAMs) of Janus films via electrospinning. Thermochromic transition temperatures of TCAMs are innovatively designed to match with response temperatures of HACJAMs, thereby enabling synchronous thermochromism and conductive anisotropy enhancement under single-temperature stimulation. The Janus-nanofiber with two micro-partitions endows HACJAMs with high conductive anisotropy and strong luminescence. An innovative strategy combining the phase transition-enhanced conductivity of W-doped VO2 with the intrinsic conductivity of polyaniline (PANI) is proposed to enhance the conductive anisotropy degree upon heating, and response temperatures of HACJAMs are regulated by adjusting W atomic percentages to tune the phase transition temperatures of W-doped VO2. Upon heating to 60, 55, and 45 °C, W-doped VO2 and PANI synergistically enhance the conductivity along the length direction o…

The impact of a graduated response to advanced COPD with enhanced support (GRACE) on unmet palliative care needs—study protocol for a single-center pilot randomized controlled trial
Resilient supply and demand networks: analysis and stress-testing framework
abstract: Abstract Supply and demand networks (SDNs) are systems of relationships that provide for the allocation of physical goods around the world. These networks are susceptible to shocks that can then propagate through the whole system. Understanding systemic risk and resilience is required to better build and support functional SDNs. In this paper, we demonstrate a new methodology for assessing SDN risk and resilience through implementing stress testing of interconnected networks. We first construct a multilayer multigraph of entities and relationships from a variety of incomplete sources and then infer relationships to construct the SDN. Then we perform forward stress testing by propagating different threat scenarios, including topological risk and resilience modeling. We also implement reverse stress testing where the goal is to evaluate a set of threat scenarios that most likely results in systemic collapse below a risk and resilience tolerance threshold. Agent-based modeling is used as a mathematical foundation for performing both forward and reverse stress testing. Our methodology is demonstrated in a case study focusing on a global copper SDN, outlining its construction, and a scenario analysis for a mine shutdown and resulting spike in copper prices.

title: PCDH15-enriched UC-MSC extracellular vesicles promote neural repair after ischemic stroke through a CEBPD-associated response
From farm to fine dining: trust is the backbone of luxury food supply chains
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how trust is built, maintained and challenged along the understudied luxury food supply chain, which is characterised by more personal transactions and higher quality stakes than conventional agri-food sectors. Design/methodology/approach Using the French Riviera caviar market as the focal empirical setting, the authors conducted 21 semi-structured narrative interviews with chefs (n = 11), distributors (n = 5), and producers (n = 5) selected through purposive and snowball sampling. The authors analysed the interviews using structuring qualitative content analysis, combining main categories derived from a theory-informed interview guide with inductively developed subcategories. Findings Trust in luxury food supply chains emerges as a relational and symbolic construct, shaped by cultural capital, artisanal values and sustained interpersonal engagement. Participants relied primarily on repeated interaction, personal credibility and proactive transparency, rather than on the transactional, system-based trust models typical of conventional food sectors. Trust expectations vary systematically across supply chain roles, while luxury value is symbolically co-created through shared narratives of rarity, craftsmanship, authenticity and heritage. Trust is also particularly fragile: operational failures can simultaneously undermine relational confiden…

title: From NIMBY versus YIMBY to place-attachments and place-logics: understanding residents’ views of place-making in South Africa and Sweden
abstract: Purpose The purpose of the paper is to further the empirical and theoretical understanding of the role of residents and their leaders in local place-making projects. Design/methodology/approach The paper compares reflections on two cases that explore the role of residents and their leaders in various place-making projects from Sweden and South Africa. Findings This study shows that residents’ attitudes towards place-making are more varied and complex than portrayed in the NIMBY-YIMBY dichotomy, and that local leaders play an important role in representing residents on place-making projects. The attitudes and actions of local leaders can vary over time, falling into four broad categories of “allies”, “opponents”, “entrepreneurs” and “guerillas”. However, the self-understanding of leaders as acting in the interests of their place is consistent across these multiple engagements, and there is an enduring and specific vision for development that informs the views and actions of leaders in both cases. This study suggests that local resident and their leaders’ motivations can be strong due to place-attachment and that reasoning is guided by local logics. Originality/value Empirically, the paper adds the perspective of residents and their leaders on the politics of place-making, suggesting that they are often the more consistent in their understanding and vision, whereas external actor…
venue: Journal of Place Management and Development

title: Management consultants – monsters or benign change agents? The case of the NSW transport asset holding entity
abstract: Purpose This study critically examines the role of private consultants in public-sector financial governance under New Public Management (NPM) and New Public Financial Management (NPFM). Focusing on the New South Wales Transport Asset Holding Entity (TAHE), the research investigates how consultancy expertise and accounting technologies were mobilised in the case study to construct a quasi-market entity that advanced short-term fiscal objectives while obscuring long-term financial realities and the public interest. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in political economy and public-interest accounting traditions, the study employs a multi-method, qualitative case study design. Informed by the theoretical lenses of consultocracy and consultology, the analysis triangulates legally vetted and publicly contested documents, including Auditor-General reports, parliamentary inquiries, financial disclosures and investigative journalism, to trace institutional decision-making and intra-firm knowledge practices. Findings The analysis demonstrates that consultants acted as powerful political-institutional actors. They shaped the structural and financial design of TAHE to classify capital funding as equity rather than as an expenditure. Crucially, distinct consultancy teams within a single Big Four firm produced contradictory asset valuations. Internal firm dynamics helped contain these co…

title: Virtual reality booking systems: drivers and ESG outcomes
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how technological, organizational and environmental factors influence the integration of 360° virtual reality-enhanced booking systems (VRBS) and examines the subsequent impact on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance in the hospitality industry. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in the technology–organization–environment (TOE) framework and stakeholder theory, quantitative data were collected from 588 four-star, five-star, and Chinese gold and platinum diamond hotels and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings Relative advantage, digital infrastructure and competitive pressure significantly drive VRBS integration, whereas cybersecurity concerns and organizational agility are nonsignificant antecedents. VRBS integration enables hotels to use resources more responsibly, while enhancing stakeholder trust and transparency, thereby improving ESG performance. Hotels prioritize visible advantages, competitive dynamics and peer behavior over internal capabilities when deciding on integration. Practical implications Hotel managers can adopt VRBS without substantial restructuring because organizational agility and cybersecurity concerns pose minimal barriers. Given the influence of competitive pressure, late-adopting hotels should implement VRBS proactively to remain competitive and meet evol…
venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Empowering Health Cadres for Integrated Management of Non-Communicable Diseases in PLHIV Communities: A Participatory Action Research Approach in Yogyakarta, Indonesia
abstract: Background: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs), including hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease, are an important health concern among People Living with HIV (PLHIV), particularly as they age. In Indonesia, HIV and NCD services are still delivered separately. Community health cadres may help bridge this gap. Objectives: To empower NCD health cadres within an older PLHIV peer-support group to improve NCD awareness, access to care, and links with health services. Methods: We used a Participatory Action Research (PAR) approach with four stages (planning, action, observation, and reflection) in Kelompok Dukungan Sebaya (KDS) Surya Senja, Yogyakarta. In the planning stage, we conducted Focus Group Discussions (FGD) with 26 members and analysed the data using narrative inquiry and thematic analysis. Together with members and health workers, we then formed and trained NCD cadres in a one-day training modelled on the Posbindu PTM (community-based NCD post), followed by routine NCD check-ups at monthly meetings. We reflected on the program using a SWOT analysis. Results: Most participants were aged >50 years (84.62%), and 73.08% reported a history of NCDs. Three themes emerged: low health literacy of NCDs, self-discrimination when accessing healthcare, and low medication adherence. In response, cadres were trained and began routine early-detection check-ups within the communi…

title: Development and perioperative evaluation of a digital health education knowledge graph and intelligent question-answering system for patients with chronic rhinosinusitis
abstract: Background Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a prevalent disease with substantial impact on quality of life. Perioperative health education is essential for patients undergoing endoscopic sinus surgery, yet conventional approaches are constrained by limited inpatient time and poor post-discharge accessibility. Patients frequently turn to unverified online sources, highlighting the urgent need for evidence-based, accessible digital health education tools. Objective To develop an evidence-based health education knowledge graph and a knowledge-base-constrained intelligent question-answering system for CRS, and to preliminarily evaluate its perioperative health education outcomes among patients undergoing endoscopic sinus surgery during the perioperative period. Methods The study was conducted in four sequential phases. First, semi-structured interviews were carried out with 12 patients with CRS selected through purposive sampling to identify their needs and preferences regarding health education. Second, relevant evidence from both Chinese and international literature was systematically retrieved and synthesized, followed by two rounds of Delphi consultation with experts to establish and refine the content of the knowledge graph. Third, the finalized health education content was manually annotated to construct a knowledge graph for structured organization and visualization. The same…

title: Anatomical, physiological, and metabolic trait adjustments in tea leaves under different intercropping systems: implications for ecological tea garden management
abstract: Introduction Intercropping is widely used to promote sustainable tea cultivation, but how different companion-tree configurations are associated with tea leaf functional traits remains insufficiently understood. This study compared leaf trait responses across four tea-based intercropping systems. Methods A replicated field experiment was conducted in a tea plantation in Zhejiang, China, comparing tea monoculture (CK), tea–persimmon (T+P), tea–pecan (T+H), and tea–persimmon–pecan (T+P+H), with three replicate plots per treatment. Leaf anatomical traits, stomatal density and dimensions, soluble protein, soluble sugars, starch, antioxidant-related indicators, and photosynthetic pigments were measured. Principal component analysis (PCA) was used to summarize multivariate trait variation. Results Intercropping generally reduced epidermal and mesophyll thickness. Relative to CK, T+P had 50.2% lower stomatal density but 32.8% longer and 35.7% wider stomata. It was also associated with 15.1%, 30.1%, and 17.4% higher soluble protein, soluble sugar, and starch concentrations, respectively, 79.6% higher total chlorophyll, and 12.1% lower malondialdehyde (MDA). In contrast, T+P+H showed the greatest mesophyll thinning and the highest MDA concentration. The first two PCA axes explained 55.77% of total trait variation and indicated clear multivariate differentiation between T+P and CK. Discu…

title: Information management and decision-making in child and adolescent mental health services in a low-resource healthcare setting
abstract: Purpose Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) in low-resource healthcare settings face workforce shortages, structural barriers and fragmented information systems. Little is known about how CAMHS professionals use information to support operational and tactical decision-making. This study describes how CAMHS professionals manage and use information to support decision-making in a low-resource CAMHS setting. Design/methodology/approach A descriptive qualitative study was conducted using two in-person focus group discussions with 17 CAMHS professionals. Participants were selected through purposive sampling, and data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The interview guide was informed by the Descriptive Model of Decision-Making Levels and Information Management in Hospitals. Findings were discussed in relation to the World Health Organization's Global Strategy on Digital Health (2020–2025). Findings The analysis developed three themes: (1) foundational conditions shaping information-driven decision-making in CAMHS; (2) workforce capacity and role-specific health information system (HIS) use; and (3) alignment between HIS and real-world care delivery and decision-making. Strengthening information-driven decision-making in CAMHS requires reliable infrastructure, system-level governance, role-specific workforce capacity building and people-centred system de…

title: How boards judge CEO readiness: the HR leadership paradox
abstract: Purpose Written for The Practice of Making Decisions section of Management Decision, this article examines how boards judge chief executive officer (CEO) readiness when the available evidence differs across candidates. The HR leadership paradox illustrates this problem. Design/methodology/approach The framework combines published empirical research on succession and executive evaluation with signaling and leadership-recognition theory. A fictional composite case illustrates the six-step routine. No primary empirical data are collected, and the routine has not been empirically validated. Findings A board should first agree on what the future role requires before comparing candidates. It should then ask whether the evidence is relevant, how clearly it shows each candidate's contribution and whether similar contributions are judged consistently. When important questions remain unresolved and a candidate has not met a requirement that must be satisfied before the vote, the board must not appoint the candidate on the available evidence. Practical implications A record documents candidates' decisions, alternative explanations, evidence that challenges initial judgments and the board's confidence in its conclusions. Once all essential requirements are met, the board must explain why remaining risks are acceptable and how it will monitor and respond to them. Originality/value The artic…

title: Non-Asthmatic Eosinophilic Bronchitis as a Cause of Corticosteroid-Responsive Chronic Cough: A Review of Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Management
abstract: Nonasthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis (NAEB) is characterized by a persistent, predominantly dry or minimally productive cough in the absence of variable airflow obstruction or airway hyperresponsiveness. The condition may follow a recurrent or persistent course, and some patients may subsequently develop asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), although the risk of progression remains uncertain. NAEB is estimated to account for approximately 5%–30% of chronic cough cases evaluated in specialist settings. Exposure to environmental allergens and occupational irritants has been implicated as a potential contributing factor, although its precise etiology and underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. NAEB shares several inflammatory features with asthma, including eosinophilic airway inflammation and increased inflammatory mediator activity. However, differences in the distribution of airway inflammation, airway remodeling, and the involvement of interleukin-13 (IL-13) and prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) may contribute to their distinct clinical characteristics. Induced sputum analysis demonstrating airway eosinophilia is the reference standard for diagnosis, while fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) may serve as a supportive biomarker but cannot reliably establish or exclude NAEB independently. Inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) remain the first-line treatment, alt…

title: SmartRef: A Low-Cost Embedded Vision-Based Referee System for Real-Time Badminton Officiating Using Edge AI
abstract: Human officiating in fast racket sports is limited by visibility, reaction time and bias, while automated line-calling and video-review systems such as Hawk-Eye depend on costly multi-camera installations and centralised processing that grassroots tournaments cannot afford. This paper presents SmartRef, a low-cost, portable, vision-based referee system that does all of its processing on a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B (8 GB) without any internet connection. Live video from a network camera (an IP camera or a smartphone streaming through DroidCam) or a pre-recorded match video is processed with OpenCV. A lightweight YOLOv5n/YOLOv8n detector locates the shuttlecock and the players, SORT/DeepSORT keeps their identities across frames, and a geometric rule checker compares their positions with a calibrated court boundary to flag ball-out and net-related events. Each violation triggers a GPIO-driven buzzer and LED, an overlay on the video frame and an entry in a Flask-based dashboard that offers a live view, a scoreboard, a timestamped event log and replay for human verification. In controlled indoor and outdoor tests, SmartRef correctly classified 46 of 50 ball in/out cases (92%) with a processing time of 50 to 80 ms per frame, worked stably up to 10 m from the camera and gave buzzer and LED alerts with 100% reliability. It was faster and more consistent than human officiating for ball in/…

title: Women's Empowerment in India: A Decade of Progress Across Sectors (2015–2025)
abstract: Between 2015 and 2025, women’s status in India shifted measurably across education, health, work, finance, and politics, propelled by a mix of constitutional change, targeted schemes, and broader social transition. This paper tracks that decade across seven linked domains (education, health, economic participation, financial inclusion and entrepreneurship, political representation, legal and workplace reform, and digital access), drawing on official statistics from the Ministry of Education’s All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE), the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), the National Family Health Survey (NFHS), and Ministry of Women and Child Development records, supplemented by peer-reviewed and independent policy research. The female Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education has exceeded the male ratio for the seventh consecutive year; the female labour force participation rate has nearly doubled since 2017–18, from 23.3% to 41.7%; over half of Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) account holders are women; and the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023, reserving one-third of the seats in the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies for women, marks a watershed for political inclusion. Alongside these gains, the paper documents persistent shortfalls in wage parity, formal employment, deci…

title: Medication Safety Risks Associated With Inappropriate Use of Non-Crushable Tablets in Enterally Fed Patients: A Nationwide Cohort Study
abstract: Background and Objectives: Hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding are at high risk of medication administration errors. In clinical practice, non-crushable oral tablets may be inappropriately prescribed, potentially resulting in adverse outcomes. This study examined the association between inappropriate use of non-crushable oral tablets during hospitalization and early post-discharge emergency department (ED) visits among patients receiving enteral feeding. Methods: We conducted a nationwide population-based cohort study using a national health insurance claims database in 2020, including 173,476 hospitalized patients receiving enteral feeding. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate the association between inappropriate use of non-crushable tablets and the hazard of the first ED visit during the 3-day post-discharge follow-up period. Results: Among 173,476 patients, 40.2% were exposed to inappropriate medication use. Exposure was associated with a significantly higher hazard of a first ED visit during the 3-day post-discharge follow-up period (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.954; 95% confidence interval, 1.721-2.217). The association varied significantly across age groups and inpatient departments, with the largest adjusted hazard ratios observed among patients aged <65 years and those treated in hematology and oncology, infectious diseases, and neurosurgery. title: Symmetrical Phase Transition of Pb/Mo(110) System Investigated by Reflection High-Energy Electron Diffraction
abstract: The process of change of the surface structures of the Pb/Mo (110) system is discussed on the basis of the reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) analysis results. The appearance of the (10×4), (2×3), (2×10), and (3×2) structures is confirmed, and the (2×3) and (2×10) structures are confirmed to possess other mirror structures with respect to the [1-10] Mo direction. The (10×4) structure maintains a nearly regular trianglular configuration, similar to the atomic arrangement along the Pb (111) plane. Regarding the (2×3), (2×10), and (3×2) structures, their features commonly indicate the line coincidence along both the [1-11] and [1-1-1] directions.

title: Cybersecurity requirements for nuclear power plant instrumentation and control systems in Ukraine: challenges and future directions for implementation
abstract: This Perspective article presents the development and practical implementation of cybersecurity requirements for nuclear power plants (NPP) instrumentation and control (I&C) systems in Ukraine. Particular attention is given to NP 306.2.237-2022 “Cybersecurity Requirements for Instrumentation and Control Systems of Nuclear Power Plants to Ensure Nuclear and Radiation Safety” (NP 306.2.237-2022) as the key regulatory instrument establishing a specialized approach to cybersecurity of NPP I&C systems. The paper examines the integration of cybersecurity requirements into the nuclear and radiation safety framework, the implementation process for I&C system developers and the operating organization, and the main technical, methodological, and organizational challenges encountered during implementation. The adoption of specialized, safety-oriented cybersecurity regulations is an essential step toward protecting nuclear I&C systems, but their practical effectiveness depends on translating general requirements into technically justified measures compatible with nuclear safety functions. On this basis, priorities for further development are proposed, and lessons of potential relevance to other countries are outlined.

title: Historical Nansen cast temperature profiles and the ocean heat content changes since 19th century
abstract: Ocean heat content (OHC) estimates rely on subsurface temperature observations whose abundance, quality, and accuracy have changed over time as oceanographic techniques and methods have developed. The majority of the available global OHC time series begins in the 1950s when the International Geophysical Year 1957-1958 (IGY) observational campaign resulted in a rapid improvement of the observational basis. However, a significant amount of subsurface temperature observations had already been accumulated before the IGY. Extending knowledge back in time beyond current estimates provides further insight into global changes in the ocean-atmosphere system. We perform a three-step quality control (QC) of the Nansen cast temperature profiles with a focus on the time period before 1970. The QC includes automated and manual control of temperature observations, along with the quality control of temperature anomalies. We use the World Ocean Circulation Experiment/Argo Global Hydrographic climatology, based on high-quality temperature observations between 1990 and 2025, as the reference. To interpolate temperatures vertically, we use the temperature anomaly method by Frankignoul (1981). This method yields smaller interpolation errors than linear interpolation and the Reiniger and Ross (1968) parabolic method. Corrections for depth bias in Nansen cast profiles are also suggested. The oldest t…

EP05.05 Prognostic value of cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers in primary central nervous system lymphoma: a substudy of the PRICELUS study
abstract: Abstract Background Primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) is a malignant brain tumour which may be cured by intensive therapy. Outcome is highly variable and available risk models such as the IELSG and MSKCC prognostic scores predict survival only to some extent. Recently, several diagnostic biomarkers measurable in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) have been identified, including the MYD88 L265P mutation, interleukin-10 (IL10), chemokine ligand 13 (CXCL13), among others. Few studies have investigated the prognostic role of this unique set of biomarkers in PCNSL. In this additional analysis of the multicenter PRICELUS diagnostic test accuracy study, we investigated the prognostic value of selected molecular and immune CSF biomarkers for survival in patients with PCNSL. Material and Methods Patients with a final diagnosis of PCNSL who underwent CSF analysis as part of the diagnostic work-up were enrolled in this multicenter prospective cohort study across five Dutch hospitals between 2021 and 2025. The primary and secondary outcomes were overall and progression-free survival (OS, PFS), respectively. MYD88 mutation was evaluated as a dichotomous marker (absent versus present), the other biomarkers were used as continuous, log-transformed values. Prognostic associations were analyzed using the KM method and univariable Cox proportional hazard regression. For secondary analysis, …

title: From ashes to agency: informal-settlement fires, intergenerational power, and democratic survival in Gauteng, South Africa
abstract: Introduction Recurrent fires in South Africa's informal settlements are governed as technical emergencies, despite being produced and experienced through unequal infrastructures, insecure tenure, and uneven state protection. This study examines how young and older residents of fire-prone informal settlements in the Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality interpret risk, respond to emergencies, negotiate recovery, and convert disaster experience into civic action. Methods We used an interpretivist narrative design combining semi-structured interviews, focus-group discussions, participant-generated photographs, ethnographic observation, and stakeholder interviews. The focal sample comprised 22 residents aged 15–35 years or 60 years and older, recruited through an environmental citizenship programme and selected for direct experience of fire-related loss, injury, or displacement. Thematic analysis integrated deliberative-democratic criteria inclusion, reason-giving, and legitimacy with a combative account of conflict and emotion as constitutive of democratic politics. Results Across prevention, response, and recovery, residents described a consistent governance asymmetry: households and neighbors generated situated risk knowledge, evacuation plans, warning networks, bucket chains, and mutual aid, whereas formal intervention was often delayed, reactive, or insufficiently responsive to…

title: Workplace health interventions in SMEs – experiences of employees performing as in-house facilitators
abstract: Purpose Facilitation is a key factor in workplace health and organizational interventions. However, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) often lack the resources needed to access professional facilitation. The purpose of this study is to examine how in-house facilitators are experienced in workplace health interventions in SMEs and to identify the qualities that enable in-house facilitators to perform this facilitation role effectively as an alternative to engaging external facilitators or internal professional process consultants. Design/methodology/approach A multiple-case study approach was used across three Danish SMEs in the manufacturing and Information Technology sectors, each of which conducted two interventions. Each company appointed two in-house facilitators among employees who had no formal facilitator training. Data were collected over six months through FishBone, Chronological Workshops and interviews with employees, in-house facilitators and managers, followed by a completion survey. Findings The in-house facilitators supported the identification of workplace health issues and contributed with contextually relevant solutions. Besides demonstrating established facilitator competencies, participants highlighted two key characteristics: (1) contextual sensitivity; the ability to align actions with the organizational environment and participant needs and (2) cre…
venue: International Journal of Workplace Health Management

title: Long-term soil organic carbon responses to management combinations under climate scenarios in wheat-based rotations: a case study from Jiangsu, China
abstract: Abstract Background Assessing cropland carbon sequestration potential requires quantifying soil organic carbon (SOC) responses to management over time and across climates. Using the General Ensemble Biogeochemical Modeling System (GEMS), we reconstructed 0–20 cm SOC in Jiangsu wheat-based rotations during 1985–2022 and compared management contributions to projected SOC sequestration during 2023–2060. A three-factor, two-level factorial design combined tillage, straw return (65%, 100%) and replacement of mineral fertilizer N with organic fertilizer N (10%, 30%). We simulated eight combinations under present climate and two Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1–2.6 and SSP5–8.5). Results Simulated regional mean SOC stock increased by 18.4 Mg C ha − 1 during 1985–2022. Under present climate, business-as-usual (BAU) management increased simulated regional mean SOC stock by 13.7 Mg C ha − 1 during 2023–2060. Raising straw return to 100% or organic fertilizer substitution to 30% added a further 10.9 and 1.7 Mg C ha − 1 to the 2060 stock, respectively. Mean annual relative SOC sequestration rates under 100% straw return remained positive but declined across successive periods, from 0.42 to 0.60 in 2023–2032 to 0.12–0.14 Mg C ha − 1 yr − 1 in 2053–2060. Each 100% straw return combination had higher SOC stock than BAU in 2060 across more than 99.6% of cropland, whereas non-BAU combination…

title: Big Data Analytics on Stock Price Prediction: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models (2018-2026)
abstract: The issue of predicting stock prices is no secret. This review looks at papers from 2018-2026 that look at various models both from a traditional ML perspective (random forests, gradient boosting, support vectors) and from a deep learning perspective (LSTM, graph networks, transformers) and how they can be applied to big data analytics. Overall deep models offer superiority on richer/higher frequency data whereas tree based models offer continual competitiveness on tabular data. However, evaluation can be very important and issues such as leakage and not considering transaction cost can occur. Section 6 provides some key findings. Section 7 details some open questions. Finally, there is a brief discussion of what is going on at a broader level within India regarding data analytics, AI adoption and financial institutions.
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Commerce, Management & Social Science

title: A Three-Tier Network Traffic Analysis and Prediction Architecture for VNFs Using SDN and Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Virtualised Network Functions (VNF) is one of the layers of Network Virtualization Function. It enables the virtualisation of network services so they no longer need to run on specialised commodity hardware. This shift reduces capital and operational expenditure for businesses or organisations. VNF offers specific benefits, but also faces significant security concerns. This work proposes a Software Defined Networks (SDN)- and Machine Learning (ML)-based defence mechanism for detecting and mitigating attacks against VNFs. The proposed solution embeds ML models to drive the SDN controller’s network traffic classification decisions. However, the current state of the art falls short. Existing ML deployments to combat cyberattacks focus predominantly on a single type of network traffic analysis, usually dictated by the dataset used. This research presents stack models for combating cyberattacks using multi-tier traffic analysis at the packet, flow, and session levels. The solution employs several techniques, including a sliding window and approximate aggregation, to facilitate flow and session levels prediction. These ensure that the model receives sufficient network traffic information before making a decision. Classification results show varying performance: best-ensemble macro-F1 scores of 0.97 at the packet level, 0.91 at the flow level, and 0.88 at the session level. T…
venue: Journal of Network and Systems Management

title: Building open communication channels
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings Staff at a large research organization rated their incident reporting system easy to use and worth using, yet four in ten were uncomfortable raising incidents with their own supervisor, which tells executives the constraint sits in the manager relationship and the feedback loop rather than the technology. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.

title: Intervention and management strategies for emergence agitation in children undergoing general anesthesia: a scoping review from a nursing perspective
abstract: Objective To map interventions for emergence agitation (EA) in children undergoing general anesthesia, clarify nursing roles and safety boundaries, and integrate the evidence into a preliminary perioperative nursing management framework. Methods This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework, its refinement by Levac et al., and the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Six databases were searched to establish a parent evidence database through January 20, 2026; forward and backward citation tracking continued through June 30, 2026. Focused screening used population, intervention, comparison, outcomes, and study design (PICOS) criteria. Two reviewers independently selected sources and extracted data; unresolved disagreements were referred to a third reviewer. Source characteristics, intervention components, and outcomes were summarized descriptively using data charting and inductive content analysis. No formal methodological quality or risk-of-bias assessment was performed. Results Eleven sources were included: two scoping reviews, one systematic review, one network meta-analysis, six randomized controlled trials, and one quasi-experimental study. Four categories were identified: preoperative preparation, family involvement, post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) recovery management, and anesthesiologist-led pharmacologic strategies requiring nursing colla…

title: Using public health department notifications to link gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men to HIV prevention care: a feasibility pilot study
abstract: Background A recent bacterial sexually transmitted infection (STI) diagnosis marks increased HIV risk; yet gay and bisexual men (GMB), and other men who have sex with men diagnosed outside specialist sexual health services may not be offered pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). Overseas-born GBM are an increasing proportion of new HIV diagnoses in Australia, and were a priority group. We evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of using mandatory STI surveillance notifications to link GBM not already on PrEP to prevention services. Methods In a pilot in Melbourne (January−September 2025), adult GBM living in the South East Public Health Unit catchment notified with syphilis, gonorrhoea, or Mpox, and not on PrEP, or managed by a high-caseload service were offered nurse-led navigation to PrEP, HIV testing, and vaccination services. Primary outcomes were feasibility (participant retention, time taken, barriers) and acceptability (5-point Likert scale). Results Of 631 STI notifications (615 individuals), 214 were eligible and 61 (28.5%) were enrolled; 39 (64%) completed 6-week follow-up. All 30 survey respondents who answered rated the intervention acceptable. Each participant required approximately 1.25–1.8 h of nurse time. Key feasibility challenges included incomplete contact information in notification data, clinician gatekeeping, and participant preference for SMS over telephon…

From Retrospective Association to Predictive Integration: A Review of AI-Based Temporal Forecasting of Urban Greenery and Its Implications for Urban Happiness
abstract: Urban greenery is increasingly recognised as a non-pharmacological, nature-based intervention for subjective well-being and mental health. However, most existing research is retrospective: it assesses the impact of greenery on people’s happiness today. Urban planning and preventive public health need to know how greenery will affect residents’ happiness in the future (for instance, in ten years). This article asks whether existing studies can answer that question. The review is based on 35 studies published between 2018 and 2026 in environmental psychology, remote sensing, artificial intelligence and urban planning. It covers four major aspects: the pathways through which greenery supports happiness, how greenery “exposure” or dose is measured, how AI technologies can help predict the dose–response effect of greenery on happiness, and statistical methods and study design. The review finds that forecasting studies seldom consider human outcomes, while well-being studies rely almost entirely on observed rather than forecasted exposure. It also identifies a problem of metric translation: indicators that closely reflect experienced greenery rarely have reliable predictive models. The article uses Ahmedabad, India, as a case to develop an approach suited to hot, rapidly developing Global South cities with limited evidence and misleading local vegetation patterns. It proposes a six-s…

title: ORS FXNet a reinforcement learning assisted dual phase LSTM framework for multi currency INR exchange rate forecasting
An updated ensemble forecasting model for district-level dengue prediction in the Mekong Delta Region of Vietnam: model refinement and evaluation
abstract: Background The original district-level dengue forecasting ensemble for Vietnam’s Mekong Delta Region (MDR) showed strong overall accuracy but had two key limitations: forecasted outbreak peaks lagged behind observed timing, and outbreaks were under-detected during periods of rapidly increasing incidence. Methods We evaluated 57 candidate models varying in spatial structure, seasonal representation, and covariates, including flexible harmonic seasonality and climate-driven covariates (mosquito thermal suitability, cumulative precipitation), assessed using the Continuous Ranked Probability Score and Brier score. The six best-performing models were combined into a revised ensemble using district- and horizon-specific Brier score weighting, trained on 2010–2015 data, cross-validated over 2016–2020 and evaluated over 2021–2025 for the on-season period (April–November), with outbreak detection judged against observed outbreaks, defined as cases above the 95th percentile of the same district and calendar month in preceding years. Results At the 3-month forecast horizon, the revised ensemble achieved 66.3% sensitivity and 89.1% specificity, compared with 43.4% sensitivity and 91.7% specificity for the original model, and overall accuracy improved from 84% to 87% (see Extended Data). Conclusions The revised ensemble, incorporating updated candidate models and outbreak-focused weighting,…

title: EP03.17 Predicting sites of tumour progression in the invasive margin of glioblastomas (PRaM-GBM Study): A multicentre pragmatic imaging study
abstract: Abstract Background Despite advances in surgery and radiotherapy, glioblastoma patients often experience progression within a year, adjacent to the resection cavity and high-dose radiotherapy region. Conventional imaging methods are not sensitive enough to detect invasive tumour cells, leaving occult tumour undetected. We have developed a diffusion tissue signature technique using diffusion tensor MRI (DTI) that can locate occult tumour and predict their pattern of progression. This multicentre, pragmatic imaging study aims to qualify our DTI method as a biomarker to predict sites of tumour progression to improve surgical and radiotherapy treatment volumes. Material and Methods Patients with imaging findings of glioblastoma for whom the operating surgeon thought they could resect >90% of enhancing tumour, and that the patient would be suitable for chemoradiotherapy were recruited. Patients with imaging findings of glioblastoma for whom the operating surgeon thought they could resect >90% of the enhancing tumour, and that the patient would be suitable for chemoradiotherapy were recruited. Patients were imaged preoperatively and at progression using diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). The DTI was processed to generate anisotropic diffusion tissue maps (DTI-q). Both sets of images were coregistered, and each pre-operative voxel was classified based on the imaging at progression …

title: The Lincolnshire Unit for Mental Health Research: a programme pre-protocol for place-based, co-produced, applied mental health research
abstract: Background Mental health research opportunities are unevenly distributed. Lincolnshire, a county in England, combines dispersed rural populations, coastal deprivation, and small urban areas, with substantial variation in mental health need and access to support. The Lincolnshire Unit for Mental Health Research (LUMHR) programme has received five years of foundational National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) funding to establish lasting research capability and generate evidence relevant locally and beyond. Methods This programme pre-protocol describes three connected themes: Connect (access), Prevent (wellbeing), and Respond (crisis and suicide prevention), informed by previous priority-setting with 520 regional stakeholders. Their common approach combines evidence synthesis and local insight, co-design or contextual adaptation, feasibility testing, and assessment of the evidence needed for subsequent decisions. Further synthesis, primary research and externally funded definitive or multicentre evaluation will be pursued where required. A county-wide observatory will connect learning from linked health records, geospatial analysis, crisis intelligence, and the Living in Lincolnshire citizen-science panel. Public involvement, inclusion, responsible research and innovation, health economics, knowledge mobilisation, and research capacity development run throughout. An…

title: EP12.08 Latent patterns of white matter injury are associated with cognitive deficits in glioblastoma
abstract: Abstract Background There is considerable variability in cognitive deficits in glioblastoma patients. The reasons for this variability in domains such as executive function, attention and language have not been clearly identified. It is also unclear what the neuroanatomical correlates of these deficits are in these patients. We applied a multivariate data-driven approach to investigate the underlying patterns of white matter damage with cognition using neuropsychological screening (NPS) tools and diffusion MRI in glioblastoma patients. Material and Methods 44 patients with glioblastoma at a single centre underwent preoperative NPS and multimodality structural and diffusion MRI. Principal component analysis was used to identify the latent cognitive deficits. Tumours were segmented on structural images. Whole brain tractometry was performed to segment the white matter tracts and the lesion load in individual tracts calculated. Partial least squares analysis was used to map the principal component scores with patterns of white matter lesion load in a single multivariate model. Tract-based spatial analysis was performed to identify specific regions of the brain associated with microstructural white matter abnormalities (Fractional Anisotropy). Results PLS analysis of tract-specific lesion load identified three independent patterns of tumour infiltration predicting cognitive impairm…

title: Spatial Prototype and Multiscale Expert Multiple-Instance Learning for Breast Cancer Subtype Prediction
abstract: Breast cancer subtype prediction from whole-slide images (WSIs) remains difficult because subtype morphology overlaps, class imbalance can bias training, and conventional multiple-instance learning (MIL) may discard relationships between neighboring patches. Evidence captured at one patch-aggregation scale may also be insufficient for every patient. We propose Spatial Prototype and Multiscale Expert Multiple-Instance Learning (SPME-MIL) for patient-level prediction of four PAM50 subtypes. SPME-MIL combines prototype-based patch aggregation, a global K-means cluster representation, and features that describe spatial relationships between neighboring patches. A WSI-level adaptation of the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) augments the less frequent classes. Using patch coordinates, we average neighboring patch features to form three aggregation scales. The Hybrid classifier conditionally refines Luminal A/B predictions from a main model. The Cascade classifier first separates Luminal from Non-Luminal tumors, then predicts the subtype within the selected group. A patient-level prediction rule selects one of their subtype probability vectors. On the held-out test set, SPME-MIL achieved an accuracy of 0.6933 and a macro-F1 score of 0.6035. The prediction rule increased macro-F1 by 0.0651 over the stronger individual classifier. SPME-MIL also achieved the highest pat…

title: An explainable multi-source framework for Parkinson’s disease diagnosis and progression prediction using speech, gait, and clinical biomarkers
abstract: Background Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder whose manifestations can be observed through speech, gait, and clinical assessment measures. Machine learning methods have shown potential for automated PD assessment; however, reported performance can be substantially affected by the validation strategy when multiple observations from the same participant are present. Objective This study presents an explainable multi-source framework for evaluating speech-, gait-, and clinical telemonitoring-based Parkinson’s disease assessment with particular emphasis on subject-independent validation. Methods Three publicly available datasets were analyzed independently because they originate from different cohorts and do not provide a common patient-level population suitable for direct multi-source assessment. The UCI Parkinson’s Speech dataset contains 195 recordings, the Parkinson’s Telemonitoring dataset contains 5,875 observations from 42 subjects, and the PhysioNet Gait in Parkinson’s Disease dataset contains 113 recordings. Speech and gait were evaluated as binary classification tasks, while total UPDRS was evaluated as a regression task. Subject-independent validation was performed using grouped cross-validation based on participant identifiers. Model performance was assessed using multiple classification and regression metrics, and SHAP-based analysis w…

title: Molecular Docking and ADMET Prediction of Piper guineense and Telfairia occidentalis Phytoconstituents Targeting DPP-4 and PPARγ Receptors
abstract: Diabetes mellitus remains a leading non-communicable metabolic disorder worldwide, driving continued interest in affordable, effective, and safe therapeutic agents from indigenous medicinal plants. This study aims to evaluate the antidiabetic potential of phytoconstituents from Piper guineense (uziza) and Telfairia occidentalis (fluted pumpkin) targeting dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4, PDB ID: 4FFW) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ, PDB ID: 5Y2O), two validated antidiabetic drug targets, using in silico methods. Phytoconstituents from both plants were retrieved from PubChem and docked against DPP-4 and PPARγ crystal structures using PyRx, with sitagliptin and pioglitazone as reference ligands. Receptor-ligand interactions were analyzed with BIOVIA Discovery Studio Visualizer 2020. SwissADME and ADMETLab were used to analyze the pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles of ligands with binding affinity comparable to the reference ligands. Of the 125 P. guineense and 77 T. occidentalis phytoconstituents docked, 14 and 8, respectively, showed binding affinities equal or superior to the standards. Notably, gamma-tocopherol and a related dihydrochromenol derivative, both from P. guineense, showed binding affinities for DPP-4 (-9.9 kcal/mol) and PPARγ (-10.7 kcal/mol) exceeding sitagliptin (-8.4 kcal/mol) and pioglitazone (-8.8 kcal/mol). Most ligands satisfied …

title: Prediction and SHAP-based interpretation of zinc removal from aqueous solution using activated charcoal via optimized hybrid machine learning models
abstract: Introduction Although much research has examined heavy‐metal adsorption from aqueous solutions on activated charcoal, predicting zinc removal is difficult because the interaction is complex and nonlinear. Traditional experimental methods are time‐consuming and expensive. High heavy‐metal removal efficiency is important for sustainable water treatment and optimizing adsorption processes. Polynomial response surface models assume low‐order smooth behavior, and kinetic and isotherm models are valid only for the conditions under which they were fitted. Methods Recently ANN have been widely used but they need large datasets and have litter interpretability. For small‐size dataset, Support Vector Regression (SVR) is most suitable model, but its performance highly relies on its parameter adjustment. Additionally, a systematic comparison between optimized SVR and ensemble SVR approaches has not been explored much. This study proposed a Fennec Fox Optimization SVR (FFO‐SVR) and two ensemble models i.e. Multivariate Adaptive Regression Splines (MARS), and General Regression Neural Network (GRNN). Four operational parameters, contact time, initial concentration, adsorbent dosage, and solution volume, were used to predict zinc removal efficiency. Results and Discussion All three models are compared using statistical performance matrices. FFO‐SVR achieved the largest coefficient of determin…

title: Multifractal Design of Protective Aluminosilicide Coatings: Saturation Kinetics, Structural Homogeneity and Microhardness Prediction in Heat-Resistant Nickel Alloys
abstract: The kinetics of thermal diffusion saturation, structure and properties of protective aluminosilicide coatings on heat-resistant nickel alloys EP539LI and ChS70 were studied. Saturation was carried out in powder mixtures based on ferroaluminum, ferrosilicon and Fe-Al-Si ligatures with the activator Na 2 SiF 6 at temperatures of 860–950 °C and holdings of 3–12 hours. For a quantitative assessment of the heterogeneous structure of the surface layer, multifractal analysis of microstructure images was used with the calculation of the Renyi dimension, the singularity spectrum f (α) and statistical parameters ( D 0 , Δ, K , Δ f (α)). Regression dependencies of microhardness on multifractal characteristics were established ( R 2 = 0.93–0.96). It has been shown that increased structural homogeneity and order (increased D 0 , Δ, and K ) correlates with increased microhardness and coating thickness. The results allow to predict optimal coating application modes and to use multifractal analysis as a quality control tool for protective layers for gas turbine engines.

title: Explainability-based virtual metrology for surface roughness prediction in lubrication-assisted turning under variable conditions
abstract: Abstract Accurate and rapidly deployable prediction of surface roughness is essential in lubrication-assisted hard turning because conventional physics-based simulations remain computationally intensive and do not readily capture lubrication-dependent thermo-tribological effects. This study developed an Artificial Intelligence-based Manufacturing Process Optimization and Design (AIMPOD) framework to model surface roughness in turning of AISI D2 steel under dry, flood, cryogenic, and minimum quantity lubrication (MQL) conditions. The parametric window included cutting speed $$V=80\text {--}307.867$$ m/min, feed rate $$f=0.05\text {--}0.24$$ mm/rev, and depth of cut $$a_p=0.15\text {--}1.20$$ mm, while the measured roughness ranged from $$R_a=0.31$$ to $$1.265~\mu \text {m}$$ . Exploratory analysis showed that feed rate was the dominant variable, with the strongest correlation to roughness ( $$r=0.74$$ ), compared with depth of cut ( $$r=0.31$$ ) and cutting speed ( $$r=-0.24$$ ). Gradient Boosting was the strongest individual learner, with $$R^2_{\textrm{test}}=0.943$$ , RMSE $$=0.05~\mu \textrm{m}$$ , and MAE $$=0.03~\mu \textrm{m}$$ . The genetically weighted ensemble achieved $$R^2_{\textrm{test}}=0.9434$$ and RMSE $$=0.0492~\mu \textrm{m}$$ , closely matching the best individual model. Genetic optimization was used to determine model-combination weights rather than machining…

Early prediction of treatment failure in anxiety and depressive disorders
abstract: Background Treatment failure rates in psychotherapy for depression and anxiety disorders, like cognitive behavioral therapy and interpersonal therapy, differ between 56 and 65%. Nevertheless, therapists often fail to detect treatment failure and overestimate treatment progress. Although supervision is commonly used to improve treatment outcomes, little is known about supervisors’ ability to detect or predict treatment failure. Routine outcome monitoring (ROM) is known to facilitate early detection of treatment failure. To improve ROM there is a need for measurable predictors that can be incorporated in the ROM, such as readiness for change or causal attributions. In this paper we study if therapists and supervisors are able to predict early treatment failure, and if illness perceptions and readiness for change are predictors of treatment failure. Methods In an outpatient mental health care center in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, 172 patients receiving cognitive behavioral therapy or interpersonal therapy for depressive or anxiety disorders were included. Early treatment failure, was assessed at session eight, approximately halfway through treatment. Treatment failure was defined as less than 50% reduction in symptoms within the clinical range of the questionnaire, or less than 25% reduction in total symptom score on the depressive and anxiety measures. Therapists’ and supervisors…

title: BI-RADS-Net: Multi-Task Learning for Structured Breast Lesion Characterization and Malignancy Prediction in Ultrasound Images
abstract: Breast ultrasound imaging is widely used for breast lesion assessment; however, automated diagnostic systems often provide limited insight into the semantic characteristics underlying their predictions. This study presents BI-RADS-Net, a multi-task deep learning framework designed to jointly predict five ultrasound BI-RADS descriptors, a continuous malignancy score, and binary benign/malignant classification. The proposed architecture employs a shared VGG-16 encoder with seven task-specific prediction heads, enabling joint optimization of descriptor classification, malignancy regression, and binary classification objectives. The framework incorporates a consistency objective intended to encourage agreement between the regression and binary classification outputs. An internal evaluation was conducted using a curated collection of 1,192 breast ultrasound images aggregated from the BUSI and BUSIS repositories. In the reported internal comparison, BI-RADS-Net achieved an accuracy of 91.1%, sensitivity of 88.7%, specificity of 92.8%, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.941. These results represent descriptive comparisons against two internal model variants and do not establish statistical significance. The study is limited by incomplete dataset-level records, the absence of verified patient-level data partitioning, and the lack of independent ext…

title: Geometry-based prediction of built imperfections for additively manufactured complex metamaterials
abstract: Abstract Despite the high structural flexibility offered by additive manufacturing (AM), the effective manufacturability of complex metamaterials with highly non-periodic architectures is often limited by process-induced defects such as unsupported overhangs, disconnected features, and enclosed cavities. These limitations are particularly critical for disordered structures, where geometric complexity precludes straightforward design rules and systematic screening. We present an algorithmic framework that relies solely on geometric criteria to detect critical features in laser-based powder bed fusion printing. The method, based on persistent homology and local geometric criteria, identifies regions prone to fabrication failure through voxel-based analysis, including unsupported material, restricted-access voids, and weak connections. These criteria are combined into a unified procedure to assess the printability of candidate structures prior to manufacturing. The approach is demonstrated on spinodoid metamaterials, whose morphologies provide an ideal test case for complex and/or disordered structures. To experimentally validate the proposed methodology, comparisons with several samples produced by laser-based powder bed fusion of metals using 316L stainless steel powder are presented. Overall, we see that all critical defects were correctly isolated from other structural arrange…

title: Intelligent prediction of time-varying transmission ratio in harmonic drive for end-effector positioning accuracy enhancement of industrial robot
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to enhance the absolute positioning accuracy of industrial robot end-effectors under dynamic operating conditions through joint-level transmission error correction. Design/methodology/approach An intelligent regression model is designed that fuses differentiable innovation search, multi-branch convolutional network, bidirectional long short-term memory network, squeeze-and-excitation attention mechanism and kernel density estimation. The model predicts instantaneous reduction ratios of the fourth, fifth and sixth joints. To fully excite nonlinear characteristics of transmission, a random path generation strategy based on nonuniform B-splines and a cryptographically strong hybrid entropy source is proposed, achieving dense coverage of the workspace. The predicted ratios are subsequently fed into a flexible-joint dynamics model, with driving torques corrected via proportional-derivative control and injected as feedforward compensation to enhance end-effector positioning accuracy under dynamic operating conditions. Findings End-effector position accuracy compensation experiments demonstrate that, compared with the fixed reduction ratio model, the mean errors in X, Y and Z directions are reduced by 40.0%, 69.4% and 71.3%, respectively, while the standard deviations are reduced by 1.6%, 13.4% and 11.8%. The proposed method not only reduces the mean end-effect…

How do incentive and penalty mechanisms enhance the credibility of blue carbon credit markets? A game-theoretic analysis of multi-stakeholder collaborative governance strategies
abstract: Introduction Protecting and restoring blue carbon ecosystems is an important nature-based solution for mitigating global warming and promoting sustainable coastal development. As blue carbon projects enter carbon markets, credit credibility is critical to realising their climate and financial benefits. Methods This study develops a tripartite evolutionary game model involving project developers, third-party verifiers, and government regulators to examine blue carbon credit governance under rent-seeking. The model distinguishes low-effort verification of genuine projects from collusive verification of fraudulent projects and combines stability analysis with numerical simulations to examine strategic interactions and policy effects. Results Results show that credible governance need not depend on sustained intensive regulation. Increasing development subsidies and reputational benefits for both parties to give compliance a payoff advantage is key to achieving an ideal governance state. Under these conditions, this state can be maintained even as regulatory intensity declines. Moreover, the incentive-based policy achieves the ideal state under all three initial conditions, while the combined incentive -fine policy further accelerates convergence. Discussion This study advances understanding of the evolutionary mechanisms underlying blue carbon credit governance and informs the sel…

title: Valorization of Vineyard Pruning Residues through Biochar Production: Effects on Soil Productivity, Long-Term Carbon Sequestration, and Circularity in Viticulture
abstract: Viticulture generates large volumes of woody pruning residues that are commonly burned or landfilled, so that both their material value and their potential as a carbon sink are lost. Pyrolytic conversion into biochar has been proposed as a route that simultaneously addresses waste management, soil productivity, and climate mitigation. This review assesses how far the evidence supports these three claims for biochar made from vineyard prunings. A narrative synthesis of 55 sources (2014-2026), identified in Scopus and by targeted supplementary searches, was organized along five axes. Quantitative values were extracted, checked for internal consistency, and classified as measured, proxy, or modeled. Between 300 and 600°C, mass yield fell from 45.2% to 32.3% and total carbon rose from 66.5% to 77.9%, while the fixed carbon recovered per unit of feedstock was unchanged (25 g per 100 g). In vineyard field trials (8-44 t ha<sup>-1</sup>), none of which is documented as having used vineyard-pruning biochar, yield responses ranged from none to +66% and soil organic carbon rose by 36% to more than 200%. Biochar recovered after 15 years retained an inertinite fraction of 93.7% (94.8% initially), whereas century-scale persistence (60-100%) is model-based. Meta-analytic sequestration rates were 8.96 Mg CO<sub>2</sub>-eq ha<sup>-1</sup> yr<sup>-1</sup> for biochar and 2.82 for returned pruni…

title: Exploring the role of circular economy in decoupling carbon emissions from economic growth in European countries
abstract: Abstract Preventing the simultaneous rise in carbon emissions along with economic growth is considered one of the solutions for achieving sustainable development whereas traditional linear economy causes excessive carbon emissions along with economic growth and causes severe environmental degradation, resource depletion, economic inefficiency, and health risk for humanity. Circular economy, an alternate economic system to linear economy, decouples economic growth from carbon emissions offers solutions to problems created by linear economy. Hence, this study inspected the role of circular economy in decoupling carbon emissions from economic growth in twenty European countries from 1998 to 2023 using cross-dependence autoregressive distributed lags model (CS-ARDL). The findings obtained through CS-ARDL The findings show that circular economy is negatively associated with the transformed GDP–CO₂ decoupling indicator, with coefficients of − 0.23 in the short run and − 0.35 in the long run, indicating stronger decoupling,, indicating a stronger long-run association between circular economy and decoupling. The results further show that renewable energy consumption and globalization are also associated with stronger decoupling of carbon emissions from GDP growth whereas an increase in energy intensity strengthens the coupling between CO₂ emissions and GDP growth. Dumitrescu–Hurlin cau…

title: Artificial Intelligence and Urban Carbon-Emission Intensity: Production-Side Evidence from China
abstract: This paper examines how artificial intelligence affects urban carbon-emission intensity from a production-side perspective. We exploit the staggered rollout of China’s National New Generation Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Development Pilot Zone (NGAIPZ) program and use a balanced panel of 288 prefecture-level cities from 2014 to 2023. Difference-in-differences estimates show that the NGAIPZ program significantly reduces urban carbon-emission intensity. Further results provide evidence consistent with potential production-side channels involving improved energy efficiency, greater green innovation, and industrial upgrading. The carbon-intensity effect is stronger in cities with weaker environmental regulation, indicating that intelligent production and management systems create larger reductions in carbon intensity where conventional regulatory pressure is limited. The effect is also more pronounced in cities with better internet infrastructure, which supports data circulation and the diffusion of AI applications. These findings indicate that AI-oriented policy can improve urban carbon efficiency alongside changes in energy use, green innovation, and the organization of production.

title: Climate Effect of Alternative Binders: Life Cycle Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Potential as a Carbon Sink
abstract: Abstract Substituting Portland cement (PC) with alternative binders offers a promising pathway to mitigate the climate impacts of the cement industry, one of the most challenging sectors to decarbonize. While substantial greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are generated during production, most alternative binders can sequester CO2 during their service life. This effect has been acknowledged from a technical perspective, yet its significant influences on the GHG footprint of alternative binders remain unresolved. In this study, we quantify the CO2 uptake of common alternative binders alongside their lifetime GHG emissions. We demonstrate that most binders can take up a larger amount of CO2 than PC during usage, due to a thermodynamically high uptake capacity or high uptake kinetics. The uptake reactions enable a dynamic CO2 loop, with 1–248% of the production emissions being recovered over a 100-year structure service life. However, when the slow reaction rate is considered, the associated climate benefits can be up to 71% lower than the theoretical apparent uptake value. Our results highlight the importance of combined CO2 uptake modeling in assessing the decarbonization potential of alternative binders, and provide a basis for justifying the capability of these binders for use as building carbon sinks.

title: Advancing Canada’s energy future: a systematic-descriptive review of CCUS and blue hydrogen for environmental sustainability
abstract: Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) and blue hydrogen are increasingly considered potential components of industrial decarbonization strategies, yet the associated evidence remains fragmented across technological, environmental, economic, infrastructure, and policy dimensions. This study conducts a systematic descriptive review of journal articles, review articles, and conference papers published between 2015 and 2026, sourced from Web of Science and ScienceDirect, to critically assess the role of CCUS and blue hydrogen in advancing Canada's environmental sustainability and net-zero objectives. The evidence indicates that the environmental performance of blue hydrogen depends heavily on production technology, CO<sub>2</sub>-capture performance, upstream methane emissions, energy inputs, and lifecycle system boundaries. In one directly comparable steam methane reforming assessment, integrating ≥ 95% CO<sub>2</sub> capture reduced lifecycle emissions from 11.99 to 6.59 kgCO<sub>2</sub>e/kgH<sub>2</sub>, while a separate oil-sands fuel-substitution study reported a 76% emissions reduction under a different system boundary. Comparisons with green hydrogen depend on electricity source, technology, geography, and lifecycle boundaries. Renewable electrolysis typically shows lower climate impacts than fossil-based methods when using low-carbon electricity. Economic viabilit…

title: Effect of Allocated Trading Places on the Performance of Small and Medium Enterprises in Kamwala, Lusaka, Zambia
abstract: The impact of trading place allocation on the performance of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Kamwala, Lusaka, is not well documented, even though allocation determines where each enterprise is located in the market. The study evaluated the influence of accessibility on sales performance, the role of strategic positioning in customer attraction, and the impact of trading place infrastructure on business development. A total of 80 SME owners/operators were surveyed using a cross-sectional survey design with both qualitative and quantitative elements. The questionnaire items were coded and analysed using descriptive statistics, a one-sample t-test, a one-factor ANOVA, and simple linear regression. Throughout, “positive” ratings combine the “significantly positive” and “major contribution” responses, and percentages are based on all 80 respondents. The mean accessibility rating was significantly different from neutral, t(79) = −5.49, p < .001: 60.0% of respondents (48 of 80) gave a positive rating to the effect of accessibility on sales, and 56.3% stated that they made 30% or more of their sales from the trading location. Strategic positioning was rated positively by 68.8% of respondents, and 45.0% rated its contribution to customer attraction as major; a one-factor ANOVA comparing the coded ratings for walk-in customer traffic and strategic positioning was significant, F(1,…

Regeneration or Replacement of Adsorbent Materials: An Economic Strategy for Activated Carbon Used in Pharmaceuticals Removal from Water
abstract: Abstract Technological advancements are leading to an upsurge in demand for adsorbents that fulfill both technical and economic aspirations for sustainable and efficient solutions to water pollution. Literature reveals that hybrid nanomaterials can meet these criteria and hold promise for niche or high-value water treatment scenarios. Despite these milestones, these materials can suffer from high costs. Even conventional adsorbents such as activated carbon face economic challenges associated with regeneration costs. A significant drawback is the lack of economic criteria for determining when regeneration should stop and replacement should become preferable. To address these challenges, this study provides a quantitative basis for determining when continued activated-carbon regeneration remains economically viable and when replacement becomes the more cost-effective option. Using previously established experimental and activity-based life-cycle costing (ABC–LCC) data, the framework introduces economically tolerable performance loss (ETPL) and examines five regeneration cycles for diclofenac (DCL), ketoprofen (KETO), and atenolol (ATE). Replacement was economically preferable for all pollutants across the five regeneration cycles, with observed performance losses of 22.60–26.75%; calculated ETPL thresholds were negative: –93.99% (DCL), –99.20% (KETO), and –100.15% (ATE), indicati…

title: Mechanical property degradation and thermal recovery of FDM-printed discontinuous carbon fiber-reinforced Onyx after moisture exposure
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the mechanical degradation caused by moisture absorption in FDM-printed discontinuous carbon fiber-reinforced nylon (Onyx) and evaluate the effectiveness of thermal recovery treatments, including conventional drying temperatures (80–150°C) and industrial Zortrax annealing cycles, in restoring mechanical performance. Design/methodology/approach The study subjected FDM-printed Onyx specimens to 24 h water immersion to induce moisture degradation. Recovery was then evaluated through controlled thermal treatments at temperatures ranging from 80°C to 150°C and through industrial Zortrax annealing profiles. Tensile testing, mass tracking during drying and scanning electron microscopy were used to assess mechanical recovery, moisture-removal kinetics and microstructural changes. Findings Moisture absorption significantly reduced yield strength and stiffness due to matrix plasticization. Thermal treatments successfully reversed much of this degradation. Higher temperatures (120–150°C) accelerated moisture removal and improved interlayer consolidation, especially near the glass transition temperature (∼114°C). Industrial annealing profiles produced the best mechanical recovery, achieving ultimate tensile strengths of approximately 90 MPa and outperforming standard 80°C drying. Scanning electron microscopy analysis confirmed improved interlaminar bo…
