title: The interactive effect of intellectual capital and knowledge-centric culture on organisational performance: the sequential roles of knowledge absorption capacity and innovation capability
abstract: Purpose Guided by the resource-based view (RBV), this study examines how intellectual capital – comprising human, structural and relational capital – contributes to organisational performance through organisational knowledge absorption capacity and innovation capability as serial mediators. In addition, the study examined the moderating role of a knowledge-centric culture. Design/methodology/approach The data were collected from employees at high-tech companies in China. Hypotheses were tested using Mplus (v.8.6). Findings The results indicate that human, structural and relational capital positively enhance organisational knowledge absorption capacity, thereby promoting innovation capability and improving organisational performance. The findings further support a serial mediation process whereby intellectual capital influences organisational performance through knowledge absorption and innovation capability. Moreover, a knowledge-centric culture strengthens the relationship between intellectual capital and knowledge absorption capacity, thereby amplifying the indirect effects on organisational performance. Originality/value This study offers an integrated explanation of how intellectual capital drives organisational performance through organisational knowledge absorption capacity and innovation capability. Identifying knowledge-centric culture as a key boundary condition moves …

title: Insights into the Physiological and Molecular Mechanism in Root Formation of Semi-lignified Branches Cuttings of Aquilaria sinensis
abstract: Aquilaria sinensis, a key agarwood source, faces population decline from overharvesting, necessitating urgent development of efficient breeding methods for conservation and economic purpose. Cutting propagation is viable, but A. sinensis’ difficult-to-root characteristic limits efficiency. Therefore, we systematically evaluated the effects of growth regulator concentration, substrate, and trimming techniques on the rooting of semi woody cuttings through orthogonal experiments combined with physiological trait detection and transcriptome analysis. The optimal treatment involved treating flat trimmed cuttings with 200 ppm ABT-6 and inserting them into a loess:peat soil (1:2) substrate. This combination achieved a maximum rooting rate of 71.25%. The rooting of cuttings involves three stages: induction (0-30 days), expression (30-40 days), and extension (40-60 days). During root induction, ABT treatment increased endogenous IAA, ZR, and GA3 levels while suppressing ABA, establishing a hormone balance beneficial for adventitious root initiation. Besides, it also changed the activities of key enzymes (POD, IAAO, and PPO) and content of nutrients, but the changing trends were different. The transcriptome analysis showed that 93 DEGs identified in phytohormone signal transduction pathway. Our results significantly improve the rooting efficiency of A. sinensis cuttings and provide an in…

title: Temperature-Regulated Dispersion and Filter Cake Formation Mechanism of Organo-Montmorillonite in Oil-Based Drilling Fluids
abstract: Abstract Maintaining stable rheological properties and effective fluid loss performance under high-temperature conditions remains a critical challenge for oil-based drilling fluids (OBDFs). Organo-montmorillonite (OMt) is widely used as a multifunctional additive in OBDFs; however, the effects of quaternary ammonium salt molecular structure and high temperature on OMt dispersion, filter cake formation, and fluid loss control mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, OMt modified with quaternary ammonium salts featuring different alkyl chain lengths and chain numbers was dispersed in white oil to investigate how modifier structure and thermal treatment influence fluid loss through changes in OMt dispersion and filter cake formation. The results demonstrate that alkyl chain structure governs the dispersion, exfoliation, and network-forming capability of OMt in the oil phase. Compared with single-chain modified OMt systems, double-chain DC18-Mt exhibits stronger exfoliation and network-forming ability, promoting the formation of a three-dimensional network structure and enhancing viscosity, yield point, and viscoelastic properties. Moreover, DC18-Mt forms a continuous and compact filter cake, whereas C18-Mt and C22-Mt generate loose and porous filter cakes, resulting in inferior fluid loss control capability. Mechanistic analysis reveals that high temperature regulates fluid loss …

title: Stereo- and Enantioselective Living Coordination Chain Transfer Cyclopolymerization of 2-Methyl-1,5-Hexadiene: A Kinetic Ratchet Mechanism for the Polymerizability of α,ω-Dienes over α-Olefins
abstract: Abstract Stereo- and enantioselective living coordination cyclopolymerization of 2-methyl-1,5-hexadiene (2-MHD) using a set of cyclopentadienyl, amidinate (CPAM) group 4 metal pre-initiators, in combination with a borate co-initiator, has been reported to produce different stereochemical microstructures of poly(methylene-1,3-(1-methyl)cyclopentane) (PMMCP). Living chain transfer cyclopolymerization of 2-MHD has also been achieved in the presence of excess equivalents of ZnEt2 to provide low molar mass, end-group-functionalized PMMCP of narrow dispersity upon a reactive quench with iodine. Successful use of 2-MHD as a monomer and prior observation of selective polymerizability of 1,5-hexadiene over 1-hexene using the sterically encumbered homochiral pre-initiator (SC, SZr)-4 are rationalized by a kinetic ratchet mechanism accessible to α,ω-nonconjugated dienes but not α-olefins. These results serve to extend the mechanistic picture of coordination cyclopolymerization of α,ω-nonconjugated dienes and provide a foundation for the design of "next-generation" polyolefins.

title: A novel mechanism of Mogroside V in Parkinson’s disease: inhibition of neuroinflammation via the COX-2/IL-17A pathway
abstract: Background Neuroinflammation is a major factor in Parkinson’s disease (PD). This study examined the neuroprotective effects and mechanisms of Mogroside V (MV), known for its anti-inflammatory properties, on PD. Methods In vivo PD mouse models were developed with striatal injections of rotenone (Rot) or α-synuclein preformed fibrils (α-Syn PFF), while the PD monkey model used PFF. 10 mg/kg MV was administered orally to mice before PD induction. Mice’s motor function, dopaminergic damage, α-Syn pathology, and inflammation were assessed. In vitro , 100 μmol/L MV was tested on SH-SY5Y cells treated with Rot or α-Syn with cell viability, reactive oxygen species release (ROS), mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), adenosine triphosphate (ATP) assays. MV’s targets and pathways were identified by network pharmacology and RNA transcriptome analysis, validated and confirmed by cellular thermal shift assay, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation. Changes of target protein expression were confirmed in PD patients’ plasma with enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and PD monkeys’ substantia nigra with Western blot analysis. Results MV markedly improved motor abilities of Rot- and α-Syn-induced PD mice, including increasing 13.53 mm/s and 17.20 mm/s of average movement speed in the open field ( P < 0.01, P < 0.001), prolonging 98.40 s and 53.40 s of the latency to fall from the…

title: Mechanism for Utilizing Academic Supervision Findings in Setting Priorities and Evaluating Follow-Up Actions for Instructional Improvement in Madrasah
abstract: Academic supervision supports instructional quality through observation, feedback, guidance, and evaluation. However, its findings are not always systematically used to determine improvement priorities and follow-up actions. This study examines how supervision findings guide instructional improvement in madrasah. A Systematic Literature Review guided by PRISMA 2020 principles searched Scopus and Google Scholar for publications from 2016 to 2026. Of 62 identified sources, 59 were accessible and screened, and 22 met the inclusion criteria. Articles addressing academic or instructional supervision, teacher development, supervision findings, feedback, coaching, follow-up, or instructional improvement were included; irrelevant, duplicate, inaccessible, and bibliographically unverifiable sources were excluded. Data were extracted using a literature matrix and analyzed thematically to identify patterns in supervision practices, interpretation, priority setting, follow-up, and evaluation. The analysis produced six stages: collection, interpretation and diagnosis, priority setting, follow-up planning, implementation of improvement actions, and evaluation and reflection. The model’s conceptual contribution is to position priority setting as an explicit decision-making stage, align follow-up with diagnosed teacher needs, and use evaluation to guide subsequent improvement. The model offers…

title: North–South distribution disparities and influencing mechanism of Vietnam’s tangible cultural heritage sites
abstract: Abstract Using a point–area analytical framework, this study integrated GIS spatial analysis and GeoDetector to examine the spatial distribution of 4245 tangible cultural heritage sites in Vietnam and its influencing mechanism, as well as the spatiotemporal and typological patterns of 153 high-level heritage sites. The results show that: (1) Overall heritage sites exhibit a spatial pattern of “north-abundant, south-scarce”, with Hanoi ranking first in both number and density of sites and forming a significant hotspot centered on the city. (2) Among high-level heritage sites, those dating from the Feudal Period are the most numerous. These sites, along with architectural and artistic monument sites and mixed monument sites, are highly concentrated in and around Hanoi. (3) The distribution of Vietnam’s heritage sites is shaped by the combined effects of natural and socio-economic factors, and the political and cultural landscape. This study provides a scientific basis for coordinated heritage conservation across Vietnam.

title: Built to Expire: Sunset Clauses as an Adaptive Mechanism in Environmental Legisprudence
abstract: Environmental legislation ages quickly. The conditions a statute is written to govern (emissions paths, technologies, scientific baselines) rarely wait for the next reform. Sunset and review clauses are the remedy most often proposed, but the scholarship proposing them is careless with its terms and too quick to assume that an expiry date, by itself, makes law adaptive. Often it does not. The article separates three devices that the debate keeps running together: the sunset clause, which ends a measure unless it is renewed; the review clause, which demands fresh justification but repeals nothing; and the survival clause, which keeps obligations alive after the measure has gone. Working from legisprudential theory, it argues that sunset and review clauses hand environmental legislation a structured occasion to justify itself anew, and that whether the occasion produces real adaptation depends on design features that can be named: who pulls the trigger, what evidence renewal must meet, what happens on expiry if

title: Study on the influence mechanism of high-dynamic droplet impact on delamination damage of aircraft coatings
abstract: Abstract When an aircraft flies through clouds or rainfields at high speed, the extremely high relative velocity between the aircraft and raindrops can cause damage or even detachment of the coating on windward structural surfaces, thereby shortening aircraft service life. Polyurethane coatings offer excellent wear resistance, weather resistance, chemical corrosion resistance, strong adhesion, and good flexibility and are therefore widely used in aerospace applications. However, research on their rain erosion resistance remains limited. Therefore, this study investigates the delamination damage mechanism under high-speed raindrop impact conditions to improve rain erosion resistance. T800 carbon fiber composite laminates were used as the substrate, onto which polyurethane coatings with different interlaminar bond strengths were applied. Based on single-jet and pulsed multijet impact test platforms, the influence of interlaminar bond strength between the coating and the substrate on rain erosion damage characteristics and the occurrence mechanism of delamination failure were systematically examined. Under single-jet impact, coatings with low interlaminar bond strength first experience interfacial adhesion failure at the impact center, leading to localized delamination. The reflected stress waves cause significant interfacial stress concentration, resulting in uneven stress transf…

title: Identification and molecular mechanism analysis of chronic pain-related biomarkers in peripheral blood classical monocytes of myocardial infarction based on single-cell RNA and bulk transcriptome sequencing
abstract: Background Chronic pain (CP) is a common and clinically relevant complication in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI), but the underlying molecular mechanisms and specific biomarkers in peripheral blood remain largely elusive. This study aimed to explore these aspects using Single-cell RNA and Bulk Transcriptome Sequencing technologies. Methods Public datasets of peripheral blood samples from AMI patients and healthy controls, including single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and microarray data, were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Single-cell data underwent quality control, dimensionality reduction, batch-effect removal, cell clustering, and annotation. Differential abundance and CP activity assessments were carried out. Differential expression analysis was done at both single-cell and peripheral blood levels, followed by enrichment analysis. Gene set variation analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were used to identify relevant genes. Mendelian randomisation was conducted to determine causal relationships, and multiple validation steps were included. Moreover, biomarker-related molecular mechanisms were explored through network construction. Finally, persistent pain behavior and associated peripheral molecular changes were further assessed in rats following myocardial infarction. Results The abundance of classical mono…

title: Mechanism of spatial stabilization of the electric arc in a ladle furnace under axial gas supply conditions under the influence of electromagnetic deflecting forces
abstract: During the secondary refining of metal in ladle furnaces (LF), the electric arc is subjected to electromagnetic forces arising from the currents of adjacent phases and the liquid metal bath. This exposure leads to arc deflection – a phenomenon known as magnetic blow, which causes uneven conical wear of graphitized electrodes. Consequently, the thermal efficiency decreases due to parasitic heating of the slag phase, necessitating a quantitative justification for effective methods of spatial arc stabilization under three-phase alternating current conditions.The aimof this work is to determine the mechanism by which axial gas supply through a hollow electrode influences the resulting electromagnetic forces acting on the arc column, as well as to identify the parameters that reduce dynamic arc deviations in the horizontal plane.The study involved analytical modeling of the electromagnetic interaction in the “electrode–arc–liquid bath” system for a three-phase delta connection scheme. The Ampère force vectors and forces induced by currents in the bath were calculated considering phase shifts (120°) and industrial frequency (50 Hz). Hodographs of the resulting deflecting forces were constructed, their maximum values determined, and the influence of the axial flow of neutral gas as an addi-tional stabilizing factor was assessed.As a resultof the study, analytical expressions were obta…

title: A two-stage study of the sintering mechanism and pore morphology evolution by phase field modeling
abstract: Abstract Sintering is a critical solid-state bonding process, which largely governs the performance of key components in power electronics and biomedicine through its pore evolution dynamics. This study employs ballistic deposition algorithm to construct polydisperse powder systems and single-pore models, integrated with phase-field simulations to elucidate pore evolution mechanisms. For polydisperse systems, in addition to the positive correlation between the initial packing density and the densification rate, the curvature difference between particles of different sizes also provides an additional capillary driving force, significantly enhancing the densification rate. Focusing on the residual pores in the system, the theory of critical coordination number ( N p ) of pores is proposed under the model conditions used in this study (two-dimensional and isotropic interfacial energy), which holds that when N p ⩾ 4 , the interfacial tension balance causes a sudden drop in the pore closure rate, consistent with the classical concept of a critical pore coordination number. By changing the diffusion coefficient, it has been found that grain boundary diffusion significantly affects the sintering rate. The body diffusion optimizes the densification process in the later stage, while surface diffusion is related to the formation of the sinter neck and the initiation of pore coarsening. A…

title: The dual random inspection mechanism promotes cooperation in public goods game
abstract: Economic experiments have shown that punishment can increase the cooperation level in public goods game. However, it is impossible to punish every defector in real life due to the punishment cost. Inspired by this fact, this paper proposes a dual random inspection mechanism, which randomly selects a certain fraction of individuals from the cooperators to become law enforcers and bear the cost of law enforcement to conduct inspections on the group. Assuming that law enforcement and inspection are one-to-one corresponding. If the law enforcers inspect the defectors, they will impose fines on the defectors. Conversely, if the cooperators are inspected, their payoffs will not be affected. Through numerical simulations, it is found that the dual random inspection mechanism can solve the social dilemma. The larger the group size, the lower the cooperation level. When the group size exceeds 50, it will no longer have a further impact on cooperation. When the fraction of law enforcement is appropriately higher than the fraction of inspection, it is more conducive to the evolution of cooperation. Reducing the cost of law enforcement, increasing fines and rewards are conducive to the emergence and maintenance of cooperation. This paper provides a new perspective for understanding the emergence of cooperation in real life.

title: Defect Passivation and Electric Field Homogenization at the Buried SnO2/Perovskite Interface via SIP-Na Modification
abstract: Abstract The nonideality of the buried SnO2/perovskite interface is a key bottleneck restricting the performance of perovskite solar cells. However, there is still a lack of in-depth understanding of the morphological characteristics and physical mechanisms of this interface. This study systematically investigated the multifunctional optimization effect of sodium 5-sulfoisophthalic acid (SIP-Na) as an interface modifier between SnO2 and perovskite. With the help of mechanical interface exposure technology, intuitive evidence has been provided for the control manipulation of buried interfaces. The scanning electron microscopy results show that SIP-Na can effectively eliminate interface voids and guide the formation of high-quality crystals with larger grain size and lower stress in the perovskite. In addition, COMSOL simulation analysis reveals that SIP-Na treatment can significantly homogenize the interface electric field distribution. Under the joint promotion of the multiple optimization mechanisms mentioned above, the final device achieved a champion efficiency of 25.36% and a high open-circuit voltage of 1.265 V. This study combines direct interface characterization and physical simulation to deeply reveal the synergistic enhancement mechanism of molecular modifiers at the buried interface, providing a new perspective and theoretical support for interface engineering resear…

title: Punch excision combined with microdermal micrografting versus electric dermabrasion combined with thin split-thickness skin grafting for stable facial hypopigmented scars: a descriptive intra-patient technical case report
abstract: Introduction This report describes clinical observations in a single patient with stable facial hypopigmented scars, who underwent two reconstructive procedures in one operative session. Punch excision combined with microdermal micrografting was performed on the left preauricular scar, while electric dermabrasion plus thin split-thickness skin grafting (thin STSG) was applied to the anatomically distinct forehead scar. The patient was followed for 12-months post-operatively to assess safety, repigmentation, item-level Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS)scores, and patient-reported cosmetic satisfaction. Methods A descriptive intra-patient case report is presented. Two scar sites with distinct baseline size, anatomical location and morphological features received different reconstructive interventions. Wound-related adverse events, clinical appearance, multispectral dermatoscopic imaging, POSAS, and subjective satisfaction were documented throughout 12-month follow-up. Results No wound infection, ulceration or graft necrosis was observed at either surgical site. Earlier visible pigment appearance was noted in the electric dermabrasion combined with thin STSG site, accompanied by clinically observed uneven pigment distribution and perceived insufficient pigment depth at 12-month follow-up. The punch-excision-based micrografting site exhibited clinically observed ho…

title: A t - SNE approach to visualising scenario-dependent coherent generator clusters
abstract: Abstract A novel data-driven method for identifying coherent generators in power systems following a significant disturbance is proposed in this paper. For the analysis of post-disturbance generator dynamics, the t-distributed Stochastic Neighbour Embedding (t-SNE) algorithm is utilised, with explicit account taken of the pre-disturbance operating point and the specific location of the disturbance, factors often overlooked by traditional linearised methods. Validation of the technique is performed on a dynamic equivalent of the Mexican Interconnected System (MIS) under varying load conditions. From the results, it is demonstrated that the identified coherent groups are susceptible to disturbance location, a critical insight for accurate transient stability assessment and dynamic model reduction. The framework is intended as an off-line analysis and planning tool. An initial assessment of noise resilience on the IEEE 118-bus system indicates that the integrity of the angle-based embedding is maintained at signal-to-noise ratios as low as 20 dB, while susceptibility to noise is exhibited by the speed-based embedding. A two-level framework is delineated, in which a reference library of embeddings is constructed during the off-line analysis, and new disturbances are assigned to the most similar reference scenario during the online phase, without t-SNE being re-executed.

title: Coordinated dual layer volt-var control for power distribution systems with electric vehicles and distributed generations
abstract: Abstract Renewable distributed generators (DGs) such as solar PVs, and vehicle-to-grid technology (V2G) are gaining traction in the power distribution sector to ensure energy security. However, renewable DGs exhibit intermittency that can cause rapid voltage fluctuations leading to frequent switching when performing voltage regulation using conventional feeder control devices such as on-load tap changers (OLTC) and capacitor banks (CB). The frequent switching can bring about increased equipment operation and maintenance costs. This issue of voltage regulation can be addressed through the 4-quadrant smart inverters functions of DGs and electric vehicles (EVs). Hence, this paper proposes a dual layer control method aimed at mitigating rapid voltage fluctuations to reduce switching operations for the feeder voltage regulating devices. Moreover, it also optimizes the reactive power operation of the inverters with the aim of reducing the aging rate of the inverters. The efficacy of the proposed method is demonstrated through a modified IEEE 123-bus system by obtaining minimized voltage deviation, optimized reactive power consumption/generation of DGs to reduce inverter aging, and optimized charging/discharging of EVs for voltage regulation.

title: VEHICLE-ODI: a relational decision architecture for orbital debris prioritization
abstract: Orbital debris is commonly addressed through detection, cataloguing, orbit determination, conjunction assessment, mitigation, post-mission disposal, active debris removal (ADR), and space-capacity methods. These layers are indispensable but do not by themselves resolve a broader allocation problem: how limited observation, avoidance, stabilization, relocation, and removal resources should be prioritized across objects, relations, debris populations, and orbital regions while preserving legal and operational constraints. This article presents VEHICLE-ODI as a relational decision architecture for that purpose. The architecture represents the debris environment as a dynamic graph, separates external relational pressure from internal consequence, retains uncertainty and admissibility as explicit decision dimensions, assigns A1-A6 decision regimes, and computes regional Orbital Tension Index (OTI) readings under declared normalization. The frozen v0.2b demonstrator processed 2,132 public catalogue-derived objects and 162,502 proxy relations across eight altitude-defined regions. A subsequent bounded evidence extension used a frozen public SATCAT acquisition filtered to 28,605 LEO model-window objects to quantify population effects, discretization sensitivity, rank identifiability, composition-sensitive regional structure, and same-population comparator agreement. Regional load was s…

title: The implications of digital leadership for productivity, innovation, and employee well-being: a systematic literature review
abstract: Purpose This systematic literature review examines digital leadership as a socio-technical capability that sustains digital transformation. Grounded in the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model, it examines which employee- and organizational-level outcomes are associated with digital leadership, which mechanisms mediate these relationships, and which contextual factors moderate these effects. Design/methodology/approach Following PRISMA 2020 principles, 47 sources published between 2020 and early 2026 were identified and synthesized, comprising 46 empirical studies and one conceptual-analytical contribution. These 46 empirical studies were appraised for methodological quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Outcomes were classified along the JD-R model’s motivational and health impairment pathways, and methodological appraisal was adopted to interpret the synthesized evidence. Findings Digital leadership correlates with more innovative work behavior, engagement, empowerment, and well-being; lower technostress; and organizational success in digital transformation, agility, and innovation performance. Because the evidence base is predominantly cross-sectional, these relationships are interpreted as correlational. Reported relationships frequently involve psychological empowerment, knowledge sharing, and digital self-efficacy as mediating dynamics, moderated by person–…

title: Digital Mindfulness as a Pedagogical Strategy for Student Engagement in Hybrid Learning: A Systematic Review
abstract: Background Hybrid learning requires students to sustain attention, regulate emotions, and use technology purposefully across physical and virtual spaces. Digital mindfulness has mainly been studied as a means of reducing psychological distress; its role as a pedagogical strategy for engagement has not been systematically synthesised. We aimed to identify the forms of digital mindfulness reported in relation to student engagement, how interventions are designed and implemented, the mechanisms through which they support engagement, and the direction of reported effects. Methods A systematic review following the PRISMA 2020 statement was conducted across Scopus, Web of Science, and ERIC for records published between January 2021 and July 2026. Eligible studies were English-language research articles in Scopus-indexed journals reporting quantitative or mixed-methods evidence. Screening was performed independently by two reviewers (Cohen’s kappa = 0.81), methodological quality was appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, and the evidence was analysed through thematic and narrative synthesis. The review followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered retrospectively on the Open Science Framework (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/ZNSMK). Results From 412 initial records, 14 articles met the inclusion criteria. Three forms of digital mindfulness were identified: psychological or disposi…

title: A proposed multi-task machine learning strategy for dual-target quorum sensing inhibitor discovery in diabetic foot ulcer biofilms
abstract: Chronic diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) pose a severe clinical hurdle, largely because of the resilience of polymicrobial biofilms. When Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa occupy the same wound environment, they can form a drug-tolerant biofilm in which context-dependent cooperation, regulated in part by species-specific quorum sensing (QS) systems, contributes to persistence. Single-target treatments do not address the regulatory programmes of both organisms. This perspective proposes, but does not implement a computational strategy that combines machine learning, multi-task virtual screening, and a staged experimental cascade to prioritize dual-acting QS inhibitors. We hypothesize that the Gram-negative LasR receptor and the Gram-positive AgrA regulator, although structurally unrelated, share enough pharmacophore-level ligandability for a single small molecule to inhibit both. Such dual inhibition of two species-specific QS pathways is distinct from direct disruption of interspecies signaling, which would require separate evidence. We distinguish established evidence from hypothesis and proposed methodology, set out a convergence test and falsifiable go/no-go criteria, and discuss data harmonization, model validation and wound-specific constraints. If the hypothesis holds, such a compound could act as an antivirulence adjuvant that may enhance the activity of conven…

title: Synchronous nano-engineering and functionalization of Ce-MOF via a mixed-ligand strategy for visual detection of tetracyclines
EP09.33 HBO-HSRT: Reversing Hypoxic Radioresistance in Recurrent High-Grade Gliomas - A Salvage Strategy with Favorable Outcomes
abstract: Abstract Background Recurrent high-grade gliomas (rHGG) pose a formidable therapeutic challenge, driven by profound intratumoral hypoxia—a hallmark fostering radioresistance, angiogenesis, and inexorable progression. pO₂ levels in HGG often fall below 2.5 mmHg, impairing radiotherapy efficacy. Hyperbaric oxygenation (HBO) transiently alleviates hypoxia, enhancing tumor radiosensitivity; we thus evaluated HBO-integrated hypofractionated stereotactic radiotherapy (HSRT) as salvage therapy for rHGG. Material and Methods Adults (>18 years) with radiologically confirmed rHGG post-standard therapy underwent daily HBO sessions (2.5 ATA, 60 min) followed within 60 min by image-guided HSRT (15-25 Gy in 5 Gy fractions over 3-5 days). MRI-based planning and stereotactic immobilization ensured precision. Results Twenty-three patients (median age 58 years; 13 GBM, 10 AA) were treated, with median follow-up of 35.9 months (range 3.9-81.9). Median PFS was 3.22 months (95% CI 1.61-6.45), with 6- and 12-month rates of 36.9% (95% CI 17.8-56.3) and 5.8% (95% CI 0.4-22.7), respectively. Median OS reached 11.7 months (95% CI 9.2-24.2). No grade ≥3 neurotoxicity occurred; tolerance was excellent. Conclusion HBO-HSRT emerges as a safe, feasible salvage option for rHGG, yielding OS comparable or superior to historical benchmarks .Hypoxia reversal likely underpins radiosensitization; prospective tri…

title: ADVANCING THE BLUE ECONOMY AS A SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT STRATEGY: AN EMPIRICAL FRAMEWORK FOR TIMOR-LESTE
abstract: The transition toward sustainable development has intensified the search for alternative economic paradigms capable of addressing ecological degradation, economic vulnerability, and social inequality. The Blue Economy, as articulated by Gunter Pauli, proposes a regenerative and systems-oriented approach emphasizing resource efficiency, biomimicry, circularity, and social inclusion. This study develops and empirically operationalizes a structural model to assess the applicability of Blue Economy principles in Timor-Leste, a Small Island Developing State (SIDS). A mixed-methods design was employed, combining a systematic literature review (n = 128 articles) with survey data collected from 214 stakeholders across fisheries, policy institutions, NGOs, and coastal communities. Using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), the analysis tests the relationships between ecological innovation, governance quality, and sustainable development outcomes. Results indicate that circular economy practices and resource efficiency significantly predict sustainability outcomes, while governance quality exerts a strong moderating effect. This study contributes by providing one of the first empirically tested Blue Economy models in a SIDS context, bridging the gap between conceptual discourse and policy-relevant evidence. Keywords Blue Economy; Sustainable Development; Biomimicry; Circular Economy; Timo…
venue: International Journal of Health and Social Sciences

title: Strengthening Legal Literacy as a Preventive Strategy against Narcotics-Related Criminal Offenses among Generation Z
abstract: Purpose: This program aims to strengthen legal literacy among Generation Z as a preventive strategy against narcotics-related criminal offenses. Specifically, it seeks to increase young people's understanding of narcotics-related criminal law, including the types of offenses, legal consequences, and risks associated with narcotics abuse, possession, distribution, and trafficking. Method: This program employs a participatory and community-based approach to strengthen legal literacy among Generation Z as a preventive strategy against narcotics-related criminal offenses. The method is designed to actively involve participants in the learning process through legal education, discussion, digital campaigns, and evaluation activities. Practical Applications: This program can serve as a preventive model for collaboration among universities, schools, families, communities, and relevant law enforcement institutions. Continuous collaboration and digital-based legal education can strengthen young people's legal awareness and contribute to the long-term prevention of narcotics-related criminal offenses. Conclusion: This program contributed to improving participants' understanding of narcotics-related criminal law, increasing legal awareness, and developing more positive preventive attitudes. The use of interactive legal education, case-based learning, digital media, and peer-based communica…

title: An Evaluation of Lightweight End-to-End Encryption Schemes for Data Confidentiality in Low-Power Long-Range IoT Communication
abstract: Reliable and secure data transmission is essential for rapidly expanding Internet of Things (IoT) appli-cations, especially at the perception layer, where devices are constrained by bandwidth and power limita-tions. Low-power, long-range IoT communication has been made possible in large part by LoRa technolo-gy. However, because its native point-to-point mode lacks application-layer security, transmitted data is vulnerable to passive eavesdropping. This study experimentally investigates the integration of three lightweight encryption schemes, namely PRESENT, Speck, and ChaCha20, within an end-to-end LoRa point-to-point architecture implemented on embedded microcontrollers. Outdoor line-of-sight experi-ments were conducted over distances ranging from 50 m to 450 m to assess end-to-end latency, packet error rate and bit error rate (PER/BER), and confidentiality enforcement under passive sniffing scenarios. The results demonstrate that application-layer encryption prevents plaintext exposure during wireless interception while introducing stable and predictable end-to-end latency. Within effective communication ranges, all schemes maintain zero PER up to 300 m, with Speck and PRESENT sustaining connectivity at extended distances under the tested configuration. The findings provide system-level insight into the prac-tical security–performance trade-off of deploying software-based li…

title: Power Quality Analysis of a Ceramic Manufacturing Unit Using Field Measurements
Smartphone visibility and digital advertising in retail checkout
abstract: Purpose This study examines how smartphone visibility and in-store digital advertising jointly influence consumer attention and impulse purchasing in retail checkout environments. Drawing on the limited-capacity model of attention and the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework, the research investigates how digital advertising, particularly its auditory features, shapes attention and impulse purchasing under own-smartphone visibility conditions. Design/methodology/approach A pretest was conducted to validate high- and low-attention zones within convenience stores, followed by two field studies in Taiwan(Study 1: N = 112; Study 2: N = 141). Construct reliability and validity were assessed using SmartPLS 4.0, and hypotheses were tested using ANOVA and SPSS PROCESS Models 4 and 8. Findings Study 1 shows that consumers whose own smartphones remained within their visual field during checkout reported lower attention to nearby products than those whose smartphones were out of sight. Study 2 shows that own-smartphone visibility was associated with greater ad-related product attention and impulsive purchase intention under silent but not sound-enabled digital advertising. Ad-related product attention statistically mediated the relationship between own-smartphone visibility and impulsive purchase intention, with the indirect effect emerging only under silent advertising. Originali…

title: Total quality management and breakthrough innovation: the role of Pricing Management Capability: evidence from developing business organizations
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the influence of total quality management (TQM) orientation on breakthrough innovation and assesses the mediating role of Pricing Management Capability in explaining this relationship among Sudanese business organizations. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the resource-based view (RBV), the study develops and tests a conceptual model linking four dimensions of TQM orientation management support, customer focus, operations management, and strategic planning to breakthrough innovation, with Pricing Management Capability as a mediating variable. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire from 242 senior managers in business organizations operating in Khartoum State, Sudan. The hypotheses were tested using structural equation modeling with AMOS. Findings The findings reveal differentiated effects across the dimensions of TQM orientation. Customer focus has a significant positive relationship with both breakthrough innovation and Pricing Management Capability, whereas management support, operations management, and strategic planning do not have significant direct effects on breakthrough innovation. Pricing Management Capability does not significantly influence breakthrough innovation and does not mediate the relationships between TQM orientation dimensions and breakthrough innovation. Practical implications Managers should avoid assum…

title: Mitigating numerical stiffness in least-squares formulations of elliptic PDEs for physics-informed neural networks
abstract: Abstract Residual-based physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) combine interior PDE and boundary residuals using mean squared errors (MSE). For elliptic boundary value problems, these formulations can show numerical stiffness causing slow training. We study a residual formulation that combines an H 0 − 1 interior residual with an H 1 / 2 boundary residual for nonzero Dirichlet boundary data. For finite-dimensional test spaces in H 1 ( Ω ) , we introduce two finite-dimensional approximations, the subspace-induced negative-order Sobolev seminorm (SINOS) and its dual counterpart (D-SINOS), and quantify their stiffness through a stiffness ratio defined with respect to the H 1 -norm. We establish continuity and coercivity estimates for both formulations and show that, for polynomial spaces of degree n , the stiffness ratios of SINOS and D-SINOS grow at most as O ( n 2 ) and O ( 1 ) , respectively. Numerical experiments recover rates of n 2.00 and n 0.05 , compared with n 6.95 and n 5.68 for MSE and L 2 -based residual losses. PINN experiments for the Poisson equation, a stationary convection–diffusion–reaction problem, and the stationary incompressible Navier–Stokes equations show that SINOS achieves consistently strong convergence and accuracy, while D-SINOS improves over MSE but does not attain the performance of SINOS. These results demonstrate that negative-order Sobolev resid…

title: A multi-technique framework integrating machine learning for source apportionment and health risk assessment of heavy metals pollution in karst agricultural soils
Occluded Robust Face Recognition Using Deep Learning
abstract: In recent times, the use of mask in public places is rising all over the world to avoid various infectious diseases specially after COVID pandemic. People are wearing masks even when they are passing through face recognition systems. Thus, it has become important to improve the facial recognition systems to make it feasible for users wearing masks. The performance of such systems has been improved significantly by using convolution neural networks (CNN) as the feature extractors. The work presented here proposes a CNN based system using LResNet50 enhanced with Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN) to facilitate multi-scale feature extraction in occluded image recognition. The proposed architecture achieved an accuracy of 94.3% and a confidence score of 91.8%.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Two’s Company, Three’s a Crowd? A Thematic Review of Teachers’ Roles in Traditional and AI-Mediated Language Learning
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to support language instruction, practice, feedback, and assessment, reshaping how teaching responsibilities are carried out. This thematic review examines the changing roles of English teachers across traditional and AI-mediated language learning, focusing on responsibilities that are transformed, retained, shared with AI, or newly emerging. The literature synthesized in this study suggests that AI can assist with instructional planning, language practice, feedback, and assessment, while teachers continue to provide pedagogical judgment, contextualized guidance, learner engagement, and human interaction. AI integration also brings additional responsibilities, including evaluating AI-generated content, aligning tools with learning objectives, promoting academic integrity, and considering ethical issues and equitable access. However, the reviewed literature offers limited insight into how English teachers experience these changes in specific local settings, particularly in Ilocos Sur. The study therefore examines the evolving relationship among teachers, learners, and AI, and how English teachers negotiate their professional roles amid technological change. It argues that AI is best understood not as an automatic substitute for teachers, but as a resource whose educational value depends on informed, context-sensitive teacher invo…
venue: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology

title: Metacognitive and affective-motivational dimensions of the ‘learning to learn’ competence among university students: a quasi-experimental study on reflective mediation
abstract: Educational mediation requires the integration of cognitive, emotional and social processes to analyse complex situations, manage conflicts and foster coexistence based on dialogue. In this context, the “Learning to Learn” competence provides a framework for addressing processes of planning, monitoring and self-regulation, alongside motivational and emotional aspects. The aim of this study was to analyse changes in the metacognitive and affective-motivational dimensions of the CECAPEU questionnaire following a training activity based on reflective mediation of school conflicts. A quasi-experimental study with a pre-test–post-test design and a non-equivalent control group was conducted with 110 third-year students on the Bachelor's Degree in Education at the University of Valencia (Spain), divided into an experimental group ( n = 91) and a control group ( n = 19). Both groups completed the CECAPEU questionnaire before and after the intervention period. The experimental group took part in a reflective mediation activity focusing on the analysis of conflict situations, the skills required for mediation and leadership styles. Pre-test–post-test differences were analysed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. The results showed significant changes in various indicators across both dimensions in the experimental group, whilst the control group showed changes in a smaller number of indi…

title: Vascular age estimation from radial pressure waveforms using multi-task deep learning with in silico model-based pretraining
abstract: Vascular age (VA) is the chronological age that best matches an individual’s arterial stiffness, and it gives an intuitive indicator of cardiovascular risk. However, conventional stiffness measures usually require specialized equipment and trained operators, which limits their use outside the clinic. We estimated VA from a single radial pressure waveform (radial PW) together with its systolic and diastolic blood pressure, using a two-phase framework. In Phase 1, a multi-kernel one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) backbone was pretrained on the in silico Pulse Wave Database (PWDB) to jointly predict chronological age and three pulse wave velocity (PWV) indices under uncertainty-based loss balancing. In Phase 2, the backbone was frozen and an ElasticNet head was fine-tuned for each in vivo cohort. Because the model infers age from the waveform rather than from recorded age, we interpret its output as VA. The framework reached a mean absolute error of approximately 7 years on both an invasive normotensive cohort and a noninvasive tonometer cohort, and in silico pretraining helped maintain performance when in vivo training data were limited. On a hypertensive cohort that was never used for training, VA exceeded chronological age by about 5 years on average. This offset was larger than in the normotensive reference, consistent with accelerated vascular aging. Ablati…

title: Machine learning for predicting in-hospital mortality in adult hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
abstract: Background Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome with high mortality in adults. Prognostic assessment remains limited, and conventional models may miss complex nonlinear interactions. We aimed to develop and internally validate interpretable machine learning models to predict in-hospital mortality in adult patients with confirmed HLH using routine clinical and laboratory data. Methods We conducted a retrospective study involving 908 adult patients with confirmed HLH. Using routine clinical and laboratory data, we developed six machine learning models. A nested cross-validation with multiple imputation was applied. The optimal model was selected through a four-level hierarchical protocol based on out-of-fold calibration, discrimination, clinical utility, and simplicity. SHAP was utilized for model interpretability. Results The Logistic Regression (LR) model was ultimately selected, as complex tree-based models suffered from severe overfitting and poor calibration. On the independent temporal validation cohort, the LR model achieved an AUC of 0.824 with acceptable calibration (slope 1.056, intercept 0.293). SHAP analysis revealed platelet count (PLT), albumin (ALB), and C-reactive protein (CRP) as the most influential predictors of mortality. Conclusions This internal validated, interpretable LR model may provide risk stratifica…

title: Secondary music education and optimism: socio-demographic factors and perceived social support for instrumental music learning in non-specialized contexts
abstract: Educational research has demonstrated the relationship between socio-pedagogical contexts, wellbeing, and the development of optimism. Likewise, music education research has shown that instrumental music learning is associated with coping strategies and positive expectations. However, in Spain there are few studies analyzing these relationships within compulsory education. Therefore, the aim of this study was to analyze levels of optimism according to socio-pedagogical variables [sex, grade level, habitat (urban/rural), educational support, and instrumental music learning] and to examine their relationship with perceived social support for instrumental music learning. The variables were assessed using a questionnaire including ten socio-pedagogical descriptors, the Battery of Scales of Specific Expectations of Control in Academic Situations – Revised and Updated (BEECESA-RA), and the Secondary Education adaptation of the Perceived Social Support for Instrumental Music Practice Scale for Spanish conservatory music students. The sample consisted of 980 Compulsory Secondary Education students from public and state-subsidized schools in Aragón and Navarra. The mean comparison analysis revealed significant differences in optimism according to the independent variables. Correlational analysis confirmed the relationship between optimism and perceived social support for instrumental mu…

title: PhenoDAE: noise-regularized latent representation learning for phenotype imputation in genomic studies
abstract: Abstract Background Missing phenotypic measurements are common in large-scale genomic studies and can reduce statistical power, distort phenotypic variation, and compromise downstream genetic analyses. Existing phenotype imputation methods primarily focus on reconstructing missing entries, but real-world phenotypic data are also affected by measurement error, environmental variation, and minor biological fluctuations, which may lead to unstable and biased imputations. Here, we present PhenoDAE, a noise-regularized phenotype imputation framework that uses auxiliary input corruption to encourage stable latent representations during phenotype reconstruction. Results Across five taxonomically diverse datasets, including loblolly pine, maize, yeast, mice, and Pacific white shrimp, and five simulated missingness levels, PhenoDAE generally achieved favorable imputation performance relative to the evaluated baseline methods. Additional experiments under missing-at-random (MAR), missing-not-at-random (MNAR), and measurement-noise settings showed generally favorable performance relative to AutoComplete, with improvements diminishing at higher missingness levels but becoming more pronounced under stronger measurement perturbations. Hyperparameter sensitivity analyses further showed that PhenoDAE maintained relatively stable performance across the evaluated range of non-zero noise settings…

title: Lightweight separation-based multi-event perception for distributed acoustic sensing
abstract: Abstract Phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry is widely used for distributed acoustic sensing, yet effective event recognition in multi-source interference environments remains a significant challenge. To address these issues, this paper proposes a lightweight and efficient separation framework based on the time–frequency interleaved gain extraction and reconstruction (TIGER) architecture. A uniform band-split strategy replaces the speech-oriented frequency allocation, while multi-scale processing and attention model the temporal and spectral structure of the mixtures. Experiments cover six event classes, two-source and three-source synthetic mixtures, and real simultaneous two-source recordings. Comparisons include ConvTasNet Base and Tiny, dual-path recurrent neural network, SuDoRM-RF, TF-GridNet, and TIGER with the adapted original band split. Uniform-band TIGER achieves per-source classification accuracies of 97.17 ± 0.16% and 94.74 ± 0.01% with 0.822 M and 0.779 M parameters in the two-source and three-source tasks, respectively. Relative to the original-band variant, it improves accuracy by 2.29 and 1.79 percentage points and scale-invariant source-to-distortion ratio by 0.509 and 0.430 dB. In the three-source task, TIGER uses 9.5% of the parameters of TF-GridNet, with an accuracy difference of 0.87 percentage points. On 21 real two-source windows, it achieve…

title: Modality effects on multimedia learning across proficiency levels: Evidence from Thai learners of Japanese
abstract: Mayer’s (2009) multimedia learning theory introduces the Modality Principle, which holds that people learn better when visuals are paired with narration rather than text. While this principle has been widely supported in studies involving native speakers, findings from research on second language (L2) learners have been less consistent. This study examined how media type (Picture + Narration, PN vs. Picture + Text, PT) and Japanese proficiency (JLPT level) influenced comprehension and watch time (i.e., time-on-task) among Thai learners. A total of 116 learners were grouped by JLPT level (N1, N2, N3) and randomly assigned to one of two media types (PN or PT). After viewing the materials, participants completed a five-item comprehension test designed to reflect different levels of cognitive processing based on Bloom’s revised taxonomy. The results of binary logistic regression analysis indicated that higher-proficiency learners performed better on items requiring higher levels of understanding and analysis, whereas no statistically significant effect of media type on comprehension was observed. Two-way ANOVA revealed both proficiency and media type affected watch time, as well as a significant interaction between the two variables. Lower-proficiency learners, particularly at the N3 level, spent more time on text-based media. These findings suggest that learner proficiency may pla…

title: A unified deep learning model for layer-resolved optical-property estimation across tissues and systems in time-domain near-infrared spectroscopy
A Blended Micro-Learning and Simulation Approach for Peripheral Intravenous Catheter Insertion: A Quality Improvement Project
abstract: Background: Peripheral intravenous catheter (PIVC) insertion is a critical nursing skill in hospital settings that is seldom practiced in undergraduate nursing programs. Nurses on a women's health medical-surgical unit in southeastern Michigan expressed a need for PIVC insertion education. Method: This quality improvement project used a blended approach of simulation-based learning and micro-learning (i.e., small tutorials, pictures, and short video clips) to teach nurses about PIVC insertion. Survey data were summarized descriptively, and independent samples t tests were used to compare pre- and post-intervention group mean scores. Results: A total of 30 nurses completed the pre-survey, and 16 completed the post-survey. Mean scores increased across all items, with a significant increase in self-reported knowledge of strategies to prevent vein blowouts ( p < .001). Conclusion: These findings have led to the integration of micro-learning and simulation-based learning into unit education for topics such as continuous bladder irrigation, nasogastric tube management, tracheostomy care, and pharmacy updates.

title: Predicting Asymmetric Organocatalysis via Machine-Learning-Driven Molecular Dynamics of Chiral Deep Eutectic Solvents
abstract: Abstract Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) serve as sustainable, low-volatility, and bio-derived alternatives to conventional organic media, aligning with the demand for green chemical processes. Beyond their role as solvents, they offer transformative potential as integrated catalytic platforms, yet the molecular determinants of their performance remain poorly understood. This study employs machine-learning-driven molecular dynamics combined with density functional theory to investigate the structure and dynamics of chiral deep eutectic solvents in asymmetric catalysis. Simulations reveal that overly persistent hydrogen-bond networks within DES components impede key reaction steps and intermediate formation, reducing efficiency. Conversely, more labile networks preserve molecular flexibility, facilitating substrate activation and enhancing conversion. Furthermore, these networks compete with interactions controlling substrate orientation, thus influencing stereocontrol. By connecting microscopic hydrogen-bond dynamics to macroscopic performance, this work provides atomistic insight into structure–reactivity relationships. The findings define a quantitative computational framework that uses hydrogen-bond descriptors to predict catalytic efficiency. This approach demonstrates the utility of artificial intelligence-driven methodologies for the accelerated optimization and rigorous be…

title: Development and validation of a machine learning–based cell death–immune prognostic model for risk stratification in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
abstract: Abstract Background Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) shows marked prognostic heterogeneity, partly driven by interactions between regulated cell death and the tumor immune microenvironment. A framework integrating multiple cell-death programs with immune states is still lacking. Methods This study integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to characterize immune–cell-death interactions in DLBCL. Immune–cell-death-related genes were identified by intersecting differentially expressed genes with immune and cell-death gene sets. A cell-death–immune score (CDIS) was constructed using 101 machine-learning combinations and evaluated in three external cohorts. This study assessed immune infiltration, cell-death transcriptional programs, cell–cell communication, ligand–target interactions, pseudotime trajectories, drug connectivity, molecular docking and virtual perturbation. In vitro assays further tested BAFF stimulation and tamoxifen treatment in DLBCL cell lines. Results We identified 159 immune–cell-death-related genes and selected 16 genes from 25 candidates to construct the CDIS prognostic model; CoxBoost plus random survival forest ranked highest (mean C-index 0.703). High CDIS was associated with suppressed transcriptional programs of immunogenic cell death and an immune-cold microenvironment with M2-like macrophage enrichment. CDIS provides incremental value ove…

title: Efficient liquid-liquid microextraction of acid black 210 dye using choline chloride-based deep eutectic solvents
abstract: Abstract Industrial wastewater often contains toxic and poorly biodegradable synthetic dyes that pose serious environmental risks. In this work, a rapid and promising extraction liquid-liquid microextraction (LLME) method based on a choline chloride-phenol deep eutectic solvent (DES, 1:2 M ratio) was developed for the extraction of Acid Black 210 (AB 210) from aqueous solutions and real water samples. Extraction conditions were systematically optimized with respect to pH, contact time, DES volume, tetrahydrofuran (THF) volume, and dye concentration. Under optimum conditions (pH 6, DES 0.8 mL, THF 1.0 mL, contact time 2 min, dye concentration 20 ppm), the method achieved approximately 95 % extraction efficiency, with limits of detection and quantification of 2.6 and 8.5 μg L −1 , respectively, and good precision (RSD 2.23–3.10 %). The method showed satisfactory recoveries in spiked tap and industrial water samples. To rationalize the high extraction performance, molecular dynamics simulations were performed to compare the affinity of AB 210 toward water and the DES. Structural, hydrogen-bonding, and energy decomposition analyses revealed stronger dye-DES interactions, driven mainly by favorable van der Waals and hydrogen-bonding contributions. The computational results corroborate the experimental findings and confirm greater affinity of the DES for AB 210. This study presents t…

title: Distributed participation, centripetal attention: Political agency in #gemoy TikTok circulation during Indonesia’s 2024 election
abstract: Digital platforms can broaden electoral participation through cultural production and circulation without necessarily redistributing political power. This article examines this tension through the circulation of #gemoy-related content on TikTok associated with Prabowo Subianto and Gibran Rakabuming Raka during Indonesia’s 2024 presidential election. Using a retrospective qualitative critical-interpretive design, the study analyzes 102 TikTok posts uploaded during the 2023–2024 campaign and archived in August–September 2026, alongside 48 retrospective interviews. Fairclough’s critical discourse analysis provides the analytical framework, complemented by concepts of platformization, connective action, affective circulation, and technological mimesis. The findings distinguish campaign-mediated participation from user-initiated extensions. Performance, commentary, satire, and evaluative reframing demonstrate expressive agency, while reposting, remixing, sound reuse, comment-to-content relays, and commercial recontextualization demonstrate circulatory agency. Commercialization transforms political symbols into merchandise, audience traffic, and portfolio value. The study conceptualizes platformed mimetic co-production to explain how users transform political material through reuse, and distributed-centripetal authorship to explain how dispersed meaning-making coexists with recurrent…

title: Hexafluoroisopropanol-Regulated Interfacial Engineering for Rapid Electrochemical Hydrogen Storage of Pyridine
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical pyridine/piperidine liquid organic hydrogen carrier (LOHC) systems with water as the hydrogen source provide an appealing approach to reversible hydrogen storage. However, the robust resonance stability and low Faradaic efficiency (FE) of pyridine hydrogenation restrict its hydrogen storage efficiency. Here, a hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) interfacial modification strategy is developed to enable the electrocatalytic hydrogenation of pyridine to piperidine over a Co9Cu catalyst with an 83% FE and a yield rate of 1.03 mmol h–1 cm–2 at −200 mA cm–2. Mechanistic studies suggest that the HFIP anion adsorbs on Co9Cu surfaces through the oxygen terminus, while the trifluoromethyl groups orient away to form a hydrophobic layer, which suppresses the hydrogen evolution reaction and enriches pyridine through dipole interactions. The 12.9 mmol h–1 hydrogenation rate with an 83% FE at 2.5 A demonstrates the promising potential of the pyridine/piperidine LOHC system and this interfacial modification strategy.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Motivation and Strategic to Overcome Barriers in Indonesia Chronic Disease Management Exercise Participation at Poltekkes Kemenkes Primary Clinic in Yogyakarta
abstract: Background: The Chronic Disease Management Program (Prolanis) in Indonesia includes regular physical activity for people with hypertension and diabetes mellitus, but sustaining attendance remains a challenge in primary care. This study aimed to explore participants' motivation, the obstacles they encountered, and their efforts to overcome them among Prolanis exercise participants at the Primary Clinic of Poltekkes Kemenkes Yogyakarta. Method: A descriptive qualitative study was conducted using two forum group discussions (FGDs) with 17 purposively selected Prolanis participants with hypertension and/or diabetes mellitus who had attended the exercise for at least one month. The FGDs were audio- and video-recorded and transcribed verbatim, and the data were analysed using inductive content analysis. The resulting categories were organised using the Social Ecological Model. Results: Three main themes were identified: motivation, barriers, and strategies for overcoming barriers. Motivation came from the desire to maintain physical and mental health, the benefits of exercise that participants experienced, and friendship with other participants. Barriers included limited time due to household chores and, for some participants, motivation that was not yet strong. Participants overcame these barriers at the individual level through commitment and fixed scheduling, at the interpersonal …

title: Assistance Audit on Revenue and Expense Recognition Based on Financial Accounting Standards (SAK) for Salon Aruni MSME
abstract: Purpose: To date, there are still MSMEs that rely on a purely cash-based accounting system and experience a commingling of business and household funds, which distorts the assessment of net operating profit. This issue is reflected in the case of the Aruni Salon MSME in Makassar, which. Method: The implementation method used a descriptive qualitative approach through a five-day audit involving on-site guidance and direct assistance (July 4–8, 2026). Practical Applications: The implementation method used an approach. The results of the community service project demonstrated the successful separation of owner’s draw from operating expenses, the correction of accrual-based revenue recognition for credit transactions, and the preparation of a valid draft monthly income statement. The PKM team also successfully transferred knowledge, as evidenced by the owner’s ability to consistently operate independent bookkeeping tools. Conclusion: The audit, conducted with guidance, successfully addressed violations of the principle of business unity and produced valid financial statements to serve as a basis for decision-making; it is recommended that this guidance be continued and expanded to similar MSMEs.

title: Interactive Digital Catalog Gamification for Donut Bouquet Innovation to Accelerate MSME Revenue
abstract: Purpose: This community service program (PKM) aims to implement a gamification-based Interactive Digital Catalog to enhance product attractiveness, strengthen digital marketing, and support the marketing performance of Donat Duo Putri MSME in Padang City. Method: This program employed a qualitative descriptive approach through several stages, including observation, interviews, partner needs identification, product innovation, Interactive Digital Catalog development, gamification feature integration, training, mentoring, and evaluation to assess the effectiveness of the program implementation. Practical Applications: The program resulted in the development of an innovative Donut Bouquet product supported by an Interactive Digital Catalog integrated with WhatsApp ordering services, a Spin Discount feature, Reward Points, and Voucher Discounts. These innovations simplified product promotion, increased customer engagement, expanded digital marketing reach, and provided a more engaging shopping experience for consumers. Conclusion: The gamification-based Interactive Digital Catalog was developed as a digital marketing innovation for Donat Duo Putri MSME. The program has the potential to enhance product attractiveness, strengthen digital marketing efforts, and provide a more interactive and engaging customer experience.

title: Overnight cold storage maintains viability and detectability of immune cells in patient skin biopsies
abstract: Abstract Background Phenotypical and functional analysis of immune cells in patient skin provides vital information to clinicians and researchers. However, it is not always possible to perform a detailed analysis of immune cells at the same site as sampling. Consequently, samples may need to be shipped or stored overnight. Objectives To compare the recovery and detection of immune cells from freshly harvested skin biopsies vs. biopsies stored overnight at 4 °C, and to determine whether collagenase D or collagenase P digestion is more suitable for flow cytometry analysis of skin biopsies that have been stored overnight. Methods Punch biopsies (4 mm) were collected from the skin of nine patients undergoing abdominoplasty surgery. Some biopsies were digested immediately, while others were stored overnight at 4 °C and digested the following morning. Digestion was performed using collagenase D or collagenase P at different concentrations and for varying durations. The viability and phenotype of the isolated cells were then assessed using flow cytometry. Results Overnight storage of skin biopsies at 4 °C did not reduce immune cell recovery compared with fresh samples. Prolonged digestion increased haematopoietic and T-cell yields but reduced CD4+ T-cell detection, especially with collagenase P. Increasing enzyme concentrations did not improve overall cell recovery. Collagenase D perf…

Climate policy uncertainty and corporate boilerplate information disclosure strategies: a perspective on attention-based view
abstract: Purpose Facing climate policy uncertainty, firms may adjust their information disclosure strategies in response to external pressures. This not only may conceal substantive transformation information but also may lead to capital misallocation, thereby hindering the process of the low-carbon transition. Drawing on the attention-based view, this paper aims to examine how climate policy uncertainty influences corporate disclosure strategies. Design/methodology/approach Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2008 to 2022, this paper empirically examines the impact of climate policy uncertainty on firms’ boilerplate disclosure of climate transition information. Findings The results indicate that heightened climate policy uncertainty significantly increases the extent of boilerplate disclosure. Mechanism analysis reveals two primary channels: curbing substantive environmental investments and reinforcing managerial risk aversion. Furthermore, moderating tests show that organizational inertia exacerbates the effect, whereas corporate digitalization and CEOs’ political background effectively mitigate it. Practical implications The findings suggest that policymakers should establish stable, long-term policy frameworks with specific and verifiable disclosure guidelines to steer firms away from symbolic compliance toward genuine green transformation. title: A genetic mutation does not equate to a confirmed diagnosis—uncertainty in the interpretation of ATP7B gene variants
abstract: Wilson’s disease (WD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the ATP7B gene. Although ATP7B genetic testing is widely used for WD diagnosis, misinterpretation of sequencing reports can lead to misdiagnosis. This paper presents four cases highlighting the pitfalls of overreliance on genetic testing without comprehensive interpretation of ATP7B sequencing results, particularly when typical clinical, biochemical, and radiological findings are absent. Through a comparative analysis, three major types of analytical misinterpretation are systematically categorized genetic variants were misclassified as pathogenic mutations because insufficient evidence of pathogenicity prevented their categorization as “Variants of Uncertain Significance” (VUS); failure to conduct further segregation analysis resulted in misdiagnosis of WD; and neglect of non- ATP7B gene variants that can present with WD-like clinical features, such as Leukoencephalopathy with vanishing white matter (VWM) and Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Involuntary Movements (NEDIM). The conclusion emphasizes that genetic test results alone cannot serve as the sole basis for WD diagnosis without established clinical, biochemical, and radiological correlation. A rigorous diagnostic process must strictly evaluate mutation pathogenicity according to ACMG guidelines, confirm mutation origin through segregation ana…

Process modelling and optimization of the removal of biophile metals from Nigerian bitumen driven by phosphonium-based ionic liquid
abstract: Abstract This study explored the process modelling and optimisation of the removal of biophile metals from Nigerian bitumen using a hydrophobic phosphonium-based ionic liquid. Bitumen extraction from oil sands was performed using a Soxhlet extractor with toluene as the solvent. Metal removal was achieved through biphasic solvent extraction employing trihexyltetradecylphosphonium chloride as the extractant, chosen for its high thermal stability, low volatility, and strong affinity for metal ions. Metal concentrations of Cu, Mn, Zn, Co, Fe, and Cr were quantified via Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometry (Model Alpha Star 4). The optimisation process utilised Response Surface Methodology (RSM), with model validation through diagnostic plots generated by Design Expert Stat-Ease software. ANOVA results (p<0.005) confirmed the model’s significance. Consistent R 2 and adjusted R 2 values indicated a good fit to the experimental data. Diagnostic plots showed a near-perfect linear fit, reinforcing the model’s accuracy. Interaction effects studied through 2D contour and 3D response surface plots indicated that increasing input variables reduced metal concentrations. Optimal conditions determined were 50 °C temperature, 60-min reaction time, and 3 % w/v ionic liquid, achieving complete Mn removal and removals of 56 %, 61 %, 51 %, 43 %, and 36 % for Cu, Co, Cr, Fe, and Zn, respectively. State-dependent action masking in tabular reinforcement learning: analytical and stochastic evaluation motivated by surgical robotics
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has considerable potential to increase autonomy in surgical robotics, but its deployment in safety-critical settings requires mechanisms for restricting actions that violate specified safety rules. We study a tabular reinforcement learning formulation in which action selection and Bellman maximization are restricted to state-dependent admissible action sets, corresponding to a form of action-masking closely related to shielding. Classical results for discounted Markov decision processes and tabular Q-learning are recalled to clarify the conditions under which an optimal stationary policy exists and Q-learning converges for a fixed finite constrained decision process. A deliberately simple two-state environment is first used to illustrate the consequences of persistent ϵ -greedy exploration when an unsafe action remains available or is excluded by the specified action mask. In this setting, once the safe action is greedy, residual unsafe-action frequency is determined directly by the exploration schedule, so the example is interpreted analytically rather than as evidence of a new learning mechanism. We then use a stochastic 30-state navigation environment to examine hazard-exposure during learning under task-only learning; a tuned reward penalty; and correct, conservative, and deliberately misspecified action masks. The tuned penalty reduced but did n…

title: Optimasi Jaringan Dengan Load Balancing Multi ISP Menggunakan Metode PCC dan Failover Untuk Meningkatkan Kualitas Kinerja Jaringan Internet
abstract: Internet connection stability is crucial for the smooth operation of a company. Relying on a single Internet Service Provider (ISP) is currently considered suboptimal because it is prone to causing downtime and traffic congestion during peak hours. Therefore, this study was conducted to develop a Multi-ISP-based network architecture to ensure service availability while optimizing data traffic distribution. By utilizing PCC Load Balancing and Failover, and applying the Network Development Life Cycle (NDLC) framework, this design was simulated using GNS3 software based on MikroTik CHR. Test results demonstrate that the Load Balancing method using the Per Connection Classifier (PCC) algorithm is highly effective at dynamically distributing network load across two ISP paths. This success is marked by a nearly twofold increase in download throughput, from 4.43 Mbps to 8.79 Mbps. Furthermore, a Quality of Service (QoS) analysis based on the TIPHON standard under peak load conditions confirmed that the bottleneck issue has been resolved. This is evident from the elimination of packet loss—which dropped from 7.92% to 0%—as well as latency of 54.5 ms and jitter of 14.1 ms, both of which fall within the “Very Good” category. Additionally, the Recursive Gateway-based failover system automatically switches to the backup ISP with a recovery time of less than 20 seconds.

title: Performance Optimization of A 433 Mhz Yagi Antenna for Extended-Range UAV-GCS Telemetry Link
abstract: The reliability of telemetry communication between an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and a ground control station (GCS) often degrades beyond 1 km when standard omnidirectional antennas are used, limiting applica-tions such as mapping and remote surveillance. This is due to the antenna's limited ability to maintain stable signal transmission. This study proposes the design, fabrication, and testing of a Yagi–Uda antenna aimed at improving the stability and extending the operational range of telemetry communication links between UAVs and their GCSs. The antenna is specifically designed and optimized for the 433 MHz frequency band, which is commonly used for low-frequency UAV telemetry. The Yagi antenna underwent simulation and experimental characterization. Measurement results showed a return loss of -42.39 dB at a center frequency of 417 MHz, with a bandwidth of 59 MHz, indicating excellent impedance matching. Field tests were conducted to validate real-world performance and showed that the antenna maintained stable and continuous communication with the UAV at a distance of up to 3.2 kilometers. This performance was supported by received signal strength in-dicator (RSSI) values consistently recorded above 100 and signal levels around -73 dBm, confirming reliable data exchange even under nonideal environmental conditions. These findings confirm that the directional Yagi antenna s…
