title: Fuel-Economy Efficiency Gaps Across Indonesian Transport Modes: A Stochastic Frontier Analysis
abstract: Improving fuel economy is a critical but underexplored dimension of urban transport decarbonisation in developing countries. This study presents an exploratory frontier-based assessment of observed fueleconomy heterogeneity across Indonesian urban transport modes, estimating how far individual performance falls below a conditional mode-specific frontier and whether those gaps are evenly distributed across users. Stochastic Frontier Analysis (SFA) is applied to survey data from 1,610 vehicle owners/drivers across surveyed Indonesian urban areas, estimating separate frontiers for each mode using 1,242 internal combustion observations. Primary mode-level frontier estimates are designated for five of the six modes; candidate fits for small cars are reported in the sensitivity analysis, but no sufficiently robust primary estimate is designated. Trucks with three or more axles show the largest frontier-relative efficiency gap (24.0%), followed by motorcycles (22.1%), two-axle trucks (21.6%) and medium/large cars (20.5%), while buses at 11.4% operate closest to their frontier. A sensitivity analysis across four outlier-trimming rules and two inefficiency distributions (48 fits, of which 25 satisfy all diagnostic criteria) shows that the freight estimates are highly stable and the motorcycle and medium/large-car estimates are moderately sensitive. For motorcycles, user characteristics …

Effective Intrusion Detection and Classification in VANET Environments Using Deep Learning Model with Optimization Algorithms
abstract: VANET (Vehicular Ad Hoc Network) is an innovative transportation technology that improves road safety and traffic management through communication and data sharing between vehicles. The attackers create various kinds of assaults to oppose the operational tasks of the network environment in VANET. Then, identifying the attacks in VANET method is extremely essential to give reliable and secure communication among each vehicle within the system. Because of this, the Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is needed in VANET to offer safety from outside attacks like Botnet, Denial of Service (DoS), and so on. These may identify assaults and provoke a response, lowering the effects on the target system. This paper develops an Intelligent Intrusion Detection and Classification using Deep Learning Model and Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithms (IIDC-DLMMOA) method in VANET Environments. The main intention of IIDC-DLMMOA technique relies on developing an effective structure for IDS in VANET communications. The hiking optimization algorithm (HOA) performs feature selection by identifying the input features that contribute most to the classification process. For the classification process, the proposed IIDC-DLMMOA designs a spatial-temporal attentive with long short-term memory (STA-LSTM) system. At last, the hyperparameter tuning optimizes a classification model of STA-LSTM method through a M…

title: Maternal and Child Health and Well-Being: A Lifecourse and Systems-Based Perspective on Integrated Care and Health Equity
abstract: Introduction: Maternal and child health remains a global public health priority amid persistent inequities in access to healthcare, preventable morbidity, and intergenerational health outcomes. Fragmented services frequently disrupt continuity of care across pregnancy, childbirth, the postpartum period, and early childhood. This study aimed to develop a conceptual framework integrating lifecourse and systems-based perspectives to strengthen integrated maternal and child healthcare and advance health equity. Methods: An integrative literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed empirical and conceptual studies retrieved from Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science. Eligible publications in English addressed maternal and child health, integrated care, health equity, and related determinants. Following systematic screening and eligibility assessment, 78 studies were included in the thematic synthesis and conceptual framework development. Results: The synthesis identified interconnected biological, social, economic, community, and health-system determinants shaping maternal and child health across the lifecourse. Integrated care connecting antenatal, intrapartum, postnatal, and pediatric services emerged as a critical pathway for strengthening continuity, early risk identification, and coordinated care. Primary healthcare integration, community-based interventions, and multisectora…

title: The pre-activation ecotone: a conceptual framework for unscheduled care and the emerging role of mobile integrated healthcare
abstract: Purpose To define the “pre-activation ecotone” as a conceptual framework for unscheduled care, representing the interval between recognition of a health need and formal health system entry, and to examine its implications for care delivery design, patient decision-making, and system integration. Design/methodology/approach A targeted narrative synthesis of literature spanning ecology, emergency medicine, health services research, and public health. Sources were identified through targeted database searches (PubMed, Scopus), gray literature review, and reference chaining, with emphasis on studies and models addressing unscheduled care access, system design, and cross-sector coordination. Because the manuscript is intended as a conceptual framework rather than a formal review of all available evidence, studies were not systematically appraised or graded. Findings In the United States, current approaches to unscheduled care prioritize expansion of episodic access points, with limited attention to the pre-engagement setting where patient-driven decisions under uncertainty often lead to emergency system activation. Evidence from emergency medical services and health services research identifies this interval as functionally distinct yet structurally underdeveloped. Mobile integrated healthcare is emerging within this space, demonstrating feasibility in addressing unmet care needs an…

title: Church Attendance Management System Based on Edge AI and MobileNetV2
abstract: Purpose: Manual attendance recording in religious institutions is inefficient and limits demographic analytics. This paper presents an edge-based face recognition system deploying MobileNetV2 on Raspberry Pi 5 for automated church attendance tracking with complete local biometric processing. Method: The system integrates with a web-based platform for demographic management and synod-compliant reporting. An 8-week field evaluation at GKI Karawaci involved 412 active congregants (drawn from a total registry of 1,247) across 32 services. The system achieved 96.8% recognition accuracy, 247 ms end-to-end latency (~4 FPS), and 8.2 W power consumption. Practical Applications: Compared to manual methods, the system eliminated per-service recording time, reduced data entry errors by 93.6%, decreased monthly administrative effort by 67.4%, and improved demographic data accuracy from 64.3% to 98.7%. Local processing ensures privacy without cloud dependency. Conclusion: This work validates deployed face recognition as a cost-effective, ethically grounded solution for improving operational efficiency in religious and resource-constrained community settings.

title: Stakeholder digital readiness for AI-driven dengue surveillance and reporting system
abstract: Background As the public health sector moves towards digital health transformation, artificial intelligence offers opportunities to improve disease surveillance, early disease detection and strengthen reporting systems. However, the adoption of these technologies depends on stakeholder knowledge, readiness, and practices. Therefore, this study assesses stakeholders’ awareness, preventative practices, digital access, and readiness for dengue surveillance in Kingston, Jamaica. Methods The study employed a cross-sectional quantitative mixed-mode survey. The questionnaire comprised of multiple choice and open-ended questions with 397 participants and 391 eligible data registrations. Participants were recruited through online channels and in-person paper-based questionnaires administered at healthcare facilities across Kingston. Quantitative data was analyzed descriptively on SPSS Version 30 with Pearson Chi-square tests and a p -value of ≤ 0.05, while qualitative components were thematically analyzed. Findings Results reveal that 72.1% of the participants reported having high readiness, 10.2% reported moderate digital readiness and 17.6% reported low readiness. 96.4% of the study participants expressed willingness to adopt AI-driven digital health tools. Yet only 31.1% of the participants who answered the question indicated high confidence, while 50.4% of the study respondents indi…

title: Explaining citizen complaints against the police: organizational, environmental and system factors
abstract: Purpose The study aims to examine variation in citizen complaints against police departments, with particular attention to how organizational characteristics, environmental context and features of complaint systems shape complaint volume. Design/methodology/approach Using data from 129 large U.S. municipal police departments, this study employs stepwise negative binomial regression to assess the impact of organizational characteristics, environmental context and features of complaint systems on complaint volume. Findings Organizational characteristics – particularly department size and educational requirements – emerge as significant predictors of complaint volume, with larger agencies generating more complaints and those requiring education beyond high school generating fewer. In contrast, community-level variables such as crime rates, unemployment and racial composition show limited explanatory power. Importantly, features of citizen complaint systems play a meaningful role. Departments that allow third-party complaints and avoid penalties for false reporting exhibit different complaint patterns, suggesting that system accessibility influences complaint levels. Moreover, the relationship between in-service training and complaints varies depending on complaint system openness, indicating that training effectiveness may depend on broader accountability structures. Practical imp…

title: On the Nature of the Be Star/White Dwarf System Nova FQ Circinus
abstract: Abstract The classical nova FQ Cir has recently been shown to have a Be star donor, and has been identified as a high mass cataclysmic variable (HMCV), with an orbital period of ∼2.04 days (twice the 1.02 day periodogram peak). Using the extensive OGLE optical archive, together with existing observations from ASAS-SN, we instead find significant modulation between ∼50 and 60 days and propose that the orbital period is likely closer to ∼62 days. We interpret the low-amplitude 1.02 day modulation as a nonradial pulsation of the Be star. We also reassess the HMCV classification based on properties of known Be star-white dwarf systems.

title: Indian Farm Distress Early Warning System – Phase 1
abstract: Agricultural distress in India can arise from the combined effects of rainfall variability, changes in crop production, fluctuations in agricultural market prices and difficulties associated with agricultural credit. Although information relating to these factors is available through different public institutions, the data are maintained in separate systems and may differ in format, coverage and frequency of update. This Phase I paper proposes the design and development of an Indian Farm Distress Early Warning System that will integrate four categories of public data: rainfall information from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), crop production and yield information from the Ministry of Agriculture, market-price information from AGMARKNET, and agricultural credit information from NABARD. The proposed workflow will prepare and combine the selected indicators, calculate a District Distress Score for the districts included in the study, apply K-Means clustering (with four clusters) for risk grouping, and use a Random Forest model to forecast next-season risk. Outputs are planned to be presented through a Streamlit web dashboard and a Power BI analytical report. This paper focuses on the problem context, objectives, related work, proposed data sources, system design and evaluation plan. It does not report implementation results or predictive-performance values; these will be…

GMR-EfficientUNet: an improved network integrating gated bottleneck convolution and multi-scale attention residual fusion for high-precision breast ultrasound mass segmentation
abstract: Abstract Breast ultrasound (BUS) is widely used in breast imaging because it is non-ionizing and well suited to dense breast tissue. However, speckle noise, blurry mass boundaries, and large variations in lesion scale remain challenging for automated segmentation. This paper presents GMR-EfficientUNet, an EfficientNet-B2/U-Net-based encoder-decoder framework that adapts a Gated Bottleneck Convolution (GBC) module and a Multi-Scale Convolutional Attention (MSCA) module from prior work and combines them with a Residual Adaptive Fusion (RAF) module for breast ultrasound mass segmentation. Within the proposed integration, GBC is applied to refine the initially fused encoder-decoder representation, MSCA performs multi-scale contextual modeling on the refined features, and RAF learns pixel-level fusion weights between the enhanced representation and the original DoubleConv feature. On the BUSI dataset, the model achieved a Dice coefficient of 82.07%, MIoU of 73.73%, recall of 83.49%, and precision of 83.62%. On the BUET dataset, it achieved a Dice coefficient of 81.70% and MIoU of 72.57%; among the evaluated models, it obtained the highest Dice, MIoU, and recall, while TransUNet achieved a higher precision. The ablation results demonstrated the effectiveness of RAF in improving segmentation performance. Additional experiments showed improved boundary localization, competitive perform…

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals that gut microbiota modulates the association between dietary imbalance and gastrointestinal symptoms in children with functional dyspepsia
abstract: Background Functional dyspepsia (FD) is a prevalent pediatric gastrointestinal disorder. Although dietary factors and gut microbiota dysbiosis are implicated in its pathogenesis, the interplay among diet, microbiota, and FD remains poorly understood. Methods This case–control study enrolled 34 children with FD and 40 healthy controls. Dietary intake was assessed using a Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ). Fecal microbiota was profiled by 16S rRNA sequencing, and untargeted metabolomics was employed to detect fecal metabolites. Clinical symptoms were evaluated using the Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS) and the Functional Gastrointestinal Disorder Symptom Screening Questionnaire (FGIDQ). Results We identified 16 differentially abundant bacterial species and 476 differential metabolites (458 downregulated, 18 upregulated). Folate intake was significantly lower in the FD group ( p = 0.0038). Three major dietary patterns were identified: pattern 1 (high-fat, high-protein dietary pattern), pattern 2 (traditional staple food dietary pattern), and pattern 3 (diverse mixed diet dietary pattern). The standardized scores for patterns 2 and 3 were significantly lower in the FD group than in the control group. title: Applying Ecosystemic Autopsy to Juvenile Delinquency: A Multi-Level Case Analysis of Adolescent Development
abstract: Juvenile delinquency is a complex developmental and social concern shaped by the interaction of behavioural, emotional, academic, familial, social, and environmental factors. Although ecological perspectives recognize these influences, an integrated examination of how risk and protective factors interact across developmental stages remains important for understanding individual pathways to delinquency. This paper applies the Ecosystemic Autopsy (EcoA) framework, grounded in Bronfenbrenner’s Ecological Systems Theory, to develop a contextualized understanding of juvenile delinquency through a retrospective qualitative single-case analysis. The case involved an 18-year-old male, assigned the pseudonym “Daniel,” selected because the available documentation covered multiple developmental and ecological domains. Data were drawn from one consolidated case review report containing psychoeducational assessments, developmental history, educational records, behavioural observations, and previous intervention records. The researcher organized the documented information into five a priori ecological categories: microsystem, mesosystem, exosystem, macrosystem, and chronosystem. The report documented difficulties in working memory, processing speed, reading comprehension, and written expression, alongside behavioural and emotional challenges. It also recorded practical and vocational strengt…

title: Multi-scale predictive control of boiler furnace temperature field based on MPC-Seq2seq
abstract: Introduction Boiler furnace temperature fields are significantly affected by strong nonlinearity and large time lags. Conventional methods exhibit limited capability in capturing spatiotemporal features and suffer from optimization delays, which restricts the efficient operation of boiler units. Methods To address this issue, this study proposes a multi-scale prediction method that combines a Lightweight Temporal Convolutional network with a Sequence-to-Sequence architecture. Wavelet packet decomposition is used to extract temperature sub-sequences, an encoding network is constructed, and a spatiotemporal dual attention mechanism is integrated to achieve accurate prediction of the furnace temperature field. In addition, a predictive control technique based on adaptive-reference-point multi-objective differential evolution is applied for combustion regulation. This technique takes multi-step prediction data as input, enhances collaborative optimization by introducing an adaptive update mechanism, and incorporates dual constraints on thermal efficiency and emissions to obtain the optimal control results. Results A 300 MW coal-fired utility boiler is selected as the research object for experimental validation. In furnace temperature prediction, the root mean square error of the proposed model is 1.53 °C, and the mean absolute percentage error under full load is 1.15%, both of whic…

title: Weekend effect on in-hospital mortality and healthcare utilization: a multi-method validation with time series analysis, Cox regression, and random forest in a Chinese tertiary hospital
abstract: Background Patients admitted on weekends may face elevated mortality risk, a phenomenon termed the “weekend effect.” While extensively studied in Western healthcare systems, evidence from Chinese tertiary hospitals remains limited, and most studies rely on single-method regression. This study had three distinct aims: (i) to estimate the association between weekend admission and in-hospital mortality; (ii) to characterize weekly temporal patterns in mortality; and (iii) to explore the variable importance of a broad set of patient-level and operational variables. Time series analysis, Cox proportional hazards modeling, and random forest were used to address these three aims, respectively. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 379,804 patients admitted to a tertiary general hospital in Shenzhen, China, from 2015 to 2023. Patients were categorized into weekday ( n = 304,693) and weekend/holiday ( n = 75,111) admission groups. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, defined as all-cause death during the index admission; patients were followed from admission to discharge, and those discharged alive were censored at discharge. Secondary outcomes included length of stay, treatment delay, nosocomial infection, and hospitalization cost. A multi-method strategy was used: (1) seasonal-trend decomposition using Loess (STL) and seasonal autoregressive integrated moving aver…

title: Clinical outcomes associated with early airway management strategies in open and closed laryngeal trauma: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Selection of an initial airway strategy in laryngeal trauma depends on injury severity and respiratory status. This study aimed to examine associations between initial airway strategy and acute airway-related complications in adults with laryngeal trauma. Methods This two-center retrospective cohort included adults with open or closed laryngeal trauma treated from May 2020 to May 2025. The primary outcome was any acute airway-related complication during the index admission. Firth penalized logistic regression adjusted for pretreatment severity, age, trauma type, admission delay, airway narrowing, and dyspnea. The analysis was restricted to Schaefer–Fuhrman grades I–III because all grade IV patients underwent initial tracheostomy. Strategy conversion and tube-removal outcomes were summarized descriptively. Results Among 206 patients, acute complications occurred in 28/76 (36.8%), 23/48 (47.9%), and 11/82 (13.4%) patients initially managed with observation, orotracheal intubation, and tracheostomy, respectively (omnibus P < 0.001). The principal model included 156 complete cases and 50 events. Compared with initial tracheostomy, observation [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 9.65; 95% confidence interval (CI), 2.99–36.66] and intubation (aOR, 11.21; 95% CI, 3.61–40.76) were associated with higher odds of complications (both P < 0.001). Airway narrowing (aOR, 2.26; 95% C…

title: Resistance to mall expansion: still not buying the destination argument
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to analyse stakeholders’ reactions to expansion arguments for an out-of-town shopping mall in a contested planning process. The proposed expansion occurs against a backdrop of growing competition from e-commerce and increasing pressure on physical retail formats. This study seeks to explain how these arguments function as a means of making expansion appear feasible and desirable for place development, and whether they remain persuasive despite critique and uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach This study is based on a document analysis of 144 formal stakeholder considerations submitted in response to the expansion vision of a Swedish shopping mall, examining how stakeholders engage with and contest expansion arguments. Findings This study identifies a destination argument that legitimises mall expansion through claims of uniqueness, experiencification and an expanded hinterland. Stakeholders frequently contest these claims, not because they lack information, but because they hold competing views on retail place development and its consequences. The findings show how destination arguments can remain influential despite substantial scepticism and critique. Practical implications The findings suggest greater scrutiny of destination arguments used to justify mall expansion. Claims of uniqueness, wider catchment areas and spillover benefits sh…

title: Mango Production Processes and Marketing Strategies in Bangladesh
abstract: In essence the marketing of mango is contingent on the linkage between production possibilities, product status and environment in which the decision is made. The study investigated the relationship between mango cultivation, harvesting, processing, the environment and regulatory framework and marketing strategies in the context of Canada’s production environment in Chapainawabganj, Bangladesh. Judgement sampling was used to get responses from professionals and business participants that are associated with the mango value chain in a quantitative survey. A total of 210 questionnaires were analysed from 260 questionnaires received. The responses were measured on a 5-point Likert scale, and examined using the partial least squares structural equation modelling in the software SmartPLS with 5000 bootstrap resamples. The composite reliabilities were between 0.782 and 0.862, while the AVEs were between 0.550 and 0.719. The strongest positive relationships were seen between harvesting (β = 0.380, p < 0.001), the environmental and regulatory context (β = 0.202, p = 0.017) and processing (β = 0.192, p = 0.037). The association between cultivation was positive but not statistically significant (β = 0.100, p = 0.219). The model had an explained variance of 40.6% and a reported Q² of 0.258 and standardised root mean square residual of 0.077 for marketing strategies. The results suggest an…

title: Utopia of Ideas - A Nozickian Utopian Defense of the Right to Moderate Digital Content
abstract: Abstract In this paper I present two presumptive considerations in favor of extensive content moderation rights for digital platforms. I first develop a defense of this system as implementing a close realization of Robert Nozick’s conception of a utopian society. I argue that granting digital platforms such rights approximates Nozick’s picture of utopia on normatively relevant metrics. Second, I present a presumptive, partly Nozickian, humility-based case against the regulation of content moderation. Surprisingly, the Nozickian framework will turn out to be in principle compatible with some powerful regulatory tools, and thus does not entail a thoroughgoing cyberlibertarianism without additional assumptions, which I briefly discuss in closing.

title: From exposure to imprint: CEO formative experiences and the architecture of accounting and financial decisions
abstract: Purpose This review explains how chief executive officers' formative experiences become organizationally consequential and why apparently similar exposures are associated with different accounting, financing, risk and stakeholder decisions. Design/methodology/approach Following the Search-Appraisal-Analysis-Synthesis (SAAS) workflow, the study maps 105 Scopus-indexed journal articles published between 2011 and 2026 using Biblioshiny and VOSviewer and conducts a structured content synthesis of 102 studies whose focal construct is an executive formative experience. Findings The literature converges around upper-echelons and imprinting perspectives but does not support a uniform “adversity produces conservatism” account. The synthesis distinguishes four adversity-related imprint families – threat vigilance and loss avoidance; uncertainty habituation, resilience or self-efficacy; scarcity orientation; and prosocial reorientation – while treating institutional socialization as conceptually distinct. Persistent imprints become observable only when later situations activate them and when executive discretion permits expression. Accounting and financing architecture provides particularly discriminating tests of these mechanisms. Originality/value The review moves beyond exposure–outcome associations by separating exposure formation, imprint content, activation, expression and observed …

title: ASSESSMENT OF RIGHT VENTRICULAR SYSTOLIC FUNCTION USING 2D AND 3D ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY IN PATIENTS WITH DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY
abstract: Background: Impaired Right Ventricular (RV) systolic function in patients with Dilated Cardiomyopathy (DCM) carries substantial prognostic significance and predicts cardiovascular death and hospitalization. Therefore, this study is intended to assess RV systolic function in patients with DCM using 2-Dimensional (2D) and 3-Dimensional (3D) Echocardiography. Aim: To correlate the 2D and 3D echocardiographic modalities for a better calibration for assessment of RV systolic function in patient with dilated cardiomyopathy Methods and Results: This hospital-based comparative cross-sectional study was conducted at KLE’S Dr. Prabhakar Kore Hospital and Medical Research Centre, Belagavi, from March 2020 to February 2021. Thirty-five patients who were hospitalized, non-hospitalized or out-patients diagnosed with DCM with or without signs of heart failure were included. This study compared various parameters assessed by 2D and 3D Echo modalities for evaluating RV size, RV volumes and RV ejection fraction (RVEF) in patients with DCM. Results: Male predominance (68.57%) has been observed in the study. The commonest (31.43%) ECG/EKG finding noted was complete or incomplete Left bundle branch block (LBBB). Severe LV systolic dilation assessed by LV internal systolic dimension (LVISd) by 2D//M-mode echo (LVISd) was noted in most of these patients (68.57%), which strongly indicates Severe LV sy…

title: Financial Literacy for Islamic Boarding School Students: Building a Fundamental Understanding of Money Management
abstract: Purpose: This community service program aimed to improve the financial literacy of students (santri) at Pesantren Muhammadiyah Cabang Tanjung Duren by enhancing their understanding of personal financial management, financial planning, income and expense management, and the importance of saving as a foundation for developing financial independence. Method: The program was conducted through a collaboration between the Faculty of Economics and Business, Universitas Trisakti, and Pesantren Muhammadiyah Cabang Tanjung Duren. The training employed an educational approach consisting of lectures, interactive discussions, and practical explanations on basic financial literacy concepts. The activities focused on introducing fundamental principles of responsible financial management and encouraging participants to apply these concepts in their daily lives. Practical Applications: The program provides practical knowledge that enables santri to manage their personal finances more effectively by planning expenditures, controlling financial resources, and cultivating saving habits. The knowledge gained can also serve as a foundation for managing small-scale entrepreneurial activities and promoting responsible financial behavior, thereby supporting the development of financial independence within the pesantren community. Conclusion: The financial literacy training successfully enhanced partici…

title: Improving MSME Financial Governance Through SIAPIK And BukuWarung Education During Industrial Visit
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to improve MSME financial governance by educating participants on digital recording applications (SIAPIK and BukuWarung), addressing the prevalent issue of manual and unstructured financial management in MSMEs. Method: This community service employed an educational approach via an industrial visit to PT. Bakpia Juwara Satoe. Methods included field observation, interactive material delivery, application demonstrations, and participatory evaluation. Practical Applications: The initiative provides MSMEs with accessible digital tools for real-time transaction recording and automated financial reporting, enhancing operational efficiency, business decision-making, and access to formal financing. Conclusion: The activity successfully enhanced participants' digital accounting literacy. Integrating industrial visits with practical application training effectively equips MSMEs to adopt systematic, accurate, and accountable financial management practices.

title: Methodology for Financial Evaluation of Investment Projects for the Production of Dual-Use Products
The broad reach of financial socialisation in the home
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether cognitive ability, gender, socioeconomic status (SES), interest in finance and country context condition the association between parental financial socialisation and young adults' objective financial knowledge and subjective financial knowledge (financial confidence). By examining both outcomes together, the study addresses a gap concerning the boundary conditions of family financial socialisation. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on data from 353 university students across Australia, New Zealand and New Caledonia, objective financial knowledge was measured using a ten-item test and financial confidence using subjective financial knowledge. Parental financial socialisation was measured with the Parent Financial Socialisation Scale (PFSS). Ordinary least squares regressions and PROCESS Model 1 moderation tests incorporated fluid intelligence, approximate numeracy, cognitive reflection, gender, SES, financial-information engagement and country controls. Common-method-bias diagnostics were also conducted. Findings Parental financial socialisation was positively associated with both objective financial knowledge and financial confidence. Fluid intelligence, approximate numeracy and cognitive reflection were associated with objective financial knowledge, whereas only cognitive reflection among the cognitive measures was associated with financia…

title: Financial Management Extension And Training For MSMEs In Saparua District, Central Maluku Regency
abstract: Purpose: To improve the financial literacy and management skills of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Saparua District, focusing on transaction recording, cash flow management, and separating business from household finances. Method: Conducted on August 13–15, 2026, involving 30 MSME participants. Activities included socialization, instructional sessions, practical exercises, and smartphone-based training using the “Buku Kas” application, evaluated descriptively. Practical Applications: Participants demonstrated increased awareness and skills in recording transactions, monitoring cash flows, and managing capital. The “Buku Kas” application provided a simple digital tool for systematic financial management. Conclusion: The program strengthened foundational financial management knowledge and provided practical digital tools for sustainable MSME management. Continued mentoring is recommended to ensure independent application use.

title: Unveiling the impact of ESG and financial stress on European banks' profitability
abstract: Purpose This study examines how Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance influences bank profitability and how this relationship is shaped by financial stress conditions in the European banking sector. Design/methodology/approach The analysis is based on panel data from 30 European banks across 13 countries over the period 2012–2021. The study employs Panel Estimated Generalized Least Squares, System Generalized Method of Moments, and quantile regression techniques to assess linear, nonlinear, and heterogeneous effects. Findings The results show that ESG performance positively affects bank profitability, while financial stress significantly reduces it and weakens ESG benefits. The relationship is nonlinear, with ESG effects strengthening beyond certain thresholds, while social factors enhance performance, environmental effects remain limited, and governance improves resilience but exhibits diminishing returns at higher levels. Practical implications Banks should strategically calibrate ESG investments, particularly governance, to balance costs and benefits, especially under financial stress. Policymakers should promote incentive-based frameworks that support ESG adoption without imposing excessive short-term burdens. Originality/value This study contributes by integrating financial stress into the ESG–financial performance nexus, highlighting nonlinear dynamics a…

title: Artificial intelligence (AI) in construction finance: transforming cost estimation, risk management and financial performance
abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming construction finance by improving cost estimation, cash flow forecasting, financial risk assessment, procurement and decision support. However, research remains fragmented across AI subfields and financial functions, limiting a comprehensive understanding of how AI creates financial value within construction organisations. This study aims to synthesise contemporary literature and develop an integrated conceptual framework of AI-enabled construction finance. Design/methodology/approach A structured integrative literature review was conducted using a transparent search and screening protocol. Forty-six peer-reviewed studies published between January 2021 and June 2026 were systematically identified, screened and coded using Gioia’s hierarchical coding methodology to examine AI subfields, construction finance applications, organisational benefits, implementation challenges and emerging research directions. Findings Machine learning (ML) and optimisation dominate existing research because of their widespread application to cost estimation, cash flow forecasting, financial risk assessment and resource optimisation. Computer vision, natural language processing, robotics and automated planning remain comparatively underexplored but demonstrate growing potential to enhance project controls, contract administration and operational eff…

title: Sharia Digital Economic Empowerment Through Financial Education And QRIS Implementation In Rural MSMEs
abstract: Purpose: This study critically analyzes Sharia digital economic empowerment for rural MSMEs, addressing the gap where QRIS infrastructure expansion precedes community cognitive readiness. Method: Using a descriptive qualitative approach based on Participatory Action Research, the study focuses on Rita Chips MSME as a purposive single case. Data were collected through participatory observation, in-depth interviews, and financial documentation across three sequential intervention stages: Sharia financial literacy education, bookkeeping assistance, and QRIS facilitation. Practical Applications: The results show that partners initially relying on unrecorded cash transactions overcame cognitive and administrative resistance through the principle of trustworthiness and clear net profit calculation, enabling smooth QRIS adoption with only infrastructural barriers remaining. Conclusion: QRIS is effective as a downstream, rather than upstream, instrument in a validated, replicable village-based Sharia digital empowerment model.

EU skilled circular migration and financial risk
abstract: Purpose This study examines which institutional and labor market conditions are associated with balanced reciprocal skilled mobility between EU country pairs and how these conditions relate to human capital allocation risk. Design/methodology/approach The analysis uses an annual panel of undirected EU27 country pairs from 2004 to 2020, restricted to pair-years in which both countries were EU members. The outcome is a weighted corridor-level index combining reciprocal balance and skilled flow volume. It captures balanced reciprocal skilled mobility, not repeated movement by the same individuals. Country-pair fixed effects, year effects, lagged predictors, mediation, moderated mediation and alternative outcome checks are applied. Findings Destination skill shortages are positively associated with balanced reciprocal skilled mobility. Qualification recognition has no statistically significant direct association with the outcome, but the recognition-to-employment-absorption pathway is positive. This indirect pathway weakens as overqualification risk rises. Research limitations/implications Aggregate pair-year flows cannot identify return or repeated movement by the same workers. The design therefore supports corridor-level inference about balanced reciprocal mobility rather than individual circular migration. The models also identify an upstream human capital allocation channel rat…

title: Pure laparoscopic donor right hepatectomy versus open donor right hepatectomy in living donor liver transplantation: A GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis
Effect of physical, psychological and demographic factors of construction craft workers on hazard recognition performance and safety risk perception
abstract: Purpose Despite advances in safety protocols, the construction industry still experiences high occupational injury rates, partly due to limitations in craft workers’ hazard recognition performance (HRP) and safety risk perception (SRP). However, prior research has largely examined antecedents of safety cognition in isolation, with limited attention to the combined effects of physical, psychological and demographic factors, including sleep quality, job stress, fatigue, education, experience and age. This study aims to examine the combined associations of physical (fatigue, sleep quality), psychological (job stress) and demographic (age, education, experience) factors to provide a more systemic understanding of safety cognition. Specifically, safety risk perception is operationalized through the Discrepancy in Safety Risk Perception Index, which measures the alignment or discrepancy between workers’ subjective risk assessments and an established expert-referenced benchmark. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional quantitative design was used, integrating structured surveys with image-based hazard identification tasks. Data were collected from 96 construction craft workers across 11 construction projects in Iran using validated instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to test the hypothesized direct and mediated pathways, with fatigue position…

title: Exploring the System Security Veil: Uncovering Domestic Motivation to Establish Capacity Remuneration Mechanisms (CRMs) (online first)
abstract: Nation states face critical trade-offs between energy security, efficiency, and climate goals when implementing Capacity Remuneration Mechanisms (CRMs). This study investigates factors influencing CRM adoption and design choices (targeted strategic reserves versus market-wide approaches) across EU member states from 2008–2021. Using logistic regression analysis on a new dataset, the research examines techno-economic, socio-technical, and political influences. Results show that while renewable integration creates legitimate security challenges, state responses reflect political preferences as much as technical necessities. Key adoption predictors include electricity heating dependence and gas energy share as well as intermittent energy, while interconnection capacity strongly predicts non-adoption — suggesting technical decisions often reflect deeper preferences about energy autonomy versus market integration. The choice between targeted and market-wide designs is influenced by party ideology, carbon intensity, and existing energy mix interests. This research reveals how functional pressures, generator interests, and politicization shape responses to system security concerns, which implies different decarbonization pathways.

title: Equilibrium models to analyse the impact of different coordination schemes between TSO and DSOs on market power in sequentially-cleared energy and ancillary services markets under load and renewable generation uncertainty
abstract: The current massive installation of distributed resources in electricity distribution systems is transforming these systems into active dispatching subjects. At the same time, the need to compensate for the intermittent generation of an increasing amount of renewable sources creates the need to acquire more ancillary services. Flexible resources in the distribution system could provide these services not only within the perimeter of the distribution network to which they are connected but also for the benefit of the transmission system. However, this requires Transmission System Operators (TSOs) and Distribution System Operators (DSOs) to coordinate their dispatching actions effectively. One critical aspect of this coordination is establishing a market architecture that limits market power. This paper presents an innovative game-theoretic approach to compare different TSO-DSO coordination models for acquiring ancillary services from distribution resources. Several schemes are considered: some with coordinated market management by TSOs and DSOs, others with sequential or independent local markets. For each scheme, the dispatching problem is formulated as a two-stage stochastic sequential game, where the first stage is the day-ahead market and the second stage is the balancing market. Nash equilibrium solutions are obtained by iteratively solving the profit maximization problem o…

title: A Risk-Based Probabilistic Transient Stability Approach for Ranking of Circuit Breakers in a Power System
abstract: Power systems are getting more complex than ever and are consequently operating close to their limit of stability. Moreover, with the increasing demand of renewable wind generation, and the requirement to maintain a secure power system, the importance of transient stability cannot be overestimated. Current deterministic industry practices of transient stability assessment ignore the probability of variables involved. With increasing system uncertainties and widespread electricity market deregulation, there is a strong inevitability to incorporate probabilistic transient stability analysis. Circuit breakers play a critical role in fault clearing and consequently in determining the system transient stability. It is important that they undergo timely and appropriate maintenance procedures based on some criterion. Considering the need of incorporating risk in modern power systems, this paper proposes a risk-based probabilistic transient stability approach for ranking of circuit breakers in a power system. A novel priority index was proposed to rank the circuit breakers based on the system transient stability risk. DIgSILENT PowerFactory software was used to conduct the required simulations on IEEE 14 bus system. The proposed risk-based framework was deemed to be efficient in identification of the circuit breakers based on their priority rank index which can aid in power system plan…

title: A Hybrid Strategy for Probabilistic Forecasting and Trading of Aggregated Wind-Solar Power: Design and Analysis in HEFTCom2024
abstract: Obtaining accurate probabilistic energy forecasts and making effective decisions amid diverse uncertainties are routine challenges in future energy systems. This paper presents the winning solution of team GEB, which ranked 3rd in trading, 4th in forecasting, and 1st among student teams in the IEEE Hybrid Energy Forecasting and Trading Competition 2024 (HEFTCom2024). The solution provides accurate probabilistic forecasts for a wind-solar hybrid system, and achieves substantial trading revenue in the day-ahead electricity market. Key components include: (1) a stacking-based approach combining sister forecasts from various Numerical Weather Predictions (NWPs) to provide wind power forecasts, (2) an online solar post-processing model to address the distribution shift in the online test set caused by increased solar capacity, (3) a probabilistic aggregation method for accurate quantile forecasts of hybrid generation, and (4) a stochastic trading strategy to maximize expected trading revenue considering uncertainties in electricity prices. This paper also explores the potential of end-to-end learning to further enhance the trading revenue by shifting the distribution of forecast errors. Detailed case studies are provided to validate the effectiveness of these proposed methods. Code for all mentioned methods is available for reproduction and further research in both industry and acad…

title: Economic evaluation and feasibility design of an electricity-hydrogen market with hydrogen-based system: Mathematical model and techno-economic analysis
Challenges and prospectives of energy storage integration in renewable energy systems for net zero transition
Congestion-Sensitive Grid Aggregation for DC Optimal Power Flow
abstract: The vast spatial dimension of modern interconnected electricity grids challenges the tractability of the DC optimal power flow problem. Grid aggregation methods try to overcome this challenge by reducing the number of network elements. Many existing methods use Locational Marginal Prices as a distance metric to cluster nodes. In this paper, we show that prevalent methods adopting this distance metric fail to adequately capture the impact of individual lines when there is more than one line congested. This leads to suboptimal outcomes for the optimization of the aggregated model. To overcome those issues, we propose two methods based on the novel Network Congestion Price metric, which preserves the impact of nodal power injections on individual line congestions. The proposed methods are compared to several existing aggregation methods based on Locational Marginal Prices. We demonstrate all methods on adapted versions of the IEEE RTS 24- and 300-Bus systems. We show that the proposed methods outperform existing approaches both in terms of objective function value error and maximum line limit violation, while exhibiting faster node clustering. We conclude that aggregation methods based on the novel Network Congestion Price metric are better at preserving the essential physical characteristics of the network topology in the grid aggregation process than methods based on Locational …

title: Integrated equilibrium model for electrified logistics and power systems
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated equilibrium model to characterize the complex interactions between electrified logistics systems and electric power delivery systems. The model consists of two major players: an electrified logistics operator (ELO) and a power system operator (PSO). The ELO aims to maximize its profit by strategically scheduling and routing its electric delivery vehicles (e-trucks) for deliveries and charging, in response to the locational marginal price (LMP) set by the PSO. The routing, delivery, and charging behaviors of e-trucks are modeled by a perturbed utility Markov decision process (PU-MDP) while their collective operations are optimized to achieve the ELO's objective by designing rewards in the PU-MDP. On the other hand, PSO optimizes the energy price by considering both the spatiotemporal e-truck charging demand and the base electricity load. The equilibrium of the integrated system is formulated as a fixed point, proved to exist under mild assumptions, and solved for a case study on the Hawaii network via Anderson's fixed-point acceleration algorithm. Along with these numerical results, this paper provides both theoretical insights and practical guidelines to achieve sustainable and efficient operations in modern electrified logistics and power systems.

Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning based demand response and energy management for heavy industries with discrete manufacturing systems
abstract: Energy-centric decarbonization of heavy industries, such as steel and cement, necessitates their participation in integrating Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and effective Demand Response (DR) programs. This situation has created the opportunities to research control algorithms in diverse DR scenarios. Further, the industrial sector’s unique challenges, including the diversity of operations and the need for uninterrupted production, bring unique challenges in designing and implementing control algorithms. Reinforcement learning (RL) methods are practical solutions to the unique challenges faced by the industrial sector. Nevertheless, research in RL for industrial demand response has not yet achieved the level of standardization seen in other areas of RL research, hindering broader progress. To propel the research progress, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL)-based energy management system designed to optimize energy consumption in energy-intensive industrial settings by leveraging dynamic pricing DR schemes. The study highlights the creation of a MARL environment and addresses these challenges by designing a general framework that allows researchers to replicate and implement MARL environments for industrial sectors. The proposed framework incorporates a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) to model energy consumption and production processes w…

title: Energy poverty and children’s subjective well-being: evidence from young lives data
abstract: This study examines the impact of energy poverty on the subjective well-being of children in four developing countries: Ethiopia, India, Peru, and Vietnam. We assess energy poverty using a multidimensional approach, leveraging data from the Young Lives study, which conducted surveys in 2006, 2009, 2013, and 2016 (Rounds 2 to 5). Our analysis focuses on the young cohort (Rounds 3 to 5) and the older cohort (Rounds 2 to 5), as these rounds include questions on children’s subjective well-being. To mitigate potential endogeneity concerns and establish causal relationships, we employ a two-stage least squares regression, using residential electricity prices at the country level as an instrumental variable. Our findings reveal that energy poverty significantly reduces children’s subjective well-being, with boys and older children more affected. Robustness checks confirm the validity of these results. Additionally, we find that health status mediates the impact of energy poverty on children’s well-being, highlighting the importance of targeted policy interventions.

title: Market-oriented operational strategy for biomass-geothermal combined power generation and hydrogen production plant
Capacity remuneration mechanisms for decarbonized power systems
abstract: Motivated by generation system adequacy concerns, many European countries have introduced capacity remuneration mechanisms (CRMs) to ensure sufficient investments in power generation . However, it is uncertain whether the existing CRMs will promote sufficient adequacy and flexibility in a decarbonized power system , where supply and demand will become more weather-dependent. We assess the effectiveness of a centralized capacity market, a strategic reserve , and a decentralized capacity market via capacity subscriptions in a climate-neutral, weather-driven power system. We develop a co-simulation of two agent-based models simulating myopia in both operational and investment decisions. We simulate weather uncertainty by running the model with 40 different weather years. Our results from a case study based on the Netherlands indicate that a strategic reserve may increase electricity price volatility in the long-term. A centralized capacity market is more cost-effective than a strategic reserve, but administratively setting its parameters is prone to over- or underprocurement. Capacity subscription allows consumers to select their desired level of reliability. Results indicate that these decentralized capacity markets may yield a clearer signal for the needed dispatchable capacity and promote demand-side response, but it may be challenging to provide long-term certainty for investo…

title: Local energy monitoring to support smart energy management and decarbonized town development
abstract: Introduction With the increase in variable renewable energy and liberalization of the electricity retail market, the integrated energy management of demand and supply has become crucial, complementing traditional energy-saving efforts. Therefore, high-resolution energy demand-side information, accounting for household attributes and owned equipment, is essential. However, previous studies have identified energy consumption based on surveys of utility bill payments; this approach does not provide detailed, hourly data on electricity demand, which changes over time owing to lifestyle patterns and weather conditions. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the actual electricity consumption in residential buildings in Shinchi Town using the developed electricity monitoring system.Material and Method In support of regional disaster recovery initiatives, we developed a regional information and communication technology (ICT) system as a network interface for residents. As part of a social experiment, network terminals of the local ICT system were distributed to approximately 100 households in the town. Power monitoring data were collected via equipment installed in home distribution boards and centrally managed by a cloud server.Results and Conclusion We analyzed electric power consumption patterns, focusing on household attributes, seasonal variations in hot-water-supply device usage, an…

title: Impact of Regional and Seasonal Characteristics on Battery Electric Vehicle Operational Costs in the U.S.
abstract: This study investigates the operational cost competitiveness of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) in the United States, considering regional climates, energy prices, and driving patterns. By comparing BEVs with plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), and the alternative use of BEVs and conventional vehicles (Convs), the analysis incorporates thermal dynamometer tests, real-world vehicle miles traveled (VMT), and state-specific energy prices. Using detailed simulations, the study evaluates energy consumption across varying temperatures and driving distances. The findings reveal that, while BEVs remain cost-effective for short trips in moderate climates, PHEVs are more economical for long-range trips and cold environments, due to the excessive cost of using external direct current fast chargers (DCFCs) and reduced BEV efficiency at low temperatures. HEVs are identified as the most cost-efficient option in regions like New England, characterized by high residential electricity prices. These insights are critical for shaping vehicle electrification strategies, particularly under diverse regional and seasonal conditions, and for advancing policies on alternative energy and fuels.

title: Sharing the shortfall: Algorithmic solutions for fair demand curtailment in zonal power markets
Online Multivariate Regularized Distributional Regression for High-dimensional Probabilistic Electricity Price Forecasting
abstract: Probabilistic electricity price forecasting (PEPF) is vital for short-term electricity markets, yet the multivariate nature of day-ahead prices - spanning 24 consecutive hours - remains underexplored. At the same time, real-time decision-making requires methods that are both accurate and fast. We introduce an online algorithm for multivariate distributional regression models, allowing efficient modeling of the conditional means, variances, and dependence structures of electricity prices. The approach combines multivariate distributional regression with online coordinate descent and LASSO-type regularization (absolute shrinkage and selection operator), enabling scalable estimation in high-dimensional covariate spaces. Additionally, we propose a regularized estimation path over increasingly complex dependence structures, allowing for early stopping and avoiding overfitting. In a case study using historical data from the German day-ahead market, the proposed method yields interpretable and well-calibrated joint prediction intervals for the 24-dimensional price distribution and provides robust performance across a range of proper scoring rules. The results underscore the importance of modeling the dependence structure of electricity prices. Furthermore, we analyze the trade-off between predictive accuracy and computational costs for batch and online estimation and provide a high-pe…

title: Loss-aware Pricing Strategies for Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading
abstract: Peer-to-peer(P2P) energy trading may increase efficiency and reduce costs, but introduces significant challenges for network operators such as maintaining grid reliability, accounting for network losses, and redistributing costs equitably. We propose a novel loss-aware pricing strategy for P2P energy markets that addresses these challenges while incentivizing participation in the cooperative energy trading market. The problem is formulated as a hierarchical Stackelberg game, where a grid operator determines network tariffs while prosumers optimize their trades based on these tariffs while guaranteeing that network constraints are satisfied. The algorithm is designed to minimize and recover their cost from the trading parties, while also minimizing the total cost of the hubs. The mechanism dynamically adjusts tariffs based on location and network topology, discouraging loss-intensive trades. Finally, the complete framework includes the computation of fair trading prices, ensuring all market participants benefit equitably. An ADMM-based hyper-gradient descent method is proposed for solving this problem. Extensive numerical simulations using the benchmark IEEE 33-bus system demonstrate significant cost reductions and improved network efficiency through reduction in network losses compared to constant tariff schemes. Results highlight the adaptability and scalability of the propose…

title: Master–Slave Game Pricing Strategy of Time-of-Use Electricity Price of Electricity Retailers Considering Users’ Electricity Utility and Satisfaction
abstract: With the establishment of a competitive electricity retail market, how to optimize the retail electricity price mechanism has become the core of all kinds of retail companies to explore. Aiming at the pricing problem of time-of-use electricity price, this paper proposes a pricing strategy based on the master–slave game model. Firstly, considering the user’s electricity utility and satisfaction factors, the comprehensive benefit function of the electricity selling company with electricity price as the decision variable and the user’s comprehensive benefit function with electricity consumption as the decision variable are established, respectively. Then, a master–slave game model is established with the electricity selling company as the leader and the user as the follower, and the reverse induction method is used to solve the model. Finally, considering the influencing factors of user response ability, different electricity price types and user types are set up for simulation. The results show that the revenue of electricity retailers can be increased by up to 170,000 yuan, and the average electricity price of users can be reduced by up to 8 yuan. It is verified that the model can effectively achieve a win-win situation for both sides and promote peak shaving and valley filling. At the same time, it is proved that the role of the model is positively related to electricity price …

title: Federated Reinforcement Learning for decentralized peer-to-peer energy trading
abstract: The rapid development of distributed energy resources has led to an increasing number of prosumers enhancing their energy utilization, thereby raising the demands on energy management technologies. As a result, the development of future smart grids is becoming increasingly important, with a particular emphasis on integrating demand-side flexibility into electricity market. To facilitate distributed interaction among prosumers, the double-side auction market enables peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading , maximizing the social welfare within the dynamic local electricity market. In this setup, prosumers can set their own bidding prices and optimize their operations and trading strategies. However, trading in double-side auction market faces limitations due to the complexity of the market clearing algorithm and the difficulty of predicting other participants’ bidding behaviors. To address these challenges, this paper models the P2P energy trading problem in the double-side auction market as a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) task. The concept of federated learning is introduced to enhance scalability among market participants while protecting the private information of individual prosumers. Additionally, the parameter-sharing framework is proposed to accelerate the learning process . To further improve the stability of MARL training, the global information of P2P energy trad…

title: Short communication: Local electricity-hydrogen market
Extrapolating the long-term seasonal component of electricity prices for forecasting in the day-ahead market
abstract: Recent studies provide evidence that decomposing the electricity price into the long-term seasonal component (LTSC) and the remaining part, predicting both separately, and then combining their forecasts can bring significant accuracy gains in day-ahead electricity price forecasting. However, not much attention has been paid to predicting the LTSC, and the last 24 hourly values of the estimated pattern are typically copied for the target day. To address this gap, we introduce a novel approach which extracts the trend-seasonal pattern from a price series extrapolated using price forecasts for the next 24 hours. We assess it using two 5-year long test periods from the German and Spanish power markets, covering the Covid-19 pandemic, the 2021/2022 energy crisis, and the war in Ukraine. Considering parsimonious autoregressive and LASSO-estimated models, we find that improvements in predictive accuracy range from 3\% to 15\% in terms of the root mean squared error and exceed 1\% in terms of profits from a realistic trading strategy involving day-ahead bidding and battery storage.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Bidding Strategies for Prosumers Trading in Double Auction-Based Transactive Energy Market
abstract: With the large number of prosumers deploying distributed energy resources (DERs), integrating these prosumers into a transactive energy market (TEM) is a trend for the future smart grid. A community-based double auction market is considered a promising TEM that can encourage prosumers to participate and maximize social welfare. However, the traditional TEM is challenging to model explicitly due to the random bidding behavior of prosumers and uncertainties caused by the energy operation of DERs. Furthermore, although reinforcement learning algorithms provide a model-free solution to optimize prosumers' bidding strategies, their use in TEM is still challenging due to their scalability, stability, and privacy protection limitations. To address the above challenges, in this study, we design a double auction-based TEM with multiple DERs-equipped prosumers to transparently and efficiently manage energy transactions. We also propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) model with distributed learning and execution to ensure the scalability and privacy of the market environment. Additionally, the design of two bidding actions (i.e., bidding price and quantity) optimizes the bidding strategies for prosumers. Simulation results show that (1) the designed TEM and DRL model are robust; (2) the proposed DRL model effectively balances the energy payment and comfort satisfaction for prosumers …

title: Expanding the economic benefits of waste gasification through carbon and green certificate markets:Optimal bidding strategies in multiple markets
The Impact of Integrating Variable Renewable Energy Sources into Grid-Connected Power Systems: Challenges, Mitigation Strategies, and Prospects
abstract: Although the impact of integrating solar and wind sources into the power system has been studied in the past, the chaos caused by wind and solar energy generation has not yet had broader mitigation solutions notwithstanding their rapid deployment. Many research efforts in using prediction models have developed real-time monitoring of variability and machine learning predictive algorithms in contrast to the conventional methods of studying variability. This study focused on the causes and types of variability, challenges, and mitigation strategies used to minimize variability in grids worldwide. A summary of the top ten cases of countries that have successfully managed variability in their electrical power grids has been presented. Review shows that most of the success cases embraced advanced energy storage, grid upgrading, and flexible energy mix as key technological and economic strategies. A seven-point conceptual framework involving all energy stakeholders for managing variability in power system networks and increasing variable renewable energy (VRE)-grid integration has been proposed. Long-duration energy storage, virtual power plants (VPPs), smart grid infrastructure, cross-border interconnection, power-to-X, and grid flexibility are the key takeaways in achieving a reliable, resilient, and stable grid. This review provides a useful summary of up-to-date research informat…

title: Deregulating Grid-Enhancing Technologies Through Financial Transmission Rights
abstract: To accommodate the increasing share of renewable energy, the transmission network needs to be upgraded. Grid-enhancing technologies (GETs) are attractive alternatives that can replace or complement grid expansion. GETs enhance grid flexibility and increase the transfer capability over the current network. A main challenge facing proliferation of GETs is the lack of proper financial incentives for their adoption and efficient operation. This paper develops a novel Financial Transmission Right (FTR) allocation mechanism to incentivize GETs installation. The model allocates maximum feasible incremental FTRs in the directions requested by investors, while keeping existing FTRs feasible. Using the concept of proxy FTRs, the investors can only obtain incremental FTRs that their investment enables through enhancing the transfer capability. The paper shows that the proposed method is revenue adequate. Two major types of GETs are presented as representative investments that are compatible with the proposed model. These include series flexible ac transmission system (FACTS) devices, such as variable-impedance FACTS and devices based on voltage-sourced converters (VSC), as well as voltage phase controllers. The proposed model is first illustrated on a 3-bus system and then implemented on the IEEE 30-bus system to show its efficiency and scalability.

title: Distributionally Fair Peer-to-Peer Electricity Trading
abstract: Peer-to-peer energy trading platforms enable direct electricity exchanges between peers who belong to the same energy community. In a semi-decentralized system, a community manager adheres to grid restrictions while optimizing social welfare. However, with no further supervision, some peers can be discriminated against from participating in the electricity trades. To solve this issue, this paper proposes an optimization-based mechanism to enable distributionally fair peer-to-peer electricity trading. For the implementation of our mechanism, peers are grouped by energy poverty level. The proposed model aims to redistribute the electricity trades to minimize the maximum Wasserstein distance among the transaction distributions linked to the groups while limiting the sacrifice level with a predefined parameter. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposal using the IEEE 33-bus distribution grid, simulating an energy community with 1600 peers. Results indicate that up to 70.1% of unfairness can be eliminated by using our proposed model, even achieving a full elimination when including a non-profit community photovoltaic plant.

title: A data-driven merit order: Learning a fundamental electricity price model
abstract: Electricity price forecasting approaches generally fall into two categories: data-driven models, which learn from historical patterns, or fundamental models, which simulate market mechanisms. We propose a novel and highly efficient data-driven merit order model that integrates both paradigms. The model embeds the classical expert-based merit order as a nested special case, allowing all key parameters, such as plant efficiencies, bidding behavior, and available capacities, to be estimated directly from historical data, rather than assumed. We further enhance the model with critical embedded extensions such as hydro power, cross-border flows and corrections for underreported capacities, which considerably improve forecasting accuracy. Applied to the German day-ahead market, our model outperforms both classic fundamental and state-of-the-art machine learning models. It retains the interpretability of fundamental models, offering insights into marginal technologies, fuel switches, and dispatch patterns, elements which are typically inaccessible to black-box machine learning approaches. This transparency and high computational efficiency make it a promising new direction for electricity price modeling.

title: Real-Time Price-Based Demand Response for Industrial Manufacturing Process via Safe Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Industrial manufacturing processes present unique challenges in implementing demand response due to their complex equipment interactions, diverse operation modes, and safety constraints. Conventional model-based optimization methods often struggle in this context, requiring complete mathematical models and accurate uncertainty distributions. In this article, we propose a model-free safe deep reinforcement learning approach for real-time scheduling of industrial manufacturing systems, ensuring constraint adherence and accommodating diverse equipment operation modes. Specifically, the approach formulates the industrial demand response problem as a constrained Markov decision process with hybrid action space, capturing the intricate interplay between variable-speed equipment and discrete actuators, while considering safety constraints. To enhance exploration and robustness, the proposed method combines Lagrange multipliers based on soft actor–critic to satisfy the constraints. The cross-attention mechanism is utilized to find the association rules between hybrid actions to solve the challenges posed by the spatial gradient of hybrid actions. The proposed approach is trained and tested on a real-world dataset, demonstrating its superior performance in achieving significant cost reductions for manufacturing while satisfying operational constraints. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis …

title: Conformal Uncertainty Quantification of Electricity Price Predictions for Risk-Averse Storage Arbitrage
abstract: This paper proposes a risk-averse approach to energy storage price arbitrage, leveraging conformal uncertainty quantification for electricity price predictions. The method addresses the significant challenges posed by the inherent volatility and uncertainty of real-time electricity prices, which create substantial risks of financial losses for energy storage participants relying on future price forecasts to plan their operations. The framework comprises a two-layer prediction model to quantify real-time price uncertainty confidence intervals with high coverage. The framework is distribution-free and can work with any underlying point prediction model. We evaluate the quantification effectiveness through storage price arbitrage application by managing the risk of participating in the real-time market. We design a risk-averse policy for profit-maximization of energy storage arbitrage to find the safest storage schedule with very minimal losses. Using historical data from New York State and synthetic price predictions, our evaluations demonstrate that this framework can achieve good profit margins with less than $35\%$ purchases.

title: Bidding in Ancillary Service Markets: An Analytical Approach Using Extreme Value Theory
abstract: To enable the participation of stochastic distributed energy resources in ancillary service markets, the Danish transmission system operator, Energinet, mandates that flexibility providers satisfy a minimum 90% reliability requirement for reserve bids. This paper examines the bidding strategy of an electric vehicle aggregator under this regulation and develops a chance-constrained optimization model. In contrast to conventional sample-based approaches that demand large datasets to capture uncertainty, we propose an analytical reformulation that leverages extreme value theory to characterize the tail behavior of flexibility distributions. A case study with real-world charging data from 1400 residential electric vehicles in Denmark demonstrates that the analytical solution improves out-of-sample reliability, reducing bid violation rates by up to 8% relative to a sample-based benchmark. The method is also computationally more efficient, solving optimization problems up to 4.8 times faster while requiring substantially fewer samples to ensure compliance. Moreover, the proposed approach enables the construction of feasible bids with reliability levels as high as 99.95%, which would otherwise require prohibitively large scenario sets under the sample-based method. Beyond its computational and reliability advantages, the framework also provides actionable insights into how reliability…

title: A Bottom-Up Approach to Optimizing the Solar Organic Rankine Cycle for Transactive Energy Trading
abstract: Solar Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC)-based power generation plants leverage solar irradiation to produce thermal energy, offering a highly compatible renewable technology due to the alignment between solar irradiation temperatures and ORC operating requirements. Their superior performance compared to steam Rankine cycles in small-scale applications makes them particularly relevant within the smart grid and microgrid contexts. This study explores the role of ORC in peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading within renewable-based community microgrids, where consumers become prosumers, simultaneously producing and consuming energy while engaging in virtual trading at the distribution system level. Focusing on a microgrid integrating solar ORC with a storage system to meet consumer demand, the paper highlights the importance of combining these technologies with storage to enhance predictability and competitiveness with conventional energy plants, despite management challenges. A methodology based on operations research techniques is developed to optimize system performance. Furthermore, the impact of various technological parameters of the solar ORC on the system's performance is examined. The study concludes by assessing the value of solar ORC within the transactive energy trading framework across different configurations and scenarios. Results demonstrate an average 16\% reduction in operat…

title: Anomaly Detection in California Electricity Price Forecasting: Enhancing Accuracy and Reliability Using Principal Component Analysis
abstract: Accurate and reliable electricity price forecasting has significant practical implications for grid management, renewable energy integration, power system planning, and price volatility management. This study focuses on enhancing electricity price forecasting in California's grid, addressing challenges from complex generation data and heteroskedasticity. Utilizing principal component analysis (PCA), we analyze CAISO's hourly electricity prices and demand from 2016-2021 to improve day-ahead forecasting accuracy. Initially, we apply traditional outlier analysis with the interquartile range method, followed by robust PCA (RPCA) for more effective outlier elimination. This approach improves data symmetry and reduces skewness. We then construct multiple linear regression models using both raw and PCA-transformed features. The model with transformed features, refined through traditional and SAS Sparse Matrix outlier removal methods, shows superior forecasting performance. The SAS Sparse Matrix method, in particular, significantly enhances model accuracy. Our findings demonstrate that PCA-based methods are key in advancing electricity price forecasting, supporting renewable integration and grid management in day-ahead markets. Keywords: Electricity price forecasting, principal component analysis (PCA), power system planning, heteroskedasticity, renewable energy integration.
